# Preface

It is not unknown to you that this **Jataka Parijata**, a work related to the modern science of astrology <note>original: "Jyotish-shastra"</note>, has now been accepted into the curriculum for the Acharya examinations <note>a high-level academic degree in Sanskrit studies</note> by all provincial government examination boards. However, following the saying "the commentary is the teacher of teachers," students found that achieving their desired goals in this difficult text was not possible even with long periods of intense labor. Consequently, students appearing for the examinations of the Government Sanskrit College of Varanasi and the Bihar Sanskrit Association repeatedly requested the Manager of the Chowkhamba Sanskrit Book Depot in Varanasi to address this. He, in turn, requested me to edit a simple commentary on this work (Jataka Parijata). Thus, with the permission of the Head of Examinations at the Government Sanskrit College of Varanasi, and with the intent of aiding students, I have completed this commentary—which illuminates the true nature of the subject—in a direct and easily accessible Sanskrit style. Furthermore, at the honorable request of the same bookstore manager, I revised the Hindi commentary written by the jewel of astrologers, Pandit Shri Matriprasad Shastri. I have revised the Hindi language almost word-for-word, and in places where I have provided my own linguistic explanations, I have used the code "Su. Sha. Ka." (Author of the *Sudhashalini* commentary). I have adorned this book with useful explanations, examples, proofs, mathematical charts, tables, and a table of contents, and have handed it over for publication to Shri Jayakrishna Das, the son of the late, great merchant Babu Haridas Gupta.

Whatever success I, a mere child with little strength, have achieved in this unfathomable ocean of knowledge is entirely due to the grace of your venerable feet. Therefore, may you learned scholars increase the enthusiasm of both the editor and the publisher by widely promoting this work produced by one of your own. I hope that the great-souled scholars, who desire the progress of their kin, will with great affection correct any errors arising from human confusion, printing mistakes, or visual fatigue, and encourage me with their feedback. For it is said:

> A slip of the foot occurs somewhere even for one who walks carefully, due to inadvertence.
> The wicked laugh at such things, but the virtuous set them right.

Furthermore, I have this submission before your honors: although I provided the publisher with an appendix filled with several highly useful subjects to be included at the end of this book, the publisher was unable to print it due to the scarcity of plates ( <term>paper</term> <note>original: "kargaja"</note> ) caused by the fury of the current Great World War <note>referring to World War II</note>. Therefore, both the publisher and I, the <unclear>editor</unclear>, beg for your forgiveness wherever the text mentions "see the appendix."

<unclear>The festival of Vijayadashami.</unclear>
<unclear>Vikram Samvat 1999 (approx. 1942 CE).</unclear>

->॥ Glory to the Divine ॥<-

# Introduction

> Victorious is that mass of radiance, composed of the three Vedas, the soul of all that moves and is stationary. <note>original: "jagattasthuṣām atmā" - a Vedic phrase referring to the Sun as the soul of the world.</note>
> The Sun, illuminating all lights by the self-existent splendor of his own soul. ॥ 1 ॥

It is well known to those learned men whose minds have been purified by all the Vedas and traditional scriptures, that in this world, for all living beings, the Veda alone is the shower of the path to ultimate well-being. There is no subject here that cannot be found by virtuous men seeking with true intent. This is the very system of governance of the Sun, the Lord and Controller of the universe; for this very purpose, the Lord first accepted the incarnation as a Fish <note>The Matsya Avatar, who recovered the Vedas from the depths of the ocean.</note>, and thus the six limbs <term>Vedangas: auxiliary disciplines for understanding the Vedas</term> which promote that knowledge—Phonetics, Ritual, Grammar, Astronomy/Astrology, Etymology, and Prosody—shall be proclaimed. As stated by the master Bhaskaracharya:

> Grammar is the mouth, Astronomy/Astrology the eyes, Etymology is called the ears, and Ritual the hands.
> Phonetics is the nose of this Veda, and the two lotus feet are Prosody, according to the ancient wise ones.

Among those six limbs, Astronomy/Astrology <term>Jyotisha: the science of light and time</term> is the primary seed of sacrifices, penance, charity, vows, and fasts, as it reveals direction, place, and time; therefore, its study and teaching are more essential than all other sciences. For this is the single conclusion of all the Vedas, auxiliary limbs, Upanishads, philosophies, Puranas, and histories: "God is to be worshipped by all of mankind through the rules of sacrifice, penance, charity, and vows." Furthermore, any action performed at the [correct] time results in success, while an action performed at the [incorrect] time results in failure; thus, there is a constant need for this science, which is the embodiment of Time. It is a general rule that everyone nourishes their own subject most abundantly. However, even with an impartial mind, it is proven that without this, no worldly or Vedic action of people attains success, as was also said by Narada:

> The pure eye of the Veda is the stainless science of Astronomy/Astrology.
> Without this, the entire collection of rituals—both those from the Vedas and those from the Law-books—is not accomplished.

Furthermore, "the Light can never be seen continuously [without its science]," thus the luminous, imperishable Lord Sun is the path to liberation (from the scripture: "The Sun is the soul of the moving and the stationary," and from the words of Varahamihira: "The path of those who are not to be reborn"). The luminous planets are portions of Him and are indeed gods (from the statement of Bhatta: "The planets are portions of the deities"). It is no exaggeration to say that they cannot be known by any science other than the multi-faceted science of Astronomy/Astrology.

Based on the sayings "The whole world is dependent on the gods" and "The planets are portions of the deities," the entire world is indeed dependent on the planets. In reality, it is only through the connection with the Sun's rays that the entire world (moving and unmoving) is born, lives, and maintains stability. Thus, three times a day... people worship the Sun with prayers such as: "May we see for a hundred autumns, may we live for a hundred autumns, may we hear for a hundred autumns, may we speak for a hundred autumns, may we remain independent for a hundred autumns, and even more than a hundred autumns." Without the science of Astronomy/Astrology, the knowledge of the position, measure, and movement of the sky, the celestial wanderers [planets], the earth, the mountains, the gods, the demons, and humans is not only difficult but impossible. Just as no living being can reach a desired or intended place safely without eyes, the path to the well-being of the world is in no way possible without the science of Astronomy/Astrology (the Eye).

<header>Introduction</header>

## Introduction

This science is not like other sciences, which are subject to doubt and are not perceptible to the senses; rather, it is entirely logical and perceptible. No other science is capable of demonstrating "this is exactly it," "it is happening right now," "it is right here," "it is only this much," or "it is exactly thus" in the way that the science of <term>Jyotisha</term><note>The traditional Indian system of astronomy and astrology, literally meaning the "science of light."</note> can. As it has been said:

> Other sciences are imperceptible; in them, there is only dispute.
> But the science of Jyotisha is perceptible, for the Sun and Moon are its witnesses.

Furthermore, this science is as follows:

> Surya, Pitamaha, Vyasa, Vashistha, Atri, Parashara,
> Kashyapa, Narada, Garga, Marichi, Manu, Angira,
> Lomasha, Paulisha, Chyavana, Yavana, Bhrigu,
> and Shaunaka—these eighteen are the promoters of the science of Jyotisha.

According to these words of the sage Kashyapa, this tradition is <term>Arsha</term><note>Derived from the Rishis or ancient seers.</note>, having been established by the eighteen preeminent sages, much like the eighteen Puranas. Additionally:

> The supreme knowledge of the movement of the planets has been revealed as a divine eye.
> By understanding the positions of the Sun and other heavenly bodies, one attains the eternal realm.

So says the <term>Surya Siddhanta</term><note>One of the most fundamental and ancient Sanskrit treatises on Indian astronomy.</note>. Likewise:

> The circle of light <note>The zodiac/heavens</note> declares the good and ill fortune of the entire world.
> He who understands the knowledge of light attains the supreme goal.

According to the words of the sage Garga. Moreover:

> One who studies the calendar <note>A practitioner of the astral sciences</note> does not suffer in hell;
> The seeker of the divine <insert>the astrologer</insert> attains a place in the realm of Brahma.

According to these words of Varahamihira <note>A 6th-century polymath and one of the most important figures in Indian astrology</note>, the necessity of studying and teaching this science arises not only from its great practical utility but also from a spiritual perspective. Thus, because it concerns the nature of the Sun—the soul of all and the ruler of the world—and relates to the <term>Gayatri</term><note>A highly revered Vedic mantra dedicated to Savitr, the solar deity</note>, there is no exaggeration in calling this science a "Philosophy" <note>original: "Darshana-shastra"</note>.

This science should be served <gloss>studied</gloss> like a <term>Kalpataru</term><note>A mythological wish-fulfilling tree</note>; as much as it is cultivated, it bears fruit. Therefore, great effort is made in this discipline. What experiential results can the application of this science produce? In this scripture composed by the great sage Kashyapa, the teacher has taught the three branches <note>original: "Skandha-traya"</note>—**Samhita**, **Tantra**, and **Hora**—for the purpose of determining the distribution of results. As Varaha says:

> The science of Jyotisha, which deals with many different subjects, is based on three branches.
> Because it brings all these together, the sages call it "Samhita" <note>A compendium</note>.
> In this, the branch dealing with mathematical calculations of planetary motion is called "Tantra."
> "Hora" is the other branch, said to be the determination of the influence of the limbs <note>referring to horoscopy or natal astrology</note>.

---

<unclear>In the Samhita branch, there is a chapter teaching the various movements of the planetary cycles and groups.</unclear>
<unclear>In the Tantra branch, there are mathematical texts such as the Siddhantas and Karanas.</unclear>
<unclear>In the Hora branch, there are divisions of texts concerning omens, natal horoscopy, Tajika <note>Persian-influenced annual horoscopy</note>, and various auspicious timings (Muhurta).</unclear>

<header>Preface</header>

# The Wishing-Tree of Astrology—

<insert>
[Diagram titled 'The Wishing-Tree of Astrology' <note>original: "Jyotiṣakalpadrumaḥ"</note>. The diagram depicts a tree with various branches of the Sciences <note>Shastras</note>.]
**Labels within the tree diagram:**
- **Roots:** Rigveda, Atharvaveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda, Phonetics <note>Shiksha</note>, Upanishads
- **Trunk:** Astrology/Astronomy <note>Jyotish</note>
- **Main Branches (Lower):** Compilation <note>Samhita</note>, Mathematical Astronomy <note>Siddhanta</note>, Natal Astrology <note>Hora</note>
- **Foliage (Sub-branches/Leaves):** Books on Omens, Books on Predictive Astrology, Architecture <note>Vastu</note>, Physiognomy <note>Samudrika</note>, Horary Astrology <note>Prashna</note>, Natal Horoscopy, Perso-Arabic Astrology <note>Tajika</note>, Algebra, Arithmetic, Mensuration, Trigonometry, Spherical Astronomy, Geometry, Calculus, Books on Astronomical Instruments, etc.
</insert>

---

Among those books of the **Compilation** <note>Samhita</note> class, only the *Great Compilation* <note>Brhat-samhita</note> authored by Varahamihira is currently available and in circulation in the world. Otherwise, the Compilations are nearly extinct, mostly suppressed or lost due to the ignorance and negligence of people.

In the **Mathematical branch** <note>Tantra-skandha</note>—the three theoretical treatises <note>Siddhantas</note> known as the *Surya-siddhanta*, *Siddhanta-shiromani*, and *Siddhanta-tattva-viveka* are in use today, along with one practical manual <note>Karana</note> called *Graha-laghava*, two mathematical texts called *Lilavati* and *Bijaganita* <note>Algebra</note>, and modern Trigonometry. In the **Natal branch** <note>Hora-skandha</note> as well, only two or three original source texts are in circulation; others seen today are merely modern compilations on the same subjects appearing under many different names. In all three branches, the ancient texts of the Sages <note>Arsha-grantha</note> were suppressed and largely disappeared during the Mughal Empire that came to this unfortunate land of India (due to the imposition of their own religious whims). By chance, a few texts have come before our eyes—those which escaped their cruel gaze. These authors, having extracted the essence of our Sages' works as opportunity permitted, composed some books in their own languages. At that time, out of a desire to accommodate them, even Varahamihira used the names of the Zodiac signs from the Greek language <note>Yavana-bhasha</note> in his work on Natal Astrology. Alas! Those names are as follows:

> *Kriya, Tavuri, Jituma, Kulira, Leya, Pathona, Juka, Kaurpya,*
> *Taukshika, Akokero, Hridroga, and Antyabha.* <note>These are Sanskritized transliterations of the Greek names for the signs: Aries (Krios), Taurus (Tauros), Gemini (Didymos), etc.</note>

Similarly, the teacher Nilakantha, in his book named *Tajika-Nilakanthi*, adopted all the technical terms from the Greek/Persian language. There are several other such books. After that, during the reign of the Europeans (which followed the Mughal Empire), whatever few of our Indian Sage-authored texts remained...

# Introduction

<page-num>4</page-num>

->**Preface**<-

<warning>The bottom third of the page is significantly blurred and damaged, making some characters difficult to distinguish with certainty.</warning>

Disregarded by the unfortunate, all have slowly moved to distant lands; thus, in India, only the **human-authored works** <note>original: "paurusha" — works composed by human scholars as opposed to divine revelation</note> produced by the moderns come into view. And these human-authored works belong only to the period within the last fifteen hundred years. This is because **Aryabhata** (who lived in 397 of the Shaka Era <note>approximately 475–476 CE</note>) is considered the first teacher of this era. Even among these human-authored works, only a few selected texts are studied by those seeking authority through the examination systems of Sanskrit committees. There, they somehow maintain a foothold, but today’s students of Sanskrit—greedy only for earning a livelihood and longing for certificates—consider themselves successful after studying just three or four books prescribed for the examination. In such a state, how could those most holy ancient and modern texts not become nearly extinct?

Now, according to the words of **Bhaskara**: "The fruit of the science of light <note>astronomy/astrology</note> is said by the ancient calculators to be prediction," and according to the words of **Varaha**: "This science reveals the ripening of the good and evil karma gathered in previous births, just as a lamp reveals objects in the darkness." Thus, the primary purpose of this science is indeed the making of predictions. However, since prediction depends on the **ascendant** <note>Lagna</note> and the **planets**, it is first necessary to have knowledge of the calculations from the **Siddhantas** <note>established astronomical treatises</note> to determine these positions. Without this, one cannot be immersed in the true essence of the science; therefore, the Great Sages expanded upon the systems of Siddhanta (theory), Karana (practical manuals), and Ganita (mathematics). 

But modern teachers and students of these systems, caught up in disputes over "fine" versus "gross" calculations, never cast their sight even once toward the path of practical application. Almost no one today, having mastered precise theoretical mathematics, actually calculates the real positions of planets for an **almanac** <note>Panchanga</note> or a **horoscope** <note>Jataka</note> and verifies them through observation <note>Vedha</note> to ensure they match what is seen by the eye. Instead, what is the use of wasting days in vain disputes under the pretext of debating precision? If they would only accept the path of calculating almanac planets using the most precise methods! In reality, only those results attained through planets calculated via the most precise Siddhanta methods—which have achieved unity between observation and calculation—reach the state of truth. As **Bhaskara** says:

> In journeys, marriages, festivals, and births, the result is clear only when the planets are clear (accurate).
> Therefore, the accurate calculation of the sky-wanderers (planets) is performed to achieve unity between observation and mathematics.

Alas! This is the very same land of India, and this is the very same science of Jyotish, where the practitioners of this knowledge used to be "knowers of the three times" (past, present, and future), and the **diviners** <note>Daivajnas</note> were truly knowers of fate. All astronomers used to construct various instruments in their own homes for the observation of planets. Yet today, those who fancy themselves diviners, wearing whatever titles they please—such as "Knower of Fate," "Crest-jewel of Mathematics," "Ornament of Jyotish," or "Jewel of Jyotish"—are generally unable to give a truthful and satisfying answer to even a single question from a petitioner. How could they not be an object of ridicule in front of them?

In this **Age of Kali** <note>the current dark age in Hindu cosmology</note>, due to the influence of the times and the hostility of peers, even though the sciences are utterly empty of great brilliant scholars, some wise men still exist here and there as before for their own sake. However, among them are those who worship the family mantra "no single thing belongs to anyone," regarding their knowledge as a private servant of their own systems; others are full of hidden doubts, and though they are skilled in their work, they are <unclear>inactive</unclear> and thus destitute. Thinking only of their bellies, they live like incapacitated parrots. In such a state, how can the progress of our country and our knowledge be possible? Our very Siddhanta is confused in many ways, and people never experience any unity of opinion. Whether what we perceive is true or related to truth... [the text here is obscured] ...how can you, the moderns, discard the worship of the science of Jyotish, which is the shower of the path of good and evil and a means of helping the world!

<summary>The author laments the decline of Indian astronomy, criticizing modern students for seeking certificates over deep knowledge and urging a return to the "Drik-Ganita" principle—where mathematical calculations must match observational reality.</summary>

# Page 5
## Introduction

The teaching of this science, the construction of instruments such as the <term>Grahadi-vedhopakarana</term> <note>instruments used for observing and piercing the positions of planets</note> as approved by tradition, and their practical application, is seen as an absolute necessity for every school, every student, and every teacher. Will the educational authorities and teachers cast even a narrow glance toward this work, which is intended for the benefit of the people of the world?

Now, let us follow the subject at hand—among the human-authored works in the <term>Hora Skandha</term> <note>the branch of astrology dealing with natal horoscopes and time</note>, the appearance of the **Brihat Jataka** is foremost <margin>(1) Even before Varaha, there were Satyacharya and Jivasharma, as their opinions are seen in the Brihat Jataka; however, because the works of Satyacharya and Jivasharma are unavailable, the world accepts Varaha as the primary source.</margin>. This text is considered the essence of the ancient sage-authored astrology and is the root of all modern human-authored astrological texts. The illustrious **Varahamihira** is the author of this jewel of a book, as he himself has stated:

->The son of Adityadasa, having obtained knowledge from him,<-
->having received the grace of a boon from the Sun at Kapitthaka,<-
->the wise Varahamihira of Avanti, having observed the final conclusions of the sages,<-
->composed this beautiful *Hora* <note>the Brihat Jataka</note>.<-

From this point forward, the title "Acharya" <note>The Great Teacher</note> refers to Varahamihira (See Chapters 3, 51-80), and the word "Hora" refers to this very work, the **Brihat Jataka**. As seen in this present book, phrases like "in the Acharya’s Hora" or "in the Hora" are used. Furthermore, the essence of this very work, titled **Laghu Jataka**, also composed by him, shines brilliantly for the benefit of those who know natal astrology. This is its opening verse:

->I have composed a treatise on the science of *Hora* in various meters after examining the scriptures.<-
->I shall now declare the essence of that very work in *Arya* verses.<-

After this, many books on the subject of natal astrology were revealed by various authors who collected thematic verses from different texts. For instance, the **Shripati Paddhati** (by Shripati), **Saravali** (by Kalyan Varma), **Sarvartha Chintamani** (by Venkatesha), **Jataka Desha** (by Gunakar), **Hora Ratnam** (by Balabhadra), **Manasagari**, **Jatakabharanam**, **Jataka Tattvam**, **Jataka Parijata** (by Vaidya Natha), and **Phaladeepika** (by Mantreshwar)—many such books decorated with diverse topics are available. Among them, this **Jataka Parijata** is useful for all matters related to natal astrology; because its qualities match its name <note>"Parijata" is the celestial wish-fulfilling tree; the title implies the book fulfills all astrological inquiries</note>, it is currently favored by teachers and scholars alike. At the beginning of this book:

->The son of the learned Sri Venkatadri, born of the Bharadvaja lineage,<-
->who was an expert in the science of light <note>Jyotish/Astronomy-Astrology</note>, the wise Sri Vaidyanatha,<-
->for the delight of the minds of the wise who know the nectar-essence of *Hora*,<-
->shall describe everything, such as the determination of the positions of the zodiac signs, in proper order.<-

By this statement, it is clear that this book was composed by the astrologer **Sri Vaidyanatha**, son of the astrologer **Sri Venkatadri** of the Bharadvaja clan. Since the author's time is not specified in this book, his actual period of composition depends on comparative analysis. This author is the son of Venkatadri, and Venkatadri was also an expert in astrology, as is clear from Vaidyanatha’s statement: "of Sri Venkatadri, an expert in the science of light." Therefore, it is inferred that this Venkatadri is the same as the author of the **Sarvartha Chintamani**. Since many original verses from the *Sarvartha Chintamani* are found inserted in the *Jataka Parijata*, the logic that this Venkatadri is Vaidyanatha’s father is consistent. However, since the time is also not seen in the *Sarvartha Chintamani*, his actual date is not clear. 

Yet, quoting from the great ocean of astrological science—"Having obtained a little from the two lotus feet of the Guru Vaidyanatha, Keshavas wrote the *Muhurta Tattvam*"—this statement from the **Muhurta Tattvam** by **Keshava** (the father of **Ganesha Daivajna**, author of the *Graha Laghava*) proves that this Vaidyanatha was the teacher of Keshava. The time of the composition of the *Graha Laghava* by Ganesha is stated as 1442 <term>Shaka</term> <note>The Shaka era starts in 78 CE; 1442 Shaka is 1520 CE</note>. If Keshava’s age at that time is assumed to be 70 years, then Keshava’s birth would be 1372 Shaka (1450 CE). If we then assume Vaidyanatha’s age was 25 years at that time, there is no inconsistency; thus, the time of Vaidyanatha’s composition of this work is estimated to be around 1397 Shaka (1475 CE) <margin>(2) In the *Ganaka Tarangini*, Mahamahopadhyaya Sudhakar Dwivedi has suggested the possibility of the identity between the elder Venkatadri and Vaidyanatha; I do not know the reason for that.</margin>.

It attempts to establish the author's date (approx. 1475 CE) by tracing his relationship as the teacher of Keshava, father of the famous astronomer Ganesha Daivajna.</summary>

# Introduction

Here, the author Vaidyanatha states:
> 'Having bowed to the works composed by Garga, Parashara, and others, and having collected the fruits of their horoscopic teachings, I create this *Jataka Parijata* <note>The "Celestial Tree of Natal Astrology"</note> for the delight of all astrologers.'

->And also—'Having gathered the essence of the *Saravali* and other primary systems, I compose this *Jataka Parijata*.'<-

By these statements, it is clear that he composed this *Jataka Parijata* by collecting the essential portions of ancient sage-authored texts, as well as compiling the core verses from later astrological classics such as the *Saravali* and *Brihat Jataka*. In fact, several verses in this book are found to be the original verses of the *Brihat Jataka* (See: chapters on non-human births, planetary evils, determination of longevity, and the system of periods/sub-periods). Some original verses from the *Saravali* and *Sarvartha Chintamani*, as well as verses collected from other texts, have been inserted by the author with slight variations in reading. I have made an effort to identify and cite the names of those source texts whenever available. Furthermore, whatever verses from other texts were mentioned to explain the meaning of the verses in this work, I have preserved them as authoritative references in the commentary. These source texts, obtained through tradition, are specified as follows: the *Garga Jataka*, *Yavana Jataka*, *Parashara Hora*, *Jataka Bharanam*, *Mandavya Jataka*, *Jatakadesha*, *Jataka Ratna*, *Hora Ratna*, *Phaladeepika*, *Brihat Jataka*, *Saravali*, *Sarvartha Chintamani*, *Muhurta Chintamani*, *Laghu Jataka*, *Siddhanta Shiromani*, *Surya Siddhanta*, *Keshaviya Jataka Paddhati*, *Jaimini Sutras*, *Muhurta Martanda*, *Prashna Marga*, *Hora Sara*, *Shripati Paddhati*, *Kala Prakashika*, and many other such works are cited here.

In this work, eighteen chapters have been determined: 1. Nature of the Zodiac Signs, 2. Names, Forms, and Qualities of Planets, 3. Non-human Births, 4. Evils/Afflictions (*Arishta*), 5. Longevity, 6. Cancellation of Fortunes, 7. Royal Yogas (*Rajayoga*), 8. Combinations of Two or More Planets, 9. Effects of Mandi and other secondary planets, 10. The *Ashtakavarga* system, 11. Effects of the 1st and 2nd Houses, 12. Effects of the 3rd and 4th Houses, 13. Effects of the 5th and 6th Houses, 14. Effects of the 7th and 8th Houses, 15. Effects of the 10th, 11th, and 12th Houses, 16. Female Horoscopy, 17. The *Kalachakra Dasha* (Time-cycle periods), 18. Periods and Sub-periods. Thus, it is said in the conclusion of the work:

> This *Jataka Parijata* is proclaimed as the foremost among all results, filled with light, and shining brilliantly with eighteen chapters.
> It describes <gloss>1</gloss> the abode of the qualities of signs, <gloss>2</gloss> the movement, positions, natures, and forms of planets,
> <gloss>3</gloss> the birth of all living beings, <gloss>4</gloss> the evils that threaten infants.
> <gloss>5</gloss> Longevity, <gloss>6</gloss> the cancellation of birth-fortunes, <gloss>7</gloss> the arising of great Royal Yogas,
> <gloss>8</gloss> the auspicious and inauspicious results of two or more planets, and <gloss>9</gloss> the effects of Mandi in order.
> <gloss>10</gloss> Then the calculations of the *Ashtakavarga* points, <gloss>11</gloss> the results of the House of Self and Wealth,
> <gloss>12</gloss> the results concerning siblings and lands, <gloss>13</gloss> the effects assigned to the houses of children and enemies.
> <gloss>14</gloss> The results of the houses of desire, death, and dharma, <gloss>15</gloss> the results of profession, gains, and loss,
> <gloss>16</gloss> the results of female horoscopy, <gloss>17</gloss> the lunar-based system, and <gloss>18</gloss> the periods and sub-periods.
> The wise Vaidyanatha, son of Venkata, by the grace of the Sun and all other planets,
> Created this path of the *Jataka Parijata* in eighteen chapters, following his family tradition, to grant success in horoscopy for the pleasure of the virtuous.

Therefore, by the phrase 'Son of Shri Venkata,' it should be understood that this path of the *Jataka Parijata* was compiled for the pleasure of the learned by the son of Shri Venkateshvara, the son of Venkatadri. Here, according to the *Ka-ta-pa-ya* <note>A traditional Sanskrit alphanumeric code used for dates and numbers</note> system, the word 'Sankalita' (compiled) equals 1553 <note>Likely referring to the Shaka year 1553, approx. 1631 CE</note>. This work of Vaidyanatha is composed of 1832 verses. However, in current printed books, the chapters—

<header>Preface</header>

# Preface

**The sum of the verses arranged in order = 11 + 87 + 80 + 107 + 124 + 102 + 181 + 118 + 138 + 73 + 97 + 149 + 82 + 103 + 84 + 54 + 111 + 177 = 1918** verses are found in total. Therefore, it is appropriate to say that 155 additional verses have entered the original text <note>The commentator is noting a discrepancy between the traditional count and the current manuscript</note>. Or perhaps, the phrase 'Gitosukashlokinim' should be explained as: 'bestowing fame (shlokinim) upon those eager for the Gita (gitosukana), i.e., those engaged in the study of this book.'

Furthermore, in this book, compared to works such as the **Brihat Jataka, Saravali, and Sarvartha Chintamani** <note>These are foundational classical texts of Indian astrology</note>, the following subjects are generally determined with greater specificity: the orbital order of the planets, variations in their entry into signs, the removal of defects, types of afflictions, certain aspects and combinations (yogas), various types of longevity calculations (ayurdaya), 'hole' planets (chidra-grahas) <note>planets indicating vulnerability or death</note>, the time of departure (death), consequences after death, various combinations for poverty and wealth, types of Royal Yogas (Raja Yogas), specific combinations, planetary combinations, the results of Mandi and other secondary planets, the 'Ganda' period <note>inauspicious transitional moments</note>, the results of the time of birth (Vela-phalam), the purification of the Ashtakavarga through trines and lordship and its results, the Ashtakavarga spread, several specifics regarding the results of the houses (bhavas), the compatibility of the bride and groom's horoscopes, the elaboration of the Kalachakra Dasha system and its results, the movement types of the Kalachakra, statements on the Kalachakra Dasha spread, variations in sub-periods (antardashas), the Dasha of departure (death), Gulika Dasha, Shula Dasha, and the results of internal lineages. Since all matters concerning humans are considered through the placement of planets and the twelve houses, the author of this book has analyzed the twelve houses and yogas in many ways based on the <term>Planetary Position</term> (current state of the planets); thus, this great book has become extremely useful to the world.

It can be said without exaggeration that even by studying this single book, one can become an expert in all the secrets of horoscopy. This is because the **Brihat Jataka**, which is the root of all modern horoscopy, is mostly incorporated within this work. With this in mind, this book is included everywhere in the curriculum for the 'Acharya' (Master's level) examinations. Because of its utility for examinations, it is treated with great respect by almost all students and scholars. However, nowadays, only a few who are devoted to commentaries are respected in the teaching and learning of the original texts; seeing the difficulty in studying and teaching this book without a commentary, I was commanded by the most compassionate Superintendent of Examinations of the Government Sanskrit College, Varanasi, and repeatedly requested by Shri Jayakrishna Das-Haridas Gupta, the head of the Chowkhamba Sanskrit Library in Varanasi, to begin writing a commentary on this book. In this holy task for the benefit of the world, by the grace of the Lord of the Universe, I achieved success quickly and without obstacles despite my limited intellect; the grace of my Guru's feet is the only seed of this success. Even in this difficult-to-fathom book, for the convenience of students, I have included useful explanations, examples, proofs, mathematical tables, and diagrams, and have provided <term>Notes</term> in specific places, which will be evident to scholars.

Now, even great and wise men may become confused in this vast ocean of a book which is hard to cross; the boldness I have shown in desiring success with my atom-like intellect, out of a child-like restlessness, is only due to the strength of the blessings of my venerable teachers. Therefore, following the maxim 'even a wise word from a child should be accepted,' and possessing the wisdom to discern like a swan separating milk from water, I pray with folded hands that you, the scholars, will distinguish 'your own virtues from my faults' and once again encourage this servant of yours.

---

The Festival of Sita's Wedding <note>Vivaha Panchami</note> }  
Vikram Samvat 1999 <note>Approx. 1942 CE</note>

Seeking refuge at the Holy Feet—  
**Shri Kapileshwara Shastri.**

> It is a source of pure abundance <note>original: "anagha-prasvini," implying a cow that gives milk without fault, or a work that yields pure knowledge</note>, a helper to the simple-minded, and a companion to the wise.
> This work is now offered at your lotus feet by **Kapileshwara**. || 1 ||

-> ॥ Salutations to the Holy Lord of Auspiciousness <note>Ganesha</note> ॥ <-

# The Celestial Tree of Natal Astrology
### (Jātakapārijāta)

### Enriched by the "Nectar-Filled" (Sudhāśālinī) and "Pure" (Vimalā) Commentaries

---

## Chapter on the Nature of the Zodiac Signs

> Having bowed to the Sun, who is the form of Vishnu (Lord of Lakshmi), Brahma, and Shiva; who is the Lord of the immortal hosts of light; who transcends illusion; and who is the Master of all living beings and the world—I shall speak the *Jātakapārijāta* (The Celestial Tree of Horoscopy), having collected the fruits of astrology composed by sages such as Garga and Parashara, for the delight of all astrologers. ॥ 1 ॥

-> * The Nectar-Filled Commentary * <-

> Constantly worshipping the Lord of Lakshmi, the beautiful lotus-eyed one residing in the temple of the heart, and the Goddess who destroys misery and grants all desires; for the sake of those who are confused by this book, the *Jātakapārijāta*, the scholar Kapileshwara in the city of Kashi <note>Modern-day Varanasi</note> composes this "Nectar-Filled" commentary.

Now, the author, born of the lineage of Bharadvaja and famous by the name <term>Shri Vaidyanatha</term> (The Lord of Physicians), desiring to compose this work on astrology titled <term>Jātakapārijāta</term> (The Celestial Tree of Natal Astrology), follows the virtuous tradition that "the entire world is dependent on the Divine" and thus worship should be offered to the Divine at the start of all auspicious works. Wishing for the successful completion of his intended subject, he performs an auspicious salutation to the presiding deity of his field, the Sun, and indicates the subject matter:

**The form of Vishnu, Brahma, and Shiva** = The Sun embodies the Trinity, as it is said: "The Sun is indeed the Triple Form." **The Lord of the immortal hosts of light** = The immortals are the gods, and the "hosts of light" are the planets and constellations; he is their master because he is their illuminator. This implies that the Sun alone illuminates all celestial lights. As stated by the astronomer Kamalakara:

> "The Sun is a sphere of fire; the planets and stars are spheres of water. They appear brilliant only when illuminated by the rays of the Sun."

**Transcending illusion** = Meaning he is of the nature of pure Truth. **The Master of all living beings and the world** = The leader and presiding soul of all moving and unmoving beings, as the Veda states: "The Sun is the Soul of the moving and unmoving world." **Lord of the Day** = The master of the day, since the activity of the day begins only with the rising of the Sun. As the mathematician Bhaskara said: "The day belongs to the Lord of the Day because it is seen only through him." **The Sun** = Having bowed to (saluted) the Sun. **Composed by Garga, Parashara, and others** = Having collected the <term>Horā-phalam</term> (The results of natal astrology) written by great sages like Garga and Parashara. **For the delight of all astrologers** = For the joy of all knowers of the science of light. The dictionary *Amarakosha* defines delight as: "Great love, joy, happiness, and gladness." **Jātakapārijāta** = Among the works of natal astrology (*Jātaka*), this book is like the *Pārijāta* (The Celestial Tree of Paradise). The *Amarakosha* notes: "There are five divine trees, of which the Parijata is one." I shall speak (compose) this book—this is the remaining sense. The use of the word "Shri" (Holy/Prosperous) at the beginning of the work is an indicator of well-being for all. ॥ 1 ॥

# With the Commentary Jataka Parijata-

## * Vimala *
<note>Vimala, meaning "The Spotless One," is the name of this specific commentary on the main text.</note>

->Having bowed to the Lord of Lakshmi <note>Vishnu</note>, the Unborn, the Lord of the Daughter of the Mountain King <note>Shiva</note>, the Sun, the Teacher,<-
->The Goddess of Speech <note>Saraswati</note>, the Son of the Mountain-Born <note>Ganesha</note>, the Son of the Wind <note>Hanuman</note>, and the Beloved of Lord Ramachandra;<-
->Having constantly bowed to my father, Chhatradhara, and my mother, Anandika,<-
->I shall speak the Vimala commentary on the Jataka Parijata for the delight of the virtuous.<-

Having bowed to the Sun God—who is the embodiment of Vishnu, Brahma, and Shiva, the lord of the heavenly bodies, distinct from illusion, and the master of all living beings in the universe—and having collected the fruits of horoscopy composed by Garga, Parashara, and others, I compose the *Jataka Parijata* for the pleasure of all astrologers. || 1 ||

**Now, he states his duty while introducing himself—**

->Born in the lineage of Bharadwaja, the son of the learned Sri Venkatadri,<-
->Who was an expert in the science of light <term>Jyotishashastra: Vedic astrology and astronomy</term>, the wise Sri Vaidyanatha,<-
->For the pleasure of the minds of the assembly of scholars who enjoy the nectar of the essence of horoscopy,<-
->Shall describe everything, such as the determination of the positions of the zodiac signs, in proper order. || 2 ||<-

Born in the lineage of Bharadwaja = born in the Bharadwaja <term>gotra: paternal lineage</term>; an expert in the science of light = skilled in the science of astrology; the learned = the scholar; the son of Sri Venkatadri = the offspring of the one named Sri Venkatadri; the wise = the learned author, myself, Sri Vaidyanatha; for the pleasure of the minds of the assembly of scholars who enjoy the nectar of the essence of horoscopy = for the joy of the minds of all those scholars who consider the essence of the horoscopic scriptures to be the very nectar of immortality; everything, such as the determination of the positions of the zodiac signs = all subjects beginning with the determination of the places of the twelve signs starting with Aries; in proper order = without skipping the sequence (meaning, in a systematic order), I shall speak. || 2 ||

I, Vaidyanatha, the son of the scholar Sri Venkatadri, an expert in the science of astrology born in the clan of the sage Bharadwaja, speak on all subjects such as the determination of the positions of the zodiac signs for the pleasure of the minds of scholars who know the essence of the horoscopic scriptures. || 2 ||

**Again, after bowing to his chosen deity, he states the subject to be performed—**

->Having bowed to the lotus feet of the Leader of the Raghu clan <note>Lord Rama</note>, which are worthy of worship by all devotees,<-
->And having collected the principal treatises such as the *Saravali*, I compose this *Jataka Parijata*. || 3 ||<-

I = Sri Vaidyanatha; of the Leader of the Raghu clan = of Ramachandra, the king of the Raghu dynasty; the lotus feet worthy of worship by all devotees = the lotus-like feet which are to be saluted by those who offer praise. "Vandaru" means one who salutes, according to the Amarakosha <note>A famous Sanskrit lexicon</note>. Having bowed to the lotus feet which are worshipful to all, and having collected the principal treatises such as the *Saravali* = having accepted the *Saravali* composed by Kalyanavarman as the primary authoritative text, I compose or create this book called *Jataka Parijata*. Now, one might ask: "It was previously said that the fruits of horoscopy were collected from Garga, Parashara, and others; why is it now said that the principal treatise *Saravali* is being collected?" It is true, but there is no contradiction, as the *Saravali* also contains the subjects favored by the ancient sages. || 3 ||

> <warning>Faded text</warning> Having bowed to the lotus feet of <unclear>Lord</unclear> Rama, and having collected the *Saravali* as the main treatise, I compose the <unclear>Jataka Parijata</unclear>. || 3 ||

### Now, the specific names of the Zodiac Signs.

->The two fish with tails and mouths apart are Pisces; Aries and Taurus are the Goat and the Bull;<-
->A human couple, one with a lute and the other with a staff, is the third sign, which they call Gemini. || 4 ||<-

# Chapter 1: The Play of the Zodiac Signs

->*Kulira*, *Karkataka*, and *Karkata* are names for Cancer; *Kanthirava*, *Simha*, *Mrigendra*, and *Leya* refer to Leo.<-
->*Pathona*, *Kanya*, *Ramani*, and *Taruni* are Virgo; *Tauli*, *Vanik*, *Juka*, *Tula*, and *Dhata* are Libra.<- <note>Verse 5</note>
->*Ali*, *Ashtamam*, *Vrishchika*, *Kaurpi*, and *Kita* are Scorpio; *Dhanvi*, *Dhanus*, *Chapa*, and *Sharasana* are Sagittarius.<-
->*Mriga*, *Mrigasya*, *Makara*, and *Nakra* are Capricorn; *Kumbha*, *Ghata*, and *Toyadhara* are the names for Aquarius.<- <note>Verse 6</note>
->The wise say *Mina*, *Antya*, *Matsya*, *Prithuroma*, and *Jhasha* are Pisces. These signs, beginning with Aries, are joined with nine quarters of the lunar mansions starting with Ashwini. These twelve celestial bodies, equal in number to the forms of the Sun, reside in the circle of the heavens and are known by the terms Field, Star, Sign, and House.<- <note>Verse 7</note>

Now, the alternative names of the signs are explained:

**Aries** (*Mesha*): *Aja*, *Vishva*, *Kriya* <note>original: "Kriya" is a Sanskritization of the Greek 'Krios'</note>, *Tumburu*, and *Adya* are synonyms for the sign of Aries.
**Taurus** (*Vrisha*): *Uksha*, *Gau*, *Taburu* <note>original: "Taburu" relates to the Greek 'Tauros'</note>, and *Gokula* are the designations for Taurus.
**Gemini** (*Mithuna*): The learned say *Dvandva*, *Nriyugma*, *Jutuma* <note>original: "Jutuma" relates to the Greek 'Didymos'</note>, *Yama*, *Yuga*, and *Tritiya* refer to Gemini.
**Cancer** (*Karkata*): *Kulira*, *Karkataka*, and *Karkata* are the names for Cancer.
**Leo** (*Simha*): *Kanthirava*, *Simha*, *Mrigendra*, and *Leya* <note>original: "Leya" relates to the Greek 'Leon'</note> are synonyms for Leo.
**Virgo** (*Kanya*): *Pathona* <note>original: "Pathona" relates to the Greek 'Parthenos'</note>, *Kanya*, *Ramani*, and *Taruni* are synonyms for Virgo.
**Libra** (*Tula*): *Tauli*, *Vanik*, *Juka*, *Tula*, and *Ghata* are synonyms for Libra.
**Scorpio** (*Vrishchika*): *Ali*, *Ashtamam*, *Vrishchika*, *Kaurpi*, and *Kita* are synonyms for Scorpio.
**Sagittarius** (*Dhanus*): *Dhanvi*, *Dhanus*, *Chapa*, and *Sharasana* are synonyms for Sagittarius.
**Capricorn** (*Makara*): *Mriga*, *Mrigasya*, *Makara*, and *Nakra* are synonyms for Capricorn.
**Aquarius** (*Kumbha*): *Kumbha*, *Ghata*, and *Toyadhara* are synonyms for Aquarius.

**Pisces** (*Mina*): The wise say *Mina*, *Antya*, *Matsya*, *Prithuroma*, and *Jhasha* are the designations for Pisces.

How are the signs, which are characterized by the <term>Nakshatras</term> <note>Lunar mansions or star clusters</note>, understood by the wise? To this, he says: "Joined with nine quarters of the stars starting with *Dastra* (Ashwini)." (Here it should be noted: each star has four quarters, and nine quarters make one sign. The twenty-seven stars starting with Ashwini have a total of 108 quarters; therefore, it is logical that nine quarters constitute one sign). "Beginning with *Kriya* (Aries)": The number is equal to the "Lord of the Day" (the Sun), meaning there are twelve, as it is said "The Sun has twelve souls." "Celestial": The signs moving in the sky are situated in a "Circle" (circular or spherical shape). "Known as *Bha*": Those which have the name *Bha* (a synonym for a sign). They also receive the names "Field" (*Kshetra*), "Star" (*Riksha*), "Sign" (*Rashi*), and "House" (*Bhavana*). Here, the Sign itself is counted by these various names.

As stated by Varahamihira in the *Brihat Jataka*:
> "Sign (*Rashi*), Triangle (*Triguna*), House (*Griha*), Star (*Riksha*), *Bha*, and Mansion (*Bhavana*) are all terms conveying the same meaning." <note>Verse 7</note>

<header>From the *Jataka Parijata* with Commentary</header>

### The Zodiac Wheel for Clear Understanding

*Meena* <note>Pisces</note>, *Antya* <note>The Last</note>, *Matsya* <note>The Fish</note>, *Prithuroma* <note>Large-scaled</note>, and *Jhasha* <note>A great fish</note> are all names for the sign of Pisces. Each *Nakshatra* <note>Lunar mansion</note> consists of four quarters. The twelve signs, beginning with Aries, contain nine quarters of these lunar mansions (starting from *Ashwini*) and revolve in the sky within the circular zodiac. These twelve signs are also known by terms such as *Kshetra* <note>Field</note>, *Riksha* <note>Star/Sign</note>, *Rashi* <note>Heap/Sign</note>, *Bhavana* <note>Mansion</note>, and *Ma* <note>Measure</note>. || 7 ||

->Now, he explains how the signs starting with Aries are the limbs of the Time-Person <note>Sanskrit: *Kalanara* or *Kalapurusha*, a personification of Time where the zodiac signs correspond to body parts</note>—<-

> The head, face-region, chest, heart, belly-part, waist, bladder, and the private region;
> The thighs, the pair of knees, then the two shanks, and the two feet are the limbs of the Time-Soul, starting with Aries in order. || 8 ||

Of the Time-Soul = He whose soul is Time itself is the Time-Soul (meaning the *Kalapurusha*). The limbs starting with Aries = Aries and the following signs are the limbs or body parts in sequential order. What are those limbs? The head, face-region, chest, heart, belly-part, waist, bladder, private region, thighs, the pair of knees, then the shanks, and the two feet.

Aries is the head; Taurus is the face-region; Gemini <gloss>(1)</gloss> is the chest; Cancer is the *Hrit* = the heart; Leo is the *Kukshi-bhaga* = the stomach; Virgo is the waist; Libra is the *Basti* = the area between the navel and the genitals; Scorpio is the *Rahasya-desha* = the private parts/genitals; Sagittarius is the two thighs; Capricorn is the pair of knees; Aquarius is the two shanks; Pisces is the two feet = the pair of legs.

The purpose of this is as follows: At the time of birth, one should predict strength and health for the limb associated with a sign occupied by a benefic planet <note>A "good" planet like Jupiter or Venus</note>, and affliction or deformity for the limb associated with a sign occupied by a malefic planet <note>A "harsh" planet like Mars or Saturn</note>. It is said likewise in the *Svalpa Jataka*:

> "One should contemplate the limbs of the Time-Person in men at the time of birth.
> Through the conjunction of good or bad planets, those limbs are either well-formed or suffering from ailments." || 8 ||

---

<gloss>( 1 )</gloss> In the *Svalpa Jataka*, Gemini is said to be the arms, as stated: "The head, face, arms, heart, stomach <unclear>......</unclear>"

<note>The translator notes that different astrological traditions sometimes vary slightly in these anatomical assignments; here the commentary notes a variation where Gemini represents the arms rather than the chest.</note>

<summary>This page defines the various names for the sign of Pisces and establishes the "Kalapurusha" system, which maps the twelve zodiac signs to specific parts of the human body for medical and physical predictions.</summary>

### Chapter on the Nature of the Zodiac Signs || 1 ||

->[Diagram of the Personification of Time with zodiac sign abbreviations mapped to body parts]<-

The arrangement of this <term>Zodiac Wheel<note>original: "Rashi Chakra"</note></term> exists within the body of the <term>Personification of Time<note>original: "Kaal Purusha"; the cosmic man whose body represents the universe.</note></term> in the following manner: **Aries** is the head, **Taurus** the face, **Gemini** the middle of the chest, **Cancer** the heart, **Leo** the stomach (belly), **Virgo** the waist, **Libra** below the navel (the pelvic region), **Scorpio** the genitals, **Sagittarius** the thighs, **Capricorn** both knees, **Aquarius** both calves, and **Pisces** represents both feet. 

The significance of this anatomical division of the Zodiac is that during birth, or at the time of a query, or during planetary transits, whichever sign is afflicted by a <term>malefic planet<note>original: "papakrant"; planets considered naturally unfavorable like Mars or Saturn.</note></term>, there will be a mark such as a mole, a wound, or a wart on the corresponding body part. Conversely, it should be specially remembered that whichever sign is occupied by a <term>benefic planet<note>original: "shubh grah"; favorable planets like Jupiter or Venus.</note></term>, that specific limb will be strong and healthy. || 8 ||

### Now, the Description of the Forms of Pisces and Others.

> Two fish with tails and heads joined in reverse; a man with a water-pot;
> A person with a scale; a man with a bow and the hindquarters of a horse; a creature with the face of a deer and the body of a crocodile.
> A human couple with a lute and a mace; a maiden in a boat with grain and a lamp;
> The remaining signs resemble the names of their own qualities, and all reside in their respective habitats. || 6 ||

<gloss>Pisces = two fish; with tails and heads joined in reverse = they should be understood as the sign of Pisces in a form where the mouth of one is joined to the tail of the other. A man with a water-pot = a man holding an empty pitcher on his shoulder...</gloss>

...in that manner, Aquarius is represented by those [carrying a water pot]. Libra is like a man holding a scale. Sagittarius is like a man holding a bow, with the lower body of a horse <note>original: "turanga-jaghana"</note>; the lower half is like a horse and the upper half is a man holding a bow in his hand. Capricorn is the Crocodile <note>The Sanskrit 'Makara' is often depicted as a sea-monster or crocodile-like creature</note> with the face of a deer. Gemini is a pair of humans, a male and a female; the female holds a lute <term>Veena: a traditional Indian stringed instrument</term> and the male holds a mace. Virgo is a maiden <note>original: "Abala"</note> standing in a boat, holding both a sheaf of grain and a fire. All the remaining signs—Aries, Taurus, Cancer, Leo, and Scorpio—resemble the qualities of their names and reside in places suited to their natures. For example, Aries is like a ram and wanders in the forest; Taurus is shaped like a bull; Cancer is like a crab and lives in water; Leo is a maned lion of the forest; and Scorpio is a scorpion that moves in holes or crevices. The purpose of knowing these forms is to identify lost or stolen items based on the characteristics of the signs. As it is said: "From the signs, one determines time, direction, and place." || 9 ||

**Description of the forms of the signs:**
Pisces consists of two fish, the tail of one touching the mouth of the other, forming a circle. Aquarius is like a man carrying a water pot on his shoulder. Libra is like a man holding a scale in his hand. Sagittarius has the upper body of a man holding a bow and the lower body, from the thighs down, like a horse. Capricorn has a face like a deer. Gemini is a couple, a man and a woman, the woman holding a lute and the man holding a mace. Virgo is a maiden sitting in a boat holding grain and fire. The remaining signs (Aries, Taurus, Cancer, Leo, Scorpio) have forms identical to their names. For instance, Aries is like a ram, Taurus like a bull, Cancer like a crab, Leo like a lion, and Scorpio like a scorpion. || 9 ||

## Now, the Description of the Places of Aries and the Others.

> The place of Aries is the ground of minerals and gems; for Taurus, it is mountain ridges, agricultural lands, and cow-pens.
> The ground for gambling, sexual pleasure, and recreation belongs to Gemini; while ponds, tank banks, and sandbanks belong to the sign of Cancer. || 10 ||
> For Leo, it is dense mountain caves and forests; for the sixth sign (Virgo), it is grassy lands, the private quarters of women, and places of craftsmanship.
> For Libra, it is cities containing the essence of all wealth and marketplaces; for Scorpio, it is places with stones, venomous creatures, and holes. || 11 ||
> For Sagittarius, it is the stable for horses, chariots, and elephants; for Capricorn (the deer-faced), it is rivers and watery forest regions.
> For Aquarius, it is places for water-pots and households; for Pisces, the habitat is rivers, oceans, and masses of water. || 12 ||

Now the dwelling places of the signs are explained. The ground of minerals and gems—where minerals are found and where gems are produced—is the dwelling place of Aries. Agricultural lands, cow-pens <note>original: "Gokula"</note>, and forests are the places for Taurus. The ground for gambling—the act of wagering <insert>gambling</insert>—sexual pleasure (the private play of man and woman), and recreation is the dwelling place of Gemini. Ponds, long tanks, and their sandbanks or shore regions are the places of Cancer. Dense mountain caves and forests are the places of Leo. Grassy lands—places where the ground is green with young grass—women, the play of couples, and places of craftsmanship or artistic construction are the territory of the sixth sign, Virgo. Cities containing the essence of all wealth—a city where the best of all goods are found—and marketplaces...

The purpose of this knowledge is to understand the place of birth and to determine the location of lost or stolen property. || 10-12 ||

The dwelling place of the Aries <note>Mesha</note> sign is land rich in metals and gems. For Taurus <note>Vrisha</note>, the habitats are mountain peaks, agricultural land, cow sheds, and forests. For Gemini <note>Mithuna</note>, the places are areas for gambling <note>original: "jua"</note>, sexual intimacy, and pleasure gardens. For Cancer <note>Karka</note>, the dwellings are the banks of step-wells and ponds. || 10 ||

For Leo <note>Simha</note>, the places are dense mountains, caves, and forests. For Virgo <note>Kanya</note>, the locations are lands green with grass, the play-areas of women and men, and workshops of artisans. For Libra <note>Tula</note>, the residence is in lands where the value of all wealth is determined, and in marketplaces; for Scorpio <note>Vrishchika</note>, it is in stones, poison, and the holes of worms. || 11 ||

For Sagittarius <note>Dhanu</note>, the dwelling is in the stables of horses, chariots, and elephants; for Capricorn <note>Makara</note>, it is in the waters of rivers and in the forest (the first half in the forest and the latter half in the water); for Aquarius <note>Kumbha</note>, the residence is in lands where pots and water vessels are kept; and for Pisces <note>Meena</note>, it is in the dwelling places of fish (lakes), rivers, oceans, and masses of water. || 12 ||

Taurus, Aries, and Aquarius = <term>Go-Aja-Ghata</term>; these are short = they have small bodies. Capricorn, Gemini, Sagittarius, Pisces, and Cancer = <term>Mriga-Nriyuk-Chapa-Antya-Karkataka</term>; these are even = they have medium bodies, neither too long nor too short. Scorpio, Virgo, Leo, and Libra are long = they have large bodies. Starting from Aries, male and female = the signs in order are male and female; for example, Aries is male, Taurus is female, Gemini is male, Cancer is female. Thus, Aries, Gemini, Leo, Libra, Sagittarius, and Aquarius are male signs. Taurus, Cancer, Virgo, Scorpio, Capricorn, and Pisces are to be known as female signs. The purpose of this is: those born in male signs are energetic/splendid, while those born in female signs are gentle. Now, he describes the arrangement of directions for the signs—"East and others." # Commentary on the Jataka Parijata

Starting with the East, the directions are assigned to the signs beginning with Aries. The signs Aries, Taurus, Gemini, and Cancer, along with their respective corners <note>the 5th and 9th houses from them</note>, are said to be situated in the East and the other cardinal points. What is meant here is this: including their own "corners"—that is, the ninth and the fifth signs from themselves—Aries, Taurus, Gemini, and Cancer are to be known as the directions starting from the East.

Specifically:
*   **East:** Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius.
*   **South:** Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn.
*   **West:** Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius.
*   **North:** Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces.

The purpose of knowing these directions is to determine the location of stolen or lost property, the direction of a thief, and so on. Furthermore, it is said: "Success is achieved with ease when one travels in the direction corresponding to the rising sign; effort becomes fruitful, whereas traveling against the direction of the rising sign causes distress."

Next, he describes the auspicious or inauspicious nature of the signs:
**Cruel and Auspicious.** Aries is cruel, Taurus is auspicious, Gemini is cruel, Cancer is auspicious. In this manner, the odd signs starting from Aries are known as "cruel" <note>masculine/harsh</note>, and the even signs starting from Taurus are known as "auspicious" <note>feminine/gentle</note>. The application is: "Cruel men are born under harsh signs, and gentle men are born in gentle houses."

Furthermore, these signs starting from Aries are to be known respectively as **Movable, Fixed, and Dual.**
For example: Aries is Movable, Taurus is Fixed, Gemini is Dual. Thus:
*   **Movable (Chara):** Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn.
*   **Fixed (Sthira):** Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius.
*   **Dual (Dvisvabhava):** Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces.

The purpose of this classification is to understand the nature of lost items or thieves, and also that those born under Movable signs have active minds, those in Fixed signs have steady minds, and those in Dual signs possess a mixed nature.

Now he indicates the rising positions and the timing of strength for the signs: **Endowed with Strength.**
Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Sagittarius, Aries, and Capricorn are endowed with strength <note>powerful</note> at night. With the exception of Gemini, these same signs are "Rear-rising" <note>original: *Prishthodaya*, rising from the back</note>. Gemini rises with its head first. The remaining signs—Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, and Aquarius—are "Head-rising" <note>original: *Shirshodaya*</note> and are powerful during the day.

Note that this statement regarding day and night strength is a general classification. The author will explain the specific nuances of strength and weakness later in this chapter in the three verses starting from verse sixteen. Regarding the "Best of Signs": at their respective times of rising, those signs are considered superior. The "Two Fish" <note>Pisces</note>, which are two fish joined head-to-tail, rise "both ways" <note>original: *Ubhayodaya*</note>, meaning the head and tail appear to rise simultaneously.

As stated in the **Brihat Jataka** as well:
> "Taurus, Aries, Sagittarius, Cancer, and Gemini are nocturnal signs. Except for Gemini, these are called Rear-rising. The rest are Head-rising and powerful during the day. The pair of large-scaled fish <note>Pisces</note> rises both ways." — Verses 13-14

---

Aries, Taurus, and Aquarius are short in stature. Capricorn, Gemini, Sagittarius, Pisces, and Cancer are of medium length. Scorpio, Virgo, Leo, and Libra are long. The twelve signs from Aries are designated as Male and Female in sequence. Aries, Gemini, Leo, Libra, Sagittarius, and Aquarius are Male signs. Taurus, Cancer, Virgo, Scorpio, Capricorn, and Pisces are Female signs.

Aries, Taurus, Gemini, and Cancer, along with their 5th and 9th signs, belong to the directions starting from the East.
*   **East:** Aries, Leo, Sagittarius.
*   **South:** Taurus, Virgo, Capricorn.
*   **West:** Gemini, Libra, Aquarius.
*   **North:** Cancer, Scorpio, Pisces.

Aries, Gemini, Leo, Libra, Sagittarius, and Aquarius are "Cruel." Taurus, Cancer, Virgo, Scorpio, Capricorn, and Pisces are "Auspicious." The twelve signs are also categorized as Movable, Fixed, and Dual-natured.
*   **Movable (1, 4, 7, 10):** Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn.
*   **Fixed (2, 5, 8, 11):** Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius.
*   **Dual (3, 6, 9, 12):** Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces. — Verse 13

Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Sagittarius, Aries, and Capricorn are strong at night. Except for Gemini, these are Rear-rising. The remaining signs (Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Aquarius) are strong during the day. These and Gemini are Head-rising. Pisces, consisting of two fish with heads and tails joined, is Both-rising. Those that rise from the back are *Prishthodaya*; those that rise from the head are *Shirshodaya*. — Verse 14

### Now, the specific Water-related classifications of Pisces and the others.

> Pisces, Scorpio, Cancer, and the first half of Capricorn are called "Watery" signs. Aquarius, Virgo, Gemini, and Taurus are "Water-seeking" <note>meaning they stay near water but are not of it</note>. The wise say that Aries, Sagittarius, Libra, and Leo are "Waterless," wandering only on dry land. || 15 ||

Pisces, Scorpio, Cancer, and Capricorn <note>specifically the first half</note> are known as "Water-dwellers" <term>Jalachara (aquatic creatures)</term>. Aquarius, Virgo, Gemini, and Taurus are "Water-dependent" <term>Toyashraya (resting near water)</term> but are not themselves aquatic. Aries, Sagittarius, Libra, and Leo are "Waterless" <term>Nistoya (without water)</term>, meaning they move upon the dry surface of the earth; so say many great sages. || 15 ||

<note>The Sanskrit text uses poetic synonyms for the signs: 'Kriya' for Aries, 'Taukshika' for Libra, and 'Kanthirava' for Leo.</note>

# On the Commentary of Jataka Parijata

-> Verse 18 <-

Bipeds <note>human signs</note> are powerful when occupying a center <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note> during the day; quadrupeds are powerful in the centers at night. All "creatures of the water" <note>literally 'insects' or 'water-dwellers'</note> possess strength during the two twilights if they are situated in the angles. || 18 ||

The second half of Sagittarius, Leo, Taurus, the first half of Capricorn, and Aries are called **Quadrupeds**. When these are positioned in the **tenth house** <note>the Midheaven</note>, they are endowed with strength.

Virgo, Gemini, Aquarius, Libra, and the first part of Sagittarius are **Human signs** (Bipeds). If these are associated with the **Ascendant** <note>the 1st house</note>, they become powerful.

The latter half of Capricorn, Pisces, and Cancer are known as **Water-dwellers**. They are powerful in the **fourth house**. The sign named Scorpio is also water-dependent; it becomes powerful when reaching the **seventh house**. As Varahamihira <note>a famous 6th-century Indian astronomer and astrologer</note> said:
> "The seventh, first, fourth, and tenth houses are called the 'Kanthaka' or 'Kendra' (Centers). In these respective places, the Insects, Humans, Water-dwellers, and Animals are powerful as stated."

Now, the strength of the signs is described according to time: **The Centers.** A human sign situated in any of the centers—the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses—is powerful during the **day**. Quadrupeds in the centers are powerful at **night**. All "Insects" <note>Note: Here the word 'insect' does not just mean Scorpio, but includes all water-dwelling signs</note> are powerful during the **two twilights** (dawn and dusk) if they are in the centers. So it is said in the *Svalpa Jataka*: "Insects are strong at twilight, humans and quadrupeds at night and day respectively." This strength of the signs should be carefully considered during both birth charts and inquiry <term>Prashna: Horary astrology where a chart is cast for the moment a question is asked</term> charts. || 16-18 ||

<margin>The second half of Sagittarius, Leo, Taurus, the first half of Capricorn, and Aries are quadrupeds and are strong in the 10th house. Virgo, Gemini, Aquarius, Libra, and the first half of Sagittarius are human signs and are strong in the Ascendant.</margin>

<margin>The second half of Capricorn, Pisces, and Cancer are water-dwellers and are strong in the 4th. Scorpio is water-based and is strong in the 7th.</margin>

### The Classification of Signs as Mineral, Vegetable, and Animal

The ancients say that the signs starting from Aries are Mineral, Vegetable, and Animal respectively; the same applies to the odd and even signs. Minerals range from gold to earth; Vegetables range from grass to trees; and the "Animal-heap" refers to living beings. || 19 ||

Now the specific names for the signs such as "Mineral" are explained. The learned say that the twelve signs starting from Aries are sequentially named **Mineral** (Dhatu), **Vegetable** (Mula), and **Animal** (Jiva).
*   **Mineral signs:** Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn.
*   **Vegetable signs:** Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius.
*   **Animal signs:** Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces.

The same applies to the **Odd and Even** signs. Aries, Gemini, Leo, Libra, Sagittarius, and Aquarius are Odd (uneven) signs. Taurus, Cancer, Virgo, Scorpio, Capricorn, and Pisces are Even signs. Regarding the doubt of what constitutes a "Mineral," etc.: Minerals include everything from gold to soil. Vegetables include everything up to grass and trees. The "Animal-heap" refers to living creatures...

# Chapter on the Nature of the Signs || 1 ||

The word *Kuta* <note>original: "कूटो"</note> refers to a sign (representing all living beings). According to the *Amarakosha* <note>A famous Sanskrit lexicon</note>: "The words *svangikaya*, *punja*, *rashi*, *tulvara*, and *kuta* are synonyms used in the non-feminine gender." This should be understood as the "Soul" or "Living Being" category. The purpose of this classification is to identify objects or substances in questions related to the delivery room or lost property. || 19 ||

The learned say that the signs starting from Aries are categorized as Mineral, Vegetable, and Soul. (Specifically: 1, 4, 7, 10 are Mineral; 2, 5, 8, 11 are Vegetable; and 3, 6, 9, 12 are Soul). They are also categorized as Odd and Even. "Mineral" ranges from gold to soil. "Vegetable" ranges from trees to grass. "Soul" refers to all living creatures. || 19 ||

### Now, the Determination of the Castes (Brahmin, etc.) of Aries and the others.

> Pisces, Scorpio, and Taurus are Brahmins; Sagittarius, Aries, and Leo are Kings (Kshatriyas).
> Aquarius, Gemini, and Libra are Merchants (Vaishyas); Virgo, Capricorn, and Cancer are Laborers (Shudras). || 20 ||

Pisces, Scorpio, and Taurus are of the Brahmin caste. Sagittarius, Aries, and Leo are Kings or the Warrior caste. Aquarius, Gemini, and Libra are Merchants. Virgo, Capricorn, and Cancer are of the Laborer caste. The purpose of this is to identify the caste of a thief, or to determine the compatibility of the bride and groom's castes during marriage.

| 12, 8, 2 | 9, 1, 5 | 11, 3, 7 | 6, 10, 4 | Alternative Opinion |

Pisces, Scorpio, and Taurus are Brahmin caste. Sagittarius, Aries, and Leo are Warrior caste. Aquarius, Gemini, and Libra are Merchant caste. Virgo, Capricorn, and Cancer are Laborer caste. || 20 ||

### Now, the Determination of Blindness, etc., of Aries and others at specific times.

> Aries, Taurus, and Leo are always blind at night; Cancer, Gemini, and Virgo at midday.
> Libra and Scorpio are deaf in the morning; Sagittarius and Capricorn are likewise in the afternoon. || 21 ||

> Capricorn and Sagittarius are lame during the two twilights; they become destroyers.
> The "Zodiacal Junction" <term>Riksha-sandhi: the sensitive point where a sign and a lunar mansion end simultaneously</term> is known to occur at the end of Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces; this is famously called *Pragandanta*. || 22 ||

Aries, Taurus, and Leo are always blind at night. The word "always" is used because their blindness never leaves them during any night. There is another reading: "blind at the Great Night," meaning they would be blind at midnight. Cancer, Gemini, and Virgo become blind at midday (the middle part of the day). Libra and Scorpio are deaf during the forenoon (the first third of the day). Sagittarius and Capricorn are likewise deaf in the afternoon (the third part of the day). Capricorn and Sagittarius are "lame" <note>original: *pangu*</note> during the two twilights (dawn and dusk). They are called "destroyers" because they bring harm; if Sagittarius or Capricorn are the rising signs during the two twilights, they cause the destruction of the newborn or the person asking the question. Regarding the "Zodiacal Junction": the ends of the signs Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces are called *Riksha-sandhi*. This is where a lunar mansion <note>Nakshatra</note> and a zodiac sign end at the same time. For example: the end of Cancer coincides with the end of the Ashlesha mansion, the end of Scorpio with Jyeshtha, and the end of Pisces with Revati.

# Commentary on the Jataka Parijata

Regarding the term *Gandanta* <note>literally "end of the cheek" or a spiritual knot</note> = the junction of two constellations (*Riksha-sandhi*) is famously known as *Gandanta* or *Lagna-Gandanta* <note>the critical junction point of the rising sign</note>. Regarding these two, the teacher Ramacharya states: "The junction of Cancer and the following sign <note>Leo</note> consists of half a *ghatika* <note>approx. 12 minutes</note>." Here, it should be understood by the wise that what Ramacharya stated regarding the "blindness" of signs—"Leo, Aries, and Taurus are blind during the day; Virgo, Gemini, and Cancer are blind at night; the last *ghatika* of the day and night are termed 'lame'"—pertains to *Muhurta* <note>electional astrology for choosing auspicious times</note> and not to *Jataka* <note>natal astrology</note>, as it differs from the present primary text. // 21-22 //

**Aries, Taurus, and Leo are blind during the Great Night (exactly midnight). Cancer, Gemini, and Virgo remain blind during Midday (noon). Libra and Scorpio are deaf during the forenoon (morning). Sagittarius and Capricorn are deaf in the afternoon (post-noon). Capricorn and Sagittarius are "lame" during the twilight hours. These periods are destructive. The ends of Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces are the constellation junctions; these are also called *Gandanta* (or *Lagna-Gandanta*). // 21-22 //**

### Now, the specific colors of Aries and the other signs.

> Red, fair, parrot-colored, and pale red; pale white, variegated, blue, and golden;
> Yellowish-brown, brindled, tawny, and white are the colors assigned to the houses beginning with Aries. // 23 //

In the houses beginning with *Tambura* <note>original: "Tambura" is a synonym for Aries</note> = the houses of Aries and the rest (meaning the zodiac signs), the colors assigned are red, fair, parrot-like, pale red, pale white, variegated, blue, golden, yellowish-brown, brindled, tawny, and white. Specifically: Aries is red. Taurus is fair. Gemini is the color of a parrot <note>vibrant green</note>. Cancer is pale red <note>original: "Patala," a pinkish or trumpet-flower color</note>. Leo is pale white. Virgo is variegated <note>multi-colored</note>. Libra is blue. Scorpio is golden. Sagittarius is yellowish-brown. Capricorn is brindled <note>a mixture of white and yellow</note>. Aquarius is tawny <note>like a mongoose</note>. Pisces is white. // 23 //

**The color of Aries is red, Taurus is white, Gemini is green, Cancer is reddish-white, Leo is white, Virgo is multi-colored, Libra is blue, Scorpio is gold-colored (yellow), Sagittarius is yellow, Capricorn is yellowish-white, Aquarius is like a mongoose, and Pisces is a bright white color. // 23 //**

### Now, the results of the strength and weakness of Aries and the others.

> Clothing, fine rice, forest fruits, the *Kandali* deer, primary grains,
> Pithy trees, mung beans, sesame and garments, sugarcane and iron,
> Weapons and horses, gold, water-born flowers, and all aquatic products;
> These are the substances said to be scarce or abundant depending on whether Aries and the others are weak or strong. // 24 //

With this verse, the author describes the commodities associated with Aries and the other signs. In "Aries and the others," these substances are said by the learned to be found in small or large quantities depending on whether the signs are weak or strong. What are they? For Aries: clothing and fine rice <note>Shali rice</note>. For Taurus: a collection of forest fruits. For Gemini: the *Kandali* <note>a specific type of deer; the commentary cites the Amarakosha dictionary to define it among varieties like the spotted deer</note>. For Cancer: the primary grains. For Leo: pithy trees <note>original: "Tvaksara," plants with sturdy bark or bamboo</note>. For Virgo: mung beans <note>known as "Moong" in the local language</note>. For Libra: sesame and clothing. For Scorpio: sugarcane and iron. For Sagittarius: weapons and horses. For Capricorn: gold and precious metals. For Aquarius: flowers born in water, such as the lotus. For Pisces: all things produced in water. The practical use of this is to answer questions regarding profit and loss. // 24 //

# On the Jataka Parijata with Commentary
## Page 15

For Venus, Saturn, the Sun, and Jupiter, the first **twenty degrees** <note>original: "nakha-amshakah," literally 'fingernail-parts' representing the number 20</note> are the **Mula-Trikona** <note>A primary root-position of strength, stronger than a standard home sign but less than an exaltation</note>; beyond that, from the twentieth to the thirtieth degree, is their own house. This means: for Venus, Saturn, the Sun, and Jupiter, in the signs of Libra, Aquarius, Leo, and Sagittarius respectively, the first 20 degrees are Mula-Trikona. After that, it is their own home.

Now he describes the Mula-Trikona and other states for the Moon, Mars, Mercury, and Rahu <note>The North Node of the Moon</note>. The first **three degrees** in the sign of Taurus are the **exaltation** <note>original: "ucca"</note> of the Moon; all the remaining parts (the remaining 27 degrees of Taurus) are the Moon's Mula-Trikona. For Mars, the first **twelve degrees** in the sign of Aries are defined as Mula-Trikona; the remaining eighteen degrees are his own house.

Now for Mercury: half of Virgo (**fifteen degrees**) is the exaltation of the son of the Moon <note>Mercury</note>; the next **ten degrees** (from the 15th to the 25th) are his Mula-Trikona; the remaining **five degrees** (from the 25th to the 30th) result in his own sign influence. Now for Rahu: for the Lord of Serpents <note>Rahu</note>, the entire sign of Aquarius is his Trikona, Gemini is his exaltation, and Virgo is his home. As stated in the *Prashna Bhairava* regarding the planets Rahu and Ketu:

> "The sign of Virgo is accepted as the home of Rahu <note>original: "vidhuntuda," the 'moon-tormentor'</note> because of his friendship with Mercury. The seventh sign from that, called Pisces, is said by the wise to be held by Ketu <note>original: "shikhina," the 'crested one'</note>."

Likewise regarding exaltation: "The exaltation of the son of Simhika <note>Rahu</note> is said to be Gemini, ruled by Mercury. The exaltation of the tail, Ketu, is said to be Sagittarius, ruled by Jupiter." || 26-28 ||

'Ni', 'Mi', and 'Cha' are known as zero, as are vowels standing alone." <note>This explains the Katapayadi system, a medieval Indian mnemonic device used to encode numbers into easily memorizable words or verses.</note>
