# Chapter 1: On the Nature of the Zodiac Signs

According to the mnemonic code, the numbers are: Always = 10; Woman = 3; Lion = 28; By me = 15; Manu = 5; Essence = 27; Water = 20. <note>These are mnemonic words used in Sanskrit to remember numbers: Nitya (10), Angana (3), Hari (28), Maya (15), Manu (5), Sara (27), and Neera (20).</note> These numbers represent the degrees of the highest exaltation <term>Paramocha: the specific degree within a sign where a planet's influence is strongest</term> for the Sun and other planets in their respective exaltation signs. Similarly, these same degrees in the opposite (seventh) signs are to be known as the points of deepest debilitation. As stated by Varahamihira <note>A famous 6th-century Indian astronomer and polymath</note>:

> "Aries, Taurus, Capricorn, Virgo, Cancer, Pisces, and Libra are the exaltation signs for the Sun and the others. The degrees of highest exaltation and deepest debilitation are ten, three, twenty-eight, fifteen, five, twenty-seven, and twenty."

In horoscopy and related fields, the mention of a planet's exaltation and debilitation is intended solely for the purpose of predicting results, not merely to calculate mathematical strength. The sages observed that a planet produces its most distinct or specialized effects at a particular degree within a sign; therefore, that degree is designated as its "exaltation," and the opposite point is its "debilitation." This should be carefully considered by the skillful. Now, the Sage Garga explains the purpose of knowing these exaltations:

> "The Sun and Moon in their exaltation signs produce a ruler of men. Even in their Trine <term>Trikona: specific auspicious zones in the zodiac</term> positions, if they are exalted, they make a person wealthy and famous."

Likewise, the effect of debilitation:

> "The Sun and Moon, if in their deepest debilitation, can make a man blind, a beggar, a fool, or one who lives off the charity of others."

The exaltation signs for the Sun and other planets are Aries, Taurus, Capricorn, Virgo, Cancer, Pisces, and Libra. The seventh sign from each exaltation sign is its debilitation sign. The highest exaltation degrees for the Sun and others are, in order: 10, 3, 28, 15, 5, 27, and 20. The deepest debilitation points are the same degrees in the seventh signs. For clarity, see the chart below. // 29 //

->**Definition of the Ten Divisions (Dashavarga) and Their Lords**<-

The Ascendant, Hora, Drekkana, Saptamsha, Navamsha, Dashamsha, Dwadashamsha, Kalansha, Trimshamsha, and Shashtiamsha <note>These are the ten ways of dividing a zodiac sign into smaller portions to refine a horoscope</note> are the divisions that bring about the destruction of sins and the arrival of prosperity for men. In odd signs, the two halves (Hora) belong to the Sun and the Moon respectively; in even signs, they belong to the Moon and the Sun. The Drekkanas (one-third divisions) are ruled by the lords of the first, fifth, and ninth houses from that sign. // 30 //

The lords of the Saptamsha (one-seventh divisions) in an odd sign start from the sign itself; in an even sign, they start from the seventh sign thereafter. // 31 //
For Sagittarius, Aries, and Leo, the Navamshas (one-ninth divisions) begin with Aries. For Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn, they begin with Capricorn. // 32 //
For Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius, the Navamshas begin with Libra. For Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces, they begin with Cancer. // 33 //
In a movable sign, the first division is Vargottama <term>Vargottama: a planet occupying the same sign in both the main chart and the 9th division, increasing its strength</term>; in a fixed sign, the middle division; and in a dual sign, the final division. // 34 //
The lords of the Dashamsha (one-tenth divisions) begin from the sign itself in odd signs, and from the ninth sign in even signs. // 35 //
The lords of the Dwadashamsha (one-twelfth divisions) follow the sequence of the signs themselves. // 36 //
In odd signs, the lords of the Kalansha (sixteenth divisions) are Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva, and the Sun. In even signs, these lords, starting with the Sun, are applied in reverse order. // 37 //

# On the Jataka Parijata with Commentary

In an odd sign, the degrees of Mars, Saturn, Jupiter, Mercury, and Venus are ruled by the Air, Wind, the Eight, the Mountain, and the Five <note>original: "समीरपवनाष्टकशैलबाणाः" - these are numerical codes (Sankhya) where Air/Wind = 5, Eight = 8, Mountain = 7, and Five = 5. This defines the span of degrees for each planet in the Trimsamsha or 30th division</note>. In an even sign, the degrees belong to Venus, Mercury, Jupiter, Saturn, and Mars, following the order of the Wind, the Mountain, the Serpent (8), and the Five-Arrows (5). || 37 || (9)

The lords of the sixtieth divisions <term>Shashtyamsas (1/60th of a sign)</term> in an odd sign begin with the "Terrible" division and follow the sequence of Demon, God, and so on. These divisions, such as "Moon-line," indicate good or bad results. In an even sign, the order is exactly reversed. || 38 || (10)

<note>The following list names the 60 specific qualities of the Shashtyamsa divisions, which determine the precise "flavor" of a planet's influence.</note>

The divisions are: 1. Terrible, 2. Rakshasa (Demonic), 3. Deva (Divine), 4. Kubera (Lord of Wealth), 5. Yaksha (Nature Spirit), 6. Kindar (Celestial Musician), 7. Fallen, 8. Family-Destroyer, 9. Poison, 10. Fire, 11. Illusion, 12. Lord of the City of the Dead (Yama). || 39 ||

13. Lord of Waters (Varuna), 14. Deva (Divine), 15. Ganesha, 16. Digit of the Moon, 17. Serpent, 18. Nectar-portion, 19. Moon, 20. Soft/Mild, 21. Tender Lotus, 22. Lord of Lakshmi (Vishnu), 23. Lord of Speech (Brahma), 24. Sky-clad (Digambara). || 40 ||

25. Mountain of the Gods, 26. Destroyer of Strife, 27. Lord of the Earth, 28. Lotus-pond, 29. Son of Saturn (Gulika), 30. Death-maker, 31. Time (Kala), 32. Forest Fire, 33. Terrible, 34. Sinful, 35. Thorn. || 41 ||

36. Nectar, 37. Nectar-rayed, 38. Full Moon, 39. Poisonous, 40. Fire of the Directions, 41. Destroyer of the Lineage, 42. Chief, 43. Decay of the Race, 44. Sinful, 45. Time, 46. Gentle, 47. Soft, 48. Cool. || 42 ||

49. Fanged, 50. Cruel, 51. Moon-faced, 52. Learned, 53. Fire of Time, 54. Rod of Punishment, 55. Weapon, 56. Pure, 57. Beneficent, 58. Unlucky, 59. Cool-rayed, 60. Nectar-Ocean, Wandering, and Moon-line. || 43 ||

## Now the Tenfold Divisions (Dasha-Vargas) of the Planets are Described.

To the question "What are the ten divisions?", the text replies: The Ascendant (Lagna), the Hora, the Drekkana, the Saptamsha, the Navamsha, the Dashamsha, the Dwadashamsha, the Kalansha (Shodashamsha), the Trimsamsha, and the Shashtyamsa. These ten divisions of men <note>meaning: in a human birth chart</note> bring about the accumulation of expenses, sins, or prosperity. It should be understood here that divisions belonging to "malefic" (cruel) planets cause expense and sin, while "benefic" (gentle) divisions bring prosperity.

**1. The Ascendants (Lagnas):** These are the own signs of the planets already mentioned.

**2. Now, the Hora:** A Hora is half a sign (15 degrees). In any sign, there are two Horas. In an **odd sign**, the first half belongs to the Sun and the second half to the Moon. In an **even sign**, the Horas of the Moon and Sun are reversed: the first belongs to the Moon and the second to the Sun.

**3. Now, the Drekkana:** These are the three-fold divisions of a sign (10 degrees each). They belong to the lords of the 1st, 5th, and 9th positions from the sign itself. For example, in Aries: the first 10 degrees belong to Mars (Lord of Aries). The next 10 degrees (up to 20) belong to the Sun (Lord of Leo, the 5th from Aries). The final 10 degrees (up to 30) belong to Jupiter (Lord of Sagittarius, the 9th from Aries). This logic applies everywhere. 

<margin>The sage Yavaneshwara holds that each planet has its own Hora, and that the lords of the 1st, 12th, and 11th signs are the Drekkana lords.</margin> 

His verse says: 
> "The first Hora belongs to the lord of the house; the second to the lord of the eleventh. The Drekkanas are known to belong to the lords of the sign itself, the 12th, and the 11th respectively."

However, Varahamihira states the widely accepted view:
> "In an odd sign, the Horas belong to the Sun and Moon; in an even sign, to the Moon and Sun. The Drekkanas belong to the lords of the house, the fifth, and the ninth."

**4. Now, the Saptamshas (Seventh-parts):** These are the seven divisions of a sign. Each part is 4 degrees, 17 minutes, and 18 seconds (4° 17' 18''). How are they known? In an **odd sign** (Aries, Gemini, etc.), the lords of the seven parts follow the sequence of the signs starting from that sign. For example, in Aries: the 1st part is Aries, the 2nd is Taurus, the 3rd is Gemini, and so on up to the 7th (Libra). In an **even sign** (Taurus, Cancer, etc.), the lords start from the **seventh sign** from that sign. For example, in Taurus: the lords start from the 7th (Scorpio), so the 1st part is Scorpio...

<summary>This page details the specific names and qualities of the 60 Shashtyamsa divisions and begins explaining the "Dasha-Varga" (Tenfold Division) system, specifically defining the Lagna, Hora, Drekkana, and Saptamsha.</summary>
<keywords>Trimsamsha, Shashtyamsa, Dasha-Varga, Hora, Drekkana, Saptamsha, Varahamihira, Yavaneshwara, Vedic Astrology, planetary divisions</keywords>

<header>Chapter on the Nature of the Signs || 1 ||</header>

# Chapter on the Nature of the Signs || 1 ||

The second belongs to Sagittarius, and thus the seven should be known up to Taurus. For clarity, the <term>Saptamsha</term><note>A divisional chart where a sign is divided into 7 equal parts of 4° 17' 8" each.</note> chart should be consulted.

5. Now, the **Navamshas** <note>The 9th divisional chart, the most important sub-chart in Indian astrology, representing the "fruit" or inner strength of a planet.</note>. A ninth part of a sign is a Navamsha, consisting of three and a half <term>Nakshatra</term> quarters <note>Specifically 3 degrees and 20 minutes</note> (3° 12' 0" <insert>sic: usually 3° 20'</insert>). There are nine such segments per sign. The method for knowing them is stated: For the signs of Sagittarius, Aries, and Leo, the Navamshas begin from Aries. In these three signs, the first belongs to Aries, the second to Taurus, the third to Gemini, and so on until the ninth, which is Sagittarius. Their lords are called the Navamsha-lords. For Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn, the nine Navamshas are declared to begin from Capricorn. For Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius, the nine Navamshas should be known to begin from Libra. For Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces, the Navamshas begin from Cancer; thus the Navamsha chart should be consulted.

Now, the **Vargottamas** <note>Literally "best division"; refers to a planet occupying the same zodiac sign in both the main chart and the Navamsha chart, increasing its strength.</note>. In a <term>Movable sign</term> (Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn), the first Navamsha (0° to 3° 20') is known as Vargottama. In a <term>Fixed sign</term> (Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius), the middle Navamsha—the fifth one (from 13° 20' to 16° 40')—is Vargottama. In a <term>Dual sign</term> (Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces), the final Navamsha—the ninth one (from 26° 40' to 30°)—is Vargottama. As stated by <term>Mihira</term><note>Varahamihira, the 6th-century astronomer and polymath.</note>:

> "The Navamshas are called Vargottama at the beginning, middle, and end of Movable, Fixed, and Dual signs respectively, and they yield auspicious results."

6. Now, the **Dashamshas** <note>The 10th divisional chart, used for determining profession and success.</note>. The tenth parts of a sign consist of three degrees (3°). There are ten in each sign. In an odd sign, the lords of the Dashamshas begin from the sign itself. In an even sign, they should be known to begin from the ninth sign from the sign in question. As stated in the <term>Parashari</term><note>The Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra, the foundational text of Indian astrology.</note>:

> "In an odd sign, count from the sign itself; in an even sign, declare it from the ninth thereof."

For clarity, the Dashamsha chart should be consulted.

7. Now, the **Dwadashamshas** <note>The 12th divisional chart, representing parents and ancestry.</note>. The twelfth parts of a sign consist of two and a half degrees (2° 30'). There are twelve in each sign. They follow the sequence of the signs: starting from the sign under consideration, the twelve signs in order are the lords of the Dwadashamshas. In Aries, they start from Aries and end in Pisces; this is how it should be known everywhere. For clarity, the Dwadashamsha chart should be consulted.

8. Now, the **Shodashamshas** <note>The 16th divisional chart, used for vehicles, luxuries, and general happiness.</note>. There are sixteen Shodashamshas in one sign. Each segment is one degree and fifty-two and a half minutes (1° 52' 30"). In an odd sign, the lords of these parts are Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva, and the Sun. In an even sign, it is in reverse: the lords are the Sun, Shiva, Vishnu, and Brahma. Regarding how the count is performed:

> "In Movable signs count from Aries, in Fixed signs from Leo, and in Dual signs always from Sagittarius. Thus the Shodashamshas are to be calculated."

For clarity, the chart should be consulted.

9. Now, the **Trimshamshas** <note>The 30th divisional chart, often used to determine character and misfortunes.</note>. There are five Trimshamsha divisions in each sign. In an odd sign, they are governed by Mars, Saturn, Jupiter, Mercury, and Venus in segments of 5, 5, 8, 7, and 5 degrees respectively. <note>The text uses poetic number-names: 'Samiira' (5), 'Pavana' (5), 'Ashtaka' (8), 'Shaila' (7), and 'Bana' (5).</note> In an even sign, the order is reversed: Venus, Mercury, Jupiter, Saturn, and Mars take 5, 7, 8, 5, and 5 degrees respectively. As stated by <term>Varaha</term>:

> "The portions of Mars, Saturn, Jupiter, Mercury, and Venus in an odd sign follow the degrees 5, 5, 8, 7, 5; in an even sign, the order and degrees are reversed."

10. Now, the **Shashtiamshas** <note>The 60th divisional chart, used for very fine distinctions in karma.</note>. There are sixty of these in one sign, and each segment consists of thirty minutes (0° 30').

# With the Commentary on Jataka Parijata

The lords of these <term>Shashtyamsas</term><note>The 1/60th division of a zodiac sign, measuring 30 minutes of arc.</note> in an **odd sign** begin with *Ghora*, *Rakshasa*, *Deva*, and so on, up to *Indulekha*. In an **even sign**, the order is reversed, starting from *Indulekha* and ending with *Ghora*. It should be understood that a Shashtyamsa ruled by an inauspicious lord yields bad results, while one ruled by a benign lord yields good results. For clarity, one should consult the Shashtyamsa chart.

The ten divisions (<term>Dashavargas</term>) are: <term>Lagna</term><note>Ascendant</note>, <term>Hora</term>, <term>Drekkana</term>, <term>Saptamansha</term>, <term>Navamansha</term>, <term>Dashamansha</term>, <term>Dwadashamansha</term>, <term>Shodashansha</term>, <term>Trimshansha</term>, and <term>Shashtyamsa</term>. These determine a person's expenses, sorrows, growth, and prosperity (auspicious divisions cause growth and fortune, while malefic divisions cause loss and sin). A <term>Hora</term> is half of a sign (15 degrees). There are two Horas in one sign. In **odd signs**, the first 15 degrees belong to the Sun and the next to the Moon; in **even signs**, the first 15 degrees belong to the Moon and the next to the Sun. A <term>Drekkana</term> (10 degrees) belongs to the sign itself for the first 10 degrees, to the 5th sign from it for the next 10, and to the 9th sign for the final 10 degrees. || 30 ||

In **odd signs**, the lords of the <term>Saptamansha</term><note>1/7th division</note> follow the order of the signs starting from the sign itself. In **even signs**, the lords start from the 7th sign away. Each Saptamansha segment is slightly more than 4 degrees, 17 minutes, and 8 seconds. || 31 ||

For Sagittarius, Aries, and Leo, the <term>Navamansha</term><note>1/9th division, the most important sub-chart in Hindu astrology</note> begins from Aries. For Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn, it begins from Capricorn. For Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius, it begins from Libra. For Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces, it begins from Cancer. Each Navamansha segment is 3 degrees and 20 minutes. || 32-33 ||

The first Navamansha of **movable signs** (Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn), the middle (5th) Navamansha of **fixed signs** (Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius), and the final Navamansha of **dual signs** (Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces) is called <term>Vargottama</term><note>Literally "best division," where a planet occupies the same sign in both the main chart and the 1/9th chart, increasing its strength.</note>. || 34 ||

In **odd signs**, the <term>Dashamansha</term><note>1/10th division</note> lords follow the sign order, and in **even signs**, they start from the 9th sign. One Dashamansha part is 3 degrees. The <term>Dwadashamansha</term><note>1/12th division</note> lords follow the sequence of the signs starting from the sign itself. One Dwadashamansha part is 2.5 degrees. || 35 ||

The 1/16th part of a sign is called <term>Shodashansha</term>. In **odd signs**, the lords are Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva, and the Sun in that order. In **even signs**, the order is reversed: Sun, Shiva, Vishnu, and Brahma. Each Shodashansha segment is 1 degree, 52 minutes, and 30 seconds. For movable signs, count from Aries; for fixed, from Leo; and for dual signs, from Sagittarius.

> "The experts of astrology should calculate the Shodashansha from Aries for movable signs, from Leo for fixed signs, and from Sagittarius for dual signs." || 36 ||

In **odd signs**, the <term>Trimshansha</term><note>1/30th division, used specifically for assessing strengths and character</note> belongs to Mars (5°), then Saturn (5°), then Jupiter (8°), then Mercury (7°), and finally Venus (5°). In **even signs**, it belongs to Venus (5°), Mercury (7°), Jupiter (8°), Saturn (5°), and Mars (5°). || 37 ||

There are 60 <term>Shashtyamsas</term> in one sign. Each segment is 30 minutes. In **odd signs**, the 60 lords range from *Ghora* to *Indulekha*. In **even signs**, they are reversed. They are as follows: 1. Ghora (Terrible), 2. Rakshasa (Demonic), 3. Deva (Divine), 4. Kubera (Wealth), 5. Yakshagana (Nature spirits), 6. Kinnara (Celestial musicians), 7. Bhrashta (Fallen), 8. Kulaghna (Family-destroyer), 9. Garala (Poison), 10. Agni (Fire), 11. Maya (Illusion), 12. Yama (Death), 13. Varuna (Water), 14. Indra (King of Gods), 15. Kala (Time), 16. Sarpa (Serpent), 17. Amrita (Nectar), 18. Chandra (Moon), 19. Mridu (Soft), 20. Komala (Tender), 21. Padma (Lotus), 22. Vishnu (Preserver), 23. Guru (Teacher), 24. Shiva (Destroyer), 25. Deva (Divine), 26. Ardra (Moist), 27. Kaliyansha (Strife), 28. Kshitisha (Lord of Earth), 29. Kamalakara (Lotus-pond), 30. Mandatmaja (Son of Saturn), 31. Mrityukara (Death-bringer), 32. Kala (Time/Fate), 33. Davagni (Forest fire), 34. Ghora (Terrible), 35. Adhama (Lowly), 36. Kantaka (Thorn), 37. Sudha (Nectar), 38. Amrita (Nectar), 39. Purnachandra (Full Moon), 40. Vishadagdha (Poison-burnt), 41. Kulanasha (Lineage-destroyer), 42. Mukhya (Chief), 43. Vamshakshaya (Family-decay), 44. Utpataka (Calamitous), 45. Kala (Time), 46. Saumya (Gentle), 47. Mridu (Soft), 48. Shitala (Cool), 49. ### 6. The Trimsamsha Chart <note>The 30th division of a sign, used primarily to determine misfortunes and character traits.</note>

#### Now, the Special Designations arising from the Ten Divisions (Dashavarga).

**When a planet occupies its Mula-Trikona <note>root-trine/primary dignity</note>, its own house, its exaltation, or its Vargottama <note>same sign in both birth and divisional charts</note> across the ten divisions,**
**The resulting combinations are given names beginning with "Uttama" and are called Vaisheshika-amshas <note>distinguished or special portions</note>. || 44 ||**
**The union of three favorable divisions is called Uttama; four is Gopura;**
**The combination of five divisions is here called Simhasana. || 45 ||**
**Two divisions is Parijata; six is the Paravata portion;**
**The seventh is Devaloka, and the eighth shall be the same. || 46 ||**
**Nine is Airavata. The results of these are given separately. || 3 ||**

Here, certain special names arising from the <term>Dashavarga</term> <note>the ten-fold system of divisional charts</note> are explained. For those born in the ten divisions—meaning those arising from the ten charts—when a planet is in its <term>Mula-Trikona</term>, own house, exaltation, or <term>Vargottama</term> (as previously mentioned), the combinations are named starting with "Uttama." Scholars say these are the <term>Vaisheshika-amshas</term>, which are special yogas <note>planetary combinations</note>. Now, what are these specific named yogas and how do they arise? He says:
"Uttama" and so on. The union of three divisions—meaning if a planet is in its own favorable division in three out of the ten charts—it is 1. Uttama. Four divisions is named 2. Gopura. The combination of five divisions is here called 3. Simhasana.
Two divisions is 4. Parijata. With the union of six divisions, it is 5. Paravata-amsha. The seventh—the union of seven divisions—is 6. Devaloka. The eighth, or the union of eight divisions, is also the same—it shall be Devaloka. The ninth—the union of nine divisions—is 7. Airavata. The union of ten—(if in all ten divisions the planet is in its own favorable place)—it becomes 8. Vaisheshika-amsha. <note>Note: The text here uses "Vaisheshika" as the highest specific rank, though the term also refers to the category as a whole.</note>
As stated in another text:
> "With the union of two divisions, there is Parijata yoga; one who knows this becomes wealthy. With three, Uttama. With four, Gopura.
> Simhasana is the yoga with five divisions; one who knows this becomes a king. With the union of six, Paravata yoga; here one becomes a great scholar of the scriptures.
> With the union of seven or eight, it is Devaloka yoga; such a person is a generous king. With nine divisions, it is Airavata yoga; here one is a universal emperor.
> With the union of ten divisions, it is Vaisheshika yoga; in this, a man is highly intelligent."

A difference is seen here according to the opinion of <term>Parashara</term> <note>an ancient sage and father of Vedic astrology</note>. His statement is:
> "Parijata occurs with two; Uttama is desired with three. With four, it is named Gopura; with five, Simhasana.
> Paravata with six; Devaloka with seven. With eight, Brahmaloka; with nine, Shakra-vahana <note>Indra's vehicle</note>.
> With ten, it shall be the Shridhama yoga."

<summary>This page details the Trimsamsha (30th division) table and explains the Vaisheshika-amsha system, where planets gain specific titles (like Royal Throne or Heaven) based on how many favorable divisional charts they occupy.</summary>

# Chapter on the Nature of the Signs || 1 ||

Now, according to some opinions, "the combination of ten divisions <note>original: 'digvarga' - 'dik' means ten, referring to the Dashavarga system</note> results in the *Vaisheshika* [special] status," and according to others, "the *Shridham* yoga is formed by the ten." However, the combination of ten divisions can only occur if all planets possess *Hora* and *Trishansha* divisions; otherwise, the combination of ten is as impossible as a flower blooming in the sky <note>A classical Sanskrit idiom for something impossible or non-existent</note>. Therefore, it should be understood by great souls that in the system where the combination of ten is possible, the *Hora* and *Trishansha* divisions must necessarily be considered for all. I shall describe the results of these specific combinations separately as the occasion arises. || 44-46<gloss>3</gloss> ||

### Now, the Table of the Ten Divisions (Dashavarga) starting with Parijata.

| 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 | 10 | Total Divisions |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|----------|
| Parijata | Uttama | Gopura | Simhasana | Paravata | Devaloka | Brahmaloka | Shakravahana | Shridhama | Yoga [Combination] |

It is the opinion of the learned that the *Uttama* and other *Vaisheshikansha* (special combinations) are produced by the combination of a planet's own Moolatrikona, its own house, its exaltation point, and its *Vargottama* <note>The same sign in both the birth chart and the 9th divisional chart</note> status, as well as the union of its ten divisions (*Dashavarga*). Among these, in the system of ten divisions: if three divisions belong to the planet's own sign, it is *Uttama*; if four, it is *Gopura*; if five, it is *Simhasana*; if two, it is *Parijata*; if six, it is *Paravata*; if seven or eight, it is *Devaloka*; and if nine, it is *Airavata* <note>The text in the table lists Shakravahana, which is a synonym for Airavata, the elephant of Indra</note> yoga. The results of these specific combinations will be explained separately. || 44-46<gloss>3</gloss> ||

### Now, the Six Divisions (Shadvarga) and Seven Divisions (Saptavarga).

-> The Ascendant, *Hora*, *Drekkana*, *Navamsha*, and *Dwadashamsha* || 47 || <-
-> And the *Trishansha*—these are the Six Divisions (*Shadvarga*) praised in auspicious works. <-
-> The Six Divisions joined with the *Saptamsha* is called the Seven Divisions (*Saptavarga*) || 48 || <-
-> In all horoscopes, this is the cause of the strength of the planets. || 3/4 || <-

### Here the author speaks of the Six and Seven Divisions — "The Ascendant," etc.

The Ascendant (*Lagna*), *Hora* <note>1/2 division</note>, *Drekkana* <note>1/3 division</note>, *Navamsha* <note>1/9 division</note>, *Dwadashamsha* <note>1/12 division</note>, and *Trishansha* <note>1/30 division</note> are called the *Shadvarga*. These six divisions are praised for use in auspicious activities. As stated by Ramacharya:
> "........the house, the *Hora*, the *Drekkana*, the *Navamsha*, the *Suryabhaga* <note>The 12th division</note>, and the *Trishansha*—these six are called the divisions; they bring good through benefics and evil through malefics."

When these six divisions are joined with the *Saptamsha* <note>1/7 division</note>, it is called the *Saptavarga* by the wise. This *Saptavarga* is the cause of determining the strength of planets in all horoscopes. Because in horoscopy, the strengths of planets are mostly considered from the *Saptavarga* alone. || 47-48<gloss>3</gloss> ||

The Ascendant, *Hora*, *Drekkana*, *Navamsha*, *Dwadashamsha*, and *Trishansha* are the *Shadvarga*. The *Shadvarga* are said to be auspicious for performing good deeds. By adding the *Saptamsha* to the *Shadvarga*, the *Saptavarga* is formed. This *Saptavarga* is said to be the basis for the strength of planets in all birth charts; that is, the strength of planets is judged through the *Saptavarga*. || 47-48<gloss>3</gloss> ||

### Now, the Names of the Houses (Bhavas).

-> *Kalpa*, *Udaya*, *Adya*, *Tanu*, *Janma*, *Vilagna*, and *Hora* [are names of the 1st house]; *Vak*, *Artha*, *Bhukti*, *Nayana*, *Swa*, *Kutumba*, and *Bha* [are names of the 2nd house]. <-
-> *Dushchikya*, *Vikrama*, *Sahodara*, *Virya*, *Dhairya*, and *Karna* are the designations of the third house. || 49 || <-
-> *Patala*, *Vriddhi*, *Hibuka*, *Chitta*, *Matri*, *Vidya*, *Yana*, *Ambu*, *Geha*, *Sukha*, *Bandhu*, and *Chatushtaya* [are names of the 4th house]. <-
-> *Dhi*, *Devara*, *Raja*, *Pitri*, *Nandana* are the five [names of the 5th house]; *Roga*, *Anga*, *Shastra*, *Bhaya*, *Shastha*, *Ripu*, and *Kshata* [are names of the 6th house]. || 50 || <-
-> *Jamitra*, *Kama*, *Gamana*, *Kalatra*, *Sampad*, *Dyuna*, *Asta*, and *Saptamagraha* are what the sages call the seventh house. <-
-> *Randhra*, *Ayu*, *Harana*, *Mrityu*, and *Vinashana* [are names of the 8th house]; *Dharma*, *Guru*, *Shubha*, *Tapas*, *Navam*, and *Bhagya* [are names of the 9th house]. || 51 || <-

# Commentary on the Jataka Parijata

->**The Names of the Houses**<-

Business, the Zenith <note>original: *meshurana*, a Greek-derived term for the 10th house</note>, knowledge, the royal seat, and action are the names for the tenth house. The eleventh, the penultimate, existence, income, and gain are the names for the eleventh house. *Rihpha*, expenditure, the twelfth, and the final are the names for the twelfth house. || 52 ||

Now, the names of the twelve houses starting from the Ascendant are stated: *Kalpa* and so on. The seven names starting with *Kalpa* refer to the Ascendant <note>the 1st house</note>. The six starting with *Speech* refer to the house of wealth <note>the 2nd house</note>. The six starting with *Dushchikya* <note>a term for the 3rd house</note> refer to the third house. The twelve starting with *Patala* <note>the underworld</note> refer to the fourth house. The six starting with *Dhi* <note>intellect</note> refer to the fifth house. The seven starting with *Disease* refer to the sixth house. The eight starting with *Jamitra* <note>the setting point</note> refer to the seventh house. The six starting with *Randhra* <note>the aperture</note> refer to the eighth house. The six starting with *Dharma* <note>duty/virtue</note> refer to the ninth house. The eight starting with *Business* refer to the tenth house. The five starting with *Eleventh* refer to the eleventh house. The four starting with *Rihpha* refer to the twelfth house. Thus say the sages. || 49-52 ||

**For the Body (1st House):** Form, Rise, First, Body, Birth, Ascendant, and *Hora*.
**For the Wealth (2nd House):** Speech, Wealth, Eloquence, Eyes, Own, and Family.
**For the Third:** *Dushchikya*, Valor, Sibling, Strength, Courage, and Ear.
**For the Fourth:** Underworld, Intellect, *Hibuka* <note>Greek: *hypogeion*</note>, Earth, Mother, Knowledge, Vehicle, Home, Happiness, Relative, and the Quadrant.
**For the Fifth:** Intellect, Divinity, King, Father <note>in some traditions</note>, Son, and the Fivefold.
**For the Sixth:** Disease, Missile, Weapon, Fear, Sixth, Enemy, and Wound.
**For the Seventh:** *Jamitra*, Desire, Journey, Wife, Prosperity, *Dyuna*, Sunset, and Seventh.
**For the Eighth:** Aperture, Longevity, Eighth, Battle, Death, and Destruction.
**For the Ninth:** Virtue, Teacher, Auspicious, Penance, Ninth, and Fortune.
**For the Tenth:** Business, Zenith, Knowledge, Royal, Seat, and Action.
**For the Eleventh:** Eleventh, Penultimate, Existence, Income, and Gain.
**For the Twelfth:** *Rihpha*, Expenditure, Twelfth, and Final. || 49-52 ||

## On the Designations of the Houses as Centers and Others

The Zenith, the Ascendant, the Wife, and the Underworld are known as the Centers <term>Kendra: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, considered the pillars of a chart</term>, Thorns, or the Fourfold. The ninth and fifth houses from the Ascendant are the Trines. The ninth is specifically called the "Great Trine" from the Ascendant. || 53 ||

The signs of the Body, Happiness, Desire, and Command <note>1st, 4th, 7th, 10th</note> are the Center designations. The *Panaphara* <term>Succedent: houses 2, 5, 8, and 11</term> houses are Wealth, Gain, Son, and the Eighth. The Expenditure, Enemy, Teacher, and *Dushchikya* <note>12th, 6th, 9th, 3rd</note> are the *Apoklima* <term>Cadent: houses 3, 6, 9, and 12</term>. The *Chaturasra* <note>square</note> refers to the eighth and fourth houses. || 54 ||

The leading teachers say the houses of *Dushchikya*, Gain, Enemy, and Command <note>3rd, 11th, 6th, 10th</note> are the *Upachaya* <term>Increasing: houses where planets grow in strength over time</term> houses. The remaining houses—the 9th, 2nd, 4th, 7th, 8th, 12th, and 1st—are known as the *Pidarksha* <note>afflicted signs</note>. These houses, if occupied or aspected by their own lords, or by the Moon, Mercury, Venus, or Jupiter, and not joined or aspected by others <note>malefics</note>, grant auspicious results at birth or at the time of inquiry. || 55 ||

Now, the specific designations of the houses such as Centers are explained: The Zenith, Ascendant, Wife, and Underworld = the 10th, 1st, 7th, and 4th houses; these are the Center, Thorn, and Fourfold designations. As stated in the *Saravali* <note>a famous 8th-century astrological text</note>:

> "The Ascendant, the 7th, the 10th, and the 4th are the Fourfold, the Thorn, and the Center names."

Here, the Trine: The 9th and 5th from the Ascendant are the Trine houses. By the word "Trine," the 9th and 5th are grasped. Regarding the "Great Trine": The wise say the 9th from the Ascendant is the Great Trine. As stated in the *Saravali*:

> "Of the Virtue <note>9th</note> and Son <note>5th</note> houses, the Trine of the Son is the Intellect <note>5th</note>, and that of Virtue <note>9th</note> is the Great Trine."

Again, the Center: The signs of Body, Happiness, Desire, and Command = 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses are the Center designations. The *Panaphara* houses: Wealth, Gain, Son, and Eighth = 2nd, 5th, 8th, and 11th houses...

# Chapter 1: The Nature of the Signs

The houses are designated as *Panaphara* <note>Succedent houses: 2nd, 5th, 8th, and 11th</note>. The houses of Loss, Enemies, Guru, and the "Third" (12th, 6th, 9th, and 3rd) are designated as *Apoklima* <note>Cadent houses</note>. As stated in the *Saravali*:
> "The houses following the Centers are called *Panaphara*, and those following them are called *Apoklima*."

The pair of Death and Kinship (the 8th and 4th houses) are known as *Chaturasra* <note>Literally "four-cornered" or square</note>. As stated by Varahamihira:
> "The fourth and eighth from the Ascendant are known as the *Chaturasra*."

Regarding *Upachaya* <note>Houses of increase or growth</note>: The leading teachers—the ancient sages—say that the 3rd, 11th, 6th, and 10th houses are the *Upachaya* houses. The remaining houses—the 9th, 2nd, 4th, 5th, 7th, 8th, 12th, and 1st—are known as *Pidarksha* <note>Afflicted or "pain-giving" signs in this specific context</note>.
As stated in the *Svalpa Jataka*: "The 3rd, 6th, 11th, and 10th are the *Upachaya* houses; those other than these are different."

Now, the auspicious or inauspicious results based on the status of the houses are described. If these previously mentioned houses are occupied by or aspected <note>The "gaze" or influence of a planet across the chart</note> by their own lords, or by Mercury, Venus, or Jupiter, and are not occupied or aspected by others, then they grant auspicious results to the native or the querent. As stated in the *Saravali*:
> "A sign is strong if it is aspected by or occupied by its own lord, or by Mercury or Jupiter, and not by others." (Verses 53-55)

The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses are named *Kendra* (Center), *Kantaka* (Thorn), and *Chatushtaya* (Quaternary). The 9th and 5th from the Ascendant are named *Trikona* (Trine). The 9th from the Ascendant is specifically called the *Tri-trikona*. (53)

The 2nd, 5th, 8th, and 11th houses are *Panaphara*. The 3rd, 6th, 9th, and 12th houses are named *Apoklima*. The 8th and 4th are *Chaturasra*. (54)

The four places—3rd, 11th, 6th, and 10th—are named *Upachaya*. The remaining 8 places (9, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 12, 1) are named *Pidarksha*. If these houses in a birth chart or a query chart are joined with or aspected by their own lords, or by Mercury, Venus, and Jupiter, and are not joined or aspected by other planets, they give auspicious results. (55)

## On the Rising Times of the Signs

> Twenty, twenty-four, twenty-eight, thirty-two, and thirty-six, then forty;
> These are the measures for Aries and the following signs in order, and for Libra and the following six in reverse. (56)

Now the rising times (ascensional periods) of the Ascendants are described. There, the measure for Aries is 20 units. For Taurus, 24 parts. For Gemini, 28 parts. For Cancer, 32 parts. For Leo, 36 parts. For Virgo, 40 parts. By reversing this sequence, the rising degrees for the six signs starting with Libra should be known.

The rising portions mentioned here pertain to a region with a 7.5-digit equinoctial shadow <note>A method of determining latitude in ancient Indian astronomy</note>. For the sake of direct calculation: the equinoctial shadow is 7.5 digits. The ascensional differences (*charadala*) are 75, 60, and 25. From these:
> "The rising times at the equator in *vighatikas* <note>units of time</note> are [specific constants]. When decreased or increased by the ascensional differences in direct and reverse order, they become the rising times for Aries and the rest."

Accordingly, the rising measures for a region with a 7.5-digit shadow are:

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Aries/Pisces | 278$^p$ - 75$^p$ = 203$^p$ | Due to small difference | 200$^p$ | Taken | Tenth-parts | 20$^\circ$ |
| Taurus/Aquarius | 299$^p$ - 60$^p$ = 239$^p$ | ,, | 240$^p$ | ,, | ,, | 24$^\circ$ |
| Gemini/Capricorn | 323$^p$ - 25$^p$ = 298$^p$ | ,, | 280$^p$ | ,, | ,, | 28$^\circ$ |

# With the Commentary on Jataka Parijata

Leo and Virgo = 219 <term>pala</term><note>A unit of time; 60 palas equal 1 ghatika (24 minutes).</note> + 60 <term>pala</term> = 349 <term>pala</term>. Here, due to a slight difference, 360 <term>pala</term> is taken; the degrees of the period are 36°.
Libra and Scorpio = 278 <term>pala</term> + 75 <term>pala</term> = 353 <term>pala</term>. Similarly, 400 <term>pala</term> is taken; the degrees are 40°.

To determine the rising time for one's own location, calculations should be made using the local equinoctial shadow according to the prescribed method. The rising portions of the signs mentioned here are fixed, intended only for determining the Ascendant and for understanding wealth and the physical limbs of the person. || 56 ||

The values for the six signs starting from Aries are 20, 24, 28, 31, 36, and 40 degrees respectively; for the six signs starting from Libra, these same values apply in reverse order. || 56 ||

->### Now, the Auspicious and Inauspicious Degrees of the Signs.<-

> *Tanu* (8), *Shara* (25), *Rarikharah* (22, 22), *Kiritino* (21), *Dhana* (4), *Guru* (23), *Hayanakha* (18, 20), *Nara* (20), *Nuka* (10).
> If these degrees of the Moon occur in Aries and the following signs, they indicate death in electional or birth astrology. || 57 ||
> *Putra* (21), *Vatu* (14), *Divyajanadhiko* (18, 8, 19), *Dhani* (9), *Viratyo* (24, 11), *Gotravayo* (23, 14), *Dhika* (19), *Dhuna* (9).
> In Aries and the following signs, these are known as *Pushkara* degrees, providing auspicious results in electional and birth astrology. || 58 ||

Now the author describes the inauspicious and auspicious degrees of the signs. In "electional or birth astrology" (*muhurta-janmadishu*), in the signs starting with Aries (*tumburadike*), if the Moon's degrees correspond to *Tanu* etc., they indicate death. For example, in Aries, *Tanu* equals 8 <note>The word 'Tanu' refers to the forms of Shiva, which are eight: Earth, Water, Air, Fire, the Sacrificer, Space, Moon, and Sun.</note>. Thus, the 8th lunar degree of Aries is inauspicious for a birth. In Taurus, *Shara* equals 25 <note>The numerical code used here follows the *Katapayadi* system, an ancient Indian mnemonic device where letters represent numbers.</note>. In Gemini, *Rari* is 22. In Cancer, *Khara* is 22. In Leo, *Kiri* is 21. In Virgo, *Tina* is 1. In Libra, *Dhana* is 4. In Scorpio, *Guru* is 23. In Sagittarius, *Haya* is 18. In Capricorn, *Nakha* is 20. In Aquarius, *Nara* is 20. In Pisces, *Nuka* is the 10th degree—these are inauspicious. It should be noted here: if the Moon is at the degree specified for the sign at the time of birth, the person's death may be predicted in the year corresponding to that number. As stated in the *Sarvartha Chintamani*:

> "The Moon in the 20th degree of Aquarius brings death; at 21 degrees in Leo; at 25 in Taurus.
> The Moon in the 8th of Aries; at 23 in Scorpio; at 22 in Cancer; at 4 in Libra.
> The Moon in the 20th of Capricorn; the 1st degree of Virgo; the 18th of Sagittarius; the 10th of Pisces.
> At 22 in Gemini, the Moon likewise grants death. Whichever lunar degrees are designated as 'death degrees,' the one born will undoubtedly face death in that many years."

Now for the auspicious degrees. In the signs starting with Aries, the degrees named *Putra* etc. are called *Pushkara* <note>Pushkara degrees are highly favorable points in the zodiac that nourish and strengthen the planets placed within them.</note> degrees; they provide auspicious results. Specifically: in Aries, *Putra* is the 21st degree. In Taurus, *Vatu* is 14. In Gemini, *Divya* is 18. In Cancer, *Jana* is 8. In Leo, *Adhika* is 19. In Virgo, *Dhani* is 9. In Libra, *Vira* is 24. In Scorpio, *Tyo* is 11. In Sagittarius, *Gotra* is 23. In Capricorn, *Vayah* is 14. In Aquarius, *Dhika* is 19. In Pisces, *Dhuna* is the 9th degree. If the Moon is at these degrees at birth, it is beneficial for the native. || 57-58 ||

## On the Habitations of the Signs starting with Aries.

Patala, Karnata, Chara, Chola, Vasundhara,

## On the Determination of the Slope of the Signs.

The direction belonging to the Lord of the sign is its slope; the fourth sign from the one occupied by the Sun is called Abhijit. In this Horashastra <note>The science of judicial astrology</note> titled Parijata, this chapter on the terminology and nature of the signs has been proclaimed. || 61 ||

->Thus, by the grace of the nine planets, in the Jatakaparijata composed by Vaidyanatha,<-
->ends the first chapter on the Nature of the Signs. || 1 ||<-

Now, while stating the slope <note>original: "plavatva," referring to the downward inclination or direction of power</note> of the planets, the author concludes the chapter. "The direction belonging to the Lord" means the direction associated with the presiding planet of that sign is the slope or low point of that sign. For example, the lord of Aries is Mars, whose direction is South; therefore, Aries is said to slope toward the South. This applies everywhere. Now for <term>Abhijit|A special 'victorious' point or intercalary lunar mansion used in specific calculations</term>: "The one named water from the Sun's position" means the fourth sign from the sign the Sun is currently transiting is called Abhijit. For example, if the Sun is in Aries, then Cancer is Abhijit.

Now, the conclusion of the chapter: In this <term>Horatantra|A system of astrology focused on birth charts and timing</term>, in the book named 'Parijata', the chapter on terminology regarding the nature of the signs has been described by me, the author. || 61 ||

The Sudha commentary on the Parijata, which delights Kapileshwara, is completed in this first chapter on the Nature of the Signs. || 1 ||

All signs slope (are inclined) toward the direction of their respective lords, and the fourth sign from whichever sign the Sun occupies is designated as Abhijit. In the book named Parijata of the Horashastra, the first chapter on terminology called "Nature of the Signs" is finished. <insert>Note by the author of Sudha-Jnana</insert> || 61 ||

->Thus ends the 'Vimala' Hindi commentary on the first chapter titled Nature of the Signs<-
->in the Jatakaparijata composed by Shri Vaidyanatha. || 1 ||<-

# Chapter 2: On the Names, Natures, and Qualities of the Planets

### First, the determination of the Sun and others as the Soul of Time, etc.

> The Sun is the Soul of Time, the Moon is the Mind, Mars is Strength, and the Son of the Moon (Mercury) is Speech.
> The Teacher of the Gods (Jupiter) is the essence of Happiness and Knowledge, Venus is Desire, and the Son of the Sun (Saturn) is Sorrow itself. || 1 ||

Now, the assignment of authority to the Sun and other planets within the "Body of Time" is described—"The Sun is the Soul," etc. The Illuminator <note>original: "Bhaskara"</note> = the Sun, is the Soul of the Time-Personified <note>The "Kalapurusha" is a concept where Time is envisioned as a cosmic human body, with different zodiac signs and planets ruling specific parts or functions.</note>. The Moon <note>original: "Indu"</note> is the Mind or the inner faculty. Mars <note>original: "Bhauma"</note> is Strength or power. The Son of the Moon = Mercury <note>original: "Budha"</note> is Speech. The Teacher of the Gods = Jupiter <note>original: "Guru"</note>, is the essence of Happiness and Knowledge. Venus is Desire or passion. The Son of the Sun = Saturn <note>original: "Shani"</note> is Sorrow. The practical application is this: at the time of birth, whichever planet is strong, the corresponding faculty of the person will be powerful; if weak, that faculty will be weak. As stated in the *Svalpa Jataka*:

> "The Soul and other faculties are known to be very strong when the sky-goers (planets) are strong. When they are weak, the faculties are weak; the opposite is traditionally held for Saturn." <note>Saturn's strength often indicates a capacity to endure or a heavy burden of the "sorrow" faculty.</note>

The division of the limbs of the Time-Personified is as follows: the Sun is the Soul, the Moon is the Mind, Mars is Valor, Mercury is Speech, Jupiter is the essence of Happiness and Science, Venus is Desire, and Saturn is Sorrow. One should know that at the time of birth, the limb of a strong planet is robust, and that of a weak planet is frail. || 1 ||

---

### On the determination of the Sun and others as Kings, etc.

> The Lord of the Day (Sun) and the Moon are Kings; Jupiter and Venus are Ministers.
> Mercury is the Prince, Mars is the Leader (General), and the Son of the Sun (Saturn) is the Servant. || 2 ||

The meaning is clear. The application: at the time of a person's birth, whichever planet is strongest makes the native <note>The person whose birth chart is being read.</note> conform to its own nature. As stated in the *Saravali*:

> "At the time of birth, strong planets bestow their own inherent nature upon men." || 2 ||

The Sun and Moon are Kings, Jupiter and Venus are Ministers, Mercury is the Prince, Mars is the Leader, and Saturn is the Messenger/Servant. || 2 ||

---

### On the alternative names of the Sun and others.

> Heli, Surya, Tapana, Dinakrit, Bhanu, Pusha, Aruna, and Arka (are names of the Sun).
> Soma, Shitadyuti, Udupati, Glau, Mriganka, Indu, and Chandra (are names of the Moon). ||
> Ara, Vakra, Kshitija, Rudhira, Angaraka, and Kruranetra (are names of Mars).
> Saumya, Taranayana, Budha, Vidvat, Bodhana, and Ashvenduputra (are names of Mercury). || 3 ||
> Mantri, Vachaspati, Guru, Suracharya, Devedya, and Jiva (are names of Jupiter).
> Shukra, Kavya, Sita, Bhrigusuta, Ahla, Asphujit, and Hanavedya (are names of Venus).
> Chhayaputra, Taranitanaya, Kona, Shanti, Arki, and Manda (are names of Saturn).
> Rahu, Sarpa, Asura, Phani, Tamas, Saimhikeya, and Agu (are names of Rahu). || 4 ||

Those who know the science call the Banner <note>original: "Dhvaja"</note>, the Crested One <note>original: "Shikhi"</note>, and Ketu by these famous names. Gulika and Mandi (are names for the secondary planet Gulika). || 4½ ||

Now the alternative names of the planets are stated. The eight names starting with *Heli* belong to the Sun. The seven names starting with *Soma* belong to the Moon. The six names starting with *Ara* belong to Mars. The six names starting with *Saumya* belong to Mercury. The six names starting with *Mantri* belong to Jupiter. The seven names starting with *Shukra* belong to Venus. The six names starting with *Chhayaputra* belong to Saturn. The seven names starting with *Rahu* belong to Rahu. The three names starting with *Dhvaja* belong to Ketu. Those who know—meaning the experts in the science of astrology—say that *Gulika* and *Mandi* are the two names for Gulika. || 3-4½ ||

The names for the Sun are: Heli, Surya, Tapana, Dinakrit, Bhanu, Pusha, Aruna, and Arka. For the Moon: Soma, Shitadyuti, Udupati, Glau, Mriganka, Indu, and Chandra. For Mars: Ara, Vakra...

# Chapter 2: On the Names, Nature, and Qualities of the Planets

...[The names of Mars are] <term>Kshitija</term> <note>born of the earth</note>, <term>Rudhira</term> <note>blood-red</note>, <term>Angaraka</term> <note>burning charcoal</note>, and <term>Krunetra</term> <note>cruel-eyed</note>. The names of Mercury are—<term>Saumya</term>, <term>Taratanaya</term> <note>son of Tara</note>, <term>Budha</term>, <term>Vid</term>, <term>Bodhana</term>, and <term>Induputra</term> <note>son of the Moon</note>. The names of Jupiter are—<term>Mantri</term> <note>the minister</note>, <term>Vachaspati</term> <note>Lord of Speech</note>, <term>Guru</term> <note>the heavy/teacher</note>, <term>Suracharya</term> <note>teacher of the gods</note>, <term>Devejya</term>, and <term>Jiva</term>. The names of Saturn are—<term>Chhayasuta</term> <note>son of Chhaya/Shadow</note>, <term>Taranitanaya</term> <note>son of the Sun</note>, <term>Kona</term>, <term>Shani</term>, <term>Arki</term>, and <term>Manda</term> <note>the slow one</note>. The names of Rahu <note>the North Node</note> are—<term>Sarpa</term> <note>serpent</note>, <term>Asura</term>, <term>Phani</term>, <term>Tama</term> <note>darkness</note>, <term>Saimhikeya</term>, and <term>Agu</term>. All these names are well-known, as stated by the learned scholars. || 3-4½ ||

### Now, the Secondary Planets (Upagrahas) of the Sun and others.

> The secondary planets are portions of the planets beginning with the Sun; <term>Kala</term> and the others are known to bestow difficult or ill results. || 5 ||
> Respectively, they are named <term>Kala</term>, <term>Paridhi</term>, <term>Dhuma</term>, <term>Ardha-prahara</term>, <term>Yamakantaka</term>, <term>Kodanda</term>, <term>Mandi</term>, <term>Pata</term>, and <term>Upaketu</term>. || 6 ||

Now the names of the <term>Upagrahas</term> <note>secondary or "shadow" planets</note> are being stated. What are these secondary planets? They are portions of the planets starting with the Sun, such as <term>Kala</term>. Here, this should be noted—every day and every night, there are portions belonging to all the planets. These nine, starting with <term>Kala</term>, are called the secondary planets. They are givers of difficult results <note>malefic influence</note>. The names of these secondary planets are: for the Sun, it is <term>Kala</term>; for the Moon, <term>Paridhi</term> (also called <term>Parivesha</term>); for Mars, <term>Dhuma</term>; for Mercury, <term>Ardha-prahara</term>; for Jupiter, <term>Yamaghantaka</term>; for Venus, <term>Kodanda</term>; for Saturn, <term>Mandi</term> (also called <term>Gulika</term>); for Rahu, <term>Pata</term>; and for Ketu, <term>Upaketu</term>. To understand the calculation of these secondary planets, one should consult the second chapter of the first half of the *Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra* <note>a foundational text of Vedic astrology</note>. || 5-6 ||

| Sat | Gulika | Kala | Paridhi | Dhuma | Ardha-yama | Yamaghanta | Kodanda | ,, |

The method for knowing the two cycles of day and night (the night cycle is to be seen on page 32)—

> Having divided the day into eight parts, one should count sequentially from the lord of the day. The eighth part is "Lordless," and the portion of Saturn is known as <term>Gulika</term>.
> The night is also divided into eight parts, counting from the fifth lord from the day-lord. The eighth segment is declared as the "Exit" <note>non-productive</note>.
> In the portion of Saturn, <term>Gulika</term> is spoken of; in the portion of Jupiter, <term>Yamaghantaka</term>; in the portion of Mars, <term>Mrityu</term> is ordained; in the portion of the Sun, it is named <term>Kala</term>.
> In the portion of Mercury, it is <term>Ardha-prahara</term>, which indicates the place of clear actions.

The portions of the planets like the Sun are the secondary planets such as <term>Kala</term>, which give difficult results. <term>Kala</term>, <term>Paridhi</term>, <term>Dhuma</term>, <term>Ardha-prahara</term>, <term>Yamaghanta</term>, <term>Kodanda</term>, <term>Mandi</term>, <term>Pata</term>, and <term>Upaketu</term> are the names of the secondary planets of the Sun and others in sequence. || 5-6 ||

### On the Physical Appearance of the Sun and Other Planets

> The Sun possesses a dark-red luster; the Moon is white-bodied and youthful;
> The son of the Moon (Mercury) has the glow of green Durva grass; Mars is a mixture of blood-red and pale-white.
> The Minister (Jupiter) has a golden-yellow body; Venus is white-bodied; Saturn is dark-bodied;
> The Lord of Serpents (Rahu) has a bluish form; and Ketu possesses a variegated or multi-colored luster. || 7 ||

Now, the body colors of the Sun and others are described. **The Sun** = <note>original: "Bhanu"</note> has a dark-red luster = | a body with a luster mixed of <unclear>copper</unclear> and red, like the Hibiscus flower. **The Moon** is white-bodied = white in color like milk, | and youthful = in the stage of youth. **The Son of the Moon** = Mercury, has the glow of green Durva grass = a dark green color like the grass. | **The Son of the Earth** = Mars, is a mixture of red and pale-white = a mixed color like coral. **The Minister** = Jupiter, is golden-bodied = | a fair or yellow body. **Venus** is white-bodied = a white body. **Saturn** is dark-bodied = black in color. **The Lord of Serpents** = Rahu, has a bluish form = an intensely blue color. **Ketu** has a variegated luster = a body mixed with many colors.
The application of this is—at the time of birth for a person, or at the time of a query for a desired object, the planet that is strongest at that moment imparts a complexion similar to its own color. || 7 ||

<note>The following section is a Hindi translation of the above Sanskrit commentary provided in the original manuscript.</note>
The Sun is a mixture of dark and red. The Moon is a white-colored youth. Mercury is green like Durva grass. A color mixed of red and white belongs to Mars. Jupiter has a fair/golden body. Venus has a white body. Saturn has a black body. Rahu has a blue-colored body and Ketu is multi-colored. || 7 ||

### On Determining the Benefic and Malefic Nature of Planets

> The Moon and the Sun are the "Luminaries"; the five starting with the Son of the Earth (Mars) are the "Star-Planets."
> The sons of Shikhi and Simhika (Ketu and Rahu) are of the nature of darkness. The benefics are the Moon, Mercury, the Teacher of the Immortals (Jupiter), and the descendant of Bhrigu (Venus). || 8 ||
> The waning Moon, Saturn, the Sun, Rahu, Ketu, and the Son of the Earth (Mars) are malefics; Mercury associated with a malefic is also a malefic.
> Among these, Jupiter and the Teacher of the Daityas (Venus) are the bestowers of great auspiciousness; the Son of the Sun (Saturn) and the Son of the Earth (Mars) are cruel. || 9 ||
> During the first ten days of the lunar month, the Moon possesses medium strength; in the second ten days, it bestows great auspiciousness.
> In the third ten days, the Moon is devoid of strength, but if it is joined with or aspected by benefics, it may become auspicious. || 10 ||

## Chapter on the Names, Natures, Qualities, and Classifications of the Planets || 2 ||

Now the auspicious and inauspicious natures of the planets are described as "The Illuminators." The Moon and the Sun are the Illuminators <note>original: "Shitakara-Prabhakarau"</note> (meaning they possess significantly more light than all the stars). The five beginning with the Son of Earth—Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, and Saturn—are "star-planets" <term>Taragrahas (planets that appear like stars)</term> and do not possess light of their own. As stated in the *Tattvaviveka*:
> "The Sun is a sphere of light; the planets and stars are spheres of water and earth. 
> They appear luminous only when illuminated by the rays of the Sun."

The "Son of the Lioness" and the "Crested One"—Rahu and Ketu—are of the nature of darkness <note>original: "Tamah-svarupau"</note>, meaning they are composed of shadow-like darkness. The Moon, Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus are auspicious (benefic planets). The waning Moon, Saturn, the Sun, Rahu, Ketu, and Mars are "sinful" (malefic planets). Mercury, when joined with a malefic planet, also becomes a malefic. As Varahamihira stated: "The waning Moon, the Sun, Mars, and Saturn are malefics; Mercury is so when joined with them."

Now, among those mentioned as auspicious and inauspicious, the degree of their effect is described. Among the stated planets, Jupiter and Venus <note>original: "Guru-Danavejyau"</note> are the most auspicious. The Son of the Sun (Saturn) and the Son of the Earth (Mars) are the most cruel and inauspicious. Regarding the Moon, its auspiciousness is determined by time. During the first ten nights of the bright fortnight <note>the waxing phase</note>, the Moon has moderate strength. During the second ten-day period (from the 11th of the bright fortnight to the 5th of the dark fortnight), the Moon is highly auspicious and very strong. In the third ten-day period (from the 5th of the dark fortnight to the New Moon), the Moon is devoid of strength and is inauspicious. However, if the Moon—even if inauspicious—is joined with or aspected by <term>benefic aspects (sight from good planets)</term>, then it becomes favorable and gives good results. || 8-10 ||

The Moon and Sun provide light. The five starting with Mars are star-planets. Ketu and Rahu are of the nature of darkness. The Moon, Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus are benefic planets. The waning Moon, Saturn, the Sun, Rahu, Ketu, and Mars are malefic planets. Mercury joined with a malefic is also a malefic. Among these, Jupiter and Venus are especially auspicious. Saturn and Mars are cruel.

From the first day of the bright fortnight for ten days, the Moon has medium strength. Then for ten days it is fully strong, and in the third ten-day period, it is powerless. However, if it is aspected by or joined with <insert>benefic planets</insert>, it becomes auspicious. || 10 ||

---

### On the Manner of Rising for the Sun and Others

> The Sun, Mars, Rahu, and Saturn always rise by the rear.
> Venus, the Moon, and Mercury rise by the head; Jupiter rises both ways. || 11 ||

Now the details of the planets' rising are given. The Sun, Mars, Rahu, and Saturn always rise by the rear <note>original: "Prishthenodyanti"</note>. The meaning is that they stand facing East. Venus, the Moon, and Mercury rise by the head <note>original: "Shirasa"</note>. Their heads appear first on the rising horizon. Jupiter <note>original: "Jiva"</note> rises both ways—by the rear and by the head. || 11 ||

The Sun, Mars, Rahu, and Saturn always rise from the back. Venus, the Moon, and Mercury rise from the head. Jupiter rises in both ways, from the back and the head. || 11 ||

Now the specific forms of the planets are described. The Sun and Mercury <note>original: "Divakarajnau"</note> have the nature of birds. The Moon <note>original: "Shashanka"</note> has a reptile-like form (including insects). Jupiter and Venus are bipeds (two-footed)—

### Now, the habitats (places of travel) of the Sun and others.

->The Moon and the teacher of the enemies of the gods <note>Venus</note> dwell in water; Jupiter and Mercury move in the houses of the wise and in villages.<-
->Mars, Rahu, Saturn, Ketu, and the Lord of the Day <note>the Sun</note> are those who wander in mountains and forests. || 13 ||<-

Now the transit locations of the planets are stated. <term>The Moon and the teacher of the enemies of the gods</term> = the Moon and Venus, <term>dwell in water</term> = they are water-dwellers. <term>Jupiter and Mercury</term> = Jupiter and Mercury, <term>move in the houses of the wise and in villages</term> = <gloss>of Jupiter and Mercury</gloss> = the houses of learned men; they move in those. Mercury moves in the village = the habitation of common people. Both are considered "civilized" or village-dwellers. <term>Mars, Rahu, Saturn, Ketu, and the Lord of the Day</term> = Mars, Rahu, Saturn, Ketu, and the Sun, <term>wander in mountains and forests</term> = mountains and woods; they have the nature of wandering and sporting in those places. The application is this: in matters of birth or divination <note>Prashna</note>, the strongest planet determines the environment of the event. || 13 ||

The Moon and Venus are water-dwellers. Jupiter and Mercury stay in the homes of scholars and are village-dwellers. Mars, Rahu, Saturn, Ketu, and the Sun are dwellers in mountains and forests. || 13 ||

### Now, the determination of the ages of the Sun and others, from childhood onwards.

->Mars is a child; Mercury is a youth; Jupiter is thirty years old; Venus is a sixteen-year-old.<-
->The Sun is fifty; the Moon is seventy years; Saturn, Rahu, and Ketu are a hundred years in number. || 14 ||<-

This is clear. The application: in matters of theft or loss, one can know the age of the thief and others. || 14 ||

Mars is a child. Mercury is a youth. Jupiter is 30 years old. Venus is 16 years old. The Sun is 50 years old. The Moon is 70 years old. Saturn, Rahu, and Ketu are 100 years old. || 14 ||

### Now, the determination of the lordship of the branches <note>the Vedas</note> and the designations of Mineral, Vegetable, and Animal.

->The lords of the branches are Jupiter, Venus, Mars, and Mercury; the planets representing minerals are Mars and the Sun.<-
->The Moon and the son of the Sun <note>Saturn</note> are primarily vegetable; Venus and Jupiter are animal; Mercury is mixed. || 15 ||<-

Now, after determining the lords of the branches, the designations of the planets such as "mineral" are stated. <term>Jupiter, Venus, Mars, and Mercury</term> = Jupiter, Venus, Mars, and Mercury, are the lords of the branches. Among them, Jupiter is the lord of the Rig Veda, Venus is the lord of the Yajur Veda, Mars is the lord of the Sama Veda, and Mercury is the lord of the Atharva Veda. As said by Ramacharya—

> "The lords of the branches are Jupiter, Venus, Mars, and Mercury."

The application—

> "The movement, body, and strength of the lord of the branch is highly auspicious."

**Now the designations of Mineral, Vegetable, and Animal.** <term>Mars and the Sun</term> = Mars and the Sun, <term>planets representing minerals</term> = those two are planets designated as "Dhatu" <note>minerals/metals</note>. <term>The Moon and the son of the Sun are primarily vegetable</term> = the Moon and Saturn are "Mula" <note>roots/vegetable kingdom</note>. <term>Venus and Jupiter</term> = Venus and Jupiter, are <term>animal</term> = they are planets that are "Jiva" <note>living beings/animals/humans</note>. <term>The son of the Moon</term> = Mercury, is <term>mixed</term> = he is a combination of mineral, vegetable, and animal; meaning he represents all three in the three parts of his influence respectively. Here are the designations according to Parashara—

> "Rahu, Mars, Saturn, and the Moon are known as mineral planets.
> The Sun and Venus are vegetable planets; the others are designated as animal."

Regarding minerals <insert>(1)</insert>, the specific details of each should be known from the planetary world of gold and so on. || 15 ||

## On the States of the Planets

> Radiant, Joyful, Stable, Peaceful, Powerful, Oppressed,

This is clear. || 16 ||
1. Radiant <note>Dipta</note>, 2. Joyful <note>Mudita</note>, 3. Stable <note>Svastha</note>, 4. Peaceful <note>Shanta</note>, 5. Powerful <note>Shakta</note>, 6. Oppressed <note>Prapidita</note>, 7. ## On Specific States based on Position

> A planet in its sign of exaltation or trine is **Radiant**; in its own house, it is **Stable**; in a friend's house, it is **Joyful**.
> One in the division of a benefic planet is **Peaceful**; one extremely pure with distinct rays of light is **Powerful**. || 17 ||
> One defeated by other planets is **Oppressed**; one in the sign or division of an enemy is **Pitiful**.
> One in the division of a malefic planet is **Wicked**; one in its sign of debilitation is **Terrified**; and one that has set <note>combust with the Sun</note> is **Impaired**. || 18 ||

Regarding "defeated by other planets": A planet defeated in planetary war <note>graha-yuddha</note> by others becomes "Oppressed." Now, what is meant by "planetary war" and how is one defeated? The conjunction of Mars and other planets is called planetary war. As it is said:

> "The meeting of planets with the Sun is called 'setting' <note>astamaya/combustion</note>; the meeting of planets with the Moon is called 'conjunction' <note>samagama</note>. The war of Mars and the others is said to occur when they are joined with one another."

The signs of a planet defeated in planetary war are:

> "One situated in the southern direction, trembling, retreating without reaching its goal, minute in size, mounted upon, distorted, lusterless, and discolored—that one is defeated."

Everything else is clear. || 17-18 ||
A planet in its exaltation or trine <note>trikona</note> is **Radiant**. In its own house, it is **Stable**; in a friend's house, **Joyful**; in the division of a benefic, **Peaceful**; one extremely pure with distinct rays of light is **Powerful**; one defeated by other planets is **Oppressed**; in an enemy's sign or ninth-division <note>navamsha</note>, it is **Pitiful**; in the division of a malefic, **Wicked**; in debilitation, **Terrified**; and a planet that has set is **Impaired**. || 17-18 ||

The Sun and other planets have the colors **copper, white, deep red, green, yellow, variegated**, and **black**. These are mentioned for the purpose of gaining knowledge about lost property and such. || 19 ||

### From the Annotated Jataka Parijata

<term>Mani</term> <note>gem or precious object</note>. For the Sun, copper; for the Moon, a gem; for Mars, gold; for Mercury, <term>shukti</term> <note>original: "शुक्तिः", literally pearl-oyster, but here glossed as a mixed metal like bell-metal or brass</note>; for Jupiter, silver; for Venus, pearls; and for Saturn, iron. 

**The Purpose:** In matters of birth or divination <note>Prashna</note>, one identifies the acquisition of materials based on the strongest planet. During a planet's auspicious period <note>Dasha</note>, one obtains its respective material; if a planet is causing affliction, one should donate that material.

**Now, the Presiding Deities:** Starting from the Sun, the presiding deities are Fire, Water, the Six-Faced One, Vishnu, Indra, Shachi, and Brahma. 
Specifically: 
*   For the Sun: Fire <note>Agni</note>. 
*   For the Moon: Water <note>Varuna</note>. 
*   For Mars: The Six-Faced One <note>Kartikeya, the god of war</note>. 
*   For Mercury: Hari <note>Vishnu</note>. 
*   For Jupiter: Indra, King of the Gods. 
*   For Venus: Shachi <note>Indra's wife</note>. 
*   For Saturn: Virinchi <note>Brahma, the Creator</note>.

**The Purpose:** To please a planet, its presiding deity should be worshipped. Before a journey, one should worship the deity of the planet ruling that direction and then depart. || 20 ||

### Now, the Gemstones of the Sun and others.

This is what all the ancient Sages say. **The Purpose:** To determine the clothing of a newborn or in divination based on the strongest planet.

### Now, the Directions.

In order starting from the East: Sun, Venus, Mars, Rahu, Saturn, Moon, Mercury, and Jupiter. This means these eight planets are the lords of the eight directions (cardinal and intermediate).

### Now, the Seasons.

Venus, Mars, Moon, Mercury, Jupiter, and Saturn are the lords of the seasons starting with Spring, determined by the <term>Drekkana</term> <note>a 10-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign</note>. Here, the knowledge of seasons is gained through the Decanate:
*   If Venus is in the Decanate of the Ascendant: **Spring**.
*   If Mars is in the Decanate: **Summer**.
*   If the Moon is in the Decanate: **Rainy Season**.
*   If Mercury is in the Decanate: **Autumn**.
*   If Jupiter is in the Decanate: **Early Winter**.
*   If Saturn is in the Decanate: **Late Winter**.

Alternatively, the seasons starting with Spring are told by the planets Venus etc., based on the Ascendant. If there is no planet in the Ascendant...

Even when many planets are present, the determination of the season <note>Ritu</note> should be stated according to the Decans <term>Drekkana: a 10-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign</term> of Venus and the others. The purpose of this is to determine the season of birth in cases of "Lost Horoscopy" <note>Nashta-Jataka: the art of reconstructing a birth chart when the birth time is unknown</note>.

## Regarding Places of Residence
The dwellings of the planets, starting with the Sun, are the abodes of the gods and so forth. Among them, the Sun’s place is the temple <note>original: "devasthanam"</note>. The Moon’s is the water’s edge or the bank of a reservoir. Mars’s is the place of fire <note>such as a kitchen or forge</note>. Mercury’s is a place of recreation or play. Jupiter’s is the treasury or storehouse. Venus’s is the bedroom. Saturn’s is a place of refuse or barren wasteland. Rahu and Ketu <note>the North and South Nodes of the Moon</note> dwell in the corners of the house; specifically, Rahu dwells in the house itself and Ketu in the corners. The purpose of this knowledge is to understand the nature of the birth-room or to locate stolen or lost property based on the strongest planet. || 22–24 ||

> The sages have said that the Sun’s garment is coarse, the Moon’s is new and beautiful, Mars’s is singed by fire, Mercury’s is water-damaged, Jupiter’s is of medium quality, Venus’s is durable, and Saturn’s is old. || 22 ||

The Sun, Venus, Mars, Rahu, Saturn, the Moon, Mercury, and Jupiter reside in and are the lords of the directions starting from the East, respectively.

Venus, Mars, the Moon, Mercury, Jupiter, and Saturn are the lords of the seasons starting with Spring <note>Vasanta</note>. The season should be identified by the Decan of Venus or other planets rising in the Ascendant. || 23 ||

The Sun’s residence is a temple, the Moon’s a reservoir, Mars’s a fire-shed, Mercury’s a playground, Jupiter’s a treasury, Venus’s a bedroom, Saturn’s a wasteland, and Rahu and Ketu reside in the house and its corners. || 24 ||

## Regarding the Geographical Divisions of the Sun and Others

> Mars rules from Lanka to the Krishna River; then Venus rules the land up to the Gautami <note>Godavari</note> River.
> Jupiter rules up to the Vindhya mountains; Mercury up to the River of the Gods <note>Ganges</note>; and Saturn rules up to the Snowy Mountains <note>the Himalayas</note>. || 25 ||

Now the regions of the planets are described. Mars <note>original: "Arah"</note> is to be known as ruling from Lanka to the Krishna River. This is the extent of Mars's region. From the Krishna River to the land ending at the Gautami River belongs to Venus. From there to the Vindhya range belongs to Jupiter <note>original: "Aryah"</note>. From there to the River of the Gods (Ganges) belongs to Mercury. From there to the Snowy Mountains (Himalayas) belongs to Saturn. Here, the regions of the Sun and Moon should be understood as previously mentioned in the verse "temple and water's edge." The Sun’s divine land is Mount Meru, and the Moon’s water edges are the great oceans. || 25 ||

The region of Mars extends from Lanka to the Krishna River. From the Krishna to the Gautami River is Venus’s; from the Gautami to the Vindhya mountains is Jupiter’s; from the Vindhyas to the Ganges is Mercury’s; and from the Ganges to the Himalayas is Saturn’s region. The regions for the Sun and Moon are not explicitly stated here, but according to the previous verse, the Sun’s should be the land of the gods (Meru) and the Moon’s should be the water (ocean). (Note by the commentator Su. Sha.) || 25 ||

## Regarding the Castes and Qualities of the Planets

> Jupiter and Venus are Brahmins; the Sun and Mars are Kings <note>Kshatriyas</note>; the Moon is the ruler of the Merchants <note>Vaishyas</note>;
> The son of the Moon (Mercury) is the lord of the Laborers <note>Shudras</note>; and Saturn is the lord of the outcasts.
> The Sun, Jupiter, and the Moon are planets of the quality of Purity <note>Sattva</note>;
> Venus and Mercury possess the quality of Passion <note>Rajas</note>; Saturn and the son of Earth (Mars) are masters of Ignorance <note>Tamas</note>. || 26 ||

Now the planets' lordship over the castes <note>Varnas</note> and the three fundamental qualities <term>Gunas: the three threads of nature—Sattva (purity), Rajas (activity), and Tamas (inertia)</term> are described. Jupiter and Venus are the lords of the Brahmin caste. The Sun and Mars are the lords of the Kings/Warriors. The Moon is the lord of the Merchant caste. Mercury is the lord of the Laborer caste. Saturn is the lord of the lowest or "last-born" classes. The purpose: when a planet is afflicted, its corresponding caste is afflicted; also, in matters of theft, one can identify the caste of the thief from the strength of the planets.

### Now, the Qualities (Gunas).

The Sun, Jupiter, and the Moon <note>original: "Aditya-Mantri-Shitakirana"</note> are the planets dominated by **Sattva** (1) <note>The quality of purity, goodness, and harmony</note>. In the Sun, Jupiter, and the Moon, the Sattva quality is most abundant. Venus and Mercury <note>original: "Shukra-Jna"</note> possess **Rajas** <note>The quality of passion, activity, and self-interest</note>. Saturn and Mars <note>original: "Shani-Dharaputra"</note> are the lords of **Tamas** <note>The quality of darkness, inertia, and ignorance</note>. 

Here, some may have a doubt: in the first verse of this chapter, it was said that "Mars is Sattva," so why is it said here that Saturn and Mars are lords of Tamas? Truly, that was said there with the understanding that "Sattva" meant "courage" <note>In a martial context, Sattva refers to the strength of spirit or bravery</note>. That type of spirit exists in all who are engaged in cause and effect. However, here "Sattva" refers to the *Guna* (inherent quality). That resides only in the Great-Souled ones. As it is said:

> "One who is **Sattvic** possesses compassion, steadiness, truthfulness, honesty, and devotion to gods and Brahmins.
> One of **Rajas** quality has a mind attached to desire, arts, and action, and is a very brave man.
> One of **Tamas** quality is a deceiver of others, foolish, lazy, prone to anger, and sleeps excessively." || 26 ||

Jupiter and Venus are Brahmins <note>The priestly/intellectual class</note>. The Sun and Mars are Kshatriyas <note>The warrior/ruling class</note>. The Moon is the lord of the Vaishyas <note>The merchant/landowner class</note>. Mercury is the lord of the Shudras <note>The service class</note>, and Saturn is the lord of the outcastes <note>original: "Antyajas"</note>.
The Sun, Jupiter, and the Moon are Sattvic. Venus and Mercury are Rajasic. Saturn and Mars are Tamasic. || 26 ||

Now the description of the planets as male, etc., and the description of their lordship over the five Great Elements <note>Mahabhutas</note> is given. The Sun, Mars, and Jupiter are male planets. Venus and the Moon are female planets. Saturn and Mercury are planets of the "sixth nature" <note>neuter/eunuch</note>. **The Application:** At the time of birth or at the time of a query <note>Prashna</note>, the strongest planet favors its own side (gender).

### Now, the Lords of the Great Elements.

Jupiter, Mercury, Mars, Saturn, and Venus are the lords of Ether, Earth, Fire, Air, and Water. Specifically: Jupiter <note>Suracharya</note> is the lord of **Ether** (Space). Mercury <note>Jna</note> is the lord of **Earth**. Mars <note>Ara</note> is the lord of **Fire**. Saturn <note>the son of the Sun</note> is the lord of **Air**. Venus <note>the minister of the enemies of the gods</note> is the lord of **Water**. Regarding the Moon, it was previously mentioned in the 20th verse as being "full of much water." **The Application:** During their respective major periods <note>Dashas</note>, the planets manifest the shadow/influence of their Great Element. || 27 ||

The Sun, Mars, and Jupiter are male planets. Venus and the Moon are female planets. Saturn and Mercury are neuter. Jupiter is the lord of the Ether element, Mercury of Earth, Mars of Fire, Saturn of Air, and Venus of the Water element. || 27 ||

<header>Chapter 2: On the Forms, Qualities, and Distinctions of the Planets</header>

## Chapter 2: On the Forms, Qualities, and Distinctions of the Planets

In order from the furthest—**following the sequence of Saturn and the others**—the Son of Shadow (Saturn), Jupiter, the Earth-born (Mars), the Day-maker (Sun), Venus, the Son of the Moon (Mercury), and the Moon; these are **situated within the wheel of light** = the stars, in the wheel of signs = the Zodiac, they are **situated** = joined together. All planets wander within their own respective zodiacal circles (<term>orbit</term> <note>original: kakṣā</note>). Among them, Saturn is at the very top; below him is Jupiter; below him is Mars; then the Sun; then Venus; then Mercury; and then the Moon. Thus it was said by **the venerable teacher Bhāskara—**

> "The sphere of the Earth is surrounded by the orbits of the Moon, Mercury, Venus, the Sun, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, and the Stars." <note>original: "bhūmeḥ piṇḍaḥ śaśāṅkajñakaviravijyārkinakṣatrakakṣā"</note>

Here, this point is most worthy of attention: the one situated at the very top has the slowest motion. The one situated at the very bottom has the greatest motion. Since all orbits consist of the same number of minutes of arc (21,600'), and the speed of all planets in terms of leagues (<term>yojana</term> <note>A traditional Indian unit of distance, roughly 8-9 miles</note>) is actually equal—

> "The planets travel 1,185,845 leagues daily in their own paths," as stated by Bhāskara.

Therefore, in a large orbit, that distance in leagues results in a small number of minutes; in a small orbit, that same distance in leagues results in many minutes. Because of this, Saturn has the slowest motion in the largest orbit, and the Moon has the fastest motion in the smallest orbit; this is clear to those who understand motion, so there is no need for further elaboration. It was said by the honorable **Bhāskara—**

> "All the orbits of the gods in the sky are marked with the minutes of the circle; in a small circle, the minutes are small, and in a large one, they are large. Therefore, these planets—the Moon, Mercury, Venus, the Sun, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn—appear to move slower and slower as they go further out from the Moon." <note>original: verses 27-30</note>
