### Regarding the Bodily Elements and Tastes of the Sun and Others.

The lords of the marrow, nerves, fat, bones, semen, blood, and skin elements are said to be, in order: Mars, Saturn, Jupiter, the Sun, Venus, the Moon, and the son of the Stars <note>Mercury</note>. || 28 ||
The lords of the salty, pungent, astringent, sweet, bitter, sour, and mixed tastes are the Moon, Sun, Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, the preceptor of the demons <note>Venus</note>, and the Knower <note>Mercury</note>. The lords of the half-year, day, fortnight, season, year, month, and moment are the Sun, Mars, Venus, Mercury, Saturn, Jupiter, and the Moon. || 29 ||

Now the bodily elements, tastes, and time-units of the planets are described. Mars, Saturn, Jupiter, the Sun, Venus, the Moon, and Mercury are stated to be the lords of the marrow and other elements in sequence. For example: Mars is the lord of the marrow. Saturn <note>original: *Arki*, son of the Sun</note> is of the nerves. Jupiter <note>original: *Ijya*, the worshipful</note> is of the fat. The Sun <note>original: *Dinesha*, lord of the day</note> is of the bones. Venus is of the semen. The Moon <note>original: *Shashabhrit*, the rabbit-bearer</note> is of the blood. Mercury <note>original: *Tarasuta*, son of Tara</note> is the lord or presiding deity of the skin. **The application:** The planet which is strongest at birth determines the dominant bodily element <term>Dhatu: the seven fundamental principles of the body</term> of the person. In questions regarding illness, one should speak of the aggravation of that specific element.

Now the tastes. The tastes of the Moon and others are salty, etc. For example: Salt for the Moon. Pungent for the Sun. Astringent for the Saturn. Sweet for Jupiter. Bitter for Mars. Sour for Venus. The six mixed tastes for Mercury. **The application:** The strongest planet at the time of conception indicates the cravings for specific tastes in the pregnant woman; likewise, at the time of birth, it indicates the knowledge of the food to be given to the mother.

Now the time-units. The half-year and others belong to the Sun and others. There, the Sun is the lord of the half-year <note>original: *Ayana*, a six-month period; there are two in a year, the Northern and Southern, starting from Capricorn and Cancer</note>. Mars is the lord of the day. Venus is the lord of the fortnight <note>15 days</note>. Mercury is the lord of the season <note>two months</note>. Saturn is the lord of the year. Jupiter is the lord of the month. The Moon is the lord of the moment <note>original: *Kshana*, equal to two Ghatis or 48 minutes</note>. **The application:** At the time of a query, whichever planet's <term>Navamsha: a one-ninth division of a zodiac sign</term> is in the Ascendant, the number of divisions from that planet to the Navamsha indicates the time (in half-years, etc.) when the planet's good or bad results will be realized. || 28-29 ||

Mars, Saturn, Jupiter, the Sun, Venus, the Moon, and Mercury are said to be the lords of the marrow, nerves, fat, bones, semen, blood, and skin elements respectively. || 28 ||

The lords of the salty, pungent, astringent, sweet, bitter, sour, and mixed tastes are respectively the Moon, Sun, Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Venus, and Mercury. The lords of the half-year, day, fortnight, season, year, month, and moment are respectively the Sun, Mars, Venus, Mercury, Saturn, Jupiter, and the Moon (The Sun gives results in six months, Mars in a day, Venus in 15 days, Mercury in two months, Jupiter in one month, and the Moon in a moment). Whichever planet's Navamsha is in the Ascendant of the query, the planet gives its result in as many half-years, etc., as there are Navamshas from that point. (Su. Sha. Kar) || 29 ||

### Regarding the Aspects of the Sun and Others on Specific Places.

There is a quarter-glance <note>aspect</note> on the third and tenth houses; half on the pair of trines <note>5th and 9th</note> for all heavenly bodies. They say there is a three-quarter glance on the pair of squares <note>4th and 8th</note> and full visual strength on the seventh house. || 30 ||

Now the aspects of the planets according to position are described. For all heavenly bodies, there is a quarter-glance (25% strength) on the third and tenth houses. All planets look at their own third and tenth houses with a quarter-glance. On the pair of trines—the ninth and fifth houses—a half-glance...

# Chapter 2: On the Names, Natures, Qualities, and Divisions of the Planets

->**The Chapter on the Nature and Qualities of Planets**<-

This means that for a moment there is a half-glance. In the pair of "squares" (the 4th and 8th houses), there is a collection of three-quarters vision. In the house of the "Bodiless One" <note>The 7th house, associated with relationships and the god of love, Kama</note>, there is full visual strength. This application applies to all planets everywhere.

Here, the logic regarding the aspects is explained: The 3rd house is the place of siblings/kin, and the 10th is the place of the father. Since people generally look upon their kin and fathers with a common or ordinary glance, the planets also have a lesser aspect on those two. A greater glance is given by people toward their children and their own fortune; likewise, the planets have a specific aspect on the 5th (children) and 9th (fortune) houses. An even greater glance is given by people toward their own happiness and their own longevity; these are the 4th and 8th houses, and thus it is the same for the planets. With an even more intense gaze, people look upon their "better half" (spouse); that place is the 7th, so is it any wonder that the planets also look there with full vision? || 30 ||

<gloss>All planets look at the 3rd and 10th from their position with one quarter-strength; at both trines (5th and 9th) with half-strength (two quarters); at the 4th and 8th with three-quarters strength; and they look at the 7th with all four quarters. Therefore, scholars say their full visual strength resides in the 7th. || 30 ||</gloss>

### On the Special Strength of the Sun and Others in Aspect

**Saturn is exceedingly powerful in the combination of quarter-glances; the Minister of the Lord of the Gods (Jupiter) is auspicious in the trine aspect.**
**The Son of the Earth (Mars) is capable with the three-quarter aspect; all inhabitants of the sky are rich in visual strength in the seventh. || 31 ||**

Now the visual strength <term>Drishti-bala: the strength a planet gains by looking at a specific house</term> of the planets is described. Saturn becomes exceedingly powerful in the combination of quarter-glances. Where other planets have only a quarter-aspect (the 3rd and 10th from their position), Saturn is strongest due to this connection. This means Saturn looks at the 3rd and 10th with full vision. The "Minister of the Lord of the Gods" (Jupiter) is auspicious in the "corner" or trine aspect—the 9th and 5th. This means Jupiter’s full vision falls on the 9th and 5th. The "Son of the Earth" (Mars) is capable and strong in the three-quarter aspect. The three-quarter aspect falls on the 4th and 8th; in those, Mars is powerful. Mars has full vision in the 4th and 8th. In the 7th house (the 7th from its own position), all "inhabitants of the sky" (all planets) are rich in visual strength. This means all planets see the 7th house fully. As stated in the *Saravali* <note>A classic 8th-century CE astrological text by Kalyanavarman</note>:

> "Saturn looks fully at the third and tenth; Jupiter at the trines;
> The Son of the Earth at the squares; and Venus, the Sun, the Moon, and Mercury at the seventh, respectively."

Now the logic is stated: Valor and the protection of the kingdom are the duties of a servant; therefore, Saturn (the servant) looks fully at those places (3rd and 10th). Similarly, knowledge and religion are taught and protected by the Guru (Jupiter); therefore, Jupiter looks fully at the place of knowledge (5th) and the place of religion (9th). In the same way, the protection of happiness and longevity is the duty of a leader; therefore, the leader Mars looks fully at the place of happiness (4th) and the place of longevity (8th). Since a wife is the "other half" of everyone, it is most fitting that all planets look fully at the house of the wife, the 7th. || 31 ||

<gloss>Saturn is strong with a one-quarter aspect strength, meaning Saturn has full vision in the 3rd and 10th houses. Jupiter is auspicious in the trine aspect (5th and 9th), meaning he sees the 5th and 9th houses fully. Mars is strong with the three-quarter aspect, meaning he sees the 4th and 8th fully. All planets have full visual strength in the 7th house. Here, the counting of houses should be done from each planet's own position. (Author of Su. Sha.) || 31 ||</gloss>

### On the Upward Gazes of the Planets

**The Lord of the Day (Sun) and the Son of the Earth (Mars) look upward; the vision of Venus and the Son of the Moon (Mercury) is a side-glance.**
**The Moon and Jupiter have a level or straight gaze; the falling of the eyes is downward for the Lord of Serpents (Rahu) and Saturn. || 32 ||**

### From the Annotated Jataka Parijata

Now follows the description of the planetary aspects and gazes. The Lord of the Day and the Son of the Earth—the Sun and Mars—possess an upward gaze. They look toward the heights. The gazes of the Poet and the Son of the Moon—Venus and Mercury—are side-long. They look with a glancing eye. The Moon and the Teacher—the Moon and Jupiter—possess a level gaze. They look straight ahead. The Lord of Snakes and the Slow-Mover—Rahu and Saturn—have a downward cast of the eye; Saturn and Rahu are downward-looking, as they gaze toward the depths. The purpose of this is to determine the nature of a person's vision based on the dominant planet at birth. || 32 ||

<note>The text uses poetic synonyms: "Lord of the Day" for Sun, "Poet" for Venus, "Teacher" for Jupiter, etc.</note>

The Sun and Mars look upward. Venus and Mercury have a side-long glance. The Moon and Jupiter look straight. Rahu and Saturn look downward. || 32 ||

### Regarding the Positional Strength of Planets

**Those planets situated in their exaltation, trine, friend’s house, decanate, sign, or divisional portion, or possessing the special "Vaisheshika" divisions,**
**And those with ascending strength or high points in the Eight-fold Division—these heavenly bodies are said to be superior in positional strength. || 33 ||**
**Those in fall, in an enemy’s house, joined or aspected by malefics, in malefic divisions or junctions, with few points or in bad portions,**
**Overpowered by the Sun’s rays or defeated—these, lacking the power of aspect and other strengths, shall not be auspicious. || 34 ||**

Now the positional strength <term>Sthana-bala: strength derived from a planet's specific location in the zodiac</term> of the planets is explained: "In their exaltation," etc. The word "own" applies to all subsequent terms. Those heavenly bodies—the planets—which are in their own exaltation, their own <term>Trikona: a specific auspicious triangular zone in a sign</term>, their own friend's sign, their own <term>Drekkana: a 10-degree subdivision or decanate</term>, their own sign, their own <term>Navamsha: the 9th divisional chart, crucial for strength</term>, or their own "Vaisheshika" grade (such as the Parijata grade and others), and those with "ascending strength"—meaning they are close to the center of the house—as it is said: "Ascending strengths are effective up to the point of the house center, beyond which they decline." Those with "high points"—meaning more than four auspicious marks in the <term>Ashtakavarga: a system of points used to calculate planetary strength</term>—are considered to have full positional strength.

Now he describes those lacking positional strength: "In fall, enemy's house, joined or aspected by malefics." Those planets that have reached their sign of fall <note>original: "Nicha"</note>, are in an enemy's house, are joined with malefic planets, are gazed upon by malefics, are in malefic divisions, are in the junctions between signs <note>original: "Sandhi"</note>, have "few points" (less than four auspicious points in the Eight-fold system), are in "bad portions" (malefic divisions), are "overpowered by the Sun's rays" (combust), or are "defeated" (losing in a planetary war)—these, being devoid of aspect-strength and other powers, are not auspicious; rather, they become inauspicious. So it was said by Varahamihira:

> "Positional strength is gained through being in one's exaltation, friend's house, trine, ninth-division, or one's own home." || 33-34 ||

Planets in their own exaltation, trine, friend's house, decanate, sign, ninth-division, special "Vaisheshika" grades like Parijata, ascending strength (house-matching), and high points (more than 4 in the Eight-fold system) are positionally strong. Conversely, those in fall or an enemy's house, joined or aspected by malefics, in malefic divisions, junctions, or with few points (less than 4), in bad portions, eclipsed by the Sun's rays (combust), or lacking aspect-strength are not auspicious—that is, they are inauspicious. || 33-34 ||

### Regarding the Directional Strength of Planets

**In the Ascendant, the Fourth House, the Seventh House, and the Tenth House, Mercury and the Immortal's Teacher, the Son of Bhrigu and the Moon,**
**Saturn, and the Son of the Earth and the Maker of Day—if so placed, they are respectively endowed with directional strength. || 35 ||**

Now he describes the directional strength <term>Dig-bala: strength gained by being in a specific cardinal direction/house</term> (house strength) of the planets. Mercury and the Teacher of the Immortals (Jupiter); the Son of Bhrigu (Venus) and the Moon; Saturn alone; and the Son of the Earth (Mars) and the Maker of Day (Sun)—if these are respectively in the Ascendant (1st), the Bottom of the Sky (4th), the <unclear>Setting</unclear> (7th), and the Mid-heaven (10th), then they possess directional strength...

They are said to be endowed with strength. For example: Mercury and Jupiter are strong in the Ascendant <note>The 1st House or 'Lagna'</note>. Venus and the Moon are strong in the fourth house. Saturn is strong in the seventh house. Mars and the Sun are strong in the tenth house. As stated by the venerable Mihira <note>referring to Varahamihira, the 6th-century polymath</note>:

> "Mercury and Jupiter are strong in the East (Ascendant); the Sun and Mars in the South (10th); Saturn in the West (7th); and Venus and the Moon in the North (4th)."

It should be understood that these planets become powerless in the seventh house from their respective positions of strength. || 35 ||

Mercury and Jupiter in the Ascendant, the fourth, the seventh, and the tenth houses respectively; Venus and the Moon; Saturn; Mars and the Sun possess Directional Strength <term>Digbala: strength gained by a planet based on the compass direction/house it occupies</term>. That is, Mercury and Jupiter are strong in the Ascendant. Venus and the Moon in the house of happiness <note>the 4th house</note>. Saturn in the seventh. Mars and the Sun are strong in the tenth. || 35 ||

### Now, Temporal Strength.

> The Moon, Saturn, and Mars are strong at night; the others during the day. They are strong in their own hour, year, month, and day.
> Benefics and malefic are strong in the two fortnights starting with the bright one; Mercury is always endowed with temporal strength. || 36 ||

Now the Temporal Strength <term>Kalabala: strength derived from the time of birth</term> of the planets is described. The Moon, Saturn, and Mars are strong at night. The others—Sun, Jupiter, and Venus—are strong during the day. They are strong in their own <term>Hora: an astrological hour</term>, their own year, their own month, and their own day. This means the Lord of the Hour is strong in its hour, the Lord of the Year in its year, the Lord of the Month in its month, and the Lord of the Day in its day. Benefics are strong in the bright fortnight <note>Shukla Paksha, the waxing moon</note>, and malefics are strong in the dark fortnight <note>Krishna Paksha, the waning moon</note>. Mercury is strong at all times. As stated by Varaha in the *Brihat Jataka*:

> "Moon, Mars, and Saturn are strong at night; Mercury is always strong; the others are strong by day. Malefics and benefics are strong in the dark and bright fortnights respectively. Temporal strength is also gained by the lords of the solstice, day, hour, and month." || 36 ||

The Moon, Saturn, and Mars are strong at night; the remaining (Sun, Jupiter, Venus) are strong by day. Mercury is strong at all times. All planets are strong in their respective astrological hours, their respective years (whoever is the Lord of the Year), their respective months, and their respective days. In the bright fortnight, benefic planets are auspicious, and in the dark fortnight, malefic planets are auspicious. || 36 ||

### Now, Motional Strength.

> The victors in planetary war, those in retrograde, those in conjunction, Venus, Mercury, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn;
> The Moon and the Sun in the northern path are endowed with greater Motional Strength. || 36 ½ ||

Now the Motional Strength <term>Cheshtabala: strength gained through planetary movement and speed</term> of the planets is described. "Victors" refers to those who have achieved victory in a planetary war <note>Graha Yuddha: when two planets are within one degree of each other</note>.

# Page 44
## Commentary on Jataka Parijata

*Vakra* means retrograde motion; *Samagama* means conjunction with the Moon. Those that have reached these states—meaning those in retrograde or joined with the Moon—are the planets Venus, Mercury, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn. Furthermore, the Sun and Moon are said to possess *Cheshta-bala* <note>Motional strength or "effort" strength</note> when they are in the "Direction of the Gods" (*Divyasha*), which refers to the Northern Path (*Uttarayana*). 

The meaning is this: The Sun and Moon are endowed with *Cheshta-bala* during the Northern Solstice. The five planets starting with Mars are endowed with this strength when they are victors in planetary combat, when they are retrograde, or when they are in conjunction with the Moon. || 36 1/2 ||

->Venus, Mercury, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn—these planets have full *Cheshta-bala* if they are victorious in war, retrograde, or joined with the Moon. The Moon and Sun have greater *Cheshta-bala* in the Northern Solstice. (According to the author of *Suryasiddhanta*) || 36 1/2 ||<-

### Now, the Natural Strength (Nisarga-bala) of the Planets.

->The planets starting with Mars, when joined with the Lord of the North, are rich in *Cheshta-bala* in sequence.<-
->In terms of Natural Strength (*Nisarga-bala*), Saturn, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Moon, and Sun are progressively stronger. || 37 ||<-
->The wise speak of the six-fold strengths (*Shadbala*) as Aspect (*Drik*), Positional (*Sthana*), Natural (*Nisarga*), Motional (*Cheshta*), Directional (*Dig*), and Temporal (*Kala*) strengths.<-
->In the "Moon-Arrows-Moon-Mountain" <note>A mnemonic for the numbers 1, 5, 1, 4, 1, 7</note> system, these divisions are explained by the sages. || 38 ||<-
->The full strength of the planets, or three-quarters, or half, arises from the sixty-fold divisions and the specific strengths gained in signs like Capricorn. || 39 ||<-

Now the author explains the Natural Strengths and their divisions. The five planets starting with Mars (*Mahisuta*) are endowed with *Cheshta-bala* when they are in the Northern direction. When planets are in conjunction, the planet situated to the North is considered to have *Cheshta-bala*. As stated by Varahamihira <note>A famous 6th-century Indian astronomer and polymath</note>:

> "The Sun and the Moon are considered to have *Cheshta-bala* in the Northern Solstice; the remaining planets have it when retrograde or in conjunction. They are also considered strong when their rays are expansive and when they are situated to the North during planetary combat."

**Regarding Natural Strength (*Nisarga*):** Saturn, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, the Moon, and the Sun are progressively more powerful in their inherent nature. Saturn has the least strength of all; Mars is stronger than Saturn, Mercury stronger than Mars, Jupiter stronger than Mercury, Venus stronger than Jupiter, the Moon stronger than Venus, and the Sun is the most powerful. As stated in the *Brihat Jataka* <note>The foundational text of Hindu astrology</note>:

> "Saturn, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Moon, and Sun are powerful in increasing order."

**Regarding the Divisions of Strength:** 
1. *Drik* = Aspect strength. 
2. *Sthana* = Positional strength. 
3. *Nisarga* = Natural strength. 
4. *Cheshta* = Motional strength. 
5. *Dig* = Directional strength. 
6. *Kala* = Temporal strength. 

These are the six strengths (*Shadbala*) for each planet. The sages say these have divisions of 1, 5, 1, 4, 1, and 7 respectively. They are as follows: 
*   **Aspect Strength:** One type. 
*   **Positional Strength:** Five types—Exaltation strength, strength from the seven divisional charts (*Saptavarga*), Odd/Even sign strength, Quadrant strength, and Decanate (*Drekkana*) strength. 
*   **Natural Strength:** Only one type. 
*   **Motional Strength:** Four types—Retrograde, Conjunction, Northern Solstice, and Declination strength. 
*   **Directional Strength:** Only one type. 
*   **Temporal Strength:** Seven types—Mid-day/Mid-night, Fortnightly, Day/Night/Three-part, Lord of the Year, Lord of the Month, Lord of the Day, and Lord of the Hour (*Hora*) strengths. (See the *Keshaviya* <note>A reference to the Keshaviya Jataka, a classical astrological text</note>).

**Regarding Strength arising from Yogas:** The strength gained from the Northern Solstice (*Saumyayana*) combined with the six-fold strengths results in specific numerical values. These are expressed in whole numbers and sixty-fold fractions (*Shashtiamshas*). The resulting strength of the planets is then determined as full, three-quarters, or half...

# Chapter 2: On the Names, Forms, Qualities, and Divisions of Planets

Page 45

Full strength is 1, three-quarters strength is $\frac{3}{4}$, and half strength is $\frac{1}{2}$. Here, regarding the strength of planets in the <term>Shadbala</term><note>The "Six-fold Strength" system used to determine a planet's potency in a horoscope.</note> calculation, when the whole integers of a planet's form are added, that planet's combined strength becomes "Full." If sixty-parts $\frac{1}{60}$ are added to that same Shadbala, the combined strength becomes "Three-quarters" $\frac{3}{4}$. Similarly, by adding <term>Vishtyansha</term><note>A specific fractional unit used in traditional astronomical calculations.</note> $3\frac{1}{60}$ to that Shadbala, its combined strength should be known as "Half" $\frac{1}{2}$. || 37-39 ||

Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, and Saturn possess greater <term>Cheshta-bala</term><note>Motional strength, related to a planet's speed and retrograde status.</note> when they are in the northern <term>Shara</term><note>Celestial latitude.</note>. In terms of <term>Naisargika-bala</term><note>Natural or inherent strength.</note>, the planets are progressively stronger in this order: Saturn, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, the Moon, and the Sun. For example: Saturn < Mars < Mercury < Jupiter < Venus < Moon < Sun. In natural strength, Saturn is the weakest and the Sun is the strongest.

The six types of strength—Aspect (<term>Drishti</term>), Positional (<term>Sthana</term>), Natural (<term>Nisarga</term>), Motional (<term>Cheshta</term>), Directional (<term>Dig</term>), and Temporal (<term>Kala</term>)—are called <term>Shadbala</term>. These have 1, 5, 1, 5, 1, and 7 subdivisions respectively. (See the Sanskrit commentary). Scholars have stated that: Aspect = 1; Position = 5; Natural = 1; Motion = 5; Direction = 1; Time = 7.

In the Shadbala of planets, by adding the planet's form (integers), sixty-parts $\frac{1}{60}$, and <term>Vishtyansha</term> $3\frac{1}{60}$, the combined strengths of the planets are derived. These are, in order: Full = 1, Three-quarters = $\frac{3}{4}$, and Half = $\frac{1}{2}$. (According to the author of *Suryasiddhanta Sharini*) || 37-39 ||

->**Now, the Measurement of Strength.**<-

Six and a half for the Sun and Jupiter; for Venus, five and a half.
Seven for the Son of the Moon (Mercury), six for the Moon; for the Son of the Sun (Saturn) and Mars, the number is five. || 40 ||

Regarding what was said in the previous verse about "forms and sixty-parts," the specific strength for each is now stated. For the Sun (<term>Inasya</term>), "six with a half added" = 6.5. For Jupiter (<term>Surch</term>), it is also 6.5. For Venus, "five with a half added" = 5.5. For the Son of the Moon (Mercury), it is 7. For the Moon, it is 6. For Saturn and Mars (<term>Saurarayoh</term>), the strength is measured as 5. These strength values are recited for planets that are powerful in the Shadbala. Venkateshwara says the same in the *Sarvartha Chintamani*:

> The Sun is powerful with six and a half; the Moon has six; the Son of the Earth (Mars) has five.
> The Son of the Moon (Mercury) has seven; Jupiter has six; Venus is powerful with five and a half.
> Saturn has exactly five; this is the combination of the six-fold strengths, otherwise they would be different.

Now, by way of context, other strength values are also illuminated:

| Planet/Type | Strength Value |
| :--- | :--- |
| General Strength | 3.0 |
| Positional Strength (<term>Sthana</term>) | 2.75 (3 minus a quarter) |
| Directional Strength (<term>Digbala</term>) | 0.75 (1 minus a quarter) |
| Motional Strength (<term>Cheshta</term>) | 0.83 (1 minus a sixth) |
| Temporal Strength (<term>Kalavirya</term>) | 1.875 (2 minus an eighth) |

The Sun, Moon, Mercury, and Jupiter have full strength. <insert>0.50</insert> Half strength is assigned to the <term>Ayana</term><note>Strength derived from the planet's declination/equinoctial position.</note> strength in separate divisions. They say Directional strength is 0.83 (1 minus a sixth); Positional strength is 2.25 (2 plus a quarter). Temporal strength is 1.66 (2 minus a third); Motional strength is 0.50 (half of a third).

For the Moon, Venus, and Jupiter, the <term>Ayana</term> strength is 0.66 (1 minus a third). Motional strength is 0.66 (1 minus a third); Temporal strength is 1.125 (1 plus an eighth). For the Son of the Sun (Saturn) and the Son of the Earth (Mars), the Directional strength is 1.50 (half of three); <term>Ayana</term> is 0.33 (one third); and Positional strength is 2.50 (two and a half). These are the strengths cited in order.

The calculation of clear/accurate strength should be done according to the *Keshaviya* <note>Refers to the *Keshaviya Jataka*, a classic text on horoscopy.</note>. || 40 ||

## On the Temporary Friendship of Planets

**Planets situated in the houses of siblings, gains, honors, the underworld, wealth, and expenses relative to one another—**
**These become temporary friends; if they are situated elsewhere, they are your enemies. || 41 ||**

Now, the temporary friends and enemies of the planets are described. Relative to one another, from whichever planet others are situated in the "sibling" (3rd), "gain" (11th), "honor" (10th), "underworld" (4th), "wealth" (2nd), and "expense" (12th) houses—those become its friends for that specific time. That planet also becomes a friend to them. If those celestial bodies <note>Sanskrit: *khaga*, literally "sky-goers"</note> are situated elsewhere (in the 1st, 5th, 6th, 7th, 8th, or 9th houses), then they are its enemies. The same applies in reverse. As shown in the illustrated chart, following the aforementioned order for the Sun: the Moon, Mercury, Mars, Saturn, Jupiter, and Venus are friends, and the Sun is a friend to them; thus, they are all mutual friends. Likewise, if these planets were in the enemy positions, the Sun would be their foe. As stated by Varahamihira <note>A famous 6th-century Indian astronomer and polymath</note>:

> "Those situated in the houses of wealth (2nd), expense (12th), income (11th), siblings (3rd), profession (10th), and family (4th) relative to each other
> are temporary friends; some say this holds even in their exaltation signs; otherwise, they are enemies." || 41 ||

# ॥ The Five-Fold Friendship Chart ॥

| | | **Temporary** | | |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| | | Friends | Neutrals | Enemies |
| **Natural** | **Friends** | Great Friend | Friend | Neutral |
| | **Neutrals** | Friend | • | Enemy |
| | **Enemies** | Neutral | Enemy | Great Enemy |

By combining <term>Temporary Friendship</term><note>Tatkalika Maitri: relationships based on the planets' current positions in a specific birth chart</note> and <term>Natural Friendship</term><note>Naisargika Maitri: the inherent, permanent relationships between planets</note>, five types of friendship are formed, ranging from Great Friend to Great Enemy. When a planet is a friend in both the temporary and natural categories, it becomes a **Great Friend**. When it is an enemy in both, it becomes a **Great Enemy**. If it is a friend in one and neutral in the other, it is simply a **Friend**. If it is neutral in one and an enemy in the other, it is an **Enemy**. Finally, if it is an enemy in one but a friend in the other, it becomes **Neutral**. 

For example, in this chart, Jupiter and Mars are in the 3rd and 4th houses from the Sun; they are the Sun's temporary friends and also his natural friends, so they become **Great Friends**. Venus, being in the 12th house, is a temporary friend but a natural enemy, so Venus becomes **Neutral** to the Sun. Saturn, being in the 7th house, is a temporary enemy and also a natural enemy, so Saturn becomes a **Great Enemy** to the Sun. Mercury, in the 2nd house, is a temporary friend and naturally neutral, so he becomes a **Friend**. Other relationships should be understood in the same way. (Commentary by S. Shastrakara) ॥ 45-46 ॥

## Now, the Determination of the Stability and Nature of Planets

> The Sun is stable, the Moon is moving, Mars is fierce, and the son of the Moon (Mercury) is mixed. 
> Jupiter is mild, Venus is light, and Saturn is described by the great sages as extremely sharp. ॥ 47 ॥

> For Moveable, Fixed, and Dual signs respectively, the lords of the 11th, 9th, and 7th houses—if they are also lords of the signs occupied by the <term>Khara-lord</term><note>The lord of the 22nd Drekkana, considered malefic</note> or <term>Mandhi</term><note>A sensitive mathematical point in a chart associated with Saturn, usually considered inauspicious</note>—become extremely powerful Obstructing Planets. ॥ 48 ॥

Now the temperaments of the planets are described. The Sun is **Stable** (steady-minded). The Moon is **Moving** (fickle-minded). Mars is **Fierce** (cruel-natured). Mercury is **Mixed** (possessing various temperaments). Jupiter is **Mild** (cool-headed). Venus is **Light** (slow or gentle nature). Saturn is described by the great sages as **Extremely Sharp** (subtle or piercing nature).

Next, the <term>Obstructing Planets</term><note>Badhaka Grahas: planets that create obstacles for specific houses</note> are discussed. For Moveable, Fixed, and Dual signs (previously mentioned), the planets located in—or the lords of—the 11th, 9th, and 7th houses respectively, become "Obstructors" if they are also the lords of the signs where the Khara-lord or Mandhi reside. 

Consider this: when analyzing a specific <term>House</term><note>Bhava</note>, if that house falls in a **Moveable** sign, then the lord of the 11th house from it is the obstructor. If the house is a **Fixed** sign, the lord of the 9th house is the obstructor. If the house is a **Dual** sign, the lord of the 7th house is the obstructor. If these lords are further linked to the Khara-lord or Mandhi, they become extremely obstructive to the matters of that house. ॥

# Chapter 2: On the Nature, Qualities, and Distinctions of the Planets

...becomes a great obstacle to the house in question. Here, the term "Khara" <note>A technical term for the 22nd Drekkana (decanate) from the rising sign, considered malefic.</note> refers to what will be described later: "The lord of the 22nd decanate from the Ascendant or the Moon is the Khara." One should understand the "Lord of the Khara" or the "Lord of the sign where Mandi (Gulika) is situated" <note>Mandi and Gulika are mathematical points or "shadow planets" in Vedic astrology used to identify malefic influences.</note> as the primary obstructors. It should be stated that during the period (Dasha) of an obstructing planet, there is a loss of the respective house's significations. Other obstructing planets are also mentioned in the *Sarvartha Chintamani* <note>A classical 17th-century astrological treatise by Venkatesha Sharma.</note>:

> "The lord of the 8th house from any specific house, or the lord of the Khara decanate, or the son of the Sun (Saturn), or the lords of Mandi and the sign it occupies, or the lord of their Navamsha <note>The 1/9th divisional chart</note>—whichever among these is cruel in nature; or the planet that is an enemy to the lord of that house or a disease-causing planet, or a planet placed in a sign with zero points (bindus) in the Ashtakavarga system—the wise astrologer should predict the destruction of the body, wealth, and other houses during the planetary periods of these factors." || 47-48 ||

The learned have said that the Sun represents a steady intellect, the Moon is fickle-minded, Mars is cruel-minded, Mercury is of a mixed nature, Jupiter is gentle-minded, Venus is of light/frivolous intellect, and Saturn is of a sharp/piercing nature.

Planets situated in the 11th, 9th, and 7th positions from Moveable, Fixed, and Dual signs respectively, or their lords, if they are also the lord of the Khara or the lord of the sign where Gulika resides, become "obstructors" (Badhakas) of those houses. (According to the author of *Suka Jataka*) || 47-48 ||

## Now, the Consideration of Specific Results from the Sun and Others.

> From the Sun, one should consider the soul, father, influence, health, power, and prosperity.
> The Moon is the maker of the mind, intellect, the favor of kings, mother, and wealth. || 49 ||
>
> From the son of the Earth (Mars), consider strength, disease, qualities, younger siblings, land, children, and kinsmen.
> The Awakener (Mercury) is the maker of education, relatives, discrimination, the maternal uncle, friends, the skin, and actions/duties. || 49 ||

> From the Lord of Speech (Jupiter), consider wisdom, constant physical nourishment (health), children, and spiritual knowledge.
> From the descendant of Bhrigu (Venus), consider the wife, vehicles, ornaments, desire, trade, and happiness. || 50 ||
>
> Saturn is the giver of longevity, livelihood, the cause of death, adversity, and prosperity.
> One should consider the paternal grandfather through the Serpent (Rahu), and the maternal grandfather through the Crested One (Ketu). || 50 ||

Now it is explained which matters should be considered from which planet. From the **Sun**, one must consider the Self (the physical body), the father (the progenitor), influence (valor), health (freedom from disease), power (or its loss), and prosperity (wealth). The **Moon** is the "doer" or significator of the mind, intellect (capacity for practical knowledge), the favor of kings (grace of authorities), the mother, and wealth/opulence. These should be judged from the Moon.

From **Mars** (the son of the Earth), one should consider strength (bravery), diseases, personal qualities, younger siblings (brothers and sisters), land, children (sons and daughters), and agnates or kinsmen. **Mercury** (the Awakener) is the significator of education, relatives, discrimination, the maternal uncle (mother's brother), friends, the skin, and one's duty or work. These matters are to be judged from Mercury.

From **Jupiter** (the Lord of Speech), one should consider wisdom, the constant nourishment of the body (general health), children, and spiritual or philosophical knowledge. From **Venus** (Bhrigu), one should consider the wife, vehicles (elephants, horses, etc.), ornaments, desire (passion), trade (commerce), and happiness. **Saturn** is the provider of lifespan, livelihood (means of living), the cause of death, adversity (sorrow), and prosperity (happiness). These must be judged from Saturn.

One should consider the paternal grandfather (father's father) through **Rahu** (the Serpent); meaning, the study of the grandfather requires Rahu. One should consider the maternal grandfather (mother's father) through **Ketu** (the Crested One). The consideration of the maternal grandfather is to be performed through Ketu.

The result is that the specified planets are taken as the "significators" (Karakas) of the mentioned houses/themes; therefore, based on their auspicious or inauspicious strength, the good or bad fortune of those life aspects should be predicted. || 49-50 ||

# The Commentary on Jataka Parijata

(1) From the **Sun**, one should consider: the father, the soul, majesty, health, power, and prosperity.
(2) From the **Moon**, one should consider: the mind, intellect, the favor of kings, the mother, and wealth.
(3) From **Mars**, one should consider: prowess, disease, qualities, brothers, land, enemies, and kin.
(4) From **Mercury**, one should consider: education, relatives, discrimination, the maternal uncle, friends, and speech.
(5) From **Jupiter**, one should consider: intellect, physical nourishment, children, and knowledge.
(6) From **Venus**, one should consider: the wife, vehicles, ornaments, desire, trade, and happiness.
(7) From **Saturn**, one should consider: lifespan, life, the cause of death, adversity, and fortune.
From **Rahu** <note>the North Node of the Moon</note>, consider the paternal grandfather; from **Ketu** <note>the South Node of the Moon</note>, consider the maternal grandfather. || 49-50 ||

### Now, the Planetary Significators of the Houses

<note>original: "अथ ग्रहाणां भावकारकत्वम्" - The technical term 'Karaka' refers to a planet that acts as a 'significator' or 'doer' for a specific area of life.</note>

The Sun, Jupiter, Mars, the Moon and Mercury, Jupiter, Saturn and Mars, Venus, Saturn, the Sun and Jupiter, Jupiter, the Sun, Mercury and Saturn, Jupiter, and the son of the Sun <note>Saturn</note> are the significators starting from the Ascendant. || 51 ||

Now the significator planets for the twelve houses starting from the Ascendant are stated. In order from the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the rising sign or 1st house</term>, the twelve houses are:
The Sun; Jupiter; Mars; the Moon and Mercury; Jupiter; Saturn and Mars; Venus; Saturn; the Sun and Jupiter; Jupiter, the Sun, Mercury, and Saturn; Jupiter; and Saturn. These are the significators. The consideration of the houses starting from the Ascendant is done through their respective significator planets. Here, Sage Parashara has mentioned one planet as the significator for each house, as per his statement:
> "The Sun, Jupiter, Mars, the Moon, Jupiter, Mars, Venus, Saturn, Jupiter, the son of the Moon <note>Mercury</note>, Jupiter, and Saturn are the house significators." || 51 ||

The significators of the twelve houses are these: the Sun for the 1st house, Jupiter for the 2nd, Mars for the 3rd, the Moon and Mercury for the 4th, Jupiter for the 5th, Saturn and Mars for the 6th, Venus for the 7th, Saturn for the 8th, the Sun and Jupiter for the 9th, Jupiter, the Sun, Mercury, and Saturn for the 10th, Jupiter for the 11th, and Saturn for the 12th. || 51 ||

# Chapter 2: On the Names, Forms, Qualities, and Divisions of the Planets

### On the Auspicious and Inauspicious Effects of Planets in Specific Positions

->If Venus, Mercury, and Jupiter are positioned in the houses of Desire, Earth, and the Son respectively,<-
->they cause misfortune in all birth charts; however, Saturn in the eighth house is always a giver of desired results. || 52 ||<-

Now, certain planets are described as givers of misfortune based on their position. "Venus, Mercury, and Jupiter" <note>original: *sitenduputrāmaravandyamanāḥ*</note> being in the "houses of Desire, Earth, and the Son" means if they are located in the 7th, 4th, and 5th houses respectively, they are said to be "givers of misfortune" <note>original: *ariṣṭadāḥ*</note> in all birth charts. Here, it should be understood that Venus in the 7th, Mercury in the 4th, and Jupiter in the 5th becomes a source of affliction. Saturn in the 8th house is always a giver of desired results. Saturn situated in the 8th house becomes a doer of good.

Regarding this subject, Mantreshwara has presented his own view in the *Phaladeepika* <note>A classic 13th-century text on Hindu astrology</note> as follows:

> Others say that the Sun in the 9th, the Moon in the 4th, Mars in the 3rd, Jupiter in the 5th,
> Venus in the 7th, and Saturn in the 8th house cause distress to the native.

**Notes —** It should also be considered that the house-based results of Venus, Mercury, and Jupiter in these specific houses are usually considered auspicious, and the result of Saturn in the 8th is usually considered inauspicious <note>The commentator is noting a contradiction between this verse and general astrological rules</note>. || 52 ||

If Venus, Mercury, and Jupiter are placed in the 7th, 4th, and 5th houses respectively, they cause misfortune in every birth chart. Saturn in the 8th house always fulfills one's desires.

### On the Physical Forms of the Sun and Other Planets

->The Sun is majestic, with a square body, dark-red limbs, and honey-colored eyes.<-
->He is of a bilious temperament, has sparse hair, and is dominated by the quality of Purity. || 53 ||<-

->The Moon is wandering by nature, soft-spoken, wise, with auspicious sight and beautiful, firm limbs.<-
->He is ever-intelligent, has a slender and rounded body, and is of a phlegmatic and windy temperament. || 54 ||<-

->Mars has a cruel gaze, a youthful form, a generous nature, a bilious temperament, and is very fickle with a thin waist.<-
->He has beautiful limbs of a reddish-pale hue, is majestic, lustful, and devoted to the quality of Darkness. || 55 ||<-

->Mercury has a body like the hue of Durva grass, clear speech, a thin frame, and is the lord of those with the quality of Passion; he is very fond of laughter.<-
->He loves causing loss, has a temperament of bile, phlegm, and wind, possesses immediate majesty and wealth, and is learned. || 56 ||<-

->Jupiter has a large frame and a big belly, is yellow in color, of a phlegmatic temperament, endowed with all virtues, and is an authority on all scriptures.<-
->He has brownish-gold hair and eyes, is pure-natured, extremely wise, possesses the marks of a great king, and is the sustainer of prosperity. || 57 ||<-

->Venus has black curly hair, is dark and beautiful, with symmetrical and lovely limbs, a gentle look, and a lustful nature.<-
->He is of a windy and phlegmatic temperament, passionate, a treasury of fortune, and a source of happiness, strength, and good qualities. || 58 ||<-

->Saturn has coarse hair and limbs, a thin frame, a body dark like Durva grass, and a phlegmatic-windy temperament.<-
->He has thick teeth, beautiful reddish-brown eyes, is of a dark disposition, devoted to his own intellect, and is lazy. || 59 ||<-
<note>The original text numbers the Saturn verse as 56, duplicating the Mercury verse number, though it follows verse 58.</note>

Now the forms of the planets are explained. **The Sun:** "Square body" <note>original: *caturasradehaḥ*</note> means the body is as wide as it is long. The rest is clear.
**The Moon:** "Wandering" means restless; "slender and rounded body" means a small spherical frame. The rest is clear.
**Mars:** "Cruel gaze" means an inauspicious look; "youthful form" means a young body. The rest is clear.
**Mercury:** "Body like Durva grass" means a green-colored body like a blade of grass. "Loves loss" means he takes pleasure in destruction. The rest is clear.
**Jupiter:** "Large frame and big belly" means his stomach and body are both large and long. "Brownish-gold hair and eyes" means his luster, hair, and eyes are of a brownish-yellow hue. "Marks of a great king" <gloss>means</gloss> he possesses the characteristics of a sovereign. The rest is clear.

# With the Commentary of Jataka Parijata

**Venus:** — *Possessing a symmetrical and beautiful body* = symmetrical = equal in length and breadth; beautiful = having limbs that are pleasing to the mind.
The rest is clear.

**Saturn:** — *Having coarse hair and limbs* = possessing stiff body hair and hard physical features. *Thick teeth* = large or stout teeth. The rest is easy to understand.

**Darkness (Rahu):** — *Devoted to intellect* = of an intellectual nature; *lazy* = prone to procrastination <note>original: "dirghasutri," literally 'long-threaded,' meaning someone who takes a long time to complete simple tasks</note>.

**The Purpose:** — At the time of birth, the strongest planet shapes the individual <term>Jataka: the person born/the newborn</term> according to its own likeness. || 53-59 ||

**The Sun (Surya):** — Majestic, of square build, dark-complexioned limbs, eyes yellow like honey, of a <term>Pitta: the fire/bile humor in Ayurvedic medicine</term> temperament, beautiful with sparse hair, and dominated by the <term>Sattva: the quality of purity, light, and goodness</term> guna. || 53 ||

**The Moon (Chandra):** — Of a wandering nature, sweet-spoken, wise, of auspicious gaze, possessing lovely and firm limbs, ever-intelligent, of a rounded body, and of a <term>Kapha and Vata: the water/phlegm and air/wind humors</term> temperament. || 54 ||

**Mars (Mangala):** — Of sinful gaze <note>referring to a harsh or piercing look</note>, youthful body, generous nature, of Pitta temperament, restless, slender-waisted, beautiful limbs of a reddish-fair hue, majestic, lustful, and of the <term>Tamas: the quality of darkness, inertia, and passion</term> guna. || 55 ||

**Mercury (Budha):** — Having a body green like *durva* grass, a clear speaker, slender body, master of the <term>Rajas: the quality of activity, passion, and energy</term> guna, very fond of joking and laughter, fond of <unclear>destruction/loss</unclear>, beautiful body, of Pitta-Kapha-Vata <note>Mercury is unique in balancing all three humors</note> temperament, possessing immediate majesty and wealth, and a learned scholar. || 56 ||

**Jupiter (Brihaspati):** — Having a large belly and tall body, yellow-complexioned, of Kapha temperament; endowed with all virtues, master of all scriptures, having tawny hair and eyes, of Sattvic nature, extremely intelligent, associated with great royal signs, and the bearer of Fortune (Lakshmi). || 57 ||

**Venus (Shukra):** — Having black and curly hair, dark-complexioned, endowed with beauty, symmetrical and pleasing limbs, an auspicious gaze, lustful, specifically of Vata-Kapha temperament, of Rajasic nature, the abode of Lakshmi, and a collection of happiness, strength, and virtues. || 58 ||

**Saturn (Shani):** — Having coarse body hair, a lean body, dark-complexioned like *durva* grass, of Kapha and Vata temperament, thick teeth, beautiful yellow eyes, of Tamasic intellect, and lazy. || 59 ||

### The Increase of Strength of Planets in Conjunction

> Saturn increases by the Sun, Mars by Saturn, Jupiter by Mars, the Moon by Jupiter ||
> Venus by the Moon, Mercury by the Teacher of Demons (Venus), and indeed the Moon is always increased by Mercury || 60 ||

Now the increase in strength of planets when in pairs is described. By the Sun, Saturn is always increased. In conjunction with the Sun, the usual faults of Saturn do not manifest; rather, at that time, Saturn becomes powerful. Similarly, by Saturn, the "Son of Earth" (Mars) is increased. The rest is clear. || 60 ||

From the Sun, Saturn; from Saturn, Mars; from Mars, Jupiter; from Jupiter, the Moon; from the Moon, Venus; from Venus, Mercury; and from Mercury, the Moon always increase. That is, the strength of Saturn increases with the Sun. The strength of Mars increases with Saturn. Likewise, the strength of Jupiter increases with Mars, the Moon by Jupiter, Venus by the Moon, Mercury by Venus, and the Moon's strength is increased by Mercury. || 60 ||

### Now, the Specific Positional Strength of Planets

> The Sun is perpetually powerful in its sign of exaltation, its own house, its own decanate <term>Drekkana: a 10-degree division of a sign</term>, its own hour, its own day, its own division, during the northern transit, in the middle of the day, at the moment of entering a sign, in a friend's division, and in the tenth house (meridian). || 61 ||
> The Moon is powerful in Cancer, in Taurus, in its own day, decanate, hour, and division; at the end of a sign, when aspected by benefics, at night, in the fourth house (happiness), and during the southern transit. ||
> If the Moon possesses all its digits <note>i.e., a Full Moon</note>, it is strong everywhere except at the junctions; if aspected by all the planets, it creates a "King's Yoga" <note>a planetary combination indicating royalty or high status</note> for men. || 62 ||

# Chapter 2: On the Names, Forms, Qualities, and Divisions of the Planets

**Mars is powerful in his own day, in his own Navamsha <note>a 1/9th division of a sign</note>, in his own Decan <note>a 10-degree division</note>, and in his own Varga <note>divisional charts</note>; likewise in the signs of Pisces, Scorpio, Aquarius, Capricorn, and Aries. He is strong at night, when in retrograde motion, in the southern direction, and at the beginning of a zodiac sign. Even in the signs of Pisces and Cancer, he bestows happiness.** (63)

**Mercury, the son of the Moon, is powerful in the houses of Virgo and Gemini, in his own day and divisional charts, and in Sagittarius—provided it is not Sunday. He is strong both day and night, during the Sun’s northern course <note>Uttarayana</note>, and in the middle of a sign. If he is in the Ascendant <note>Lagna</note>, he always grants an increase in fame and strength.** (64)

**Jupiter, the teacher of the gods, is powerful in Pisces, Scorpio, Sagittarius, and Cancer, in his own divisions and day, at midday, during the northern course, and in the middle of a sign. Even in Aquarius or his sign of debilitation <note>Capricorn</note>, he is strong. In the 1st, 4th, or 10th houses, he bestows great wealth.** (65)

**Venus is auspicious when in his exaltation, his own divisions, or his own day; in the middle of a sign; in the houses of enemies, the 12th house, or the house of younger siblings; in the 4th house; in the afternoon; in planetary war; in conjunction with the Moon; in retrograde motion; or when positioned in front of the Sun.** (66)

**Saturn is exceedingly powerful in Libra, Capricorn, and Aquarius; in the 7th house; during the southern course; in his own house or day; during his planetary period <note>Dasha</note>; at the end of a sign; in planetary combat; during the dark fortnight <note>waning moon</note>; and when in retrograde motion in any house.** (67)

**Rahu, the Lord of the Dragon’s Head, is powerful in Aries, Scorpio, Aquarius, Virgo, Taurus, and Cancer, and especially in the 10th house. Ketu, the Dragon’s Tail, is powerful at the end of Virgo, and in Taurus and Sagittarius; at night; and during the appearance of portents or comets.** (68)

**Planets endowed with the aforementioned strengths become weak if they have reached their "root" <note>Moola-trikona or specific debilitation points</note>. In such cases, the results described for house positions, yogas, and planetary periods will not fully manifest.** (69)

Now, the specific conditions for the strength of planets are explained:

**The Sun ( ☉ )**: He becomes powerful in his degree of exaltation ( ☉ 10° <note>Aries</note>), in his own sign ( ♌ <note>Leo</note>), in his own Decan, his own Hora <note>1/2 sign division</note>, his own day <note>Sunday</note>, his own Navamsha, during the northern course, at midday, at the beginning of a sign, in the first half of a friend's Navamsha, and in the 8th house from the Ascendant.

**The Moon**: She is powerful in Cancer (her own house), Taurus (exaltation), her own day (Monday), her own Decan, Hora, and Navamsha; at the end of a sign (the 9th Navamsha) if aspected by benefics; at night; in the 4th house from the Ascendant; and during the southern course (the six signs starting from Cancer). Regarding the mention of "the end of a sign," this excludes the junctions <note>Sandhi</note> of Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces. It is said: *Without the junctions—meaning the ends of Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces—the "Bearer of all Arts" (the Full Moon) is powerful everywhere.* If this Moon is aspected by all the planets wandering the sky, she creates a **King’s Union** <note>Rajayoga; a combination for high status</note> for those born. This means a Full Moon aspected by all planets creates a royal yoga.

**Mars (Ara)**: He becomes powerful on his own day (Tuesday), in his Navamsha, Decan, and Varga; when placed in the signs of Pisces, Scorpio, Aquarius, Capricorn, and Aries; at night; in retrograde; in the southern direction; and at the beginning of a sign. Likewise, in the 10th house from the Ascendant, even if in the sign of Cancer <note>his debilitation</note>, he bestows happiness to the native. This means he is auspicious in the 10th even in a weak sign. As it is said: *"He in whose 10th house Mars resides is born as the light of his lineage."*

**Mercury (Indusunu)**: He is powerful in Virgo and Gemini (his two houses), on his own day (Wednesday), in his own divisions, in Sagittarius, and at all times (day and night) except on Sundays (meaning Mercury is weak on the Sun's day). He is also strong during the northern course. If at the time of birth or a query he is in the Ascendant and in the middle of a sign (the 5th Navamsha), he always grants an increase in fame and strength.

**Jupiter (Surejya)**: He is powerful in Pisces, Scorpio, Sagittarius, and Cancer; in his own divisions and day (Thursday); at midday; during the northern course; in the middle of a sign (5th Navamsha); and in Aquarius. In the 1st, 4th, and 10th houses, even if in his sign of debilitation (Capricorn), he bestows much wealth. That is, Jupiter is beneficial in the 1st, 4th, and 10th houses even when debilitated. It is famously said:
> "What can all the other planets do, if Jupiter is placed in a quadrant <note>Kendra; the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note>?"

# With Commentary on the Jataka Parijata

**Venus**—In its sign of exaltation <note>Pisces</note>, in its own divisional charts <term>varga: sub-divisions of a sign that refine a planet's influence</term>, on its own day <note>Friday</note>, in the middle of a zodiac sign, in the 6th, 12th, 3rd, or 4th houses from the Ascendant, during the afternoon (the third part of the day), as well as in planetary combat <term>graha yuddha: when two planets are within one degree of each other</term>, when joined with the Moon, and when in retrograde motion while positioned ahead of the Sun—in these cases, it becomes auspicious.

**Saturn**—In the signs of Libra (its exaltation), Capricorn, and Aquarius (its own houses), in the 7th house from the Ascendant (its own direction), during the Southern Transit <note>the Sun's movement from Cancer through Sagittarius</note>, in its own decan <term>drekkana: a 10-degree division of a sign</term>, on its own day <note>Saturday</note>, during its own major period <term>dasha: a planetary time cycle</term>, in planetary combat at the end of a sign, and if it is retrograde during the dark fortnight <note>the waning moon phase</note>, it possesses superior strength in all houses and signs.

**The Lord of Serpents (Rahu)**—In the signs of Aries, Scorpio, Aquarius, Virgo, Taurus, and Cancer, and in the 10th house from the Ascendant, it becomes powerful.

**The Crested One (Ketu)**—In the signs of Virgo, Pisces, Taurus, and Sagittarius, at night, and during the appearance of an omen-comet <note>original: "utpata-ketu"</note>, it becomes strong. The definition of an "omen" <insert>utpata</insert> is stated by Varahamihira:

> "That which is a reversal of nature is generally termed an 'omen.' Whether occurring on the earth, in the sky, or in the heavens, they become progressively more grave."
> "Ketu is positioned twelve signs away from the Sun when the Sun is fifteen signs away from the constellation occupied by the Full Moon."

Regarding the aforementioned planetary strengths, a specific distinction is made: even if those planets possess the described types of strength, if they have "gone to the root" <note>meaning they are at the very beginning or junction of a house/sign</note>, they become powerless. Planets situated at the very beginning of a house are weak because that point has "zero degrees" <note>niranshatva</note> of that specific house's influence. Therefore, it should be understood that the predicted results for these planets in various houses, yogas, and time-periods will not fully manifest.

---

**The Sun**—Is always powerful in its exaltation sign, decan, hour <term>hora</term>, on Sunday, in its ninth-part division <term>navamsha</term>, during the Northern Transit, at midday, at the beginning of a sign, in a friend's ninth-part division, and in the 10th house from the Ascendant. || 61 ||

**The Moon**—Is strong in Cancer, Taurus, on its own day, decan, hour, and ninth-part division, at the end of a sign when aspected by <note>viewed by</note> benefic planets, at night, in the 4th house, and during the Southern Transit. A full-orbed and strong Moon, if not at a junction <term>bhasandhi: the unstable edge between signs</term> and aspected by all other planets, creates a "Royal Yoga" for humans. That is, one born under this alignment becomes a king. || 62 ||

**Mars**—Is strong on its own day, in its ninth-part and decan divisions, at night in Pisces, Scorpio, Aquarius, Capricorn, and Aries, when in retrograde, in the South, and at the beginning of a sign. It gives happiness in the 10th house even when in Cancer <note>where it is technically debilitated</note>. || 63 ||

**Mercury**—Is strong in Virgo and Gemini, on its own day, in its own divisions, in Sagittarius, during both day and night (always) except on Sundays, and during the Northern Transit. If it is in the middle of a sign and placed in the Ascendant, it always increases one's fame and strength. || 64 ||

**Jupiter**—Is strong when in Pisces, Scorpio, Sagittarius, and Cancer, in its own divisions and day, on other days during the Northern Transit, in the middle of a sign, and in Aquarius. Even in its sign of debilitation, if placed in the 1st, 4th, or 10th houses, it grants great wealth. || 65 ||

**Venus**—Is auspicious (strong) in its exaltation sign (Pisces), its own divisions and day, in the middle of a sign, in the 6th, 12th, 3rd, and 4th houses, in the afternoon, during planetary combat, when with the Moon, and when retrograde while ahead of the Sun. || 66 ||

**Saturn**—Is strong in Libra, Capricorn, and Aquarius, in the 7th house, during the Southern Transit, in its own decan and day (Saturday), during its major period, at the end of a sign, in combat, and if retrograde during the dark fortnight, it is powerful in every sign. || 67 ||

**Rahu**—Is powerful in Aries, Scorpio, Aquarius, Virgo, Taurus, and Cancer, and in the 10th house. **Ketu**—is strong in Pisces, Taurus, and Sagittarius, at night, during omens, and during the rising of a comet. || 68 ||

# Chapter 2: On the Names, Forms, Qualities, and Divisions of Planets

As previously described, even these powerful planets become fruitless when they are positioned at the very root of a house <note>The 'root' or Bhava-Madhya refers to the exact center or beginning point of an astrological house</note>. Therefore, in such houses, yogas <note>planetary combinations</note>, or during their major periods (dashas), they do not yield their full results. ॥ 69 ॥

### On the Downward and Upward Facing Directions of Planets

> Planets situated in the first six signs from the Sun are "Downward-facing."
> Those situated in the latter half from the Sun are "Upward-facing" and grant happiness and wealth. ॥ 70 ॥
> Positioned in the celestial sphere in order are Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, the Sun, Venus, Mercury, and the Moon.
> Among them, the one in the lowest position is stronger; Rahu stays at the head of the Earth's sphere. ॥ 71 ॥

Now, the order of the planets' positions is explained by defining their upward and downward orientations. <term>Dinesha</term> (Lord of the Day) means the Sun. Planets situated in the "first six" signs—meaning those present in the first half of the zodiacal circle relative to the Sun—are "Downward-facing." Similarly, planets situated in the "latter half" from the Sun—meaning those in the second half of the zodiacal circle—are "Upward-facing."

It should be understood as follows: In the houses where the Sun is located, specifically in the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 12th, 11th, and 10th houses from the Sun, the planets are "Downward-facing" and have diminished luster. This means they lose their brilliance due to their proximity to the Sun <note>This refers to the concept of combustion, where a planet's light is swallowed by the Sun's glare</note>. Conversely, planets in the other six houses—the 4th, 5th, 6th, 7th, 8th, and 9th from the Sun—are "Upward-facing" and possess great luster. Planets situated far from the Sun shine brilliantly; therefore, being "Upward-facing," they grant happiness and wealth. By implication, those that are "Downward-facing" are lusterless and should be considered inauspicious.

### On the Order of Planetary Positions

In the <term>Bhanam</term> (the signs and constellations), the order of the planets' orbits from highest to lowest is: Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Sun, Venus, Mercury, and the Moon. Among these, the one in the lowest position—the Moon—is the strongest of all. (This can be called <term>Kaksha-bala</term> or orbital strength). The idea is that their strength is determined by this order of position at birth.

### Description of Rahu's Position

Rahu is situated at the "head" of the <term>Mahimandala</term> (the Earth's sphere), meaning in its shadow. What is being said here is this: In the direction opposite to the Sun, the shadow of the Earth's sphere takes a conical shape; that itself is Rahu. As stated by the venerable Bhaskara: "Rahu resides in the shadow-orb of the Earth." ॥ 70-71 ॥

->Planets in the first six signs from the Sun are downward-facing, and planets<-
->in the second six signs from the Sun are upward-facing; these give happiness and wealth. ॥ 70 ॥<-

->In their respective orbits, the order is Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Sun, Venus, Mercury, and<-
->the Moon. Among these, the lowest (the Moon) is more powerful (it is appropriate to<-
->call this orbital strength). Rahu stays at the head (in the shadow) of the Earth's disk. ॥ 71 ॥<-

### The Failure of Planets in Specific Houses and Positions

> The Moon with the Sun; Mercury in the fourth; Jupiter in the house of children (5th); Mars in the house of family (2nd);
> Venus in the house of enemies (6th); and Saturn in the house of the spouse (7th);
> from the Ascendant, these all become fruitless. ॥ 72 ॥

Now it is explained where specific planets become "fruitless" (fail to give results). <term>The Moon with the Sun</term> means the Moon joined with the Sun in any sign becomes fruitless. On the New Moon day (Amavasya), the Sun and Moon join, and there the Moon becomes devoid of light. <term>Mercury</term> in the 4th house from the Ascendant. <term>Jupiter</term> in the 5th house. <term>Mars</term> in the 2nd house. <term>Venus</term> in the 6th house (the side of the enemy). <term>Saturn</term> in the 7th house (the spouse). In all these cases, the word "fruitless" applies. The meaning is that these planets, in these specific circumstances, do not produce any of their own good results. ॥ 72 ॥

->The Moon with the Sun, Mercury in the 4th house from the Ascendant, Jupiter in the 5th, Mars in the 2nd,<-
->Venus in the 6th, and Saturn in the 7th—these become fruitless. ॥ 72 ॥<-

### Now, the Neutralization of Faults.

> Mercury destroys the fault of Rahu; Saturn destroys the faults of both.
> Mars destroys the faults of three; Venus destroys the faults of four. || 73 ||
> Jupiter destroys the faults of five; the Moon destroys the faults of six.
> The Sun destroys seven faults, especially when in the Northern Transit. || 74 ||

Now the neutralizers of faults are described. The fault of Rahu = the fault arising from Rahu being in an unfavorable house, etc., is destroyed or neutralized by Mercury. This means if at the time of someone's birth Rahu is inauspicious, but Mercury is strong, then Mercury pacifies the fault created by Rahu. The same logic applies throughout. "Of both" = Saturn destroys the faults of both Mercury and Rahu. "Of three" = Mars <note>original: "Bhumija," son of the earth</note> destroys the faults of Rahu, Mercury, and Saturn. "Of four" = Venus <note>original: "Danavarcita," the one worshipped by demons</note> destroys the faults of Mars, Mercury, Saturn, and Rahu. "Of five" = Jupiter <note>original: "Devamantri," the counselor of the gods</note> destroys the faults of Mars, Mercury, Venus, Saturn, and Rahu. The Moon destroys the faults of six, and the Sun destroys "seven faults" = the faults created by all the planets. If the Sun is in the Northern Transit <term>Uttarayana: the period between the winter and summer solstices when the sun moves northward</term>, he especially destroys the faults of all the celestial wanderers. Because the Sun is exceedingly powerful in the Northern Transit, the specific term "especially" is used. || 73-74 ||

<note>The following paragraph is a Hindi summary of the Sanskrit verses above</note>
Mercury destroys the fault of Rahu. Saturn destroys the faults of these two. Mars destroys the faults of these three. Venus destroys the faults of these four. Jupiter destroys the faults of these five. The Moon destroys the destruction of these six. The Sun kills seven faults. If the Sun is in the Northern Transit, he destroys faults in a special capacity.

### Now, the Manner in which Planets Cause Affliction.

> The Sun always causes mental distress through fire-related diseases, increase in fever, inflammation, consumption, diarrhea, and other such ailments, as well as through kings, gods, Brahmins, and servants. || 75 ||
> The Moon causes distress through anemia, water-borne diseases, jaundice, chronic cold, and diseases caused by women, as well as through the groups of Goddess Kali, gods, and married women. || 76 ||
> The Son of Earth (Mars) quickly causes fear through swelling of the testicles, phlegm, weapons, fire, glandular sores, ulcers, and diseases born of poverty, as well as through the followers of Virashaiva and Bhairava. || 77 ||
> Mercury causes suffering through diseases of the private parts, stomach, eyes, and mouth, as well as wind-disorders, leprosy, sluggish digestion, and colic, and through the beloved servants and spirits of Vishnu. || 78 ||
> Jupiter causes sorrow and abdominal tumors through the curses of teachers, gods, and Brahmins. Venus causes fear through disorders involving women, urinary diseases, and through gods and people who provide one's favorite food. || 79 ||
> Saturn causes distress through poverty, one's own past karma, ghosts, thieves, and joint pains. Ketu causes distress through itching, smallpox, enemies, artificial or magical diseases, and through those of low caste who have abandoned proper conduct. || 80 ||
> Rahu <note>original: "Vidhuntuda," the piercer of the moon</note> causes great fear in men through epilepsy, smallpox, hanging, hunger, eye diseases, worms, the departed, and ghosts, as well as through death by strangulation, loss of appetite, and leprosy. || 81 ||

Now the types of afflictions caused by inauspicious planets are described—
The Sun <note>original: "Divakara"</note>—always causes mental impurity or distress through fire-diseases, increase in fever, burning, consumption (wasting), and diarrhea, as well as through kings, deities, Brahmins <note>original: "Avanideva," gods of the earth</note>, and servants. || 75 ||
The Moon—causes distress through anemia, water-disorders, jaundice, chronic cold, and diseases born of the seed, as well as through the groups of the Goddess Kali, the gods, and married women. || 76 ||

# Chapter 2: On the Names, Forms, Qualities, and Divisions of the Planets

**The Son of the Earth = Mars** — Through diseases arising from swollen testicles <note>original: "pīnabīja"</note>, phlegm, weapons, fire, eye-gland infections, ulcers, and poverty; as well as through **Heroes = warriors**, **the attendants of Shiva = skull-bearers**, and **Bhairavas = ghosts and spirits**, he **quickly = very soon** **causes fear = creates terror. || 77 ||**

**The Moon-born = Mercury** — Through secret diseases <note>referring to private parts</note>, stomach ailments, invisible (hidden area) diseases, wind disorders <note>Vata imbalances</note>, leprosy <note>or chronic skin conditions</note>, weak digestive fire, colic, and dysentery; as well as through **the Wise = scholars**, **the beloved servants of Vishnu = Vaishnava ascetics**, and **beings = ghosts**, he causes intense suffering. || 78 ||

**The Teacher of Indra = Jupiter** — Through the faults of curses—meaning the harsh words—of **the Preceptor = the teacher**, **the Gods**, **the Elders = superior persons**, and **the Earth-gods = Brahmins**, he causes grief, as well as abdominal tumors <note>original: "gulma"</note>.

**The Priest of the Demons = Venus** — Through urinary disorders <note>original: "prameha"</note> caused by female-related imbalances, and through fears caused by demons, non-divine spirits, and one's own desired women, he causes sorrow. || 79 ||

**The Son of the Sun = Saturn** — Through the fault of poverty, the fault of one's own past actions, ghosts, and thieves, along with joint diseases, he causes distress. **Ketu** — Through itching, smallpox <note>original: "masūri"</note>, diseases caused by enemies or one's own actions, and through the loss of one's proper conduct <note>original: "nijācāratyāgena"</note> and low-born groups or outcasts, he gives sorrow. || 80 ||

**The Devourer of the Moon = Rahu** — Through **Epilepsy = the falling sickness**, **Smallpox = the cool goddess <note>original: "śītalā"</note>**, **The Rope = binding or hanging**, **Infection = contagious disease**, **The Eye = eye diseases**, and worm infestations; through these diseases, and through ghosts, spirits, and demons, by hanging (or imprisonment), by loss of appetite, and by leprosy, he causes fear in men. || 81 ||

If the Sun is inauspicious, it always creates afflictions in the mind through fire-diseases, increased fever, burning sensations, consumption <note>tuberculosis</note>, diarrhea, and other such ailments, as well as through kings, gods, Brahmins, and servants. || 75 ||

If the Moon is inauspicious, it troubles one with anemia, water-disorders <note>edema</note>, jaundice, chronic cold, and other such diseases, as well as diseases arising from women and from the goddess Kali, demons, and groups of women. || 76 ||

If Mars is inauspicious, it quickly gives fear through swollen testicles, phlegm, weapons, fire, glandular diseases, wounds, and poverty-born ailments, as well as through warriors, the attendants of Shiva, and Bhairava-spirits. || 77 ||

If Mercury is inauspicious, it causes special suffering through secret, stomach, eye, wind, leprosy, weak digestion, colic, and malabsorption diseases, and through the beloved servants of Vishnu. || 78 ||

If Jupiter is corrupted, it causes grief and abdominal tumors through the curse-faults of the preceptor, gods, elders, and Brahmins. If Venus is unfavorable, there may be urinary disorders from female-related imbalances. Fear arises from demons and from one's own women. || 79 ||

If Saturn is inauspicious, it creates distress through the fault of poverty, one's own actions, ghosts, and thieves. If Ketu is corrupted, it gives distress through joint diseases, itching, smallpox, ringworm, diseases caused by enemies, the loss of one's religious conduct, and from low-born classes. || 80 ||

If Rahu is unfavorable, men face fear from epilepsy, smallpox, hanging, contagious diseases, eye diseases, worm infestations, ghosts, and spirits, and fear arises from imprisonment, loss of appetite, and leprosy. || 81 ||

### Now, the Time of the Ripening of Planetary Results in a Sign.

> The Sun and the Son of the Earth, Saturn and the Cold-rayed Moon, 
> Jupiter and the Minister of the Lord of the Demons <note>Venus</note>, give their results 
> when positioned at the beginning, the end, and the middle of a sign respectively. 
> The Son of the Stars <note>Mercury</note> provides results at all times. || 82 ||

Now he states the time when the planets' results ripen within a zodiac sign. **The Sun = Ravi**, **the Son of the Earth = Mars**, **Saturn and the Cold-rayed Moon = Saturn and the Moon**, **Jupiter and the Minister of the Lord of the Demons = Jupiter and Venus**—these planets give results when positioned at the beginning, end, and middle of a sign respectively. This is what is meant: the Sun and Mars give results at the beginning of a sign; Saturn and the Moon...

## From the Commentary on Jataka Parijata

At the end of a sign, Jupiter and Venus give results in the middle of a sign. Similarly, the son of the Star (the Moon) = Mercury, gives results at all times. Mercury produces the results of a sign throughout the entire duration of that sign. As stated by the teacher Ramacharya:
> "The Sun and Mars give results at the beginning of a sign; Venus and Jupiter in the middle; the son of the Moon (Mercury) always; and the Moon and Saturn at the end." <note>original: "राश्यादिगौ रविकुजौ फलदौ..."</note>

### On the Worship of the Lords of the Elements for Diseases Born of the Elements

**For the pacification of all diseases born from the provocation of a particular element <term>Dhatu: the physical constituents of the body like blood, marrow, etc.</term>, one should quickly worship the Lord of that element through recitation of mantras, water offerings, fire sacrifices, and charity. Thus, with minds freed from the fear of disease and grief, all men shall be endowed with happiness, fame, and strength. || 83 ||**

Now the remedy is described. For the pacification = the removal of all those diseases (previously mentioned) produced = arisen from the provocation of a specific planet's element, one should worship the Lord of that element = the planet that governs the element causing the disease. This is done through recitation (chanting the specific planet's mantra), water offerings <term>Tarpana: a ritual pouring of water</term>, fire offerings <term>Homa</term>, and charity. By doing so quickly = speedily, all men become those whose minds/inner selves are liberated from the grief caused by the fear of disease. They become endowed with happiness, fame, and strength. The meaning is that by properly worshipping the afflicted planet, one is freed from disease and quickly prospers in happiness. || 83 ||

By whichever element's provocation diseases occur, for their pacification and to please their Lord, through swift mantra-recitation, water offerings, fire sacrifices, and charity, all men—becoming free from disease, grief, fear, and anxiety—are joined with happiness, fame, and strength. (From the Su. Sha. Kar) || 83 ||

### On the Determination of the Stages of Planets, such as Infancy

**Infant, Youth, Adult, Old, and Dead—these are the stages in an odd sign in sequence. By dividing the thirty degrees <note>A zodiac sign consists of 30 degrees</note>, these same stages are to be applied in reverse for even signs. || 84 ||**

Now the stages of the planets, such as infancy, are determined. In an odd sign <term>Vishama-rashi: Aries, Gemini, Leo, etc.</term>, the five stages are known in order as Infant, Youth, Adult, Old, and Dead. In an even sign <term>Sama-rashi: Taurus, Cancer, Virgo, etc.</term>, by <unclear>reversal</unclear> = in the opposite order, the five stages starting from "Dead" occur. Now, a doubt arises as to how the division of these stages in a single sign is structured. It is said: the stages are made by dividing the thirty degrees. When the five segments are created by equal division of the thirty degrees, then each segment consists of six degrees. In odd signs, the first six degrees are "Infant." The next six degrees are "Youth." Then "Adult." Then "Old." Then "Dead." In an even sign, the five stages occur in the order: Dead, Old, Adult, Youth, and Infant. As stated by Parasara <note>A legendary sage and father of Vedic astrology</note>:

> "The Infant stage is declared for the first six degrees in an odd sign, then Youth, then Adult, then Old, and then Dead in sequence. The stages of the planets are said to be the opposite in an even sign."

The verse regarding the purpose/effect is by the same author:

> "The Infant stage gives little result; the Youth stage gives half; the Adult stage gives full results for men; the <unclear>Senior</unclear> or Old stage gives weak results, and the stage called Dead gives no result (or bad results)." || 84 ||

In an odd sign, planets reach the stages of Infant, Youth, Adult, Old, and Dead within the thirty degrees. That is, up to 6 degrees is Infant; after 6 up to 12 degrees is Youth; after 12 up to 18 degrees is Adult; after 18 up to 24 degrees is Old; and after that is the Dead stage. In an even sign, the stages of the planets are: first Dead, then Old, then Adult, then Youth, and finally Infant, each lasting for 6 degrees. || 84 ||
