## Now, the States of Waking and Others

> Scholars say a planet is "Awake" when in its exaltation or its own division.
> It is "Dreaming" in a friend's division, and "Sleeping" in a debilitated or enemy's division. || 85 ||

Now the waking and other states of the planets are described. Being in the degree of exaltation <note>the point where a planet is strongest</note> or in its own <term>Navamsha</term> <note>a 1/9th divisional chart used for fine-tuning strength</note> is called "Awake" (<term>Jagrat</term>). If a planet is in its exaltation or its own division, it is in the "Awake" state. Being in a friend's division (<term>Suhrid-navamsha</term>) indicates the "Dreaming" state (<term>Svapna</term>). Being in the degree of debilitation <note>the point where a planet is weakest</note> or an enemy's division is called "Sleeping" (<term>Supta</term>). If a planet is in its fall or an enemy's division, it becomes "Sleeping." || 85 ||

<gloss>Scholars say planets are awake in their exaltation and own division. Planets in a friend's division are in a dreaming state. In debilitation or an enemy's division, they are called sleeping.</gloss>

## Now, the Timing of Results Given by Planets

> A planet in a "Head-first" rising sign gives results at the start of its period.
> In a "Back-first" rising sign, at the end; and in a "Both-ways" sign, always. || 86 ||

Now the timing of when planets give their results based on their zodiac signs is described. A planet situated in "Head-first" (<term>Shirshodaya</term>) signs <note>Signs like Leo or Virgo that rise head-first on the horizon</note> gives results at the beginning of its <term>Dasha</term> <note>planetary time period</note>. A planet in a "Back-first" (<term>Prishthodaya</term>) sign <note>Signs like Aries or Taurus that rise tail-first</note> gives results at the end of its period. Likewise, a planet in a "Both-ways" (<term>Ubhayodaya</term>) sign—specifically Pisces—gives results "always," meaning throughout the entire period. As stated in the *Brihat Jataka*:

> "In Back-first, Both-ways, and Head-first signs, the results of the periods are given at the end, middle, and beginning respectively." <note>original: "पृष्ठोभयकोदयश्चेद्गान्तस्त्वेऽन्तः प्रथमेषु पाकदाः"</note>

In this specific quote, a difference is seen regarding the "Both-ways" sign. Sage Garga also says:
> "The results are given at the beginning, end, and middle in Head-first, Back-first, and Both-ways signs. The lord of the period should be judged based on its position at the start of the period." || 86 ||

<gloss>Planets in Head-first signs give results at the start of the period. Those in Back-first signs give results at the end. Those in Both-ways signs give results throughout.</gloss>

> the divisions of planetary actions, forms, and qualities are proclaimed by the grace of the planets. || 87 ||

# Chapter 3: On Non-Human Births

Now, the third chapter is explained. In this chapter, the subjects are first non-human births <note>original: *viyonijanma*; literally "birth from a different womb," referring to animals, plants, or minerals</note>, then conception, and the rules of birth. First, it is explained what is meant by "non-human birth." The term "non-human birth" refers to the origin of all creatures other than humans, such as animals, birds, and both moving and stationary living things. In this chapter, the method of non-human birth is first described, as stated in the *Horasastra* of the teacher Varahamihira—

-> When the cruel planets are very strong and the gentle planets are weak, and a neuter planet is in a cardinal house or aspecting it, <-
-> one should declare a creature of a form similar to the twelfth-part occupied by the Moon, provided that sign is designated as non-human. ॥ 1 ॥ <-

"By the cruel planets" <note>original: *krūragrahaiḥ*</note> means: at the time of birth or at the time of a query <note>a branch of astrology where a chart is cast for the moment a question is asked</note>, the "cruel" planets—the Sun, Mars, Mercury when joined with malefic planets, Saturn, and the waning Moon—are endowed with great strength. The "gentle" planets <note>original: *saumyaiḥ*; the benefics</note>—the auspicious planets—are weak and devoid of strength. "In a neuter" <note>original: *klībe*</note> refers to a neuter planet (either Saturn or Mercury) being in a "cardinal house" <note>term: *catuṣṭaya*; the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses of a horoscope</note>. Or, by the aspect of that: when the strong malefics and weak benefics are present and the neuter planet aspects the Ascendant <note>term: *lagna*; the rising sign</note>—this is the second combination. Then, one should declare a non-human creature of a form "similar to the twelfth-part" <note>term: *dvādaśāṃśa*; a 2.5-degree division of a zodiac sign</note> occupied by the Moon. If that twelfth-part is designated as non-human (other than human), then one should speak thus; otherwise, it is different. If the Moon is in the twelfth-part of Aries, one should predict the birth of a sheep or goat; if in Taurus, a bull or buffalo; if in Leo, a lion or tiger; and so on everywhere. Thus it is said in the *Saravali*:

> "When the cruel planets are joined with great strength and the gentle ones are weak, and the Moon is in a non-human division, 
> and a neuter planet is in a cardinal house or aspects the rising sign, a non-human birth occurs. 
> At the time of conception, birth, or a query, the creature will be similar to the twelfth-part 
> in which the Moon or the Ascendant is situated."

**Notes—** The number of small creatures should be known through the twelfth-parts within the Ascendant. ॥ 1 ॥

In this third chapter, the description of non-human birth is given first. By the word "non-human" <note>original: *viyoni*</note>, one should understand animals, birds, insects, aquatic creatures, trees, plants, etc., other than humans.

At the time of a query or birth, one should declare a non-human birth of the same species as the twelfth-part in which the Moon is currently located. For example, if the Moon is in the twelfth-part of a four-footed sign, it is a quadruped; if in an aquatic sign, an aquatic creature. This applies everywhere. Even then, specifically according to the signs: in the twelfth-part of Aries, sheep, goats, etc.; in Taurus, bulls, buffaloes, etc. Thus it is known everywhere. This consideration should only be made if the twelfth-part occupied by the Moon is non-human; otherwise, one should declare a human birth. In the stated condition, if malefic planets are strong, auspicious planets are weak, and a neuter planet is in a cardinal house, it is the first combination; if malefic planets are strong, auspicious planets are weak, and a neuter planet aspects the Ascendant, it is the second combination for a non-human birth. (Commentary by S. S. Kar) ॥ 1 ॥

-> The malefics are strong and in their own divisions, while the benefics are in the divisions of others and weak. <-
-> If the Ascendant is also designated as non-human, one should also predict a non-human birth here. ॥ 2 ॥ <-

Now another method for knowing non-human birth is stated. "Strong" means powerful; "malefics" are the previously mentioned cruel planets; "in their own divisions" <note>original: *svabhāgagāḥ*</note> means situated in their own ninth-part <note>term: *navāṃśa*; a 3-degree 20-minute division</note>. "Benefics" are the auspicious planets; "in the divisions of others" <note>original: *pārakye*</note> means existing in the ninth-part of another planet and being "weak" or without strength. If the Ascendant at that time is also non-human (Aries, Taurus, Cancer, Scorpio, etc.), then in this combination also, one should predict a non-human birth similar to the twelfth-part occupied by the Moon. ॥ 2 ॥

When malefic planets are in their own ninth-parts, auspicious planets are weak and situated in the ninth-parts of others, and the Ascendant is a non-human sign (Aries, Taurus, Cancer, Scorpio, etc.), then one should declare a non-human birth according to the twelfth-part of the Moon. ॥ 2 ॥

<header>Chapter on Non-Human Births || 3 ||</header>

# Aries is the head; Taurus the face and throat; the others are the feet and shoulders, the back, the chest, and the sides.
# The belly, the anus, the genitals and testicles, the haunches, and the tail—these are the limbs of the quadruped. || 3 ||

Now the placement of the zodiac signs <term>Rashi: the twelve signs of the zodiac</term> on the bodies of non-humans is explained. Among non-humans, quadrupeds (animals) are primary, so the signs are mapped onto their limbs. Aries is the head. Taurus is the face and throat—face meaning the mouth, and throat meaning the neck. The others, starting from Gemini, follow in order as the feet, shoulders, and so on. For clarity, one should view a diagram of a quadruped marked with the zodiac signs. The purpose of this is: strength and health are found in the limb associated with a beneficial planet, while wounds or injuries occur in the limb associated with a malefic planet. || 3 ||

->**Because of the prominence of quadrupeds in non-human births—**<-

The division of zodiac signs in an animal's body is as follows: Aries is the head, Taurus the mouth and neck, Gemini the front legs and shoulders, Cancer the back, Leo the chest, Virgo the two sides, Libra the belly, Scorpio the anus, Sagittarius the two hind legs, Capricorn the penis and scrotum, Aquarius the haunches (both sides of the rump), and Pisces is the tail. || 3 ||

# One should declare the colors in a non-human birth based on the rising sign's subdivision, or from the conjunction and aspect of planets.
# Having observed similar influences, state the number; and by the planets situated in the seventh house, state the stripes on the back. || 4 ||

Now the knowledge of the animal's color is explained. One should state the colors in a non-human birth based on the rising sign's subdivision <term>Navamsha: a one-ninth division of a zodiac sign used for detailed analysis</term> or from the conjunction and aspect of planets on the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</term>. This means: whatever planet is situated in the Ascendant, its color should be assigned to the animal. If no planet is present, the color of the planet that aspects (looks at) the Ascendant should be stated. If the Ascendant has no planetary conjunction or aspect, then the color of the sign belonging to the specific Navamsha division of the Ascendant should be used. "Having observed similar" means that if the Ascendant is joined or aspected by many planets, many colors should be mentioned; among them, the color of the strongest planet will be the most dominant. "By those in the seventh" means the planets located in the seventh house from the Ascendant; one should state the number of stripes or markings on the animal's back based on them. As stated by Kalyanavarman <note>A famous 6th-century Indian astrologer, author of the Saravali</note>:

> "By the signs rising at birth, or by their subdivisions, or by the planets conjoined or aspecting;
> One should declare the respective color, or a mark or wound on the body.
> From the combination of the planet and its subdivision, know the colors...
> Those in the seventh house indicate stripes on the back equal to their own color," etc.

**Notes—Both of the above verses are found in the Brihat Jataka <note>The foundational 6th-century text on Vedic astrology by Varahamihira</note>. || 4 ||**

# With the Commentary of Jataka Parijata

The color of the creature <note>original: "viyoni" - referring to non-human births such as animals</note> or a lost object should be determined by the planet situated in the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the time of birth</term>, according to the 19th verse of the 2nd chapter. If no planet is in the Ascendant, use the color of the planet that aspects <note>looks upon</note> the Ascendant. If the Ascendant is neither occupied nor aspected by any planet, use the color of the Ascendant's <term>Navamsha: a one-ninth subdivision of a zodiac sign used for fine-tuning predictions</term>. If multiple planets are in the Ascendant, multiple colors are indicated; among them, the color of the strongest planet will be predominant. If the Navamsha of the Ascendant belongs to the sign occupied by its own lord, use that color alone (discarding the previous rules). Lines or markings on the back of the creature are determined by the planet situated in the seventh house. || 4 ||

->If the lords of the 4th and 1st houses are in the 1st and 4th houses, a four-footed birth occurs.<-
->If the lord of the Ascendant or the 4th house is joined with Rahu or Ketu, it is the birth of a beast. || 5 ||<-

Now, the birth of four-footed animals is described. "Sukhangeshau" means the lords of the 4th and 6th houses; "Dehambugau" means situated in the 1st and 4th houses (meaning the 6th lord in the 1st and the 4th lord in the 4th). In such a case, a "Chatushpada" or four-footed birth occurs. This is one combination. The second combination is: if the "Dehesho" (Lord of the Ascendant) or the "Sukhape" (Lord of the 4th house) is joined with "Ahiketu" (Rahu and Ketu respectively), the birth of a beast should be predicted. || 5 ||

If the Lord of the 4th and the Lord of the Ascendant are placed in the Ascendant and the 4th house, a four-footed animal is born. If the Lord of the Ascendant or the Lord of the 4th is joined with Rahu or Ketu, know it to be the birth of an animal. || 5 ||

### On the birth of specific animals through the aspect of specific planets.

->If aspected by Venus, a cow is born; if joined or aspected by Saturn, a buffalo.<-
->If joined with Rahu or Ketu, a sheep/goat; if with a malefic, other animals. || 6 ||<-

If the Ascendant of the time is aspected by Venus, the birth of a cow should be declared; the rest is clear. || 6 ||
If Venus aspects the Ascendant, a cow is born; if Saturn is joined or aspects, a buffalo; if Rahu or Ketu are joined, a sheep or goat; if joined by malefic planets (Sun, Mars, waning Moon, or Mercury joined with malefics), know it to be the birth of other animals. || 6 ||

### On the planetary positions causing the birth of land or water creatures.

->If the Ascendant is a bird-Drekkana, or joined by a strong planet in the last Navamsha,<-
->Or in the Navamsha of Mercury, birds of land or water are born from the aspect of Saturn and Moon. || 7 ||<-
->When the Ascendant, Moon, Jupiter, and Sun are weak, the birth of trees occurs; the distinction between land and water types is made by the Navamsha.<-
->As many planets as there are in land or water signs, so many trees of those types are produced. || 8 ||<-

Now the knowledge of bird births is stated. "Khaga" (bird): If the Ascendant is a "Pakshi-Drekkana" <note>Bird-decante: specific 10-degree segments of Gemini, Leo, Libra, or Aquarius</note> (refer to the Drekkana chapter of Brihat Jataka), or if the last Navamsha is rising in the Ascendant joined by a strong planet, or if the Ascendant is in the Navamsha of Mercury (Virgo or Gemini) and joined by a strong planet—in these three combinations, through the aspect or conjunction of Saturn and the Moon, birds of land or water are born. In all three combinations, if aspected or joined by Saturn, they are land birds; if aspected or joined by the Moon, they are water birds. As stated in the *Saravali*:

> "If a bird-decante rises, joined by a strong planet, or in the final Navamsha, or in a Navamsha of Mercury, birds of land or water are born from the aspect of Saturn and the Moon." || 7 ||

### Now the knowledge of the birth of trees is stated.

When the Ascendant, Moon, Jupiter, and Sun are all devoid of strength, the birth of trees should be predicted. Regarding the decision of whether they are water-born or land-born: the distinction is made by the Navamsha. <unclear>Joined with the lord of the Navamsha</unclear> <unclear>the distinction between water and land</unclear>—strength in its own field, the "Tarumukha" or origin of the tree. <unclear>This means if a movable Navamsha rises in the Ascendant, water-born trees</unclear> <unclear>should be declared.</unclear> Otherwise, they are land-born.

<header>Chapter on Non-Human Births || 3 ||</header>

# Chapter on Non-Human Births || 3 ||

Now, he describes the number of trees—**The planet that is the lord of the land or water sign** = Whichever planet is the lord of the land-sign or water-sign, however many signs it is distant from the Ascendant <note>Lagna</note> to the sign it occupies, that is the number of trees produced from land or water respectively. || 8 ||

If a bird-decante <note>original: "Dreshkana"; a 10-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign</note> is in the Ascendant (the 2nd of Gemini, 1st of Leo, 2nd of Libra, or 1st of Aquarius), then one should predict the birth of a bird (1).

If the Navamsha <note>a 1/9th division of a sign</note> of a Moveable sign (Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn) is in the Ascendant and is occupied by a strong planet, one should predict the birth of a bird (2).

If the Navamsha of Mercury (Gemini or Virgo) is in the Ascendant and contains a strong planet, one should predict the birth of a bird (3).

In these three combinations, if there is an aspect or conjunction with Saturn, it is a land-dwelling bird; if with the Moon, it is a water-dwelling bird. || 7 ||

The method for knowing the birth of trees is this: if at the time of birth the Ascendant, Moon, Jupiter, and Sun are all weak, then predict the birth of a tree. If the Ascendant-Navamsha is a water sign, it is a water-tree; if a land sign, it is a land-tree. The number of trees is equal to the number of signs the lord of the land or water sign is away from the Ascendant. Multiply this number by three if the planet is in its exaltation or in retrograde motion <note>original: "vakra-gati"</note>, and double it if the planet is in its own Vargottama <note>occupying the same sign in both the main chart and the Navamsha</note>, Navamsha, or sign. (According to the author of Su. Sha.) || 8 ||

->Now, the specific types of trees produced by the Sun and other planets.<-

> The Sun produces trees with internal strength; the Son of the Sun (Saturn) produces ugly or useless trees.
> The Moon produces trees full of milky sap; Mars produces those abounding in thorns.
> Jupiter and Mercury produce fruitful and fruitless trees respectively; Venus produces flowering trees.
> The Moon again produces smooth/oily trees; the Son of the Earth (Mars) produces bitter-tasting shrubs. || 9 ||

> A benefic planet in a malefic sign produces a beautiful tree in poor soil; the opposite occurs otherwise.
> As many Navamshas as the planet has moved away from its own, so many trees of that specific nature are born. || 10 ||

Regarding what was said previously about the divisions made by the Navamsha, he now explains the specific knowledge based on the lord of the Navamsha. The Sun = if the Sun is the lord of the Navamsha, it produces trees with "internal essence" <note>original: "antahsaran"</note> = those whose strength or core is inside (such as the Shishpa tree, etc.). The Son of the Sun = Saturn produces "unfortunate" <note>original: "durbhagan"</note> = ugly or stunted trees. The Moon <note>original: "Tuhinakirana"</note> produces those "endowed with milk" = sap-bearing trees like the Banyan. Mars produces "rich in thorns" = thorny trees like the Khadira. Jupiter and Mercury = produce fruitful and fruitless trees. Jupiter produces those that bear fruit; Mercury produces those that are fruitless and never bear fruit. Venus produces flowering trees like the Champaka. The Moon <note>original: "Indu"</note> again produces "smooth" trees like the Deodar and others. The Son of the Earth = Mars also produces "bitter shrubs" = trees with a bitter taste. The word "again" <note>original: "bhuyah"</note> is used here because both the Moon and Mars are credited with two types of production. || 9 ||

Now he describes the birth and number of trees based on the nature of benefic and malefic planets. If a benefic planet (the lord of the land or water sign) is in a malefic sign, it produces a beautiful tree but in "bad ground" = born in poor soil. Otherwise = if a malefic planet is in a benefic sign, it produces the opposite—an ugly tree in a good location. Thus it is established: "A benefic in a benefic sign produces a beautiful tree in good soil; a malefic in a malefic sign produces an ugly tree in poor soil." Now, however many Navamshas the lord of the land/water sign has moved from its own Navamsha into another, there will be that many trees of that specific type (corresponding to the nature of the Navamsha lord). As Kalyanvarma says:

> "As many Navamshas as have passed into another from its own, so many trees,
> whether land-born or water-born, should be declared according to the previous calculation." || 10 ||

### Now, the Rules for Impregnation (Nisheka)

> When Mars and the Moon are the cause, menstruation occurs every month. When the Moon (the "cool-rayed one") enters the "afflicted signs" <note>the 1st, 2nd, 4th, 5th, 7th, 8th, 9th, or 12th houses from the woman's natal Moon</note> and is aspected by Mars, it is the time for conception. Otherwise, when the Moon is in a different position and aspected by a masculine benefic planet, the woman unites with the man. || 11 ||

Now the rules for impregnation are explained. Since the menstrual period is primary, the nature of the menses is defined first, followed by the timing of the couple's union. For women, every month (*pratimāsam*) the menses (*ārtavam*) occurs. The cause (*hetu*) is Mars (*Kuja*) and the Moon (*Indu*). Mars and the Moon are the instruments of the blood that flows from the secret parts of women every month. Because the Moon is of the Water element and Mars is of the Fire element; the water itself is the blood, and the fire is the bile (*pitta*). When the blood is stirred by bile, it transforms into the form of menses. As stated by **Kalyanavarman** <note>Author of the Saravali, a famous 10th-century astrology text</note>:

> "The Moon is water and Mars is fire; water is the blood and fire is the bile. Thus, when the blood is agitated by bile, menstruation begins in women."

Now, the menses suitable for conception is defined. When the Moon (*anuṣṇadīdhitau*) enters an "afflicted sign" (*pīḍarkṣaṃ*)—which means a non-upachaya sign <note>The 3rd, 6th, 10th, and 11th houses are 'Upachaya' (improving) signs; all others are non-upachaya</note> relative to the woman's birth sign—and is aspected by Mars, the menses becomes capable of conceiving a child. However, this excludes children, the elderly, the sick, and the barren. As it is said:

> "If the Moon is in the lower signs (non-upachaya) and is seen by the son of the Earth (Mars), then the menses is fit for conception; this is not desired for the barren, the old, the sick, or the very young."

Next, the possibility of union with a man is stated. When the Moon is situated otherwise (*ato’nyathāsthe*)—meaning in an Upachaya sign relative to the man's birth sign—and is aspected by a masculine benefic planet (*śubhapuṅgrahekṣite*)—specifically Jupiter (*Guru*)—the woman (*kāminī*) in her fertile period unites with the man (*nareṇa*). Only such a planetary combination constitutes a union of the couple suitable for conception. As it is said:

> "If the Moon is in an Upachaya house and is aspected by Jupiter, one should predict the union of woman and man; otherwise, not at all."

This consideration of union should be performed when the menses is purified (on the fourth day).

> "When the woman has bathed at the end of her period, if the Moon is in an Upachaya sign and is seen by a strong Jupiter, then union with the husband occurs."

The author himself will state further ahead:

> "The odd nights here are unfit for impregnation; the even nights are praised as givers of sons." || 11 ||

<header>Chapter on Non-Human and Human Births || 3 ||</header>

# Chapter on Non-Human and Human Births || 3 ||

Blood flows from the wombs of women for three days every month. This is called <term>Rajodarshana</term> <note>menstruation; literally "the appearance of the menses"</note>. The causes of menstruation are Mars and the Moon, because Mars represents the fire element and the Moon is watery. If, during menstruation, the Moon is not in an <term>Upachaya</term> <note>houses of increase: 3, 6, 10, and 11</note> position from the woman's birth sign, but is instead in the 1st, 2nd, 4th, 5th, 7th, 8th, 9th, or 12th houses, and Mars views it with a full aspect in the current transit, then such menses are capable of sustaining a fetus. If the Moon is in an Upachaya sign but Mars does not aspect it, the menses of that time are fruitless. If the Moon is in the man's Upachaya sign and Jupiter views it with a full aspect, and if the man and woman unite at that time, a conception will certainly occur. However, this consideration does not apply to barren women, children, the elderly, or eunuchs. || 11 ||

->Just as the setting sign <note>the 7th house</note> meets its pair, so should the nature of the union be described.<-
->If the setting sign is aspected by or joined with malefic planets, it is with anger; if with benefics, it is with playfulness and laughter. || 12 ||<-

Now, having understood the time for conception, the author explains the method of knowing the nature of the sexual union. The "setting sign" refers to the seventh sign from the <term>Adhana Lagna</term> <note>the ascendant at the moment of conception</note> or the <term>Prashna Lagna</term> <note>the ascendant at the moment of a query</note>. Just as the union occurs in the "womb" of the seventh sign, so should the nature of the <term>Mithunaprayoga</term> <note>the act of sexual union</note> be described. One should say that the union in this conception was performed in that very manner. If the seventh sign is a "four-legged" sign <note>quadruped signs like Aries or Taurus</note>, then the union was like that of quadrupeds. If it is a water-dwelling sign, then it was of that kind; the union should always be described as being similar to the nature of the sign. Furthermore, he describes whether the union was with conflict or love. In the "setting" (the seventh sign from the <term>Nisheka Lagna</term> <note>the ascendant of the consummation</note>), if it is aspected by or joined with "non-virtuous" planets (malefics), the union is "with anger" (accompanied by quarreling). If the setting sign is aspected by or joined with "desired" planets (benefics), the union is "with playfulness and laughter" (accompanied by love). Otherwise, it is ordinary. Thus it is said in the *Saravali* <note>a classic 8th-century astrological text by Kalyanavarman</note>:

> "Just as the two-legged and other signs from the ascendant perform union in the seventh,
> In that same way, the conception of men should be commanded.
> When the setting sign is joined or aspected by inauspicious planets, the village-act <note>sex</note> is with anger and strife.
> When with benefics, the union is gentle, as described in the *Vatsyayana Sutras* <note>the Kama Sutra</note>." || 12 ||

One should describe the union as being similar to the seventh sign from the query or the conception ascendant. If Aries is in the seventh, the union is like a goat. If Taurus is there, the union is like a bull. In this way, describe the union for the subsequent signs when they fall in the seventh. If malefic planets are in the seventh or aspect that house, the union is "with anger" (joined with conflict), and if benefic planets are in the seventh or aspect the seventh house, the union is with love and playfulness. || 12 ||

->When the Sun, Moon, Venus, and Mars are in their own divisions, or when Jupiter is in a trine or the ascendant,<-
->Conception indeed occurs even for those who seem seedless; how then could it be fruitless for the powerful? || 13 ||<-

Now he describes the combinations for the possibility of pregnancy. "Sun, Moon, Venus, and Mars in their own divisions" means they are in their own <term>Navamsha</term> <note>the 1/9th divisional chart, used to determine the hidden strength of planets</note>. Wherever these four planets are in a sign, if they have reached their own Navamsha, then certainly a child (offspring) will be formed in the womb. This is one combination. Or, he gives another combination: "When Jupiter is in a trine or the ascendant"—if Jupiter is in the 1st, 5th, or 9th house, then also a child is born. Here, in the absence of the first full combination, it is required for the Sun and Venus to be in the man's Upachaya signs and the Moon and Mars to be in the woman's Upachaya signs, while also being in their own Navamshas, for the possibility of offspring. Thus it was said by Varaha <note>Varahamihira, the 6th-century polymath</note> in the *Svalpa Jataka*:

> "When for men, the Sun and Venus are strong, in their own houses or Upachaya signs,
> And for women, Mars and the Moon are likewise, then the birth of a fetus occurs." ||

# Section on Pregnancy with Questions

### The Combination for Conception (Garbhayoga)

<insert>
He describes the failure of these combinations. These combinations for the birth of offspring are fruitless and ineffective for men and women who lack vitality <note>original: "vīrya," referring to reproductive essence or potency</note> (impotent individuals). Just as the rays of the moon <note>original: "himāṃśoścandrasya," the cool-rayed one</note> are useless to those who are blind from birth, even though the rays are present, so it is here—this is the analogy. Since the birth of offspring is only possible through the union of menses and semen <note>original: "rajo-vīryābhyām"</note>, the fruitlessness for those lacking these is entirely appropriate.
</insert>

The method for knowing whether there is a pregnancy or not is as follows: If at the time of the query <note>the moment the astrologer is asked</note> or the time of conception, the Sun, Moon, Jupiter, and Mars are in their own Navamshas <term>Navamsha: A one-ninth division of a zodiac sign used for fine-tuned analysis</term>, then pregnancy is certain. If this is not the case, but in the man's Upachaya houses (3rd, 6th, 10th, or 11th) the Sun and Venus are in their own Navamshas, then also say pregnancy is possible. Alternatively, if Mars and the Moon are in their own Navamshas in the woman's Upachaya houses, then also say pregnancy is possible. Or, if Jupiter is in the fifth, ninth, or the first house (Ascendant), then also say pregnancy is possible. All these combinations <note>yogas</note> are fruitless for an impotent person, just as the beauty of the moon's rays is useless to a blind man. || 13 ||

-> If at the time of conception, Mars and Saturn are in the seventh house from the Sun and Moon respectively, they cause disease for the man and woman. If they are in the twelfth and second houses, they cause death; similarly, if they are joined with one and aspected by the other, they are intended for death. || 14 || <-

Now he describes the auspicious and inauspicious effects for the couple from the time of conception until delivery. If at the time of conception, Mars and Saturn <note>original: "kujārkajau," the son of the Earth and the son of the Sun</note> are in the seventh house <note>original: "smaragau"</note> from the Sun and Moon respectively, then they provide disease to the man and woman. Mars and Saturn in the seventh from the Sun cause disease to the man. Saturn and Mars in the seventh from the Moon cause disease to the woman. Similarly, if they are in the twelfth and second houses: if Mars and Saturn are on both sides of the Sun, it leads to the death of the man; if Mars and Saturn are on both sides of the Moon, it leads to the death of the woman. Furthermore, if the Sun is joined with one of Mars or Saturn and aspected by the other, it is intended for the death of the man; likewise, if the Moon is joined with one and aspected by the other, it is intended for the death of the woman. In this regard, it should be understood everywhere that the stronger planet causes the disease etc., in its own month.
For example—Here (1) Sun, Mars, Saturn = for the man. Moon, Mars, Saturn = for the <unclear>woman</unclear>.
Here (2) Sun, Saturn, Mars and Mars, Saturn = for the man.
Moon, Saturn, Mars and Saturn, Mars = for the woman. || 14 ||

# Chapter on Non-Human Births and Others || 3 ||

If Mars and Saturn are present <note>in the relevant astrological houses</note>, they cause the death of the man in their respective months. # Chapter on Non-Human Births and Others || 3 ||

The Sun and Venus are designated as father and mother during the day; Saturn and the Moon are so designated at night. For the paternal uncle and maternal aunt, the reverse applies. These are auspicious if they are situated in odd and even signs respectively. || 15 ||

Now, the author describes the auspicious and inauspicious effects on the father and others based on the time of conception <term>Nisheka: the act of impregnation or the first ritual of conception</term>. If conception occurs during the day, the Sun represents the father and Venus represents the mother. If conception occurs at night, Saturn represents the father and the Moon represents the mother. During the day, Saturn represents the paternal uncle and the Moon represents the maternal aunt. At night, the Sun represents the paternal uncle and Venus represents the maternal aunt—this should also be understood for the time of birth. The purpose is stated: "These are auspicious if they are situated in odd and even signs." During the day, if the Sun is in an odd sign <note>Aries, Gemini, Leo, etc.</note>, it is auspicious for the father; at night, it is auspicious for the paternal uncle. During the day, if Venus is in an even sign <note>Taurus, Cancer, Virgo, etc.</note>, it brings good to the mother; at night, to the maternal aunt. If Saturn is in an odd sign at night, it brings good to the father; during the day, to the paternal uncle. If the Moon is in an even sign at night, it is auspicious for the mother; during the day, for the maternal aunt. By implication, if they are in the opposite positions, it should be considered inauspicious.

<insert>Notes—Here verses 11-15 belong to the *Brihat Jataka* <note>A foundational 6th-century Sanskrit text on Hindu astrology by Varahamihira</note>. || 15 ||</insert>

In daytime conception, the Sun is the father, Venus the mother, Saturn the paternal uncle, and the Moon the maternal aunt. In nighttime conception, Saturn is the father, the Moon the mother, the Sun the uncle, and Venus the aunt. The purpose of these designations is that in daytime conception, the Sun in an odd sign (1-3-5-7-9-11) is auspicious for the father, and in nighttime conception, it is auspicious for the uncle. In daytime conception, if Venus is in an even sign (2-4-6-8-10-12), it is auspicious for the mother, and at night, for the aunt. If Saturn is in an odd sign during nighttime conception, it is auspicious for the father, and during the day, for the uncle. If the Moon is in an even sign during nighttime conception, it is auspicious for the mother, and during the day, for the aunt. Otherwise, one should predict inauspicious results. || 15 ||

When the Moon <note>original: "Cold-rayed one"</note> is in a woman's non-upachaya house <note>the 1st, 2nd, 4th, 5th, 7th, 8th, 9th, or 12th houses</note> and is aspected by Mars, the resulting menstruation is indeed capable of producing a fetus; otherwise, it is fruitless. When this occurs, and the Moon is in the man's upachaya house <note>the 3rd, 6th, 10th, or 11th houses</note> and aspected by Jupiter, the man should perform the act of conception. This should be done at a time that is not to be rejected, including the Mula constellation, endowed with good qualities, and free from forbidden times like Parva <note>lunar transitions</note>. || 16 ||

Now, after defining the menstruation capable of conception, the author describes the timing for the act. When the Moon is in a woman's non-upachaya house (as previously mentioned) and is aspected by Mars, the menstruation that occurs is certainly "fruit-giving," meaning capable of holding a fetus. In any other state, that menstruation goes to waste. While the Moon is in the woman's non-upachaya house, the man should perform the act of conception when the Moon is in his own upachaya house and is aspected by Jupiter. The idea is that conception between the couple occurs during such a planetary alignment.

Regarding the specific timing for conception: it should be done at a time that is "not to be rejected," which is prescribed as including the Mula constellation (though some authors disagree), free from forbidden times like Parva, and endowed with good qualities. Now, in this context, the things to be avoided during conception are listed:

> "One should avoid the three types of Gandanta <note>junction points between signs/constellations</note>, the death and birth constellations, and the end of Mula.
> Avoid the constellations of Ashwini and Revati, days of eclipses, the Patas, and Vaidhriti.
> Avoid the day of the parents' Shraddha <note>ancestral memorial feast</note>, the daytime, the first half of Parigha, and sexual union with one's wife during these times.
> Avoid days struck by solar portents, the house of death from the birth constellation, and malefic constellations.
> Avoid Bhadra, the sixth lunar day, the Parva days, twilight, Tuesdays, and Sundays..."

If the Moon is in a woman's <term>Anupachaya</term> <note>The 1st, 2nd, 4th, 5th, 7th, 8th, 9th, or 12th houses from the birth sign; these are considered 'non-accumulating' houses</note> and is aspected by Mars, the menses occurring at that time is capable of producing a pregnancy. # On the Duration of the Fertile Period for Women.

> The masters of the science say that the 'Season-Tree' of women lasts for sixteen nights from the start of the menses. The first four nights are not suitable for conception; the subsequent even-numbered nights are praised for granting sons. || 17 ||

The fertile period for women lasts for sixteen nights from the appearance of the menses. Among those, the first four nights are considered forbidden for conception. Of the remaining twelve nights, the even-numbered ones—the 6th, 8th, 10th, 12th, 14th, and 16th—are productive of sons and are highly praised. This is supported by the authorities stating "not the first four nights" and "on even nights." || 17 ||

The fertile period is said to be 16 nights from the start of a woman's menses. Among these, the first 4 nights are not fit for conception. In the remaining 12 nights, the even nights (6th, 8th, 10th, 12th, 14th, and 16th) are excellent for the act of conception and result in the birth of a son. — *Subodhini Shastra Commentary* || 17 ||

# On the Specific Results of Conception from the Fourth Night Onwards.

> A son of short life, a daughter, a lineage-builder, a barren woman, a son, a beautiful woman, a lordly man, a deformed woman, a wealthy man, a sinful woman, a righteous man, a prosperous woman, and an all-knowing man: these are produced in order from the fourth night. || 18 ||

During the fertile period, starting from the fourth night (the first three are forbidden; the fourth is pure, as the text says: "A woman becomes touchable by her husband on the fourth day after bathing"), the results are as follows: Conception on the 4th night produces a short-lived son. On the 5th, a daughter. On the 6th, a son who continues the lineage. On the 7th, a barren woman (a daughter who will have no children). On the 8th, a son. On the 9th, a beautiful daughter. On the 10th, a powerful or capable son. On the 11th, an ugly daughter. On the 12th, a wealthy son. On the 13th, a sinful daughter. On the 14th, a righteous son. On the 15th, a prosperous daughter. On the 16th, an all-knowing son is born. Understanding this arrangement for conception, a lover should approach his wife. || 18 ||

Conception on the 4th night produces a short-lived son; 5th night, a daughter; 6th night, a son who continues the lineage; 7th night, a barren woman; 8th night, a son; 9th night, a beautiful daughter; 10th night, an influential son; 11th night, an ugly daughter; 12th night, a wealthy/fortunate son; 13th night, a sinful daughter; 14th night, a righteous son; 15th night, a daughter like the Goddess of Fortune; and on the 16th night, an all-knowing son is born. — *Subodhini Shastra Commentary* || 18 ||

# On Planetary Positions Creating the Birth of Sons and Others.

> If the Sun is in the 8th house from the 8th <note>i.e., the 3rd house</note> at the time of conception, a son is born. Or, if the Sun is in a trine from the Ascendant of conception. || 19 ||
> If this Ascendant of conception is aspected by or joined with benefics, the one born will be long-lived, fortunate, and will reach the end of all branches of knowledge. || 20 ||

# Chapter on Non-Human Births || 3 ||

> If the Ascendant, the Sun, Jupiter, and the Moon are strong and situated in odd signs and masculine subdivisions <term>Navamshas; a 1/9th division of a zodiac sign</term>, one should predict a male birth. If those same planets are in even signs and feminine subdivisions, they cause the birth of a female.
> Jupiter and the Sun in an odd sign produce a male; the Moon, Venus, and Mars in an even sign produce a female.
> If these planets are in dual-natured signs <term>Dvisvabhāva; Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces</term> and are aspected by Mercury, they produce twins according to their own nature. || 21 ||
> Even Saturn, if placed in an odd sign (excluding the Ascendant), causes a male birth relative to the Ascendant. One must declare whether the newborn is male or female after observing the strength of the aforementioned planets. || 22 ||

From the time of conception <term>Adhāna; the moment of fertilization</term>, if the Sun has moved to the eighth house from the eighth—that is, the third house from the Ascendant—a son is born (1). Alternatively, if the Lord of the Day (the Sun) is in a trine—either the ninth or the fifth house—from the conception Ascendant, the birth of a son should be predicted (2). Furthermore, if this conception Ascendant is aspected by or joined with benefic planets, the one born will be long-lived, fortunate, and learned in all sciences (3). As shown in this chart: Sun = (1) Yoga <note>astrological combination</note>. Sun or Sun = (2) Yoga. Jupiter, Moon, Mercury, Venus = (3) Yoga.

->Now, the knowledge of distinguishing between female and male births from the moving sign <note>the current Ascendant</note> or the conception Ascendant is explained. By the "strong ones" is meant:<-

By the Ascendant, Sun, Jupiter, and Moon being powerful and situated in odd signs and masculine subdivisions. This is what is meant: if at that time the Ascendant, Sun, Jupiter, and Moon are endowed with the previously mentioned six-fold strength <term>Shadbala; a mathematical calculation of planetary power</term> and are in odd signs and odd subdivisions, then one should predict a male birth. However, if those same factors—the Ascendant, Sun, Jupiter, and Moon—are in even subdivisions and even signs, the birth of a female should be declared. If the planets are distributed between both types, the result follows the majority. In case of a tie, the side with greater strength prevails. Jupiter and the Sun in an odd sign generate a male. The Moon, Venus, and Mars <note>original: "Vakra", a name for Mars meaning 'the crooked'</note> situated in an even sign generate a female.

"In dual-natured signs": if those same planets (Jupiter, Sun, Moon, Venus, and Mars) are in the subdivisions of dual-natured signs and are aspected by Mercury, they produce twins <note>original: "Yamalau"</note> according to their own side. Here, this should be considered: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces are the four dual-natured signs. Among them, Gemini and Sagittarius are masculine; Virgo and Pisces are feminine. Therefore, if Jupiter and the Sun are in the subdivisions of Gemini or Sagittarius and are aspected by <unclear>Mercury</unclear>, then two males should be predicted. Similarly, if the Moon, Venus, and Mars are in the subdivisions of Virgo or Pisces and are seen by <unclear>Mercury</unclear>, they produce a pair of girls. If the planets are placed in both types, a mixed pair—meaning one boy and one girl—should be known as the <unclear>resulting</unclear> twins.

# Birth of Twins (3)

Here are the examples—(1) In the chart:
Sun = 4|3; Jupiter = 8|9; Moon = 10|3;
Ascendant = 2|9; Saturn = 6|3; These indicate a male birth.
(2) In the chart—Ascendant = 11|9; Sun = 10|6;
Jupiter = 3|5; Moon = 1|2; Mars = 7|3; Venus =
11|17; Saturn = 9|9; These indicate a female birth.
(3) In the chart—Sun = 2|27; Jupiter = 11|9;
A pair of males. Moon = 11|28; Venus =
4|29; Mars = 7|9; A pair of females.

From all the planets placed in this third chart, the birth of twins <note>literally "Gemini-birth" or "couple-birth"</note> may occur. This is merely a conceptual illustration.

Now, in the absence of the aforementioned combinations <term>Yogas: specific planetary alignments</term>, the knowledge of a hermaphrodite or neuter birth via Saturn is explained. Saturn—excluding the specific Ascendant of the time—if situated in an odd-numbered sign from the Ascendant, specifically within the odd houses starting from the third, becomes a maker of male birth. This means if Saturn is in the 3rd, 5th, 7th, 9th, or 11th houses, a male birth should be predicted. Here, one must observe the strength of the "odd-planets" <note>planets in odd-numbered signs</note> which cause male or female birth; if the male-causing planet is stronger, then a male is born; if the female-causing planet is stronger, then a woman or female child is predicted. As stated in the *Saravali*:

> "Leaving the Ascendant, Saturn in an odd house gives birth to a son.
> Having observed the strength of the birds <note>metaphor for planets</note> in the combination, one should declare a lord or a woman." || 19-22 ||

If the Sun is in the 3rd house from the Ascendant (which is the 8th from the 8th house of conception), a son is born. Or, if the Sun reaches a trine (5th or 9th house) from the conception Ascendant, a son is born. || 19 ||

If there is an aspect <note>a planetary "look" or influence</note> from a benefic planet on this conception Ascendant, the newborn will be long-lived, fortunate, and a knower of all sciences. || 20 ||

At the time of conception, birth, or inquiry, if the strong Ascendant, Sun, Jupiter, and Moon are in odd signs and odd <term>Navamshas: a one-ninth division of a zodiac sign</term>, predict the birth of a son. If those planets are in even signs and even Navamshas, know it to be the birth of a girl. If strong Jupiter and Sun are in odd signs, it is a son; if strong Moon, Venus, and Mars are in even signs, it is a girl. If Jupiter, Sun, Moon, Venus, and Mars are in the Navamshas of dual signs (Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces) and Mercury aspects them, know it to be the birth of twins. Here, if Jupiter and Sun are in the male portions (Gemini/Sagittarius) of a dual sign, two sons; if Moon, Venus, and Mars are in the female portions (Virgo/Pisces) of a dual sign, two daughters; if both combinations exist, predict one son and one daughter. || 21 ||

In the absence of the above combinations, if Saturn is situated in an odd house (3-5-7-9-11) excluding the Ascendant, predict a male birth; otherwise, know it as a female birth. One should decide between male or female birth based on which side of the aforementioned planetary factors is stronger. || 22 ||

# Combinations for Neuter Birth

> If the Moon and Sun aspect each other, or if Saturn and Mercury do so;
> If Mars in an even sign aspects the Sun in an odd sign, or if the Moon and Ascendant are so situated;
> If Venus and the Moon are in even and odd signs respectively and are aspected by Mars;
> If Venus, the Ascendant, and the Moon are in male portions—these six are combinations for a neuter birth. || 23 ||

Now the combinations for a neuter <note>hermaphrodite or non-binary</note> birth are described. If the Moon and Sun (situated in odd signs) do not aspect each other—that is, the Moon does not see the Sun and the Sun does not see the Moon—that is one combination for a neuter birth.

### Now, the Combination for the Birth of Triplets:

When the rising sign and the planets are in dual-natured <term>Navamshas</term><note>A Navamsha is a 1/9th division of a zodiac sign, used for fine-tuning predictions</note> and are aspected by Mercury situated in its own Navamsha. This is what is meant: if Mercury, staying in its own Navamsha, aspects the planets and the <term>Lagna</term><note>The Ascendant or rising sign</note> which are positioned in the Navamshas of dual-natured signs <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces</note>, then triplets in the womb should be predicted. Among them, the gender pair is determined by the influence of the Navamsha. If Mercury is in a male (Gemini) Navamsha, then there are two males and one female. If Mercury is in a female (Virgo) Navamsha, then there are two females and one male; thus triplets should be declared. By "unmixed" (equal degrees), it means triplets of the same gender. Here it should be noted: if Mercury in a Gemini Navamsha aspects planets and the rising sign that are in Gemini or Sagittarius Navamshas, then three males are born. Similarly, if Mercury in a Virgo Navamsha aspects planets and the rising sign in Virgo or Pisces Navamshas, then three females should be predicted. Thus says Kalyan Varma in the *Saravali*:

> "When the Lagna and the Moon are in even signs and are aspected by a strong planet, the dwellers of the sky <note>planets</note> always declare twins in the womb.
> When the Moon and Venus are in even signs, and Jupiter, Mars, Mercury, and the Lagna are in odd signs, or if they are strong in dual-natured signs, one should predict a male and a female here.
> If Mercury is in a Gemini Navamsha, there will be one girl and two boys; such is the triplet.
> When the Son of the Moon <note>Mercury</note> aspects the planets and the Lagna joined with dual-natured Navamshas:
> If in a Virgo Navamsha, two girls and a boy are placed in the womb.
> When Mercury, staying in a Gemini Navamsha, aspects planets and the Lagna that have reached Gemini or Sagittarius Navamshas, then there are three males in the womb.
> When the Son of the Cool-Rayed One <note>Mercury</note> in a female portion <note>Virgo</note> aspects the planets and the rising sign situated in Virgo or Pisces Navamshas, then there are three females in the womb." || 24 ||

If the Moon and Venus are in even signs, and Mercury, Mars, Jupiter, and the Lagna are in odd signs, then predict the birth of twins (one boy and one girl). If the Lagna and Moon are in even signs and any of the male planets (Sun, Mars, Jupiter) aspect them, then also predict the birth of one boy and one girl. If the aforementioned Mercury, Mars, Jupiter, and the Lagna are strong in even signs, the same result is known. And if the aforementioned planets and Lagna are present in dual-natured Navamshas and Mercury, situated in its own (3rd/6th) Navamsha, aspects them, there are three children in the womb. Here, twins/pairs should be stated according to Mercury's position; meaning if Mercury is in a male (Gemini) Navamsha, then two boys and one girl. If Mercury is in a female (Virgo) Navamsha and aspects the rising planets in dual-natured portions, then two girls and one boy should be said. In equal portions—meaning if Mercury is in a Gemini portion and aspects planets in Gemini and Sagittarius portions—then 3 males. Likewise, if Mercury is situated in a Virgo Navamsha and aspects planets in Virgo and Pisces Navamshas, then 3 girls should be predicted. — Author of *Su. Sha.* || 24 ||

However, because it is impossible for a human womb to carry a full pregnancy of so many to term, it should be understood that the miscarriage of that pregnancy occurs in the month associated with the planet that is weak at that time.

# In the Annotated Jataka Parijata

->If the lord of the 6th house is related to the body (the 1st house) and Mercury is in the 6th house,<-
->And if the birth occurs in a sign ruled by Mercury, that person is a female hermaphrodite. || 33 ||<-
->If Saturn is in the place of Mercury, male hermaphroditism occurs. || 1/2 ||<-

Now the combinations for male, female, and neuter identities are described. If the lord of the 6th house is related to the body—meaning related to the Ascendant <note>Lagna</note> (either through aspect or conjunction)—and Mercury is placed in the 6th house; and if the birth occurs in a sign of Mercury—meaning the Ascendant is either Gemini or Virgo—then the person born is a "female neuter," meaning the wife or the female aspect attains neuter characteristics. In that same context, "Saturn in the place of Mercury" means if Mercury is joined by Saturn in the aforementioned combination, then "male neuter" status occurs, meaning the male himself attains neuter characteristics. It is also stated in the *Sarvartha Chintamani*:

> "When the lord of the 6th is in a sign of Mercury in the Ascendant, and the lord of the Ascendant is in a sign of Mercury, the one born is a neuter with a wife; but if joined by Saturn etc., the male is the 6th <note>referring to the neuter category</note>." || 33 1/2 ||

At the time of conception <note>Nisheka</note> or birth, if the lord of the 6th is related to the Ascendant (present in the Ascendant or aspecting it), Mercury is in the 6th house, and the birth is in Mercury's signs (Gemini or Virgo), the wife is neuter. If Saturn is here with Mercury, the man is neuter. || 33 1/2 ||

->If the lord of the conception Ascendant and the lord of the 3rd house are in the Ascendant, twins are born. || 3 ||<-

## Combinations for Foot-First Births

->If at conception the lord of the 3rd is joined with the Lord of Serpents <note>Rahu</note>, one is born by the feet. || 34 ||<-
->* With Rahu in the Ascendant and the lord of the Ascendant in the 10th, the feet come first. || 1/2 ||<-

Now the combinations for a foot-first delivery <note>breech birth</note> are stated. If the lord of the 3rd house and Rahu are in the conception Ascendant, the child is "foot-born" (emerging from the mother's womb feet-first). Likewise, if Rahu is in the Ascendant and the lord of the Ascendant is in the 10th house <note>Karma-bhava</note>, it should be said that the feet are born first. As stated in the *Sarvartha Chintamani* (3.43.2):

> "When the lord of the Ascendant is in the 10th and the Ascendant is joined by the Lord of Serpents, a foot-birth occurs."

If the conception Ascendant is joined by the lord of the 3rd and Rahu, birth is by the feet. If Rahu is in the Ascendant and the lord of the Ascendant is in the 10th, the birth is feet-first. || 34 1/2 ||

8. The verse beginning "If the Ascendant is with a malefic..." is self-explanatory.

9. In the following three combinations, birth wrapped in the cord should be predicted: (a) the Ascendant is between two malefics and contains Rahu; (b) Mars is in the Ascendant aspected by the Sun; (c) Saturn is in the Ascendant aspected by Mars.

# Precise Jataka Parijata

If the Ascendant <note>Lagna: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</note> contains a malefic planet, is aspected by malefic planets, is joined with Rahu or Ketu <note>the north and south nodes of the moon</note>, or is situated in a sign owned by a malefic planet, the child is born entwined in the umbilical cord. || 41 ||

If the Ascendant is hemmed between cruel planets and joined with Rahu, or if Mars is in the Ascendant and aspected by the Sun, or if Saturn is in the Ascendant and aspected by Mars, the body of the newborn child will be wrapped in the umbilical cord. || 42 ||

-> **Now, the planetary positions indicating the time of delivery.** <-

> * At that time <note>original: "tatkale"</note>, the sign of the twelfth-part <term>Dvadasamsa: a 2.5-degree division of a zodiac sign</term> occupied by the Moon—when the Moon later reaches that same sign in the future, and the portion of the day or night corresponding to the rising portion has passed, that is when they say the birth occurs. || 43 ||
> If the birth-conception <term>Nisheka: the moment of conception</term> occurs when a Navamsa <note>a 3.24-degree division</note> of Saturn (Capricorn or Aquarius) is rising and Saturn is in the seventh house, the delivery occurs after three years.
> If this same rule applies to the Moon, it causes delivery after twelve years. This stated rule should be considered with logic even at the time of birth. || 44 ||

Now he explains the knowledge of the time of delivery from the time of conception or from a query. "At that time" means at the time of conception or the time of the query. Note the twelfth-part <note>Dvadasamsa</note> of the sign in which the Moon is placed. When the Moon, moving forward, reaches that same sign in the tenth month, the delivery should be predicted.

**Here is an example:** On the fifth day of the bright half of the month of Magha, at someone's time of conception, the Longitude of the Moon = 5s 2° 15' 10" <note>5 signs, 2 degrees, 15 minutes, 10 seconds; placing it in Virgo</note>. There, the ninth twelfth-part of Virgo belongs to Taurus. Therefore, when the Moon reaches Capricorn (the fifth sign from Taurus) in the tenth month (the month of Kartika), the delivery should be predicted.

**Now, calculating the birth star <note>Nakshatra</note>:** The elapsed portion of the Taurus twelfth-part = 0° 15' 10" = 15' (approximately). Since the full measure of a twelfth-part is 150', and this corresponds to the total minutes of a circle, then for 15':
(1800' X 15') / 150' = 180'.
Each sign has nine quarters <note>Charanas</note>, so one quarter is 200' minutes. Therefore, 180' ÷ 200 = 1st quarter (approx). Thus, it should be said that the birth will occur in the first quarter of Capricorn (which is the second quarter of the Uttarashadha star).

**Now, knowledge of the time of day or night:** "The portion of the day or night that rises." The day and night signs were explained in the fourteenth verse of the first chapter. Note whether the rising portion of the Ascendant at conception is designated as day or night. This means: whatever degrees of the day/night Navamsa have passed in the conception Ascendant, the twice-born <note>Brahmins/Astrologers</note> say the birth occurs after that much time of the day or night has passed.

**Example calculation:** Suppose the conception Ascendant is 3s 7° 1' 15". Here, the fourth Navamsa of Cancer belongs to Libra. Libra is a day-sign, so the birth occurs during the day. To find the desired time <note>Ishtakala</note>: The elapsed portion of the fourth Navamsa = 12' 15". By proportion, if the full measure (200') gives the day's duration (26.30), then what does 12' 15" give?
(26.5 X 12.25') / 200' = 11.40 (approximately). Therefore, the birth should be said to occur at 11 Ghatis and 40 Palas <note>traditional units of time</note> during the day. || 43 ||

**Now he describes combinations for delayed delivery:** If a Navamsa of Saturn (Capricorn or Aquarius) is rising at the time of conception and Saturn is in the seventh house, the delivery of that fetus occurs after three years. But if this same rule applies to the Moon—meaning the Navamsa of Cancer is rising and the Moon is in the seventh house from the Ascendant—then [the text continues]...

# Now, combinations indicating birth without the Simanta sacrament.

> If the lords of the father's house and the house of action are in bad houses, while the lord of the body is strong, the son is undoubtedly born without the *Simanta* <note>Simantonnayana: a traditional Hindu 'baby shower' or parting-of-the-hair ceremony performed during pregnancy for the mother's and child's well-being</note> and other sacraments.
> If a malefic planet is in the eleventh house or the eleventh house belongs to a malefic, he will not have the *Simanta* ceremony. || 45 1/2 ||

The author has used the term 'Pitri' (Father) for the fifth house <note>original: "Dhi-Devaraja-Pitri-Nandana-Panchakani"</note>. However, in the *Sarvartha Chintamani* it is seen:
"If the lords of the tenth and ninth houses are in bad houses and the lord of the ascendant is strong, then the person is born without the *Simanta* ceremony. If the eleventh house contains a malefic or is a malefic sign, the person is born without the ceremony."
Therefore, 'Pitri-Karmeshvarau' should be understood as the lords of the ninth and tenth houses. In that case, at the time of birth, the lords of the 9th and 10th are in 'bad' houses <note>the 6th, 8th, or 12th houses</note>. The rest is clear. || 45 1/2 ||

If at birth the lords of the 9th and 10th houses are in bad positions and the lord of the 1st house is strong, say the son was born without the *Simanta* and other rites. If there is a malefic in the 11th house or the 11th house is a malefic sign, consider that child devoid of the *Simanta* sacrament. || 45 1/2 ||

# With Commentary on Jataka Parijata

> If Saturn is in the Ascendant, or if Mars has reached the Setting [7th House],
> or if the Lord of the Night [the Moon] is situated between the Son of the Moon [Mercury] and Venus. || 47 ||

If the Moon does not aspect <note>In Vedic astrology, "aspect" refers to a planet 'looking' at a house or another planet, influencing its effects.</note> the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the rising sign on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</term>, then the birth is said to occur in the absence of the father. If the Sun has departed from the mid-heaven (the 10th house) — meaning it is in the 11th or 9th house — and is situated in a Moveable Sign <term>Chara Rashi: signs like Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn that indicate movement</term> at the time of birth, the father of the newborn is abroad. In that case too, it must be specified that the Moon does not aspect the Ascendant. As stated in another text:

> When the Sun is in a Moveable Sign and situated in the 9th or 8th house,
> the child's father is in a foreign land, provided the Ascendant is not aspected by the Moon. || 46 ||

Alternatively, if Saturn is in the Ascendant, or if Mars has reached the 7th house, or if the Moon is placed between Mercury and Venus (meaning one is in the 2nd house from the Moon and the other in the 12th), the birth is said to occur in the absence of the father.
It is also stated in the *Svalpa Jataka*:
> "When the Moon does not aspect the Ascendant, or when the Moon is between Mercury and Venus;
> the birth is of one whose father is absent, or when Saturn is in the Ascendant or Mars is in the 7th." || 47 ||

If in the birth chart the Moon does not see the Ascendant, then the father of that child was absent at that time. If the Sun is in a Moveable Sign and in any of the 8th, 9th, 11th, or 12th houses, know the father to be in a foreign land. If the Moon does not aspect the Ascendant and the Sun is in a Fixed Sign <term>Sthira Rashi: Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius</term> and in any of the 8th, 9th, 11th, or 12th houses, know the father to be absent but in the same country. If the Moon does not aspect the Ascendant and the Sun is in a Dual Sign <term>Dvisvabhava Rashi: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces</term> and situated in any of the 8th, 9th, 11th, or 12th houses, know the father to be midway between his own country and a foreign land. || 46 ||

Alternatively, if Saturn is in the Ascendant, know the father to be absent; or if Mars is in the 7th, know the father to be absent; or if the Moon is between Mercury and Venus (one in the 2nd and one in the 12th from the Moon), know the birth to be in the absence of the father. || 47 ||

> The positions of the planets indicate whether a child is legitimate, "field-born," etc.
> If the Ascendant or the Moon is in the sign of a benefic planet,
> and is associated with the divisions of Jupiter, the child born is Legitimate. || 48 ||
> If Jupiter is not aspected by Mars, and the Sun and Moon are in their own divisions,
> or associated with Mercury and endowed with strength, the child born is "Field-born." || 49 ||
> If the Moon is in a division of Saturn, and Saturn is joined in the 5th house,
> aspected by the Sun and Venus, the son is "Born of a Remarried Woman." || 50 ||

If the Ascendant or the Moon is in a sign belonging to a benefic planet <note>Benefics are naturally auspicious planets like Jupiter, Venus, or a strong Moon</note> and if the divisions <term>Varga: harmonic sub-charts used for fine-tuning predictions</term> of Jupiter are present there, then this newborn is called *Aurasa* = legitimate (born of one's own father). Now, if Jupiter is not being looked upon by Mars, and the Moon along with the Sun is in its own division, or is joined with Mercury and is strong, then this newborn is called *Kshetraja* <note>Literally "born of the field"; historically referring to a child sired by a proxy or under specific social circumstances</note>. Furthermore, if the Moon is in a division of Saturn, and Saturn is situated in the 5th house, and both are aspected by the Sun and Venus, the child is a *Paunarbhava* son. One born of a *Punarbhu* is *Paunarbhava*. A *Punarbhu* refers to a married woman who has been married again to another man. || 48-50 ||

At the time of birth, if the Ascendant or the Moon belongs to the sign of a benefic planet and is endowed with the division of Jupiter, know this child to be legitimate. || 48 ||
If Jupiter is not seen by Mars, and the powerful Sun and Moon are in their own divisions and with Mercury, the one taking birth is *Kshetraja* (produced from one's mother and another man). || 49 ||

<header>Chapter on Non-Standard Births || 3 ||</header>

If the Moon is in the division of Saturn, and the Sun is in the fifth house joined with Saturn and aspected <note>In Vedic astrology, an 'aspect' or 'drishti' is when one planet 'looks at' or influences another from a specific distance.</note> by Venus, then the person born is to be known as a *Paunarbhava* <note>A child born to a woman who has remarried.</note>. || 50 ||

# The Planetary Combination for a Child Born to an Unmarried Woman

> If the twelfth house is aspected by the Sun, or if the Moon and Sun are in each other's divisions, or if the Moon and Sun are joined together, this man becomes a *Kanina*. || 51 ||

Now, the birth of a child to a maiden is discussed. The verse is clear in its meaning. *Kanina* means born of an unmarried girl. This is according to the *Amarakosha* <note>A famous ancient Sanskrit thesaurus</note> which states: "A *Kanina* is one born of a maiden." || 51 ||

If the twelfth house is aspected by the Sun, or if the Moon is in the Sun's division and the Sun is in the Moon's division respectively, then the one born is a *Kanina*, meaning the son of an unmarried girl (a maiden). || 51 ||

# The Combination for an Adopted Son

> If Mandi <note>A mathematical point in the sky, also called Gulika, considered a 'shadow planet' with a malefic influence.</note> is aspected by or joined with the Moon, and is joined with or aspected by the son of the Sun (Saturn), the man becomes an adopted son (*Dattaputra*).
> If Saturn and Mars are joined in the seventh or the fifth house, and are not aspected by other planets, one should designate him a *Kritrima* son.

Now the combination for an adopted son is stated. If Mandi (Gulika) is aspected by the Moon, and is joined with Saturn or aspected by Saturn, then the man born will be an adopted son; it should be known that he will become the adoptee of someone.
Now the *Kritrima* <note>A 'made' or 'artificial' son; someone who is treated as a son due to circumstances rather than formal adoption rituals.</note> son is discussed. If at the time of birth Saturn and Mars are in the seventh or fifth house and there is an absence of aspects from other planets, then the person born should be designated a *Kritrima* son. This means that due to some cause, this person enjoys the status of a son to someone else. || 52-53 ||

If the Moon aspects Gulika, and Gulika is joined with Saturn or aspected by Saturn, the one born becomes the adopted son of someone. || 52 ||

If Saturn and Mars are in the seventh or fifth house and there is no aspect from other planets, the person born is called a *Kritrima* son, meaning for some reason (such as being raised, nourished, or through affection) he will become the son of someone else. (According to the author of *Suka Jataka*) || 53 ||

# Combinations for Illegitimacy

> If the lords of the first and fourth houses have exchanged places from the birth lagna (ascendant); or if the lord of the first or the lord of the fourth is joined with the Banner (Ketu) or the Serpent (Rahu), the birth is by another. || 54 ||
> If Jupiter does not aspect the Ascendant or the Moon, or if they are not in the same house; or if they are not joined with a division of Jupiter, then one should declare the birth to be from a secret union. || 55 ||
> Born on a Sunday with the second lunar day and the Swati star; or a Wednesday with the seventh lunar day and the Revati star; or a Saturday with the twelfth lunar day and the Shravishtha star—those born in these are said to be from another. || 56 ||
> Those born on the lunar dates called *Bhadra* <note>The 2nd, 7th, and 12th days of the lunar fortnight.</note>, joined with "three-footed" stars <note>Stars that span across two zodiac signs, such as Krittika or Punarvasu.</note>, on the days of Saturn, the Sun, or Mars, are known to be born of others. || 57 ||
> If Jupiter aspects neither the Ascendant nor the Moon, nor the Moon when joined with the Sun; or if the Moon is joined with the Sun and a malefic planet, they say with certainty the birth is by another. || 58 ||
> If the Moon is in a sign of Jupiter, or joined with Jupiter in another sign, or in Jupiter's decan or division, then birth by another is not accepted. || 59 ||

Now the combinations for illegitimacy (*Jaraja*) are stated. If at birth the lord of the first house is in the house of the lord of the fourth, and the lord of the fourth is in the house of the lord of the first (this is stated because the non-luminary planets own two signs each); or, if either the lord of the first or the lord of the fourth is joined anywhere with Rahu or Ketu, then the birth of the person is said to be by another man. These are three combinations. || 54 ||

Now, regarding the cancellation of this "foreign birth" combination: If the Moon is placed in a sign of Jupiter (Sagittarius or Pisces), or is joined with Jupiter in another sign, or is in a <term>Drekkana</term> <note>A 10-degree subdivision of a sign.</note> or <term>Navamsha</term> <note>A 3-degree 20-minute subdivision, the 9th part of a sign.</note> belonging to Jupiter, then the child is not considered to be born of others. This is the cancellation of the Parajata Yoga. || 59 ||

# Chapter on Non-Human Births, etc. || 3 ||

### On the Father’s Imprisonment at Birth, etc.
> If two malefic planets are in malefic signs and situated in the 7th, 9th, or 5th houses from the Sun, the father is imprisoned; whether in a foreign land, his own land, or on a journey depends on the Sun's zodiac sign. || 60 ||

Now the combination for the father’s imprisonment is explained. "Two malefic planets" <note>original: *ashobhanau*</note> refers to Saturn and Mars. If they are in signs ruled by malefic planets and are located in any of the 7th, 9th, or 5th houses from the Sun, then the father of the newborn is imprisoned <note>original: *baddha*, meaning bound or incarcerated</note> in a prison or similar place. The location is determined by the Sun's sign: if the Sun is in a movable sign <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn</note>, he is in a foreign land; in a fixed sign <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius</note>, in his own land; and in a dual sign <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces</note>, he is on a journey or path. || 60 ||

->Combination for imprisonment on a journey.<-

If two malefic planets are in malefic signs (1, 3, 8, 10, 11) <note>Aries, Gemini, Scorpio, Capricorn, Aquarius</note> and are in the 7th, 9th, or 5th house from the Sun, know that the father is in bondage at the time of the child's birth. If the Sun is in a movable sign, the father is bound in a foreign land. If in a fixed sign, in his own land; if in a dual sign, he is bound while traveling. || 60 ||

### On the Place of Birth.

>

> If Saturn is in the Ascendant in a sign ruled by the Moon and is aspected by Mercury, the Sun, and the Moon respectively, the birth should be declared to be in a pleasure-house, a temple, or on barren land. || 64 ||
>
> If Mars aspects a human Ascendant, the birth is in a cemetery; if Venus and the Moon aspect it, in a beautiful place; if Jupiter, in a place of fire-rituals; if the Sun, in a palace, temple, or cowshed; if Mercury, in an artisan’s workshop. || 65 ||
>
> Birth occurs on a path if the sign and Navamsha <note>a 1/9th division of a sign</note> are movable; in a house if fixed. If in its own sign or Navamsha, it is in one's own home. The result should be given based on the strength of the two <note>the sign and its lord</note>. || 66 ||

(These are two combinations). || 61 ||

# With the Commentary on Jataka Parijata

If [Saturn] is aspected <note>In astrology, an 'aspect' is when one planet 'looks' at another from a specific distance, influencing its effects.</note>, birth should be declared to take place in a hidden spot <gloss>= in a prison</gloss>. If the **Ascendant** <term>Lagna: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</term> is the sign of Cancer or Scorpio, and Saturn is situated there and aspected by the Moon, birth should be declared to take place in a pit <gloss>= in a well (or a ditch)</gloss>. || 63 ||

If Saturn is present in a **watery sign** <term>Jalachara Rashi: signs like Cancer, Scorpio, or Pisces associated with water</term> in the Ascendant and is aspected by Mercury, then birth occurs in a pleasure house; if aspected by the Sun, then in a temple; if aspected by the Moon, then in barren or salty land. || 64 ||

If Saturn is in a **masculine sign** <gloss>= a male zodiac sign in the Ascendant</gloss> and Mars <gloss>= Kuja</gloss> views it <gloss>(the term 'viewing' or aspecting applies to all following cases)</gloss>, birth occurs in a cremation ground; if Venus and the Moon <gloss>= Sita and Indu</gloss> view it, in a lovely place <gloss>= beautiful grounds</gloss>; if Jupiter views it, in a sacrificial fire-chamber <gloss>= a room for Homa/rituals</gloss>; if the Sun views it, in a royal palace, a temple, or a cowshed <gloss>= King's house, house of gods, or cattle pen</gloss>; and if Mercury <gloss>= Jna</gloss> views it, in an artisan's workshop <gloss>= a room for painting, books, or creative works</gloss>. || 65 ||

In the absence of these specific combinations, the author provides another method for knowing the place of birth: birth should be declared in a place corresponding to the nature of the Sign and the **Navamsha** <term>Navamsha: a 1/9th subdivision of a zodiac sign used for fine-tuned predictions</term>, whether it be a path, a movable house, or a fixed house. This means: if the Ascendant is a movable or fixed sign, and the Navamsha within that Ascendant is also movable or fixed, then birth is in the environment associated with that sign or subdivision <gloss>= the path of travel or specific region</gloss>. Furthermore, if any sign in the Ascendant is in its own subdivision <gloss>= attaining its own Navamsha</gloss>, birth should be declared in one's own home <gloss>= the family's own house</gloss>. Regarding the doubt of whether to prioritize the Ascendant sign or the Navamsha sign, it is said: "The result comes from the stronger of the two." Birth should be predicted based on the environment of whichever is stronger between the Ascendant sign and the Navamsha sign. || 66 ||

---

If the full Moon is in Cancer, Mercury is in the Ascendant, and Jupiter is in the 4th house (house of happiness), the person is known to be born on a boat. Or, if the Ascendant is a watery sign and the Moon is in the 7th house, birth is also known to be on a boat. || 61 ||

If the birth Ascendant is a watery sign and the Moon is also in a watery sign, birth is in water. If the full Moon aspects the Ascendant, birth is also in water. If the Moon is in the 10th, 4th, or 1st house from a watery Ascendant, the result is the same. || 62 ||

If Saturn is in the 12th house from the birth Ascendant and the Moon, and is aspected by a malefic planet, birth is in a prison (jail). If the Ascendant is Scorpio or Cancer, Saturn is there, and the Moon aspects it, birth is in a pit. || 63 ||

If Saturn in a watery sign is in the Ascendant and Mercury aspects it, birth is in a pleasure pavilion (chamber of delights). If the Sun aspects it, birth is in a temple. Similarly, if the Moon aspects Saturn, birth is in barren land. || 64 ||

If the birth Ascendant is a masculine sign and Mars aspects Saturn there, birth is in a cremation ground. If Venus and the Moon aspect it, birth is in a beautiful house; if Jupiter aspects it, in a house of fire-rituals or a kitchen; if the Sun aspects it, in the house of a king or a deity, or a cowshed; and if Mercury aspects it, birth is in a house of arts/crafts. || 65 ||

Regarding the knowledge of the place of birth mentioned previously, in their absence, another combination is given—in the Ascendant of movable and fixed signs, birth should be described in a land similar to the sign and the Navamsha sign (the specific land assigned to that sign). If the Ascendant of any sign is in its own Navamsha, birth is in one's own house. Should one describe the land of the sign or the Navamsha? The answer to this doubt is that one should describe the land of whichever is stronger. (Commentary by Su. Sha.) || 66 ||
