### On the Death of an Abandoned Child

If the Moon is in the Ascendant <note>the 1st house</note> and is aspected by a malefic planet, and Mars is in the 7th house, the abandoned child perishes. Likewise, if the aforementioned Moon <note>in the Ascendant, aspected by the Sun</note> is in the 11th house from Mars and Saturn, the child abandoned by the mother dies. If the Moon is aspected by a benefic planet, the child comes into the hands of a person of the same class <note>varna</note> as that planet and lives. If aspected by others <note>malefic planets</note>, even if the child goes into the hands of another, they do not live; they certainly die. || 68 ||

**If the Moon situated in the Ascendant is aspected by malefic planets (Sun, Saturn) and Mars is in the 7th house, the child abandoned by the mother dies. If the Moon (in the Ascendant, aspected by the Sun) is in the 11th house from Mars and Saturn, the abandoned child dies. In that situation, if the Moon is aspected by a benefic planet, the child falls into the hands of a person of the caste corresponding to that planet and survives. If the Moon is aspected by malefic planets, the child dies even after being taken in by another. (According to the author of Su. Jna.) || 68 ||**

### On the Place of Birth

Birth occurs in the house of the father or mother based on their respective strengths; or in places like a tree-shed if benefic planets are in their signs of debilitation. If the Ascendant and the Moon are not aspected by several planets together, the birth occurs in a secluded place. || 69 ||

The planets representing the father and mother were mentioned previously <note>in verse 15</note>. At the time of birth, if the maternal planet is strong, birth is in the mother's house; if the paternal planet is strong, birth is in the father's house. If all benefic planets are in their signs of debilitation, birth occurs under a tree, in a garden, or on a riverbank. If the Ascendant and the Moon are not aspected by three or more planets located in a single sign, the birth occurs in a secluded place. Conversely, if they are aspected by three or more planets in one sign, birth occurs in a crowded place. || 69 ||

**If the paternal planets (Sun, Saturn) are strong, consider the birth to be in the house of the father or paternal uncle. If the maternal planets (Moon, Venus) are strong, consider the birth to be in the house of the mother or maternal aunt. If benefic planets are in debilitated signs, birth occurs under a tree, in a wooden hut, on a riverbank, or on a mountain. If many planets in one sign do not aspect the Ascendant and the Moon, birth is in a lonely place. If many planets aspect them, birth is in a community of people. || 69 ||**

If the Moon is in a sign of Saturn, or in the 4th house and aspected by Saturn, or joined with Saturn, the birth bed is in a dark place or on the ground if planets are debilitated. The delivery of the fetus follows the nature of the rising sign. Malefic planets in the 7th or 4th houses from the Moon cause distress to the mother. || 70 ||

# With the Commentary on Jataka Parijata

If the Moon is in a sign of Saturn <note>Capricorn or Aquarius</note> or in its Navamsha <note>a 1/9th divisional chart</note>, or in the fourth house from the Ascendant, or aspected by Saturn <note>viewed by Saturn's astrological gaze</note>, or in a watery sign <note>Cancer or Pisces</note>, or joined with Saturn, then the delivery of the woman is said to take place in **darkness**. However, in these specific configurations, if the Moon is aspected by the Sun, there is indeed light.
> "If the Moon is seen by the Sun, one should declare that light is present,"
as per the traditional teachings. If three or more planets are in their signs of debilitation <note>their weakest positions</note>, the birth is said to take place on the **ground**.

### Now, the delivery of the fetus is described:
The manner in which the sign of the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</term> rises determines the **delivery of the fetus**. If the Ascendant is a "Rear-rising" sign <note>Prishthodaya: signs that rise with their back first, like Aries or Taurus</note>, the birth is face-down, showing the back. If it is a "Head-rising" sign <note>Shirshodaya: signs like Leo or Virgo</note>, the birth is face-up with the belly positioned upwards. If it is a "Both-rising" sign <note>Ubhayodaya: Pisces</note>, the birth is sideways.

### Now, the yoga for the mother’s suffering.
The wise say that if **malefic planets** <note>such as Mars or Saturn</note> are joined with the Moon, or placed in the seventh or fourth house from the Ascendant, the mother suffers great **distress** during childbirth. It is also stated in the *Saravali*:
> "Distress to the mother occurs when cruel planets are in the seventh house or joined with the Moon." || 70 ||

If the Moon is in Saturn's sign (10, 11) or Navamsha, or in the 4th house from the Ascendant, or seen by Saturn from any sign, or in a watery (4, 12) sign, or anywhere with Saturn, one should say the delivery was in the dark. In these combinations, if the Sun aspects the Moon, the previously mentioned result does not occur; meaning, a lamp must be present in the delivery room at the time of birth. If more than three planets are in debilitated signs, birth is on the floor. If birth is in a Head-rising sign, the child's face is upward (born supine). If it is a Rear-rising sign, the child is born face down. If birth is in Pisces, the child is born on its side, as this is a "Both-rising" sign. If the Lord of the Ascendant or the Lord of the Navamsha is retrograde, the delivery is reversed, meaning the feet likely emerged from the womb first. If at the time of birth malefic planets are with the Moon, or in the 7th or 4th from the Ascendant, the mother would have suffered much pain during delivery. || 70 ||

---

### Now, knowledge of the lamp and the door in the delivery room.
> The oil is from the Moon, the wick from the Ascendant; the lamp's position is from the Sun's sign, and the earth etc. <note>the container</note> is also known thus.
> The door of the structure is known by the planets situated in the angles <note>houses 1, 4, 7, and 10</note> or by those endowed with strength. || 71 ||

Now the knowledge of the lamp etc., in the delivery room and the knowledge of the house door is explained. The oil in the lamp is told from the Moon; if the Moon is at the beginning of a sign, the lamp-vessel is full of oil; at the end of a sign, it is empty; in the middle, it is half-full. The wick is told from the Ascendant. If the Ascendant is at the start of the sign, the wick is newly placed; in the middle, it is half-burnt; at the end of the sign, the wick is fully burnt. The nature of the lamp is told by the sign the Sun occupies. If the Sun is in a "Movable" sign, the lamp was carried/moving; in a "Fixed" sign, the lamp was stationary in one place; in a "Dual" sign, the lamp was moved from one place to another.

### Now, knowledge of the door in the delivery room.
The door in the delivery room is told by the planets situated in the **angles** (1, 4, 7, 10) from the Ascendant. The direction of the planet in the angle indicates the direction the door faces. If there are many planets in the angles, the direction is determined by the strongest among them. If there are no planets in the angles, the door faces the direction of the Ascendant sign. || 71 ||

If at the birth time the Moon is at the beginning of a sign, the lamp is full of oil. The oil corresponds to the degrees the Moon has traveled. If at the end of the sign, the lamp is empty. Similarly, if birth is at the start of the Ascendant, a full wick; in the middle degrees, a half-burnt wick; at the end, a fully burnt wick. If the Sun is in a Movable sign, consider the lamp moving; if Fixed, stationary; if Dual...

# Chapter 3: On Non-Human Births and Other Matters

The lamp should be said to be in the direction of the zodiac sign occupied by the Sun. Alternatively, the Sun rotates through the eight directions over the course of the eight watches <note>A 'prahara' or watch is a three-hour period</note>; the lamp is in whichever direction the Sun occupies at that time. The color of the wick matches the color associated with the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</term>. If many planets are in Cardinal houses, use the direction of the strongest planet. ->**On the Nature of the Delivery Room**<-

If Saturn is strong, the house is old or renovated; if Mars, it is burnt; if the Moon, it is new;
If the Sun, it is full of wood and sturdy; if Mercury, it is built by many craftsmen;
If Venus, it is beautiful, decorated with pictures, and new; if Jupiter, it is a strong mansion.
Based on the planets in the zodiac, one should describe the surrounding structures as taught. || 72 ||

Now the nature of the delivery room is described. The phrase "endowed with strength" applies to all planets. The meaning is clear. Now, "based on those in the zodiac" means the planets situated near the planet causing the birth yoga; "surrounding structures" means one should describe the layout in all directions as instructed. Here, this should be noted: the planets situated in front, behind, or to the side of the planet signifying the birth house create neighboring houses or outbuildings similar to themselves according to their own positions.

As stated in the *Saravali* <note>A classic 8th-century CE astrological treatise by Kalyanavarman</note>:
> "Through the conjunctions of houses and planets, one should contemplate the neighboring houses:
> Temples, water-sheds, fire-places, treasuries, pleasure gardens, or places for rubbish.
> The sleeping chamber is determined by the combinations of the Sun, Moon, Mars, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn, and Mercury." || 72 ||

If Saturn is strong at the time of birth, the delivery room is old; if Mars is strong, it is burnt; if the Moon is strong, it is new and—during the bright fortnight—freshly plastered; if the Sun is strong, it is sturdy and full of wood; if Mercury, it has various designs; if Venus, it is beautiful, charming, decorated with many pictures, and new; if Jupiter, it should be called firm (strong). Whichever planet's house-characteristics are found, there will be as many houses in front or behind it as there are planets situated in front or behind that planet. || 72 ||

->**On the Direction of the Delivery Room**<-

With Aries, Cancer, Libra, Scorpio, and Aquarius, the residence is in the East or North; in the houses of Jupiter and Mercury <note>Sagittarius, Pisces, Gemini, and Virgo</note>, it is in the North.
With Taurus, the residence is in the West; Capricorn and Leo are in the Southern part. || 73 ||

Now the knowledge of the direction of delivery for all things is stated. If the Ascendant is any of the signs Aries, Cancer, Libra, Scorpio, or Aquarius, the delivery room is in the Eastern part. In Sagittarius, Pisces, Gemini, and Virgo, it is in the Northern part. In the sign of Taurus, it is in the Western part. In Capricorn and Leo, the delivery room should be said to be in the Southern part. || 73 ||

If any of the signs Aries, Cancer, Libra, Scorpio, or Aquarius are in the Ascendant <note>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</note>, or if the Ascendant falls in the subdivisions <term>Amshas</term> of these signs, the birth is said to take place in the eastern part of the building. # On the Location of Birth within the Delivery Room

> The signs starting from Aries occupy the East and other cardinal directions in pairs; the dual-natured signs are placed in the corners. One should also describe the bed in the same manner as the building, using the feet of the bed situated at the sixth, third, ninth, and twelfth positions. || 74 ||

In the delivery room, the twelve signs are placed starting from the East in pairs (two signs per cardinal direction). Similarly, the dual-natured signs <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces</note> starting from Gemini are placed in the four corners starting from the Southeast. This means the birth should be declared to have occurred in whichever direction the Ascendant sign is located within the delivery room. The same logic applies to the bed. For clarity, one should examine the two diagrams. Regarding the bed, wherever a dual-natured sign falls, there is a depression or slant; wherever a malefic planet <note>Planets like Mars or Saturn</note> is situated, an injury or defect should be predicted. || 74 ||

If the Ascendant is Aries or Taurus, the birth is in the East of the room; Gemini is Southeast; Cancer or Leo is South; Virgo is Southwest; Libra or Scorpio is West; Sagittarius is Northwest; Capricorn or Aquarius is North; and Pisces is the Northeast part. The same should be considered for the bed (cot). The specific detail here is the placement of the Houses <term>Bhavas</term> on the bed: the Ascendant and the 2nd house are at the head; the 3rd house is the right-side head-post; the 4th and 5th houses are the right side-rail; the 6th house is the right-side foot-post; the 7th and 8th houses are at the foot of the bed; the 9th house is the left-side foot-post; the 10th and 11th houses are the left side-rail; and the 12th house is the left-side head-post. The purpose of this is to say that whichever part of the bed corresponds to a dual-natured sign, that part will be bent/curved, and whichever part contains malefic planets, that part will have an injury or break. (According to the author of Muhurta Shastra) || 74 ||

# Chapter on Non-Human Births and Other Matters || 3 ||

If the planets are outside the house, or similarly unseen—meaning they are positioned within the houses surrounding the Ascendant <note>The 'Lagna' or rising sign</note>—one should describe the women present inside the house as being equal in number to those planets. Other teachers say otherwise: that if the planets are in the visible portion of the sky, they are outside, and if in the invisible portion, they are the midwives <term>Upasutika</term><note>Attendant women or midwives present at the birth</note>. Thus says Jiva: "The midwives are determined by the planets situated in the middle of the rising sign. Those in the northern half are outside, while those in the southern half are known to be inside." This is noted as the opinion of other teachers by the phrase "otherwise by others."
This is also stated in the *Svalpa Jataka*:
> "Those in the northern half are inside, and those in the visible half of the wheel are outside." || 75 ||

At the time of birth, there will be as many midwives (attendant women) as there are planets between the Ascendant and the Moon. The color, appearance, and age of these midwives should be described as similar to those planets. The "invisible half of the wheel" is said to be from the Ascendant to the seventh house. As many planets as are there, that many women will be inside. Women equal to the planets from the 7th to the 12th house will be outside. If a planet is retrograde or in its exaltation, the number is tripled; if it is in its exaltation division <term>Navamsha</term>, its own division, or its own decan <term>Drekkana</term>, the number is doubled. || 75 ||

### Now, the Knowledge of the Native's Appearance and Form

**The body is like the lord of the Ascendant's ninth-division <term>Navamsha</term>, or like the most powerful planet.**
**The complexion is like the lord of the ninth-division occupied by the Moon; the limbs are distributed starting from the Ascendant.** || 76 ||

The body of the newborn should be described as similar to the lord of the specific ninth-division <term>Navamsha</term> of the birth Ascendant. Alternatively, the body should be described as similar to the strongest planet at that time. Or, the person born will have a complexion similar to the lord of the ninth-division in which the Moon is situated. Regarding "limbs distributed starting from the Ascendant": this means the limbs are divided starting from the head, corresponding to the Ascendant and subsequent houses. This is what is meant: just as previously the signs were established in the body of the "Time-Person" <note>The *Kala Purusha*, or cosmic man</note> starting with the head, face, heart, etc., here too, the twelve houses starting from the Ascendant are to be placed on the limbs of the newborn's body. Among them, in the large-scale measurement of the bodily instrument, a long sign will have a long-sign lord, and a short sign will have a short-sign lord; accordingly, the large or small proportions of the limbs should be described. || 76 ||

In the birth Ascendant, the form of the child should be described as similar to the planet whose ninth-division <term>Navamsha</term> is rising, or similar to whichever planet has the most strength among all planets. If the strength of the sign is greater, it follows the Ascendant's ninth-division; if the planet's strength is greater, it follows the planet's likeness. The child's complexion is known by the lord of the ninth-division where the Moon is placed. Here, the 12 houses starting from the Ascendant are applied to the 12 limbs starting from the head (just as the 12 signs were applied). The purpose is that the limb associated with a sign of "large measure" will be large, and the limb of a "small measure" sign will be small. However, this is only consistent if the lord of that sign, also being of large measure, is present in that large sign. (Commentary by Su. Jna. Kara) || 76 ||

**The throat, eyes, ears, nose, cheeks, chin, and face are the Ascendant and following—**
**Then the neck, shoulders, arms, sides, heart, chest, and navel.**
**Then the bladder, penis, and anus; then the testicles, thighs, and then the knees,**
**The calves and feet; the left side is indicated by the rising decans in three ways.** || 77 ||

Now, the three-fold classification of the houses in the body of the newborn according to the decans <term>Drekkana</term> <note>A 10-degree division of a zodiac sign</note> is explained. If the first decan is rising in the Ascendant, the division of limbs starts from the head; in the second decan, from the neck; and in the third decan, from the bladder. There, the left limbs are indicated by the setting signs (12, 11, 10, 9, 8, 7) and the right limbs by the rising houses (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6). For clarity, the "Human Wheel" diagram should be consulted; enough of this elaboration. || 77 ||

Therefore, according to these <term>Drekkana</term><note>A decan, or a 10-degree division of a zodiac sign; each sign has three</note>, the twelve houses are arranged in three sections. These are the divisions of the limbs according to the decans. In this system, the parts from the 1st to the 7th house are known as the right side of the body, and from the 7th to the 12th as the left side. || 77 ||

## Knowledge of Marks on the Body at Birth

> If a malefic planet is present in that part, one should predict a scar; if a benefic is present or aspecting, predict a mark like a mole. 
> If the planet is in its own sign or Navamsha, or in a fixed sign, the mark is present from birth; otherwise, it is acquired later in life. 
> Saturn causes marks from stones or wind; Mars from fire, weapons, or poison; Mercury from the earth. 
> The Sun causes marks from wood or four-legged animals; the Moon from horned animals or water-born creatures; others (benefics) cause auspicious marks. || 78 ||
> In whichever part three planets including Mercury are situated, 
> there will certainly be a mark, whether auspicious or inauspicious. 
> A malefic in the 6th house causes a scar on the body part corresponding to that sign; 
> if aspected or joined by benefics, it results in a mole or a beauty mark. || 79 ||

The purpose of the three-fold division of signs mentioned previously is now explained. In those parts (the head etc. in the first decan; the throat etc. in the second; the pelvis etc. in the third), if a malefic planet is situated, one should predict a <term>Vrana</term><note>A wound or scar</note>. If a benefic planet aspects or is joined there, one should predict a <term>Tilamashaka</term><note>A mole, freckle, or birthmark</note> on that part of the body. If the planet causing the scar is in its own sign or <term>Navamsha</term><note>A one-ninth division of a sign, used for fine-tuning predictions</note>...

# Chapter on Non-Human Births || 3 ||

If [the planet causing a mark] is in a fixed sign and a fixed <term>Navamsha</term><note>A one-ninth division of a zodiac sign, used for fine-tuning predictions</note>, then the scar or wound should be declared as present from birth. Otherwise—meaning in other signs or divisions—the scar or wound occurs later in life due to some external cause. The specific cause of such an accidental wound is determined by the planet involved. For instance, if Saturn is the cause, it is due to a stone or wind-related accident, and so forth; the meaning is straightforward. || 78 ||

Now, in whichever body part the three other planets (whether benefic or malefic) are situated along with Mercury, as previously shown, a wound or mark will certainly occur on that limb. A malefic planet in the sixth house from the <term>Ascendant</term><note>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the time of birth</note> causes a wound on the body. Where exactly? It is said: in the part of the body corresponding to that sixth house (according to the <term>Kalapurusha</term><note>The "Time-Person," a concept mapping zodiac signs to specific human body parts</note>). If that malefic in the sixth house is aspected by benefic planets, then a mole or a freckle appears. If it is joined with benefics, it results in a "Lakshman"—meaning a distinctive auspicious mark on that limb. || 79 ||

A malefic planet causes an injury or wound on whichever of the aforementioned limbs it occupies. If that malefic is also with a benefic or seen by one, then a mole, wart, or similar mark occurs. If the planet causing the wound is in its own sign or its own Navamsha, or in a fixed sign or fixed division, the mark will exist from birth. If not, the mark will appear later. If Saturn causes the mark, it comes from a stone or wind; if Mars, from fire, a weapon, or poison. If Mercury, from falling on the ground; if the Sun, from wood or a four-legged animal. If the Moon, the wound is caused by a horned animal or a water creature. Jupiter and Venus do not cause wounds; they are auspicious. || 78 ||

In whichever part—left or right—three planets (benefic or malefic) are joined with Mercury, a mark must be predicted on that limb. The wound or injury will occur during the <term>Dasha</term><note>Planetary period or cycle of influence</note> of the strongest among those planets. If a malefic is in the sixth house from the Ascendant, it will cause a wound on the limb corresponding to that sixth house according to the rule "the head of the Time-Soul." If the planet in the sixth house is aspected by a benefic, it causes a mole. If joined with a benefic, it creates a "good mark" on that limb. || 79 ||

# Chapter 4: On Arishta (Portents of Death)

### First, the uncertainty of lifespan within the first twelve years.

Now, the chapter on *Arishta* <note>Arishta refers to planetary combinations indicating misfortune, illness, or death, specifically in childhood.</note> is explained. Even if a long life is indicated, because death can occur for children within the first twelve years due to various causes, the author speaks of the uncertainty of life from birth until the twelfth year—

> For those born from a womb, the span of life cannot be determined with certainty until twelve years have passed. Due to the sinful deeds committed by the mother or the father, and because of *Bala-grahas* <note>Child-seizing spirits or planetary influences specifically affecting infants.</note>, the child meets its end. || 1 ||
> In the first four-year period, the child suffers due to the mother's unrighteousness; in the middle four years, due to the accumulation of sins earned by the father. In the final four years (up to twelve), the child meets destruction due to its own past faults. || 2 ||

For all living beings, even if there are yogas <note>astrological combinations</note> for long life, that lifespan should not be definitively predicted within twelve years of birth. This is because in that first twelve-year period, the child may die due to the sins of the mother and father and by child-seizing spirits. Specifically: in the first four years, death occurs by the mother's sins; in the second four-year period (ages 5–8), by the father's sins; and in the third four-year period (ages 9–12), the child meets death due to its own past faults (which manifest as *Balarishta*). Therefore, until the twelfth year, one should perform prayers, fire sacrifices, and other rituals to remove the inauspicious faults of children. As stated by the teacher Vaidyakuta: "The lifespan cannot be known until twelve years have passed. One should ensure the protection of the child through prayers, sacrifices, and medical treatments. Some die from the faults of parents, some from child-spirits, and others from *Arishta* yogas; thus, child death is of three kinds." || 1-2 ||

<margin>Within twelve years of birth, life cannot be certain because of parental sins and spirits. || 1 ||</margin>
<margin>The 12 years are divided into three parts of 4 years each: Mother's sin (0-4), Father's sin (4-8), and own sins (8-12). || 2 ||</margin>

### The divisions of lifespan based on Arishta.

> The wise say there are eight years of *Balarishta* (infant misfortune) at the start; then *Yogarishta* (misfortune from planetary combinations) lasts until twenty. "Short life" is up to thirty-two; "Middle life" is up to seventy; and "Full life" ends at a hundred. || 3 ||

The wise state that the first eight years are *Balarishta*. Following that, until the twentieth year, it is *Yogarishta* (caused by adverse planets). Thirty-two years is considered *Alpayu* (Short Life), seventy years is *Madhyamayu* (Middle Life), and one hundred years is *Purnayu* (Full Life). It will be said later: "The combination for Middle Life is from thirty-two years up to seventy," and "Full Life is from seventy to a hundred." Here, it should be understood that life beyond a hundred is also called Full Life. It is also said in the *Sarvartha Chintamani*:
"Before thirty-two is Short Life; beyond that is Middle Life. Up to seventy is the standard, and beyond that is considered Long Life. Those who know these matters praise a lifespan beyond a hundred as the best." || 3 ||

<margin>0-8: Balarishta; up to 20: Yogarishta; up to 32: Short; 32-70: Middle; 70-100: Full. 100-120 is the ultimate limit. || 3 ||</margin>

### Planetary positions causing Arishta.

> If the Moon is placed in the 6th, 8th, or 12th house from the Ascendant, and is aspected by malefic planets, the child meets death quickly. || 4 ||

---

<gloss>✽ Note on the text: In another version, the phrase "to determine the span" should be read instead of "to determine the time of birth."</gloss>

<note>Technical Vocabulary:
- **Arishta:** Ill-fortune or portents of death.
- **Balarishta:** Specifically refers to the danger of death in early childhood.
- **Yogarishta:** Death caused by specific mathematical combinations of planets.
- **Alpayu/Madhyamayu/Purnayu:** Categories of lifespan (Short, Middle, Full).
- **Japa-Homa:** Ritual chanting and fire offerings used as remedies.
- **Bala-graha:** "Child-seizers," supernatural or planetary forces believed to cause pediatric illnesses.</note>

<header>Chapter on Misfortune (Arishta) || 4 ||</header>

If at the time of birth the Moon is situated in any of the 6th, 8th, or 12th houses <note>These are the 'Dusthana' or difficult houses in a horoscope</note>, and is aspected by a malefic planet (**Mars, Saturn, Rahu, Ketu**) other than the Sun, the child meets with death even if Jupiter—the teacher of the gods—is positioned in the Ascendant (Lagna). By saying "even if the teacher of the gods is in the Ascendant," it is implied that usually, Jupiter in the Ascendant is a destroyer of misfortunes.

> "Jupiter alone, if strong and placed in the Ascendant, destroys a multitude of misfortunes, just as a bow to the Wielder of the Trident <note>Lord Shiva</note> destroys a multitude of sins."

However, if the Moon is in the 6th, 8th, or 12th house and is aspected by a malefic, then even with Jupiter in the Ascendant, the child's death is certain. The sense is that this is a "Powerful Misfortune" (Prabala Arishta) || 4 ||

-> If at the time of birth the Moon is in the 6th, 8th, or 12th house and is seen by a malefic planet (**Mars, Saturn, Rahu, Ketu**) other than the Sun, the child dies even if Jupiter is in the Ascendant; that is, this is a powerful misfortune yoga. <margin>Author of Mukta Shastra</margin> || 4 || <-

> If the Moon is joined with a Gandanta star <note>The transitional points between water and fire signs</note> and is aspected by or joined with a malefic, the child meets his end. Likewise, if the Moon is in a "Death Degree" (Mrityu-bhaga) and is aspected by a malefic, the child perishes || 5 ||

"Gandanta" refers to the previously mentioned junctions (**Ch. 1, Verse 22**). Their stars are: "The last two ghatikas <note>A unit of time, approx. 24 minutes</note> of Revati, Jyeshtha, and Ashlesha, and the first two ghatikas of Mula, Ashwini, and Magha." If the Moon is in any of these and is aspected by or joined with a malefic planet, the child goes to destruction = death. Alternatively, if the Moon is in the "Death Degree" of any sign (**see Ch. 1, Verse 57**) and is observed by a malefic planet, it results in the same = death || 5 ||

-> If the Moon is in a Gandanta Nakshatra and is aspected by or joined with a malefic, or if the Moon is in a Death Degree and aspected by a malefic, the child attains death (dies) || 5 || <-

### Now, the Misfortune Yogas for Father and Others.

> The father, mother, sibling, maternal uncle, maternal grandmother, maternal grandfather, and the child;
> These are quickly destroyed in order by the Sun and others when malefics occupy the 5th and 9th houses || 6 ||
> If the Sun and Moon are in the 4th house and Saturn is in the 7th, it leads to the death of the mother.
> Whenever a malefic planet from the Ascendant goes to the 6th house, it is the cause of a sibling's destruction || 7 ||
> If the Moon and the Ascendant sign are aspected by malefics and lack the aspect or association of benefics,
> And if the teacher of the Lord of Immortals <note>Jupiter</note> has fallen from the centers (Kendras), the mother of the newborn meets her end || 8 ||

Now the death yogas for the father and others are described. If the 5th or 9th house from the Ascendant is a malefic sign and the Sun or other planets are positioned there, one should predict the quick destruction of the father and others. Specifically: with the Sun, the father; with the Moon, the mother; with Mars, the sibling; with Mercury, the maternal uncle (mother's brother); with Jupiter, the maternal grandmother (mother's mother); with Venus, the maternal grandfather (mother's father); and with Saturn, the death of the child = the native himself occurs || 6 ||

Furthermore, if the Sun and Moon are in the 4th house from the Ascendant and Saturn is in the 7th house, this yoga causes the death of the mother. Similarly, a malefic planet in the 6th house from the Ascendant is the destroyer of a sibling. Here, the repetition of "whenever" suggests that a malefic in the 6th house during a transit year also destroys siblings || 7 ||

Now, another yoga for the mother's death: If the Ascendant and the Moon are both aspected by malefic planets and are neither aspected by nor associated with benefic planets, and Jupiter is not in a center (Kendra) <note>Houses 1, 4, 7, or 10</note>, then the mother of the newborn meets her destruction = she dies. Conversely, if the Moon is associated with or aspected by benefics and Jupiter is in a center, it will be auspicious for the mother || 8 ||

-> If the 5th or 9th houses are malefic signs and the Sun etc. are in them, then in order: father, mother, brother, uncle, maternal grandmother, maternal grandfather, and the child are <unclear>quickly</unclear> destroyed || 6 || <-

# With Commentary on Jataka Parijata

If the Sun and Moon are situated in the fourth house and Saturn is in the seventh, one should predict the death of the mother. If a malefic planet is in the sixth house from them, it causes the destruction of the brother. || 7 ||

If the Ascendant and the Moon are aspected by malefic planets and are not aspected by or associated with benefic planets, and if Jupiter is not in a quadrant <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note>, the mother of the newborn shall meet her end. || 8 ||

## Now, Combinations for Death During Pregnancy.

> If the Moon is with Saturn, the Sun is in the twelfth house from the Ascendant, and Mars is in the fourth house, then the mother dies while pregnant. || 9 ||

> If the Ascendant and the Moon are devoid of the aspect of benefics and are placed between inauspicious planets, all authorities say that the pregnant woman meets her end, whether these conditions occur together or separately. || 10 ||

> If malefic planets are in the sixth, twelfth, and eighth houses, devoid of benefic planets, or if Venus or Jupiter are placed between two malefics, the woman with her child dies immediately. || 11 ||

> If malefic planets are in the Ascendant and the seventh house, devoid of the association or aspect of benefics, the pregnant woman meets death by a weapon <note>This could refer to surgical intervention or injury</note> when the Lord of the Month is weak or afflicted. || 12 ||

Now, the combinations for the death of a woman endowed with virtue are described. Therefore, if the Moon is joined with Saturn and the Sun in the twelfth house, and Mars is in the fourth house, then the mother—meaning the mother of the fetus—being <term>pregnant</term> (sagarbhā) <term>perishes</term> (vipadyate), i.e., dies. This consideration is appropriate at the <term>time of conception</term> (niṣeka-kāla), as death while pregnant is not possible at the moment of delivery <note>meaning the state of being 'pregnant' ends at birth</note>. Therefore, if this combination occurs during <term>impregnation</term> (garbhādhāna), the death of the pregnant woman occurs. **Another combination**—If at the time of conception the Ascendant and the Moon are simultaneously in one place or separately devoid of the aspect of benefic planets and are situated between two malefic planets, then the pregnant woman meets death. It is also stated in the *Brihat Jataka*:

> "When the Ascendant and the Moon are situated between two malefics and are not aspected by benefics, whether together or separately, one should say the woman perishes while pregnant."

The death should be predicted in the month belonging to the strongest planet among those forming the combination. **Combinations for death while pregnant.**

Now, if malefic planets are in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth houses and no benefics are among them; or if Venus or Jupiter are between two malefics, then the woman with her child—meaning the woman along with her son—dies <term>immediately</term> (sadyaḥ), meaning right from the time of labor. This is a consideration for the time of birth. Even in <term>conception</term> (niṣeka), the death of the pregnant woman should be predicted from this combination. Now, if two malefic planets—Mars and the Sun—are respectively in the Ascendant—

## Combination for Death by Weapon.

—and the seventh house (meaning Mars is in the 1st and Sun is in the 7th), and if they are devoid of the association or aspect of benefic planets, then the pregnant woman meets death by a <term>weapon</term> (śastreṇa), such as a sword or sharp instrument, when the Lord of the Month (to be described in verse 17) is a destroyer or powerless. Here it is said—at the <term>time of conception</term>, whichever planet is weak, in the month over which it has lordship,

the pregnant woman meets death through a weapon. It is also stated in the *Brihat Jataka*—

<note>original: "सगर्भा, मरणयोग, निषेककाल, गर्भाधान, शस्त्रकृतमृत्यु, जातकपारिजात, बृहज्जातक"</note>
<note>The text references the 'Lord of the Month,' a concept in Vedic astrology where each month of pregnancy is ruled by a different planet; if that planet is weak, the pregnancy is at risk during that specific month.</note>

### Now, the combinations for the death of the mother of the newborn.

->If malefic planets are in the 4th or 10th house from the Moon, devoid of the aspect of benefics,<-

Now the combinations for the death of the mother of the newborn are explained. If malefic planets are in the 4th or 10th house from the Moon, devoid of benefic aspects and lacking strength, the mother of the child born at that time meets her end (death). Alternatively, if malefic planets are in the 10th house from the Sun <note>original: "Vasarekha"</note> and are devoid of benefic aspects, it should be said that the mother of the newborn meets death. Furthermore, if a strong Sun is aspected by or joined with Saturn and is in the 3rd house from Venus, or if the waning Moon joined with a malefic is in the 3rd from Venus, then the mother dies with the son (together) very soon—meaning at the time of delivery.

Furthermore, if the Sun or Mars is in the 8th house from the Ascendant, aspected by a malefic (Saturn) and devoid of benefic aspects, and the Moon <note>original: "Lord of the Stars"</note> is waning and set, then the mother of the newborn dies. Furthermore, if the birth occurs during the day and Mars is in the 9th or 7th sign from Venus, and is aspected there by a malefic (Sun or Saturn) and devoid of benefic association or aspect, and the Moon is weak, the mother of the newborn meets her destruction (dies). Similarly, if the birth occurs at night and Saturn <note>original: "Son of the Sun"</note> is in a trine (5th or 9th) from the Moon, aspected by a malefic (Sun or Mars) and devoid of benefic association or aspect, and the Moon is weak, the mother of the newborn meets death. > Saturn in a trine from the Moon indicates the death of the mother at night.
> Similarly, Mars in the same position from Venus during the day, aspected by a malefic, does the same. || 13-16 ||

# In the Jataka Parijata (with Commentary)
## Page 64

If in the 7th, 8th, or 10th month <note>referring to lunar months or houses from the Moon</note> there are malefic planets in the 8th house, and they are not aspected by benefic planets, the mother dies. Alternatively, if malefic planets are in the 10th from the Sun and are not aspected by benefics, the mother's death occurs.

If a strong Sun is aspected by or joined with Saturn and is in the 3rd or 8th from Venus, or if a waning Moon is with a malefic planet in the 3rd from Venus, the mother dies along with the child immediately upon delivery. || 14 ||

If the Sun or Mars is in the 8th from the birth <note>the Ascendant</note>, aspected by malefics and not seen by benefics, and the Moon is lacking in its increasing digits (the dark fortnight), then the mother of that newborn reaches the abode of Yama <note>original: "यमपदको प्राप्त हो"; meaning she dies</note>.

If the birth is during the day and the Sun is in the 9th or 5th from Venus, or if the birth is at night and Saturn is in the 9th or 5th from the Moon, and these are aspected by malefics without the aspect of benefics, and the Moon is powerless, then the mother is destroyed. || 16 ||

->**Now, the Lords of the Months of Gestation (from the Hora)**<-

**The embryo, the mass, the sprouts, the bones, the skin, the hair, and consciousness:
Venus, Mars, Jupiter, the Sun, the Moon, Saturn, and Mercury are the rulers. Thereafter,
The Lord of the Ascendant, the Moon, and the Sun are the lords respectively.
They declare good or bad fortune according to the nature of the lord of the month. || 17 ||**

Now, the lords of the ten months from conception <term>Nisheka: the act of impregnation</term> until delivery and the condition of the fetus are described. Starting from the first month, the conditions such as the embryo (kalala) and the planets such as Venus (Sita) are the lords of the months in sequence.

Namely: In the first month, the fetus is <term>Kalala: the mixing of semen and blood</term>; here Venus is the lord of the month. In the second month, it becomes a <term>Ghana: a solid mass or lump</term> as the semen and blood harden; here Mars is the lord of the month. In the third month, the <term>Ankura: sprouts</term> or the emergence of limbs like hands and feet occurs; here Jupiter is the lord. In the fourth month, the appearance of bones occurs; here the Sun is the lord. In the fifth month, the <term>Charma: skin</term> is produced; here the Moon is the lord. In the sixth month, the <term>Angraja: hair</term> appears; here Saturn is the lord. In the seventh month, <term>Chetanata: consciousness</term> or the emergence of life-breath occurs; here Mercury is the lord.

Thereafter, according to the saying in the *Laghu Jataka* <note>A foundational text by Varahamihira</note> "From eating, to agitation, to delivery": in the eighth month, <term>Ashana: eating</term> occurs, where the living being in the womb draws the essence of what the mother has eaten and drunk through the umbilical cord; here the <term>Adhana-Lagnesha: the Lord of the Ascendant at the time of conception</term> is the ruler. In the ninth month, agitation occurs; here the Moon is the lord of the month. In the tenth month, <term>Prasava: delivery</term> or birth takes place; here the Sun is the lord.

Regarding these, they declare good or bad results according to the nature of the month's lord. Whichever planet is strong at the time of conception, the fetus thrives in that planet's month. If a planet is "discolored" (weak), there is pain for the fetus in that month; likewise, if a planet is "afflicted" (oppressed), a miscarriage should be predicted in that month. As stated in the *Laghu Jataka*:

> "Pain from the turbid, a fall (miscarriage) from the oppressed, and nourishment from the clear (strong) planets." || 17 ||

When pregnancy occurs, in the first month the fluids boil. In the second month, they solidify into a lump. In the third month, sprouts (head, hands, feet) emerge. In the fourth month, bones are created. In the fifth month, skin is created. In the sixth month, hair; in the seventh month, consciousness (movement of head and limbs). The lords of these seven months are Venus, Mars, Jupiter, the Sun, the Moon, Saturn, and Mercury respectively. In the eighth month, the child eats what the mother eats. In the ninth month, the child stirs in the womb. In the tenth month, the child is born. The lord of the eighth month is the Lord of the Ascendant. The lord of the ninth is the Moon, and the lord of the tenth is the Sun. If the lord of the month is afflicted, it causes miscarriage in its month; if weak, it causes pain; if strong, it provides nourishment. || 17 ||

# Chapter 4: On Omens of Misfortune (Arishta)

### On the Comfort of the Fetus

> If the Moon and the Ascendant are occupied by benefic planets, or if benefics are placed in the trines, the seventh, the second, the fourth, or the tenth houses, and if malefic planets are in the third, eleventh, or twelfth houses, the fetus remains healthy and happy, provided it is aspected by the Sun. || 18 ||

Now the combination for the nourishment of the fetus is explained. Where the Moon <note>original: "Shashanka"</note> is located at the time of conception or birth, if benefic planets are present there—either together or separately—or if benefics are placed in the following positions from the Ascendant or the Moon: the trines (5th and 9th), the seventh <note>wife/partner's house</note>, the second <note>wealth</note>, the fourth <note>happiness/home</note>, or the tenth <note>profession/sky</note> houses; and if malefic planets are in the third, eleventh, or twelfth <insert>(3, 11)</insert> houses from the Moon or Ascendant, and the fetus is aspected by the Sun, it remains healthy. This means that in the aforementioned combination, if the Ascendant or the Moon is seen by the Sun, the fetus is "happy," meaning it will be delivered easily. As stated in the *Saravali* <note>A classical 8th-century astrological treatise by Kalyanavarman</note>:
-> "With benefics joined with the Ascendant or Moon, or placed in the trines, seventh, fourth, tenth, or second houses, and malefics in the third, eleventh, and twelfth, the fetus is happy if aspected by the Sun." || 18 || <-

If at the time of conception the Ascendant and Moon are together or separate, joined by benefics, and benefics are in the 5, 9, 7, 2, 4, or 10 positions from them, and malefics are in the 3 or 11, and the Ascendant or Moon is aspected by the Sun, the fetus remains healthy. (According to the author of *Suka Jataka*) || 18 ||

### On the Combinations for the Father's Death

> If the Sun is in the twelfth house along with Saturn, and the waning Moon is in the seventh house from the Ascendant, the wise declare the separation from the father. If aspected by a benefic, this occurs within three years. || 19 ||

> If the Moon is in a movable sign during a night birth and is aspected by Mercury, the father dies in a distant land. If Saturn is in a movable sign joined with the Sun during a night birth, the father dies in a foreign country. || 20 ||

Now the combinations for the death of the newborn's father are explained. If the Sun is with Saturn <note>original: "Sasute," literally 'with the son' (Saturn is the son of the Sun)</note> in the twelfth house from the birth Ascendant, and the waning Moon <note>original: "Kshayendu"</note> is in the seventh house, the wise say there will be an immediate separation from the father (death). In this combination, if there is an aspect from a benefic planet, the father's death occurs within three years. || 19 ||

<margin>Combinations for the father's death.</margin>

#### On the Death of a Father Residing Abroad at Birth

If the birth occurs at night <note>original: "Kshapayam"</note> and the Moon is in a movable sign <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn</note> and is aspected by Mercury, the child's father dies having gone to a distant region. Alternatively, if the birth is at night and Saturn is in a movable sign joined with the Sun, the father dies while in a foreign land. || 20 ||

If Sun and Saturn are in the 12th house and the waning Moon is in the 7th, know the father's separation is immediate. If benefics aspect them, know the separation occurs in three years. || 19 ||

In a night birth, if Mercury aspects the Moon in a movable sign, say the father dies in a far country. If Saturn is with the Sun in a movable sign at night, the father's destruction occurs abroad. || 20 ||

### On the Combinations for the Infant's Death

> If the waning Moon is in the Ascendant and malefic planets are in the angles or the eighth house, the child dies. If benefics are in the eighth or sixth houses and aspected by malefics, the child reaches the city of Death within a month. || 21 ||

Now the combinations for the death of the newborn are explained. If the Moon is waning (weak) and in the Ascendant, and a malefic is in an angle <note>1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th house</note> or in the eighth house, the newborn...

The child dies. This is because of the scriptural teaching: "If the Moon is waning in the Ascendant <note>Lagna</note> and malefic planets are in the quadrants <note>Kendra</note> or the eighth house <note>Randhra</note>, death occurs." Furthermore, if the benefics <note>Saumya</note> are situated in the eighth or sixth houses and are aspected by malefic planets, the newborn child reaches the city of Death <note>Yama-puri</note> within a month. In this combination, the child lives for one month and dies thereafter. || 21 ||

*If the waning Moon is in the Ascendant, and malefic planets are in the quadrants or the eighth house, the child may die. If benefics in the eighth or sixth houses are aspected by malefics, that child goes to the abode of Yama within one month.* || 21 ||

->If Saturn, Mars, and the Sun are together in the eighth house or the sixth house,<-
->and are neither joined with nor aspected by benefics, they cause the immediate death of the newborn.<- || 22 ||

If Saturn, Mars, and the Sun—these three malefics—are joined together in the eighth house <note>Randhra-sthita</note> or the sixth house <note>Ripu-rashi-yata</note>, and if they are not joined with or aspected by benefics <note>Saumya</note>, then they cause the immediate death of the newborn. This means the child dies as soon as they are born under this combination. || 22 ||

*If Saturn, Mars, and the Sun are together in the eighth or sixth house and are not joined with or aspected by a benefic planet, they provide immediate death for the native.* || 22 ||

->If Mars is in the seventh house in the Navamsha <note>a 1/9th divisional chart</note> of the Moon,<-
->and is devoid of any aspect from a benefic, the infant meets death in the seventy-seventh star.<- || 23 ||
->If Saturn, Mars, and the Sun are joined in the house of children <note>the 5th house</note>,<-
->one should predict the death of the newborn in the seventy-seventh star.<- || 24 ||

If Mars <note>Bhauma</note> is in the seventh house from the Ascendant and is positioned in a Navamsha belonging to the Moon, and is without the aspect of a benefic, then the child born will die in the seventy-seventh star <note>Tara</note>. This means from the birth star, counting to the seventy-seventh star—which is the twenty-third star of the third cycle—death occurs. For example, one born in Ashwini would die in Dhanishta of the third cycle. Similarly, if Saturn, Mars, and the Sun—these three—are joined in the house of children <note>Putra-sthana</note>, meaning the fifth house, one should predict the death of the infant in the seventy-seventh star. || 23-24 ||

*If Mars is in the seventh house in the Moon's Navamsha and is without the aspect of a benefic planet, the child dies in the 77th star.* || 23 ||
*If Saturn, Mars, and the Sun are in the house of children (5th house), the death of the native occurs in the 77th star.* || 24 ||

->If Mars is in a Navamsha of the Moon or in the Navamsha of the Ascendant,<-
->and is not aspected by Jupiter, while the Moon is in the house of children,<-
->the child quickly reaches the abode of Yama <note>the God of Death</note>.<- || 25 ||

If Mars <note>Dharasuta</note> is in a Navamsha of the Moon anywhere, or in the Navamsha of the Ascendant <note>Lagnamsha</note>, and is not aspected by Jupiter <note>Jiva</note>, and the Moon <note>Sudhakara</note> has gone to the house of children <note>Nandana-rashi</note>, meaning the fifth house, the child born quickly reaches the place of Yama <note>the end of life</note>; this means they die. || 25 ||

*If Mars is in the Moon's Navamsha or the Ascendant's Navamsha without the aspect of Jupiter, and the Moon is in the fifth house, the child dies.* || 25 ||

# Chapter on Portents of Death (Arishta) || 4 ||

### Chapter on Portents of Death || 4 ||

> If the <term>Lord of the Ascendant</term> <note>The planet ruling the first house of the horoscope</note> is in its sign of debilitation, or if it occupies the eighth house from the Ascendant, and likewise if <term>Saturn</term> <note>literally: "Son of the Sun"</note> is similarly debilitated or set in the seventh house, the person born will have a body as if dead, suffering greatly, and will reach the realm of <term>Yama</term> <note>The God of Death; literally: "the world of Vivasvat's son"</note> with much difficulty. || 26 ||

The <term>Lord of the Ascendant</term> = the ruler of the first house, being in its <term>debilitation</term> = its weakest zodiacal sign, or occupying the <term>eighth house</term> <note>original: vilagnābhāṃśaṃ</note>, and <term>Saturn</term> = the planet Shani, being likewise in its sign of debilitation or in the seventh house—the child born under such conditions will have a body like a corpse = a body afflicted by various pains, and with great agony will go to the realm of Vivasvat = the city of the dead; this means the child dies.

---

->In another text:<-

> "If the Lord of the Ascendant is debilitated and the Son of the Sun (Saturn) is in the eighth house, one should know that life is maintained with great difficulty, and the child perishes as if already dead."

This is seen in other works. However, since it is stated elsewhere (Chapter 2, Verse 52) that Saturn in the eighth house usually grants favorable results, the interpretation of Saturn being in the seventh house is more appropriate here, as it is also said (Chapter 2, Verse 72) that "Saturn in the seventh house is fruitless." || 26 ||

If the <term>Lord of the Ascendant</term> is in a debilitated sign or in the eighth from the Ascendant, and Saturn is likewise debilitated and in the seventh, the body of the born child, afflicted like a corpse, goes to the house of Yama. || 26 ||

> If the <term>planets</term> <note>literally: "sky-goers"</note>, led by the Sun, are devoid of strength and are situated in <term>Apoklima</term> houses <note>The 3rd, 6th, 9th, and 12th houses, considered weak positions in classical astrology</note>, those who know the science say the life of the newborn will last only two months or three seasons <note>six months</note>. || 27 ||

If the <term>planets</term> = the celestial bodies, led by the Sun and others, are "shaken of their power" = weak, and are residing in the <term>Apoklima</term>—(3rd, 6th, 9th, 12th) positions, then the experts = the wise, declare the lifespan of that child to be two months or three seasons = six months. It is also stated in the <term>Shukra Jataka</term>:

> "When all planets are situated in Apoklima houses and are devoid of strength, the lifespan is declared to be either six months or two months." || 27 ||

Here is an example—Sun = 5s 3° 15'; Moon = 5s 2° 10'; Mars = 8s 9° 20'; Mercury = 5s 2° 15'; Jupiter = 2s 3° 15'; Venus = 5s 20° 30'; Saturn = 11s 4° 20'; Rahu = 8s 12° 15'. This is how the example is calculated. || 27 ||

If weak planets like the Sun and others are in <term>Apoklima</term> (3, 6, 9, 12), the wise say the lifespan of that child is two or six months. || 27 ||

> If the <term>Moon</term> <note>literally: "the rabbit-marked"</note> is in the <term>Ascendant, 6th, 8th, or 12th houses</term>, aspected by a malefic planet and lacking the aspect of a benefic planet, and the <term>Angles</term> <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</note> are devoid of benefic planets, the newborn departs from their life. || 28 ||

If the <term>Moon</term> = Chandra, is in any of the houses—Ascendant, 6th, 8th, or 12th—and is seen by any malefic planet while being devoid of the sight of benefic planets, and if the <term>Angles</term> (1, 4, 7, 10) are empty of benefic planets, the child born goes to a separation from life = death. This is also heard in the tradition: "When the Moon is in the 12th, 8th, 6th, or the rising sign, joined with a malefic and lacking benefic aspect." || 28 ||

If the Moon is in the Ascendant, 6th, 8th, or 12th, and malefic planets see it while it is devoid of the aspect of benefics, that child shall die. || 28 ||

# With the Commentary on Jataka Parijata—

->If Saturn is in the seventh house or in the ascendant, and the Moon is in a watery sign or in Scorpio,<-
->while benefic planets are in the angles, the death of the newborn occurs quickly, as taught by the Greeks. [Verse 29]<-

If Saturn is in the seventh house or the ascendant (1st house); the Moon is in a watery sign <note>Signs like Cancer, Capricorn, or Pisces</note> or in Scorpio; and the benefic planets <note>Jupiter, Venus, or Mercury</note> are in the angles (houses 1, 4, 7, or 10), the death of the newborn should be declared as occurring very quickly, according to the teachings of the Great Teacher of the Greeks <note>original: "Yavanacharya"; refers to the historical influence of Greco-Egyptian astrology on Indian systems</note>. [29]

If Saturn is in the 7th or 1st house, the Moon is in a watery sign or Scorpio, and benefics are in the angles, the person born will be destroyed quickly. [29]

->If Jupiter is in a sign owned by Mars or in its sign of debilitation,<-
->and the birth occurs during the three twilights, the child meets death within a month. [30]<-

If Jupiter is in a sign of Mars (Aries or Scorpio) or in its sign of debilitation (Capricorn), and the child is born during the "three twilights"—the first twilight being 72 minutes <note>original: "3 ghatis"</note> before sunrise; the middle twilight being 36 minutes before and after midday; and the evening twilight being 72 minutes after sunset—the child born then meets death within a month; he lives for one month and then dies. In the variation "at the three junctions" <note>original: "Sandhitraye"</note>, it refers to the junctions between Cancer/Leo, Scorpio/Sagittarius, and Pisces/Aries. As stated in the *Sarvartha Chintamani*:

> "If Jupiter is in its debilitation or in a sign of Mars,
> and birth occurs during the three junctions, it grants death within a month." [30]

If Jupiter is in the house of Mars or in its debilitated sign (Capricorn), and birth occurs in any of the three twilights, that person will die in one month. [30]

->If Mars, the Sun, and Saturn are in the eighth house, the newborn meets death within a month.<-
->If Ketu has risen in the birth star, the one born there goes to the God of Death in just two months. [31]<-

If Mars, the Sun, and Saturn are present in the eighth house from the birth ascendant, the child born attains death within a month. Furthermore, in whichever lunar mansion <note>Nakshatra</note> Ketu <note>the South Node of the Moon</note> has risen (see the commentary on Chapter 2, Verse 68), a child born in that mansion goes to Yama <note>the God of Death</note>—meaning he dies—within two months. It is said in the *Saravali*:

> "If Mars, the Sun, and Saturn are in the house of death (8th) or in a house of Mars, the man surely dies within a month, even if protected by the God of Death himself.
> He who is born in the lunar mansion where Ketu has risen,
> one should predict death for that newborn within two months." [31]

If Mars, the Sun, and Saturn are in the eighth house, that person will die in one month. The child born in the lunar mansion in which Ketu rises finds death in 2 months. [31]

->If two malefic planets are in the ascendant and the seventh, and the Moon is joined with a cruel planet,<-
->and is not aspected by benefics, death will occur before long. [32]<-

## Chapter on Inauspicious Signs (Arishta) || 4 ||

> "When a malefic planet is in the Ascendant <note>Lagna: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</note> and another is in the seventh house <note>the house of setting</note>, and the Moon is joined with a cruel planet and lacks the aspect <note>astrological gaze or influence</note> of any benefic planet, then the newborn shall meet death immediately; it cannot be otherwise." || 32 ||

If malefic planets occupy both the first and seventh houses, and the Moon is joined by a cruel planet while not being seen by any auspicious planets, the child will die quickly. || 32 ||

> "If the waning Moon is in the twelfth house, and malefic planets are in the first and eighth houses, and no benefic planets are in the angles <note>Kendra: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</note>, one should predict swift death." || 33 ||

Simple meaning of the verse: || 33 ||

If the waning Moon is in the 12th house, malefic planets are in the 1st and 8th houses, and there are no auspicious planets in the angles, know that death will occur soon. || 33 ||

---

> "The Moon, joined with a cruel planet and situated in the 7th, 12th, 8th, or 1st house, brings death if it is not seen by benefic planets located outside of the angles." || 34 ||

<margin>If the Moon is joined by a malefic planet and is placed in any of the houses—7th, 12th, 8th, or 1st—and is not observed by benefic planets situated outside the angles (meaning in houses other than 1, 4, 7, or 10), it causes death. Therefore, if benefics were in the angles, death would not occur.
Similarly, in the *Saravali* <note>A classic 8th-century Sanskrit text on astrology by Kalyanavarman</note>:</margin>

> "When the Moon is in the 12th, 8th, 7th, or 1st house, joined with malefics and devoid of a benefic's aspect, and the angles are empty of auspicious planets, it causes the immediate destruction of the newborn." || 34 ||

If the Moon, joined by a cruel planet, is in the 7th, 12th, 8th, or 1st house, and auspicious planets are neither in the angles nor casting their sight upon it, then that child shall die. || 34 ||

> "If the Moon is in the 6th or 8th house and is seen by a malefic, death comes quickly. If seen by a benefic, life lasts eight years; if seen by both <note>mixed</note>, life lasts half that—four years. If seen by powerful malefics while a benefic is in the 6th or 8th, life lasts one month. Likewise, if the Lord of the Ascendant is with the 7th Lord..." || 35 ||

If the Moon is in either the 6th or 8th house and is observed by a malefic planet, death occurs quickly. However, if the Moon in the 6th or 8th is seen by a benefic, the lifespan is eight years. If that same Moon is seen by "mixed" planets (both malefic and benefic), then it is half of eight—meaning the child lives four years and then dies. Therefore, if the Moon in the 6th or 8th is not seen by anyone, there is no *Arishta* <note>ill-fortune</note>. Furthermore, if a benefic is in the 6th or 8th house but is seen by powerful malefic planets, the child lives for one month. Likewise, if the Lord of the Ascendant <note>the planet ruling the rising sign</note> is with the spouse-house lord <note>7th lord</note>...

# With the Commentary on Jataka Parijata

If the Moon is in the **seventh house** <note>the house of partnerships and death-inflicting power</note> and is **defeated by a malefic** <note>original: "papa-vijite" — losing in a planetary war to a naturally harmful planet like Mars or Saturn</note>, the child lives for only one month and then dies. However, a specific exception should be noted here: if the birth occurs during the **bright fortnight at night**, or during the **dark fortnight during the day**, the Moon situated in the sixth or eighth house does not cause harm to the newborn, even if aspected by both beneficial and harmful planets.

> "If birth occurs in the bright half of the lunar month at night, or in the dark half during the day, the Moon—even if placed in the house of enemies (6th) or death (8th) and viewed by both good and evil planets—protects the infant from calamities with effort, like a father, and does not kill." — as stated in the verse. || 35 ||

<note>The Hindi commentary clarifies: If the Moon is in the 6th or 8th house and seen by malefics, the child dies quickly. If seen by benefics, death occurs in eight years. If benefics in those same houses are overpowered by strong malefics, or if the Moon is in the 7th house defeated by a malefic, death occurs in 1 month.</note>

->**If the Moon is eclipsed and joined by a malefic, and Mars is in the house of death,**<-
->**Both mother and child die; if the Sun is in the ascendant, death is by a weapon.**<-
->**When the Sun or Moon rises in the ascendant, and malefics are in the trines or the house of death,**<-
->**Death occurs if they are strong and not joined or seen by benefics.**<- || 36 ||

If the Moon is with a **malefic** <note>specifically Saturn</note> and is **eclipsed** <note>original: "graste" — joined with Rahu, the North Node</note> in the **ascendant** <note>the 1st house/rising sign</note>, and **Mars** is in the **house of death** <note>the 8th house</note>, then both the mother and the child die. If the **Sun** is in this position, the death of mother and child is caused by **weapons** <note>original: "sashastra-jah" — such as a sword or surgical instrument</note>. Here, "joined by a malefic" in relation to the Sun should be interpreted as being with Saturn, Mercury, or the Moon, as Mercury and the Moon can also take on a malefic nature in certain conditions.

Furthermore, if the **Sun** or the **Moon** is in the **ascendant**, and **malefics** are in the **trines** <note>the 5th or 9th houses</note> or the **house of death** (8th), and these malefics are **strong** while the Sun or Moon is not joined or aspected by **benefics** <note>Jupiter, Venus, or Mercury</note>, the death of the newborn must be predicted. As it is said:

> "When the Moon is eclipsed, a malefic is in the ascendant, and Mars is in the 8th, the child dies with the mother. If the Sun is in the Moon's place, death is by a weapon. If the Moon or Sun is in the ascendant and strong malefics are in the trines or the 8th, without the sight or company of benefics, the Yavana masters declare immediate death."

By implication, if in these combinations the Sun or Moon is joined or seen by powerful benefics, the misfortune is canceled. || 36 ||

<note>The Hindi summary repeats: Eclipsed Moon + malefic in 1st house and Mars in 8th = death of mother and child. Sun in 1st house = death by weapon. Sun/Moon in 1st and strong malefics in 5th, 9th, or 8th without benefic help = immediate death.</note>

->**When Saturn, the Sun, the Moon, and Mars occupy the 12th, 9th, 1st, and 8th houses,**<-
->**Death of living beings occurs quickly if they are not aspected by a strong Jupiter.**<- || 37 ||

# Chapter on Portents of Death (Arishta) || 4 ||

If the planets are not aspected <note>original: "na vīkṣitāḥ"; seen or influenced by the astrological gaze</note> by a strong Jupiter <note>original: "Guru"</note>, then for living beings, death occurs very quickly.
As it is said:
> "If the Moon, Sun, Saturn, and Mars are joined in the twelfth, ninth, first, or eighth houses,
> they cause the death of the newborn immediately, provided they are not aspected by Jupiter."

This is according to the traditional teachings.

In this context, it is impossible for all planets situated in the twelfth, ninth, ascendant <note>Lagna</note>, and eighth houses to be simultaneously ignored by Jupiter's gaze. Therefore, some may be seen and others not. In such a combination, death is not immediate but occurs after some time. If Saturn, the Sun, the Moon, and Mars are situated in the twelfth, ninth, ascendant, and eighth houses respectively (not necessarily in that exact order), and if all are not seen by Jupiter, then the combination is possible. Here, if Jupiter is in the fifth house, he would see all of them, and the <term>Arishta</term> <note>a planetary combination indicating misfortune or death</note> would be neutralized. Refer to the chart. || 37 ||

<note>The following paragraph is a translation of the preceding Sanskrit commentary into Hindi.</note>

If Saturn is in the 12th, the Sun in the 9th, the Moon in the Ascendant, and Mars in the 8th, and a strong Jupiter does not aspect them, the child dies quickly. If Jupiter aspects some and not others, it is merely a portent of ill fortune. A weak Jupiter, even if he aspects them all, does not provide a <term>Parihara</term> <note>remedy or cancellation of an ill omen</note>. If Jupiter is in the 5th house, he will be able to see all the houses (1st, 9th, 12th, 8th). Then the cancellation of the defect should be understood. || 37 ||

**The Moon, joined with a malefic planet and placed in the fifth, seventh, ninth, twelfth, first, or eighth house, leads to death, provided it is not joined with or aspected by strong Venus, Mercury, or Jupiter. || 38 ||**

"Joined with a malefic" means with a naturally harmful planet. "Cold-rayed" refers to the Moon. If the Moon is in the fifth, seventh, ninth, twelfth, first, or <unclear>eighth house</unclear> and is not associated with or seen by the three natural benefics—Venus, Mercury, and Jupiter—in a strong state, it becomes the cause of death for the newborn.
As stated in the *Saravali* <note>A classic 8th-century astrological treatise by Kalyanavarman</note>:
> "Malefics in the eighth, seventh, twelfth, first, or trine houses, joined with a waning Moon
> and not seen by strong benefics, bring about the end of life." || 38 ||

If the Moon is joined with a malefic planet and is in the 5th, 7th, 9th, 12th, 1st, or 8th house, and strong Venus, Mercury, and Jupiter do not aspect it, the child's death occurs quickly.

->Concerning death within a year.<-

**When the Moon reaches the position of the strongest planet in the combination, or its own sign, or the ascendant sign, and is aspected by a strong malefic, death occurs within a year; so it is said by the Sages. || 39 ||**

Now, the timing for portents whose duration was not previously specified is explained. In an <term>Arishta Yoga</term> <note>unfavorable planetary alignment</note> of unspecified timing, when the Moon reaches the sign occupied by the strongest planet in that yoga, or when the Moon reaches its own sign (Cancer), or the sign of the Ascendant, death should be predicted within a year. The meaning is this: among the planets causing the ill omen at birth, whichever is strongest—when the Moon in its transit reaches the sign where that planet was placed, or when the Moon returns to its birth position, or when it reaches the sign of the birth ascendant, death occurs within a year. In all three cases, the planet must be strong. The implication is that in an unspecified Arishta, the subject does not live beyond a year.

<summary>This page details specific planetary alignments involving the Moon and malefic planets that predict infant mortality, while emphasizing that a strong Jupiter can neutralize these "Arishta" omens. It also provides a method for timing death within a year based on the Moon's transit over key points in the birth chart.</summary>

<page-num>102</page-num>
<header>In the Jataka Parijata with Commentary—</header>

Now, one might ask: since the Moon passes through all zodiac signs every month, why is it said that death occurs at the end of a year? The answer is that it happens not merely when the Moon passes through those signs, but when it is strong <note>possessing high positional or temporal strength</note> and simultaneously aspected <note>influenced by the gaze of</note> by malefic planets. In whichever month the strong Moon, aspected by malefics, reaches the previously mentioned positions during its transit, death will certainly occur. This has been stated by the ancient sages. It is also said in the *Saravali* <note>A foundational 8th-century astrological text by Kalyanavarman</note>:

> "When the Moon reaches the position of the strongest planet in the yoga, or its own sign, or the Ascendant, and is strong yet aspected by malefics, the time of death shall be at the end of the year." || 39 ||

In cases where the specific timing for the results of *Arishta* <note>ill-fortune or planetary afflictions</note> is not written, the affliction will occur when the transiting Moon reaches the sign of the strongest planet among those forming the combination. Alternatively, the ancient sages have said that if the Moon, while strong and aspected by malefic planets, transits through its own sign or the Ascendant sign, death occurs within one year. (S. Sh. Kar) <note>Translator/Commentator's initials</note> || 39 ||

# On a Life Span of Two Years

> If retrograde Saturn occupies a house of Mars and is situated in a quadrant, the house of an enemy, or the house of destruction, and is aspected by a powerful Mars, the child born lives for two years. || 40 ||

When Saturn is retrograde <note>appearing to move backward from Earth's perspective</note> and is placed in a house of Mars (Aries or Scorpio), and is located in a quadrant (1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses), or in the house of enemies (6th house), or the house of destruction (8th house), and is aspected by Mars who has attained full strength, then the newborn child lives for two years and dies thereafter. || 40 ||

If retrograde Saturn is in a house of Mars (1 or 8) and is in a quadrant, or in the 6th or 8th house, and is seen by a strong Mars, a child born at such a time lives for up to two years. || 40 ||

# On a Life Span of Three Years

> Jupiter in a house of Mars, situated in the eighth house, with its form aspected by the Sun, Moon, Mars, and Saturn, and devoid of the aspect of Venus, brings the newborn to the other world in three years. || 41 ||

When Jupiter, located in a house of Mars, is in the eighth house from the Ascendant, and its form is aspected by—that is, it is seen by—the Sun, Moon, Mars, and Saturn, and is also devoid of the aspect of Venus <note>original: *Bhargava*, a name for Venus as the descendant of Bhrigu</note>, then it brings the newborn child to the other world, meaning it causes death, in three years. It is stated in another text:

> "Jupiter in Aries or Scorpio in the eighth house, aspected by the celestial bodies but without Venus, causes death after three years. Similarly, retrograde Saturn in the sixth or eighth house aspected by a strong Mars causes death in two years." || 41 ||

If Jupiter is in the eighth house in a sign of Mars (this combination is possible in Aries or Scorpio Ascendants) and is aspected by the Sun, Moon, Mars, and Saturn, but not by Venus, that child will die in three years. || 41 ||

<summary>This page details specific planetary configurations (yogas) that predict short life spans of one, two, or three years for a newborn, emphasizing the roles of retrograde Saturn, Jupiter in Mars' signs, and the lack of protective aspects from Venus.</summary>

### Now, Death in the Fourth Year.

> If Mercury is in Cancer, occupying the sixth or eighth house from the Ascendant, and is aspected by the Moon, the person born—even if endowed with all strength—meets their end in four years. || 42 ||

->Lifespan of 4 years<-

When Mercury <note>original: "Saumya"</note> is situated in the sign of Cancer <note>original: "Karkirashi"</note> and is in the 6th or 8th house from the birth ascendant, and is aspected <note>viewed by the astrological "glance"</note> by the Moon <note>original: "Sudharashmi," literally "the nectar-rayed one"</note>, the person born, even if they possess full physical vitality, will meet their end—meaning death—within four years. So it is said in the *Saravali* <note>A classical 8th-century astrological treatise by Kalyanavarman</note>:
“Mercury in the house of Cancer, situated in the 6th or 8th from the rising sign, with its form seen by the Moon, kills within four years.” || 42 ||

*If Mercury is in Cancer in the 6th or 8th from the birth ascendant and the Moon sees it, the child dies in the fourth year even if fully healthy.* || 42 ||

---

### Now, Death in the Fifth Year.

> With the Sun, Moon, Mars, and Jupiter together in one place; or with Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, and the Moon together; or with the Sun, Saturn, Mars, and the Moon; death surely occurs in five years. || 43 ||

Wherever there is a conjunction of the Sun, Moon, Mars, and Jupiter; or a conjunction of Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, and the Moon; or a conjunction of the Sun, Saturn, Mars, and the Moon, death certainly occurs within five years. On this, Gunakara says:
“By the Sun, the Moon, and the son of the Earth <note>Mars</note> joined together in one house; or by the son of the Sun <note>Saturn</note>, Jupiter, and Venus <note>Note: the Sanskrit commentary mentions Venus here, though the primary verse lists the Moon</note>, death comes in exactly five years.” || 43 ||

*If Sun-Moon-Mars-Jupiter are together, or Mars-Jupiter-Saturn-Moon are together, or Sun-Saturn-Mars-Moon are together, they cause the child's death in 5 years.* || 43 ||

---

### Now, a Lifespan of Six Years.

> When Saturn is placed in a Navamsha <note>a 1/9th divisional sign</note> belonging to the Moon, and is aspected by the Moon, and the Lord of the Ascendant is also joined with the Moon's sight, the lifespan of the one born is limited to six years. || 44 ||

->Lifespan of 6 years<-

When—at the time of birth—Saturn <note>original: "Manda," the slow-mover</note> is anywhere in a *Navamsha* of the Moon, and is aspected by the Moon <note>original: "Shitakara," the cool-rayed one</note>, and the Lord of the Ascendant is also aspected by the Moon, then the lifespan of the newborn is measured at six years. After that, they pass away. || 44 ||

*If Saturn is in the Moon's Navamsha and is seen by...*

## On Death in the Seventh Year

> If the *Drekkana* <note>A decan, or 10-degree division of a zodiac sign</note> rising in the Ascendant is of the type known as *Nigala* (fetters), *Ahi* (serpent), *Vihanga* (bird), or *Pashadhara* (noose-bearer), and is joined by a malefic planet and not aspected by its own Lord, it leads to death in seven years. || 45 ||

If any one of the *Drekkanas* named *Nigala*, *Ahi*, *Vihanga*, or *Pashadhara* is at the birth-ascendant, and if it is occupied by a malefic planet and not aspected by its own Lord (the ruler of that decan), then it becomes the cause of death for the newborn within seven years. So says Gunakara:

> "The *Drekkanas* of the Serpent, Jackal, Noose, and Bird, if rising in the Ascendant with malefic planets and not aspected by their lords, grant death in seven years."

<margin>Death in 7 years</margin>
Here, the *Nigala*, *Ahi*, *Vihanga*, and *Pasha Drekkanas* are to be understood by the verse to be mentioned later (Chapter 5, Verse 55): "The middle, last, and first decans of Cancer, Pisces, and Scorpio are the Serpents. The second of Scorpio is the Noose, the first of Capricorn is the Fetters, and the first of Leo is the Bird." || 45 ||

If in the Ascendant there is a *Nigala*, *Ahi*, or *Pashadhara* decan joined with a cruel planet and not aspected by its own lord, the child dies in seven years. || 45 ||

---

## On Death in the Seventh or Eighth Year

> If the Sun, Saturn, and Mars are in the Ascendant, and a waning Moon is in the seventh house in a sign of Venus, and is not aspected by the Teacher of the Gods (Jupiter), death occurs in either seven or eight years. || 46 ||

In the birth-ascendant there should be the Sun, Saturn, and Mars; a waning Moon should be in the seventh house in a sign of Venus (meaning Libra). Venus has two houses, Taurus and Libra, but since the Moon is exalted in Taurus, taking Libra is more appropriate. The seventh sign is Libra, hence "in the seventh house in a sign of Venus" is stated. Some explain this as the waning Moon being in the seventh house in any sign of Venus. However, that is not my view. When the Sun is in the Ascendant, the Moon in the seventh would be full, not waning; therefore, the wise must deliberate on this <note>The commentator is pointing out an astronomical contradiction: if the Sun is in the 1st house and Moon in the 7th, it is a Full Moon, not a waning one</note>. If such a Moon is not aspected by Jupiter, then death occurs in seven or eight years. || 46 ||

If the Sun, Saturn, and Mars are in the Ascendant, and the waning Moon in the 7th house (Venus's sign) is not aspected by Jupiter, the child dies in seven or eight years. || 46 ||

---
