### Regarding Death in the Eighteenth Year
> If the Lord of the 8th house and the Lord of the Ascendant <note>Lagna</note> have exchanged signs, and neither are benefic planets,
> Or if they are situated in the 12th or 6th houses and are not aspected by Jupiter, the person dies in their eighteenth year. || 58 ||

The Lord of the 8th house <term>Randhresha: the planet ruling the house of death</term>, and the Lord of the Ascendant <term>Lagnadhipati: the planet ruling the first house/self</term>—if these two are not benefics (meaning they are malefic or lack association with auspicious planets) and have exchanged signs (the Lord of the Ascendant is in the 8th house and the Lord of the 8th is in the Ascendant), or if they are without the influence of Jupiter <note>Guru</note> and are placed in the 12th <note>Riphpha</note> or 6th <note>Ari</note> houses, then the person born under this alignment meets their end in their eighteenth year. || 58 ||

<gloss>If the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the 8th are both malefic, in each other's houses, or in the 12th or 6th houses without Jupiter's influence, the child dies in the 18th year.</gloss>

### Regarding Immediate Death
> When Saturn is situated in a Navamsha <note>a 1/9th divisional chart sign</note> ruled by Jupiter, and is aspected by Rahu,
> While the Lord of the Body <note>Ascendant</note> is not seen by benefics, the newborn perishes immediately.

### Regarding Death in the 19th Year
> But if that Lord is in its sign of exaltation, the lifespan is nineteen years. || 59 ||

Wherever Saturn <note>Manda</note> may be, if it is in the Navamsha of Jupiter (Sagittarius or Pisces) and is aspected by Rahu, and the Lord of the Body (the Lord of the Ascendant) is not aspected by any benefic planets, the child born dies immediately upon birth.

In this same combination, if "that Lord" (the Lord of the Ascendant) is in its exalted portion <term>Tungabhaga: the specific degree of highest strength</term>, then the lifespan is nineteen (19) years, after which death occurs. || 59 ||

<gloss>If Saturn is in Jupiter's Navamsha, Rahu aspects it, and the Lord of the Ascendant is not seen by benefics, the child dies at birth. If that Lord is in an exalted sign, the age is 19 years.</gloss>

### Regarding Death in the 20th Year
> If malefic planets are in the Kendras <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</note> and are not aspected by the Moon or benefics,
> Or if the Moon is in the 6th or 8th house, the person lives happily until the end of twenty years. || 60 ||

When malefic planets are present in the Kendras (1, 4, 7, 10) and are not aspected <note>seen</note> by the Moon <note>Nishakara</note> or other benefic planets (Mercury, Jupiter, Venus), or if the Moon <note>Shitarashmi</note> is in the 6th or 8th house from the Ascendant (while malefics are in the Kendras), the subject lives happily until the end of twenty years, after which they meet death. || 60 ||

<gloss>If malefics are in the Kendras and not seen by the Moon or benefics, or if the Moon is in the 6th or 8th, the child remains happy for 20 years and then dies.</gloss>

### Now, Death in the 22nd Year.

> If the Sun is joined with Jupiter in the Ascendant in the sign of the "Insect," and the Lord of the Eighth house is in a <term>Kendra</term><note>A "Kendra" or angular house refers to the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses of a birth chart, considered the pillars of strength.</note>, death occurs in the twenty-second year. || 61 ||

"In the sign of the Insect" = the Sun is in the sign of Cancer; "joined with Jupiter" = with the planet Jupiter; "in the Ascendant" means the rising sign should be Cancer and both the Sun and Jupiter should be located there. Furthermore, if the Lord of the Eighth house from the Ascendant is in a <term>Kendra</term> (1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th house), then the person born dies in their twenty-second year.

Now, a doubt arises: in the chapter on definitions, the verse "The eighth, Scorpio, and the 'Insect' signs" identifies the "Insect" as the sign of Scorpio. Why then is "Insect" interpreted here as Cancer? It is said in response: if Scorpio were taken as the "Insect," then the eighth house from it would be Gemini. Its lord is Mercury. Mercury can never be in the <term>Kendras</term> (1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th) from the Sun when the Sun is in the Ascendant <note>Due to astronomical proximity, Mercury is never far from the Sun</note>. If "Kendra" only meant the first house, the text would have simply said "the Lord of the Eighth is there." Therefore, accepting the authority of Varahamihira that "the Insect can refer to Cancer," it is interpreted as Cancer here. || 61 ||

If the Sun with Jupiter is in the sign of Cancer in the Ascendant and the Lord of the Eighth is in a <term>Kendra</term>, the person dies in their 22nd year. || 61 ||

---

### Death in the 26th or 27th Year.

> If Saturn is in the Ascendant in an enemy's sign, and the benefic planets are in <term>Apoklima</term> houses, death may occur in the twenty-sixth or twenty-seventh year. || 62 ||

When Saturn is in the Ascendant in a sign belonging to its enemy (meaning the Lord of the Ascendant is an enemy of Saturn, and Saturn sits there), and the benefics (auspicious planets) are situated in <term>Apoklima</term><note>The 3rd, 6th, 9th, and 12th houses, which are considered weaker positions in Vedic astrology.</note> houses (3, 6, 9, 12), the death of the person born will occur in the twenty-sixth or twenty-seventh year. || 62 ||

If Saturn is in an enemy's sign in the Ascendant and the benefic planets are in <term>Apoklima</term>, the lifespan of that person should be known as 26 or 27 years. || 62 ||

If the Lord of the Eighth house is a malefic planet and is "aspected by Jupiter" (seen by Jupiter from anywhere), and the "Lord of the Birth" (the ruler of the Moon sign) is "aspected by a malefic" (seen by a cruel planet) and is "situated in the eighth" (gone to the eighth house), the death of the person born will be in the twenty-eighth year. || 63 ||

### Regarding death in the 29th year.

> If the Moon is aided by Saturn and the Sun is situated in the eighth house, the person born will go to the city of Yama <note>The abode of the God of Death</note> in their twenty-ninth year. || 64 ||

The Moon being "aided by Saturn" means it is connected to Saturn (either by occupying the same sign or through an aspect). If the Sun is also situated in the eighth house from the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</term>, then the person born will go to the city of Yama—meaning they are led to the house of death—in their twenty-ninth (29) year. || 64 ||

If the Moon is a companion to Saturn and the Sun is in the eighth house, the subject travels to the city of Yama, or dies, in the 29th year. || 64 ||

### Regarding death in the 27th or 30th year.

> If the Lord of the Night is between the lords of the birth sign and the eighth house, and Jupiter is in the twelfth, death occurs at age twenty-seven or thirty. || 65 ||

When the "Lord of the Night" (the Moon) is positioned between the Lord of the Birth Sign <note>The ruler of the Ascendant</note> and the Lord of the Eighth House <note>The house associated with longevity and death</note>, this is what is meant: one of these two lords is in the twelfth house from the Moon and the other is in the second house. If Jupiter is also in the twelfth house from the Ascendant, the person's death occurs in the twenty-seventh (27) or thirtieth (30) year. || 65 ||

If the Moon is between the Lord of the Birth and the Lord of the Eighth, and Jupiter is in the 12th house, the child's death occurs at the age of 27 or 30 years. || 65 ||

### Regarding death in the 32nd year.

> If the Lord of the Eighth is in a Cardinal house and the Lord of the Ascendant is devoid of strength, the person has a lifespan of thirty years and dies in the thirty-second year. || 66 ||

> If the Moon is waning and joined by a malefic planet, while the Lord of the Eighth is in a Cardinal house or the eighth house itself, and the Ascendant is joined by malefics and weak, one meets death in the thirty-second year. || 67 ||

Simple meaning: || 66 ||

Now, if the "Hare-marked one" (the Moon) is waning (during the dark fortnight) and joined by a malefic planet <term>Papagraha: planets like Mars or Saturn that are considered naturally inauspicious</term>, and the Lord of the Eighth is in a Cardinal house (1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th) or in the eighth house, and the Ascendant is joined by malefics and lacks strength, the person meets death in the thirty-second year.

In the illustrated charts: The first combination involves (Mars and Mercury). The second combination involves (Moon, Saturn, Rahu, and Mars) and should be considered accordingly. || 67 ||

If the Lord of the Eighth is in a Cardinal house and the Lord of the Ascendant is without strength, the person lives to 30 and dies in the 32nd year. || 66 ||

If the waning Moon is with a malefic, the Lord of the Eighth is in a Cardinal or the eighth house, and there is a malefic in the Ascendant which is weak, that child dies in the 32nd year. || 67 ||

## Now, the Combinations for Short Life.

> If the Lord of the Ascendant is weak and malefic planets are situated in the 6th, 8th, or 12th houses, and there is no aspect or conjunction from benefic planets, the person will have a short life or be childless. || 68 ||
>
> If the Lord of the 8th house or Saturn <note>original: "Bhanuja," literally 'son of the Sun'</note> is in a cruel 1/60th division <term>Shashtyamsa: a subtle divisional chart used in Vedic astrology to determine the nature of a planet</term>, and the Lord of the 8th is conjoined with malefic planets, one should predict a short life. || 69 ||
>
> If the 12th and 2nd houses are occupied by malefic planets, lack the aspect of benefics, and are in cruel 1/60th divisions, one should predict a short life. || 70 ||

Thus ends the classification of childhood afflictions, planetary afflictions, and short life spans occurring within the first thirty-two years of life.

Now, the combinations for short life are explained in detail. If malefic planets are present in the 6th, 8th, or 12th houses from the Ascendant, and the Lord of the Ascendant is weak (lacking strength) and devoid of the aspect or conjunction of benefic planets, the person born will have a short life or be childless (without offspring). Alternatively, another combination is stated: if the Lord of the 8th house or Saturn is in a cruel 1/60th division (refer to the Shashtyamsa chart in the first chapter) and the Lord of the 8th is conjoined with malefic planets, one should predict a short life for the native. Or, if the 12th and 2nd houses from the Ascendant are conjoined with malefic planets, lack the aspect of benefics, and fall into cruel 1/60th divisions, then one should predict a short life for the native. || 68-70 ||

In this section on childhood afflictions, the various types of afflictions and short life spans occurring within thirty-two years have been described.

## Now, the Cancellation of Afflictions.

Now, even if the previously mentioned negative afflictions exist, they can be neutralized by certain planetary combinations. Therefore, these combinations for the "breaking of afflictions" <term>Arishta-bhanga: the cancellation of planetary ill-effects</term> are now stated:

> If the Lord of the Ascendant is exceedingly strong, conjoined with or aspected by benefic planets, situated in a quadrant <term>Kendra: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, considered the pillars of a horoscope</term>, and free from the aspect of malefic planets, the native lives a long life endowed with good fortune. || 71 ||

If the Lord of the Ascendant (the ruler of the birth sign) is exceedingly strong (a planet is fully strong when in its own divisions), conjoined with benefics, aspected by such benefics, situated in a quadrant (the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses), and free from the aspect of malefic planets—then even if negative afflictions exist, the native lives a long life, possessing great fortune and the enjoyment of happiness. As it is said—

## Now, the Cancellation of Evil Omens by the Moon.

<margin>
The Moon, if full in body or situated in the sign or division of a benefic, becomes the destroyer of all evil omens, especially if aspected by Venus. || 72 ||
</margin>

"Full in body" means the full disc of the Moon; "situated in the sign or division of a benefic" means placed in the zodiac sign or the divisional portion <note>Amsha</note> of a benefic planet. (Here, by the word "also," it should be understood that even a waning Moon is effective if placed in a benefic sign or division). He becomes the destroyer or annihilator of all <term>Arishtas</term> <note>evil omens or planetary combinations indicating misfortune/death</note>. Furthermore, the Moon aspected by Venus especially destroys all evil omens. As stated by Varahamihira <note>A famous 6th-century Indian astronomer and astrologer</note>—

> "The Moon, full-bodied, situated in a benefic sign, and placed between benefics, effects the cancellation of evil omens, especially when aspected by Venus." Thus. || 72 ||

If the Full Moon is in a benefic planet's sign or a benefic division, it destroys all <term>Arishtas</term>; if Venus aspects it, it becomes an even more specific destroyer of evil. || 72 ||

## Now, the Cancellation of Evil Omens by Benefic Planets.

<margin>
If one among Jupiter, Venus, or Mercury is powerful in a quadrant and free from association with malefics, it immediately effects the cancellation of the evil omen. || 73 ||
</margin>

"One among Jupiter, Venus, or Mercury" means any one of these three; "powerful" means situated in its own divisional strength <note>Varga</note>; "in a quadrant" means placed in any one of the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses from the Ascendant. If such a planet is free from the aspect or conjunction of malefic planets, then it immediately—very quickly—effects the cancellation of the evil omen. Varahamihira also stated in the *Svalpa Jataka*—

> "If any one of Mercury, Venus, or Jupiter is powerful and has reached a quadrant, and if it is without the company of cruel planets, it leads to the immediate cancellation of the evil omen." Thus. || 73 ||

If even one among Jupiter, Venus, and Mercury is powerful and in a quadrant, and has no association with a malefic planet, it immediately destroys the evil omen. || 73 ||

## Now, the Cancellation of Evil Omens by the Moon.

<margin>
Whether situated in its sign of exaltation, its own house, the division of a friend, or the division of a benefic; whether full or aspected by benefics; or even in its own division—if the Moon is free from the aspect of enemies and not joined or aspected by malefics, it destroys a difficult evil omen just as the Sun destroys a mass of frost. || 74 ||
</margin>

The Moon (the "Hare-bearer"), if situated in its sign of exaltation (Taurus), or in its own house (Cancer), or in the divisions <note>Varga: divisional charts used in Vedic astrology to determine planetary strength</note> of its friends, or in the divisions of a benefic planet (Mercury, Jupiter, or Venus), or if it is full-orbed and aspected by benefic planets, or situated in its own divisions—if such a Moon is free from the aspect or conjunction of enemies and free from the conjunction or aspect of malefic planets, then it destroys even the most difficult and severe misfortune. Here is a comparison: just as the Sun (the "Day-jewel") destroys a dense mass of frost and snow with its rays, in the same way, the Moon situated in the aforementioned conditions destroys even a multitude of misfortunes. || 74 ||

Just as the Sun destroys very thick fogs (frost) through its rays, similarly the Moon—when in its exaltation (Taurus), or its own house (Cancer), or in the divisions of its friends, or in benefic divisions, or if it is full-orbed and aspected by benefics, or in its own divisions—provided it is not joined by the aspect or conjunction of its enemies, destroys even the most difficult misfortunes. || 74 ||

If birth occurs during the night in the bright fortnight, or during the day in the dark fortnight, the Moon—whose form is aspected by benefics and malefics respectively—certainly protects the newborn from calamities even if it is placed in the houses of destruction or enemies, just as a father protects his child. || 75 ||

Now, the remedy for the lunar misfortune mentioned in verse 35 (regarding the Moon in the house of enemies or destruction) is being stated. If birth occurs in the bright fortnight <note>Shukla Paksha: the waxing phase of the moon</note> during the night, or in the dark fortnight <note>Krishna Paksha: the waning phase</note> during the day, and the Moon is aspected by benefics and malefics respectively, then even if it is in the "enemy" or "destruction" houses (the 6th or 8th houses), it certainly protects the newborn child from calamities. Just as a father protects his own son from dangers with great effort, so too the Moon, characterized by these traits, protects the child from misfortunes even from the 6th or 8th houses and does not allow death. Thus it is said in the *Jataka Bharanam*:
"If birth is at night in the waxing phase, or by day in the waning phase, the Moon—even if in the 6th house—if aspected by benefic and malefic planets respectively, protects the child like a father." || 75 ||

If birth is in the bright fortnight at night or in the dark fortnight during the day, the Moon—aspected by benefics and malefics—protects the native even if it is in the 6th or 8th house, just as a father protects his child. || 75 ||

->**Now, the cancellation of misfortune caused by Jupiter.**<-

Jupiter (the "Minister of the King of Heaven"), if very powerful, possessing brilliant rays, and situated in a center <term>Kendra: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses of a birth chart, considered the pillars of strength</term>, will surely pacify many difficult misfortunes, just as a single prostration performed with devotion to the Wielder of the Trident (Lord Shiva) destroys many sins. || 76 ||

If Jupiter, being extremely powerful (possessing great strength) and having shining rays, is situated in a center (any of the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses), then he alone surely pacifies or destroys many difficult "sins" (misfortunes). What then if other benefic planets were also in the centers? Just as a single prostration offered with a humble spirit and devotion to the Wielder of the Trident (Mahadeva/Shiva) destroys many difficult sins and stains accumulated through various births and actions, similarly, a single powerful Jupiter in a center destroys various misfortunes of the native. As it is said:
"The Minister of the King of the Gods (Jupiter) destroys hundreds of thousands of defects when placed in a center." || 76 ||

If Jupiter, possessing full strength and a clear orb, is in a center (1, 4, 7, 10), he alone surely destroys many difficult misfortunes. Just as a single bow made with devotion to Lord Shankara (Shiva) destroys the most difficult sins. || 76 ||

# With the Commentary on Jataka Parijata

## The Cancellation of Ill-fortune by the Ascendant Lord
> If the Lord of the Ascendant is endowed with strength and situated in a trine <note>the 1st, 5th, or 9th houses</note> or a quadrant <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note>, the child born even under an ill-omened yoga will certainly live. || 77 ||

Simple Meaning: If the Lord of the Ascendant is strong and placed in a trine or a quadrant, the child born in an ill-omened combination will surely survive. || 77 ||

## The Cancellation of Ill-fortune by Planets
> Those in whose birth planets are situated in their signs of exaltation or occupy their own signs, such planets undoubtedly make the newborn child long-lived. || 78 ||

Exaltation = situated in their respective highest signs; or occupying their own signs = situated in their own zodiac signs (the plural indicates three or more planets). Those who have such planets at the time of birth, the child born is made long-lived; there is no doubt in this. The sense is that three or more planets in exaltation or their own signs become destroyers of ill-fortune. || 78 ||

In whose birth many planets are in exaltation or in their own houses, those planets make the child long-lived without a doubt. || 78 ||

## The Cancellation of Ill-fortune by Rahu <note>The North Node of the Moon</note>
> Rahu in the third, sixth, or eleventh house, if aspected by benefics, immediately destroys all sins <note>afflictions</note>, just as the wind destroys a heap of cotton. || 79 ||
> Rahu in the Ascendant of Aries, Taurus, or Cancer constantly protects the child, just as a pleased King protects a man who has committed an offense. || 80 ||

Rahu situated in the 3rd, 6th, or 11th from the Ascendant, if <note>original: 'chirikshito', likely 'nirikshito'</note> seen by benefics = auspicious planets, then it immediately destroys all 'durita' = the entire ill-fortune. The metaphor is: like the 'maruta' = wind destroys a 'tulasanghatam' = a pile of cotton. Furthermore, if Rahu is present in the Ascendant of 'Aja-Vrisha-Karki' = any of Aries, Taurus, or Cancer, then it constantly and perpetually protects the born child. Then the defect of ill-fortune does not overcome him. As it is said:
> "Rahu in the third, sixth, or eleventh, joined with a benefic or aspected by one, then certainly pacifies all ill-fortune." Thus says Shaunaka <note>An ancient sage and author</note>.

Likewise—
> "As the Sun destroys darkness, Rahu in the 3rd, 6th, or 11th aspected by benefic planets destroys the defects arising from birth. Even in Taurus or Cancer, it is the destroyer of all ill-fortune." Thus in the Kalaprakashika <note>A classical text on electional astrology</note>.

Here, a metaphor is illustrated by the latter half. 'Prasanna' = with a delighted heart, a 'Prithivipati' = King (becoming forgiving), just as he protects a 'kritaparadham' = a man who has committed a fault, so too Rahu, characterized by the aforementioned traits, favorably protects a child <note>original: 'sidosha', likely 'dosha'</note> filled with the defects of ill-fortune. || 79-80 ||

If Rahu is in the 3rd, 6th, or 11th from the Ascendant and auspicious planets look upon it, then just as the wind destroys a heap of cotton, in the same way, Rahu destroys all suffering. || 79 ||

In Aries, Taurus, or Cancer Ascendants, Rahu constantly protects the child in the same way a <unclear>pleased</unclear> King protects a criminal. || 80 ||

## Again, the Cancellation of Ill-fortune by the Moon
> The Moon, joined with auspicious divisions <note>vargas</note>, aspected by benefics, and full of its web of light, quickly destroys the entire ill-fortune of the newborn, just as Garuda <note>the divine eagle</note> destroys a snake. || 81 ||

Therefore, predict death only after careful consideration."

## From the Commentary on Jātaka Pārijāta

Now, the measure of **Middle Life** <note>Sanskrit: Madhyamāyuḥ</note> is stated: longevity above thirty-two (32) years and up to seventy (70) years is considered Middle Life.

Now, in this context, several varieties of Middle Life collected from other texts are written here:

->Malefic planets located in the square houses <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</note> from the Ascendant create Middle Life.<-
->The same applies from the Moon, if the planets are not aspected by or joined with benefics.<-

When benefics are in the divisions of malefic planets or in the Sun's sign, and malefics are in the square houses, this is a combination for Middle Life, provided the benefics are excluded from the square houses.
If benefics are in the 5th and 10th houses, the Sun is in the 8th, and the Moon is in the 12th, while Jupiter and Venus are in the same sign, the person born then has Middle Life.
If a malefic planet is the Lord of the 8th house and is with the Moon in a square or a trine, and is aspected by malefic planets in the sky, the person born reaches thirty-three (33) years.
When the Moon is in the sign of Mars in the Ascendant and is weakened by cruel planets, while the auspicious planets are outside the squares, death comes at exactly thirty-three years.
When Saturn is in the Ascendant joined with the Moon, and Mars is in Aquarius, the lifespan is thirty-three (33) years.
If Jupiter and Venus are not in the squares, the Lord of the Ascendant is joined with a malefic, and the planets are in the "declining" houses <note>The 3rd, 6th, 9th, and 12th houses</note> at twilight, the lifespan of the one born is thirty-six (36) years.
When the Sun is between malefic planets in the Ascendant in an enemy's house, the person born is afflicted by disease and has a maximum life of thirty-six (36) years.
When the Ascendant is between cruel planets, its Lord is in a dual sign, and Jupiter is in the 6th house, the person born goes to death in thirty-seven (37) years <note>original: "Munivahni," where Muni=7 and Vahni=3</note>, as declared by the best of the Shastras.
If the Lord of the 8th house is in the Ascendant in a fixed sign, and the 8th house is not joined by a benefic, that man dies at forty (40) years.
If the Lord of the Ascendant is in the 8th house with a malefic, and the benefics are outside the squares but aspecting, the son born reaches death at forty (40) years; this Shastra is never otherwise.
If the Lord of the 8th house is with Mars in the Ascendant, in a fixed sign or a movable division, and is in the 12th or 8th house, the person born meets death at forty-two (42) years.
When Jupiter is in a square, Saturn is in the 10th, and the Ascendant is a movable sign, the life is forty-four (44) years.
When the Lord of the 8th house is in a square and Mars occupies the Ascendant, while the Sun and Saturn are in the 3rd or 6th, one lives for forty-four (44) years.
When Mars is in its exaltation in the Ascendant, Jupiter is setting, and Saturn is in the 10th, the person born is wealthy and a knower of many sciences, but dies in <note>The word Vedābdhi numerically signifies 44 (Veda=4, Abdhi=4), though the printer has provided the numeral 40.</note> forty-four (44) years.
When the Lord of the birth sign is in the 8th house with a malefic, and the Lord of the Ascendant is in the 6th house with a malefic, or even if strong but devoid of benefic aspects, one dies at forty-five (45) years.
When the Moon is full in Aries in the Ascendant and aspected by a benefic, a king is born; but if he lacks the periods <note>Dasha</note> of malefic planets, he dies at forty-eight (48) years.
When the Moon is in its best division <note>Vargottama</note> in the Ascendant aspected by malefics, and the benefics are powerless, the life is forty-eight (48) years.
When the Lord of the Ascendant is in the division of the 8th house, and the Lord of the 8th is in the division of the Ascendant, and they are joined with malefics, the person born lives fifty years.
In a birth with a dual sign rising, if Saturn and the Moon are in the 12th or 8th house, the human born there lives for fifty-two (52) years.
If Saturn is in the Ascendant with a companion, and the Moon is in the 12th or 8th, the person born—though of good character and possessing knowledge of Vedanta—meets death at fifty-two (52) years.
When Jupiter is in Sagittarius in the Ascendant and Mars is in the 8th with Rahu, death is in the 57th year. When the Lord of the 8th is in the 7th and the Moon is with malefics in the 6th, death is in the 58th year.

### Chapter on Fatal Combinations (Arishta) || 4 ||

If the Lord of the Ascendant <note>Lagnastha: the planet ruling the rising sign</note> is in the division of Saturn and is joined with the Lord of the Eighth House <note>the house of death</note>, and the Moon is in the 6th, 8th, or 12th house, the person born lives for fifty-eight (58) years.

When all planets are situated in the 6th, 8th, and 12th houses in a "King-making" combination <note>Nripala Yoga</note>, the maximum lifespan of the person born in this combination is fifty-eight years || 58 ||

For one whose cardinal houses <note>Kendras: 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</note> are occupied by malefic planets, while the Ascendant is free from cruel planets, life does not extend beyond sixty years if malefic planets are also in the 5th house.

If the Lord of the Ascendant is in the 12th house, or is waning and joined with a malefic, life does not exceed sixty years, provided Jupiter is not in the Ascendant.

If the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the 12th house are malefic and situated in the house of death (8th), the man born in this combination is said to have a lifespan of sixty (60) years.

With Saturn in the Ascendant, the Moon in the 4th, Mars in the 7th, and the Sun in the 10th—even if joined by Venus, Jupiter, or Mercury—a ruler of men lives for sixty years.

When the Lord of the Ascendant is in the 10th house, and the planet Jupiter is aspected by Mercury, Jupiter, and the Moon, it makes the person born a wealthy lord of the earth, but he meets his end at sixty.

With Venus in the Ascendant, Mercury and Saturn in the cardinal houses, and planets in their highest exaltation situated in the 3rd or 11th houses, one becomes a lord of the earth but dies at sixty.

If Jupiter is in the 8th house, the Ascendant is Aquarius, and malefic planets are in the cardinal signs, the person—though a virtuous scholar of all sciences—reaches his end at sixty (60).

If a malefic is in a cardinal house, the Lord of the Ascendant is in the 12th, and the Lord of the 8th is in the house of fire <note>likely referring to the 3rd or a specific fiery sign</note>, the person born, though of good character, brings disgrace to his family and passes to the other world.

If the Lords of the Ascendant and the Birth Sign are in cardinal houses joined with the Lord of Death, and Jupiter is absent from the four cardinal houses, the end comes at sixty-five (65) years.

When the Moon is in the Ascendant but in an inauspicious state, Saturn is debilitated, and the Sun is in the 7th house, the man in this combination is very happy but lives for sixty-five (65) years.

If the Lords of the Ascendant and the Birth Sign have gone to the house of death, and the Lord of Death is in a cardinal house, the man born in this combination becomes famous and wealthy; his death is declared at sixty-six (66) years according to the saying of Nandaka, or it may occur in the 30th year depending on the planets.

With Jupiter in the Ascendant joined by Mercury and the Sun, Saturn in Pisces, and the Moon in the 12th, the man born is wealthy but meets death at sixty-six (66) years.

The Sun with the Lord of the Constellation in the 10th house, Saturn in the Ascendant, and Jupiter in the 4th; a man born in this combination becomes a lord of the earth but dies at sixty-eight (68).

When the Sun, Mars, and Saturn are joined together and Jupiter is devoid of strength, and the Moon is in the 12th or 5th house, one generally lives for seventy (70) years.

If Saturn is debilitated in a cardinal or trine house, and Mercury is in a cardinal house with the Sun, the person born is a scholar, righteous, and wise, living for seventy years.

If a strong benefic is in a cardinal house and the 8th house is devoid of benefics, and the Lord of the Ascendant is aspected by malefics, he lives for seventy (70) years.

With Mars in the 5th house, Saturn debilitated, and the Sun setting <note>in the 7th house</note>, the man born in this combination shall go to his death at seventy (70). || 4 ||

If the Lord of the Ascendant is endowed with strength, Jupiter is in a cardinal (1, 4, 7, 10) or trine (5, 9) house, and malefic planets are in the 6th, 8th, or 12th, there is a medium lifespan. || 8 ||

# From the Jataka Parijata with Commentary

After thirty-two years and up to seventy years, the combination for a medium lifespan occurs.

## Now, the Combinations for a Full Lifespan

> If the four houses of the angles <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</note> are occupied by benefic planets, and the Lord of the Ascendant is joined with a benefic and aspected by Jupiter, one should predict a full lifespan. || 85 ||
>
> If the Lord of the Ascendant is situated in an angle and is joined with Jupiter and Venus, or is aspected by them, one should predict a full lifespan. || 86 ||
>
> If three planets are in their signs of exaltation and are joined with the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Eighth House, and the eighth house is free from malefic planets, one should predict a long life. || 87 ||
>
> If three planets are placed in the eighth house and are in their signs of exaltation, friendly signs, or their own divisional charts, and the Lord of the Ascendant is endowed with strength, one should predict a long life. || 88 ||
>
> If either Saturn or the Lord of the Eighth House is joined with any planet situated in its sign of exaltation, one should predict a long life. || 89 ||
>
> If malefic planets are placed in the 3rd, 6th, and 11th houses, and benefics are in the angles and trines, and the Lord of the Ascendant is strong, one should predict a full lifespan. || 90 ||
>
> If the 6th, 7th, and 8th houses are occupied by benefic planets, and the 3rd, 6th, and 11th houses contain malefic planets, one should predict a long life. || 91 ||
>
> If malefic planets are in the 12th and 6th houses while the Lord of the Ascendant is in an angle; or if malefic planets are in the 8th house while the Lord of the 10th house is in its sign of exaltation—in both these combinations, it is widely agreed that one attains a long life. || 92 ||
>
> If the ruler of the sign occupied by the Lord of the Eighth House is placed in a certain sign, and the ruler of that sign and the Lord of the Ascendant are both in angles, then life is determined by that influence. || 93 ||
>
> If the Ascendant falls in a dual sign <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces</note> and its Lord is in an angle, or in its sign of exaltation or its primary triangular strength <term>Moolatrikona: a specific favorable position for a planet</term>, the fortunate person lives for a long time. || 94 ||
>
> If the Ascendant is in a dual sign and two malefic planets are in angles from the Lord of the Ascendant at birth, one should declare a long life for him. || 95 ||
>
> If the Sun, Saturn, and Mars are in the divisions of movable signs, while Jupiter and Venus are in the divisions of fixed signs, and the remaining planets are in the divisions of dual signs, the person born then lives for a hundred years. || 96 ||

Now, those combinations in which born men enjoy a full lifespan are being summarized. There, even the verses with simple meanings are explained for the understanding of students. **In the four** = in the angles (1, 4, 7, 10). **By benefics** = by being joined with benefic planets, meaning benefic planets should be residing in the angles. **The Lord of the Ascendant** being joined with any one of the benefic planets and **aspected by Jupiter** = seen by Jupiter; for one born under this, a **full lifespan** (above seventy and up to a hundred) **should be predicted**. (1) || 85 ||

**The Lord of the Ascendant** = the master of the birth sign, **situated in an angle** (placed in any of the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses), **joined with Jupiter and Venus, or by those two** = by Jupiter and Venus, if the Lord of the Ascendant situated in an angle is also aspected, for that person a **full lifespan should be predicted**. (2) || 86 ||

**By three planets, whether benefic or malefic** = by planets **in exaltation** = gone to their respective signs of highest strength, and joined with the **Lord of the Ascendant** and the **Lord of the Eighth House** <note>the house of longevity</note>, and the **eighth house** being **free from malefics** = devoid of malefic planets; for one born in this combination, a **long life should be predicted**. (3) || 87 ||

# Chapter on Portents of Longevity: Chapter 4

If three planets (whether <term>malefics</term><note>planets with a naturally harsh influence, like Mars or Saturn</note> or <term>benefics</term><note>planets with a naturally gentle influence, like Jupiter or Venus</note>) are situated in the eighth house <note>the house of death and longevity</note>, or are in their signs of exaltation, or in the divisions of their friends, or in their own divisions, and the <term>Lord of the Ascendant</term><note>the planet ruling the rising sign at birth</note> is endowed with strength (situated in its own division, etc.), one should predict a long life for the person born. (4) || 88 ||

If at the time of birth, wherever Saturn or the Lord of the Eighth House is placed, they are joined by any planet situated in its own sign of exaltation, one should predict a long life for that person. (5) || 89 ||

If at the time of birth, the <term>malefics</term> (Sun, Mars, Saturn, Mercury joined with a malefic, the waning Moon, Rahu, and Ketu) are placed in the 3rd, 6th, or 11th houses, and the <term>benefics</term> (Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, and the waxing Moon) are placed in the <term>angles or trines</term><note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, 10th, 5th, or 9th houses</note>, and the Lord of the Ascendant is strong, one should predict a full lifespan for that person. (6) || 90 ||

If at the time of birth, the benefic planets are in the 6th, 7th, or 8th houses, and the malefic planets are in the 3rd, 6th, or 11th houses, then one should predict a long life for the person born. (7) || 91 ||

If at the time of birth, the malefic planets are in the 12th and 6th houses, and the Lord of the Ascendant is in an angle (1, 4, 7, 10) (8); or if the malefic planets are in the 8th house and the Lord of the 10th house is in its sign of exaltation (9); then in both of these combinations (8 & 9), the person born attains a long life; this is the consensus of the ancient elders. || 92 ||

<margin>If the lord of the sign where the Lord of the Eighth House resides, and the Lord of the Ascendant, are both placed in angles, then one should predict a long life as mentioned before. For example: here the Lord of the Eighth is Jupiter, placed in the 10th house; the lord of the sign Cancer (where Jupiter is) is the Moon, who is placed in Virgo; the lord of Virgo is Mercury; if the Lord of the Ascendant and Venus are in angles, then a "Long Life Combination" should be declared. (10) || 93 ||</margin>

(11) || 94 ||

# With the Commentary on Jataka Parijata

If the planets are situated in **Dual** <note>original: *dvisvabhava*; referring to Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces</note> signs (3, 6, 9, 12) or their Navamshas <note>a 1/9th divisional chart used for precision</note>, then a person born under this yoga <note>planetary combination</note> becomes a **centenarian** = living for a hundred years (13). || 66 ||

Now, regarding the thirteen types of long-life combinations mentioned previously, the measure of long life is stated: a full lifespan is defined as being from **seventy to one hundred years** = from seventy years (70) up to the end of a hundred (100 years) is considered a full life (long life).

If the four cardinal houses (1, 4, 7, 10) <term>Kendras: the pillars of the horoscope</term> are occupied by benefic planets, and the Lord of the Ascendant <note>Lagnesha</note> is joined with a benefic and aspected by Jupiter, it grants a full lifespan. || 85 ||

If the Lord of the Ascendant is in a cardinal house joined with Jupiter and Venus, or if Jupiter and Venus aspect it, it grants a full lifespan. || 86 ||

If three planets are in their signs of exaltation <note>where a planet is at its maximum strength</note> and are joined with the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the 8th house, and the 8th house is free from malefic planets, it grants a full lifespan. || 87 ||

If there are three planets in the 8th house, or if they are in their exaltation, friend's sign, or their own divisional vargas, and the Lord of the Ascendant is strong, it grants long life. || 88 ||

If Saturn or the Lord of the 8th house is joined with any planet situated in its sign of exaltation, it grants a long life. || 89 ||

If malefic planets are in the 3rd, 11th, and 6th houses, while benefic planets are in the cardinal (1, 4, 7, 10) or trinal (1, 5, 9) houses, and the Lord of the Ascendant is strong, they grant a full lifespan. || 90 ||

If the 6th, 7th, and 8th houses are joined with benefic planets, and the 3rd, 11th, and 6th houses contain malefic planets, they create long life. || 91 ||

If malefic planets are in the 12th and 6th houses and the Lord of the Ascendant sits in a cardinal house, or if malefic planets are in the 8th house and the Lord of the 10th house is in its exaltation, many scholars agree that these two combinations result in long life. || 92 ||

If the Lord of the 8th house is in a certain house, and the ruler of the sign where that lord is placed, along with the Lord of the Ascendant, are both in cardinal houses, long life results. || 93 ||

One born with a Dual sign <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces</note> as the Ascendant, where the Lord of the Ascendant is in a cardinal house or in its exaltation or its *Moolatrikona* <note>a primary root-sign of strength</note>, shall live for a very long time and be fortunate. || 94 ||

One who has a Dual sign Ascendant at birth and has two malefic planets in cardinal houses from the Lord of the Ascendant will have a long life. || 95 ||

If the Sun, Saturn, and Mars are in the Navamsha of Moveable signs, Jupiter and Venus are in the Navamsha of Fixed signs, and the remaining planets (Moon, Mercury, Rahu, Ketu) are situated in Dual signs, the person born of this yoga lives for a hundred years. || 96 ||

->**Now, the Measure of a Full Lifespan.**<-

->**A full life is from seventy to the end of a hundred.**<-

After seventy years, up to one hundred years, is considered a full lifespan.

Sun, Jupiter, and Mars: if they are in the Navamsha of Saturn (Capricorn or Aquarius) anywhere, or if they are in the 9th house <note>Dharma-sthana</note> and situated in the Navamsha of that same 9th house sign, and are strong, and the Moon <note>Himanshu</note> is in the Ascendant and strong, then the person born has a lifespan equal to a *Yuga* <term>Yuga: a vast cosmic age</term> and possesses wealth.

# Chapter on Misfortunes || 4 ||

> If the Sun, Mars, and Jupiter are situated in the <term>Navamsha</term> <note>a 1/9th divisional chart used for fine-tuning strength</note> of Saturn, and are placed in the ninth house or are powerful in their divisional signs, and the Moon is in the Ascendant, the person possesses wealth and a lifespan lasting until the end of an era.

<margin>If Jupiter and Saturn are in the 9th (Dharma) or 10th (Karma) houses, in the same degree of a <term>Navamsha</term>, and are seen by benefics (auspicious planets), and the Sun is in the Ascendant (at sunrise), then the person born in this combination becomes a long-lived <term>Muni</term> (an ascetic or sage).</margin>

If Jupiter and Saturn are at the same degree and situated in the 9th or 10th house, and are aspected by auspicious planets at sunrise, the person born in this combination is a long-lived sage (ascetic). || 98 ||

->Now, regarding immeasurable lifespan.<-

> If Jupiter is with the Moon in the Ascendant of Cancer, and the son of the Moon (Mercury) and the son of Bhrigu (Venus) are in the <term>Kendras</term> (angles), and the remaining planets are in the 11th, 6th, and 3rd houses, there is an immeasurable lifespan in this world. || 99 ||

<margin>If the Ascendant is the sign of Cancer and Jupiter and the Moon are there, and Mercury and Venus are in the <term>Kendras</term> (1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses), and the remaining planets (Sun, Mars, Saturn, Rahu, Ketu)—the malefics—are placed in the 11th, 6th, and 3rd houses, then in this combination, the lifespan of the person born is immeasurable, even without mathematical calculation. This means one should not calculate the age for one born in this yoga, as it is impossible to limit. As stated in the *Saravali* <note>a classic 8th-century astrological text</note>: "With Jupiter and Moon in Cancer Ascendant, Mercury and Venus in the angles, and the rest in the 3rd, 6th, and 11th, a man possesses immeasurable life."</margin>

If Cancer is the Ascendant and Jupiter and the Moon are in it, Mercury and Venus are in the angles, and the remaining planets (Sun, Mars, Saturn, Rahu, Ketu) are in the eleventh, sixth, and third houses, then the lifespan is immeasurable. || 99 ||

->Now, the planetary position providing a god-like appearance.<-

> When malefics are absent from the <term>Trikonas</term> (trines), the <term>Kendras</term> (angles) are devoid of benefics, and the eighth house is free of malefics, the one born is like an immortal. || 100 ||
> If the planets from Saturn to Mars are situated from the Ascendant onwards and are endowed with <term>Vaisheshika-amsha</term> <note>specific high-quality divisional strengths</note>, the one born is like an immortal. || 101 ||

If malefic planets are not in the trines (5th and 9th houses), auspicious planets are not in the angles (1st, 4th, 7th, 10th), and the eighth house is also free of malefic planets, the person born is like an immortal (god-like). || 100 ||

<header>From the Jataka Parijata with Commentary</header>

If the planets starting from Saturn and ending with Mars <note>original: "शुन्यादिभौमपर्यन्तं" - referring to the traditional order of the seven visible planets</note> are situated in the Ascendant and other houses, and are endowed with *Vaisheshika* portions <term>Vaisheshika-amsha: a technical measurement where a planet gains strength by occupying its own or exalted divisions in the ten-fold varga system</term>, then the person born becomes like an immortal god. || 101 ||

If there are no malefic planets in the trines <note>the 5th and 9th houses</note>, no benefic planets in the angles <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</note>, and the eighth house is free from malefic influence, the person born under such a combination is like a deity. || 100 ||

If the planets from Saturn to Mars are placed in the Ascendant and other houses and occupy their respective *Vaisheshika* portions, the person born shall be equal to a god. || 101 ||

->**Now, the attainment of incalculable life.**<-

**If the Ascendant is the end of Aries with Jupiter or Venus present there, the Moon is in the middle portion of Taurus, and Mars is in the *Simhasana* portion, the person born attains an incalculable lifespan through sacred chants.** || 102 ||

Now the combination for incalculable life is described. If the Ascendant is the final portion of the sign Aries and Jupiter or Venus is situated there; if the Moon <note>original: "निशाकरे" - the Night-maker</note> is in the middle (5th) Navamsha <term>Navamsha: a 1/9th division of a zodiac sign</term> of Taurus; and if Mars <note>original: "धराजे" - the Son of the Earth</note> is in the *Simhasana* portion <term>Simhasana-amsha: "Throne-portion," when a planet is in its own or exalted division in five specific vargas</term>, the person born attains a lifespan beyond counting through the practice of *Mantras* <note>sacred chants or formulas</note>. The meaning is that one born in this combination becomes a master of mantras and, through the power of chanting and rituals, achieves an extremely long life. || 102 ||

If the end of Aries is the Ascendant joined with Jupiter or Venus, the Moon is in the middle Navamsha of Taurus, and Mars is in its *Simhasana* portion, the person shall have incalculable life through the power of mantras. || 102 ||

->**Now, being equal to a Sage.**<-

**If Saturn is in the *Devaloka* portion, Mars is in the *Paravata* portion, and Jupiter is in the *Simhasana* portion in the Ascendant, the person born becomes equal to a Sage.** || 103 ||

Now the combination for attaining the status of a Sage <note>original: "मुनित्व" - the state of a Muni or silent ascetic</note> is described. He at whose birth Saturn is in the *Devaloka* portion <term>Devaloka-amsha: "Heavenly-world portion," strength in seven vargas</term>, Mars is in the *Paravata* portion <term>Paravata-amsha: "Pigeon/Highest portion," strength in six vargas</term>, and Jupiter is in the *Simhasana* portion in the Ascendant, that person becomes equal to a sage. || 103 ||

If Saturn is in *Devaloka* portion, Mars is in *Paravata* portion, and Jupiter is in *Simhasana* portion in the Ascendant, the person born shall be like a sage. || 103 ||

->**Now, life until the end of the Age.**<-

**If Jupiter is in an angle in the *Gopura* portion, Venus is in a trine in the *Paravata* portion, and the Ascendant is Cancer, he lives until the end of the Age.** || 104 ||

When Jupiter is in an angle <note>1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th house</note> and has attained the *Gopura* portion <term>Gopura-amsha: "City-gate portion," strength in four vargas</term>, Venus is in a trine (9th or 5th house) and has attained the *Paravata* portion, and the birth occurs in the Cancer Ascendant, that man lives until the end of the *Yuga* <note>a vast cosmic cycle of time</note>. || 104 ||

If Jupiter is in the *Gopura* portion in an angle, Venus is in the *Paravata* portion in a trine, and the Ascendant is Cancer, he lives until the end of the age. || 104 ||

->**Now, the attainment of the state of Brahman.**<-

**If the Ascendant is Cancer with a Sagittarius portion, and Jupiter is situated therein, and three or four planets are in the angles, the person born goes to the state of Brahman.** || 105 ||

**If the Ascendant is joined with Jupiter, Saturn is in the seventh house, the Moon is in Virgo, and the Ascendant is Sagittarius with an Aries portion, the person born goes to the Supreme State.** || 106 ||

At the time of birth, if the Ascendant is the sign of Cancer and it is the Navamsha of Sagittarius, and Jupiter <note>original: "देवेन्द्रपूजिते" - the one worshiped by the Lord of Gods</note> is situated there, and three or four planets are in the angles, then that person attains the state of Brahman—union with the Absolute...

# Now, the Sevenfold Nature of Longevity.

Infant fatality, that born of planetary combinations, short life, and by their cancellation, middle and long life;
Divine life, and that attained through yogic practice, mantras, and rituals—these seven types of longevity are proclaimed. || 107 ||

->Thus, by the grace of the nine planets, in the Jataka Parijata composed by Vaidyanatha,<-
->ends the Fourth Chapter on Infant Fatality.<-

---

Now, the seven divisions of longevity are described. First is **Infant Fatality** <term>Balarishta: planetary combinations suggesting death in early childhood</term>, lasting up to eight years. Second is **Combination-born Fatality** <term>Yogaja-arishta</term>, up to twenty years. Third is **Short Life**, up to thirty-two years. By the cancellation or overcoming of these three, the fourth is **Middle Life**, up to seventy years. Beyond that is **Long Life**, up to one hundred years, which is the fifth. Then comes **Divine Life**, equal to the gods, which is the sixth. Beyond even that is **Incalculable Life**, produced by yogic practice, mantras, and rituals, which is the seventh; thus there are seven divisions of life. By the cancellation of each preceding type, the life extends to the next. However, the measures of longevity shown here do not manifest, even if the planetary combinations exist, for those who are engaged in wicked deeds or improper conduct. As was said by Keshava in the section on longevity:

> "This applies to those who are righteous, of good character, and eat wholesome food; it does not apply to the sinful." || 107 ||

The *Sudha* commentary on the *Parijata* was composed by Kapileshwara. This fourth chapter, named "Arishta" (Fatalities), is now complete. || 4 ||

(1) Infant fatality up to 8 years, (2) Combination fatality up to 20 years, (3) Short life up to 32 years; by their cancellation (4) Middle life up to 70 years, (5) Long life up to 100 years, after that (6) Divine life, and thereafter (7) Incalculable life through yogic practice and the performance of mantras, etc. These seven types of life-spans are described. (According to the author of Sudha-Shastra) || 107 ||

**Thus ends the "Vimala" Hindi commentary on the fourth chapter of the Jataka Parijata.**

# Chapter 5: On the Determination of Lifespan

Now, the chapter on the determination of lifespan is explained. In this regard, the consideration of lifespan should only be undertaken for those born who are free from the previously mentioned *Arishta* yogas <note>combinations of planets indicating early death</note>. When the inquiry into lifespan arises, the spans of life specified by the ancients such as Parashara and others are stated here:

**The lifespans arising from Nature (Nisarga), the Body (Pinda), Degrees (Ansha), Rays (Rashmi), the Wheel (Chakra), Nakshatras (Lunar Mansions), and the Eight-fold Divisions (Ashtakavarga)—collecting those which were spoken of by Parashara and others, I shall speak of them in order. || 1 ||**

*Nature (Nisarga), etc.*: Having collected the eight types of lifespans—Nature, Body, Degrees, Rays, Wheel, Nakshatra, and Ashtakavarga—which were spoken of by the sages Parashara and others, I shall speak of them in order. || 1 ||

<gloss>Parashara and others have described the lifespans known as Nisargayu, Pindayu, Lagnayu, Anshakayu, Rashmijayu, Chakrayu, Nakshatrayu, and Ashtakavargajayu; having collected these, I state them in sequence.</gloss>

## The Number of Years in the Natural Lifespan (Nisargayu)

**Twenty, one, two, nine, eighteen, twenty, and fifty are the years for the planets beginning with the Sun; these are declared in order as the number of years in the Natural Lifespan of the planets. || 2 ||**

Now, the number of years for the Sun and others in the *Nisarga* system should be understood. For the Sun = 20 years. For the Moon = 1 year. For Mars = 2 years. For Mercury = 9. For Jupiter = 18. For Venus = 20. For Saturn = 50.
It is also said in the *Saravali* <note>A classic 8th-century astrological text by Kalyanavarman</note>:
> "Twenty, one, two, nine, eighteen, twenty, and fifty; these are the numbers of years for the Sun and others arising from Nature."

The years of the Natural Lifespan stated here are for when the planets are in their signs of exaltation <note>term: "Uchcha-gate" - the position where a planet is most powerful</note>. At the actual time of birth, some years are reduced based on their positions; the clarification of this should be seen further ahead. || 2 ||

<gloss>The natural lifespan of the planets is as follows: 20 years for the Sun, 1 year for the Moon, 2 years for Mars, 9 years for Mercury, 18 years for Jupiter, 20 years for Venus, and 50 years for Saturn.</gloss>

## The Number of Years in the Pindayu (Planetary Body Lifespan)

**Nineteen, twenty-five, fifteen, twelve, fifteen, twenty-one, and twenty are the years of the Pindayu for the planets beginning with the Sun when they are in their respective exaltations. || 3 ||**

Now the Pindayu years of the planets are stated. For the planets beginning with the Sun situated in their own exaltations, the years of Pindayu are read as nineteen and so on; these are shown externally. For the Sun = 19 years. For the Moon = 25 years. For Mars = 15 years. For Mercury = 12 years. For Jupiter = 15 years. For Venus = 21 years. For Saturn = 20 years.
Similarly in the *Saravali*:
**Nineteen for the Sun, twenty-five for the Moon. Fifteen for the Son of the Earth (Mars), and twelve for Mercury.**
**Fifteen years for Jupiter, and twenty-one for Venus. Twenty for the Son of the Sun (Saturn) is the Pindayu when situated in their exaltations.**
Also in the *Brihat Jataka* <note>The "Great Birth" manual by Varahamihira, c. 6th century</note>:
> "By Maya, Yavana, Manittha, and Shakti and others, the years for the Sun and the rest are ordained: nineteen, fifteen, five, two, five, eleven, and ten, added to ten <note>This is a coded Sanskrit numerical notation</note> when in their highest exaltation signs."

The years stated here are the measures of the maximum lifespan of the respective planets. These years apply to planets situated in exaltation. The clarification for their actual positions at the time of birth should be seen further ahead. || 3 ||

<gloss>The Pindayu for the Sun and other planets situated in their exaltation signs is as follows: 19 years for the Sun, 25 years for the Moon...</gloss>

->**Now, the Method for Rectifying the Pindayu <note>Pindayu refers to the "corpus" or total sum of years assigned to planets based on their positions.</note>.**<-

> The planet, subtracted by its own point of exaltation, should be subtracted from the circle of the zodiac if it is less than six signs. || 4 ||
> If it is greater than six signs, it should be left as it is; then converted into minutes and multiplied by its own assigned years. || 4 ||
> There, when divided by 21,600 <note>The number 21,600 represents the total minutes in a circle of 360 degrees (12 signs).</note>, the result obtained—
> In years, months, days, and minutes—is indeed called the longevity arising from the *Pinda* method. || 5 ||
> If the planet, diminished by its exaltation, is less than six, it is subtracted from the zodiac;
> Converted to minutes and multiplied by its own years of life, then divided by the minutes of the circle.
> The result obtained for the Sun and other planets is the years of life granted;
> The Sages say this follows the order of half-value at the point of fall <note>The "point of fall" or debilitation is 180 degrees opposite the exaltation point.</note> for both the *Pindayu* and *Naisargika* systems. || 6 ||

Now, the rectification of longevity is explained—meaning, the calculation is performed to determine exactly how much longevity a planet grants at a specific time. **The planet subtracted by its own exaltation** = the planet minus its highest point. **If less than six signs** = if it is less than a half-circle, then it is subtracted from the **circle of the zodiac** = twelve signs. If the resulting planet is **greater than six signs**, it should be kept **as it is**, without further alteration.

This is what is being said: From whichever planet the longevity is being calculated, one should subtract that planet's point of exaltation. If the exaltation point is greater than the planet's position, one should add twelve signs to the planet and then subtract the exaltation. If the planet (minus exaltation) is less than six signs, subtract that value from twelve signs. If it is more than six signs, leave it as it is. Then, that resulting figure is **converted into minutes** and **multiplied by its own years** = the standard years of life assigned to that planet. In that product, when **divided by 21,600** (represented by the mnemonic *kha-abhra-rasa-candra-locana* <note>A traditional Sanskrit numerical code: kha=0, abhra=0, rasa=6, candra=1, locana=2, read right-to-left as 21,600.</note>), the result obtained in years, months, days, etc., is called the **rectified longevity** by the wise. This same subject is covered in the sixth verse as well. Where it says "divided by the zodiac," it should be interpreted as "subtracted from the zodiac (12 signs)." || 4-6 ||

**Here the rationale <term>Upapatti: mathematical proof or logical derivation</term> is stated:**
When a planet is at its point of exaltation, it grants its full recorded years of life. From that exaltation point, the life-granting power decreases equally in both directions until it reaches its point of fall (debilitation), where only half the life remains, according to the rule: "At the fall, it is half." Therefore, to find the distance between the planet's current position and its exaltation, the "planet minus exaltation" calculation is performed. Since a distance of six signs (180 degrees) reduces the longevity by half, the proportion is:

$\frac{\text{Desired Distance} \times \text{Longevity Factor}}{\text{6 Signs}}$ — The result subtracted from the full longevity gives the longevity at the desired position.

$\therefore \text{Longevity at desired position} = \text{Full Longevity} - \frac{\text{Full Longevity} \times \text{Distance}}{\text{2} \times \text{6}} = \frac{\text{12} \times \text{Longevity} - \text{Longevity} \times \text{Distance}}{\text{12}}$

$= \frac{\text{Longevity ( 12 - Distance )}}{\text{12}}$. This explains why, if the planet-minus-exaltation is less than six signs, it is subtracted from the zodiac (1) <note>This ensures the calculation accounts for the planet moving toward or away from the point of maximum strength.</note>.

Now, if the distance between the planet and its exaltation is more than six signs—meaning the planet has passed its point of fall and is moving back toward its exaltation—the logic is: at the point of fall, the life is half; it then increases until it is full at the exaltation point. In the six signs from fall to exaltation, it increases by half.

Therefore, the proportion is $\frac{\text{Desired Distance} \times \text{Longevity Factor}}{\text{6}}$, and the result added to the "fall-longevity" (half of the full life) becomes the longevity at the desired position.

$\therefore$ Longevity at the desired position = Longevity at exaltation + $\frac{\text{Difference} \times \text{Longevity at exaltation}}{2 \times 6} = \frac{6 \times \text{Longevity at exaltation} + \text{Longevity at exaltation} \times \text{Difference}}{12}$

$= \frac{\text{Longevity at exaltation } (6 + \text{Difference})}{12}$. Here, "Difference" = the distance from the planet's debilitation point; therefore, 6 + Difference = the distance from the exaltation point.

Thus, it is established that the calculation follows the distance from the exaltation point as the planet moves forward from its debilitation (2).
In these two forms (1) and (2), which are expressed in zodiac signs, when converted into minutes of arc <note>original: "liptīkṛtayoḥ"</note>, the divisor is 12 $\times$ 30 $\times$ 60 = 21,600'. By this, everything is proven, so let us not dwell further on the details. || 4-6 ||

The clarification of <term>Pindayu</term> <note>Longevity based on planetary positions at birth</note> and <term>Nisargayu</term> <note>Longevity based on the natural years assigned to planets</note> is as follows—Subtract the exaltation point from the longitude of the planet. If the resulting value is less than 6 signs, subtract it from 12 signs; if it is more than 6 signs, keep it as it is. Convert that value into minutes of arc and multiply it by the years of the planet's natural or Pindayu longevity. Divide that by 21,600. The resulting years, months, days, and minutes <note>original: "daṇḍa"</note> obtained will be the <term>Spashtayu</term> <note>rectified or clear longevity</note> of that planet derived from the Pindayu or Nisargayu systems. || 4-6 ||

For example—The longitude of Mercury is 1s 9° 29' 49". Mercury's exaltation point is 5s 15° 0' 0". Subtracting the exaltation point from Mercury's longitude, the remainder is 7s 29° 29' 49". This difference is greater than 6 signs (if it were less than 6 signs, it would have been subtracted from 12). Therefore, the minutes of arc for this difference were calculated as 14,369' 49". Multiplying this by Mercury's Pindayu (12 years) gives 172,437' 48". Dividing this by 21,600, Mercury's longevity in years etc. becomes 7y 5m 27d 1m. This is the rectified Pindayu. The clarification of Nisargayu is done in the same way. (By the author of Sudhakara Shastra) || 4-6 ||

->### Now, the Reduction of Longevity in the Ascendant.<-

> If a planet is at its debilitation point, its longevity is reduced by half; if it is between exaltation and debilitation, the reduction is proportional.
> The longevity of the <term>Hora</term> <note>Ascendant/Lagna</note> is equal to the number of Navamshas <note>1/9th divisions of a sign</note> it has passed; others say it is equal to the number of signs.
> Excluding Mars <note>original: "vakra"</note>, planets in an enemy's house lose one-third of their longevity.
> For planets that have set <note>combust by the Sun</note>, half is discarded, except for Venus and Saturn. || 7 ||
> Excluding the son of the Earth (Mars), those in enemy positions lose a third; those in debilitation lose half.
> Those that have set (become combust) lose half, except for Venus and the son of the Sun (Saturn). || 8 ||

Now, the reduction of the previously stated longevity based on the planet's position is described. When a planet is at its debilitation point, its longevity is reduced by half from the full amount stated. If the planet is between its exaltation and debilitation points, a proportion <note>Rule of Three</note> should be applied. For example: if for a distance of half a circle (10,800') between exaltation and debilitation, half of the stated longevity is lost, then what is lost for the desired planet's distance from exaltation? The result should be subtracted from the maximum longevity; the remainder will be the rectified longevity (<term>Pindayu</term> or <term>Nisargayu</term>) of the desired planet.

Now, the longevity of the Ascendant (<term>Lagnayu</term>). In the <term>Hora</term> (Ascendant), the longevity is equal to the number of <term>Navamshas</term>—meaning, however many Navamshas have been passed by the Ascendant in whichever sign it occupies, that many years (and months etc. by proportion) should be known as the longevity of the Ascendant. Here, some other teachers say the longevity of the Ascendant is equal to the number of signs. However many signs have been traversed by the Ascendant, that many years are given. As <margin>Manittha says</margin>:

> "The years are equal to the signs of the Ascendant, and months etc. are by proportion.
> Those skilled in the science of the Ascendant <note>Hora Shastra</note> desire this as the longevity contribution of the Ascendant."

Now, the reduction of the already established longevity: Excluding <term>Vakra</term> (Mars), for planets situated in an enemy's house <note>original: "ripugṛha"</note>, one-third (1/3) of their established personal longevity is lost. The implication is that Mars does not lose longevity even when in an enemy's house. It has been said—

# Chapter on the Granting of Longevity (Ayurdaya) || 5 ||

"Except for the son of the Earth <note>Mars</note>, planets situated in the houses of enemies destroy one-third of their own longevity," so says Badarayana <note>An ancient sage and authority in astrology</note>.

Likewise, excluding Venus and the son of the Sun <note>Saturn</note>—that is, leaving out Venus and Saturn—planets whose light is destroyed by the Sun—meaning those whose brilliance is diminished because they are combust <note>too close to the Sun</note>—lose half of their longevity. Even when combust, Venus and Saturn do not lose their longevity; however, for other planets that are combust, half of their established longevity is lost. || 7 ||

Regarding the eighth verse, because its meaning is similar to the previous (7th) verse, it has not been explained separately to avoid repetition. || 8 ||

The full longevity stated for planets in their sign of exaltation <note>highest strength</note> is reduced by half when they are in their sign of debilitation <note>lowest strength</note>; that is, the longevity of planets in debilitation is halved. For example, the Sun's longevity in Aries <insert>Sign 0</insert> at 10 degrees is 20 years, while in Libra <insert>Sign 6</insert> at 10 degrees it is 10 years. This should be understood for all planets. If a planet is between its exaltation and debilitation points, one should understand the value through proportion <term>Anupata: mathematical rule of three</term>. For instance, if 6 signs (10,800 minutes of arc) cause a reduction of half the longevity, what would the reduction be for the specific distance between this planet and its exaltation point? Here, one should calculate the distance between the planet and its exaltation point on both sides and apply the proportion. Subtract the result from the full longevity to get the planet's "Rectified Body-Longevity" <term>Spashta Pindayu</term> or "Natural Longevity" <term>Nisargayu</term>. Except for Mars, a planet in an enemy's house destroys one-third (1/3) of its longevity. Mars receives full longevity even in an enemy's house. Except for Venus and Saturn, all planets destroy half of their longevity when combust. Venus and Saturn receive full longevity even when combust. (According to the author of Surya Siddhanta) || 7-8 ||

### Now, the Reductions for the 12th House and Others

> The whole, a half, a third, a fourth, a fifth, and a sixth part are reduced from the twelfth house backwards for malefic planets.
> For benefic planets, the reduction is half of that. If multiple planets are in one sign, only the strongest one causes the reduction; so says Satyacharya. || 9 ||

> Among those situated in a single sign, he who is specifically superior in strength
> reduces the portion as stated; no other planet situated there does so. || 10 ||

"For malefics" = cruel planets; "from the twelfth house" = the 12th house of the horoscope; "backwards" = in reverse order. If malefic planets are situated starting from the 12th house back to the 7th house, then the whole, half, third, fourth, fifth, and sixth parts of their longevity are reduced. For example, a malefic in the 12th house removes the entire longevity. In the 11th, it removes half. In the 10th, a third. In the 9th, a fourth. In the 8th, a fifth. In the 7th, it removes a sixth part. "For benefics, half" means if benefic planets are in those same positions, they remove half of what was stated for the malefics. Thus, a benefic in the 12th removes half. In the 11th, a fourth. In the 10th, a sixth. In the 9th, an eighth. In the 8th, a tenth. In the 7th, it removes a twelfth part. Likewise, for those "situated in one sign," when two or more planets are in the same house, only the strongest planet among them reduces its specific portion as taught, and no other planet of lesser strength does so; this is what the teacher Satyacharya says. As it is said:

> "Among those situated in a single sign, he who is specifically superior in strength
> reduces the portion as stated; no other planet situated there does so."

Here, the tenth verse spoken by Satyacharya supports the meaning of the previous verse. || 9-10 ||

If a malefic planet is in the 12th house, the full longevity is reduced. In the 11th, half; in the 10th, a third; in the 9th, a quarter; in the 8th, a fifth; and in the 7th, a sixth part is reduced. For a benefic planet, half of these amounts will be reduced. For example, in the 12th, half; in the 11th, a quarter; in the 10th, a sixth; in the 9th, an eighth; in the 8th, a tenth; and in the 7th, a twelfth part is reduced. If two, three, or many planets are in the same place, the portions of all planets are not reduced; only the portion of the one who is most powerful among them is reduced. That is, whatever reduction is prescribed for a malefic or benefic in that house, it will only apply to the one strongest planet. Although the waning Moon and Mercury associated with malefics are considered cruel...

### Now, the Reduction for a Malefic in the Ascendant.

Multiply the total longevity by the number of elapsed Navamsas <note>A Navamsa is a 1/9th division of a zodiac sign, equal to 3 degrees and 20 minutes</note> including the fractional part already risen; then divide by one hundred and eight (108). The resulting value is the loss of longevity. This occurs when a malefic planet is present in the Ascendant. If that malefic is aspected by a benefic planet, only half of the calculated loss is removed. || 11 ||

One should multiply the individual longevity of the planets by the degrees of the Ascendant converted into minutes. Divide that product by 21,600 <note>The total number of minutes in a full circle of 360 degrees</note>. The resulting years and months should be subtracted from the planet's calculated longevity. || 12 ||

This calculation is performed when a malefic is in the Ascendant. If that malefic is aspected by a benefic, subtract only half of that result. This procedure should be applied to the <term>Pindayu</term> <note>Longevity based on planetary positions</note> and <term>Nisargikayu</term> <note>Natural longevity system</note> systems, but it is not to be performed in the <term>Amshayu</term> <note>Longevity based on Navamsa divisions</note> system. || 13 ||

Now the author explains the reduction for a malefic planet in the Ascendant. **When a malefic** = a cruel planet **is present in the Ascendant** = situated in the Lagna, **multiply by the elapsed Navamsas including the fractional part** = the number of Navamsas that have risen (passed), multiplied by the total longevity calculated for the planet. This is what is meant: the degrees passed by the Ascendant at that time should be converted to minutes and divided by two hundred (200) to find the elapsed Navamsas with their fractions. Multiply each planet's calculated longevity by this, and divide by one hundred and eight (108). The resulting longevity is the "destruction" = it is lost. Therefore, that amount should be subtracted from the total calculated longevity of the planet; the remainder is the planet's clear (rectified) longevity. Now, if that same malefic in the Ascendant is **aspected by a benefic** = seen by a favorable planet, then by this method, only **half** = 1/2 of the calculated loss goes to **destruction** = is lost, not the full amount. Once this is done, the rectified years of the planets' periods (Dashas) are produced.

The same point is stated again: **By converting to minutes.** Multiply the individual longevity of the planets by the **Ascendant degrees** = the degrees passed by the Ascendant, **converted to minutes**. Divide that by **sky-space-sun-moon-back** <note>A traditional Sanskrit numerical code (Bhuta-sankhya) where Sky=0, Space=0, Sun=6, Moon=2, read backwards as 21,600</note> (21,600). The resulting years etc. should be subtracted from the planet's calculated longevity to get the clear longevity. This action is to be taken when a malefic is in the Ascendant. If that malefic is aspected by a benefic, subtract half the result. **In the system known as Amshayu** = longevity based on divisions, this action is not to be performed. The idea is that in Amshayu, even if a malefic is in the Ascendant, there is no loss of longevity. This should be done for Pindayu and **Nisargikayu** (Natural longevity). Just as the work was done for Pindayu, it must be done for Natural longevity as well. Regarding this, Kalyanavarman says: "Multiply the longevity of each planet by the minutes of the Ascendant's Navamsa. Divide by the minutes of the circle (21,600) and subtract the resulting years. This applies when a malefic is in the Ascendant; if aspected by a benefic, it is half."

Now the mathematical rationale (derivation) is stated—Since it is said "the hour (Lagna) is proportional to the division," we see a decrease in planetary longevity based on the Ascendant's Navamsa. At the start of the Ascendant, the loss is zero; at the end of the Ascendant, the loss is 1/12th of the total longevity. The proportion for the nine Navamsas of one sign is:

If for 9 Navamsas, the loss is equal to 1/12th part, then for the desired elapsed Navamsas of the Ascendant, what is it?
$\frac{Longevity}{12} \times \frac{Elapsed\ Navamsas}{9} =$

$\frac{Longevity \times Elapsed\ Navamsas}{108} =$ The degrees of longevity to be subtracted. $\therefore$ Thus it is proven.

Now, in the form $\frac{Longevity \times Elapsed\ Navamsas}{108}$, if we multiply both the divisor and the dividend by two hundred (200), we get the minutes of the elapsed Navamsas of the Ascendant.
- In one Navamsa, there are 200 minutes. Thus, the divisor becomes 21,600.

$\frac{Longevity \times Elapsed\ Navamsas \times 200}{108 \times 200} = \frac{Longevity \times Ascendant\ Minutes}{21,600}$
