# Chapter on the Determination of Lifespan || 5 ||

Therefore—multiply the minutes of the Ascendant's portion by the individual lifespan of the planets and divide by the total minutes of the circle (21,600); this method stated by <term>Kalyanavarma</term><note>A famous 6th-century astrologer, author of Saravali</note> is also logical. || 11-13 ||

Now, the refinement process is as follows: The number of <term>Navamshas</term><note>A 1/9th division of a zodiac sign, equal to 3 degrees and 20 minutes</note> of the Ascendant that have already passed are called the "risen Navamshas." By using the rule of three on the portion of the current Navamsha that has passed at birth, and adding that result to the risen Navamshas, one obtains the "Corrected Risen Navamsha." Convert this into minutes. If there are <term>malefic planets</term><note>Natural "cruel" planets like Mars or Saturn</note> in the Ascendant, multiply this by the lifespan total of the desired planet and divide by 108. The resulting value should be subtracted from that planet's years. If a <term>benefic planet</term><note>Natural "gentle" planets like Jupiter or Venus</note> fully aspects (looks at) that malefic in the Ascendant, then only half of that result should be subtracted.

Regarding this refinement, some teachers interpret it thus: If there are malefics in the Ascendant, multiply the total lifespan of all planets by the Corrected Risen Navamsha, divide by 108, and subtract the result from the total sum. If there is a benefic in the Ascendant, subtract half of that result. The remainder is the lifespan of all planets. Then, calculate the individual years for each planet. || 11 ||

Convert the degrees passed in the Ascendant into minutes, multiply them by the individual lifespan of each planet, and divide by 21,600. Subtract the result from the mathematically derived lifespan of the planets; the remainder is the "clear" or corrected lifespan of the planet. However, this process should only be performed if a malefic planet is in the Ascendant. If that malefic is aspected by a benefic, only half the resulting years should be subtracted. Note that this specific method is not used in the <term>Anshayu</term><note>Lifespan calculated by degrees</note> system. The procedure for <term>Nisargayu</term><note>Natural lifespan system</note> should be done similarly to <term>Pindayu</term><note>Lifespan based on planetary exaltation</note>. || 12-13 ||

### Now, the Calculation of the Ascendant’s Lifespan.

> In these systems, if the Ascendant is strong, discard the signs and convert the remaining portion into minutes. Divide this by two hundred; the resulting years and months should be added to the Ascendant's lifespan. || 14 ||
>
> Experts in the science of <term>Hora</term><note>Astrology</note> desire the Ascendant's lifespan to be equal to the number of signs passed, with months calculated by proportion. || 15 ||

Now the Ascendant's lifespan is being determined. "In these" means that just as the lifespan of planets is calculated, so too is the lifespan of the Ascendant calculated in the Pindayu and other systems. There, if the Ascendant is "strong" (endowed with its six-fold strength), discard the full signs and convert the passed degrees into minutes. Divide these by two hundred; the resulting years, etc., are the Ascendant's lifespan. Regarding the measure of the Ascendant's lifespan, it is not stated exactly like the planets, for the scriptures say: "The Ascendant's contribution is equal to its Navamshas; others say it is equal to the signs." Here, when the minutes of the Ascendant are divided by 200, we get the number of Navamshas; thus, the view that "the Ascendant's contribution is equal to its Navamshas" is consistent. Now the view "others say it is equal to the signs" is explained: however many signs (Aries, etc.) have passed in the Ascendant, that many years are granted, with months determined by proportion. For months, the proportion is: if 1800 minutes (one sign) equal 12 months, then how many months do the passed minutes of the Ascendant equal? Add these to the years to find the Ascendant's lifespan. On this, <term>Keshava</term><note>A medieval authority on astrological mathematics</note> says:

> "The years are derived from the degrees... some say the Ascendant's life is equal to its Navamshas, others say more. Whichever lord is stronger, that should be taken by others... but the view that it is equal to the Navamshas is the primary one to be accepted."

Because of this statement, it is also my opinion that the Ascendant's lifespan should be taken as equal to its Navamshas. || 14-15 ||

## Commentary on Jataka Parijata

In the previously mentioned methods of <term>Ayurdaya</term> <note>calculation of longevity</note>, if the <term>Lagna</term> <note>the Ascendant or the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</note> is strong—meaning it is aspected by its own lord, Jupiter, or Mercury—then one should exclude the sign of the <term>Lagna</term> and convert the elapsed degrees into minutes. By dividing those minutes by 200, the resulting years and months constitute the <term>Lagnayu</term> <note>longevity contributed by the Ascendant</note>. Some authorities hold the opinion that the number of signs passed by the <term>Lagna</term> equals the number of years, and for the remaining degrees, a rule of three is applied: if 1800 minutes equal 12 months, what do the elapsed minutes equal? The total years and months thus obtained represent the <term>Lagnayu</term>. However, the former opinion is supported by the majority of scholars. (Su. Sha. Kar) || 14-15 ||

### Regarding the Sixfold Reduction (Shadvidha-Harana)

> If the cruel planets are in the Ascendant, setting, in an enemy's house, in debilitation, or moving toward a planet; or if they are placed in the 12th, 11th, 10th, 9th, 8th, or 7th houses; after performing the sixfold reduction for the Sun and other planets, and adding the remaining years to the longevity of the Ascendant, the total equals the lifespan. || 16 ||

Now the sixfold <term>Harana</term> <note>reduction or subtraction of years from the calculated lifespan due to unfavorable planetary conditions</note> is described:
1. <term>Krurodaya-Harana</term>: Reduction due to a malefic planet in the Ascendant.
2. <term>Astangata-Harana</term>: Reduction due to a planet being combust (too close to the Sun).
3. <term>Ripukshetra-Harana</term>: Reduction due to a planet being in an enemy's sign (excluding Mars).
4. <term>Nichagata-Harana</term>: Reduction due to a planet being in its sign of debilitation.
5. <term>Khagopagana-Harana</term>: Reduction due to planets being in conjunction.
6. <term>Vyayadi-Harana</term>: Reduction for planets situated in the 12th, 11th, 10th, 9th, 8th, and 7th houses.

After applying these six reductions to the Sun and other planets, the remaining planetary years are added to the <term>Lagnayu</term>. The sum of these eight (the seven planets plus the Ascendant) constitutes the <term>Spashtayu</term> <note>the distinct or corrected lifespan</note> of the person born. || 16 ||

The essence is: after all reductions, the remaining years of the Sun and other planets must be summed with the years of the Ascendant. This total equals the human lifespan. (Su. Sha. Kar) || 16 ||

### Regarding Amshakayu (Longevity based on Navamsha)

> Jiva Sharma says that according to his own view, the great lifespan is one-seventh of the maximum life. The longevity is equal to the number of Navamshas <note>the 1/9th division of a sign</note> elapsed by the planet; this is very similar to the statement of Satya. || 17 ||
> In Satya's teaching, convert the desired planet's position into minutes and divide by 200. If the result exceeds the signs, the remainder gives the months and other units. || 18 ||
> The years are tripled if the planet is in its exaltation or retrograde, and doubled if in its Vargottama, own Navamsha, or own sign. This is the specific detail in my teaching; other things are the same as previously stated. || 19 ||
> However, here the planet gives years equal to its Navamsha, and a powerful Ascendant gives years equal to its sign. The reduction for a malefic in the Ascendant is not to be applied here, nor are the years from the first method used. || 20 ||
> The teaching of Satya is superior here, but some make it unsuitable through excessive multiplications. In the case of multiple multipliers, only the highest one should be applied. || 21 ||

Now the measure of longevity according to the views of <term>Jiva Sharma</term> and <term>Satyacharya</term> is explained. Among them, <term>Satyacharya's</term> <term>Amshakayu</term> <note>longevity based on the 1/9th divisional chart</note> is preferred by the learned. In this method, the sign itself is not the primary factor. <term>Jiva Sharma</term> states that the contribution of each planet is one-seventh (<term>Svaramsha</term>) of the maximum lifespan (which is 120 years and 5 days), resulting in approximately 17 years, 1 month, 22 days, 8 ghatis, and 34 palas per planet. This is for planets in exaltation; for those in debilitation, it is halved. As <term>Jiva Sharma</term> said:

> "The years for the planets [Sun to Saturn] in exaltation are 19, 25, 12, 15, 12, 8, and 4 respectively; in debilitation, they are half of that." <note>original: "समदशौ द्वियमौ वसवो वेदाग्नयो..."</note>

# Chapter 5: On the Determination of Longevity

->The calculation should be done through proportional distribution; whatever remains here<-
->should be treated by those skilled in the principles of mathematics just as in the Pindayu system.<-

Therefore, the sage Jivasharman performed all the operations, such as the clarification of longevity, in an identical manner; the only difference lies in the recitation of the years. However, this specific longevity [calculated by Jivasharman] is not accepted by anyone. <note>Jivasharman’s system is often cited in classical texts only to be refuted in favor of more accurate methods.</note> Now, the opinion of the teacher Satyacharya is stated. The longevity of a planet is equal to the number of the sign of the *Navamsha* <term>Navamsha: A one-ninth division of a zodiac sign, used for fine-tuning astrological strength</term> occupied by that planet. For example, if a planet is in the Leo *Navamsha* in any sign, then its longevity is 5 years; if in the Capricorn *Navamsha*, it is 10 years, and so on for all cases. This statement of Satyacharya attains "great similarity"—meaning it shares a likeness with the statements of many other teachers. As it is said:

> "Longevity arises from the combination of the sign, the portion, and the movement," says Yavaneshvara. <note>original: "Ayushi rashyanshakacharyogat"</note>

By saying that Satya’s words attain great similarity, it is implied that Varahamihira also favors Satya’s opinion. On this point, Badarayana also says:

> "The signs, degrees, and minutes should be multiplied by twelve and nine [respectively] from the planet's revolutions.
> When divided by twelve, the remainder gives the years, months, days, and minutes in order."

Now, the calculation of longevity according to Satyacharya’s method is performed by Varahamihira. In the method taught by Satya (where longevity equals the number of the *Navamsha* sign occupied), one should take the desired planet and convert its position into minutes. When this is divided by two hundred, the quotient obtained—if it exceeds twelve—should be cleared of cycles (divided by twelve). The remainder represents the years. The implication is that the *Amshayu* (longevity based on portions) does not exceed twelve years per planet. Similarly, the months and other units are derived from the remainder. The remainder from the division by two hundred is multiplied by twelve and divided by that same divisor (200) to get the months. Likewise, the remainder of the months is multiplied by thirty and divided by the divisor to get the days. The remainder of the days is multiplied by sixty and divided by the divisor to get the *Dandas* <term>Danda: A unit of time equal to 24 minutes</term>.

**Example:** At that time, a planet is at 2 signs, 5 degrees, 10 minutes, 0 seconds.
Its total minutes = 3910.
Divided by two hundred: 3910 ÷ 200 = 19, with a remainder of 110.
Since 19 is greater than twelve, the remainder after dividing by twelve = 7.
Therefore, 7 years.
The previous remainder 110 is multiplied by twelve: 110 × 12 = 1320.
Divided by the divisor: 1320 ÷ 200 = 6 months.
The remainder 120 is multiplied by thirty: 120 × 30 = 3600.
Divided by the divisor: 3600 ÷ 200 = 18 days.
Thus, the resulting longevity is 7 years, 6 months, 18 days, and 0 minutes.

Now, he states a special rule regarding this longevity method of Satyacharya: "Exaltation," etc. Those planets which are in their exaltation or are in retrograde motion <note>original: "Vakropagata"</note>—the longevity given by them must be tripled. This means the mathematically calculated longevity is multiplied by three for retrograde planets. For those in their own "Best Division" (*Vargottama*), *Navamsha*, Sign, or *Decan* <term>Decan: A ten-degree division of a sign</term>, the longevity given by them must be doubled. The sense is that for those in their own divisions, the longevity is twice as much. In the longevity system spoken by you (Satyacharya), this is the specific rule: triple for exaltation/retrograde and double for own divisions. It is implied that this is not mentioned by anyone else. All other reductions—such as halving for debilitation, reducing by a third for an enemy's house, or halving for combustion <note>original: "Astangata" - when a planet is too close to the sun</note>—should be understood in Satya’s method just as they were stated in the first method (of the previous teachers).

Now, he states a special rule for the longevity of the Ascendant (*Lagna*) in Satya’s method: "But here specifically," etc. In this system of Satyacharya, the Ascendant gives longevity proportional to its degrees and portions. The years are equal to the number of the sign of the *Navamsha* occupied by the Ascendant. For example, in the Aries *Navamsha*, it is one year; in the Taurus *Navamsha*, two years; and so on, increasing up to twelve years for the Pisces *Navamsha*. The months and other units should be calculated by the same proportional method used for the planets. If the *Hora* (Ascendant) is endowed with strength—meaning the Ascendant is aspected by its own lord, Jupiter, or Mercury—

# With the Commentary on Jataka Parijata

<page-num>132</page-num>
<header>With the Commentary on Jataka Parijata</header>

If the horoscope is characterized by the described traits, then it is "equal to the signs" = the number of years given in the lifespan calculation corresponds to the number of signs from Aries onwards that have been traversed by the Ascendant. Even there, the months and other units should be known according to the portion of the sign already traversed. Thus it was said by **Badarayana** <note>An ancient sage often cited in astrological texts</note>:
> The lifespan contribution of the Ascendant is also determined by its strength; it grants years equal to the signs traversed, and the results for degrees and minutes are found through proportion.

Here, in the lifespan system of the Satya school <note>original: "Satyamatamshurdaye"</note>, the reduction that is performed according to the methods of previous teachers—such as the reduction for a malefic rising or for a planet being visible in the second half of the visible hemisphere—should not be performed. Similarly, the clarification of the lifespan should not be done using the years previously taught like "nine, moon, arrows, and twins" <note>A mnemonic for 25, 19, etc.</note> nor by the rule "the planet's contribution is a fraction of the maximum lifespan."

Now, regarding this matter of lifespan, he explains the acceptance of the Satya school's opinion—**Satya etc.** In this calculation of lifespan, the instruction of Satya is better = more correct than that of other teachers. However, even though the Satya method is superior, some make it "unfit" = they ruin it through "multiple multiplications" = by multiplying the value three times for being in exaltation, and so on. For example, if a planet is in its own "six-fold division" <term>Shadvarga: a system of six divisional charts used to assess planetary strength</term>, they double the lifespan because it is in its own house. If it is also in its own decan <term>Drekkana: a 10-degree subdivision of a sign</term>, they double it again; if it is in its exaltation, they triple it. Through such repeated calculations, a state of "infinite regress" or instability occurs. As it is said:
> Double the value if the planet is in the best division (Vargottama), its own sign, its own decan, or its own ninth-part (Navamsha). Triple it if it is in retrograde or exaltation; these should be applied respectively.

In this way, through multiple multiplications, they make the Satya method unfit. Therefore, in the case of "multiplicity" = when repeated calculations are possible, only the one that is "greatest" = the highest value should be applied. If doubling is required repeatedly, it should be doubled only once. Where both doubling and tripling are applicable, it should be tripled only once. If tripling is required repeatedly, it should be tripled only once. This is the view favored by the Great Teachers. Thus says the teacher **Varaha** <note>Varahamihira, the 6th-century polymath</note> in his *Svalpa Jataka*:
> Double the value once if it is in the best division (Vargottama) or its own ninth-part. Triple it for retrograde motion or exaltation. If both doubling and tripling are applicable, triple it only once.

Just as only one great calculation is performed in the case of multiplicity, similarly, if multiple reductions are applicable, only one reduction—the greatest one—should be performed. Thus says the **Lord Garga**:
> ... "Then, even if many others are applicable, only one should be performed—whichever among them is the greatest. Even then, the multiplication should be done only once, using the highest value." || 18-21 ||

In the third verse of this chapter, the planetary lifespan was stated in the order of 19 years for the Sun, 25 years for the Moon, etc. However, it is the opinion of Jivasharma that the maximum lifespan for humans is 120 years and 5 days. There are seven planets starting with the Sun; the equal lifespan for all of them when in exaltation is 57 years, 1 month, 21 days, 8 ghatis, 34 palas, and 17 vipalas <note>Traditional units of time: 1 Ghati = 24 minutes</note>. In debilitation, it is half of this: 28 years, 6 months, 15 days, 34 ghatis, and 17 vipalas. Values in between are determined by proportion. The rules for the "Wheel of Action" and "Nodes" are the same as previously stated. This matter was stated by Jivasharma based on his own reasoning alone. No one else agrees with this. The measure stated by Varahamihira, following the school of Vallaneshvara and Satyacharya, is the correct one.

In any sign, the years of planetary lifespan should be known as equal to the number of the ninth-part (Navamsha) the planet occupies. For example, being in the first Navamsha (Aries) gives 1 year; in the second (Taurus) 2 years; and so on, increasing up to 12 years for the twelfth Navamsha (Pisces). This opinion of Satyacharya is agreed upon by the majority of teachers. See the Sanskrit commentary. || 17 ||

According to the school of Satyacharya, the determination of lifespan is as follows: convert the degrees and minutes of the longitude of the planet into a "total of minutes" <term>Kalapinda: the sum total of arc-minutes</term> and divide it by 200. The quotient obtained should be known as years. If the quotient is more than 12, divide it by 12 and take the remainder as the years. After dividing by 200, multiply the remainder by 12 and divide again by 200 to get the months. Multiply the remainder by 30...

# Chapter on the Determination of Longevity (Ayurdaya) || 5 ||

Multiply the remainder by 60 and divide by two hundred to obtain the days. Multiply that remainder by 60 and divide by 200 to obtain the *ghati* <note>a unit of time equal to 24 minutes</note>; multiply the next remainder by 60 and divide by 200 to obtain the *pala* <note>a unit of time equal to 24 seconds</note>.

See the Sanskrit commentary for an example. (Sudhakar Shah) || 18 ||

The rationale for this is: according to the rule "equal to the signs and *navamshas* <note>the ninth part of a zodiac sign, used as a primary unit for calculating years of life</note> traversed by the planet," the years are determined by the planet's position. Therefore, by dividing the total minutes (*kala*) of the signs and degrees traversed by the planet by 200, the quotient is the number of *navamshas*.
$\because$ 1 *navamsha* contains 200 minutes.
$\therefore$ (Planet's traversed minutes) $\div$ 200 = *navamshas* = years.

Since the number of zodiac signs is only 12, if the number of *navamshas* (years) exceeds 12, it is appropriate to divide by 12.

Regarding the remainder: if 200 minutes equal 1 year (12 months), then the months etc. are derived from the remaining minutes using the ratio $\frac{12 \times \text{remainder}}{200}$. (Sudhakar Shah) || 18 ||

In the opinion of Satyacharya, there is this specific detail: if a planet is in its sign of exaltation or is in retrograde motion, the years of life obtained should be tripled. If a planet is in its *vargottama navamsha* <note>occupying the same sign in both the main chart and the ninth divisional chart</note>, its own *navamsha*, its own *drekkana* <note>a ten-degree subdivision</note>, or its own sign, the value should be doubled. All other operations should be performed as previously described. For a planet in an enemy's sign, one-third is deducted, and for a planet that is combust (except for Venus and Saturn), half is deducted. Reductions should also be made according to the verse **"Sarvardha..."** regarding the *chakra-pata* <note>reductions based on a planet's placement in specific houses relative to the ascendant</note>. || 19 ||

Here, in Satyacharya’s view, the Ascendant (*Lagna*) gives a lifespan equal to its traversed *navamshas*. If the Ascendant is strong (aspected by or occupied by its lord, Jupiter, or Mercury), it gives years equal to the traversed signs. In Satyacharya’s system, the reductions usually applied for malefic risings should not be performed. Furthermore, the final calculation of life should not be derived from the previously mentioned *Pindayu* <note>longevity based on planetary planetary contributions</note> or *Nisargayu* <note>natural longevity</note> methods.

Satyacharya’s opinion is considered superior to those of Maya and Jivasharma. However, a doubt arises: if a planet is in its own house, it is doubled; if it is also in its own *navamsha*, it would be doubled again; if in its own *drekkana*, doubled again; if in *vargottama*, doubled again; if retrograde, tripled; and if exalted, tripled again—leading to an infinite or absurd result. The resolution to this doubt is in the latter half of the verse: even if there are multiple reasons to double, double only once. Even if there are multiple reasons to triple, triple only once. Where there are reasons for both doubling and tripling, triple only once. In the case of reductions, if multiple reductions apply, only one will be taken (except for *chakra-pata*, which is applied to all); specifically, between a 1/2 and 1/3 reduction, the 1/2 reduction is taken. Where there is both a reduction and an increase, first apply the primary reduction, then apply the primary increase. In the reduction process, first account for the loss from *chakra-pata*, then other reductions, and finally the increases. This is the *Anshayu* <note>longevity based on divisional portions</note> system. The Teacher <note>referring to Varahamihira</note> has accepted *Anshayu* as the most authoritative, setting aside *Pindayu* and *Nisargayu*. In other views, *Anshayu* is used if the Ascendant is strongest, *Pindayu* if the Sun is strongest, and *Nisargayu* if the Moon is strongest. || 21 ||

### Now, Longevity derived from Rays (Rashmijayu).

**Ten, nine, eight, five, five, seven, and eight are the rays for the Sun and the other planets respectively when in their highest exaltation. || 22 ||**
**Subtract the planet's position from its exaltation point; if the result exceeds six signs, subtract it from twelve signs. Convert this to minutes and multiply by the ray-values. Divide by the total minutes in a circle to find the years and other units. This is called the longevity born of the rays of the Sun and others. || 23 ||**

Now the calculation of the rays of the planets is described. For the Sun and others located in their exaltation points—

There are rays numbering ten and so on. The Sun has ten. The Moon has "cows" = nine <note>The word 'Gau' (cow) is a Sanskrit numerical symbol for 9</note>. Mars has "arrows" = five. Mercury has "arrows" = five. Jupiter has "mountains" = seven. Venus has "Vasus" = eight <note>The Vasus are a group of eight deities</note>. Saturn's "arrows" = five rays are to be known. Planets in their sign of debilitation <term>Neecha: the point where a planet is weakest</term> are devoid of rays; planets moving from debilitation toward exaltation <term>Uccha: the point where a planet is strongest</term> are called "facing toward rays," and those moving from exaltation toward debilitation are called "facing away." Thus it is said in the *Saravali*:

> "Ten for the Sun in its exaltation, nine for the Moon, and five for the son of Earth (Mars).
> Five for the son of the Moon (Mercury), seven for the teacher of the gods (Jupiter), eight for the descendant of Bhrigu (Venus), and five for Saturn.
> Thus in the scriptures of Great Indra, and those spoken by Manittha and Badarayana.
> Seven rays are specified for each of the lordly planets <note>This refers to an alternative school of thought</note>.
> All these are authoritative due to the words of the Sages, but the number seven is also used.
> According to many statements, a planet in its debilitation becomes devoid of rays.
> One fallen from debilitation is 'facing rays,' and one fallen from its exaltation is known as 'facing away.'"

Now, the calculation of a planet's rays between its exaltation and debilitation points: Subtract the planet's exaltation point from the desired planet's position. If the resulting value is less than six signs, or if it exceeds six signs, subtract it from the "Circle" (12 signs). Convert this into minutes of arc <term>Kalika: 1/60th of a degree</term>, multiply it by the planet's specific ray-count at exaltation, and divide by the total minutes in the zodiac (21,600'). The result is the lifespan in years etc., generated by the rays of the Sun and others; so say the wise. Here, the author of the present text, like in the *Pinda* lifespan system, accepts a full ray when the planet is exalted and half of that when it is debilitated. In the interval of six signs between debilitation and exaltation, half the ray remains; therefore, the result is obtained by a proportion based on the distance between the desired planet and its exaltation.

$R. — \frac{R.}{2} \times \frac{A}{6} = \frac{R. \times 12 - R. \times A}{12}$
---
$\frac{R. ( 12 - A )}{12} = \text{Desired Rays.}$

However, the author of *Saravali* stated that a planet in debilitation has zero rays—"in debilitation it shall be devoid of rays." He also gave a verse for calculating rays at a desired position:

> "Subtract the debilitation point; if it exceeds six signs, subtract it from the Circle (12).
> Multiply by its own rays; from that, its rays are produced."

According to this view, the ray is full at exaltation, diminishes on both sides, and reaches zero at debilitation. If there is a lack of rays at debilitation and maximum rays at exaltation, then in the six-sign interval between the planet and its debilitation, the calculation of rays is achieved by proportion. If the distance from the debilitation point exceeds six (i.e., past the exaltation), it must be subtracted from the Circle, because the decrease in rays is equal on both sides of the exaltation point.

### Translation of the Hindi Summary

The lifespan rays (Rashmi-Ayur) for the Sun and other planets in their exaltation signs are ten and so on. Sun 10, Moon 9, Mars 5, Mercury 5, Jupiter 7, Venus 8, and Saturn 5 are the lifespan rays.

Subtract the exaltation point from the desired planet. If the result is less than 6 signs, subtract from the Circle (12), convert to minutes, multiply by the ray-value, and divide by the zodiac minutes (21,600) to get the years. The teachers call this the Ray-Lifespan of the Sun etc. For specifics, see the Sanskrit commentary.

> If in an enemy's division, the eighth part is lost; if in an enemy's sign, a twelfth part is lost. || 24 ||

# Chapter on the Determination of Longevity || 5 ||

> When the planets are combust <note>original: "astangateṣu," meaning disappearing in the sun's glare</note>, one should reduce the calculated life-span by half, except for Saturn and Venus <note>original: "dānavapūjitaṃ," the preceptor of the demons</note>. The longevity granted by the planets through the sum of their rays is said by the ancient sages to be taught in the Mahendra Shastra. || 25 ||

If a planet is situated in its own sign, in its sign of exaltation, in the house of a great friend, or is in retrograde motion, the rays obtained through calculation are doubled. At the end of a retrograde period, the rays are reduced by one-eighth part. If the planet is in the sign of an enemy, a reduction of one-twelfth part should be made. Excepting Saturn and Venus <note>original: "śukraṃ"</note>, if other planets are combust, their value is reduced by half. Even if Saturn and Venus are combust, there is no loss. As it is said:

> The rays are doubled in a friend's twelfth-division and tripled in one's own. Similarly, they are doubled when retrograde, in exaltation, or in one's own sign. In an enemy's twelfth-division or in debilitation, they are reduced by a sixteenth part. A planet that is combust is considered rayless, except for Saturn and Venus. — Thus says the *Saravali*.

By this method, the rays obtained for the planets and their sum constitute the "Ray-born Longevity" <note>longevity equal to the total number of rays</note>. The noble teachers say this was declared by the teacher named Mahendra. The results of the various sums of rays can be seen in Chapter 36 of the *Saravali*. They are not recorded here for fear of making the text too long. || 24-25 ||

-> If a planet is in its own sign, exaltation, a very friendly house, or retrograde, double the calculated rays. At the end of retrogradation, subtract an eighth. In an enemy's place, subtract a 12th part. Except for Saturn and Venus, if a planet is combust, discard half. The longevity of the planets is equal to the sum of all rays; this is the teaching of the Mahendra Shastra as stated by great scholars. || 24-25 || <-

## Now, the Cycle Longevity (Chakrayu).

> The group of years of life-span is derived from the remaining portions of the asterism-degrees <note>original: "tārakāṃśa," the degrees of the nakshatra</note> yet to be traversed by the seven planets starting with the Sun. The learned call this "Cycle Longevity" (Chakrayu), derived from the direct or indirect movements of the Sun and others. || 26 ||

Now Cycle Longevity is described. A detailed explanation of Cycle Longevity is to be seen in Chapter 17. Here, only a general direction is given. The group of years is calculated from the remaining portions of the degrees of the stars yet to be traversed by the seven planets starting with the Sun. The meaning is this: for each of the seven planets from the Sun onwards, one should calculate the remaining years of life proportionally from the degrees of the nakshatra <note>lunar mansion</note> remaining to be traversed, and their sum becomes the Cycle Longevity. The proportion is: if the full measure of a nakshatra gives 60 years of life, then what do the remaining ghatis <note>a unit of time, 24 minutes</note> give? Thus the longevity for all is found separately. In Chapter 17, the specific years are read as: "21, 7, 9, 10, 16, and 4 are the years for the Sun and others respectively." The sages call this Cycle Longevity of the Sun and other planets, produced from the direct and indirect movements. || 26 ||

-> The group of years remaining from the traversed portions of the stars for the seven planets starting with the Sun is the longevity; or, that which is obtained from the direct/indirect movement of the Sun etc. is called Cycle Longevity by the learned. || 26 || <-

## Now, the Period Longevity (Dashayu).

> The years and other units produced from the remaining ghatis of the junction-stars <note>original: "yogatārā"</note> traversed by the nine planets starting with the Sun, as well as the longevity produced from the Ashtakavarga <note>a system of points based on planetary positions</note>—all this is declared by those who know the science of longevity. || 27 ||

By this, Period Longevity (Dashayu) is described. The details of Dashayu are to be seen in Chapter 18. A little is said here. It is the years etc. produced from the remaining ghatis of the junction-stars of the nine planets starting with the Sun. This means: whatever years are produced by proportion from the remaining ghatis of the nakshatras in which the nine planets are situated, that is their Period Longevity. Furthermore, the experts in the subject of longevity declare that the longevity produced from the Ashtakavarga is also included in this. In Ashtakavarga longevity, the traversed and remaining...

The intent is that the calculation must be performed. Now, Parashara and others refer to the "Dasha longevity" by another name: "Nakshatra longevity" <note>Longevity based on the lunar mansions</note>. In this system, the nine planets starting with the Sun are the lords of the first cycle of nine constellations beginning with Krittika; the second cycle of nine starting with Uttara Phalguni; and the third cycle of nine starting with Uttara Ashadha. If the birth occurs in Krittika, it is the Sun's Dasha; if in Rohini, the Moon's, and so on in order. These sequential planets and their year-durations as stated by Parashara are:

The Sun, Moon, Mars, Rahu, Jupiter, Saturn, Mercury, Ketu, and Venus are the lords in order starting from Krittika. Their years are, in order:
Six, ten, seven, eighteen, sixteen, nineteen, seventeen, seven, and twenty. These are for the planets in exaltation.

Sun = 6; Moon = 10; Mars = 7; Rahu = 18; Jupiter = 16; Saturn = 19; Mercury = 17; Ketu = 7; Venus = 20. These are the values when exalted. Similarly, 3, 5, 3, 9, 8, 9, 8, 3, 10 are the years of longevity for the constellations when in debilitation. // 27 //

The remaining portion of the constellation (measured in ghatis, etc.) at birth determines the Dasha longevity. However, wise men say that the longevity derived from the *Ashtakavarga* <note>A system of points based on planetary positions</note> constitutes the "full" or complete longevity. // 27 //

### Now, the Selection of Longevity Methods

->When the Lord of the Ascendant is endowed with strength and aspected by benefics, one should use the *Amshayu* <note>Longevity based on divisional charts</note> method.<-
->When the Sun is strong, use the *Pindodbhava* <note>Also known as Pindayu; based on planetary exaltation degrees</note> method; when the Moon is strong, use the *Naisargika* <note>Natural longevity</note> method. // 28 //<-
->When the Sun is in exaltation and others are strong in angles (Kendras) or trines (Konas); or when all are in their signs of exaltation; or when the Moon is exceptionally strong in the *Shasha* or *Hamsa* yogas <note>Specific auspicious planetary combinations</note>; // 29 //<-
->In such cases of long-life yogas and other mathematical combinations; or in lunar yogas where the Moon is in the fourth house and endowed with strength; // 30 //<-
->In *Mahapurusha* yogas <note>Great Person combinations</note> where strength is predominant, and in all *Raja Yogas* <note>Royal combinations</note>, Parashara says to use the *Paindya* (Pindayu) method. // 31 //<-
->If Jupiter is in the Ascendant, the Sun in the 10th house, and the Moon in the 4th or 7th house with great strength; and if benefics are in angles, trines, or upachayas <note>Houses of growth: 3, 6, 10, 11</note> while malefics are in cadent houses (Apoklima), use *Paindya*. // 32 //<-
->Use *Paindya* when the Sun is strongest; *Nisarga* when the Moon is strongest; *Rashmija* <note>Longevity based on rays of light</note> for Mercury; *Bhinnashtakavarga* for Mars; *Kalachakra* for Venus; // 33 //<-
->*Dashayu* for Jupiter; *Samudaya* for Saturn; and the leading teachers say that if the Ascendant is the strongest, the *Amshayu* method should be used. // 33 //<-

Now, it is explained which of the aforementioned longevities should be accepted: "When the Lord of the Ascendant..." etc. If the Lord of the Ascendant is strong (in its own Varga, etc.) and aspected by benefic planets, *Amshayu* should be taken. If the Sun is stronger at birth, then *Pindodbhava* (Pindayu) should be taken. If the Moon is strong, one should use *Naisargika* longevity. Thus, the longevity associated with whichever planet is most powerful should be accepted. If two among the Ascendant, Sun, and Moon are of equal strength, then the average of those two longevities is taken. If all three are equally strong, one should take one-third of the sum of the three longevities. If the Ascendant, Sun, and Moon are all devoid of strength, then the longevity taught by Jeevasharma (which states the maximum life is 120 years and 5 days) should be taken. As stated by the teacher Keshavacharya:

> "Amshayu is used when the Ascendant is strongest, Paindya when the Sun is strongest, and Nisarga when the Moon is strongest. If two are equal, take half their sum; if three are equal, divide the sum of the three by three. If all three are weak, then the longevity is determined by the method of the sages." // 24 //

## Chapter 5: On Longevity (Ayurdaya)

In other planetary combinations mentioned in verses 26-32, the *Pindayu* <note>Longevity based on planetary positions</note> method should be accepted. Furthermore, if at the time of birth the Sun is the strongest (most powerful among all), *Pindayu* is used. If the Moon is strongest, *Nisargayu* <note>Natural longevity</note> is used; if Mercury is strongest, *Rashmijayu* <note>Longevity based on rays</note>; if Mars is strongest, *Ashtakavargayu* <note>Longevity based on the eight-fold points system, to be explained later</note>; if Venus is strongest, *Kalachakrayu* <note>Longevity based on the wheel of time</note>; if Jupiter is strongest, *Dashayu* <note>Longevity based on planetary periods</note>; if Saturn is strongest, *Samudayayu* <note>Collective longevity</note>. If the Ascendant (Lagna) is strongest, *Amshayu* <note>Longevity based on divisional longitudes</note> occurs. Thus have the great ancient teachers spoken. || 29-33 ||

The author of the *Sudhashalini* commentary now determines which longevity calculation should be selected from those previously mentioned. If, at the time of birth, among the Lord of the Ascendant, the Sun, and the Moon, the Lord of the Ascendant is the strongest and is aspected by a benefic planet, then *Amshayu* should be taken. If the Sun is strongest, take *Pindayu*; if the Moon is strongest, take *Nisargayu*. If two planets are of equal strength, take the average of their two longevity results—for example, if the Sun and the Lord of the Ascendant are equal in strength, take the average of *Amshayu* and *Pindayu*. If the Sun and Moon are equal, take the average of *Pindayu* and *Nisargayu*. If the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon are equal, take the average of *Amshayu* and *Nisargayu*. If all three are of equal strength, one should take one-third of the sum of all three longevity calculations. || 28 ||

Sage Parashara has stated that *Pindayu* should be taken when the Sun is in its sign of exaltation, other planets are endowed with strength and located in the Centers (houses 1, 4, 7, 10) or Trines (5, 9), or if all planets are in excellent houses, or if they are strong and form *Shasha Yoga* or *Hansa Yoga* <note>Specific auspicious planetary combinations</note>. It should also be used in various types of long-life combinations, Lunar combinations (*Sunapha, Anapha, Durudhara*), and even in the fourth Lunar combination (*Kemadruma*) if the Moon is strong, as well as in *Mahapurusha* yogas and various *Raja Yogas* <note>Royal combinations indicating high status</note>. || 29-31 ||

If Jupiter is in the Ascendant, the Sun is in the 10th house, the Moon is strong in the 4th or 7th, benefic planets are in the Centers (1, 4, 7, 10), Trines (5, 9), or *Upachaya* houses (3, 6, 10, 11), and malefic planets are in *Apoklima* houses (3, 6, 9, 12), then *Pindayu* should be selected. || 32 ||

Consider another variation: if at birth the Sun is strong, use *Pindayu*; if the Moon is strong, *Nisargayu*; if Mercury is strong, *Rashmijayu*; if Mars is strong, *Ashtakavargayu*; if Venus is strong, *Amshayu*. Here, the longevity of the strongest among the eight <note>The seven planets plus the Ascendant</note> should be accepted. In case of equal strength, the longevity should be determined by dividing the sum by the number of equal factors. So say the teachers. || 33 ||

### On the Rectification of Longevity

> Multiply all the years and other units of longevity by *Nishvala*.
> Divide by *Matanga*; the result obtained is called longevity according to Solar measure. || 34 ||

Now, the method for converting the previously calculated spatial longevity into Solar measure (years, etc.) is described. The longevity calculated previously is "spatial" because it is derived from the zodiacal positions (signs, etc.). However, what is required is "Solar time," as years, half-years, seasons, and eras are defined here by Solar movement. Therefore, multiply the entire longevity (years, etc.) by *Nishvala*. Here, according to the *Katapayadi* <note>A system of Sanskrit numerical notation where letters represent numbers</note> code <unclear>vargabhairaiha</unclear>, *Nishvala* = 360. After multiplying by that, divide by *Matanga* = 365. The result obtained is said by the learned to be the longevity in Solar measure. In this context, in one Solar cycle (12 signs), there are 360 degrees. Similarly, in one Solar year, there are approximately 365 days. That is to say, 360 degrees are traversed by the Sun in 365 days. Therefore, it is logical that the longevity years multiplied by 360 and divided by 365 become Solar years. However, this is a rough calculation, as it ignores approximately 15 hours, 30 minutes, and 22 seconds each year. || 34 ||

Multiply the years and other units of longevity by 360 and divide by 365; the quotient obtained is the longevity in Solar measure. || 34 ||

Those who are devoted to the path of righteousness (Dharma), who are devotees of the twice-born <note>Brahmins</note> and the gods, who are disciplined in their diet, and who have conquered their senses...

# With the Commentary on Jataka Parijata

For those humans who possess honor, eloquence, and the boundaries of good conduct and character, this noble lifespan has been declared by the wise. || 35 ||
Those who are sinful, greedy, thieves, and revilers of the Gods and Brahmins, and those who eat all things <note>referring to forbidden foods like meat and intoxicants</note>, such men meet an untimely death. || 36 ||
For those with wavering faith in Dharma <note>righteousness/duty</note>, the ill-behaved, the hateful, those who steal the property of Brahmins and Gods, those who are terrifying to all, the foolish, and the backbiters; for those devoid of their own religious conduct, those who live by sinful deeds, those who do not follow the scriptures, and the ignorant—for them, there is accidental or premature death. For others, there shall be the highest lifespan; so say the knowers of the scriptures. || 37-39 ||

Now, it is explained in five verses who is eligible for the lifespan illustrated and who is not. The meaning of the verses is straightforward. The calculated lifespan is possible for those who are righteous and of good conduct. For the sinful and those engaged in evil deeds, the lifespan—even if calculated by mathematics—does not manifest. Sinners die in "untimely death" <note>original: *akale*</note> despite their allotted lifespan. Now, it is often heard that "no one dies before their time"; then how do sinners die untimely? It is said: the lifespan calculated here is a definition based on the ideal. Specifically, the time within the inhalation and exhalation of a man with healthy senses is called a *Prana* <term>Prana: a unit of time based on one breath</term> <unclear>here</unclear>. Six of these *Pranas* make one *Pala*. Sixty *Palas* make one *Ghatika*. Sixty *Ghatikas* make one day. Thirty days make one month. Twelve months make one year. Thus, those who have conquered their senses live the years of life as they were calculated. This is because for the self-controlled and the righteous, the inhalations and exhalations exit in a regulated manner. For the sinful and those engaged in bad deeds, due to the ill-health of the body, the inhalations and exhalations (*Pranas*) exit in an irregular manner (in a quantity greater than the standard). Accordingly, their time also transforms. For this very reason, even a hundred-year lifespan is exhausted by some in 30 years and by others in 40 years, according to their own breaths. Therefore, it is said as it is heard:

> "By celibacy and penance, the Gods warded off death." <note>original: *Brahmacharyena tapasa deva mrityumapaghnata*</note>

Thus, one who desires long life must also make an effort. It was also said by Keshava:

> "This [lifespan] belongs to those who eat wholesome food and possess desirable qualities and character; it does not belong to the sinful." || 35-39 ||

Those who are engaged in religious deeds, are devotees of the twice-born <note>Brahmins</note> and Gods, eat wholesome food, and have conquered their senses; those who possess honor, eloquence, patience, and are devoted to the boundaries of a good family—theirs is this declared lifespan, so say the scholars of noble intellect. || 35 ||

Those who are sinful, greedy, thieves, revilers of Gods and Brahmins, and eaters of all things like wine and meat—those men meet an untimely death. || 36 ||

Those whose intellect is wavering regarding Dharma, who are ill-behaved and malicious, who steal the wealth of Brahmins and Gods, who give fear to all, backbiters, those devoid of their own religious conduct, those who earn a living through sinful acts, and fools who do not believe in the scriptures—they meet with accidental death. || 37-39 ||

---

### Now, the Lifespans of Various Species.

For vultures, owls, parrots, crows, and snakes, the lifespan is a thousand years.
For hawks, monkeys, bears, and frogs, it is declared to be three hundred years. || 40 ||
For demons <note>Rakshasas</note>, it is proclaimed to be one hundred and fifty.
For humans and elephants, the wise know it to be one hundred and twenty. || 41 ||
For horses, the number is thirty-two; for donkeys and camels, it is twenty-five.

# Chapter on the Determination of Longevity || 5 ||

For bulls and buffaloes, the lifespan is twenty-four years. || 42 ||
The lifespan of peacocks is twenty years, and for goats and similar animals, it is sixteen.
For the swan, it is fourteen <note>original: "panca-navakam" (five plus nine)</note>, and for the cuckoo and parrot, it is twelve years. || 43 ||
The same applies to pigeons; for the rooster, it is eight years.
For bulbuls <note>original: "budbuda," likely referring to small water-birds or bulbuls</note> and other egg-born creatures, the lifespan is said to be seven years. || 44 ||

These verses are easy to understand. Having determined the birth time of non-human births <term>Viyoni-janma: births other than human, such as animals or birds</term>, one should calculate their longevity in the same way as human longevity, using the proportion of the maximum lifespan of that particular species. For example, if the maximum human lifespan is taken as 120 years and 5 days, then by that proportion, one calculates what the lifespan would be based on the maximum lifespan of that specific animal species. || 40-44 ||

Vultures, owls, parrots, crows, and serpents have a lifespan of a thousand years. Quails, monkeys, bears, and frogs have a lifespan of three hundred years. Demons <note>Rakshasas</note> have a lifespan of 150 years. Humans and elephants have a lifespan of 120 years. The horse's lifespan is 32 years. The lifespan of a donkey or camel is 25 years. The lifespan of a bull or buffalo is 24 years. The peacock's lifespan is 20 years. For goats, rams, etc., the lifespan is 16 years. The swan's lifespan is 14 years. The cuckoo and parrot have a lifespan of 12 years. The pigeon also has a lifespan of 12 years. The rooster's lifespan is 8 years. For bulbuls, the lifespan is said to be 7 years. || 40-44 ||

### Periods of Misfortune (Arishta Dasha)

If a weak malefic planet sits in even one of the three divisions <term>Trimandala: the 1st, 5th, and 9th houses of a horoscope</term> and is not joined by a benefic planet, one should predict death at the end of that planet's period. || 45 ||
The period of planets situated in the junction of two signs <note>Rashi-sandhi</note> brings disease. Death occurs for men during the period of a planet that has reached the thirtieth degree of a sign. || 46 ||
If a malefic planet is in the sixth or eighth house, is aspected by an enemy, and is placed in the house of a malefic, men are said to die during its sub-period, or during the period of a planet defeated in planetary war. || 47 ||
The fifth period of Mars brings death; the sixth period of Jupiter brings death. The fourth period of Saturn brings death, and the fifth period of Rahu <note>the North Node of the Moon</note> brings death. || 48 ||
Periods of planets that are in debilitation, in an enemy's sign, or rendered powerless—specifically the 3rd, 5th, or 7th periods <note>Vipratyari-naidhana</note>—bring death, especially if joined by malefics. || 49 ||
During the sub-periods of the lords of the 2nd and 7th houses <note>the "killer" houses</note> or the lords of specific houses of interest, the destruction of that house's significance occurs through the planets associated with or aspecting them. || 50 ||
Death may occur when Saturn reaches the sign containing the lord of the eighth house's subdivision <note>Trishansha</note>, or when it reaches the ninth-division <note>Navamsha</note> sign of that lord. || 51 ||

Now, the periods of misfortune based on planetary placement are described—"In the three divisions," etc. In the three divisions = the Ascendant, the fifth, and the ninth houses; if a weak malefic planet stays in even one of these (the 1st, 5th, or 9th) and that malefic is not joined by any benefic = auspicious planet, then at the end of that malefic planet's period <term>Dasha</term>, one should predict the death of the subject. Regarding these three divisions, the *Jataka Desha* states that the presence of four or more planets indicates long, medium, or short life respectively:

> "By four or more planets residing together in the Ascendant, fifth, or ninth houses, those born have long, medium, or short lives."

During the periods of planets located in the junction of signs, the subject becomes ill. Furthermore, death occurs for men during the period of a planet that has traversed to the thirtieth degree of a sign. Placed in a malefic house = if some malefic planet has gone into the sign of a malefic planet and is situated in the sixth or eighth from the Ascendant, and is "aspected by an enemy" = seen by its own enemy...

# Page 140
## With the Commentary on Jataka Parijata

If a malefic planet <note>original: "papa-graha"</note> is aspected by another, then during the major period <note>term: Mahadasha (the primary planetary cycle in a person's life)</note> of a planet defeated in planetary war <note>term: Graha Yuddha (when two planets are in close proximity, the one with lower longitude is considered "defeated")</note>, and during the sub-period <note>term: Antardasha (a secondary cycle within the Mahadasha)</note> of that malefic planet, the wise say that death occurs for men. This is what is meant: in the major period of every planet, there are sub-periods of all planets. At that time, a malefic planet characterized by the aforementioned traits causes the death of a person during its own sub-period within the major period of a planet defeated in war.

If the fifth major period from the birth period belongs to Mars <note>original: "Ara/Bhauma"</note>, it brings death during that Mars period. Similarly, the 6th period of Jupiter, the 4th of Saturn, and the 5th of Rahu <note>note: Rahu is the North Node of the Moon</note> become givers of death. Likewise, for a planet that is in its sign of depression <note>term: Neecha (the zodiac sign where a planet is weakest)</note>, its 3rd period (Vipat) is dangerous; for a planet in an enemy's house, its 5th period (Pratyari) is dangerous; and for a planet that is "confounded" or combust <note>term: Astangata (hidden by the Sun's light)</note>, its 8th period (Naidhana) becomes the cause of death. This means one dies in that period. If those same periods are associated with malefic planets, then they cause death with particular certainty.

Whichever house <note>term: Bhava (an astrological house representing specific life areas)</note> is being considered, the lord of the 2nd house and the 7th house <note>note: these are known as Marakas or "death-inflicting" houses</note> from that specific house will cause the destruction of that house's significations during their major and sub-periods. For example, if considering the 3rd house, the destruction of the 3rd house should be predicted during the periods of the lords of the 4th and 9th houses <note>note: because the 4th is the 2nd from the 3rd, and the 9th is the 7th from the 3rd</note>. This logic should be applied everywhere. Here, death should not only be predicted in the periods of the 2nd and 7th lords, but also if the significator planets <note>term: Karakas (planets that naturally represent a specific topic)</note> of those houses are joined with or aspected by those 2nd and 7th lords. The significator planets have been mentioned previously (in Chapter 2, Verse 51).

The lord of the one-third division <note>term: Drekkana (a 10-degree decan of a zodiac sign)</note> of the 8th house from the birth ascendant is also significant. This is what is said: the specific decan that is rising at the time of birth must also be considered for the 8th house. If the first decan is at the ascendant, the first decan of the 8th house should be taken; if the second, the second; if the third, the third. This is because of the upcoming statement: "The 22nd decan from the rising sign is the cause of death." When Saturn reaches (by transit <note>term: Gochara (the current movement of planets across the sky)</note>) the sign where the lord of that decan is situated, or when Saturn reaches the sign of the sub-chart <note>term: Navamsha (the 1/9th divisional chart used for fine detail)</note> where that decan lord is placed, the death of the native occurs. In this matter, one should choose between the sign and the sub-sign based on which is stronger. || 45-51 ||

---

If even in one of the three divisions <note>original: "mandala"</note> there is a weak malefic planet not joined by a benefic, predict death at the end of its period. || 45 ||

The periods of planets situated in the junctions <note>original: "sandhi"</note> between signs cause disease. In the periods of planets that have exceeded 30 degrees <note>note: meaning they are transitioning out of a sign</note>, the death of men occurs. || 46 ||

Malefic planets situated in the 6th or 8th houses, aspected by enemies and placed in malefic signs, cause the death of men during their sub-periods within the period of a planet defeated in war. || 47 ||

If the 5th period from birth is Mars, the 6th is Jupiter, the 4th is Saturn, and the 5th is Rahu, these periods are death-inflicting. The 3rd period of a planet in depression, the 5th of a planet in an enemy's house, and the 8th of a planet combust by the Sun cause death. If those periods are related to malefic planets, death is certain.

Loss of a house's significations should be predicted during the major and sub-periods of the lords of the 2nd and 7th houses from the house under consideration, especially if the significator of that house is joined with or aspected by those lords.

Death should be predicted when Saturn transits the sign occupied by the lord of the decan of the 8th house at birth, or when Saturn transits the sign of the Navamsha occupied by that decan lord. || 48-51 ||

# Chapter 5: On the Determination of Longevity

### Regarding the <term>Chidra Grahas</term> <note>Vulnerable or "piercing" planets that indicate the timing of death.</note>

->The lord of the eighth house, the planet situated in the eighth, the planet aspecting the eighth, and the Lord of the <term>Khara</term> <note>The 22nd decanate from the rising sign.</note>;<-
->The planet joined with the lord of the eighth, and the lord of the sixty-fourth Navamsha <note>A 1/9th division of a sign; the 64th is a sensitive point in predictive astrology.</note>;<-
->And the bitter enemy of the lord of the eighth—these are known as the seven <term>Chidra Grahas</term>.<-
->Among these, the one who is most powerful will cause death during its planetary period.<-
->Death of any specific house's significance occurs during the period of a powerful planet<-
->situated in the twelfth from that house, or the lord of that twelfth house, without a doubt.<-

Now, the <term>Maraka Grahas</term> <note>Death-inflicting planets.</note> are described. (1) The lord of the eighth house from the ascendant; (2) a planet situated in the eighth house; (3) the planet which has the greatest aspectual strength upon the eighth house; (4) the Lord of the <term>Khara</term>, which is the lord of the 22nd <term>Drekkana</term> <note>A 10-degree division of a zodiac sign; there are 36 in total.</note> counted from the Decanate of the birth ascendant; (5) a planet joined with the lord of the eighth house, or the lord of the sign where the eighth lord is placed; (6) the lord of the sixty-fourth (64th) <term>Navamsha</term>—this is calculated from the Navamsha occupied by the Moon at birth, or specifically the lord of the 8th house's Navamsha from the Moon's Navamsha; (7) the planet which is the bitter enemy of the lord of the eighth house. These are called the seven <term>Chidra Grahas</term>. Among these seven, whichever planet is the strongest, one should predict the death of the person during its <term>Daya</term> <note>Planetary period or Dasha.</note>.

This logic should be applied to the consideration of every house <note>e.g., to find the "death" of father's matters, look at the 8th from the 9th house.</note>. An alternative view is taught: or, from whichever house is being considered, death of that house's matters occurs during the period of the planet situated in the 12th from it, or the lord of that 12th house, whichever is stronger. There is no doubt in this. Regarding this, there is a variant reading in the text *Phaladeepika*:

> "One may meet death in the period of a planet that is weak, 
> whether it is situated in the twelfth from a house or is the lord of that twelfth."

The lord of the 8th (1), situated in the 8th (2), aspecting the 8th (3), the Lord of the Khara (4), joined with the 8th lord (5), the lord of the 64th Navamsha (6), and the bitter enemy of the 8th lord (7)—these are the seven <term>Chidra Grahas</term>. Predict death in the period of the strongest among these. Death occurs in the period of the planet that is stronger between the one in the 12th from a house or the lord of that 12th.

### Regarding the Nature of the <term>Drekkanas</term> <note>Decanates.</note>

->The Decanates in Cancer, Pisces, and Scorpio—the middle, the end, and the first respectively—are Serpents.<-
->The second of Scorpio is a Noose; the first of Capricorn and Leo are respectively a Fetter and a Bird.<-
->The twenty-second Decanate from the birth ascendant is the <term>Khara</term>.<-
->The sixty-fourth Navamsha is calculated from the position of the Moon.<-

Now the natures of the <term>Drekkanas</term> are described. The middle (2nd) Decanate of Cancer, the final (3rd) of Pisces, and the first of Scorpio are called "Serpent" Decanates. The second of Scorpio is named "Noose" (*Pasha*). The first of Capricorn is named "Fetter" (*Nigada*). The first of Leo is the "Bird" (*Vihanga*) Decanate. Further details should be sought in the chapter on Decanates in the <term>Brihat Jataka</term> <note>original: "Grihajataka" - a famous foundational text by Varahamihira.</note>. The purpose of this was mentioned previously in verses such as "A bird, serpent, or boar in the Decanate..." and "In the divisions of the ascendant..." etc. Furthermore, in the <term>Shatpanchashika</term> <note>A classic text on Horary astrology.</note>—

> "From the <term>Amsha</term><note>The Navamsha or 1/9th division of a sign</note> wealth is known; from the <term>Drekkana</term><note>A decan or 1/3rd division of a sign</note> thieves are considered.
> From the zodiac signs, time, direction, and place are known; and from the Lord of the Ascendant, age and caste are determined."

Now, the **Khara** <note>literally "harsh" or "sharp"</note> is defined. The 22nd decan counted from the decan occupied by the Ascendant (<term>Lagna</term>) at the time of birth is called the **Khara** decan. If the birth is in the first decan of the Ascendant, then the first decan of the 8th house from the Ascendant is the Khara. Similarly, if the birth is in the second decan of the Ascendant, the second decan of the 8th house is the Khara. That Khara is also the 64th <term>Navamsha</term> <note>1/9th division</note> from the Navamsha in which the Moon (<term>Sudhakara</term>) is placed at birth. Whichever Navamsha of a house the Moon occupies, the Navamsha of the same numerical order in the 8th house is the Khara. Since there are 9 Navamshas and 3 decans per sign, 7 signs × 9 = 63 Navamshas, and 7 signs × 3 = 21 decans. Adding the current one makes the calculation consistent. The purpose of the Khara is stated: "The Lord of the Khara is a <term>Maraka</term> <note>death-inflicting</note> planet." Likewise, in the *Brihat Jataka*:

> The 22nd decan is declared by the sages to be the cause of death.
> Its lord, or the lords of the 8th and 11th houses, grant departure from this world according to their own qualities. || 55-56 ||

Now the forms of the decans are described: The 2nd decan of Cancer, the 3rd of Pisces, and the 1st of Scorpio are called **Serpent** (<term>Bhujanga</term>). The 2nd of Scorpio is the **Noose** (<term>Pasha</term>), the 1st of Capricorn is the **Fetter** (<term>Nigada</term>), and the 1st of Leo is the **Bird** (<term>Vihanga</term>).
The 22nd decan from the birth decan—which is the corresponding decan in the 8th house—is called 'Khara'. That 'Khara' is also the 64th Navamsha from the Moon's position. (Commentary) || 55-56 ||

### On the Designations of Life, Body, and Death.

> The Ascendant multiplied by five and added to <term>Mandi</term><note>A sensitive mathematical point/sub-planet</note> is the **Breath** (<term>Prana</term>) of living beings.
> The Moon's position multiplied by eight, added to the position of Mandi, is the **Body** (<term>Deha</term>).
> The position of <term>Gulika</term><note>Similar to Mandi, often used interchangeably</note> multiplied by seven and added to the Sun is **Death** (<term>Mrityu</term>).
> If the sum of Life and Body is significantly greater than Death, the person born lives long. || 57 ||

The current Ascendant should be multiplied by five, then added to Mandi (Gulika); this becomes the **Prana-sphuta** or **Jiva** (Life) of the being. Then, the longitude of the Moon should be multiplied by eight and added to the longitude of Gulika; this is called **Deha** (Body). Then, the longitude of Gulika should be multiplied by seven and added to the Sun (<term>Divanatha</term>); this is called **Mrityu** (Death). If the sum of Life and Body is greater than the Death value (**Death < Life + Body**), the person born lives a long life. Conversely, if the sum of Life and Body is less than the Death value (**Death > Life + Body**), one should predict a short life. (Commentary) || 57 ||

### On the Time of Departure.

> When Saturn transits the sign resulting from the sum of Life, Death, and Body, there is a loss of wealth.
> Or when Saturn enters the trines to that sign, or the sign indicated by its Navamsha, one should predict death for men. || 58 ||

# Chapter on Longevity || 5 ||

**When Saturn enters the trine of a house, the wise should predict the destruction of that house.**
**When Jupiter reaches the trine of the lord of a house, death [of that house's significations] occurs. || 56 ||**

When Saturn—by transit—passes through the sum of the previously calculated <term>Jiva</term> <note>Life-force point</note>, <term>Mrityu</term> <note>Death point</note>, and <term>Deha</term> <note>Body point</note> signs, one should predict the loss of wealth. Furthermore, when Saturn enters the trine houses (the 5th or 9th) from that sum, or when Saturn enters the sign corresponding to the <term>Navamsha</term> <note>The 1/9th divisional chart position</note> of that sum, one should predict the death of the person. || 58 ||

When Saturn enters the trine (5th or 9th) from any house, the wise say that house is destroyed. For example, in the consideration of the house of wealth, if Saturn enters the 6th or 10th house <note>which are trines to the 2nd house of wealth in certain systems, or specifically affecting the 2nd</note>, one should declare the loss of wealth; this applies everywhere. Likewise, when Jupiter reaches the trine (5th or 9th) from where the lord of a house is situated, the "death" of that house occurs. If Jupiter enters the trine from the Lord of the Ascendant, the person dies; if from the Lord of Wealth, loss of wealth and family occurs; if from the Lord of Siblings, the death of a sibling—thus, the consideration for each house should be performed individually. || 59 ||

<note>The following section repeats the above rules in Hindi vernacular for the reader's ease.</note>
When Saturn reaches the sign resulting from the sum of the aforementioned <term>Jiva</term>, <term>Mrityu</term>, and <term>Deha</term> by transit, loss of wealth should be predicted. Or, when Saturn goes to the 5th or 9th house from that sum, or to the sign of its Navamsha, it causes the death of men. || 58 ||

If Saturn is in the trine from a house, scholars say the house is destroyed; or death occurs when Jupiter reaches the trine of the house lord. || 59 ||

**The Lord of the sum of the Ascendant, the Sun, and Mandi—whichever house he occupies,**
**When Jupiter (the one worshiped by Indra) or its trine is reached by transit, the person meets death. || 60 ||**

**Subtract the position of Yamakantaka from the longitude of the Lord of the Ascendant;**
**When Jupiter enters the sign corresponding to the Navamsha of that remainder, death occurs without a doubt. || 61 ||**

**Subtract Saturn from the longitude of Mandi; when Saturn transits that sign, its Navamsha, or its trine, death occurs.**
**When Saturn enters the Decanate (Drekkana) of the sum of the five "smoky" planets, death also occurs. || 62 ||**

At the time of birth, take the precise longitudes of the Ascendant, the Sun, and <term>Mandi</term> <note>A sensitive mathematical point/sub-planet</note>. Find the Lord of the sign resulting from their sum. When Jupiter (the teacher of the gods) transits the sign occupied by that Lord, or transits the trine from that Lord, the person dies. || 60 ||

From the longitude of the <term>Lord of the Ascendant</term>, subtract the longitude of <term>Yamakantaka</term> <note>A mathematical point associated with Jupiter</note>. Note the sign of the remainder and its Navamsha. When Jupiter transits that position, the person's death occurs; of this, there is no doubt.

Here, the method for knowing Yamakantaka is mentioned in passing:

> **Divide the day into eight parts and count from the Lord of the Day.**
> **The eighth part is lordless; the portion of Saturn is known as Gulika.**
> **The night is also divided into eight parts, counting from the fifth day-lord.**
> **The eighth segment is called the "completion."**
> **The portion of Saturn is called Gulika; the portion of Jupiter is Yamakantaka.**
> **The portion of Mars is called Mrityu; the portion of the Sun is called Kala.**
> **The portion of Mercury is Ardha-prahara, the shower of clear actions.**

Just as one calculates the <term>Gulika-ishta</term> <note>The specific time for Gulika</note> and then calculates the <term>Gulika</term> position like an Ascendant, one should daily calculate the <term>Yamakantaka-ishta</term> and then calculate the Yamakantaka position like an Ascendant. || 61 ||

Subtract the Sun’s son (Saturn) from the Mandi-longitude (the calculated position of Gulika). <note>Mandi and Gulika are "shadow planets" or sensitive points used in Vedic astrology to determine malefic influences.</note> In whatever sign the remaining degrees fall, when Saturn arrives in a trine (the 5th or 9th house) from that sign based on the day of the week, death may occur. Furthermore, when Saturn enters the sign corresponding to the decan <term>Drekkana: a 10-degree division of a zodiac sign</term> of the sum of the five "non-luminous" sub-planets (Dhuma, etc.), death may occur. Regarding this, the method for calculating Dhuma and the others is as follows:

Add four signs and thirteen degrees to the Sun's position; this is called **Dhuma**, a great defect that destroys all undertakings. Subtract Dhuma from twelve signs (the full circle) to get **Vyatipata**, which is also harmful. Add six signs to Vyatipata to get **Parivesha**, a bringer of misfortune. Subtract Parivesha from twelve signs to get **Indrachapa** (the Rainbow), also harmful. Add seventeen degrees and some minutes to Indrachapa to get **Ketu** (the Comet-point), which is like poison. Adding one sign to Ketu returns you to the Sun's position as before. These are known as the non-luminous planets, considered malefic defects.

When Jupiter enters the sign (or its 5th/9th trines) owned by the lord of the sum of the longitudes of the Ascendant, the Sun, and Gulika, a person meets their death. || 60 ||

Subtract the position of Yamakantaka from the longitude of the Ascendant's lord. When Jupiter transits through the sign indicated by the resulting Navamsha <term>Navamsha: a 1/9th division of a sign, crucial for fine-tuning predictions</term>, death occurs without a doubt. See the Sanskrit commentary for the method of calculating Yamakantaka. || 61 ||

Subtract Saturn from the longitude of Gulika. When Saturn transits the 5th or 9th sign from the sign indicated by that remainder's Navamsha, death occurs. One should also predict death when Saturn enters the sign indicated by the decan of the sum of the five sub-planets starting with Dhuma. || 62 ||

> When Jupiter reaches the Navamsha indicated by the Mandi-longitude, and Saturn reaches the Dwadashamsha <term>Dwadashamsha: a 1/12th division of a sign</term> of that same point, and the Sun is in the trine of that decan, death occurs. It may also happen at the rising of the Sun in the degrees resulting from the sum of the Ascendant, Moon, and Mandi. || 63 ||

"When Jupiter reaches the Navamsha indicated by the Mandi-longitude" means when Jupiter enters the sign that was the Navamsha of the calculated Gulika. "Saturn reaches the Dwadashamsha" means when Saturn arrives at the 1/12th division of that same Gulika. Now the month of death is described: when the Sun enters the trine (5th or 9th) of the decan occupied by Mandi, death occurs. Regarding the specific degree: death should be predicted at the rising of the Sun when it reaches the degrees equal to the sum of the Ascendant, the Moon, and Mandi. || 63 ||

When Jupiter is in the Navamsha of Gulika, Saturn is in its Dwadashamsha, the Sun is in the trine of the decan, and the Sun reaches the degrees of the combined Ascendant-Moon-Gulika, death occurs. || 63 ||

> The wise say the Navamsha of the sum of the Ascendant and Mandi indicates the month of death. The "Death-Moon" is found from the sum of Gulika and the Moon, and the "Death-Ascendant" from the sum of the Ascendant, Saturn, and the Moon. || 64 ||

Here, the month, the Moon's position, and the Ascendant at the time of death are explained. This is the simple meaning. || 64 ||

# Chapter 5: On the Determination of Lifespan
## Page 145

If the Navamsha <note>A 1/9th division of a zodiac sign, used for fine-tuning astrological predictions</note> is Aries, it signifies 1 month; if Taurus, 2 months; if Leo, the 5th month, and so on. Similarly, by the combination of **Gulika** <note>A mathematical point in the sky considered the "son of Saturn," often associated with obstacles or death</note> and the Moon, death occurs when the Moon reaches the sign equivalent to that sum (the **Niryana** <note>Death-dealing</note> Moon). Likewise, the Ascendant (Lagna) of death should be known from the sum of the Ascendant, Gulika, and the Moon. (According to the author of *Sudarshana Shastra*) || 64 ||

> Multiply Gulika and Saturn by nine; 
> when Saturn reaches the sign and degree of their sum, death occurs. || 65 ||
> When Saturn transits the sign resulting from the sum of the positions 
> of the lords of the 6th, 12th, and 8th houses, 
> or their trines (the 5th or 9th signs from them), there is fear of death for men. || 66 ||

-> These two verses explain the specific calculation. || 65-66 ||<-

Multiply Gulika and Saturn by nine; when Saturn arrives in the sign and degree resulting from their sum, death occurs. || 65 ||

By adding the exact longitudinal positions of the lords of the 6th house, 12th house, and 8th house <note>These houses are traditionally associated with debt, loss, and death respectively</note>, one obtains a specific sign. When Saturn in its transit passes through that sign, or the 5th or 9th signs from it, humans face the fear of death. || 66 ||

> Multiply Jupiter by nine, and add Saturn and the position of Gulika 
> both multiplied by nine; then again add Saturn and Gulika 
> multiplied by nine. Add this entire sum to the position of Jupiter. 
> When Jupiter transits the Navamsha sign obtained from this total, 
> that is the time of death for men. || 67 ||

*Nandahate* = Jupiter multiplied by nine; *Virinchigunitam* = Saturn multiplied by nine; *Mandisphutam* = the clear position of Gulika should be added. To that sum, again add *Ankavriddhi* = nine times *Inajam* = Saturn and *Mandatmajam* = Gulika. This resulting sum is added to the clear position of *Deveshapurohita* = Jupiter. When Jupiter, in its transit, reaches the sign and Navamsha resulting from this calculation, it is the time of death (*Niryana-kala*). The practical result of this is: multiply the current clear Jupiter by ten, add Saturn and Gulika multiplied by eighteen; when Jupiter transits the Navamsha of the resulting sign, death should be predicted. By this, the year of death is known, as Jupiter's transit determines the year. || 67 ||

Multiply the clear Jupiter by 9, and add to it Saturn and Gulika (each multiplied by 9). Then add Saturn and Gulika multiplied by 9 again, and add that entire sum to the clear Jupiter. When Jupiter transits the **Navamsha** sign of that total sum, it should be understood as the time of death. (According to the author of *Sudarshana Shastra*) || 67 ||

> Multiply the Sun's position by nine, and add Saturn and Gulika 
> multiplied by nine; then add Gulika multiplied by nine once more. 
> When the Sun reaches the sign and degree of that sum, it is the time of death. || 68 ||

Now another timing of death is described. *Bhanusphute* = the clear Sun multiplied by *Navahate* = nine; multiply *Ravijam* = Saturn and *Mandi* = Gulika by the number nine and add them to the Sun's position. To that sum, again add *Mandi* (Gulika) multiplied by nine. When *Pushani* = the Sun, through its transit, reaches the sign and Navamsha resulting from this calculation, the time of death should be declared. From the previous verses (65-67), the year of death is determined; from this verse (68), the month will be known. This is because the Sun's transit through the signs determines the months. || 68 ||

In the clear Sun multiplied by nine, add Saturn and Gulika multiplied by 9. Then add Gulika multiplied by 9 again. When the Sun transits the sign corresponding to the Navamsha of that sum, it should be known as the time of death. This identifies the month of death. Year...
