# Page 146
### From the Jataka Parijata with Commentary

->**Multiply the years of the planetary periods of the planets associated with the lord of the fifth house by the number of days in a month (or divide by twelve); the remainder indicates the month of death for men. Alternatively, this may be calculated using the planets associated with the lord of the ascendant. || 69 ||**<-

At the time of birth, take the planets associated with the lord of the fifth house <note>Sanskrit: *Sutesha*, the ruler of the 5th house of the zodiac</note>. Take the sum of the years of their planetary periods <note>Dasha years</note> and divide by the "Lord of Days" (the number twelve, representing the months of the year). The remainder indicates the month in which the person's death is predicted. Alternatively, the month of death should be known through the planets associated with the lord of the ascendant <note>Sanskrit: *Lagnesha*, the ruler of the 1st house</note>. One should total the Dasha years of the planets joined with the lord of the ascendant and divide by twelve; the remainder tells the month of death. If no planets are associated with either the lord of the ascendant or the lord of the fifth house, then the calculation should be performed using only the Dasha of the lord of the ascendant or the lord of the fifth house alone, as previously described. || 69 ||

**The teachers say that by dividing the sum of the Dasha years of the planets associated with the lord of the 5th house by 12, the remaining number indicates the month of death; or they say the same regarding planets associated with the lord of the ascendant. || 69 ||**

->**Multiply the longitude of the Moon by nine; then add the longitudes of Gulika and Saturn, each multiplied by nine. The resulting Navamsha <note>a 1/9th division of a sign</note> occupied by the Moon shall be the one that bestows death. || 70 ||**<-

This verse calculates the position of the Moon at the time of death. The explanation should be understood as similar to verses 67 and 68. The calculation is: $(9 \times \text{Moon}) + (18 \times \text{Saturn}) + (9 \times \text{Jupiter})$. <note>The Sanskrit commentary provides a slightly different formula: $(9 \times \text{Moon}) + (18 \times \text{Saturn}) + (9 \times \text{Gulika})$</note>. When the Moon enters the Navamsha resulting from this sum, death occurs. || 70 ||

**Multiply the clear longitude of the Moon by 9, multiply Saturn and Gulika by 9, add them together, and then add Gulika multiplied by 9 again; the Moon in that resulting Navamsha becomes the giver of death. || 70 ||**

->**If birth occurs during the day, the fatal Dasha should be calculated from the star (Nakshatra) resulting from the sum of the longitudes of the Sun and Saturn. If birth occurs at night, the Dasha beginning from the star resulting from the sum of the Moon and Rahu is inauspicious. || 71 ||**<-

Now the knowledge of the fatal planetary period <note>Sanskrit: *Niryana Dasha*</note> is explained. If the birth is **during the day**, then one should calculate the star <note>Nakshatra</note> obtained by adding the clear longitudes of the Sun and Saturn. The planetary period belonging to that star is known as the "Death-Inflicting Period." If the birth is **at night**, then the star obtained by adding the longitudes of the Moon and Rahu <note>the North Node</note> becomes the inauspicious period for death. The calculation of the star is based on the clear longitude of the planets. Convert the longitude into minutes, divide by 800; the quotient gives the number of passed stars, and the remainder gives the elapsed portion of the current star by proportion $(\frac{60 \times \text{Remainder}}{800} = \text{Elapsed portion of current star})$. The Dasha of the planet ruling that current star is the starting fatal period. To understand the Dashas of the planets based on the stars, the following table is provided:

| Sun | Moon | Mars | Rahu | Jup. | Sat. | Merc. | Ketu | Ven. | Planets |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 6 | 10 | 7 | 18 | 16 | 19 | 17 | 7 | 20 | Years |
| Krittika | Rohini | Mrig. | Ardra | Punar. | Pushya | Ashle. | Magha | P. Phal. | Stars (1) |
| U. Phal. | Hasta | Chitra | Swati | Vish. | Anur. | Jyesh. | Moola | P. Shad. | Stars (2) |
| U. Shad. | Shrav. | Dhan. | Shat. | P. Bhad. | U. Bhad. | Revati | Ashwini | Bharani | Stars (3) |

The clarification of these Dashas can be seen in the 18th chapter, in the section on planetary periods. || 71 ||

**If birth is in the day, the star resulting from the sum of the Sun and Saturn is the first Dasha of death; that is, the Dasha of the planet ruling that star is known as the fatal period.**

In a night birth, the constellation <note>Nakshatra</note> resulting from the conjunction of the Moon and Rahu <note>the North Node of the Moon</note> should be known as the first period <note>Dasha</note> of departure <note>death</note>. Knowledge of the constellation and the period based on the precise positions of the planets should be sought in the Sanskrit commentary. || 71 ||

### ->Now, the Cause of Departure.<-

> The twenty-second decan <note>Drekkana; a 10-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign</note> from the rising sign is the cause of death.
> The lord of that decan indicates the manner of departure according to the rules. || 72 ||

Now, the cause of departure—meaning, what will be the instrument of death for the person born—is explained: "From the rising." From the rising sign <note>Lagna</note> at birth, the twenty-second (22nd) decan—whichever decan the birth falls in, the twenty-second decan from that point falls in the eighth house <note>the house of death</note> (see verse 56)—becomes the cause of death. The lord or ruler of that twenty-second decan indicates the departure or death through the specific afflictions associated with that planet (as stated in Chapter 2, verses 75–81). As stated by Varaha <note>Varahamihira, the classical astronomer-astrologer</note>:

> "The twenty-second decan is called the cause of death by the wise.
> Its lord, or even a planet occupying it, grants departure according to its own qualities." || 72 ||

The 22nd decan from the rising sign is the cause of death. Its ruler indicates the departure through its own specific nature. || 72 ||

> Know that if a strong benefic planet resides in the seventh house from the Navamsha <note>a 3°20' subdivision</note> occupied by Mandi <note>a mathematical point or 'son of Saturn'</note> at birth, death is surely peaceful.
> If the Son of Earth <note>Mars</note> is there, death is by battle; if the Son of the Sun <note>Saturn</note>, by thieves and the like, or by demons <note>spirits/ghosts</note>, or by snakes; if the Sun, by fear of the King; if the waning Moon, by water. || 73 ||

At birth, in whichever sign's ninth-part <term>Navamsha</term> Mandi (also called Gulika) is placed, if a strong benefic planet resides in the seventh house from that position, then at the time of death, the person surely dies with ease and happiness. Likewise, if the Son of Earth (Mars) has gone to the seventh house from that Mandi-occupied Navamsha sign, the person's death will be through battle or war. If the Son of the Sun (Saturn) is there, death occurs through thieves, hunters, demons (ghosts or spirits), or by the bite of snakes and such. If the Sun is there, death occurs through fear of the King (execution or state punishment). If there is a waning Moon, one dies by drowning in water. It is also said:

> "Benefics in the seventh house from the Navamsha occupied by Mandi grant a good death;
> Malefics there cause a bad death. Among them, the Sun causes death from the King;
> The waning Moon in water; Mars in battle; Saturn from imprisonment;
> Rahu from snakebite or perhaps from the touch of poison." || 73 ||

If a strong benefic is in the 7th sign from the Navamsha where Mandi sits at birth, death will certainly be peaceful. If Mars is there, death in battle; if Saturn, death by thieves, demons, or snakes; if the Sun, by royal punishment; if the waning Moon, death by water. || 73 ||

> Death occurs from the imbalance of the element associated with the strong planet that aspects the eighth house.
> From the Sun: fire, water, weapons, fever, or diseases of phlegm and thirst.
> From the lord of the eighth house or the lord of the rising sign, or based on the aspect of Time,
> In the 'hole' <note>eighth house</note> or its Navamsha, if in a movable, fixed, or dual sign: in a foreign land, in one's own home, or on the road. || 74 ||

At birth, the eighth house <term>Randhra</term> from the rising sign is aspected by a strong planet; death should be predicted from the imbalance of the element <term>Dhatu</term> belonging to that planet. There, from the Sun, it is from the fury of fire. From the Moon, by drowning in water...

# Jataka Parijata with Commentary
<page-num>148</page-num>

...by Mars, death is caused by weapons or tools. By Mercury, from the agitation of a fever. By Jupiter, from phlegm <note>original: "kapha," one of the three humors in Ayurvedic medicine</note>. By Venus, from the pangs of hunger. By Saturn, from the pangs of thirst. Death should be predicted through these resulting diseases. If the eighth house is aspected <note>term: aspected (drishti) — when a planet "looks at" or influences another house from its position</note> by many powerful planets, death occurs through a combination of many bodily disorders. Now, if the lord of the eighth house is in the ascendant <note>term: ascendant (lagna) — the rising sign at the time of birth</note>, death is caused by diseases affecting the specific limb of the "Time-Person" <note>note: "Kala Purusha," the personification of the zodiac where Aries is the head, Taurus the face, etc.</note> represented by that rising sign. Regarding the location of death: if the eighth house falls in a movable sign <note>note: Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn</note> or its sub-division, death occurs in a foreign land. If in a fixed sign <note>note: Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius</note>, it occurs in one's own home. If in a dual-natured sign <note>note: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces</note>, death occurs on a journey or path away from home. || 74 ||

If a powerful planet aspects the eighth house, death occurs through the aggravation of the bodily element <note>term: dhatu — the physical constituents of the body</note> associated with that planet. If the Sun aspects, it is by fire; if the Moon, by water; if Mars, by weapons; if Mercury, by fever; if Jupiter, by phlegm; if Venus, by hunger; and if Saturn, by thirst. If the lord of the eighth is in the ascendant, death occurs via the limb corresponding to that sign. If the eighth house sub-division is a movable sign, death is abroad; if fixed, at home; if dual, on the road. || 74 ||

> If the eighth house is a "lonely house," not aspected by powerful lords of the planets like the Sun and others, nor occupied by them, then death comes through the lord of the decanate <note>term: decanate (drekkana) — a 10-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign</note> of that eighth house. || 75 ||

If the eighth house is not aspected or occupied by powerful major planets like the Sun, then death occurs in a "lonely house" (an uninhabited place). In this case, death is caused by the lord of the 22nd decanate <note>note: the 22nd decanate from the ascendant is traditionally considered a "fatal" point in Vedic astrology</note>. The death will be caused by the aggravation of the bodily element associated with that decanate lord. || 75 ||

If the eighth house is not aspected or joined by strong planets, death occurs in a lonely place. Here, death should be attributed to the disease of the element belonging to the lord of the decanate in the 8th house. || 75 ||

> Death occurs through the disease of the specific element of the Sun or other planets present in the eighth, or by the suffering caused by their "wicked servants" <note>term: upagrahas — secondary or shadow planets</note>. If the eighth house is joined by a benefic planet, death is peaceful; if by a malefic, it involves great lamentation. || 76 ||

If the Sun or other planets are situated in the eighth house, the person dies from a disease born of that planet's specific element, or from the pain caused by that planet's "wicked servants" (secondary mathematical points like Kala, etc.). If malefic planets (Sun, Mars, Saturn, Rahu, Ketu) are in the eighth, death involves great lamentation and agony. If joined by benefics (Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Moon), the person attains death peacefully and without distress. || 76 ||

Death is caused by the disease of the planet's element or its secondary planet. If a malefic is in the eighth, death is painful; if a benefic is there, death is happy/peaceful. || 76 ||

> If Mars is in Libra, the Sun is in Taurus, and the Moon is in the house of Saturn <note>Capricorn or Aquarius</note>, death will occur in the midst of poison. || 77 ||

> If a waning Moon is in the eighth house and is aspected by a powerful Saturn, death will occur from diseases of the anus or fire, or by a weapon. || 78 ||

> If the Sun and the Moon are in the eighth or in trine houses <note>1st, 5th, or 9th</note> from the ascendant, death will be caused by a fall from a mountain, by a lightning strike, or by a collapsing wall. || 79 ||

> If Mars and the Sun are in each other's signs and occupy center houses <note>1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th</note> relative to the lord of the eighth house, the person will meet their end through the anger of a king, or by a spear or excellent weapon. || 80 ||

# With the Commentary on Jataka Parijata

<page-num>158</page-num>

...by a skilled outcaste. According to the *Amarakosha* <note>A famous Sanskrit lexicon</note>, "Nishada, Shvapacha, Antevasin, Chandala, and Pukkasa" are terms for various outcaste groups; death shall occur because of such a person. || 81 ||

<term>Lord of the Ascendant</term> (Lagnasya) = the ruler of the birth sign. <term>In the portion of death</term> (Nidhanashasye) = situated in the 64th <term>Navamsha</term> <note>A 1/9th division of a zodiac sign; the 64th Navamsha is a sensitive point associated with vulnerability</note> from the Navamsha occupied by the Ascendant. This means the birth occurs in a specific Navamsha, and the ruler is in the 8th house position relative to that. Or, if the Lord of the Ascendant is "combust" = hidden by the rays of the Sun, or situated in a void house, the person dies in a place <insert>bereft of kinsmen</insert> = far from relatives, on the bare ground, due to <insert>the affliction of hunger</insert> = suffering caused by the desire to eat. || 82 ||

If the <term>Lord of Life and the Lord of the Ascendant</term> = the rulers of the 8th and 1st houses, are <insert>devoid of strength</insert> = weak, and if the "Son of Earth" (Mars) is joined with the <term>Lord of the 6th house</term>, then the learned scholars say with certainty that the person's death will occur in <insert>battle</insert> = war, by means of a weapon. || 83 ||

When the <term>Lord of the Ascendant</term> is joined with the <term>Lord of Vehicles</term> = the ruler of the 4th house, and also joined with the <term>Lord of Speech</term> = the ruler of the 2nd house, the person's death occurs from <term>indigestion</term> (Ajirna) or eating bad food. Alternatively, if the <term>Lord of the Wife</term> = the ruler of the 7th house, is accompanied by the rulers of vehicles and wealth (the 4th and 2nd houses), death occurs from indigestion. || 84 ||

The <term>Lord of the Navamsha of the 10th house</term> (Bhuktyanshapah) = the ruler of the 9th-part division of the 10th house, if joined with the "Son of the Sun" (Saturn) or <term>placed in a bad house</term> (the 6th, 8th, or 12th), then the person's death should be predicted by "eating poison" = consuming venom. Now, if that same ruler is joined with the "Serpent" = Rahu <note>The North Node of the Moon</note> or with "Shikhi" (Ketu) <note>The South Node of the Moon</note>, then the person's death occurs by <insert>binding with a rope</insert> = being tied or hung by a cord. There is a variation in the text found in the <term>Sarvartha Chintamani</term> <note>A major 17th-century astrological treatise</note>:

> "If the rulers of the 10th Navamsha are joined with Saturn or placed in bad houses, death is by poison. If joined with Rahu or Ketu in bad houses, they say death is by hanging." || 85 ||

When the Moon is waning = weak in strength, and joined with any one of Mars, Rahu, or Saturn, and <term>situated in the 8th house</term>, death occurs through the affliction of ghosts, fire, or water. If the waning Moon is in the <term>8th house</term> with Mars, it is by ghosts; with Rahu, by fire; with Saturn, by water. Likewise, if the waning Moon is so situated in a bad house (6, 8, or 12), then death occurs from the fear of <term>Epilepsy</term> <gloss>Epilepsy</gloss> = the disease of falling fits. || 86 ||

If the Moon is in the Ascendant, the Sun is weak in the 8th house, Jupiter is in the 12th from the Ascendant, and a malefic planet is in the 4th house (the house of happiness), that person's death will occur by falling from a bed or similar object. || 81 ||

If the Lord of the Ascendant is in the "Death Navamsha" (the 64th) or is combust with the Sun or in the 6th house, the person dies of hunger in a place devoid of their kinsmen (alone). || 82 ||

If the rulers of the 8th and 1st houses are weak and Mars is with the ruler of the 6th house, the person's death occurs in battle. Specifically, death is by a weapon. || 83 ||

If the ruler of the Ascendant is joined with the ruler of the 4th and the ruler of the 2nd (Jupiter), death is by indigestion. If the ruler of the 7th is with the rulers of the 4th or 2nd, death is by indigestion. || 84 ||

If the Navamsha lord of the 10th house is with Saturn or in a bad house, one dies by eating poison. If joined with Rahu or Ketu, one dies by a rope around the neck (hanging). If joined with Mars, Rahu, and Saturn, death is by ghosts, fire, or deep water. If the waning Moon is in a degraded position, death occurs from the fear of <term>Epilepsy</term> (falling sickness). || 85-86 ||

If [the Moon or Jupiter] is aspected <note>In astrology, an 'aspect' is when one planet 'looks' at another from a specific distance, influencing its effects.</note> by a malefic planet <note>original: "papagraha"; refers to planets like Saturn or Mars that generally bring challenging results.</note>, one should predict death from consumption <note>original: "kshayaroga"; historically refers to tuberculosis or a wasting disease.</note>. || 88 ||

When Rahu <note>The North Node of the Moon, considered a shadow planet in Vedic astrology.</note> is in the house of death <note>The eighth house.</note> and is aspected by a malefic planet, death will occur from boils, heat-related diseases, or from the affliction of a snake <note>original: "sarpadosha"; can mean a literal snakebite or a karmic curse.</note>. || 91 ||

# Now, the Combinations for the Severing of Hands and Other Limbs.

If Saturn is in the ninth house and Jupiter is in the third, or if they are in the eighth and twelfth houses respectively, the person born will suffer the loss of their hands. If Rahu, Saturn, and Mercury are situated in the tenth house, the person born under this combination will likewise be deprived of their hands. ॥ 63 ॥

<gloss>In the ninth house from the Ascendant (Lagna) is Saturn, and Jupiter is in the third house; or if those two, Saturn and Jupiter, are respectively in the eighth (death) and twelfth (loss) houses, then the person born suffers the severing of the hands. For that person, the cutting of the hands occurs. Furthermore, if Rahu, Saturn, and Mercury are in the tenth house (the house of action), then in this combination, the person born is joined with the severing of the hands. This means the person born would be without hands.</gloss> Here, the authority of the *Sarvartha Chintamani* <note>A classic 17th-century Sanskrit text on predictive astrology</note> states:

> If Saturn is in the ninth or with Jupiter in the third, the hands are severed; or if the Sun is in the eighth or twelfth.
> If the Moon is in the seventh or joined with the eighth lord, or with Mars, or with Jupiter. So it is said. ॥ 93 ॥

<note>If Saturn is in the 9th house and Jupiter is in the 3rd, the person's hands may be cut. Or if Saturn is in the 8th and Jupiter is in the 12th, the same result is predicted. If Rahu, Saturn, and Mercury are in the 10th house, the person will be without hands. (According to the author of Su. Sha.) ॥ 93 ॥</note>

If the lord of the eighth house is aspected by Venus, or if the Sun or Saturn is joined with the Lord of Serpents (Rahu), or if they are placed in a cruel <term>Shashtyamsa</term> <note>A 1/60th division of a zodiac sign used for fine-tuned predictions</note>, they say the person will suffer the severing of the head. ॥ 64 ॥

If Saturn is in the Ascendant, Rahu is in the seventh, Venus is in the sign of Virgo, and a waning Moon is in the seventh house, the person will have their hands severed along with their feet. ॥ 65 ॥

<gloss>If the lord of the eighth house (the house of death) is aspected by Venus, or if the Sun or Saturn is joined with the Lord of Serpents (Rahu), or if joined with a cruel Shashtyamsa (meaning situated in an inauspicious 1/60th division), if birth occurs then, the severing of that person's head occurs. The sense is that a man born in this combination dies by decapitation.</gloss> Here is a variation in the text:

> 'If the Lord of the Day (the Sun) is aspected by Venus and Jupiter, or if Saturn is joined with the Lord of Serpents (Rahu)'—so it is in the *Sarvartha Chintamani*. ॥ 94 ॥

<gloss>If Saturn is in the Ascendant, Rahu is in the seventh house, Venus is in the sign of Virgo, and the waning Moon (the dark Moon) is in the seventh house, the person born will have their hands severed along with their feet. This means a man born in the stated combination would indeed be without hands and feet.</gloss> Here is another reading from the *Sarvartha Chintamani*:

> If Saturn is in the Ascendant, Rahu is in the seventh, Venus is in the tenth, and the Moon is in Aquarius in the seventh house, he will be severed of hands and feet. ॥ 65 ॥

<note>The diagrams mentioned in the source describe planetary positions leading to death by specific causes like heat, snake bites, or bile disorders, illustrating the grim nature of these specific "death-dealing" combinations.</note>

## From the Commentary on Jataka Parijata

If such a birth occurs, one should predict the death of the native by the horns of a cow or by being struck by a spear <note>original: "shula-nipata"</note>. The meaning is that in this combination, a cow may kill the man with its horns, or someone may pierce him with a spear. || 99 ||

If the Sun is in the 10th house, Mars is in the 4th, no auspicious planets are present, and Mercury is in the Ascendant <note>the first house or rising sign</note>, then the native's death occurs by the horns of a cow or bull, or by being struck with a spear. || 99 ||

---

> **If the auspicious planets are in the tenth or fourth houses, or in the Ascendant or eighth, and are aspected by malefic planets, death occurs by a spear-strike.**
> **If the Moon is in the Ascendant, the son of the Sun (Saturn) is in the fourth house, and Mars is in the tenth, death occurs due to faults arising from a quarrel.** || 100 ||

Auspicious planets <note>benefics like Jupiter or Venus</note> in the tenth, fourth, Ascendant, or eighth houses, when aspected by malefic planets <note>planets with a harsh influence like Saturn or Mars</note>: this means that if the benefics are situated in these specific houses from the Ascendant and are seen by malefics, then the native's death will occur by a "spear-strike," meaning by being pierced by a spear or similar weapon. Furthermore, if the Moon is in the Ascendant, Saturn is in the fourth house, and Mars is in the tenth house, death occurs through faults arising from a quarrel <insert>or dispute</insert> <note>The original print is missing the syllable 'da' in the word for 'dispute'</note>. || 100 ||

If benefics are in the 10th, 4th, 1st, and 8th houses and are aspected by malefics, death is by a spear-strike. If the Moon is in the 1st, Saturn in the 4th, and Mars in the 10th, death is by a quarrel. || 100 ||

When the Sun is in the Ascendant and the Moon is in the seventh house <note>the house of the spouse</note>, and they are observed by malefic planets, death occurs from the fear of a quarrel or the fear of water. Furthermore, if the Sun and Moon are in the birth Ascendant and the other planets (Mars, etc.) are situated in dual signs <term>Dual signs: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces</term> and are aspected by malefic planets, then death occurs from "many waters" (deep water) <unclear>drowning</unclear> or from the horns or fangs of animals. || 101 ||

# Chapter on Longevity || 5 ||

If the Sun and Moon are in the rising sign of Pisces joined with a malefic <note>a planet with a harmful influence, like Mars or Saturn</note>, and a malefic is in the eighth house, death is caused by a woman. If Mars is in the fourth house, the Sun in the seventh, and Saturn and the Moon are in the eighth, death occurs due to a specific type of food. || 103 ||

**Sun and Moon** <note>original: "shashiravi"</note> = the Moon and Sun; if in **Pisces rising** <note>original: "minodaye"</note> = Pisces ascendant; **joined with a malefic** = joined with either Mars or Saturn; and a **malefic** = Mars or Saturn is present in the eighth house from the ascendant (there is another reading here: "aspected by a malefic," which would be interpreted as the ascendant being viewed by a malefic planet); the person's death is **caused by a woman** <note>original: "ramanikritam"</note>. The meaning is that death occurs due to the enmity of a woman. Now, if **Mars** <note>original: "bhaume"</note> is in the **fourth house** <note>original: "sukhe"</note>, or if the **Sun** <note>original: "dinakare"</note> is in the **seventh house** <note>original: "madasthaye"</note>, and **Saturn** <note>original: "mande"</note> and the **Moon** <note>original: "shashini"</note> have gone to the eighth house, the death of the person is **caused by a specific food** <note>original: "annavisheshajanyam"</note> = it should be said to occur from eating a specific grain (such as *kodrava* <note>Kodo millet, which can be toxic if fermented or infected</note>). || 103 ||

If Pisces is the rising sign, the Sun and Moon are there with a malefic, and there is a malefic in the 8th house, death is by a woman. If Mars is in the 4th, the Sun in the 7th, and Saturn and Moon in the 8th, death is by some grain. || 103 ||

If Saturn is in the second house, the Moon in the fourth, and Mars is situated in the tenth, one meets death caused by a wound. If Mars is in the fourth, the Moon in the second, and the Sun has gone to the tenth house, death is from an elephant, horse, or vehicle. || 104 ||

-> Simple Meaning || 104 || <-

---

If Saturn is in the 2nd house, the Moon is in the 4th, and Mars is in the 10th, death occurs from a wound <note>original: "vrana"</note>.

If Mars is in the 4th, the Moon is in the 2nd, and the Sun is in the 10th, death occurs from a vehicle such as an elephant or horse. || 104 ||

If Saturn is in the eighth, the Moon is weak in the tenth, and the Sun is in the fourth, death is by a falling piece of wood. If the Lord of the Ascendant is between malefics and joined with Ketu, and the eighth house from the ascendant is joined with a malefic, death occurs from the mother's wrath. || 105 ||

**Saturn in the eighth** <note>original: "randhre"</note> = in the eighth house from the birth ascendant; the **Moon** <note>original: "shashanke"</note> is **weak** (in its sign of debilitation or a foe's house) in the **tenth house** <note>original: "viyati"</note>; and the **Sun** <note>original: "bhanau"</note> is in the **fourth house** <note>original: "sukhe"</note>, the person's death is **by a falling piece of wood** <note>original: "nibhrutakasthahatena"</note> = death by the impact of a falling designated piece of timber. The **Lord of the Ascendant** <note>original: "jananalagnapatau"</note> is **with Ketu** <note>original: "saketau"</note> (another reading says "in a center," meaning houses 1, 4, 7, or 10). **Between malefics** <note>original: "papantare"</note> = the Lord of the Ascendant is flanked by malefic planets (one in the 2nd and another in the 12th from it); and the **eighth house from the ascendant** is joined with a **malefic** <note>original: "khalena"</note>, death occurs from the **mother's wrath** <note>original: "matrikopat"</note> = due to the hostility of one's own mother. In this combination, the person's mother is wicked, and death results from her anger. || 105 ||

> If the Sun is in the Ascendant, Saturn in the 5th, the Moon in the 8th, and the Son of Earth <note>Mars; original: "Dharasunau"</note> has gone to the 9th, death occurs from the fear of a tree or a lightning strike. || 107 ||

## On the Knowledge of the Direction of Death

> If at a daytime birth, a night-strong sign is rising;
> or if at a nighttime birth, a day-strong sign is rising;
> death occurs in the direction of the planet that is strongest in positional strength
> among the lord of the rising Navamsha, those occupying it, or those aspecting it. || 116 ||

Now the direction of death is explained. If the birth is during the day and the Ascendant is a sign strong at night (Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Sagittarius, or Capricorn), or if the birth is at night and the Ascendant is a sign strong during the day (Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Gemini, or Aquarius), then one looks to the lord of the rising Navamsha, the planets joined with it, and the planets aspecting it. Among these, the person dies in the direction of the planet that possesses the greatest positional strength <term>Sthana-virya: the strength a planet gains by being in a specific sign or house</term>. || 116 ||

In a day birth with a night-strong sign or a night birth with a day-strong sign, the person dies in the direction of the strongest planet among the Navamsha lord, the planets therein, and the planets aspecting it. || 116 ||

<header>With the Commentary on Jataka Parijata—</header>

What is meant by the unrisen <term>Navamsa</term><note>A one-ninth division of a zodiac sign, used for fine-tuned predictions.</note>? The number of <term>Ghatikas</term><note>A unit of time equal to 24 minutes.</note> corresponding to that portion represents the duration of "delusion" (unconsciousness or stupor) at the time of death. If that portion is aspected by its own <term>Navamsa</term> lord, the duration remains as calculated. If aspected by malefic planets, the time is doubled; if aspected by benefic planets, the duration of this state of delusion is tripled.

Now, the fate of the body is determined by the 22nd <term>Drekkana</term><note>A ten-degree division of a sign; the 22nd Drekkana from the rising sign is considered highly significant for death.</note> from the Ascendant. If this is **cruel** (malefic), **watery**, **gentle** (benefic), or **mixed**, the body meets its end respectively by **fire, water, drying up, or being consumed by beasts**. The meaning is this: if the 22nd Drekkana is **malefic**, the body is consumed by fire after death. If it is a **watery Drekkana**, the body is cast into water. If it is a **benefic Drekkana**, it is "mixed," meaning it dries up <note>Likely referring to burial or natural decomposition</note>. If it is a **mixed Drekkana**, it is eaten by **beasts** such as dogs and jackals. As it has been said—

> "The delusion at the time of death is equal to the unrisen portion of the Navamsa; it is doubled or tripled if aspected by its lord or by benefics.
> Likewise—by fire, water, or mixed means; by ashing, saturation, or drying; the fate of the corpse is to be considered through the divisions of the house of death." Thus says Varahamihira <note>A famous 6th-century Indian astronomer and astrologer</note>.

The specific cruel, watery, benefic, and mixed Drekkanas to be discussed can be found in the ninth chapter (**verses 113-115**) of this work. || 117 ||

Based on the remaining (to be enjoyed) <term>Navamsa</term> of the Ascendant, calculate the proportion of time in <term>Dandas</term><note>Equivalent to a Ghatika, 24 minutes</note>. If the lord of that Navamsa aspects it, that is the duration of delusion. If malefic planets aspect the Ascendant Navamsa, double the calculated time; if benefics aspect, triple it. This indicates how long the person remains unconscious at the time of death.

Now the fate of the corpse is described. If the 22nd <term>Drekkana</term> from the birth Ascendant (the Drekkana of the 8th house) is cruel, the body is burnt in fire. If it is watery, it is set adrift in water. If it is benefic, it is buried in the earth. If it is mixed, it is eaten by dogs, jackals, etc. (Commentary by Su. Sha.) || 117 ||

->### Now, Knowledge of the Soul's Destination After Death.<-

**Jupiter, the Sun and Mars, the Moon and Venus, and Mercury and Saturn—**
**These lead to the worlds of Gods, Mortals, Ancestors, and Hell respectively, if they occupy the Ascendant at the time of death. || 118 ||**

Now the knowledge of the soul's destination (<term>Gati</term>) after death is explained. **Jupiter**; **the Sun and Mars**; **the Moon and Venus**; and **Mercury and Saturn**—if these are positioned in the **Ascendant of the time of death** (the zodiac sign rising at the moment one passes away), they lead the soul respectively to the **worlds of Gods, Mortals, Ancestors, and Hell**. Jupiter in the death-ascendant leads the deceased to the world of the Gods. The Sun and Mars lead to the world of Mortals. The Moon and Venus lead to the world of the Ancestors. Mercury and Saturn lead to the world of Hell. In the *Svalpa Jataka*, Varahamihira mentions the destination based on the planetary positions at the time of birth:

> "The lords of the 6th, 8th, and 12th Drekkanas lead to the Gods, Ancestors, Animals, and Hell, when placed in the 7th, 6th, or 8th houses."

Furthermore, in the same text:
> "If Jupiter is exalted in the 6th, 8th, or a quadrant, or if Pisces is the Ascendant, and the other planets are weak, they say the soul attains Liberation (<term>Moksha</term>) at death."

By observing the phrase "at death" in the subsequent verse, it is clear that Varahamihira also approves of determining the destination from the Ascendant at the moment of death. || 118 ||

Regarding the destination after death: if Jupiter is in the Ascendant at the time of death, the soul goes to the **God-world** (Heaven). If the Sun and Mars are there, it goes to the **Mortal-world**. If the Moon and Venus are there, it goes to the **Ancestor-world**. And if Mercury and Saturn are there, it goes to **Hell**. (Commentary by Su. Sha.) || 118 ||

# Chapter 5: On the Determination of Longevity
<note>original: "Ayurdayadhyaya"</note>

->The Earth-circle begins with the Tumburu group of four; the Atmosphere-circle is said to begin with the Lion’s Abode. The Heaven-circle arises from the group starting with the Bow. The soul and death meet in these worlds. (119)<-

The movement of the soul is now explained according to the rising sign <term>Lagna; the zodiac sign ascending on the eastern horizon</term> at the time of death. 

**The Earth-circle** <note>original: "Bhuchakra"</note>: The first four signs—Aries, Taurus, Gemini, and Cancer—are called the Earth-circle. 
**The Atmosphere-circle** <note>original: "Bhuvashchakra"</note>: The next four signs—Leo, Virgo, Libra, and Scorpio—are called the Atmosphere-circle. 
**The Heaven-circle** <note>original: "Suvashchakra"</note>: The final four signs—Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, and Pisces—are called the Heaven-circle by the learned. 

The purpose of these circles is explained: "The soul and death meet in these worlds." Whichever circle the rising sign belongs to at the moment of death, the soul travels to that world after passing. If one dies when the rising sign is among the first four (Aries to Cancer), they go to the Earthly realm. If among the middle four (Leo to Scorpio), they go to the Atmospheric realm. If among the final four (Sagittarius to Pisces), they go to the Heavenly realm. (119)

<margin>Aries, Taurus, Gemini, and Cancer are the Earth-circle; if these are the signs at death, the soul goes to the Earthly world. Leo, Virgo, Libra, and Scorpio are the Atmosphere-circle. The remaining—Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, and Pisces—are the Heaven-circle. (Author: Su. Sha.)</margin>

->If the lord of the twelfth house occupies a cruel sixtieth-division and is aspected by malefic planets, the soul goes to the hellish world. The same occurs if Rahu is in the twelfth house joined with Mandi and the lord of the eighth, and is aspected by the lord of the house of enemies. (120)<-

Another combination is described: If the lord of the twelfth house <note>The house of loss and liberation</note>—calculated from either the birth sign or the death sign—occupies a malefic <term>Shashtyamsa; a 1/60th division of a sign</term> and is aspected by malefic planets, the soul goes to a hellish realm. Furthermore, if Rahu <note>The North Node of the Moon</note> is in the twelfth house, joined with Mandi <note>a mathematical point associated with Saturn</note> and the lord of the eighth house, and is aspected by the lord of the sixth house (the house of enemies), the same result occurs: the person goes to hell. (120)

->If a benefic planet is in its sign of exaltation in the twelfth house, aspected by both malefic and benefic planets and placed in a favorable divisional chart, one should predict the vast enjoyment of heaven. Or, if the lord of the tenth house is Jupiter, placed in the twelfth house and aspected by benefic celestial dwellers, the person attains immortality. (121)<-

If a benefic planet is in its highest state of strength (exaltation) and placed in the twelfth house, and is in a favorable divisional chart while being aspected by both malefic and benefic planets, one should declare that the deceased will experience the great joys of heaven. Alternatively, if the lord of the tenth house (the house of actions) is Jupiter <note>original: "Purandara-guru," the teacher of Indra</note> and he is placed in the twelfth house while being aspected by other benefic planets, the deceased attains "immortality" or a divine status. The meaning is that one born or dying under this combination reaches the rank of a deity. (121)

->When Jupiter is in the Sagittarius sub-division, endowed with strength, and placed in the rising sign of Cancer, and three or four planets are in the cardinal houses, the soul travels to the Abode of Brahma. (122)<-

Now the combination for attaining the Abode of Brahma <note>The highest spiritual realm</note> is described. When Jupiter is in the <term>Navamsha; 1/9th divisional chart</term> of Sagittarius, is full of strength, and is placed in the rising sign of Cancer (here, Cancer is the rising sign and Jupiter is located within it. Since Cancer is the sign of Jupiter's exaltation and the Sagittarius sub-division is Jupiter's own, Jupiter becomes exceptionally powerful there, hence the term "endowed with strength")...

It is said: If three or four celestial planets are situated together in the <term>angles</term><note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses of a birth chart, known as 'Kendra' or 'Kantaka'.</note>, the person born (or dying) at that time attains the <term>Abode of Brahma</term><note>Brahmapada: a high spiritual realm of existence.</note>. In this state of enjoyment, they reach the status of Brahma. || 122 ||

If powerful Jupiter is in the <term>Navamsha</term><note>A one-ninth division of a zodiac sign used for fine-tuned analysis.</note> of Sagittarius while Cancer is the rising sign, and three or four planets are in the angles, one attains the Abode of Brahma. || 122 ||

**If Sagittarius is the rising sign, with Jupiter in the <term>Tumbura</term> division, and Venus is in the descendant,**
**while a strong Moon is situated in Virgo, one attains the supreme, eternal realm. || 123 ||**

Now the <term>Yoga for Liberation</term><note>Moksha Yoga: a planetary configuration indicating the soul's release from the cycle of rebirth.</note> is described. If Sagittarius is the rising sign (<term>Lagna</term>), and Jupiter is in the <term>Tumbura-amsha</term><note>Specifically the Navamsha of Aries within the sign of Sagittarius.</note>, and Venus (the "Preceptor of the Demons") is in the descendant (the 7th house from the rising sign), and a strong Moon is in Virgo (which becomes the 10th house when Sagittarius rises), then the person born or dying attains the supreme state—the eternal realm free from birth and death. This is called the <term>Abode of Vishnu</term><note>Vishnupada: the highest spiritual destination in Vaishnava theology.</note>. From there, they do not return to this world. As the Blessed Lord Krishna said:

> **"That which is called the Unmanifest and Imperishable is said to be the supreme goal. Having attained it, they do not return; that is My supreme abode."**
> **"From the realm of Brahma downwards, all worlds are subject to return, O Arjuna. But having attained Me, O son of Kunti, there is no rebirth." — Thus in the Bhagavad Gita.**

Here is the Yoga for Liberation as stated by Varahamihira in the *Svalpa Jataka*:

**If exalted Jupiter is in the 6th, 8th, or an angle, or if the rising sign is Pisces,**
**and the remaining planets are weak at birth or death, they say one attains the state of liberation. || 123 ||**

If Jupiter is in the rising sign of Sagittarius in the Aries Navamsha, Venus is in the 7th house, and a strong Moon is in the sign of Virgo, then after death, one attains the supreme state (Liberation). || 123 ||

### Conclusion of the Chapter

**The natural life-span, the primary years of life, the calculation of the precise time of death, the various types of death,**
**and all things arising from the time of departure have been proclaimed by the grace of the Sun and other planets. || 124 ||**

->Thus, by the grace of the nine planets, in the *Jataka Parijata* composed by Vaidyanatha,<-
->ends the Fifth Chapter: On the Determination of Life-span. || 5 ||<-

# Chapter on Longevity (Ayurdaya) || 5 ||

One may suffer death through various means: from a fall from a mountain peak if the Sun and Mars are in certain positions; from a well if Saturn, the Moon, and Mars are in the 4th, 7th, and 10th houses. If the Sun and Moon are in the Ascendant in a watery sign and aspected by malefic planets, death occurs by drowning. <note>The text lists specific astrological combinations (yogas) that predict the physical cause of death, such as fire, weapons, or diseases.</note>

If Saturn is in Cancer and the Moon is in Capricorn, death is caused by dropsy <term>Jalodara: an accumulation of fluid in the abdomen</term>. If the Moon is between two malefic planets in a sign owned by Mars, death comes from weapons or fire. In the sign of Virgo, death may arise from blood disorders or consumption <note>original: "shosha," likely referring to tuberculosis or wasting diseases</note>.

If malefic planets occupy the 9th and 11th houses without the aspect of benefics, death occurs in captivity or through hanging, especially if the <term>Drekkana: a 10-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign</term> is associated with "nooses" or "fetters." If the Moon is in the 7th house in Virgo, Venus is in Aries, and the Sun is in the Ascendant, death occurs in one's own home due to a woman.

If Mars is in the 4th house and the Sun or Saturn is in the 10th, while the waning Moon is with malefic planets in the 5th, 8th, or 9th, the body is pierced by a spear. If the Sun is in the 4th and Mars is in the 10th, aspected by the waning Moon and Saturn, death is caused by a blow from a wooden club.

Death may also result from blows with a staff, from smoke, fire, or imprisonment, depending on the placement of the Sun, Moon, Mars, and Saturn in the 1st, 4th, 9th, or 10th houses. || 6 ||

When Mars, the Sun, and Saturn occupy the 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, death is caused by weapons, fire, or the wrath of a king. If Saturn, the Moon, and Mars are in the 2nd, 4th, and 10th houses, the body perishes due to wounds or worms. || 7 ||

A fall from a vehicle occurs if the Sun is in the 10th and Mars is in the 4th. If Mars is in the 7th and Saturn, the Moon, and the Sun are in the Ascendant, death is caused by being crushed by a machine. || 8 ||

If the waning Moon is in the 8th house and Saturn is aspected by a powerful Mars, death results from diseases of the private parts, worms, weapons, or fire. || 9 ||

If the Sun and Mars are in the 7th, Saturn is in the 8th, and the waning Moon is in the 4th, one dies among birds. If Mars, Saturn, and the Moon are in the 1st, 5th, 8th, or 9th houses, death is caused by a fall from a mountain, a lightning strike, or a falling wall. || 10 ||

The 22nd <term>Drekkana</term> is said by the wise to be the primary cause of death. Its lord, even if otherwise weak, bestows death according to its own nature. || 11 ||

The place of death should be determined by the nature of the rising sign or its Navamsha. The state of consciousness at the time of death depends on the portion of the sign that has not yet risen; this is doubled or tripled if aspected by its own lord or by benefic planets. || 12 ||

The nature of the corpse and its final state—whether consumed by fire, water, or other elements—should be considered based on the planets in the 8th house, as explained in the great treatises. || 13 ||

The lords of the Decanates <note>Drekkanas</note> occupied by the Sun and Moon determine the soul's destination: the world of the gods, the ancestors, animals, or hell. This is judged by the strength of the planets and their positions in exaltation or otherwise. || 14 ||

Liberation <term>Moksha: release from the cycle of rebirth</term> occurs if the lord of the 6th, 8th, or 12th house is in the 12th, or if Jupiter is in a quadrant or the 8th house while in its sign of exaltation. If the planets are weak, the soul returns to other states. || 15 ||

The detailed commentary on these verses by Bhattotpala should be consulted. They are not written here for fear of making the book too long.

The "Nectar" commentary on the Parijata, composed by Kapileshwara, is thus completed for this fifth chapter titled "Longevity." || 5 ||

By the grace of the Sun and the other nine planets, I, <insert>Vaidyanatha the Astrologer</insert>, have described the various methods of calculating longevity, such as Nisargayu, and the different types of death in this fifth chapter. (Su. Sha. Kar) || 125 ||

->composed by Sri Vaidyanatha the Astrologer.<-

# Chapter 6: On the Cancellation of Birth Fortunes

## First, the Definition of the Cancellation of Birth Fortunes.

Some combinations are the cancellations of **Royal Unions** <note>original: "Rajayoga"; combinations indicating power and status</note>, some are called **Reka** or **Poverty Unions** <note>original: "Daridryayoga"</note>.
Some are **Servitude Unions** <note>original: "Preshyayoga"</note> and some are named **Kemadruma** <note>a specific lunar void combination</note>; these four shall be the causes of the destruction of a birth's fortune. || 1 ||

Now, the chapter on the **Cancellation of Birth Fortunes** <term>Jataka-bhanga: the neutralization of good planetary results</term> is explained. Here, it is asked: what is meant by the "cancellation of birth fortune"? The text says "Some." The cancellations of **Royal Unions** = those combinations which destroy the Royal Union in which a person is born to be a king (such as "Sun in Aries in the Libra Navamsha," etc., which will be described later). Some are **Reka**, meaning **Poverty Unions** (such as "when the Lord of the Ascendant is devoid of strength," etc.). Some are **Servitude Unions** (such as "Mars in the tenth house," etc.). And some are **Kemadruma Unions** (such as "when the Moon is in the Ascendant without flanking planets," etc.). These four are the "Birth-Fortune Destroyers." The implication is that if even one of these four combinations exists at the time of birth, that person's life becomes essentially fruitless. || 1 ||

*How many? Several combinations that destroy Royal Unions, several Poverty Unions called Reka, several Servitude Unions, and several Kemadruma Unions—these four types are said to be the "Cancellations of Birth Fortune" (the destroyers of auspicious combinations). (Commentary by Su. Sha.)* || 1 ||

## Royal Cancellations.

If the **Sun** <note>original: "Dinakara"</note> is in **Aries** but in the **Libra Navamsha** <note>a 1/9th divisional sign</note> and is aspected by malefic planets, the subject is penniless.
When the **Son of Bhrigu** (Venus) is in the sign of **Virgo** and in the **Virgo Navamsha**, the subject is a beggar. ||
If the **Lord of Day** (the Sun) is in its sign of debilitation and at its point of deepest debilitation,
even one born as the eldest son of a most noble royal family will be destitute of wealth, children, wife, and food. || 2 ||

It is described here how a person born under certain combinations becomes miserable even if born a king. **Even the eldest son of a noble royal family** = even the first-born in the best of royal lineages. If the **Sun** is in the sign of **Aries** (its exaltation) but in the **Libra Navamsha** (specifically between 20° and 23°12' of Aries) and is seen by malefic planets, then that person becomes penniless. This means that although the first son in a royal family usually becomes king, if such a combination exists at his birth, he (even being the King's eldest son) will be poor. Similarly, if **Venus** <note>original: "Bhrigusuta"</note> is in the sign of **Virgo** and also in the **Virgo Navamsha** (specifically the 9th Navamsha of Virgo, between 26°40' and 30°), the person born becomes a beggar or a petitioner. Furthermore, if the **Sun** is in its sign of debilitation = **Libra**, and specifically at its point of deepest debilitation = the 10th degree (6 signs and 10 degrees), then he (though a royal prince) will be **destitute of wealth, children, wife, and food** = lacking riches, offspring, a spouse, and sustenance. The meaning is that he becomes entirely unfortunate. || 2 ||

*If the Sun is in Aries in the Libra Navamsha and malefic planets look upon it, the subject is poor. If Venus is in Virgo and in the Virgo Navamsha, he is a beggar. If the Sun is in its debilitated sign (Libra) at the point of deepest debilitation (10°), then the subject, even if from a noble royal family, is deprived of Lakshmi (wealth), children, wife, and food.* || 2 ||

If **Jupiter** <note>original: "Amaraguru"</note> is joined by **Saturn, Mars, and Rahu** <note>original: "Manda-Ara-Ahi"</note> and is aspected by **Venus and Mercury** <note>original: "Shukra-Induputra"</note>,
the person born, even in a lowly body <note>meaning a low-caste or humble birth</note>, attains all knowledge and wealth.
If the **Lord of Stars** (the Moon) and the **Sun** <note>original: "Taranatha-Vikarttanau"</note> are in the same house and are aspected by **Saturn** <note>original: "Saura"</note>,
the person born earns his livelihood through low or degraded means. || 3 ||

## Chapter on Natal Rites || 6 ||

**The Teacher of the Immortals** <note>original: "Amaragurau" - a title for Jupiter</note> = Jupiter, **joined with Saturn, Mars, and Rahu** <note>original: "Mandarahisamanvite"</note>, and **aspected by Venus and the son of the Moon** <note>original: "Shukrenduputraikshite" - Mercury is the son of the Moon</note>, the person born—even if they are of the Shudra class <note>the laboring class in the traditional caste system</note>—attains all knowledge and wealth. As stated in the *Sarvartha Chintamani* <note>A classic 17th-century Sanskrit text on astrology</note>:
> "When Jupiter is joined with Rahu and Saturn, and aspected by Venus or Mercury, even a Shudra attains the qualities of a Brahmin <note>the priestly/scholarly class</note>, having acquired all knowledge."

When the **Lord of the Stars and the Divider of Day** <note>original: "Taranathavikarttanau" - the Moon and the Sun</note> = the Moon and the Sun, are **placed in the sixth house** <note>original: "Gadagatau" - the house of disease and enemies</note> and are aspected by **the son of the Sun** <note>Saturn</note>, then the person born gains their **livelihood through lowly means** = the methods prescribed for the livelihood of the lower classes (such as service/slavery). This means that even if one is born into a noble family, under this planetary alignment, they will follow a lowly occupation. || 3 ||

If Jupiter is joined with Saturn, Mars, and Rahu, and is seen by Venus and Mercury, the person born—even in a Shudra family—attains complete knowledge and Lakshmi <note>the goddess of wealth</note>!
If the Moon and Sun are in the sixth house from the Ascendant and Saturn looks at them, that person shall find their living through lowly work. || 3 ||

> If the son of the Sun <note>Saturn</note> is in a Cardinal house <note>houses 1, 4, 7, or 10</note> or in the Ascendant, not seen by benefic planets, and the person is born during the Time-Hour <term>Kala-hora: a specific planetary hour of the day</term> of the son of the Earth <note>Mars</note>, they become a beggar and a slave.
> If the Moon is in Aries with Mars, not seen by benefics but seen by Saturn, one becomes a beggar.
> If the Sun, Moon, and Saturn are all in Cardinal houses, one will have a dull body <note>lacking intelligence</note>, be without wealth, and eat the scraps of others. || 4 ||

**The son of the Sun** = Saturn, being in a **Cardinal house** (1, 4, 7, 10) or in the **Ascendant** = the first house, **not seen by benefic planets** = not aspected by auspicious planets, and if the person is born during the **Time-Hour of the son of the Earth** <note>Mars</note>, they become a beggar, a petitioner, and a slave or servant to others. Furthermore, if the **Moon** is in the **sign of Aries** **with Mars** <note>original: "Sarudhire"</note>, **not seen by benefics** = auspicious planets, and **seen by Saturn**, the person becomes a beggar. Here, the *Sarvartha Chintamani* says: If the Moon is in Aries and seen by the son of the Sun, one eats the food of alms; if seen by the son of the Earth:

> One is deprived of fortune if the Ascendant or Moon is joined with or seen by the son of the Sun.
> Lacking the sight of benefic planets... <note>The text here refers to complex calculations of the Time-Hour</note>
> If the Lord of the Time-Hour is Mars, and Saturn is in a Cardinal house or the Ascendant,
> Without the sight of benefic planets, one becomes a slave, living on alms and of a dull nature.

When **Saturn, the Moon, and the Sun** <note>original: "Arkendvakkaih"</note> are **in Cardinal houses** (1, 4, 7, 10), the person born has a **dull body** = a body lacking in wisdom/intelligence, is **without wealth** = poor, and **eats the food of others** = eats the leftovers of others.

->Regarding this, the method for knowing the Time-Hour (Kala-hora):<-

Multiply the elapsed ghatikas <note>units of 24 minutes</note> of the day by two, divide by five, and the remainder... the Lords of the Time-Hours follow in order from the Lord of the Day. || 5 ||

If Saturn is in a Cardinal house or the Ascendant, not seen by benefics, and born in the Hora of Mars, the man is a beggar and a slave. If the Moon is in Aries with Mars, not seen by benefics and seen by Saturn, he is a beggar. If Saturn, Moon, and Sun are in Cardinal houses, he has a dull body, is poor, and eats the leavings of others. || 4 ||

> If Saturn is in a Cardinal house, the Moon is in the Ascendant, and Jupiter is in the twelfth house,
> The person born is a beggar, drowned in an ocean of grief, and gone to a foreign land.
> If the Lord of the ninth house <note>house of fortune/religion</note> is in the twelfth house and a malefic planet is in a Cardinal house...

> One born [under these signs] becomes devoted to sin, lives on the wealth of others, and is devoid of knowledge. || 5 ||

When **Saturn** <note>original: "Mande"</note> is situated in a **cardinal house** <term>Kendra: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses of a birth chart</term>, the **Moon** is in the **ascendant** <term>Lagna: the house representing the self</term>, and the **Lord of Speech** (Jupiter) has gone to the **twelfth house** <note>original: "astame," though the commentary clarifies the 12th house of loss</note>, the person born becomes a beggar, immersed in an ocean of grief and anxiety, and goes to a foreign land. Furthermore—if the **Lord of the 9th house** (the house of fortune) is in the **12th house**, and a **malefic planet** is in a cardinal house, the person will be devoted to sin, will consume the wealth and food of others, and will be ignorant. || 5 ||

> If Jupiter is joined with Rahu or Ketu and is aspected by a malefic, one performs lowly deeds;

Wherever **Jupiter** <note>original: "Jive"</note> is joined with **Rahu** <term>the North Node of the Moon</term> or **Ketu** <term>the South Node of the Moon</term>, and is **aspected** <note>seen by the astrological "glance" of a planet</note> by a **malefic** (such as Saturn, Mars, or the Sun), the person born performs lowly deeds even if born into a high-status family. If **Jupiter** is in its **sign of fall** <note>original: "Niche" - Capricorn</note> and is seen by other planets in their fall (malefics), even a **Brahmin** <note>original: "Vipra" - a member of the priestly class</note> becomes a performer of extremely despicable and evil acts.

On this matter, the author of the *Sarvartha Chintamani* <note>A classic 17th-century astrological treatise</note> says:

> If Jupiter is with Ketu or Rahu and aspected by a malefic, one becomes an outcast.
> If Jupiter is in a lowly division or joined with lowly planets, even a twice-born man becomes such. ||

If the **Moon** and the **Lord of the Ascendant** are joined with the **Sun** <note>original: "Divanathanen" - Lord of the Day</note> and are aspected by **Saturn**, then the person born will be "Nindri"—always sleepy or lethargic. Likewise, if **malefic planets** are situated in the **tenth house** <note>original: "Mana-sthitair" - the house of profession and honor</note> and are devoid of the **aspect** of **benefic planets**, the person becomes a servant of others. || 6 ||

If Jupiter is with Rahu or Ketu and malefic planets see it, the person performs lowly deeds. If Jupiter is in its sign of fall and is seen by a planet in its fall, the person, despite being a Brahmin, performs great evils.

If the Moon is in its sign of fall with the Sun and Saturn sees it, the person is lethargic. If malefic planets are in the tenth house and benefics do not see them, one becomes a servant. || 6 ||

<header>Chapter on the Destruction of Fortunes || 6 ||</header>

### Chapter on the Destruction of Fortunes || 6 ||

->If the Lord of Fortune is in the house of loss, malefic planets are in the house of siblings, and the Lord of Loss is in the house of wealth,<-
->the person born eats bad food, suffers from imprisonment, and is devoted to the wives of others. ||<-
->If all planets are in their signs of debilitation or in enemy divisions, and are in houses other than the house of action,<-
->the person is devoid of knowledge, intellect, wife, and sons; he is angry and always lives on alms. || 7 ||<-

**Lord of Fortune** = the ruler of the 9th house <note>The 9th house governs luck, father, and religion.</note> **in the house of loss** = gone to the 12th house; **malefic planets in the house of siblings** = located in the 3rd house; **Lord of Loss in the house of wealth** = the ruler of the 12th house located in the 2nd house. The person born **eats bad food** = consumes forbidden or low-quality food; he is **with imprisonment etc.** = suffers through tortures and restraints; he is **devoted to the wives of others** = absorbed in the wives of other men.

**Now, if all planets are in their signs of debilitation or in enemy divisions** = some in their lowest point of strength <term>Neecha: the sign where a planet is weakest</term> and some in the divisions of their planetary enemies; **in houses other than the house of action** = excluding the 10th house <note>The 10th house is the house of career and public standing.</note>, being situated in any other houses. The man born will be **devoid of knowledge, intellect, wife, and sons**; he is **angry** = of a wrathful temperament; and likewise **always lives on alms** = becomes a beggar. || 7 ||

->( 1 )<-  ->( 2 )<-

<margin>If the 9th lord is in the 12th, malefic planets are in the 3rd, and the 12th lord is in the 2nd, the native eats bad food (meat, garlic, onion, etc.), suffers bondage, and enjoys the wives of others. If all planets are in debilitation or enemy divisions and outside the 10th house, one lacks wisdom, family, and begs for food. </margin>

->If the Lord of the Ascendant is in the house of loss, a malefic is in the sky, and Mars is with the Moon,<-
->the person born goes to foreign lands, abandons happiness and wealth, and becomes poor. ||<-
->If the Lords of the Ascendant and the Moon-sign are not joined by benefics, or are combust, and the Lord of Fortune is in the house of loss,<-
->the person born loses wife and sons and becomes the destroyer of his lineage. || 8 ||<-

**Lord of the Ascendant** = the ruler of the 1st house **in the house of loss** = gone to the 12th house from the Ascendant; **a malefic** = one of the cruel planets, either Saturn or the Sun, **in the sky** = in the 10th house; and there **Mars is with the Moon** (Mars and Moon are joined together in that place). Then the person born **goes to foreign lands, abandons happiness and wealth, and becomes poor.**

**Lords of the Ascendant and the Moon-sign** = the ruler of the 1st house and the ruler of the sign where the Moon is placed; if they are **not joined by a benefic** = not with a lucky planet, **or are combust** <term>Astangata: rendered powerless by being too close to the Sun</term>; and the **Lord of Fortune** = ruler of the 9th house **in the house of loss** = in the 12th house. If a birth occurs under these conditions, the person **loses wife and sons** = his wife and children die, and he becomes a **destroyer of the lineage**. It is also said in the ***Sarvartha Chintamani*** <note>A famous 17th-century astrological treatise by Venkatesha Sharma.</note>:

> "If the Lord of the Ascendant is in the 12th, a malefic is in the 10th, and the Moon is joined with Mars, 
> the person born is cursed, lives in foreign lands, begs for food, and has a suffering body. 
> If the Lord of Fortune is in the 12th with a malefic, and the Lord of the Ascendant is with the Sun, he destroys the lineage; 
> he loses sons, wealth, and wife, especially if these planets are not joined or aspected by benefics." || 8 ||

# Page 168
## From the Annotated Jataka Parijata

If the <term>Lord of the Ascendant</term><note>Lagnēśa: The planet ruling the first house of the birth chart, representing the self.</note> is in the twelfth house, and there is a malefic planet in the tenth house, and Mars is joined with the Moon therein, then that person will live in a foreign land, be deprived of happiness and wealth, and become poor.

If both the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Moon-sign are not associated with benefic planets or are <term>combust</term><note>Astangata: A planet rendered weak or invisible by being too close to the Sun.</note>, and the Lord of the ninth house is in the twelfth house, the person will be without a wife and sons, and will be the destroyer of his own lineage. (According to the author of Sudha-Shala) || 8 ||

-> If the <term>cardinal houses</term><note>Kendra: The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, the pillars of a horoscope.</note> are occupied by both benefic and malefic planets, and the Moon is aspected by the Lord of the Ascendant while situated in a <term>Navamsha</term><note>A 1/9th divisional chart used for fine-tuning planetary strength.</note> of Saturn, the person destroys his lineage and is without wife or children. If Mercury and Venus are in the seventh house, Jupiter is in the fifth house, a malefic is in the fourth house, and there is a malefic in the eighth house from the Moon, those born under such a configuration are destroyers of their lineage. || 9 || <-

The commentary explains: In the cardinal houses (1, 4, 7, 10), if both benefics and malefics are present; and the Moon is aspected by the Lord of the Ascendant anywhere in the chart; and the Moon has reached a Navamsha of Saturn (Capricorn or Aquarius); then the man born is a "destroyer of the lineage" and "without wife or children." As stated in the *Sarvartha Chintamani*:

<margin>If benefics and malefics are in the cardinal houses, and the Moon is aspected by the Lord of the Ascendant, and if joined in a Saturnian division, one becomes a destroyer of the lineage and wifeless.</margin>

If Mercury and Venus are in the "House of Desire" (the 7th house from the Ascendant), Jupiter has gone to the "House of Children" (the 5th house), a malefic is in the "House of Happiness" (the 4th house), and a malefic planet is in the eighth house from the Moon's position, then the men produced are destroyers of their lineage. || 9 ||

If there are benefic and malefic planets in the cardinal houses (1, 4, 7, 10), the Moon is seen by the Lord of the Ascendant and is in Saturn's Navamsha, the person will be the destroyer of the family and be without wife and sons.

If Mercury and Venus are in the 7th house, Jupiter is in the 5th, a malefic is in the 4th, and a malefic is also in the 8th from the Moon, then those born will be the destroyers of the lineage. (Author of Sudha-Shala) || 9 ||

-> If the Moon is at the end of a <term>movable sign</term><note>Chara-rashi: Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn.</note>, at the beginning of a <term>fixed sign</term><note>Sthira-rashi: Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius.</note>, or in the middle of a <term>dual sign</term><note>Dvideha: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces.</note>, and is devoid of strength, and if the Ascendant is unoccupied by the "lords of the sky" (planets), then the <term>Yoga of Kings</term><note>Kshitipala-yoga: A combination indicating royal power or high status.</note> meets its destruction. || 10 || <-

When the Moon is at the very end of movable signs (Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn), at the beginning of fixed signs (2, 5, 8, 11), or in the middle of dual-natured signs (3, 6, 9, 12), and is weak; and the birth Ascendant is "abandoned" by the planets (meaning no planet resides in the 1st house), then the "King-protecting" combination or Royal Yoga is destroyed. Thus in the *Jatakeshwara*: "When the Moon is waning in the final or initial portions of movable signs..."

# Chapter 6: The Chapter on the Cancellation of Fortunate Births
<note>original: "जातकभङ्गाध्यायः" (Jātaka-bhaṅga-adhyāyaḥ). This chapter discusses "Bhanga" or the breaking/cancellation of positive yogas (planetary combinations).</note>

If the Moon is not aspected <note>aspected: "looked upon" by the influence of another planet</note> by even a single planet, then the destruction of royal power occurs.
The meaning is that in this combination, even one born into a royal family does not obtain the kingdom. || 10 ||

If the Moon is weak and positioned at the very end of a Moveable sign, the beginning of a Fixed sign, or the middle of a Dual sign, and no planets are present in the Ascendant <note>Lagna: the rising sign on the eastern horizon at birth</note>, the "Royal Union" <term>Rajayoga: a planetary combination indicating power and status</term> is destroyed. || 10 ||

---

If the lords of the Ascendant, the Moon-sign, and the Ninth House, along with the Sun, Moon, and Jupiter, are located in the <insert>divisional</insert> portions of their enemies, or are in the portions of the lords of their signs of debilitation <note>debilitation: the sign where a planet is at its weakest</note>, the person becomes a follower of others. || 11 ||

The Ascendant is the birth-lagna. The "sign" is the sign occupied by the Moon at birth. The "Ninth House" is the house of fortune from the Ascendant. If their lords—namely the Lord of the Ascendant, the Lord of the Moon-sign, and the Lord of the Ninth—as well as the Sun, Moon, and Jupiter, are in enemy <term>Navamsha: a one-ninth divisional chart used for fine-tuned analysis</term> or in the Navamsha of the lord of their debilitation sign, then the person born becomes a follower or servant of others. || 11 ||

---

If Venus, Mercury, and the Moon are in the center houses <term>Kendra: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</term> and Rahu <note>the North Node of the Moon</note> is in the Ascendant, the person destroys their prescribed duties and becomes like a low-born person. || 12 ||

When the Moon is in the "sky" (10th house), Venus is in the "desire" (7th) house, and a malefic planet—any one of the Sun, Mars, or Saturn—has reached the ninth house from the Ascendant, the person born is a destroyer of their family. Furthermore, if Venus, Mercury, and the Moon are in the centers, and Darkness <note>original: "Tamasi" referring to Rahu</note> has entered the birth Ascendant, the person destroys their own ordained duties; even if born in a high family, being devoid of proper conduct, they become equal to the lowest. || 12 ||

# Chapter on the Destruction of Fortunes || 6 ||

If the Moon and Mercury are in the tenth house, are aspected <note>viewed by the astrological "gaze" of a planet</note> by malefic planets, are conjoined with malefic planets, are in a debilitated Navamsha <note>a 1/9th divisional chart where a planet is at its weakest</note>, and are devoid of any aspect from benefic planets, then that person will certainly be a killer of birds. || 15 ||

### **If the Lord of the Ascendant is in the 5th or 2nd from the Moon, while malefic planets are in the 8th house from the Moon, and the Moon is in the 10th house, the person born lives by a very despicable profession. || 16 ||**

At the time of birth, if the Lord of the Ascendant <term>Lagnapati: the planet ruling the rising sign</term> is in the 5th or 2nd house from the Moon; and if the non-benefics <note>original: "saumyetareṣu" - those other than the gentle ones</note>, meaning the malefic planets, are in the 8th sign from the Moon; and if the "Cool-Rayed One" <note>original: "śītakare" - a poetic name for the Moon</note> is in the 10th house from the Ascendant. 
The result is this: The Moon should be in the 10th; from it, the Lord of the Ascendant should be in the 5th, 2nd, or 11th; and in the 8th, 10th, or 5th from the Moon, there should be malefic planets. Then the person born lives by a very despicable profession <note>original: "atiheyavṛttyā" - a low or contemptible livelihood</note>. 
Here is the reading from the *Sarvartha Chintamani* <note>A famous 13th-century astrological treatise</note>:
> **If the Lord of the Ascendant is in the 5th or 2nd from the Moon, or if malefic planets are in the 8th, and the Night-Maker <note>the Moon</note> is in the 10th, then the person born lives by a very despicable profession. || 16 ||**

<margin>If the Lord of the Ascendant is in the 5th or 2nd place from the Moon, and malefic planets are in the 8th sign, and the Moon is in the 10th, then that person shall live by an extremely low livelihood. || 16 ||</margin>

Venus and Jupiter <note>original: "bhṛgudevapūjyau" - Bhrigu's descendant and the teacher of the gods</note> have entered a debilitated or inimical Navamsha; and if the Son of the Day-Lord <note>original: "vāsaranāthaputre" - Saturn, the son of the Sun</note> is situated in the Navamsha of either Venus or Jupiter, the man born suffers great sorrow, is devoid of sons and a wife <note>original: "sutadārahīnaḥ"</note>, and being luckless, he survives only with extreme difficulty <note>original: "kṛcchreṇa"</note>.
There is a variation in the text of the *Sarvartha Chintamani*:
> **If Jupiter is in a debilitated or inimical Navamsha, and Saturn is in that same Navamsha, the person born is exceedingly miserable, devoid of children and wife, and lives through hardship, being luckless. || 17 ||**

<margin>If Venus and Jupiter are in the Navamsha of a debilitated or enemy sign, and Saturn is in the Navamsha of Jupiter or Venus, then the person remains without a wife or sons and, becoming unfortunate, lives somehow with great suffering. (According to the author of Su. Sha.) || 17 ||</margin>

# With Commentary on the Jataka Parijata

> All malefic planets situated in angles, in their signs of debilitation, or in enemy signs, if aspected by benefics occupying the 12th, 8th, or 6th houses, destroy a Royal Union <note>Rajayoga: a planetary combination indicating power and status</note> even for great kings; so too do planets in debilitation, in enemy signs, or in cruel sixtieth-divisions. || 18 ||

**All malefics** = the Sun, Mars, Saturn, and the waning Moon or malefic Mercury; **situated in angles, debilitation, or enemy signs** = if they are in the angles (1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses), or in their signs of fall, or in the signs of their enemies; and **aspected by those in the 12th, 8th, or 6th** = if they are seen by benefic planets who have gone to the houses of loss, death, or debt; then these great planets destroy—that is, ruin—the Royal Union. Furthermore, **debilitation, enemy, or cruel sixtieth-divisions** = those planets which are in their sign of fall, in an enemy's sign, or in a cruel <term>Shashtyamsa</term> <note>A 1/60th division of a zodiac sign used for fine-tuned analysis</note> also destroy the Royal Union. The implication is that in such a yoga, even one born into a royal family does not receive the fruits of royalty. As stated in the *Saravali*:

-> All cruel planets in angles, in debilitation or enemy signs, not joined or seen by benefics, <-
-> even if benefics are in the 12th, 6th, or 8th, then the ruin of a king occurs. || 18 || <-

If all malefic planets are in angles, or debilitated, or in an enemy's house, and are seen by benefics located in the 12th, 8th, or 6th houses, the destruction of Rajayoga should be predicted. Similarly, planets in debilitation, enemy signs, and malefic sixtieth-divisions destroy Rajayoga. (Commentary by S.S. Kar) || 18 ||

> If Saturn, the Moon, and the Sun are situated in angles and are not aspected by benefics, the person becomes a drinker of intoxicants. If these same planets are in cruel or enemy sixtieth-divisions or debilitated portions, the person is engaged in wicked deeds and follows the wives of others. || 19 ||

**Saturn, the Moon, and the Sun** = if these three are **situated in angles** and if they are **not aspected by benefics** = not seen by auspicious planets, then the person born becomes a **drinker of intoxicants** = a consumer of wine (a drunkard). If those same three—Saturn, Moon, and Sun—are joined with **cruel or enemy sixtieth-divisions or debilitated portions**, then the person born is **engaged in wicked deeds** = performs despicable acts, and is **a follower of the wives of others** = lusts after the wives of others. || 19 ||

If Saturn, the Moon, and the Sun are situated in angles and are not seen by a benefic planet, the native will be a drinker of wine. If those three planets are in the sixtieth-division of a cruel or enemy planet and in a debilitated portion, he will be involved in evil deeds and enjoy the wives of others. || 19 ||

> If Venus is debilitated, in the house of religion, and joined with a malefic, and if it is aspected by a malefic, the person is a striker of the twice-born. If Venus is in the 12th house in a benefic sign but in the sub-division of the Sun's son, the person will be the son of a female servant's husband. || 20 ||

**In debilitation** = residing in its sign of fall; **Venus** = the planet Bhrigu; **in the house of religion** = in the 9th house; **joined with a malefic** = joined with any malefic planet; and in such a state **aspected by a malefic** = seen by any malefic planet, the person born is a **striker of the twice-born** = a killer of Brahmins <note>Twice-born/Dvija refers to the upper castes, specifically Brahmins here</note>. Furthermore, if **Venus** is in the **12th house** in a **benefic sign** and has gone to the **sub-division of the Sun's son** = the <term>Navamsa</term> <note>A 1/9th divisional chart</note> of Saturn, the person born will be the **son of a female servant's husband** = the son of a maidservant. The meaning here is: if the 12th house is a sign of a benefic planet, but the Saturn-Navamsa falls within it, and Venus is situated there, the person born is the son of a maidservant. || 20 ||
