## Now, the Rekha and Other Yogas

> If the Lord of the Ascendant is devoid of strength and is aspected by the Lord of the House of Defeat (the 8th house), and if Jupiter—the Guru of the Gods—has its rays obscured by the Sun (is combust), the configuration known as Rekha occurs. Furthermore, if the Lord of the Navamsha occupied by the Lord of the 4th House has its light extinguished by the Sun and is aspected by the Lord of the 12th House, the Rekha Yoga is formed. || 21 ||

Now the Rekha Yogas are explained. **The Lord of the Ascendant** <note>Lagnesha</note> = the ruler of the first house; **devoid of strength** = weak; **aspected by the Lord of the House of Defeat** = viewed by the ruler of the 8th house; **Jupiter** <note>Purandara-guru</note> = the planet Jupiter; **rays obscured by the Sun** = together with the Sun, its rays are lost (combust). In such a case, the Rekha Yoga occurs. This configuration is named Rekha. **The Lord of the Navamsha occupied by the Lord of the 4th House** = the ruler of the specific divisional sign where the 4th house ruler is placed; **light extinguished by the Sun** <note>Tigmanshu-supta-dyutau</note> = its light is destroyed by the Sun, meaning it is combust; and if it is **aspected by the Lord of the 12th House** <note>Riph-esha</note> = viewed by the ruler of the 12th, then the birth results in the Rekha Yoga. || 21 ||

---

If the weak Lord of the Ascendant is aspected by the Lord of the 8th and Jupiter is combust with the Sun, the 'Rekha' Yoga is formed.
If the Navamsha lord associated with the Lord of the 4th is combust with the Sun and aspected by the Lord of the 12th, the 'Rekha' Yoga occurs. || 21 ||

> If the Lord of the 4th House is aspected by the Lord of the 6th and joined with the Lord of the 8th, while the Lord of the 10th is in the 5th house and the Lord of the Ascendant is in its sign of debilitation, one possesses Rekha. Or, if the Benefics are in the 8th, 6th, or 12th houses, and the Malefics are in the Centers or Trines (1, 4, 7, 10, 5, 9), and the Lord of the 11th House is weak, one is cursed with Rekha. || 22 ||

**The Lord of the 4th House** <note>Sukha-pati; literally 'Lord of Happiness'</note> = wherever it is, if it is **aspected by the Lord of the 6th**; **joined with the Lord of the 8th** = placed together with it; and **the Lord of the 10th** <note>Manesha; Lord of Honor</note> = the ruler of the 10th house is **in the 5th house**; and **the Lord of the Ascendant** = the ruler of the birth sign is **in its sign of debilitation** <note>Nicha; the lowest point of a planet's strength</note>, the person born in this combination has Rekha Yoga. Furthermore, if **Benefics** = auspicious planets are in the **8th, 6th, or 12th houses** <note>the 'Dusthanas' or difficult houses</note>, and **Malefics** = inauspicious planets are in the **Centers or Trines** (1, 4, 7, 10, 5, 9), and the **Lord of the 11th House** <note>Labha-pati; Lord of Gains</note> is **weak**, then one is cursed with Rekha; meaning, such a combination is explained by people as the Rekha Yoga. || 22 ||

# Chapter 6: The Chapter on the Cancellation of Horoscopes
<page-num>175</page-num>

If the Lord of Fortune <note>the ruler of the 9th house</note> is combust <note>hidden by the sun's rays</note> with the Sun, and the Lord of the 9th house is in its sign of debilitation <note>its weakest position</note>, and the Lord of the 2nd house <note>wealth</note> is also debilitated, then the **Reka** Yoga is formed. || 23 ||

-> If any three planets are in their signs of debilitation, or if they are obscured by the rays of the Sun <note>combust</note>, and the Lord of the Ascendant <note>Lagnapa</note> is situated in a "bad house" <note>the 6th, 8th, or 12th houses</note> or is otherwise devoid of strength, the **Reka**-producing Yoga occurs.
If malefic planets are situated in the Ascendant, the 2nd, 9th, 10th, 4th, 5th, 7th, or 3rd houses, and are aspected by debilitated planets, enemies, or other malefics, they grant the fruits of the **Reka** Yoga during the ninth part of that person's lifespan. || 24 || <-

If any three planets are in their respective signs of debilitation, or are "covered by the rays of the Lord of Day" <note>original: "dinesh-kirana-chhanna," meaning combust by the Sun</note>—meaning their light is destroyed—and the Lord of the Ascendant is in a "bad house" <note>Dusthana</note>—meaning one of the 6th, 8th, or 12th houses—or is powerless, the **Reka** Yoga is formed.
The terms *Hora* (Ascendant), *Vitta* (2nd), *Nava* (9th), *Aspada* (10th), *Mukha* <note>original: "Sukha," the 4th</note>, *Dhi* (5th), *Kama* (7th), and *Anuja* (3rd) refer to the houses. If malefics <note>original: "khala," cruel planets</note> situated in these houses are aspected by debilitated, enemy, or malefic planets, they produce the results of the **Reka** Yoga during the ninth portion of the native's life. This means such a combination is called **Reka**. By specifying "aspected by debilitated, enemy, or malefic planets," it is implied that if they are aspected by exalted, friendly, or benefic planets, they will not produce the **Reka** results. || 24 ||

If any three planets are debilitated or combust, and the Lord of the Ascendant is in a bad house or is weak, the **Reka** Yoga occurs.
If malefic planets are located in the 1st, 2nd, 9th, 10th, 4th, 5th, 7th, or 3rd houses, and are in debilitation, in an enemy's house, or aspected by a malefic, they give the fruit of **Reka** Yoga in the 9th part of the native's life. || 24 ||

-> One, two, or three malefic planets located in the Ascendant, 2nd, and 3rd houses respectively, and similarly in the houses following those, grant the **Reka** results at the beginning, middle, and end of life, provided they are aspected by enemies, malefics, or debilitated planets. || 25 || <-

If one, two, or three malefic planets <note>original: "khala-dyuchara"</note> are respectively in the *Kalpa* (Ascendant), *Sva* (2nd), and *Vikrama* (3rd)—meaning one malefic in the 1st, two in the 2nd, and three in the 3rd.
"And similarly in the houses following"—in the same manner for the next groups: one in the 4th, two in the 5th, three in the 6th; one in the 7th, two in the 8th, three in the 9th; and one in the 10th, two in the 11th, and three in the 12th. In such cases, for men (the natives), the **Reka** results are given respectively in the first third of life, the middle third of life, and the end of life.
This is what is said: If at birth one malefic is in any of the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses <note><term>Kendras</term>: the angular houses</note>, it gives **Reka** results in the first part of life. If two malefics are in the 2nd, 5th, 8th, or 11th <note><term>Panapharas</term>: the succedent houses</note>, it is in the middle of life. If three malefics are in the 3rd, 6th, 9th, or 12th <note><term>Apoklimas</term>: the cadent houses</note>, they give **Reka** results in the final stage of life.
This only applies if they are aspected by an enemy, a malefic, or a debilitated planet; by implication, if aspected by a friend, a benefic, or an exalted planet, they do not produce **Reka**. The specific fruits of **Reka** will be described in verses 26 and 27. || 25 ||

If 1 malefic planet in the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses is aspected by an enemy, malefic, or debilitated planet, it gives **Reka** results in the first stage of life. If 2 malefics are in the 2nd, 5th, 8th, or 11th houses, it is in middle age. If 3 malefics are in the 3rd, 6th, 9th, or 12th houses, they give the fruit of **Reka** Yoga in the final stage of life. || 25 ||

### The Results of Reka Yoga

-> One born under **Reka** is devoid of knowledge, penniless, lives with the poor, is lustful, angry, troubled in mind, but has a pleasant appearance <note>or "is tasteful"</note>, lacks good fortune, yet is clever. He eats food obtained by begging, is dirty, fond of disputes, filled with envy and rage, a slanderer of gods and Brahmins, and is daily criticized by his wife and children. || 26 || <-

### Now, the Yogas for Poverty (Daridra Yogas).

**If the Lord of the 8th house is stronger than the Lord of the 9th house, or if the Lord of the Ascendant is Jupiter,**
**And if the Lord of the 11th house is outside the quadrants, scorched by the rays of the Sun, and devoid of strength, the person is poor. || 28 ||**

Now, some Poverty Yogas (Daridra Yogas) are described. If the planet ruling the 8th house is stronger than the planet ruling the 9th house, or if Jupiter is the Lord of the Ascendant and is combust with the Sun outside of the quadrants, and the Lord of the 11th house is weak, the native becomes poor. || 28 ||

**And the son of the Moon (Mercury) is in the Ascendant with the Sun in a debilitated division, one is a beggar. || 29 ||**

When Jupiter, Mars, Saturn, and Mercury are—as the case may be—in the 11th, 6th, 12th, 8th, or 5th houses, or are in their respective signs of debilitation <note>The sign where a planet is at its weakest</note>, or are hidden by the Sun's rays (combust), and are aspected by non-benefics (malefic planets like Mars, etc.), and if Mercury is in the Ascendant joined with the Sun (combust) and also in a debilitated Navamsha <note>A specific 1/9th divisional chart</note>, then the person born becomes a beggar. || 29 ||

If Jupiter, Mars, Saturn, and Mercury are debilitated and situated in the 11th, 6th, 12th, 8th, or 5th houses, or are overcome by the Sun's rays, one becomes a beggar. If Saturn is in the 9th house (Fortune) and malefic planets look upon it, and Mercury is with the Sun in the Ascendant in a debilitated division, one becomes a beggar. || 29 ||

**And the Lord of the 12th house is stronger than the Lord of the Ascendant, debilitated, and struck by the Sun's rays, one is poor. || 30 ||**

# Chapter on the Cancellation of Fortunes || 6 ||

If the Lord of the 12th house is stronger than the Lord of the Ascendant, and is situated in its sign of debilitation <note>The sign where a planet's influence is weakest</note> or is combust <note>original: "ravikarabhirihato" - struck by the rays of the sun</note> by the Sun's rays, then the person born becomes impoverished. || 30 ||

If Jupiter, Mercury, Venus, Saturn, and Mars are placed respectively in the 8th, 6th, 12th, 5th, and 10th houses, and the Lord of the 12th is specifically stronger than the Lord of the Ascendant while in a debilitated sign or scorched by the Sun's rays, one becomes poor. || 30 ||

---

->If Venus, Jupiter, the Moon, and Mars are debilitated at birth,<-
->and placed in the 10th, 11th, 9th, 7th, or 5th houses, the person becomes poor.<-
->If Venus is in the Ascendant, Jupiter in the 5th, Mars in the 11th,<-
->and the Moon in the 3rd house, all being debilitated, the person becomes a beggar. || 31 ||<-

Venus, <term>Arya</term> <note>Jupiter</note>, <term>Dvijaraja</term> <note>The Moon, literally 'King of the twice-born'</note>, and <term>Bhumitanaya</term> <note>Mars, literally 'Son of the Earth'</note>—if these are debilitated at the time of birth and situated in the 10th, 11th, 9th, 7th, or 5th houses, the person born will be poor and destitute. Furthermore, if <term>Danavapujita</term> <note>Venus, 'The priest of the demons'</note> is in the Ascendant, <term>Amaraguru</term> <note>Jupiter, 'The priest of the gods'</note> is in the 5th, <term>Gharanandana</term> <note>Mars</note> is in the 11th, and <term>Ratrikara</term> <note>The Moon, 'The night-maker'</note> is in the 3rd house, and all are in their respective signs of debilitation, the person born becomes a beggar living on alms. This means that when all the mentioned planets are in the specified houses and in their signs of debilitation, the subject becomes a beggar. || 31 ||

---

If at the time of birth Venus, Jupiter, the Moon, and Mars are in their signs of debilitation and placed in the 1st, 10th, 9th, 7th, or 5th houses, the subject becomes poor.

If Venus is in the 1st, Jupiter in the 5th, Mars in the 11th, and the Moon in the 3rd house, and all are debilitated, the subject becomes a beggar. || 31 ||

---

->If the Ascendant is a movable sign and in a movable Navamsha, and is<-
->aspected by Saturn and a debilitated Jupiter, one becomes a beggar.<-
->Excepting the signs owned by Jupiter, if Jupiter is in the 6th or 12th house,<-
->the person born becomes poor. || 32 ||<-

If the birth Ascendant is a <term>Movable Sign</term> <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn</note> and is also in a <term>Movable Navamsha</term> <note>A 1/9th divisional chart where the sub-sector is also a movable sign</note>, and is aspected by Saturn and a debilitated Jupiter (situated in Capricorn), then the person born becomes a beggar.

Furthermore, excluding the signs of Jupiter <note>Sagittarius and Pisces</note>, if Jupiter is placed in the 6th or 12th house, the person born becomes poor. This implies that if Jupiter is in its own signs, even if in the 6th or 12th house, it does not cause poverty. || 32 ||

If the Ascendant is in a movable sign and movable Navamsha, and is aspected by Saturn and debilitated Jupiter, the subject becomes a beggar. If Jupiter is not in its own sign but is in the 6th or 12th house, the subject becomes poor. Here it should be specifically noted that if Jupiter is in its own home, it is not harmful. (Commentary by Sudhakar Sharma) || 32 ||

-> If a person is born when a **fixed sign** is in the ascendant, and all **malefic planets** are situated in the angles or trines, while the **benefic planets** are outside the angles, he will eat the food of beggary and be supported by others. (33) <-

If a **fixed sign** <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius</note> is in the ascendant (the 1st house), and all **malefics** (cruel planets) are in the **angles or trines** <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, 10th, 5th, or 9th houses</note>, and all **benefics** (gentle planets) are outside the angles—meaning they are in the **succedent** or **cadent** houses <term>Panaphara/Apoklima: houses 2, 5, 8, 11 and 3, 6, 9, 12 respectively</term>—then the person born will be a "beggar-eater," earning a living through solicitation and being maintained by others. (33)

*If birth occurs in a fixed ascendant, all malefics are in angles/trines, and benefics are outside the angles, that person eats by begging and is raised by others.* (33)

-> If a person is born at night with a **movable sign** in the ascendant, and the **benefic planets** are in the trines or angles but lack strength, while the **malefic planets** are outside the angles, he constantly resorts to eating the food of beggary. (34) <-

At night, if a **movable sign** <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn</note> is the ascendant, and the **benefics** are **weak** (lacking essential power) while situated in the trines or angles (5th, 9th, 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses), and the **malefics** are outside the angles (in the succedent or cadent houses), then the person born constantly—at all times—resorts to begging. A person born under such a combination always eats the food of alms. (34)

*If it is a night birth with a movable ascendant, benefics are weak in the trines/angles, and malefics are not in the angles, the person makes a living by begging every day.* (34)

-> Malefics in their **signs of depression** make one a performer of evil deeds; benefics in their **signs of depression** make one a hidden sinner. If Jupiter is in its sign of depression in the house of action, or if Mars is in its sign of depression in the house of children, the result is the same. (35) <-

If at the time of birth the **malefics** (Sun, Mars, Saturn, or the waning Moon) are in their **signs of depression** <term>Neecha: the zodiac sign where a planet is at its weakest</term>, the person becomes a performer of evil deeds. If the **benefics** are in their signs of depression, the person is a "hidden sinner," committing sins in secret. If **Jupiter** is in its sign of depression <note>Capricorn</note> in the **house of action** (the 10th house—this occurs in an Aries ascendant), or if **Mars** is in its sign of depression <note>Cancer</note> in the **house of children** (the 5th house—this occurs in a Pisces ascendant), the result is the same: the person becomes a performer of evil deeds. (35)

*If all malefics are depressed, the person is a sinner. If benefics are depressed, they are a secret sinner. If Jupiter is depressed in the 10th or Mars is depressed in the 5th, the person is a sinner.* (35)

-> Planets reaching their **signs of exaltation** but placed in **depressed divisional charts** quickly give the person lowly results. Planets in their **signs of depression** but placed in **exalted divisional charts** produce auspicious results. (36) <-

Planets (whether benefic or malefic) that have reached their **exaltation signs** <term>Ucha: the sign where a planet is strongest</term> but are in a **depressed Navamsha** <note>the 1/9th divisional chart used for fine-tuning strength</note>—meaning they are in an exaltation sign but a depression division—will quickly give the person "lowly" or inauspicious results. Conversely, if those planets are in their **signs of depression** but are in an **exalted Navamsha** (reaching the division of their exaltation sign while in a depressed sign), they will produce **auspicious** or good results for the person. As is also stated in the *Sarvartha Chintamani*:

> "The lords of planets who are in depression at birth but in their exalted divisions bring fortune equal to a King. Even if in exaltation, if they are in depressed divisions, the planets do not produce such fortune."

---

In this context, other **combinations for poverty** <term>Daridra Yoga</term> are also written:

> If the Lord of Wealth is with a malefic, and the House of Wealth is occupied by a malefic, and the Lord of Wealth is combust <note>hidden by the Sun's light</note>, the man is devoid of riches.
> When the Lord of Wealth is in the 6th, 8th, or 12th house, and the House of Wealth is joined by a malefic, the man is indeed penniless.

# Chapter 6: The Chapter on the Cancellation of Birth Fortunes
-> <note>Sanskrit: Jatakabhanga-adhyaya</note> <-

If the lord of the first house <term>Ascendant; the sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</term> is located in the twelfth house <note>the house of loss</note>, or is specifically joined with a cruel planet, or is weak and combust <term>hidden by the sun's glare</term>, and the benefic planets are also weak, the person born becomes destitute.

When the lord of the Ascendant is devoid of strength and the lord of wealth <note>the 2nd house lord</note> is combust, while strong cruel planets occupy the angles <term>the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</term>, the human born will be poor.

If the house of wealth is joined with a cruel planet and is aspected by a cruel planet, and the lord of wealth is joined with the Sun, one will be struck by poverty.

Again, if the house of wealth is joined with a cruel planet and aspected by a cruel planet, and the lord of wealth is in the third house, the person is known by the name "Poor."

If malefic planets are in the four angles and a malefic is situated in the house of wealth, one should recognize this as a Poverty Yoga <term>a specific planetary combination</term>, which brings about the ruin of one's own lineage.

* If Saturn is joined with the Sun and also joined with Venus, then this Poverty Yoga will dry up even existing wealth. (36)

<margin>If a planet in its sign of exaltation <note>highest strength</note> is in a debilitated <note>weakest</note> division in the <term>Navamsha; the 1/9th divisional chart</term>, it quickly gives low results to the native. If it is in its sign of debilitation but in an exalted division, it gives auspicious results.</margin>

### The Results of Poverty Yoga

> One becomes unfortunate, with impaired senses, of wicked intellect, censured by wife and children, eating food obtained by begging, living in difficult circumstances, speaking harshly, and devoted only to filling the belly and carnal desires.
>
> Intent on earning through injustice every day, speaking with malice, being a "thorn" to others, the heart always attached to the wives of others, lowly, blind, mute, or dull-witted. (37)
>
> Born in Poverty Yoga, one becomes fond of quarrels, a leper, a destroyer of the well-being of others, ungrateful, a talkative person, devoid of devotion to priests <note>original: "Bhusura," meaning "gods of the earth" or Brahmins</note>, joined with a wicked wife, and having diseased nails. (38)

Now, in these two verses, the results of the previously mentioned Poverty Yogas are told in summary. These two verses have clear meanings. (37-38)

A person born in Poverty Yoga is luckless, has sensory defects, a crooked mind, is blamed by his family, lives on alms, stays in bad conditions, uses foul language, is obsessed with eating and lust, gathers wealth through daily injustice, speaks harshly, is troublesome, always desires others' wives, is base, blind, mute, or stupid, loves conflict, suffers from skin diseases, harms others' interests, is ungrateful, talks too much, lacks faith in the learned, has a bad spouse, and has ugly nails. (37-38)

### The Yogas of Servitude
-> <note>Sanskrit: Preshya Yoga; combinations indicating one who serves others</note> <-

If the Sun is in the 10th house, the Moon in the 7th, Saturn in the 4th, Mars in the 3rd, and Jupiter is in the 2nd house while a movable sign is on the Ascendant, one born at night will be a worker for others. (39)

If Venus is in the 9th, the Moon in the 7th, and Jupiter is the lord of the 2nd or the Ascendant, or if the lord of the 8th is in the 10th and a fixed sign is on the Ascendant, the fears of servitude arise. (40)

If the lord of the Ascendant is at a "junction" <term>Sandhi; the border between two signs</term> at night, and a malefic planet is in an angle, one becomes a servant. If Saturn, Moon, Jupiter, and Venus are in the sky in angles or trines, and are at junctions while a fixed sign is ascending, the same occurs. (41)

If Jupiter is in the "Airavata" division <note>a highly auspicious divisional strength</note> at a junction, and the Moon is in an excellent division but outside the angles, and it is the dark fortnight of the month at night with Venus in the Ascendant, one lives by the work of others. (42)

One becomes a servant if Mars, Jupiter, and the Sun are at the junctions of the 6th, 4th, and 10th houses. If the Moon is in a malefic division but an auspicious sign, and Jupiter is in the Ascendant, one will be a worker for others. (43)

If Jupiter is in Capricorn <note>original: "Mriganana," the deer-faced sign</note>, and the Moon is in the 4th house while other planets are in the 6th, 8th, and 12th houses, the person born always enters into the service of others. (44)

# From the Commentary on Jataka Parijata

Page 180

One attains those combinations for service. When the **Sun** is in the **tenth house**, the **Moon** (lord of the night) is in the **seventh house**, **Saturn** is in the **fourth house**, **Mars** (son of the earth) is in the **third house**, and the **Ascendant** is a **movable sign** (Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn), and **Jupiter** (teacher of the gods) is in the **second house**; a person born at **night** under these conditions becomes a worker for others—a servant. || 39 ||

When **Venus** is in the **ninth house**, the **Moon** is in the **seventh house**, **Jupiter** is the **lord of the second or first house** <note>meaning Jupiter must be the ruler of the wealth house or the ascendant</note>, and **Mars** (son of the earth) is in the **eighth house**, a person born with a **fixed sign** as the Ascendant becomes a servant of great renown. This means that people born under this specific service-combination are endowed with fame and glory.

Now, regarding the phrase "with a fixed Ascendant and Jupiter as the lord of the second or first house": if Scorpio or Aquarius were the Ascendant, then Jupiter could be the lord of the second house. However, with a fixed Ascendant, Jupiter can never be the lord of the first house, because both of Jupiter's signs (Sagittarius and Pisces) are **dual signs** <note>original: "dvidvattva", referring to mutable/common signs</note>. This point should be carefully considered by the learned. || 40 ||

If the birth is at **night**, the **lord of the movable Ascendant** has reached a **junction** <note>original: "sandhi", the transitional point between two zodiac signs, specifically the end of Cancer, Scorpio, or Pisces</note>, and **malefic planets** are situated in the **cardinal houses** <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note>, the person born becomes a servant. Furthermore, if the birth is during the **day**, and **Saturn, the Moon, Jupiter, and Venus** are in the **cardinal or trine houses** (1st, 4th, 7th, 10th, 5th, or 9th) while also being in **junctions**, and the **Ascendant is a fixed sign** (Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius), then the person born will likewise be a servant. || 41 ||

If **Jupiter** is in the **Airavata division** <note>a high-quality divisional strength; see Chapter 1, verses 45-48</note> and is in a **junction**, and the **Moon** is in its own **Varga divisions** <note>see Chapter 1, verse 45</note> but is located **outside the cardinal houses**, and the birth occurs at **night** during the **dark fortnight** with **Venus** in the **Ascendant**, that person lives by the work of others. This means they become another's servant. || 42 ||

If **Mars, Jupiter, and the Sun** have reached the **junctions of the sixth, fourth, and tenth houses** respectively—that is, Mars is at the junction of the 6th, Jupiter at the 4th, and the Sun at the 10th—and the **Moon** is in a **benefic sign** but has entered a **malefic Navamsha** <note>a 1/9th divisional chart segment ruled by a harsh planet</note>, and **Jupiter** is not joined with the **lord of the Ascendant** regardless of where they are placed, the person born is a worker for others—a servant. || 43 ||

When **Jupiter** (the one worshiped by Indra) is in **Capricorn** <note>the sign of its debilitation or lowest strength</note> and that sign happens to be the **sixth, eighth, or twelfth house**, and the **Moon** is in the **fourth house** from the birth Ascendant, the person born constantly and without end remains in **service to others**—they attain a state of servitude. || 44 ||

<margin>If the Sun is in the 10th, Moon in the 7th, Saturn in the 4th, Mars in the 3rd, Jupiter in the 2nd, and the Ascendant is a movable sign (1, 4, 7, 10) at a night birth, it is called Preshya Yoga.</margin>

<margin>If Venus is in the 9th, Moon in the 7th, Mars in the 8th, and Jupiter is the lord of the 1st or 2nd with a fixed Ascendant, it is Preshya Yoga; the servant born is famous.</margin>

<header>Chapter on the Rites of Birth || 6 ||</header>

If the Moon, Jupiter, and Venus are placed in the <term>Kendras</term> <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note> or <term>Trikonas</term> <note>the 1st, 5th, or 9th houses</note> and are located at the <term>Sandhi</term> <note>the junction or border between two signs or houses</note>, and if the <term>Lagna</term> <note>the Ascendant or rising sign</note> is a fixed sign, the native becomes a servant. || 41 ||

If Jupiter is at a junction in the <term>Airavata Amsha</term> <note>a specific high-quality division of a sign in Vedic astrology</note>, the Moon is in an excellent divisional rank but outside the <term>Kendras</term>, the birth occurs during the night of a waning moon, and Venus is in the Ascendant, then the person lives by doing the work of others. || 42 ||

If Mars, Jupiter, and the Sun are situated at the junctions of the 6th, 4th, and 10th houses, the Moon is in a division of a malefic planet, and Jupiter is joined with the Lord of the Ascendant in a benefic sign, then the person will be one who performs the work of others.

If Jupiter is in Capricorn and located in the 6th, 8th, or 12th house <note>these are considered 'dusthana' or difficult houses</note>, and the Moon is in the 4th from the Ascendant, then that native will always be one who performs the work of others. (According to the author of *Surya Jataka*) || 43 ||

->**Now, the results of the Yoga for Servitude.**<-

> A sinful soul, fond of quarrels, harsh in speech, a slanderer of the gods of the earth <note>original: "Bhu-devata," referring to Brahmins</note>,
> Devoid of knowledge and fortune, a lover of wicked pleasures, filled with envy and anger;
> Devoted to lying, jesting, and deception, preoccupied with the genitals and the belly <note>meaning lust and gluttony</note>,
> Pitiful, with an unstable mind, yet clever at enduring insults—such is one born in the Yoga of servitude to others. || 45 ||

Now, the general result of the previously mentioned Yogas for servitude is stated in simple meaning by this verse:

"A sinful soul..." || 45 ||

A person born in the Yoga of servitude is a sinful soul, fond of quarrels, bitter-spoken, a slanderer of Brahmins, devoid of education and luck, wicked, a seeker of base pleasures, possessed of jealousy and anger, a liar, absorbed in cheating, preoccupied with filling his stomach and chasing women, pitiful, of a flickering mind, and clever at bearing insults. || 45 ||

->**Now, the Yogas for Physical Deformity.**<-

> If the birth occurs in Aries, Taurus, or Sagittarius as the Ascendant and it is aspected by a malefic planet, there will be defective teeth.
> If Saturn is in the seventh house, or if Mars is with Rahu <note>the North Node of the Moon</note> in the seventh house and is weak, the person will be physically deformed. || 46 ||

If the birth Ascendant is Aries, Taurus, or Sagittarius, and if it is aspected by—meaning seen by—any malefic planet, the person born will have defective or distorted teeth. Furthermore, if Saturn, or Mars joined with Rahu (Mars-Rahu), is in the seventh house and is weak—meaning devoid of strength—the person born will be physically deformed. The meaning is that some limb of the person born in this Yoga will be missing or impaired. || 46 ||

If the birth is in Aries, Taurus, or Sagittarius Ascendant and a malefic planet looks upon it, the native's teeth will be defective. If Saturn is in the 7th, or if Mars with Rahu is weak in the 7th, the person will be deformed. || 46 ||

> If the Moon is in the tenth from the Ascendant, Mars is in the seventh,
> and the Sun is in the second house, the man will be physically deformed. || 47 ||

If the Moon is in the tenth from the Ascendant, Mars is in the seventh, and the Sun is in the second house, the man will be physically deformed. || 47 ||

# With Commentary on Jataka Parijata

**If Mercury is in a trine <note>the 5th or 9th house</note> and the other planets are devoid of strength, then the mouth, feet, and hands are doubled.**
**One is speechless if the Moon is in Taurus and malefic planets are in the junctions of signs; if aspected by a benefic, one speaks after a long time. || 48 ||**

Now the combinations for doubled limbs and muteness are described. If Mercury is in a trine—meaning situated in the 9th or 5th house from the birth ascendant—and all other planets besides Mercury are weak wherever they may be, the person born will be endowed with double the number of mouths, feet, and hands. This means one born under this alignment would have two faces, four arms, and four legs. If the Moon is in Taurus and malefic planets are in the "sign junctions" <term>Bhasandhi: the transitional points between water and fire signs, specifically the ends of Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces</term>, the person born is speechless, or mute. If in this alignment the Moon is aspected <note>viewed</note> by benefic planets, then the person produces speech after a long time. By implication, if the Moon is aspected by malefics, the person remains mute. If aspected by a mix of planets, the result follows the stronger influence. As stated by Garga:

> When malefics are at the ends of Cancer, Scorpio, or Pisces, and the Moon is in Taurus, one is mute if aspected by malefics; if aspected by benefics, one gains speech after a long time.
> The wise should understand the result according to the strength of the mixed planets. || 48 ||

If Mercury is in a trine <note>5th or 9th</note> from the ascendant and all other planets are weak anywhere, the person's mouth, feet, and hands are doubled—meaning two mouths, 4 feet, and 4 hands. If the Moon is in Taurus and all malefic planets are in the sign junctions, the person will be mute. If in this yoga the Moon is seen by a benefic planet, that person speaks after many days. || 48 ||

**If Saturn and Mars are in a benefic sign-division, one is born with teeth;**
**A hunchback if the Moon is in its own sign in the ascendant and aspected by Saturn and Mars.**
**A cripple if Pisces is in the ascendant and aspected by Saturn, Moon, and Mars;**
**If a malefic and the Moon are in a junction, one is dull-witted, unless there is a benefic aspect. || 49 ||**

Now the birth combinations for being born with teeth, being a hunchback, a cripple, or dull-witted are described. If Saturn and Mars are in a "benefic division"—meaning in a sign of Mercury (Gemini or Virgo) or in a Navamsha <note>a 1/9th sub-division</note> of Mercury—then the person born in this yoga has teeth, appearing with teeth already present at birth. Regarding the hunchback: if the Moon is in its own sign (Cancer) and is in the ascendant, and is aspected by Saturn and Mars, the person born is a hunchback <note>original: "Kubja" or "Koovar", a Dwarf</note>. Regarding the cripple: if Pisces is the rising sign (ascendant) and is aspected by Saturn, the Moon, and Mars, the person born is a cripple <note>original: "Pangu" or "Langra", one with impaired legs</note>. If a malefic (Saturn, Mars, or the Sun) and the Moon are both in a sign junction (the ends of Cancer, Scorpio, or Pisces), the person born is "Jada"—meaning deprived of the sense of hearing, or deaf <note>original: "Dull"</note>. If in these four yogas there is no aspect from benefic planets, only then does the stated result fully manifest. If a benefic aspect exists, the four aforementioned yogas become fruitlless, as stated in the Saravali:

> "...all yogas become fruitless when aspected by benefic planets." || 49 ||

If Saturn and Mars are in the Navamsha of Mercury <note>the 3rd or 6th division</note> in any sign, the child is born with teeth. If the Moon is in its own sign <note>4: Cancer</note> in the ascendant and is aspected by Saturn and Mars, the person will be a hunchback. If the Pisces sign is the birth ascendant and is aspected by Saturn, Moon, and Mars, the person will be a cripple. If the Moon and malefic planets are in the sign junctions and there is no aspect of a benefic planet, the person will be dull <note>deaf</note>. || 49 ||

**If aspected by Saturn, Moon, and Sun, one is a dwarf when the end of Capricorn is the ascendant.**
**With the decanates of the 5th, 9th, and ascendant occupied by malefics, one is without arms, legs, or a head. || 50 ||**

**Mars situated in the decanate of the ascendant, aspected by Saturn, Sun, and Moon,**
**Makes one headless; similarly in the 5th house, it makes one without arms. || 51 ||**

# Page 183
### From the Jataka Manjari: Chapter 6

Now, the combinations for dwarfism and physical deficiencies are described. **Capricorn at the end of the Ascendant** = if the last ninth-part <note>Navamsha</note> of the sign of Capricorn is rising at the birth, and it is **aspected by Saturn, the Moon, and the Sun** = seen by these three planets, the person born is a dwarf with a small body. Regarding the phrase **"Intelligence, Fortune, and Rising"**: Intelligence refers to the 5th house, Fortune to the 9th house, and Rising to the 1st house <note>Lagna</note>. If the decanates <term>Drekkana: a 10-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign</term> occupying these three houses are joined by malefic planets and aspected by Saturn, the Moon, and the Sun, the person born will be without arms, without legs, or without a head, respectively. 

Specifically, if the decanate in the 5th house is joined by the malefic **Mars** <note>original: Angaraka</note> and aspected by the Sun, Moon, and Saturn, the person born is **armless** (without hands). If the decanate in the 9th house is joined by Mars and aspected by the Sun, Moon, and Saturn, the person born is **legless** and meets with misfortune. If Mars is in the decanate of the Ascendant (1st house) and is aspected by Saturn, the Moon, and the Sun, the person born is **headless** (without a head).

As stated by the Sage Garga:
> "Mars in the decanate of the Ascendant, seen by Saturn, the Sun, and the Moon, makes one headless; similarly in the 5th house, one is deprived of arms.
> ->In the 9th house, it causes leglessness, provided no benefic planets aspect the position."<-

It should be understood from Garga’s words "provided no benefic planets aspect" that if there is an aspect from a benefic planet, these negative combinations are cancelled. The explanation of verse 51 is simply a clarification of the decanates in the 5th, 9th, and Ascendant mentioned in verse 50; therefore, no further elaboration is needed. || 50-51 ||

If the Ascendant is the end of Capricorn (27°-30°) and Saturn, the Moon, and the Sun look upon it, one is a dwarf. If the decanates of the 5th, 9th, and Ascendant are joined by malefic planets, the person is respectively without hands, feet, or a head. || 50 ||

If Mars is in the decanate of the Ascendant and Saturn, the Sun, and the Moon see it, one is headless; if this same combination occurs in the 5th, one is handless. (From the author of Sukshma Jataka) || 51 ||

->With the Sun and Moon joined in Leo in the Ascendant, aspected by Mars and Saturn,<-
->one is sightless; if aspected by both benefics and malefics, the eyes are bleary.<-
->The Moon in the house of loss destroys the left eye, and the Sun destroys the other (the right).<-
->These combinations are said to be inauspicious, but become manageable if aspected by benefics.<- || 52 ||

Now, the combinations for impaired vision are described. **Leo as the Ascendant with the Sun and Moon joined** = if the Sun and Moon are in the sign of Leo at the time of birth, and **aspected by Mars and Saturn** = seen by these two, the person born is **sightless** (blind). In that same combination, if they are **aspected by both benefics and malefics**, the person born has **bleary eyes** <gloss>Blear eyed</gloss> = eyes that are inflamed or watery. 

Note the following: If only the Sun in the Leo Ascendant is aspected by Mars and Saturn, then the right eye is blind; if aspected by a mix of planets, the right eye is bleary. If only the Moon in the Leo Ascendant is aspected by Mars and Saturn, the left eye is blind; if aspected by both benefics and malefics, the left eye is bleary. Regarding **"the house of loss"**: If the Moon is in the house of loss from the Ascendant (the 12th house), it destroys the **left eye**. Then the person born is blind in the left eye. The Sun in the house of loss destroys the **other** = the right eye. Regarding **"not said to be auspicious"**: All the previously mentioned combinations are inauspicious = they give bad results. However, if they are **aspected by benefics** = seen by benefic planets, they become **manageable** <note>original: yapya</note>. This means they do not give the full negative result but only a partial one. This is also stated in the *Saravali*:

> ->If at the time of conception or birth the Sun and Moon are in Leo in the Ascendant,<-
> ->and are seen by Mars and Saturn, one is born blind.<-
> ->If the Sun and Moon are seen by both fiery (malefic) and benefic planets, they cause bleary eyes.<-
> ->I shall now describe how the destruction of the eyes occurs:<-
> ->The Moon in the 12th house destroys the left eye if it is weak.<-
> ->The Sun likewise destroys the other; if aspected by benefics, these conditions are mitigated.<-

**Notes—** These previously mentioned verses are a summary from the *Brihat Jataka* regarding considerations for the time of conception; however, since the same text notes "at birth, at conception, or at the time of inquiry," these should also be considered at the time of birth. || 51 ||

If the Sun and Moon are in the Leo ascendant and are aspected <note>Aspected: In astrology, when one planet "looks at" or influences another from a specific distance.</note> by Mars and Saturn, the child will be sightless. If both auspicious and inauspicious planets aspect them, the eyes will be like bubbles <note>Likely referring to cataracts or protruding eyes</note>. If the Moon is in the 12th house, it destroys the left eye, and if the Sun is there, it destroys the right eye. These combinations occur due to the influence of inauspicious planets. Here, the influence of auspicious planets reduces the severity of the result. || 52 ||

### A man is brave, sluggish, and has distorted vision if the Sun is in the ascendant; if in Aries (its exaltation), he has diseased eyes; if in Leo, he is night-blind; if in Libra, he is impoverished; and if the Sun is in the Cancer ascendant, he has bubble-like eyes. || 53 ||

Now, the combinations for eye disorders based on the position of the Sun are described. When the Sun is in the ascendant at the time of birth, the person born is brave = <term>a warrior</term>, sluggish (one who performs tasks slowly), and has "middle vision" or squinted eyes. This is the general result of the Sun in the ascendant. The specific variations for the Sun in Aries, Leo, Libra, and Cancer ascendants are now stated. If the Sun is in the Aries ascendant (its sign of exaltation), the person has diseased eyes. If the Sun shines in the Leo ascendant, the person born is blind at night (nyctalopia). If the Sun is in the Libra ascendant (its sign of debilitation), the person born is impoverished = poor. If the Sun is in the Cancer ascendant, the person born has bubble-like eyes = <gloss>eyes with white spots or cataracts</gloss>. As stated in the *Brihat Jataka*:
> "Brave, sluggish, with impaired vision, and heartless when the Sun is in the body (ascendant); in Aries, he has healthy but dim vision; in Leo, he is night-blind; in its fall (Libra), he is blind and lowly; in the house of the Moon (Cancer), he has bubble-eyes; in the second house, he has much wealth but it is seized by the king, and he suffers from mouth diseases."

If the Sun is in the birth ascendant, the person is brave (fond of battle), sluggish (a slow worker), and has distorted vision. If the Sun is in the Aries ascendant, there is disease in the eyes. With the Sun in the Leo ascendant, one becomes <term>night-blind</term>. If the Sun is in the Libra ascendant, one is poor. If the Sun is in the Cancer ascendant, the eyes are very small. || 53 ||

### If the Sun and Moon are together or separate in the 12th house, they take away the left and right eyes. Malefics in the 6th and 8th houses also destroy them—the left in the 6th and the right in the 8th. || 54 ||

If the Sun and Moon are together in the 12th house from the ascendant, they destroy both eyes of the person born. If those same Sun and Moon are in the 12th house separately, they take away the right and left eyes respectively; meaning, if only the Sun is in the 12th, it destroys the right eye, and if only the Moon is in the 12th, it destroys the left eye. Regarding <term>the 6th and 8th houses</term>: Malefics = inauspicious planets situated in the 6th and 8th houses destroy the eyes. There, malefics in the 6th house destroy the left eye, and malefics in the 8th house destroy the right eye. So it is also said in the *Sarvartha Chintamani*:
> If the Sun and Moon are in the 12th house and lack the influence of auspicious periods, the person becomes blind. If only one of them is in the 12th without auspicious influence, the person becomes one-eyed.

It should be understood from the statements in *Sarvartha Chintamani* that if there is an aspect from an auspicious planet on these combinations, the negative result does not occur.
If both the Sun and Moon are in the 12th house, one is blind in both eyes. If only the Sun is in the 12th, the right eye is blind, and if only the Moon is in the 12th, the left eye is blind. If malefic planets (Mars, Saturn, Rahu, Ketu, Sun) are in the 6th or 8th houses, the eyes become blind. Here too, malefics in the 6th destroy the left eye and in the 8th destroy the right eye. || 54 ||

### If the Sun is in the ascendant or the 7th house and is joined or aspected by the son of the Sun (Saturn), it quickly destroys his right eye; but if joined by the son of the Moon (Mercury) and Saturn, it destroys the left. || 55 ||

The Sun in the ascendant or the 7th house, if joined or aspected by Saturn <unclear>if it is so</unclear>, then the right eye of that person is quickly...

# Chapter 6: Chapter on the Destruction of Fortunes ##

...would destroy or ruin. If that same Sun is located in the Ascendant <note>Lagna: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</note> or the seventh house, and is joined by Rahu <note>the North Node of the Moon</note> and the Son of the Earth <note>Mars</note>, then it destroys the left eye. || 55 ||

If the Sun is in the Ascendant or the 7th house and is aspected by Saturn, or if Saturn is with the Sun, it destroys the right eye of the person born. If the Sun in the Ascendant or 7th house is joined with Rahu and Mars, it destroys the left eye. (According to the author of *Suryasiddhanta* or similar authority) || 55 ||

> If the Lord of Day <note>the Sun</note> and the Moon have gone to the twelfth house, and the malefic planets are in the sixth, eighth, and twelfth houses; a malefic in the sixth house destroys the left eye, while one in the eighth house destroys the eye of the right side. || 56 ||

"The Lord of Day and the Moon" refers to the Sun and Moon. If they are in the twelfth house from the birth Ascendant, and similarly the "non-benign" <note>malefic</note> planets are in the houses of enemies (6th), death (8th), and loss (12th)—the word "but" here indicates an alternative case—then both eyes of the person born are destroyed. "Destroys" means: a malefic planet in the sixth house destroys the left eye. Likewise, a malefic in the eighth house destroys the right eye, and so on. This verse carries the same meaning as verse 54. || 56 ||

Or, if the Sun and Moon are in the twelfth, and there are malefics in the 6th, 8th, and 12th houses, then the planet in the 6th house destroys the left eye and the planet in the 8th house destroys the right eye. || 56 ||

> If Mars is the Lord of the Second House and is in the eighth from the Sun and Moon (when they are together), and the Son of the Sun <note>Saturn</note> is in the house of enemies or loss (6th or 12th) from the Sun and Moon, the person is blind. If the Moon is in the eighth, twelfth, or sixth house, and Saturn is with Mars, the person's sight is destroyed. || 57 ||

"Mars etc.": If Mars is the Lord of the Second House <note>the house of wealth and face</note> and is in the eighth (death) house from the Sun and Moon (when they are in the same place), and Saturn is in the 6th or 12th from the Sun and Moon, the person born is blind. "Eighth etc.": If the Moon is in the 6th, 8th, or 12th house from the Ascendant, and Saturn is joined with Mars at birth, the person born becomes "sightless" (deprived of eyes).

If Mars is the Lord of the Second and is in the 8th house from the Sun and Moon, and Saturn is in the 6th or 12th house, the person born is blind. If the Moon is in the 8th, 12th, or 6th house and Saturn is with Mars, then the eyes are destroyed! (According to the author of *Suryasiddhanta*) || 57 ||

> If the Moon is in the sixth, the Sun in the eighth, Saturn in the house of loss (12th) from the Ascendant, and Mars is in the house of wealth (2nd), then even Indra <note>the King of Gods</note> would surely become blind. || 58 ||

"Sixth etc.": If the Moon is in the 6th from the Ascendant, the Sun in the 8th, Saturn in the 12th, and Mars in the 2nd house, a man born under this combination—even if he were equal to the great Indra—will surely (certainly) be blind. And so it is said in the *Brihat Jataka*:

> When the Sun, Moon, Mars, and Saturn are situated in the eighth, sixth, second, and twelfth houses in any manner, they cause blindness in men through the afflictions of these powerful planets. || 58 ||

<header>From the Jataka Parijata with Commentary</header>

...If the Moon is in the 6th house, the Sun in the 8th, Saturn in the 12th from the Ascendant, and Mars in the 2nd, then by this yoga even <term>Indra</term><note>The king of the gods; used here to emphasize that even the most powerful person cannot escape the karma of the stars.</note> would surely be blind. ॥ 58 ॥

->**If the Lord of the Wealth house is with the Lord of the Ascendant in a bad house, there is loss of eyes; or if the Lord of the Wealth house is with Venus and the Moon in the Ascendant.**<-
->**If the Lord of the Eyes is in the Ascendant, one is night-blind; but if it is in its exaltation or with a benefic planet, they say it is not so.**<- ॥ 59 ॥

*Commentary:* "If the Lord of the Wealth house"—meaning the Lord of the 2nd house—is with the Lord of the Ascendant in a "bad house" (the 6th, 8th, or 12th), then one should predict the destruction of the eyes for the native. "Or"—meaning subsequently—if the "Lord of the Eyes" (the Lord of the 2nd house) is with <term>Asphujit</term><note>original: "Asphujit" - a classical name for the planet Venus.</note> and the Moon in the Ascendant, the person becomes "night-blind" <gloss>Night blind</gloss>. However, if that Lord of the 2nd house is in its "exaltation" <note>The sign where a planet is at its maximum strength.</note> and joined by a benefic planet, the wise say such blindness does not occur. ॥ 59 ॥

*Hindi Translation:* If the Lord of the 2nd house is joined with the Lord of the Ascendant and placed in the 6th, 8th, or 12th, the eyes will be blind. If the Lord of the 2nd is in the Ascendant with Venus and the Moon, the native will be night-blind. If that Lord of the 2nd is in an exalted sign or aspected by a benefic planet, it will not be so, meaning the eyes will be good. (Sudha-Shalinikar) ॥ 29 ॥ <note>The numbering 29 likely refers to a specific sub-commentary's sequence.</note>

### Now, the Yogas for Diseases:

->**If Rahu is in the Ascendant with Mars or Saturn, the ancients say it causes "Large Seed" (enlarged scrotum).**<-
->**If the Lord of the Ascendant is in the 8th house with Rahu or with Gulika, the same should be said.**<- ॥ 60 ॥
->**If Rahu is in the Ascendant, Gulika in a trine, and Mars with Saturn in the 8th, it is the same.**<-
->**If the Lord of the Navamsha occupied by the Lord of the Ascendant is with Rahu, Mars, or Gulika, it is the same.**<- ॥ 61 ॥

*Commentary:* Now, some yogas for diseases are described. "If Rahu is in the Ascendant" with Mars, or if Saturn is in the Ascendant with Rahu, the learned elders say the native will have <term>Brihad-beeja</term><note>original: "Brihad-beeja" - literally "large seed," referring to scrotal swelling or Hydrocele.</note>. "If the Lord of the Ascendant" is in the 8th house with Rahu, or with <term>Mandi</term><note>original: "Mandi/Gulika" - a mathematical point in the sky considered a "son of Saturn" and generally malefic.</note> in the 8th house (the word "and" here indicates another variation), the same should be said, meaning the native will have an enlarged scrotum. ॥ 60 ॥

"In the Ascendant"—if Rahu is in the birth Ascendant and Gulika is in a "trine" (the 5th or 9th from the Ascendant), and Mars with Saturn is in the 8th house, then likewise <term>Brihad-beeja</term> should be predicted. "The Lord of the Navamsha"—the Lord of the <term>Navamsha</term><note>A 1/9th divisional chart used for fine-tuning predictions.</note> occupied by the Lord of the Ascendant—if he is joined with Rahu, Mars, or Gulika (meaning joined with any malefic), then the same result as mentioned before (enlarged scrotum) should be known. ॥ 61 ॥

*Hindi Translation:* If Rahu is in the Ascendant with Mars or Saturn, the native has <term>Brihad-beeja</term> (large scrotum). If the Lord of the Ascendant is in the 8th house with Rahu or Gulika, the native has <term>Brihad-beeja</term>. ॥ 60 ॥

If the Ascendant is with Rahu, Gulika is in a trine, and Mars is in the 8th with Saturn, then <term>Brihad-beeja</term> occurs. If the Lord of the Navamsha occupied by the Lord of the Ascendant is with Rahu, Mars, or Gulika, it is <term>Brihad-beeja</term>. ॥ 61 ॥

### Now he describes the yoga for an unstable or insane intellect:

> If the Sun and Moon are in the Ascendant or a trine, and Jupiter is in the third house or a quadrant, the person born at that time will have an insane intellect, especially if the Ascendant is at the beginning of Sagittarius. || 80 ||

"In the Ascendant or a trine" means: if the Ascendant is at the beginning of Sagittarius <note>original: *sharasana-adau*</note>, and the Sun and Moon <note>original: *dinanatha-chandrau*</note> are in the 1st, 5th, or 9th houses, and Jupiter is in the 3rd house <note>original: *shaurya*</note> or a quadrant <note>1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note>, then the person born at that time possesses an insane intellect. This means the person born under this influence lacks a stable or receptive mind.

In the fourth line, instead of "if the Ascendant is at the beginning of Sagittarius," the author of the *Sarvartha Chintamani* <note>A famous 13th-century astrological treatise</note> reads "if the birth occurs on a Saturday or Tuesday." Similarly, in the *Jatakadesha*:

> If the Sun and Moon are in the 9th or 5th houses, and Jupiter is in the 3rd or a quadrant, and the birth occurs on a Saturday or Tuesday, the person will be fickle and like one insane.

Thus, in that version, the interpretation is the same except for the requirement of birth on a Saturday or Tuesday. || 80 ||

-> If the Sun and Moon are in the Ascendant or a trine, Jupiter is in the 3rd or a quadrant, and the Ascendant is in the beginning of Sagittarius, the native has an insane intellect. || 80 || <-

### Now he describes the yogas for mental confusion, dullness, and alcoholism:

> If Mercury and the Moon are in a quadrant but lack auspicious divisions, there will be confusion. If Saturn, the Moon, and the Sun are in a quadrant, the person will be dull-witted and a consumer of intoxicants. || 81 ||

"In a quadrant" means: if Mercury and the Moon are in the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses and lack auspicious divisions <note>original: *saumyamsha-hinau*</note>—meaning they are placed in the <term>Navamsha</term> <note>a 1/9th divisional chart used for fine-tuning strength</note> of malefic planets—then the native will suffer from <term>Aberration of the mind</term> <note>mental confusion or wandering</note>. If Saturn, the Moon, and the Sun are all in quadrants, the person born under this yoga will be dull-witted <note>original: *jada*</note> and a consumer of honey <note>a euphemism for wine or liquor</note>. || 81 ||

-> If Mercury and the Moon are in a quadrant or lack auspicious divisions, that man is possessed by confusion. If Saturn, the Moon, and the Sun are in a quadrant, the native is a drinker of wine and dull-witted. || 81 || <-

### Now he describes the yogas for secret diseases and throat diseases:

> If the Moon is with Saturn and in the Navamsha of Cancer, Aquarius, or Scorpio, there is secret disease. If the Moon is in the fourth house, in its own Navamsha, and joined by malefics, there is throat disease. || 82 ||

"With Saturn" means: if the Moon is joined by Saturn and placed in the Navamsha of Cancer, Aquarius, or Scorpio, the person born will have a secret disease <note>original: *guhyarogi*</note>, meaning a disease in the private parts. Regarding the Moon: if the Moon is in the "happiness" house <note>the 4th house</note>, in the Navamsha of that same house, and joined by malefic planets, the native will have a throat disease. || 82 ||

-> If the Moon is with Saturn in the Navamsha of Cancer, Aquarius, or Scorpio, one has a secret disease. If the Moon is in the 4th house or its division and joined by a malefic planet, one has a throat disease. || 82 || <-

### Now, the combinations for leprosy and skin diseases are described:

> Excluding the Lord of the Ascendant, if other planets are situated in the Ascendant, one should predict skin disease.
> If Saturn is there, it is blue; if the Sun, it is red; if Mars, it is white.
> If the Moon is in the <term>Navamsha</term><note>A 1/9th divisional chart sign</note> of Cancer, Pisces, or Capricorn, and is joined by Saturn or Mars, and lacks the aspect or association of beneficial planets, one should predict skin disease for the person. || 86 ||

**Excluding:** This means setting aside the Lord of the Ascendant (<term>Lagnapati</term>). If other planets are located in the Ascendant at the time of birth, the person will suffer from skin disease. It should be understood that if the Lord of the Ascendant itself is in the Ascendant, skin disease does not occur. Regarding the types of skin disease: if Saturn (<term>Bhanusuta</term>, "Son of the Sun") is in the Ascendant, it is "blue" leprosy; if the Sun (<term>Chandakirana</term>, "The Hot-Rayed One") is in the Ascendant, it is "red" leprosy; if Mars (<term>Bhumija</term>, "Son of the Earth") is in the Ascendant, it is "white" leprosy (vitiligo). Furthermore, if the Moon is in the Navamsha of Cancer, Pisces, or Capricorn and is joined by Saturn or Mars, and is without the influence of "gentle" (beneficial) planets by association or aspect, then the person born will suffer from <term>Kushtha</term> <note>original: "कोढ़-चरकादि" - refers to leprosy or chronic skin conditions like psoriasis</note>. || 86 ||

Excluding the Lord of the Ascendant, if other malefic planets are in the Ascendant, the person will have skin disease. If it is Saturn, call it blue; if the Sun, red; if Mars, white. If the Moon is joined with Saturn or Mars in the Navamsha of Cancer, Pisces, or Capricorn without beneficial influence, call it skin disease. || 86 ||

### Now, another combination for diseases of the private parts is described:

> If the Moon is joined with a malefic in the sign occupied by the Lord of the Eighth House, and the Lord of the Eighth is aspected by Rahu, the person suffers from secret diseases.
> Likewise, if the Eighth House is occupied by four or three malefic planets; however, if joined by a beneficial planet, the person remains free from disease. || 87 ||

**Joined with a malefic:** If the Moon is with any malefic planet in the sign belonging to the Lord of the Eighth House (<term>Randhrapa</term>). And if the Lord of the Eighth House is aspected by "the Serpent" (<term>Sarpa</term>, meaning Rahu), the person born will have a "secret disease" (<term>Guhyaroga</term>) <note>Refers to ailments of the private organs or rectum</note>. Regarding the Eighth House: if it contains four or three malefic planets, the same result (secret disease) occurs. However, if a "gentle" (beneficial) planet is present in that combination, the person will be healthy and free from disease. || 87 ||

If the Moon, joined by a malefic, is in the sign of the Lord of the Eighth, and Rahu looks upon the Lord of the Eighth, the person will have a secret disease (such as hemorrhoids/piles). If the eighth house has four or three malefics, the result is the same. If a benefic is present, the disease does not occur. || 87 ||

### Now, the combinations for urinary painfulness and blood diseases are told:

> If the Moon is in a watery sign and its Lord is in the Sixth House, and is aspected by planets in watery signs, there is difficulty in urination.
> If the Moon is in the Eighth or Sixth House aspected by Mars, and Saturn is in the Ascendant, the person suffers from blood disease. || 88 ||

**Watery sign:** If the Moon is in a watery sign <note>Cancer, Scorpio, or Pisces</note> and the Lord of that sign is in the Sixth House, and it is aspected by planets situated in watery signs (the second half of Capricorn, Cancer, or Pisces), the person suffers from <term>Mutrakricchra</term> <note>Painful or difficult urination/dysuria</note>. **Defeat:** If the Moon is in the Eighth (<term>Paribhava</term>) or Sixth (<term>Ripu</term>) house and is aspected by Mars, and the Ascendant is joined by Saturn (<term>Ravisuta</term>), the person attains a blood-born disease. As stated in the *Sarvartha Chintamani*:

> "When the Moon is in a watery sign and the Lord of that house is in the sixth,
> aspected by a planet in a watery sign, one should predict urinary difficulty." || 88 ||

### Now, he describes indigestion and jaundice—

> If the lord of the eighth house is weak, and the Ascendant is aspected by malefic planets, and the eighth house is aspected by Saturn, the person born will suffer from a disease that obstructs eating. If the Moon is with Mars in the sixth house, one suffers from jaundice caused by vomiting and dizziness. If the Sun, Moon, and Mars are together in the sixth house, the person suffers from colic and spreading skin eruptions. || 62 ||

**Born etc.** The lord of the eighth house <note>original: "randhreshvara"</note> is **weak** = lacking strength; the **Ascendant** = the rising sign at birth is **aspected by malefic planets** = seen by them; and the **eighth house** <note>original: "paribhavasthana"</note> is **aspected by Saturn** = combined with the sight of Saturn; then the person born will certainly be struck by **a disease obstructing the consumption of food** (a blockage in the throat during eating). Likewise, in the *Prashna Marga*:

> "The Ascendant aspected by a malefic, the eighth house aspected by Saturn, and the lord of the eighth house without strength—this combination causes obstruction to eating."

**Vomiting, dizziness, etc.** When **with Mars** = joined with the planet Mars, and the **Moon is in the house of enemies** = situated in the sixth house, one acquires **jaundice** <note>original: "pandu," often referring to anemia or liver disorders like jaundice</note> arising from vomiting and dizziness. When the **Sun, Moon, and Mars are joined** = situated together in the sixth house, the person born **suffers from colic and spreading eruptions** = a spreading of pain and skin sores; as the *Amarakosha* dictionary states: "Prasara means spreading." He attains = receives this. || 62 ||

If the lord of the 8th is weak, the Ascendant is aspected by malefics, and the 8th house is aspected or occupied by Saturn, the native is struck by the disease of food-obstruction (food getting stuck in the throat). If the Moon is with Mars in the house of enemies (6th), there is jaundice from wind disorders. If the Sun, Moon, and Mars are in the 6th house, the native has colic. (Author of Sudhashalini) || 62 ||

Furthermore, if **Mars** <note>original: "avanina," literally 'son of the earth'</note> is **with the lord of the Ascendant** and situated in the **Ascendant** = the birth sign, and the **lord of the enemies** = the lord of the sixth house is in a **quadrant (1, 4, 7, 10)** or in the **Ascendant**, **the same occurs**, meaning an illness caused by sorcery should be declared. || 63 ||

## From the Commentary on Jataka Parijata

When the Sun or Mars occupies the 12th house <note>the house of loss and expenditure</note>, the Moon is in the 6th house <note>the house of enemies and disease</note>, Saturn is in the 8th house <note>the house of death and longevity</note>, and the Lord of the Ascendant <term>Lagnasha: the planet ruling the rising sign</term> is placed in a harmful division <term>Papamsha: a Navamsha or 1/9th subdivision ruled by a malefic planet</term>, the person born will suffer from chronic nasal catarrh <term>Pinasa: a severe or chronic congestion/sinusitis</term>. 

Similarly, in the *Sarvartha Chintamani* <note>a classical 17th-century astrological treatise</note>:
> With the Moon in the 6th, Saturn in the 8th, a malefic in the 12th, and the Lord of the Ascendant joined with a malefic division, one should predict chronic nasal disease.
> If Saturn is in the 6th house with Gulika <note>a mathematical point considered a "shadow planet" with a cruel nature</note> and is aspected by <note>looked upon by</note> the Sun, Mars, or Rahu, and lacks the aspect or association of benefic planets, the person will suffer from asthma, cough, and consumption <note>tuberculosis or wasting diseases</note>. || 96 ||

If Saturn is with Gulika in the 6th house and is aspected by the Sun, Mars, and Rahu, and is devoid of the influence of auspicious planets, the native will have diseases related to cough, asthma, and consumption. If a malefic planet is in the 12th house, the Moon in the 6th, and Saturn in the 8th, and the Lord of the Ascendant is in a malefic subdivision anywhere, the native suffers from chronic nasal catarrh. (According to the author of *Sushloka-Shataka*) || 96 ||

-> Now he describes two combinations for dropsy and long-term illness: <-

> If Saturn is in Cancer and the Moon is in Capricorn, the person born suffers from dropsy <term>Jalodara: abdominal swelling due to fluid accumulation</term>.
> If Saturn is with Mars in the 6th house, aspected by the Sun and Rahu, and the Lord of the Ascendant is weak, the person becomes a long-term sufferer of disease. || 97 ||

**Commentary:** "Mande" refers to Saturn. When Saturn is in the sign of Cancer and the Moon is in Capricorn, the person born suffers from dropsy. "Sare" means with Mars. When Saturn is with Mars in the 6th house and is aspected by the Sun and Rahu, and the Lord of the Ascendant is weak <note>lacking "Shadbala" or positional strength</note>, the person becomes a "Dirgharogi"—one who remains ill for a very long time. 

Similarly, in the *Sarvartha Chintamani*:
> When Saturn and Mars are together in the 6th house, aspected by the Sun and Rahu, and the Lord of the Ascendant is devoid of strength, the man will be a long-term sufferer. || 97 ||

If Saturn is in Cancer and the Moon is in Capricorn, the native will have dropsy. If Saturn, joined with Mars in the 6th house, is seen by the Sun and Rahu, and the Lord of the Ascendant is weak, he will be chronically ill. || 97 ||

-> Now he describes the combination for short stature: <-

> One is short of stature if Mars is in its own house in the 4th or 3rd, while Mercury and Saturn are in the Ascendant.
> Wise men say the same if Mars is in its own sign, Mercury is in the 4th or 3rd house, and the Lord of the Ascendant is joined with Saturn. || 98 ||

**Commentary:** "Hrasva" means short. If Mars is in its own house (Aries or Scorpio) and is located in the 4th house <note>Sukha-bhava</note> or 3rd house <note>Vikrama-bhava</note>, and Mercury and Saturn are in the Ascendant <note>1st house</note>, the person born will be of short stature. Alternatively, if Mars is in its own sign (1st or 8th), Mercury is in the 4th or 3rd house, and the Lord of the Ascendant is joined with Saturn, the wise say the person will be short. || 98 ||

# Chapter 6: The Chapter on the Cancellation of Birth Fortunes
## Page 166

If Mars is in its own sign <note>Aries or Scorpio</note>, Mercury is in the 4th or 3rd house, and Saturn is in the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</term>, the person born will be short in stature. If Mars is in its own house, Mercury is in the 3rd or 4th, and the Lord of the Ascendant is anywhere with Saturn, the person will also be short. (According to the author of *Sushloka-Gyanakar*) || 98 ||

->**Now, regarding the Horoscope**<-

Now Varahamihira <note>A famous 6th-century Indian astrologer</note> explains the combinations for birth with physical defects and the state of one's spouse in the *Hora* <note>Horoscopy</note>:

> If the Moon and the Sun are situated in the 12th and 6th houses from the Ascendant, they say the birth is of one who, along with his wife, has only one eye.
> If Venus and the Sun are in the 7th, or in the 9th and 5th houses, they desire to call the person one with a deformed spouse. || 66 ||

**Commentary:** "From the Ascendant" means from the birth sign. If the Moon and the Sun are in the 12th and 6th houses—meaning one is in the 12th and the other in the 6th—then the birth is of a "one-eyed person along with his wife." One born under this combination, together with his spouse, attains one-eyedness; the man himself is one-eyed, and his wife is also one-eyed. "In the 7th" means if Venus and the Sun are both in the 7th house from the Ascendant, or both in the 9th, or both in the 5th, the wise call the person "one with a deformed spouse" <note>original: *vikaladara*</note>, meaning a wife with missing or impaired limbs. One born under this combination has a wife with physical disabilities. Thus it is said in the *Saravali* <note>A classic 10th-century astrological text</note>:

> If the Moon and the Sun are in the 12th and 6th houses from the Ascendant, all the sages say the man born will, in sequence, have only one eye along with his wife.
> If Mars and Venus are in the 7th, the man born will have a deformed spouse. The learned should also consider this if they are in the 5th or 9th houses. || 99 ||

If the Moon and the Sun are in the 12th or 6th positions from the Ascendant, the person and his wife each have only one eye. If Venus and the Sun are in the 7th, or in the 9th or 5th, the teachers have said the result is that the wife will have deformed limbs. (According to the author of *Sushloka-Gyanakar*) || 99 ||

---

->**Now he explains the combinations for ear diseases and tooth diseases—**<-

> Malefics <note>planets like Saturn or Mars</note> placed in the 9th, 11th, 3rd, or 5th houses, if not aspected by benefics <note>planets like Jupiter or Venus</note>,
> certainly cause hearing impairment; and in the 7th house, they cause dental deformities. || 100 ||

**Commentary:** "Malefics" refers to the cruel planets. If they are placed in the 9th, 3rd, 11th, or 5th houses and are not "aspected"—meaning seen—by "benefics" or auspicious planets, then by rule they destroy the sense of hearing. If those same malefics are situated in the 7th house from the Ascendant and are not seen by auspicious planets, they cause "dental deformity" <note>original: *radavaikrityakara*</note>, meaning ugliness or irregularity of the teeth. And so it is said in the *Saravali*—

> If Jupiter is in a *Vargottama* <note>Vargottama: a planet occupying the same zodiac sign in both the main chart and the divisional ninth chart, increasing its strength</note> or other auspicious divisions, and is placed in the Ascendant or the fourth house, or is otherwise powerful; and if the other planets are in the second, eleventh, or fourth houses, and the Lord of the Ascendant is strong, the person born attains happiness. || 101 ||

Regarding *Vargottama*: Jupiter being in *Vargottama* or other auspicious divisions—*Vargottamas* are defined as the first, middle, or last portions of movable, fixed, and dual signs respectively, which yield auspicious results. By the word "others," we should include the *Moolatrikona* <note>Moolatrikona: a planet's favorite sign where it is very potent</note> and its own divisions. If Jupiter is so placed in the Ascendant (first house) or the *Rasatala* (fourth house), or is otherwise endowed with strength; and if the other planets are in the houses of wealth, gains, or growth (the second, eleventh, and fourth houses); and the Lord of the Ascendant is powerful, the person born attains happiness. || 101 ||

If Jupiter is in a *Vargottama* or other auspicious division and is in the 1st or 4th house, or is strong, and all other planets are situated in the 2nd, 11th, or 4th houses, and the Lord of the Ascendant is strong, then the person born will experience many kinds of happiness. || 101 ||

### Now, the Chapter on Royal Yogas (Rajayoga) || 7 ||

Now the chapter on Royal Yogas is explained. Herein are described those combinations under which men are born to be kings:

> If planets are situated in Virgo, Pisces, Gemini, Taurus, Leo, Sagittarius, and Aquarius, the person will be a great and famous king, surrounded by armies, intoxicated elephants, and four-fold forces of cavalry. 
> Those born with planets in Libra, Aries, Taurus, and Pisces become lords of the entire earth; if planets are in the centers <note>centers: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</note> of Taurus, Sagittarius, and Pisces, one becomes a world-ruler of great fame. || 1 ||

Regarding "Virgo, Pisces, etc.": Virgo and Pisces are well known; "Human-pair" means Gemini; "Go" means Taurus; "Hari" means Leo; Sagittarius and Aquarius are well known. If the planets are situated in these seven signs according to their possibility, then the man born will be a king—vast, great, and famous—thronged by armies, rutting elephants, and the four-fold military divisions (infantry, cavalry, chariots, and elephants). Those born with planets in Libra, Aries, Taurus, and Pisces become lords of the whole...

# Chapter on Royal Yogas || 7 ||

Lord of Fortune = He becomes the lord of the entire earth. Now, if all planets are situated in the <term>Kendras</term> <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses of a horoscope, considered the pillars of strength</note> specifically in the signs of Taurus, Sagittarius, and Pisces—Taurus is the Bull, Sagittarius is the Bow, and Pisces is the Final sign—then the person born becomes a man of vast fame = extremely renowned, and a Lord of the Earth, a King. || 1 ||

If all planets are situated in the signs of Virgo, Pisces, Gemini, Taurus, Leo, Sagittarius, and Aquarius, then that person becomes a famous king endowed with armies, intoxicated elephants, and herds of horses. He whose birth time has all planets in Libra, Aries, Taurus, and Pisces becomes the master of the entire globe. He whose birth time has all planets situated in Taurus, Sagittarius, and Pisces, and they are in the <term>Kendras</term>, becomes a king. || 1 ||

->One born when all planets are in Virgo, Aries, Libra, Leo, and Aquarius becomes a protector of the earth.<-
->When planets are in the third, fifth, and fourth houses, he becomes the ruler of many wealthy lands.<-
->If three planets are in the third, fourth, and fifth houses, two are in the second and ninth,<-
->and the remaining two are in the first and seventh houses, he becomes a righteous king.<- || 2 ||

One born with all planets in Virgo, Aries, Libra, Leo, and Aquarius becomes a protector of the earth, a king. <term>Duschikya</term> = the third house, <term>Pratibha</term> = the fifth house, <term>Rasatala</term> = the fourth house; by planets being in these, he becomes a ruler of many wealthy lands = the master of many riches and countries. Now, if three planets are in the third, fourth, and fifth houses. And if two planets are situated in the second and ninth houses. And the remaining two are in the first and seventh houses, then the one born becomes a righteous king. Here this is said: if all seven planets are situated individually, as far as possible, in the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th, 7th, and 9th houses, then he becomes a king of religious nature. And so it is said in the *Bhavakutuhala* <note>A classic 16th-century astrological text by Jivanatha Jha</note>:

> When each planet occupies a single house at birth, it is called an 'Ekavali' (Single String),
> Like a pearl necklace, it is the crest-jewel ornament for the crowns of all kings.
> One born under this destroys hosts of enemies, delights in the company of celestial maidens,
> Possesses a multitude of virtues, and becomes a man who is a mine of wisdom.

He in whose birth time all planets are situated in Virgo, Aries, Libra, Leo, and Aquarius becomes a king. He in whose birth time all planets are in the 3rd, 4th, and 5th houses becomes the owner of much wealth and land. That man in whose birth time 3 planets are in the 3rd, 4th, and 5th houses, 2 planets are in the 2nd and 9th, and the remaining two planets are in the 1st and 7th (meaning all planets are spread across the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th, 7th, and 9th houses) becomes a righteous king. || 2 ||

->If all planets are in the Hora of the Moon, one born becomes a famous lord of men.<-
->Benefics in the ninth and eleventh houses, and malefics in the sixth and tenth, make a king.<- || 3 ||

All planets being in the <term>Hora</term> <note>A division of a zodiac sign into two halves; the first half of even signs and second half of odd signs belong to the Moon</note> of the Moon. Because it is said: "A Hora is half a sign; in odd signs they belong to the Sun and Moon, and in even signs to the Moon and Sun." In the second half of signs 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 and the first half of signs 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, the Moon's Horas occur. If all planets are in these as far as possible, then the man born becomes famous = renowned, a lord of men, a king. Regarding Benefics: the Benefics = Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, and the waxing Moon, being in the ninth and eleventh houses; and Malefics = the waning Moon, Sun, Mars, and Saturn, being in the sixth and tenth houses; then the one born becomes a lord of men, a king. || 3 ||

If all planets are in the Moon's Hora, a person born at such a time becomes a famous king. If benefics are in the 9th and 11th houses and malefics are in the 6th and 10th, the subject becomes a king. || 3 ||
