# Page 272
### From the Jataka Parijata with Commentary

->**When the lords of the auspicious planets are powerful and situated in the Ascendant, the tenth, or the seventh houses,**<-
->**and Mars and Saturn are placed in the ninth and eleventh houses, one becomes a king delightful in all virtues. || 4 ||**<-

If powerful benefic <note>auspicious</note> planets are located in the Ascendant <note>1st house</note>, the tenth, or the seventh houses, and Mars is in the ninth while Saturn is in the eleventh, then the person born will be a king endowed with all excellent qualities. || 4 ||

At the time of birth, if powerful auspicious planets are found in the first, tenth, and seventh houses, and Mars and Saturn are in the ninth and eleventh, he will be a king adorned with all virtues. || 4 ||

---

->**If the Ascendant or the Moon is in a Vargottama position, and is aspected by planets other than the Moon**<-
->**situated in the fourth, tenth, or seventh houses, one becomes a leader of men. || 5 ||**<-

Regarding *Vargottama* <term>Vargottama: A planet occupying the same zodiac sign in both the main birth chart and the 9th divisional chart (Navamsha), greatly increasing its strength</term>: If the Ascendant (the rising sign) is in its own *Vargottama* portion, or if the Moon is in its *Vargottama* portion, and is aspected <note>glanced at/influenced</note> by planets other than the Moon—meaning the other planets—situated in the fourth, tenth, and seventh houses, the person born becomes a leader of men, a king. As stated in the *Brihat Jataka*:
> If the Ascendant or the Moon is in *Vargottama* and is aspected by four or more planets (excluding the Moon), twenty-two types of kings are known to be born.

Here, if the Moon aspects the Ascendant, it is not counted as an "aspector" in this specific rule; hence the phrase "planets excluding the Moon" is used. This is based on the *Prajapatya* saying: "Let the Moon look as it wishes, it is not counted as an aspecting planet [for this specific yoga]." || 5 ||

At the time of birth, if the Ascendant or the Moon is in *Vargottama* and all planets (excluding the Moon) situated in the 4th, 10th, and 7th houses aspect it, he becomes a king. || 5 ||

---

->**When Venus is in the Ascendant in the constellation of Ashwini and is aspected by all planets,**<-
->**one is born as the foremost of a royal lineage, a destroyer of enemy clans, and devoted to many women. ||**<-
->**Leaving aside debilitated portions, if three or more planets are in their own divisions**<-
->**and one is in the Ascendant, he is a lord of the earth; if five or more, he is wealthy. || 6 ||**<-

Regarding *Ashwini*: When Venus is in the Ascendant in the *Ashwini* Nakshatra <note>the first lunar mansion</note> and is aspected by all [six] planets (Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Saturn), the person born is the foremost of a royal family (a Great King), a destroyer of enemy clans, and enjoys the company of many women. As stated in the *Jatakadesha*:
> Venus in the Ascendant in *Ashwini*, aspected by all planets, makes one a protector of the earth who has conquered the circle of his enemies.

Regarding "Leaving aside": Avoiding the *Navamsha* <note>9th division</note> of a debilitated sign, if three or more planets are situated in their own *Navamsha* divisions and one of them is in the Ascendant, the person born becomes a "Lord of the Earth" (a king). If five, six, or seven planets are in their own divisions, the person becomes a wealthy king. As it is said:
> Avoiding debilitated portions, if three or more are in exalted positions and one is in the Ascendant, they make a lord of the earth. If there are five such planets, it is the same; with two or four, they are merely very wealthy. || 6 ||

If at birth Venus is in the *Ashwini* constellation in the Ascendant and all planets aspect it, he will be the leader of a royal family, a destroyer of enemies, and a lover of many women.

Leaving aside the debilitated *Navamsha*, if three or more planets are in their own *Navamsha* and even one is in the Ascendant, he becomes a king. If five or more planets are in their own *Navamsha*, he becomes a wealthy king. || 6 ||

**"Equal to that"** etc. When the <term>Son of Bhrigu</term><note>The planet Venus (Shukra)</note> is endowed with strength and is situated in the <term>Gain</term><note>The 11th house</note> or the <term>Loss</term><note>The 12th house</note> position from the Ascendant, the person born is "equal to that," meaning they become wealthy and like a king. **"Two or three"** etc. If two or three <term>sky-travelers</term><note>Planets (Grahas)</note> are in their <term>exaltation</term><note>The sign where a planet's influence is strongest</note>, and the Moon is in <term>the Crab</term><note>Cancer (Karkata), its own sign</note>, and the <term>Ascendant</term><note>Lagna; the rising sign at birth</note> is endowed with full strength and is aspected by or joined with its own lord, Jupiter, or Mercury, the person born is honored everywhere and becomes a king respected by all people. || 10 ||

If at the time of birth even one planet is in its highest exaltation and is aspected by a <term>great friend</term><note>Adhi-mitra; a planet in a highly favorable relationship</note>, the person becomes a lord of the earth (a king). If a strong Venus is in the eleventh or twelfth house, one should know the result is as previously stated. If two or three planets are in exaltation, the Moon is in Cancer, and the Ascendant is fully strong, one becomes a king honored everywhere. || 10 ||

> **If all the benefics are in the Upachaya houses, and the malefics are in the Ascendant**
> **Or in the house of honor, having conquered the multitude of enemies, he is a cruel protector of the earth.**

> **And aspected by both benefics and malefics, he is a very fickle king or equal to one. || 11 ||**

**"All"** etc. If all the <term>benefic planets</term><note>Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, and the waxing Moon</note> are situated in the <term>Upachaya</term><note>Houses of increase: 3rd, 6th, 10th, and 11th</note> houses, and all the <term>malefics</term><note>Sun, Mars, Saturn, and the waning Moon</note> are in the Ascendant or have gone to the <term>Honor</term><note>The 10th house</note> position, then the person born is a "conqueror of the multitude of enemies," meaning one who uproots the family of his foes, a protector of the earth (king), and "cruel," meaning of a sinful or harsh mind. The meaning is that a man born in this mentioned combination becomes a powerful but sinful-minded king.

**"In the Sun"** etc. If the Sun is joined with the <term>Maker of Night</term><note>The Moon (Nishakara)</note> in the seventh house, and is in its own exaltation, trine, or other personal divisions, and is aspected (seen) by both benefics and malefics, the person born is a "fickle" king, meaning of a restless mind, or becomes equal to a king. || 11 ||

If at the time of birth all benefic planets are in the Upachaya (3, 6, 10, 11) houses and malefic planets are in the Ascendant or the tenth, then he is a cruel king who conquers all groups of enemies. If the Sun, situated in exaltation or similar divisions, is in the seventh house joined with the Moon and is seen by both auspicious and inauspicious planets, he will be a very restless king or like a king. || 11 ||

> **If the Son of Earth is in the Ascendant of Sagittarius, Aries, or Leo, aspected by a friend, he is the creator of a kingdom won by his own strength.**
> **If the Sun, Moon, and Jupiter are in the third, ninth, or fifth houses and are endowed with power, the protector of men is equal to Kubera. || 12 ||**

# Page 206
## Commentary on the Jataka Parijata

If that [Mars] is situated and aspected <note>original: "drishte", meaning viewed by the light of another planet</note> by a friendly planet, the person born becomes a self-made ruler of a kingdom—one who enjoys a kingdom acquired through their own valor. In this yoga <note>a specific planetary alignment</note>, even one not born into a royal family acquires a kingdom through their own prowess. Thus it is said in the *Phaladeepika* <note>a classic 16th-century astrological text</note>:

> Mars, when situated in the signs of Aries, Leo, or Sagittarius and aspected by a friendly planet, makes one a lord of the earth.

Regarding the "Third House" <note>original: "Duschikya", a technical term for the 3rd house</note>: If the Sun, Moon, and Jupiter are endowed with strength and are located respectively in the third, ninth, and fifth houses from the Ascendant or from Mars, then the person born becomes a king equal to Kubera <note>the Hindu god of wealth</note>, possessing an inexhaustible treasury. And so it is stated in the *Saravali* <note>an 8th-century foundational text by Kalyanavarman</note>:

> If Jupiter, the Moon, and the Sun are in the fifth, ninth, and third houses from Mars, then that person becomes a king or equal to Kubera in wealth. || 12 ||

If Mars is placed in the Ascendant in the signs of Sagittarius, Aries, or Leo and is aspected by its friend, the person born at that time will be the enjoyer of a kingdom created by his own strength. If the strong Sun, Moon, and Jupiter are in the third, ninth, and fifth houses, he shall be a king like Kubera. (Su. Sha. Kar.) || 12 ||

---

> When a planet is in its sign of depression <note>term: "Neecha", the sign where a planet is weakest</note> at birth, if the lord of that depression sign or the lord of that planet's exaltation sign is in a quadrant <note>term: "Kendra", the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note> from the Moon or the Ascendant, he becomes a righteous emperor. || 13 ||

Regarding "Depression": At the time of a man's birth, if a planet is in its own sign of depression, and the lord of that depression sign, or the lord of the sign where that depressed planet would be exalted—either both these lords or even just one of them—is situated in a quadrant (1, 4, 7, 10) from the Moon or the Ascendant, then the person born becomes a righteous emperor (a merit-filled sovereign of the whole earth).

In the *Phaladeepika* as well: If a planet is in depression, and the lord of the house it occupies, or the lord of the sign where that depressed planet is exalted, is in a quadrant from the Ascendant or the Moon, he will be a king of full-fledged wealth, an emperor, most righteous, whose feet are saluted by other kings, and possessed of splendor, fame, and fortune.

He at whose birth a planet is in a sign of depression, if the lord of that depression sign or the lord of that planet's exaltation sign is situated in a quadrant from the Ascendant or the Moon, he becomes a righteous and universal emperor. (Su. Sha. Kar.) ||

> If the lord of the Navamsha <note>term: "Navamsha", a 1/9th divisional chart used for fine-tuning strength</note> occupied by a depressed planet is in a trine or a quadrant, or if the Ascendant is a movable sign and its lord is in a movable sign or Navamsha, the person born becomes a lord of the earth or exceedingly powerful. || 14 ||

# Chapter 7: On Rajayoga (Royal Combinations)

### Verse 14
**Regarding the Debilitated:** If at the time of birth, a planet is situated in its sign of debilitation <note>the sign where a planet is at its weakest</note>, but the lord of the <term>Navamsha</term> <note>a 1/9th divisional chart used for fine-tuning strength</note> occupied by that debilitated planet is placed in a <term>Trikona</term> (the 5th or 9th house) or a <term>Kendra</term> (the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th house); and if the birth occurs in a <term>Movable Sign</term> <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn</note> as the Ascendant, or if the Lord of the Ascendant is in a Navamsha of a Movable Sign, then the person born becomes a lord of the earth—a King—or an extremely powerful and wealthy individual.

As stated in the *Sarvartha Chintamani*:
> If the lord of the Navamsha of a debilitated planet is in a Kendra or Trikona, and the Ascendant or its lord is in a Movable sign or Navamsha, one becomes a King.

**Hindi Commentary Translation:** If at birth the Navamsha lord of a debilitated planet is in a Trikona or Kendra, and the birth Ascendant is a Movable sign, or the Lord of the Ascendant is in a Movable Navamsha, that person becomes a King or highly influential. || 14 ||

### Verse 15
> If the Lord of the House of Honor <note>the 10th house</note> is placed in the house of defeat <note>the 8th house</note> but is in the *Paravata* Navamsha <note>a specific high-strength divisional dignity</note>, or is in its own sign of exaltation, its own sign, or a friend's Navamsha, one becomes a King of Kings.
> If Jupiter is in its sign of debilitation in the Ascendant, and a malefic planet is in the 8th house associated with that sign's Navamsha, then also one becomes a King of Kings. || 15 ||

**Explanation:** Regarding "Honor": If the Lord of the 10th house is in the 8th house, but attains the *Paravata* portion <note>original: "Paravatansha"</note> or is in its exaltation, own sign, or a friend's Navamsha, the person born becomes a King of Kings <note>original: "Rajadhiraja"</note>. Regarding the Ascendant: If Jupiter <note>original: "Purandara-guru"</note> is in its sign of debilitation (Capricorn) in the Ascendant, and a malefic planet is in the 8th house (Leo) and is also in the Navamsha of that 8th house (specifically the 64th Navamsha from the Ascendant), the person becomes a King of Kings. 

**Example:** In the first yoga <note>combination</note>, Saturn as the 10th Lord is in the 8th house in the Navamsha of Libra (its exaltation), creating the yoga. In the second yoga, Jupiter is in the 3rd Navamsha of a Capricorn Ascendant, and the Sun is in the 3rd Navamsha of the 8th house. || 15 ||

# Page 208
## Commentary on the Jataka Parijata

**Regarding Jupiter:** When Jupiter (the planet of wisdom) is situated in the 12th house <note>the house of loss or liberation</note>, and Saturn, as the lord of the 3rd house, is in the 11th house <note>the house of gains</note>, or if the Sun is in the 11th house. Here it is asked: under what conditions does Jupiter's placement in the 12th house produce this effect? It is said: when the Lord of the Ascendant <term>Lagnesha: the planet ruling the rising sign</term> is Jupiter himself and is placed in the 12th house, the person born becomes a **King of Kings**. Thus it is stated in the *Sarvarthachintamani* <note>a famous 13th-century astrological treatise</note>:

> When Jupiter is in the 12th, the Sun in the 11th, or Saturn is the lord of the 3rd;
> If the Lord of the Ascendant is Jupiter and is in the 12th, the man becomes a King of Kings.

It should be considered here that Saturn can only be the lord of the 3rd house when Jupiter is the Lord of the Ascendant if the Ascendant is Sagittarius.

**Regarding the Lord of Fortune:** The Lord of Fortune <term>Bhagyasha: the ruler of the 9th house</term> resides in a certain "divisional portion" <term>Navamsha: a 1/9th subdivision of a sign</term>. If the ruler of that portion is in the 5th house or the 4th house from the Ascendant, the person born becomes a king. Furthermore, if Mercury is aspected by <note>looked upon by</note> or joined with Jupiter, that person becomes a **King's favorite**. As it is said:

> When the ruler of the Navamsha occupied by the Lord of the 9th is in the 4th
> Or in the 5th house, the man becomes the best among kings.

-> (1) &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Thus from the *Sarvarthachintamani* || 16 || <-

A person born when Jupiter is in the 12th, Saturn as the 3rd lord is in the 11th, or the Sun is in the 11th, and Jupiter as the Ascendant lord is in the 12th, becomes a protector of the earth (a king). If the ruler of the Navamsha where the 9th lord is placed sits in the 5th or 4th house, he becomes a king. If Mercury is aspected by Jupiter or they are together, he becomes a favorite of the king. || 16 ||

> If Mercury is in a quadrant and aspected by the Lord of the 9th,

> If Saturn is in a quadrant or a trine, in its sign of exaltation or its "root-trine" sign,
> And is aspected by the Lord of the 11th and is strong, he becomes equal to a king. || 17 ||

**Regarding the Lord of Fortune:** When Mercury is in a quadrant <term>Kendra: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</term> and is aspected by the Lord of the 9th (wherever he may be), and Jupiter is in the <unclear>rising</unclear> Ascendant, the person being born attains equality with kings. In this combination, the person born becomes like a king.

Without debilitated planets = if a birth occurs free from planets in their signs of depression, then the person born becomes equal to the lord of the earth = like a king. If Rahu is in the house of action (10th), Saturn is in the house of gains (11th), the Lord of Fortune (9th) aspects them, and the Lord of the Ascendant (1st) is not joined with a planet in its sign of depression, he shall be equal to a king. <note>Author: Jnana Kar</note> || 19 ||

# If two, three, or four great planets are in their signs of depression, but are in an auspicious sixtieth-division, or are endowed with their own exaltation signs or divisions, the person is a righteous universal emperor. || 20 ||

Regarding "Debilitated": If two, three, or four great planets (not five or more, due to the specific proportion) are in their respective signs of depression but are in an auspicious sixtieth-division <term>shashtyamsa: a subtle 1/60th division of a sign</term>, or are in the ninth-division of their own exaltation signs. # Chapter on Royal Combinations || 7 ||

When planets are placed in each other's signs, or each in their own sign, or joined together in another's sign, or in full aspect <note>original: "purna-kshiti", referring to planets facing each other 180 degrees apart</note> with one another, or located in the same divisional chart <note>term: varga; a sub-division of a zodiac sign used for fine-tuning predictions</note>... so says **Parasara**.
Furthermore, combinations arising from the relationship between pairs of house lords are described by Parasara—

1. <gloss>1</gloss> Lords of Gains and Wealth, 2. <gloss>2</gloss> <gloss>3</gloss> Lords of Wealth and Valor, 3. <gloss>3</gloss> <gloss>4</gloss> Lords of Valor and Property, 4. <gloss>4</gloss> <gloss>5</gloss> Lords of Property and Intelligence.
5. <gloss>5</gloss> <gloss>6</gloss> Lords of Intelligence and Enemies, 6. <gloss>6</gloss> <gloss>9</gloss> Lords of Enemies and Fortune, 7. <gloss>9</gloss> Lords of Intelligence and Death, 8. <gloss>9</gloss> Lords of Death and Fortune.
9. <gloss>9</gloss> <gloss>10</gloss> Lords of Fortune and Action, 10. <gloss>10</gloss> <gloss>11</gloss> Lords of Action and Gains, 11. <gloss>12</gloss> Lords of Loss and Gains, 12. <gloss>12</gloss> Lords of Self and Loss.

These twelve combinations are always remembered as: 1. The Combination for Gains, 2. The Royal Servant, 3. The Army Commander.
4. The Minister, 5. Harsh Deeds, 6. The Royal Combination <note>term: Raja Yoga; a configuration indicating high status or power</note>, 7. Death of the Beloved.
8. Loss of Fortune, 9. The Royal Combination, 10. Land and Wealth, 11. Expense of Debt.
12. Loss of Wealth. || 21 ||

At the time of birth, if the lords of the 10th (Action) and 9th (Fortune) houses from the Ascendant <note>term: Lagna; the rising sign on the eastern horizon at birth</note>, or the 10th and 9th from each other, are joined and placed in each other's signs, or are in mutual angles <note>term: Kendra; the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note>, or aspect each other, and are related to the lord of the 2nd (Wealth), the person becomes wealthy. If they are joined or aspected by the lords of the 4th and 1st houses, he becomes the master of great wealth and vehicles. || 21 ||

If six planets are situated in their signs of exaltation <note>term: Uccha; the specific zodiac sign where a planet's influence is strongest</note>, one becomes a King of Kings and lord of the whole earth. If five planets are exalted and Jupiter is in the Ascendant, one becomes the protector of all people. || 22 ||

Regarding the "six": If any six planets are in their respective exaltation signs, then a "King of Kings" or a universal emperor is born. If five planets are exalted and Jupiter is in the Ascendant, the person becomes a ruler of all people, a highly respected king. Here, if a higher number of "cruel" planets <note>term: Papa-graha; malefic planets like Mars or Saturn</note> are exalted, the result is diminished. As stated in the *Brihat Jataka*:

> The Greeks <note>original: "Yavanas"</note> say that if cruel planets are in their exaltation, the king will be of a cruel mind. However, according to Jivasharma, if five planets are exalted, a lord of the earth is born.

According to Jivasharma's view, if there is a majority of malefic planets, the person is not a king but merely wealthy.
As his saying goes:

> Those born with malefic planets in exaltation do not become kings. Rather, they become endowed with wealth, but are angry and fond of quarrels.

Essentially, Varahamihira has given a general statement here without distinguishing between benefic and malefic planets. Furthermore:

> "With three or more planets in exaltation, those born in royal families become kings. With five or more, even those born in other families become kings; the same applies to planets in their trines <note>term: Trikona; the 1st, 5th, or 9th houses</note>."

In this statement by Varahamihira, three or four exalted planets make a prince a king. Five, six, or seven exalted planets make even one born in a common family a king—how much more so then for a prince. || 22 ||

If Saturn is in the Ascendant in Aquarius and four planets are in their exaltation, one becomes a lord of the entire earth. If Mercury is in the Ascendant in Aries and Jupiter is exalted (in Cancer), one becomes a ruler of men. || 23 ||

If Saturn is in the Aquarius Ascendant and four planets are exalted, one becomes a universal emperor. There is another reading: "If Saturn is in the second house," then it should be interpreted as Saturn being in the house of wealth. Also, if Mercury is in the Aries Ascendant and Jupiter is in its exaltation (Cancer), the person born is a ruler of men. || 23 ||

# From the Annotated Jataka Parijata

<page-num>212</page-num>
<header>From the Jataka Parijata with Commentary</header>

**If the Moon is in the rising sign of Taurus and is aspected <note>aspected: in astrology, this refers to the "glance" or mathematical relationship between planets</note> by the other six planets, the person becomes a lord of the earth <note>original: kshitinayakah; a king</note> in very early childhood. If one planet is in its exaltation <note>original: tunga; the sign where a planet is strongest</note> and the others are in their own or friendly signs, one attains enjoyments equal to a ruler of men. || 24 ||**

*Commentary:* "The Moon etc." If the Moon is shining in the rising sign of Taurus (which is its sign of exaltation), and is aspected by the other six planets (Sun, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, and Saturn), the one born becomes a lord of the earth—a king—even in childhood (in boyhood itself). "Exaltation etc." If one planet is situated in its exaltation, and the other six planets are in their own signs or in the signs of their friends. This is what is meant: if any one planet has reached its exaltation and the other six planets are either in their own signs or friendly signs, then the person born attains fortune equal to a ruler of men; meaning, he becomes like a king. || 24 ||

<margin>If a person has the Moon in Taurus at birth and the other six planets look upon it, he becomes a king in very early childhood. If one planet is exalted and all others are in their own or friendly houses, his fortune is like that of a king.</margin>

---

**If Jupiter is with the Moon and Mars in either a Vargottama <note>Vargottama: a planet occupying the same sign in both the main chart and the 9th divisional chart, increasing its strength</note> or a Pushkara portion <note>Pushkara-ansha: specific auspicious degrees within a zodiac sign</note>, a ruler of men is born. If the Moon is full-bodied <note>full moon</note>, placed in the tenth house <note>original: karma-sthit; the house of career and action</note>, and joined with the aspect of a benefic <note>benefic: a naturally "good" planet like Venus or Jupiter</note>, a lord of the earth is born. || 25 ||**

*Commentary:* "Vargottama etc." If Jupiter is with Mars and the Moon (Mars, Moon, Jupiter) in a Vargottama (the previously mentioned best division of its own class) or in a Pushkara portion—certain degrees in every sign are read as auspicious Pushkara portions (see Chapter 1, Verse 58)—the one born becomes a ruler of men, a king. "In the tenth house etc." If the Moon is full-bodied (the full orb on the day of the Full Moon), situated in the tenth house, and joined with the aspect of a benefic planet, the one born becomes a lord of the earth, a king. || 25 ||

<margin>If Jupiter is with Mars and the Moon in Vargottama or Pushkara-ansha, he becomes a king. If the full Moon is in the tenth house aspected by a benefic, he becomes a king.</margin>

---

**If the Moon is in Sagittarius joined with Jupiter and Venus, and Mercury is in the rising sign, and Mars is in Virgo, and the son of the Sun <note>Saturn</note> is in the "face-house of the deer" <note>Capricorn; the fourth house in this specific alignment</note>, a king is born, endowed with extraordinary strength and honored by all rulers of the earth. || 26 ||**

*Commentary:* "Jupiter etc." If the Moon is joined with Jupiter and Venus (Jupiter, Venus, Moon) in Sagittarius; and the son of the Moon, Mercury, has reached the rising sign (the Ascendant); and the son of the Earth, Mars, has gone to the sign of Virgo; and the son of the Sun, Saturn, is in the "face-house of the deer"—Capricorn itself is the "face-house," and it is the fourth house—situated there (meaning he has reached the fourth house in Capricorn).

<header>Chapter on Royal Combinations (Raja Yoga) || 7 ||</header>

### Chapter on Royal Combinations (Raja Yoga) || 7 ||

The meaning of this is as follows: If Saturn is in the tenth sign, Capricorn, which serves as the fourth house <note>The house of happiness and comforts</note>, and Jupiter, Venus, and the Moon are in the ninth sign, Sagittarius, which is the third house; and at that time the Ascendant <term>Lagna|The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</term> is Libra with Mercury situated there, and Mars is in the sixth sign, Virgo, in the twelfth house—then the person born is endowed with extraordinary strength, meaning they are immensely powerful. They become a King of Kings, worshipped by all lords of the earth and saluted by all monarchs. || 26 ||

If at the time of birth, the Moon joined with Jupiter and Venus is in Sagittarius, Mercury is in the Ascendant, Mars is in Virgo, and Saturn of Capricorn is in the fourth house, then that person, possessed of great strength, becomes a King revered by all other Kings. || 26 ||

> If Mercury, the Moon, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn are situated respectively in Virgo, Pisces, Gemini, Sagittarius, and Capricorn, a ruler of men is born. If the Ascendant is Pisces with a full and powerful Moon, Mars is in its exaltation <note>Mars is exalted in Capricorn</note>, and the son of the Sun (Saturn) is in Aquarius, a lord of men is born. || 27 ||

**Regarding "Virgo etc.":** Situated in Virgo, Pisces, Gemini, Sagittarius, and Capricorn; [these refer to] Mercury, the Moon, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn. This is what is said: If Mercury is in Virgo, the Moon in Pisces, Mars in Gemini, Jupiter in Sagittarius, and Saturn in Capricorn, then the person born becomes a ruler of men, a King. Here, only the signs are specified, not the houses. However, in the *Brihat Jataka*, Varahamihira has described the placement of these same planets in these same signs with respect to specific houses. For example:

> With Saturn in Capricorn as the Ascendant, and the Moon and others in the third, sixth, ninth, and twelfth houses, one becomes famous, possessing great virtues and renown, a leader of a multitude.

Thus, in the *Saravali* <note>A classical 8th-century astrological text by Kalyanavarma</note>:

> If Saturn is in Capricorn in the Ascendant, the friend of the night-lotus (the Moon) is in Pisces, and the son of the Earth (Mars) is in the house of Mercury (Gemini) having left Virgo; if Mercury is in Virgo and the Minister of the Gods (Jupiter) is in Sagittarius, then the person born becomes a King equal to the Lord of the Gods (Indra) and attains great glory.

In that case, Saturn would be in the Ascendant in Capricorn. Mercury would be in the ninth house in Virgo. The Moon would be in the third house in Pisces. Mars would be in the sixth house in Gemini. And Jupiter would be in the twelfth house in Sagittarius.

**Regarding "Pisces Ascendant":** When the Moon is of full body (full moon) and endowed with strength, and the Ascendant is the sign of Pisces; Mars is in its exaltation (Capricorn); and the son of the Sun (Saturn) is in Aquarius, a lord of men is born. As stated in the *Saravali*:

> When Pisces is rising with the Moon, a King is born, full of all arts (digits), with the son of the Earth (Mars) in exaltation in Capricorn, and the son of the Sun (Saturn) in Aquarius. || 27 ||

If at the time of birth Mercury, the Moon, Mars, and Saturn are situated respectively in Virgo, Pisces, <note>In the Sanskrit commentary this is 'Gemini', but here the Hindi text reads 'Cancer'</note> Cancer, Sagittarius, and Capricorn, then he becomes a King. If the Ascendant is Pisces and the full, strong Moon is there, Mars is in exaltation (Capricorn), and Saturn is in Aquarius, he becomes a King. || 27 ||

### With Commentary on the Jataka Parijata

->If the Son of the Earth <note>Mars</note> is in the sign of the Goat <note>Capricorn</note> at the rising, and the Moon is in the sign of the Crab <note>Cancer</note>, one becomes a ruler of the earth.<-
->If the Son of the Earth, the Sun, and the Teacher of the Gods <note>Jupiter</note> are placed in the Goat, the Ram, and the Pot <note>Capricorn, Aries, and Aquarius</note>, one becomes a king of men. || 28 ||<-

**Commentary:** "If the Son of the Earth" means Mars. If Mars is in the rising sign of Capricorn, and the Moon is in Cancer (which would be the 7th house), then the person born is a ruler of the earth, a king. "Son of the Earth, etc.": Mars, the Sun, and Jupiter. "Placed in the Goat, the Ram, and the Pot": meaning Mars in Capricorn, the Sun in Aries, and Jupiter in Aquarius. If they are so situated, the person born is a king of men. || 28 ||

<gloss>If at a person's birth Mars is in Capricorn ascendant and the Moon is in Cancer, he becomes a king. If Mars, the Sun, and Jupiter are situated respectively in Capricorn, Aries, and Aquarius, he becomes a king.</gloss>

---

->If the Full Moon is joined by a planet other than the Lord of the Ascendant, and is aspected by Venus, Mercury, and the Teacher of the Gods, one is a king.<-
->If Jupiter, Venus, and Mars are in their Vargottama divisions, and the malefics are not in the center houses, one is a king of men. || 29 ||<-

**Commentary:** "If the Full Moon": the Moon endowed with all its digits. "Joined by a planet other than the Lord of the Ascendant": joined by any planet except the ruler of the rising sign. If such a Moon is "aspected by Venus, Mercury, and the Teacher of the Gods": seen by one or all of them, the person born is a king. Furthermore, if Jupiter, Venus, and Mars are "in their Vargottama divisions": placed in the same sign in both the main chart and the ninth-division <term>Navamsha: a 1/9th sub-chart used to determine a planet's true strength</term> chart; and if the "malefics" (Sun, Saturn, and the waning Moon) are not "in the center houses" (the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses), then the man born becomes a king of men. || 29 ||

<gloss>If at birth the Moon is joined by a planet other than the ascendant lord and is aspected by Venus, Mercury, and Jupiter, he is a king. If Jupiter, Venus, and Mars are in Vargottama and malefics are not in the angles, he is a king.</gloss>

---

->If all the heavenly bodies are in the Head-rising signs, and the Moon is in the Crab aspected by or joined with benefic planets, one is a lord of the earth.<-
->If the Lord of the Ascendant is in the 9th or 10th house, and the Moon is in the Ascendant, one becomes a lord of the world. || 30 ||<-

**Commentary:** "All the heavenly bodies": all planets excluding the Moon. "In the Head-rising signs": situated in the signs Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Gemini, or Aquarius. If the Moon is "aspected by or joined with benefic planets" and shines in the "Crab" (the rising sign of Cancer), the person born is a lord of the earth. On this point, the *Saravali* <note>A famous 8th-century astrological treatise by Kalyanavarman</note> says:

> "When all planets are in Head-rising signs, even if in debilitation or enemy divisions, but the Moon is in its own house <note>Cancer</note> in the Ascendant, aspected by benefics and full of digits, it gives a kingdom filled with jewels, elephants, and horses."

"Lord of the Ascendant": the ruler of the rising sign. If he is in the 9th or 10th house, and the Moon is "joined with the Ascendant" (meaning the Moon is in the 1st house), the person born becomes a lord of the world, a king. || 30 ||

<gloss>If all planets are in Head-rising signs (Gemini, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Aquarius) and the Moon is in Cancer aspected by benefics, he is a king. If the ascendant lord is in the 9th or 10th and the Moon is in the ascendant, he is a king.</gloss>

# Chapter on Royal Yogas || 7 ||

**Half of the Bow:** The thousand-rayed one <note>the Sun</note>, should have reached the first half of the Bow <note>Sagittarius, specifically the first 15 degrees</note>. In that same place—in the half of the Bow—the Lord of the Stars <note>the Moon</note> should be present (along with the Sun). When the Son of the Sun <note>Saturn</note>, possessing great strength <note>having reached his own place</note>, is in the Ascendant <note>the sign of Capricorn</note>, and the Son of the Earth <note>Mars</note> is in his exaltation <note>also in Capricorn, meaning he is in the Ascendant along with Saturn</note>—if this should be the case, then the person born becomes the Lord of the Earth <note>a King</note>. His enemies, abandoning their own valor and strength out of fear and terror, bow down to him from afar. For those enemies are rendered lusterless, burnt by the fire of the majesty <note>the fire of his prowess</note> produced by the aforementioned planetary combination. The sense is that even powerful enemies inevitably come under the subjection of one born under this yoga.

And so says Mandavya:
> When the Sun and the Moon are in the sign of the Lord of Speech <note>Jupiter's sign, Sagittarius</note>,
> and Mars, along with Saturn, is in the sign of the Deer <note>Capricorn</note> endowed with strength,
> then that virtuous man attains power as a crest-jewel among kings,
> before whom opponents tremble in the face of battle as if before Death himself.

Likewise, Varahamihira also says:
> "With Mars exalted, the Sun and Moon in Sagittarius, and Saturn in the Ascendant, one becomes a lord of the earth." (Verse 31)

<margin>If the Sun is in the first half (15°) of Sagittarius, the Moon is also there, Saturn is very strong in the Capricorn Ascendant, and Mars is exalted (in Capricorn), then enemies, burnt by the fear of his majestic fire, abandon their prowess and bow from a distance. (Commentary by Su. Sha.)</margin>

> One whose birth-lord is situated in an Upachaya house from the Moon,
> while the benefics are in the quadrants and in the Navamsha of a benefic,
> and those called malefics are devoid of all strength—
> such a man becomes a lord of men, equal to Indra in power. || 32 ||

**Upachaya, etc.:** For a man whose birth-lord <note>the lord of the Ascendant</note> is situated in an **Upachaya** <term>Upachaya: Houses of growth (3rd, 6th, 10th, and 11th)</term> house from the Moon; and the benefics <note>Mercury, Jupiter, and the waxing Moon</note> have reached the **Quadrants** <term>Kendra: The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</term> and have also entered the **Navamsha** <term>Navamsha: The ninth-part harmonic division of a sign</term> of a benefic planet's sign; and those called malefics <note>the Sun, Mars, Saturn, and the waning Moon</note> are devoid of all strength <note>lacking positional and other strengths, i.e., very weak</note>—that person born becomes a lord of men, a king, equal to Indra in his personal prowess. || 32 ||

<margin>At the time of birth, if the Ascendant lord is in an Upachaya (3, 6, 10, 11) position from the Moon, the benefics are in the Navamsha of a benefic sign and placed in a quadrant, and the malefics are in every way devoid of strength, then that man becomes a king equal to Indra in power. (Commentary by Su. Sha.)</margin>

> If at a creature's birth the Sun is seeking his exaltation in a trine,
> the Moon is in her own sign, and Jupiter is situated in Cancer,
> he rules over the Earth, which is filled with many jewels. || 33 ||

**Seeking Exaltation:** For a creature <note>a human</note> at the time of birth, if the Sun is "seeking his exaltation" <note>desiring to go to his exaltation sign of Aries, meaning he is at the end of Pisces</note> and is in a **Trine** <note>the 5th or 9th house from the Ascendant</note> (this implies the Ascendant is either Cancer or Scorpio)...

(If the Sun is "aspiring for its exaltation" <note>original: "उच्चाभिलाषी" - moving toward its highest point in Aries</note> and is situated in a trine <note>the 1st, 5th, or 9th houses</note>) then if the Moon is situated in its own sign (Cancer), and if Jupiter is also in Cancer (in its exaltation and joined with the Moon), then that person born becomes a ruler of the earth, filled with various kinds of jewels. # **Even if the Sun is in its own trine or in exaltation, and the Sun, Venus, and Mercury are in their own Navamshas,**
# **if they are in the third, sixth, or eighth positions from the Moon, they make even a cowherd a lord of the earth. || 34 ||**

Regarding this: If the Sun is in its own trine <note>original: "मूलत्रिकोणे" - Mula-trikona, a specifically powerful area of a sign; for the Sun, this is Leo</note> or in its exaltation (Aries). If the Sun, Venus, and Mercury are in their own respective <term>Navamshas</term> <note>a 1/9th division of a zodiac sign used for fine-tuning strength</note>—meaning the Sun is in the Leo Navamsha, Venus is in the Navamsha of Taurus or Libra, and Mercury is in the Navamsha of Gemini or Virgo. If those three are in the third, sixth, or eighth positions from the Moon—the Sun being third from the Moon, Venus being sixth, and Mercury being eighth—then they make the one born, even if born in a family of cowherds <note>original: "गोपाल" - Gopala</note>, like a lord of the earth (a king). How much more so then for one born into a royal family? || 34 ||

*If at birth the Sun is in its Mula-trikona or exaltation, and the Sun, Venus, and Mercury are in their own Navamshas and located in the 3rd, 6th, and 8th houses from the Moon, they make even a cowherd equal to a king. || 34 ||*

---

# **When the Sun, Moon, Mercury, and Venus are in the tenth house in the Navamshas of friends,**
# **not in enemy houses, nor invisible, nor in fall,**
# **that man becomes a king, at whose march the dust is dampened by the flow of ichor from his elephants. || 35 ||**

Regarding "Sun, Moon...": If the Sun, Moon, Mercury, and Venus are in the <term>tenth house</term> <note>the house of career and public standing</note>, each in the Navamsha of a friendly planet, and these four planets are not in the houses of their enemies. (The enemies of these four are Venus, Saturn, Moon, and Sun <note>referring to specific planetary relationships</note>; their houses are 2, 7, 10, 11, 4, 5—they should not be in these). Nor should they be "invisible" <note>original: "अदृश्यै" - combust or hidden by the Sun's rays</note>. Here, planets become invisible when with the Sun, but only if the degrees of separation are very small. Therefore, the Moon, Mercury, and Venus should have a greater distance from the Sun than the required degrees. Also, the Sun "disappears" at night, so the birth should be during the day. Nor should they be in "fall" <note>original: "नीचै" - debilitation</note>. These four should not be in signs 7, 8, 12, or 6. One should consider this: in the tenth house, if the signs are Aries, Gemini, or Sagittarius, and the Sun, Moon, Mercury, and Venus are in friendly Navamshas, then that man born becomes a lord of the earth (a king). For that king, during his military expeditions, the very dust of the road is settled by the sprinkling of <term>ichor</term> <note>original: "मदजल" - Mada-jala; the fluid secreted by elephants in rut, a poetic symbol of a massive army</note> from his elephants...

# Chapter on Royal Yogas || 7 ||

By the sprinkling of their <note>the elephants'</note> spray, the dust is settled—that is, it is brought to a state of moisture. The meaning is that a person born under this yoga <term>Yoga: a specific planetary combination</term> travels surrounded by a multitude of elephants and horses. || 35 ||

If at the time of birth the Sun, Moon, Mercury, and Venus are in the divisions of friendly planets <note>original: "mitranshaka"</note>, are located in the tenth house, are not in the signs of enemies, are not combust <note>hidden by the Sun's glare</note>, and are not in their signs of debilitation, then that man becomes a King. During his travels, the dust of the earth is dampened by the ichor <note>maddened temple-fluid</note> of his intoxicated great elephants. || 35 ||

---

**The son of the Earth <note>Mars</note>, when strong and occupying his sign of exaltation, if aspected by the Sun, Moon, and the Lord of Speech <note>Jupiter</note>, makes one a Lord of Men. Even if born of humble origin, such a person is capable of protecting the entire earth. || 36 ||**

"The son of the Earth" etc. If Mars <note>original: "Bhauma"</note>, being strong—endowed with directional strength and other potencies—occupies his sign of exaltation, which is Capricorn; and if he is aspected <note>viewed</note> by the Sun, Moon, and Jupiter, then even if the person is of "base" origin <note>original: "kutsitah," meaning born into a lowly family</note>, he becomes a Lord of Men <note>a King</note> capable of ruling the entire world. || 36 ||

If at a man's time of birth Mars is in his exalted sign and is strong, and the Sun, Moon, and Jupiter look upon him, then even if he is without a noble lineage, he shall become a King capable of protecting the whole circle of the earth. || 36 ||

---

**With Mercury in the Ascendant, Jupiter in the seventh, the Moon in Cancer in the fourth house of happiness, and the son of Bhrigu <note>Venus</note> situated in the sky <note>the tenth house</note>, one rules the earth free from disease and agitation. || 37 ||**

"Mercury in the Ascendant" etc. Mercury in the rising sign <note>the Lagna</note>; Jupiter gone to the seventh house from the Ascendant; the Moon being spotless <note>the bright waxing Moon</note> and situated in the fourth house in the sign of Cancer; and Venus <note>original: "Bhargavanandana"</note> having gone to the tenth house. This is what is said: by the phrase "the Moon in Cancer in the fourth house," it implies the Ascendant is Aries. In that case, Mercury is in Aries, Jupiter is in the seventh house (Libra), and Venus is in the tenth (Capricorn). A person born thus is free from disease, lives in peace, and rules the earth. The sense is that he rules for a long time without fear. || 37 ||

If Mercury is in the first house, Jupiter in the seventh, the full Moon in Cancer in the fourth, and Venus in the tenth house, then that man rules the earth without any disturbance. || 37 ||

---

**The Moon, full and endowed with primary strength, even if acting alone, makes the one born a Lord of Men and a subduer of enemies. || 38 ||**

"Primary" etc. The Moon, possessing all its digits <note>full</note> and joined with primary strength—either strength of position or strength of exaltation—even if acting alone in such a state, makes the person born a ruler of men and a destroyer of foes. It should be noted here: even the Moon alone, if placed in a favorable house or in its sign of exaltation, bestows kingship. || 38 ||

If at the time of birth even just the full Moon is endowed with primary strength, it makes the child a King who subdues his enemies. || 38 ||

# Chapter 7: The Chapter on Royal Yogas (Raja Yoga)

If at the time of birth, the Sun is in the Ascendant <note>Lagna</note> in the sign of Leo, but is free from the Venusian division <note>Navamsha</note>, and Mercury is in Virgo, then that person becomes a King even if born into a lowly family. This combination is likely to occur during the month of Bhadrapada <note>August-September</note>. (According to the author of *Sukra Jataka*) || 43 ||

-> If Saturn and Mars are placed in the 10th, 5th, or the 1st house, <-
-> and the full Moon resides in a sign ruled by Jupiter, the one born shall be a King. || 44 || <-

**Commentary:** If Saturn and Mars are situated in the 10th <note>Mana</note>, 5th <note>Putra</note>, or the 1st <note>Udaya/Lagna</note> houses; and the Moon, endowed with full digits <note>Full Moon</note>, shines in a sign of Jupiter (either Sagittarius or Pisces), the person born will become a King. || 44 ||

If Saturn and Mars are in the 10th, 5th, or the Ascendant, and the full Moon is in Jupiter's sign (9 or 12), the child born at such a time becomes a King. (According to the author of *Sukra Jataka*) || 44 ||

When the Lord of the Ascendant is strong and placed in a Cardinal house <note>Kendra: 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th</note>,
it creates a Royal Yoga for men.
If it is aspected by a friendly planet, even one born
in a lowly lineage becomes a King or one honored by Kings.

**Commentary:** The meaning is straightforward. || 45 ||

If the Lord of the Ascendant <note>Lagnasha</note> is strong and located in a Cardinal house, it creates a Royal Yoga for humans. If that planet is aspected by a friend, then even if born in a lowly family, one becomes a King or is worshipped by Kings. || 45 ||

-> If the Lord of the Ascendant, situated in its sign of exaltation, <-
-> certainly aspects the Moon, the person born in this world becomes a Ruler <-
-> who conquers millions of enemies with hosts of elephants, armies, and horses. || 46 || <-

**Commentary:** If the Lord of the Ascendant, residing in its own house of exaltation, aspects the Moon (wherever it may be situated), the rest is clear. For an example, see the chart provided for verse 45. || 46 ||

If the exalted Lord of the Ascendant looks upon the Moon, then that person will surely be a famous King who conquers millions of enemies, possessing an abundance of elephants, horses, and armies. || 46 ||

-> If the Moon, endowed with full digits, is placed in a Cardinal house <-
-> other than the Ascendant, and is aspected by Jupiter and Venus, <-
-> the man born shall become a King. || 47 || <-

**Commentary:** This is self-explanatory. || 47 ||

If the Moon is fully strong in a Cardinal house (4th, 7th, or 10th) excluding the Ascendant, and is aspected by Jupiter and Venus, the child born at such a time becomes a King. || 47 ||

-> If the Lord of the Ascendant is in a Cardinal house, <-
-> without being in its sign of debilitation, combustion, or an enemy's sign, <-
-> and is not joined by any other planet, he will be a Sovereign King. || 48 || <-

**Commentary:** If the Lord of the Ascendant, avoiding its sign of debilitation, conjunction with the Sun <note>combustion</note>, and its enemy's sign, is placed in a Cardinal house—meaning the Cardinal sign is not the Lord's debilitation, solar conjunction, or enemy's home—and is not joined by any other planet, the one born will be a Sovereign <term>Chakravarti: a universal ruler or Emperor</term>. || 48 ||

If at the time of birth, the Lord of the Ascendant is in a Cardinal house (other than in debilitation, combustion, or an enemy's sign) and is not joined by any other planet, he becomes a Sovereign King. || 48 ||

<header>Chapter 7: On Raja Yogas (Royal Combinations)</header>

If the Moon is joined with Saturn in the eleventh house <note>the house of gains</note>, the fourth house <note>the house of happiness/comforts</note>, or the tenth house <note>the house of profession</note>, the person born is a king if born into a royal family; otherwise, they become as wealthy as a king. || 53 ||

*Regarding the eleventh house:* This is clear. || 53 ||

If Saturn and the Moon are in the eleventh, fourth, or tenth house, one born in a royal family becomes a king, and others become as wealthy as a king. || 53 ||

If the Lord of the Ascendant <term>Lagnapathi: the planet ruling the first house of the birth chart</term> is situated in an Upachaya house <term>Upachaya: the 3rd, 6th, 10th, or 11th houses, associated with growth and improvement</term>, the Moon is in the ninth house <note>the house of fortune/piety</note>, and strong benefic planets are in the quadrants <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</note> while occupying favorable divisional charts, the person becomes a king. Furthermore, if Jupiter and the Moon are in Taurus, and the Lord of the Ascendant is strong and placed in a trine <note>the 5th or 9th house</note> without being aspected <note>viewed</note> by Saturn or Mars, the person born becomes a ruler of the earth. || 54 ||

*Regarding the birth:* "Lord of the Ascendant" means the ruler of the birth sign; "situated in an Upachaya" means placed in any of the 3rd, 6th, 10th, or 11th houses; "Moon in the place of piety" means in the 9th house; "endowed with strength" means possessing positional strength; "benefics" means naturally auspicious planets; "occupying favorable divisions" means in the divisional charts of benefic planets; "in quadrants" means in the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses. In such a case, the person becomes a king. Regarding "Jupiter and the Moon": if Jupiter and the Moon are in Taurus, the Lord of the Ascendant is strong and in a trine (5th or 9th house), and is "devoid of the aspect of Saturn and Mars" (meaning not seen by them), then the person becomes a ruler of the earth. On this point, the *Saravali* <note>A classic 8th-century astrological treatise by Kalyanavarman</note> says the same regarding the latter half of the verse:

> If Jupiter and the Moon are in the Taurus ascendant, and the Lord of the Ascendant is strong and placed in a trine, and is not joined or aspected by the Sun, Saturn, or Mars (even if they are strong), he becomes a king endowed with fame who has destroyed all his enemies. || 54 ||

If a person's Lord of the Ascendant is in an Upachaya house, the Moon is in the ninth, and strong benefics are in quadrants in favorable divisions, he becomes a king. If Jupiter and the Moon are in Taurus and a strong Lord of the Ascendant is in a trine, not aspected by Saturn and Mars, he becomes a king. || 54 ||

When the Sun has entered the sign of Pisces and the Moon is in the Cancer ascendant, a king is born. However, if any of these [planets] are aspected by or joined with enemies or debilitated planets, they do not grant the "Bhu-pala Yoga" <note>The combination for being a protector of the earth/king</note>. || 55 ||

*Regarding the Sun:* When the Moon is in the Cancer ascendant and the Sun has entered Pisces (which is the 9th house for a Cancer ascendant), the person born is a king. This yoga <note>planetary combination</note> is likely to occur during the bright half of the month of Chaitra <note>March-April</note>. Regarding "enemies": if all the aforementioned yogas are aspected by "enemies" (inimical planets) or "debilitated planets" (those in their weakest signs), then they do not grant the royal status. This means the stated Raja Yogas are cancelled under those conditions. || 55 ||

# With the Commentary on Jataka Parijata

If the Sun is in the sign of Pisces and the Moon is in the Cancer Ascendant <note>The 'Ascendant' or 'Lagna' is the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</note>, the person born becomes a king. However, if the aforementioned planets that cause royal yogas are aspected by <note>In astrology, 'aspected' means being 'looked at' or influenced by the energy of another planet</note> their enemies or planets in debilitation, they do not produce a royal yoga. (According to the author of *Suka Jataka*) || 55 ||

> Even a single planet in its exaltation, aspected by a friend, produces a king endowed with many virtues; if joined with a friend, the king is successful. If the planets are in enemy signs or debilitation, the person is destitute, unhappy, foolish, diseased, troubled by kin, and associated with violence and sin. || 56 ||

**Commentary:** Even one planet in its own sign of exaltation <note>Exaltation is the sign where a planet is at its maximum strength</note>, if aspected by a friendly planet, makes the person born a king endowed with many virtues. If that exalted planet is joined with a friendly planet, it produces a successful king. Regarding the phrase "destitute" (*vivasu*): if the planets causing these yogas are in enemy signs or signs of debilitation <note>Debilitation is the sign where a planet is at its weakest</note>, the person born is destitute (lacking wealth; the *Medini* lexicon defines *vasu* as water, wealth, or gems). They are also unhappy (miserable), foolish, diseased (sickly), troubled by family, and prone to sinful acts of violence. || 56 ||

Even a single planet situated in exaltation, aspected by a friend and joined with a friendly planet, produces a king of many virtues. Planets in enemy or debilitated positions produce those without wealth or happiness, the diseased, those tormented by relatives, and those of wicked character prone to sins like violence. || 56 ||

> If Saturn is in the Ascendant in Sagittarius, Pisces, Libra, Aries, Capricorn, or Aquarius, the person will have a handsome body, be a king, a scholar, and a leader of towns and villages. || 57 ||

**Commentary:** The meaning is clear. However, there is a disagreement regarding Aquarius; as follows:

->The twelfth division of Aquarius in the Ascendant is not praised by the Yavana <note>Greek or Western</note> astrologers.<-
->If this were so, all signs in the Ascendant would yield undesirable results.<-
->Because of the combination of the Water-pot (Aquarius), it is not the opinion of all the authors of the Shastras.<-
->Therefore, the Aquarius Ascendant is inauspicious at birth, but not its specific divisions. || 57 ||<-

If Saturn is in the Sagittarius, Pisces, Libra, Aries, Capricorn, or Aquarius Ascendant, the native has a beautiful body, is a king, a scholar, and a headman in the town or village. || 57 ||

Now, with this verse, the author explains the details of how planets give auspicious and inauspicious results:

> From exaltation, Mula-trikona, own sign, friend's sign, enemy's sign, debilitation, or combustion with the Sun, the auspicious fruit is respectively: full, three-quarters, half, one-quarter, very little, and nil. || 58 ||

**Commentary:** A planet in its exaltation gives full auspicious results. In its *Mula-trikona* <note>A specific favorable area of a sign, slightly less powerful than exaltation</note> it gives three-quarters (3/4) results. In its own sign, it gives half (1/2) results. In a friend's sign, it gives one-quarter (1/4) results. In an enemy's sign, it gives less than a quarter (1/8). In its sign of debilitation or when combust (*arkaga*, meaning hidden by the Sun's light), it is fruitless, meaning it gives no auspicious results. Note that for inauspicious results, the order is reversed: an exalted planet gives no inauspicious results, while a debilitated or combust planet gives full inauspicious results. || 58 ||

Planets like the Sun give full auspicious results in exaltation. In *Mula-trikona* three parts, in their own sign half, in a friend's house 1/4, in an enemy's house very little, and in debilitation or combustion they are fruitless.

### Now, the Five Great Person Yogas (Pancha Mahapurusha Yogas).

> When Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, and Saturn are strong and occupy their Mula-trikona, exaltation, or own signs while situated in a Kendra, they create the Ruchaka, Bhadra, Hamsa, Malavya, and Shasha yogas respectively. || 59 ||

**Commentary:** When the strong planets—Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, and Saturn—occupy their *Mula-trikona*, exaltation, or own signs, and are situated in a *Kendra* <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses of a birth chart, considered the pillars of the horoscope</note>, they create the Ruchaka, Bhadra, Hamsa...

# Chapter 7: On Royal Yogas (Raja Yoga)

The Malavya, Charu-Shasha, and other yogas are formed as follows. That is to say: if a strong Mars is placed in its sign of <term>Moolatrikona</term><note>A specific favorable zodiacal position, slightly less powerful than exaltation but stronger than a standard "own sign" placement</note>, its exaltation sign, or its own sign, and is situated in a <term>Kendra</term><note>A "pivot" or "angle" house: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses of an astrological chart</note>, then the **Ruchaka Yoga** is formed. Similarly, Mercury forms the **Bhadra Yoga**; Jupiter forms the **Hansa Yoga**; Venus forms the **Malavya Yoga**; and Saturn forms the **Charu-Shasha Yoga**. As stated in the *Jatakabharana*:

> "When Mars and the other planets, in order, occupy their own houses, exaltation signs, or pivots, they form the yogas known as Ruchaka, Bhadra, Hansa, Malavya, and Shasha." || 59 ||

If strong Mars is in its Moolatrikona, own house, or exaltation house and is situated in a pivot, "Ruchaka" yoga occurs. If it is Mercury, "Bhadra" yoga occurs. If it is Jupiter, "Hansa" yoga occurs. If it is Venus, "Malavya" yoga occurs, and if it is Saturn, "Shasha" yoga occurs. || 59 ||

### On the Results of Ruchaka Yoga

> One born in the auspicious Ruchaka Yoga possesses a body endowed with strength, is possessed of wealth, fame, and good character, is a scholar of the scriptures, skilled in the chanting of mantras and <term>Abhichara</term><note>Incantations or rituals, sometimes associated with protective or aggressive magic</note>, a king or equal to one. He has a beautiful body with a reddish luster, is charitable, a conqueror of enemies, wealthy, and happy throughout a life of seventy years, commanding armies and horses. || 60 ||

Through this verse, the results for those born in Ruchaka Yoga are described. The meaning is straightforward. || 60 ||

A person born in Ruchaka Yoga has a body full of strength, is endowed with fame and character, is a scholar, skilled in the repetition of mantras and rituals, a king or similarly wealthy, possesses beauty with a red glow and a soft body, is generous, a conqueror of foes, wealthy, and happy until the age of 70, possessing armies and horses. || 60 ||

> If even one among the lords of the 9th, 11th, or 2nd houses is in a pivot from the Moon, and if Jupiter himself is the lord of the 11th house, the person attains the status of a Lord of an Unbroken Empire. || 61 ||

Regarding the "Lord of the 9th," etc.: If even one among the lords of the 9th (Dharmesha), 11th (Labhesha), or 2nd (Dhaneshvara) houses is in a pivot from the Moon (meaning in the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th house from the Moon's position), and if Jupiter is the lord of the 11th house, then the person born attains the status of a Lord of an Unbroken Empire—meaning they become a universal emperor—through their own valor.

If the lord of the 9th, 11th, or 2nd house is in a pivot from the Moon, and the lord of the 11th is specifically Jupiter, it makes the person the master of an unbroken kingdom. || 61 ||

### On the Results of Bhadra Yoga

# From the Garga Hora

Through this verse, the author explains the timing for the realization of the results of the yogas mentioned previously and those to be mentioned hereafter:
> Whichever planet is the creator of a yoga, if it is strong and associated with a "victorious" aspect, it bestows its results during its own major period <note><term>Dasha</term>: a planetary time-cycle in Indian astrology</note> in configurations such as Adhi Yoga. || 66 ||

"Whichever..." etc. Strong = endowed with strength based on its position, etc. Or "associated with a victorious aspect" = seen or joined by a planet that has won in planetary war; otherwise, it would be weak. Here is the definition of a "conquered" <note>defeated</note> planet:
> "A planet situated in the southern direction, trembling, not reaching its position, distorted, without longevity, mounted upon, deformed, low, or discolored—that is called 'conquered'."

Such a planet, which is the "creator" or significator <note><term>Karaka</term>: a planet that acts as a functional cause for a specific result</note> of a yoga, as well as in the Adhi Yogas (refer to verses 113-115 of this same chapter regarding the Moon and Ascendant Adhi Yogas), bestows its results during its own period. It should be understood that during the period of a strong planet, the yoga it occupies is realized. Conversely, during the period of a planet that is "conquered," or in its sign of debilitation or an enemy's sign, there is a loss of the house or yoga it signifies. || 66 ||

Whichever planet is the significator of any yoga, if it is strong and aspected by or joined with another strong planet, that planet gives the fruit of that specific yoga during its period. Similarly, if that significator planet is weak, situated in its debilitation or an enemy's house, and aspected by a weak planet, it destroys its house and yoga during its period. (Commentary by Su. Sha.) || 66 ||

### Now the Sunapha, Anapha, Dhurudhura, and Kemadruma Yogas.

If the Moon is situated in the Ascendant or in the seventh house, and is devoid of the aspect of Jupiter, the **Kemadruma** <note>a yoga often associated with poverty or isolation</note> occurs. If the planets are associated with very few "points" <note>referring to the Ashtakavarga system of numerical strength</note>, even if they are kings of planets, they give the results of Kemadruma and all become fruitless. || 71 ||
When there are planets in the second and twelfth houses on both sides of the Moon, it is called **Sunapha** and **Anapha** respectively. || 72 ||
The combination is called **Dhurudhura** when planets (excluding the Sun) are in both places. In the absence of these three combinations, one should declare the result of **Kemadruma**. || 73 ||

Now he describes the Kemadruma Yoga—"Situated in the Ascendant" etc. If the Moon is in the Ascendant or in the seventh house (the house of desire) and is devoid of "Jupiter's state" (meaning the sight/aspect of Jupiter), the Kemadruma Yoga occurs. Furthermore, if all planets are associated with very few "points" (meaning few auspicious marks in the *Ashtakavarga* <note>a system of eight-fold calculation</note>) and are "fruitless" (devoid of strength), they also produce the results of Kemadruma Yoga. The specific results of Kemadruma Yoga will be stated in verse 82. || 71 ||
Next, he explains the Sunapha, Anapha, and Dhurudhura Yogas with a pair of verses. From the "Cold-Rayed One" (the Moon), if there is a planet other than the Sun in the second house, it is called **Sunapha**. If there is a planet other than the Sun in the twelfth house from the Moon, it is called **Anapha** by the wise. If there are planets other than the Sun on "both sides" (in both the second and twelfth houses) from the Moon, it is called **Dhurudhura** (written as *Dhurudhura* in other texts). In the absence of these three mentioned yogas—meaning when the second and twelfth houses from the Moon are empty—one should state the result of **Kemadruma Yoga**; in other words, Kemadruma occurs then. Thus says Varahamihira in the *Laghu Jataka*:

> Excluding the Sun, planets in the 12th from the Moon create Anapha; in the 2nd, Sunapha.
> When in both, it is Dhurudhura. Anything else is called Kemadruma.

This should also be noted: whether the Sun is in the second or twelfth from the Moon or not, he does not participate in forming these Yogas. The five planets starting with Mars (Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn), either individually or combined, create Sunapha in the 2nd and Anapha in the 12th. Thus, with five planets, there are 31 variations each of Anapha and Sunapha. Similarly, with the five planets in the second and twelfth houses, individually or combined, 180 variations of Dhurudhura should be known. Their details can be seen in the commentary by Utpala on the *Brihat Jataka*. They are not written here for fear of making the book too long. That statement in the *Brihat Jataka*—

# With the Commentary on Jataka Parijata

There are three hundred and eleven (311) varieties of Sunapha and Anapha, and one hundred and eighty (180) variations of the Durdhura <note>original: "Daurudhare"</note> yoga. By applying the desired permutations and combinations in sequence, one arrives at these totals; once the logic is applied, the method is concluded. || 73 ||

**Notes**—The detailed explanation of the variations of Sunapha and other yogas mentioned here should be seen later (in verse 83, within the language charts).

---

If the Moon is in the Ascendant <term>Lagna; the sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</term> or in the seventh house and is not aspected by Jupiter, the "Kemadruma" yoga occurs. If planets possess few points in the Ashtakavarga <term>a system of points used to determine planetary strength</term> and are devoid of strength, they produce the results of Kemadruma yoga. || 71 ||

If planets other than the Sun are in the second and twelfth positions from the Moon, the "Sunapha," "Anapha," and "Dhurdhura" <note>original: "Dhurandhara"</note> yogas are formed. If these three yogas are absent, it is Kemadruma yoga. That is to say: if there are planets other than the Sun in the second house from the Moon, it is Sunapha; if in the twelfth, it is Anapha; if planets are in both places (2nd and 12th), it is Durdhura yoga. If there are no planets in the second or twelfth from the Moon, it is Kemadruma (the yoga that gives the fruit of poverty). || 72-73 ||

Now, other poverty-inducing yogas <term>Daridra yogas</term> that give results similar to Kemadruma are described:

> If the Moon is with the Sun, aspected by a planet in its debilitation, and situated in a malefic division <term>Papamshaka; a subdivision of a sign ruled by a naturally cruel planet</term>, one attains the Yoga of Poverty. Likewise, if at a night birth, a malefic planet aspects or occupies the eighth house from the Ascendant containing a waning Moon, the same occurs. || 74 ||

*Commentary:* "With the Moon" means joined with the Sun; "aspected by a planet in debilitation" means seen by a planet in its lowest state of dignity; "in a malefic division" means existing in a malefic Navamsha <term>a 1/9th sub-division of a zodiac sign</term>. In such a case, the native attains the Yoga of Poverty (equivalent to Kemadruma). Regarding "waning Moon": if in a night birth, from the Ascendant containing a waning Moon (during the dark fortnight), a malefic planet is in the eighth house, or if that house is aspected by a malefic, the Yoga of Poverty occurs. || 74 ||

If the Moon is with the Sun, aspected by a debilitated planet, and in a malefic Navamsha, the Yoga of Poverty occurs. In a night birth, if a malefic planet aspects or sits in the 8th house from a waning Moon in the Ascendant, it is the Yoga of Poverty. || 74 ||

# Chapter on Royal Unions (Rajayoga) || 7 || 226

### If the Moon is afflicted by Rahu or other malefic planets and is aspected by a malefic, one quickly falls into poverty.

**If the Moon is afflicted by Rahu and others:** When the Moon is afflicted by Rahu <note>original: "Vidhumtuda," a poetic name for the eclipse-demon Rahu</note> and other malefic planets, and is also aspected <note>The "aspect" or *drishti* is a planetary gaze that influences other houses</note> by a malefic, the person born quickly enters a state of poverty. **From the Ascendant:** If malefic planets occupy the four angular houses (1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th) <term>Kendra: the four central pillars of a horoscope</term> from the Ascendant, or from the Moon <note>original: "Nishakara," the Night-Maker</note>, the person born quickly becomes poor. || 75 ||

## With the Commentary on Jataka Parijata

If Saturn and Venus are in their signs of debilitation <note>The sign where a planet is weakest</note>, in the house of an enemy, or in the divisions of malefic planets, and they either aspect each other or occupy the same sign, then even one born into a royal family will fall into poverty. || 78 ||

> If the Moon is joined with a malefic, in a malefic's house, or in a malefic's division at night,
> and is aspected by the lord of the tenth house while lacking strength, the Kemadruma Yoga occurs.
> If the Moon is joined with a cruel planet in its sign of debilitation and is aspected by the lord of the ninth house,
> or if the Moon is waning at night and in its sign of debilitation, the Kemadruma Yoga is formed for the native. || 79 ||

**Commentary:** Regarding the Moon: If the Moon is "lacking strength" (weak), joined with a malefic planet, or (alternatively) situated in the house or the ninth-division <term>Navamsha: a 1/9th sub-division of a zodiac sign used for fine-tuning predictions</term> of a malefic planet at "night," and is "aspected" (viewed) by the "lord of the sky" (the lord of the 10th house), the Kemadruma Yoga occurs. Furthermore, if the "Moon" is joined with a "cruel" (malefic) planet, has reached its sign or division of debilitation, and is aspected by the "lord of the place of fortune" (the lord of the 9th house), then Kemadruma occurs. Additionally, if the Moon is "waning" (during the dark fortnight) at a "night" birth and is "joined with its debilitation" (occupying its weakest sign), the Kemadruma Yoga is formed for the person born. || 79 ||

If the Moon is joined with a malefic planet, is in a malefic's sign, or in a malefic's ninth-division, is aspected by the lord of the 10th house in a night birth, and is weak, then Kemadruma Yoga occurs.

If the Moon is with a cruel planet in its debilitated division and the lord of the 9th house aspects it, or if at night the waning <note>A horizontal line is drawn through the following word, possibly indicating deletion.</note> Moon is in its sign of debilitation, the Kemadruma Yoga occurs for those born at that time. || 79 ||

### Now, the Exceptions to Kemadruma Yoga.

> If the Moon or Venus is in a quadrant and aspected by Jupiter, the Yoga of poverty does not exist.
> If the Moon is joined with benefics or placed between benefics and aspected by Jupiter, the Yoga of poverty does not exist. || 80 ||
> If the Moon is in the house or division of a great friend or its own exaltation and is aspected by Jupiter, the native is free from poverty.
> If the full Moon is joined with a benefic, placed in the tenth house in its exaltation, and aspected by Jupiter, the native will not be poor. || 81 ||

**Commentary:** Now the author explains when the previously mentioned Kemadruma Yogas are "broken" (cancelled) through two verses starting with "Nishakare" (The Moon). If the "Moon" or "Venus" is placed in a "quadrant" (the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses) and is "aspected" (viewed) by "Jupiter," the Yoga of poverty does not occur. Furthermore, if the Moon is "joined with a benefic" (a favorable planet) or "placed between benefics" (situated between two favorable planets in the same sign) and is "aspected by Jupiter," the Yoga of poverty does not occur. Even if the previous definitions of the Yoga are met, it will not take effect under these conditions. || 80 ||

If the Moon has reached the house or ninth-division of a "great friend" or its "own exaltation" <note>The sign where a planet is at its maximum strength</note> and is aspected by Jupiter, then even if the previous definitions were present, the native is "free from poverty" (the results of Kemadruma). If the Moon is a "full orb" (Full Moon), joined with a benefic planet, located in the "sky" (the 10th house) in its "own exaltation" (Taurus), and aspected by Jupiter, the native will not suffer the poverty associated with Kemadruma. || 81 ||

Even if the characteristics of Kemadruma Yoga are present, if the Moon or Venus is in a quadrant and is aspected by Jupiter, the poverty (Kemadruma) Yoga does not occur. If the Moon is joined with a benefic planet or is between benefic planets and Jupiter aspects it, the poverty Yoga does not occur. || 80 ||

If the Moon is in the house of a great friend, in its own sign of exaltation, or in its own house or ninth-division and Jupiter aspects it, the native is free from poverty; that is, the Kemadruma is cancelled. The Full Moon...

# Chapter 7: Chapter on Royal Combinations (Raja Yoga)

If a benefic planet is in the Ascendant <note>Lagna</note>, or if a planet is exalted in the 10th house and is aspected by Jupiter, the person does not become poor. (Author of *Sushloka-Shataka*) || 81 ||

Now, with this verse, the author describes the results for one born under the previously mentioned *Kemadruma* combinations <note>Kemadruma Yoga is a specific planetary configuration usually associated with hardship or lack of support</note>:

> When the *Kemadruma* combination is present in any birth chart,
> The Royal Combinations <note>Raja Yogas</note> are destroyed, just as elephants are at the sight of a lion. || 82 ||

Regarding this verse: In any birth chart, if the previously mentioned *Kemadruma* combination occurs, the Royal Combinations are destroyed. If at anyone's time of birth there are Royal Combinations, but there is also a *Kemadruma* present, then those Royal Combinations are rendered useless due to the flaw of the *Kemadruma*. The meaning is that at that time, the person becomes poor rather than a king. Here is the metaphor: "Just as elephants at the sight of a lion"; just as elephants flee upon seeing a lion <note>original: "hari"</note>, in the same way, Royal Combinations become fruitless upon encountering a *Kemadruma*. || 82 ||

If a *Kemadruma* combination exists at the time of someone's birth, then even if they have Royal Combinations, they become unsuccessful. The point is that the *Kemadruma* combination destroys even a Royal Combination. Just as a lion destroys elephants. (Author of *Sushloka-Shataka*) || 82 ||

## In the *Hora* <note>Referring to Varahamihira's Brihat Jataka</note>

The four combinations starting with *Sunapha*, which were spoken of by Varaha <note>Varahamihira, the 6th-century astronomer/astrologer</note> in the *Brihat Jataka*, are now explained according to other opinions:

> Excluding the Sun, the *Sunapha*, *Anapha*, and *Durudhara* combinations are said to be formed by planets in the second, the last <note>12th</note>, or both positions from the Moon. Otherwise, according to other powerful authorities, it is *Kemadruma*. However, *Kemadruma* is not desired <note>does not occur</note> if the Moon is in a cardinal house <note>Kendra: 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th</note> or is joined by a planet. Some say these occur in the cardinal houses and the ninth-divisional charts <note>Navamsha</note>, but those sayings are not well-known. || 83 ||

Regarding "Excluding": From the Moon <note>original: "Shitanshu"</note>, excluding the Sun, by planets (Mars and others) situated in the second, the last, or both (second and twelfth), the three combinations *Sunapha*, *Anapha*, and *Durudhara* are produced respectively. Otherwise, when both the second and twelfth from the Moon are empty, the *Kemadruma* combination is stated by many other teachers. This is what is said: when the second and twelfth places from the Moon are devoid of planets, *Kemadruma* occurs. 

He now states the cancellation of *Kemadruma*: "In a cardinal house." If the Moon is in a cardinal house from the Ascendant (1, 4, 7, 10), or if it is joined by planets like Mars and others, the *Kemadruma* combination is "not desired," meaning it does not occur. 

He states the opinions of others: "Some." Some, such as Shrutakirti and others, say these combinations occur in the cardinal houses and the ninth-divisional charts <note>Navamsha</note>. That is to say, if a planet like Mars is in the 4th from the Moon, it is *Sunapha*; in the 10th, it is *Anapha*; in both 4th and 10th, it is *Durudhara*. If both are empty, it is *Kemadruma*. Thus Shrutakirti says:

> By planets in the fourth from the Moon, *Sunapha* is declared; by those in the tenth, *Anapha*.
> By those in both, *Durudhara*; otherwise, the combination is named *Kemadruma*.

The same applies to the ninth-divisional charts <note>Navamsha</note>. That is, in whichever sign's Navamsha the Moon is placed, if there are planets like Mars in the second sign from that Navamsha sign, it is *Sunapha*; in the twelfth, *Anapha*; in both, *Durudhara*. If both are empty, it is known as *Kemadruma*. Thus says Jivasharma:

> In whichever sign-portion <note>Navamsha</note> the Moon is placed at birth,
> The combination formed by planets in the second from that is called *Sunapha*.
> In the twelfth, it is known as *Anapha*; by planets in both the second and twelfth,
> The *Durudhara* combination is spoken of; otherwise, it is remembered as *Kemadruma*.
