<header>In the Annotated Jataka Parijata—</header>

Furthermore, this view is not favored by the great teachers. That is why it is said—they are not famous in their pronouncements. Those teachers who hold the opinion that these yogas occur "in the centers <note>Kendra: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</note> and the ninth-division charts <note>Navamsha: a sub-divisional chart used for fine-tuning predictions</note>" are not considered authoritative or famous in their predictive accuracy. || 83 ||

If any planet from Mars onwards (excluding the Sun) is in the 2nd house from the Moon, the **Sunapha** yoga is formed. If any planet other than the Sun is in the 12th house from the Moon, the **Anapha** yoga is formed. If planets other than the Sun are in both the 2nd and 12th houses from the Moon, the **Durudhara** yoga is formed. If there are no planets in either the 2nd or 12th houses from the Moon, the **Kemadruma** yoga is formed.

If the Moon is in a center <note>Kendra</note> or if any other planet is in a center, the **Kemadruma** yoga is cancelled. Some believe these yogas also occur from the Moon's position in the centers and the ninth-division chart. However, this opinion is not well-known. See the Sanskrit commentary. || 83 ||

Here, in this context, I will clarify the statement from the *Brihat Jataka* <note>A foundational 6th-century astrology text by Varahamihira</note>—
> "There are thirty-one varieties each of Sunapha and Anapha; one hundred and eighty varieties of Durudhara. These are derived through the mathematical combinations of the planets, moving through the different positions."

I will now demonstrate the explanation of this verse—there are 31 variations of the Sunapha and Anapha yogas. There are 180 variations of the Durudhara yoga. These variations are exhausted through the method of mathematical combinations <note>term: Ichha-vikalpa (mathematical permutations based on choice)</note> and the process of shifting positions. For example—Sunapha and Anapha yogas are formed by these five planets: Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, and Saturn. Therefore, the combinations of five are: <insert>
| 5 | 4 | 3 | 2 | 1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
</insert> Thus, by the method of mathematical expansion <note>Prastara</note>, using the digits 1, 5, 10, 10, 5, 1, the variations are: first option 5, second 10, third 10, fourth 5, fifth 1. In this way, the total yogas are 31.

**First Option**—If there is only 1 planet in the 2nd from the Moon—Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, or Saturn—there are five variations. **Second Option**—Mars-Mercury, Mars-Jupiter, Mars-Venus, Mars-Saturn; Mercury-Jupiter, Mercury-Venus, Mercury-Saturn; Jupiter-Venus, Jupiter-Saturn; Venus-Saturn. In this way, the second option has 10 types. **Third Option**—Mars-Mercury-Jupiter, Mars-Mercury-Venus, Mars-Mercury-Saturn, Mars-Jupiter-Venus, Mars-Jupiter-Saturn, Mars-Venus-Saturn; Mercury-Jupiter-Venus, Mercury-Jupiter-Saturn, Mercury-Venus-Saturn; Jupiter-Venus-Saturn. In this way, the third option has 10 types. **Fourth Option**—Mars-Mercury-Jupiter-Venus, Mars-Mercury-Jupiter-Saturn, Mars-Mercury-Venus-Saturn, Mars-Jupiter-Venus-Saturn, Mercury-Jupiter-Venus-Saturn. In this way, there are five variations of the fourth option. **Fifth Option**—Mars-Mercury-Jupiter-Venus-Saturn. In this way, there is 1 variation of the fifth option. From these five options, 31 variations of Sunapha yoga are formed. Similarly, there are 31 variations of Anapha yoga.

<header>Chapter on Royal Yogas (Rajayoga) || 7 ||</header>

Now, through two verses spoken by Varaha <note>referring to Varahamihira, the 6th-century astronomer and astrologer</note>, the results of the four yogas—Sunapha and the others—are described. The verses are simple in meaning. Among them, the results of Sunapha, Anapha, and Durudhara are auspicious. The essential point is that the result of Kemadruma is inauspicious. || 84-85 ||

A person born in the **Sunapha Yoga** <note>formed when there are planets, excluding the Sun, in the 2nd house from the Moon</note> becomes a king through wealth earned by his own hands, or becomes as wealthy as a king, famous, and possessed of glory. Everyone obeys the commands of a person born in the **Anapha Yoga** <note>formed when there are planets in the 12th house from the Moon</note>; he is free from disease, virtuous, of famous reputation, an enjoyer of the senses—sound, touch, sight, taste, and smell—possesses a beautiful body, and is free from mental sorrows. || 84 ||

A person born in the **Durudhara Yoga** <note>formed when there are planets in both the 2nd and 12th houses from the Moon</note> is a partaker of various enjoyments and happiness, endowed with wealth and vehicles, charitable, and possesses excellent servants. A person born in the **Kemadruma Yoga** <note>formed when there are no planets in the 2nd or 12th houses from the Moon</note>, even if born into a royal family, becomes filthy, sorrowful, base, penniless, a servant, and wicked. || 85 ||

## Now, the Results of Sunapha Yoga Created by Mars and Others.

> The person born is a fierce king, violent, bold, of steady intellect, 
> possessed of wealth and valor, and prone to anger when Mars is in the second house from the Moon. || 86 ||
> 
> Skilled in the Vedas, scriptures, arts, and singing, possessing a beautiful body, 
> high-minded, speaking kindly, and righteous when Mercury is in the second house from the Moon. || 87 ||
> 
> Superior in all sciences, prosperous, a family man, dear to the king, 
> and possessing fame equal to a king when Jupiter is in the second house from the Moon. || 88 ||
> 
> Possessed of valor, women, wealth, land, and industriousness, very wealthy, 
> rich in four-legged animals <note>original: "chatuspada" referring to livestock like cows, horses, and elephants</note>, and royal splendor when Venus is in the second house from the Moon. || 89 ||
> 
> Honored by all those residing in towns and villages, wealthy, wise, 
> and expert in all tasks when Saturn is in the second house from the Moon. || 90 ||

Now, the results of the Sunapha Yoga produced by Mars and the other planets are stated—through the following five verses. These individual results occur when only one planet, such as Mars, is in the second house from the Moon. If two, three, or more planets are in the second house, then the result should be declared as a mixture of those influences. The verses are simple in meaning. || 86-90 ||

If **Mars** is in the wealth (2nd) house from the Moon, the person born at such a time is of fierce intellect, violent, courageous, wealthy, powerful, and an angry king. || 86 ||

If **Mercury** is second from the Moon, he is skilled in the arts of the Vedas and scriptures—and in singing—possesses a beautiful body, is high-minded, speaks for the welfare of others, and is a righteous soul. || 87 ||

If **Jupiter** is second from the Moon, he is proficient in knowledge, prosperous, has a family, is a favorite of the king, and is as famous as a king. || 88 ||

If **Venus** is second from the Moon, he is courageous, possesses women, wealth, and land, is hardworking, very rich, endowed with four-legged animals (oxen, cows, horses, elephants, etc.), and possesses royal fortune. || 89 ||

If **Saturn** is second from the Moon, he is honored by all people living in the towns and villages, is wealthy, intelligent, and expert in all works. || 90 ||

## Now, the Results of Anapha Yoga Created by Mars and Other Planets.

> Proud, eager for battle, angry, bold, a leader of thieves,

# With the Commentary of Jataka Parijata

->**The Results of Jupiter in the 12th from the Moon**<-

One honored by kings, highly intelligent, possessing the qualities of depth and strength of character, pure, and wealthy in both property and riches—such is the person with Jupiter in the twelfth house from the Moon. || 93 ||

->**The Results of Venus in the 12th from the Moon**<-

A "God of Love" to young women <note>original: "yuvati-jana-kandarpa"; implying great physical attraction</note>, later possessing wealth in livestock, wise, and abundant in wealth and grain—such is the person with Venus in the twelfth house from the Moon. || 94 ||

->**The Results of Saturn in the 12th from the Moon**<-

Broad-shouldered, virtuous, a leader, later possessing wealth in livestock, one whose words are heeded, but having a difficult or wicked wife—such is the person with Saturn in the twelfth house from the Moon. || 95 ||

Now, the results of Mars and other planets situated in the twelfth house from the Moon (forming the <term>Anapha Yoga</term> <note>Anapha Yoga occurs when planets other than the Sun occupy the 12th house from the Moon, influencing the native's subconscious and resources.</note>) are described in these five verses. The results for each planet are stated individually. If two or more planets are combined, the results should be interpreted as a mixture of their qualities. The meaning of the verses is clear. || 91-95 ||

If **Mars** is in the 12th from the Moon: The person is proud, courageous in battle, prone to anger, a leader of house-thieves <note>likely implying a leader of a rough or rogue group</note>, steadfast, and protective of their own body. || 91 ||

If **Mercury** is in the 12th from the Moon: The person is an expert in the Gandharva arts (music), a writer, clever, a poet, an orator, has a beautiful body, is famous, and is honored by kings. || 92 ||

If **Jupiter** is in the 12th from the Moon: The person is honored by kings, exceptionally wise, possesses deep virtues, is of "Sattva" (pure/harmonious) quality, pure, occupies a high position, and is very wealthy. || 93 ||

If **Saturn** is in the 12th from the Moon: The person has long arms, is virtuous, a leader, possesses wealth in livestock, is influential in speech, but has a wicked wife. || 95 ||

### Now, the Results of Dhurandhara Yoga
<note>Dhurandhara Yoga, often referred to as Durudhara Yoga in other texts, occurs when the Moon is flanked by planets in both the 2nd and 12th houses.</note>

If the Moon is between **Mercury and Mars**: The person is a liar yet virtuous, skillful, very cunning, greedy, appears older than they are, and is attached to unchaste women. || 96 ||

If the Moon is between **Mars and Jupiter**: The person gains wealth through their own work, is joyful, famous, but troubled by enemies; they are devoted to their own home and character but face hardships. || 97 ||

If the Moon is between **Mars and Venus**: The person is athletic, handsome, cruel, joyful, possesses good desires and wealth, but lacks character due to fear. || 98 ||

If the Moon is between **Mars and Saturn**: The person is devoted to low-minded women, is angry, wealthy, a backbiter, has many enemies, and is never satisfied. || 99 ||

If the Moon is between **Mercury and Jupiter**: The person is righteous, a scholar of the scriptures, an orator, a good poet, surrounded by good people, and famous. || 100 ||

If the Moon is between **Mercury and Venus**: The person is fond of dancing and singing, handsome, sweet-spoken, fortunate, wise, and has a brave nature. || 101 ||

If the Moon is between **Saturn and Mercury**: The person travels from country to country, is respectable, but not very wealthy or educated; they are hostile toward their own kinsmen. || 102 ||

If the Moon is between **Jupiter and Venus**: The person is like a king, prosperous, an expert in ethics/policy, courageous, famous, and has a pure mind. || 103 ||

If the Moon is between **Saturn and Jupiter**: The person is happy, endowed with humility, scientific knowledge, education, beauty, and virtue; they are wealthy and a peacemaker. || 104 ||

If the Moon is between **Venus and Saturn**: The person follows the conduct of elders, belongs to a noble family, is a master over skillful women, is wealthy, and is a favorite of kings. || 105 ||

When the planets forming the yoga are in their signs of exaltation, their own signs, or the signs of their friends, the person born certainly attains all the results mentioned. The great sages like Parashara <note>Parashara is considered the father of Vedic astrology and author of the foundational text Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra.</note> and others state that the same results apply if the planets are in their own <term>Navamsha</term> <note>A one-ninth divisional chart used to determine the hidden strength of planets.</note> or in the houses of their friends. || 106 ||
If the Moon is joined with Rahu or Ketu <note>The North and South Nodes of the Moon, often called 'shadow planets'.</note>, or if Rahu is in the 12th house from the Moon, or if the planets creating the yoga are in their signs of debilitation or are combust <note>Too close to the Sun to be effective.</note>, the learned masters say the results will be mixed. || 107 ||

Now, the results of the <term>Durudhara Yoga</term> <note>A configuration where planets occupy the 2nd and 12th houses from the Moon, effectively 'flanking' it.</note> are described in twelve verses. Here, the specific results should be judged by the relative strength of the planetary combinations mentioned. The verses are clear in their meaning. || 66-107 ||

One born with the Moon between Mercury and Mars is a liar, yet virtuous, clever, a great rogue, compassionate, greedy, and attracted to older women. || 96 ||

One born with the Moon between Mars and Jupiter is wealthy through their own work, famous, troubled by enemies, and always residing in their own home. || 97 ||

One born with the Moon between Mars and Venus is athletic, handsome, lustful, of a cruel nature, cheerful, wealthy, and lacks character due to fear (behaving like one who is mad). || 98 ||

One born with the Moon between Mars and Saturn is devoted to a criticized woman, angry, wealthy, a slanderer, has many enemies, and is impatient. || 99 ||

One born with the Moon between Mercury and Jupiter is righteous, a knower of the scriptures, eloquent, an excellent poet, keeps company with good people, and is famous. || 100 ||

One born with the Moon between Mercury and Venus is immersed in music and dance, handsome, a pleasant speaker, has a beautiful body, fine intellect, and a courageous nature. || 101 ||

One born with the Moon between Saturn and Mercury travels to many countries and is honored there, but may not possess great learning or wealth, and is an enemy to his own kinsmen. || 102 ||

One born with the Moon between Jupiter and Venus is like a king; such a person is prosperous, a master of policy, brave, famous, and pure of heart. || 103 ||

One born with the Moon between Saturn and Jupiter is happy, endowed with humility, science, learning, beauty, and good qualities; he is wealthy and brings peace to others. || 104 ||

One born with the Moon between Venus and Saturn follows the conduct of elders, is of noble birth, the husband of a woman lacking in qualities, wealthy, and a favorite of the king. || 105 ||

The sages like Parashara have said that these results are certain to occur if the yoga-causing planets are exalted, in their own houses, in their own divisional signs, or in the houses of their friends. || 106 ||

The great scholars have said that if the Moon is with Rahu or Ketu, or if Rahu is in the 12th house from the Moon, or if the planets causing the Durudhara Yoga are debilitated or combust, the results will be mixed. || 107 ||

## Now, the Shakata Yoga.

If Jupiter is in the 6th or 8th house from the Moon, and is not in an angular house <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses.</note> from the Ascendant, the combination is called <term>Shakata</term> <note>Literally 'The Cart' Yoga; it implies a life of ups and downs, like the turning of a wheel.</note>. || 108 ||

Now the Shakata Yoga is explained: If Jupiter is in the 6th or 8th from the Moon, and that Jupiter is not in a <term>Kendra</term> (angle) from the Ascendant—meaning it is not in the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses—then the Shakata Yoga is formed.
As stated in the *Phaladeepika* <note>A famous 13th-century astrological treatise by Mantreswara.</note>:
"When the Moon is in the 6th, 8th, or 12th from Jupiter, and Jupiter is not in an angle from the Ascendant, it is Shakata." || 108 ||

If Jupiter is in the 6th or 8th from the Moon and is not in an angle from the Ascendant, it is known as the 'Shakata' Yoga. || 108 ||

### Now, the Result of Shakata Yoga.

> Even if born into a royal family, one born under Shakata Yoga <note>original: "Shakata-yoga-jah"; Shakata means "wagon" or "cart"</note> becomes destitute. Constantly tormented by the power of distress and exertion, he becomes disliked by the king. || 108 ||

By this verse, the result of Shakata Yoga is stated in plain meaning. || 109 ||
A person born in Shakata Yoga, even if belonging to a royal lineage, becomes poor, is perpetually distressed by numerous troubles and efforts, and is disliked by the sovereign. || 109 ||

### Now, the Results of Parijata and Other Varga Positions.

> A planet in the Parijata division brings happiness and health when in the highest categories. If in the Gopura division, it grants cattle and wealth; if in the Simhasana division, it creates majesty. || 110 ||
> A planet joined with the Paravata portion grants men extensive knowledge, fame, and fortune. If in Devaloka, it gives many vehicles and armies; if situated in Airavata, it grants kingship.

The results of the Parijata and other divisions <term>Vargas: specific divisional strengths of planets</term> mentioned in the first chapter (verses 45-46) are stated here in these two verses in plain meaning. || 110-111 ||
A planet staying in its Parijata portion (Chapter 1, verses 45-47) gives happiness. A planet in an excellent category <note>Uttama-varga</note> makes one free from disease. If a planet is in the Gopura portion, it gives cows and wealth. A planet in the Simhasana (Throne) portion gives majesty (prosperity). A planet joined with the Paravata portion causes men to obtain knowledge, fame, and abundant wealth. A planet joined with Devaloka gives many vehicles and an army, and if situated in the Airavata portion, it makes one a king. || 110-111 ||

### Now, the Lowly and Other Yogas.

> Lowly, middling, and best results occur when the Moon is in a Kendra or other house from the Sun, regarding humility, wealth, knowledge, and intellectual skill. If the Moon is in its own or a great friend's division during the day or night, and is aspected by Jupiter or Venus, one becomes wealthy and happy. || 112 ||

Now, he describes the Lowly (Adhama), Middling (Madhya), and Best (Varishtha) Yogas based on the positions of the Sun and Moon—"Adhama" etc. When the Moon <note>original: "Shashini"</note> is situated in a Kendra or other house from the Sun <note>original: "Arka-kendra-adi-samsthe"</note>, the humility, wealth, knowledge, and intellectual skill are Lowly, Middling, or Best. This is what is said: When the Moon is in a Kendra <term>Kendra: 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th house</term> from the Sun, it is Adhama (Lowly) Yoga; in that, humility, wealth, knowledge, and skill are lowly. When the Moon is in a Panaphara <term>Panaphara: 2nd, 5th, 8th, or 11th house</term> from the Sun, it is Sama (Middling) Yoga; in that, humility etc. should be called middling. When the Moon is in an Apoklima <term>Apoklima: 3rd, 6th, 9th, or 12th house</term> from the Sun, it is Varishtha (Best) Yoga; in that, humility etc. should be called best. Thus it is said:
> "When the Moon is in a quadrant (Kendra) etc. from the Sun <note>original: "Sahasrarashmitashchandre"</note>, wealth, intellect, and skill are respectively diminished, middling, and best." So says the Parashari.

Regarding "Ahani" (by day): If during the day or night, the Moon is in its own division or in the Navamsha <term>Navamsha: a 1/9th divisional chart</term> of a great friend, and is aspected by Jupiter or Venus respectively. If by day the Moon is in its own or a great friend's division and is aspected by Jupiter, or if by night it is aspected by Venus, the person born becomes wealthy and happy. As it is said:
> "When the Moon is in its own division or a great friend's division during the day and is seen by Jupiter, the one born there is endowed with wealth and happiness.
> The Moon in its own or a great friend's division, seen by the Minister of the Demons (Venus), during the nights, creates fortune <unclear>filled with hunger and water (?)</unclear>." So says the Parashari. || 112 ||

If the Moon is in a Kendra (1, 4, 7, 10) from the Sun, it is Lowly (Adhama); if in a Panaphara (2, 5, 8, 11), it is Middling (Madhyama); if in an Apoklima (3, 6, 9, 12), it is Best (Varishtha) Yoga. As stated—

### Now, the Adhiyoga from the Moon (Chandradhiyoga).

When auspicious planets are in the seventh, sixth, and eighth houses from the Moon, it is the Adhiyoga of the Moon. In this yoga, the births of army commanders, royal ministers, and kings occur. Those born under it possess wealth, happiness, and prosperity; their enemies are destroyed, and they live long lives free from disease and fear. || 113 ||

Now the Adhiyoga from the Moon is explained: "By auspicious planets..." etc. From the Moon's position, in the seventh, sixth, and eighth houses, when auspicious planets (Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus) are placed as far as possible, it is Adhiyoga. This combination is named Adhiyoga. Its results are stated: in this Adhiyoga, the birth of a **Commander** (leader of the army), a **Minister** (royal counselor), or a **King** (ruler of the earth) occurs. One born in Adhiyoga becomes a king, a minister, or a commander. Furthermore, those born then possess wealth and happiness, have their enemies slain, are long-lived, and are free from the fear of disease. As it is said:

<margin>
"When auspicious planets are in the sixth, seventh, or eighth from the Moon, the person born should be known as a king, a minister, or an army leader. According to Badarayana <note>An ancient sage and authority on astrology</note>: If the auspicious planets are strong, one becomes a ruler of the earth; if of medium strength, a minister; and if of low strength, an army commander." || 113 ||
</margin>

<note>This diagram illustrates the planetary positions for Chandradhiyoga.</note>

**Notes**—If there are cruel planets <note>Malefics like Mars or Saturn</note> in the sixth, seventh, and eighth houses from the Moon, it is "Pap-adhiyoga" (Inauspicious Adhiyoga); with mixed planets (both cruel and auspicious), it is a "Mixed Yoga." This is based on the saying: "As with the auspicious, so it is said for the cruel and the mixed."

If auspicious planets are in the sixth, seventh, or eighth house from the Moon, "Adhiyoga" occurs. In this yoga, the birth of a commander, a royal minister, and a king takes place. Those born in this are endowed with wealth, happiness, and grandeur, and are without enemies, disease, or fear. || 113 ||

### Now, the Adhiyoga from the Ascendant (Lagnadhiyoga).

When auspicious planets are situated in the sixth, seventh, and eighth houses from the Ascendant (<term>Lagna</term>), and are not joined or aspected by cruel planets, and when cruel planets are absent from the fourth house, the famous Lagnadhiyoga occurs. || 114 ||

In Lagnadhiyoga, one becomes the author of many scientific treatises, is educated and humble, and holds a position of power. Such a person is a leader, free from deceit, a great soul, and endowed with fame, wealth, and virtues in the world. || 115 ||

Now the Adhiyoga from the Ascendant is explained: "From the Ascendant..." etc. From the birth-ascendant, by being situated in the sixth, seventh, and eighth houses, the auspicious planets (Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus) should not be joined by cruel planets, nor aspected by cruel planets; and the cruel planets should be excluded from the fourth house. This means: all auspicious planets should be in the 6th, 7th, and 8th houses from the Ascendant as far as possible...

### Commentary on Jataka Parijata

There should be no malefic planet <note>original: "papagraha"; planets like Mars or Saturn that are considered naturally harsh</note>, nor should there be the aspect of a malefic planet, and there should be no malefic planets in the fourth house. Then the famous **Lagna Adhi Yoga** is formed. As it is said:
> When the benefics <note>original: "saumya"; gentle planets like Jupiter, Venus, or Mercury</note> are situated in the 6th, 7th, and 8th houses from the Ascendant <note>original: "Lagna"</note>, and are not aspected by or joined with malefics, this is Lagna Adhi Yoga. If malefics are present, one is deprived of happiness. — *From Jatakadesha*.

The results of Lagna Adhi Yoga are explained in the following verses (114-115) which have a simple meaning.

**Notes**—It is nearly impossible for there to be no malefic planets or their aspects in all three houses (6th, 7th, and 8th) from the Ascendant. If malefics are placed in any house, some house will inevitably be aspected or occupied by them. Therefore, my intended meaning is that the 6th, 7th, and 8th houses should specifically be free from the conjunction of malefic planets.

If there are benefic planets in the 6th, 7th, and 8th positions from the Ascendant, and they are not aspected by or joined with malefics, and there is no malefic in the 4th house (the house of happiness), then **"Lagna Adhi Yoga"** occurs. || 114 ||

A person born in Lagna Adhi Yoga will be the author of many scientific treatises <note>original: "shastras"</note>, humble despite their learning, possessed of great power and authority, a leader, sincere, a great soul, and endowed with fame, wealth, and virtues in the world. || 115 ||

## The Gaja-Kesari Yoga
<note>Gaja-Kesari translates to "Elephant-Lion," symbolizing great strength and dominance.</note>

> When Jupiter <note>original: "Devaguru"</note> is situated in a quadrant <note>term: Kendra; the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note> from the Moon <note>original: "Mriganka"</note>, they call it Gaja-Kesari. Or, if the Moon is aspected by Venus, Jupiter, and Mercury, and these planets are neither in their debilitation <note>term: Neecha; the sign where a planet is weakest</note> nor combust <note>term: Asta; too close to the Sun to be visible</note>, it is Gaja-Kesari. || 116 ||
> One born in Gaja-Kesari Yoga will be energetic, possessed of wealth and grain, intelligent, virtuous, and a favorite of the King. || 117 ||

Now the Gaja-Kesari Yoga is described. From wherever the Moon is placed, if Jupiter is in a quadrant from it, the authorities say **Gaja-Kesari Yoga** is formed. Furthermore, if the **Moon** is aspected by **Venus, Jupiter, and Mercury**—provided they are not **debilitated or combust**—then **Gaja-Kesari Yoga** occurs. The results are explained in the simple verses 116-117.

If Jupiter is in a quadrant from the Moon, **"Gaja-Kesari"** Yoga occurs. If Venus, Jupiter, and Mercury are not in their debilitated signs or combust, and they aspect the Moon, **"Gaja-Kesari"** Yoga occurs. || 116 ||

A person born in Gaja-Kesari Yoga is energetic, possesses wealth and grain, is highly intelligent, virtuous, and dear to the King. || 117 ||

## The Amala Yoga
<note>Amala means "stainless" or "pure."</note>

> If at the time of birth, a benefic planet is placed in the 10th house <note>original: "Karma-sthana"</note> from either the Moon or the Ascendant, the person's "stainless" (Amala) fame shall remain on earth until the end of their life, and their prosperity shall never perish. || 118 ||
> When the 10th house from the Ascendant or the Moon is joined by a benefic, this yoga is called Amala; one's fame lasts as long as the moon and stars. || 119 ||
> Respected by kings, a great enjoyer of life, a donor, dear to kinsmen, and a benefactor of others is the one born in Amala Yoga. || 120 ||

Now he describes the fruitful **Amala Yoga** <note>Amala means "spotless" or "pure"</note>—with the three verses beginning with "Whose," etc. If at the time of a person's birth, a benefic planet (Mercury, Jupiter, or Venus) is situated in the tenth house from the Moon-sign <note>original: "Shashi-lagna" or "Chandra-lagna"</note>, then the yoga named **Amala** occurs. For one born at that time, throughout their entire life <note>original: "until the end of life"</note>, their spotless fame shall remain imperishable upon the earth.

Their fame shall last as long as the moon and stars—meaning that as long as the moon and stars exist (until the end of the cosmic cycle), their fame remains in the world. The rest is self-explanatory. || 118-120 ||

One who has a benefic planet in the tenth house from the Moon at birth possesses a pure reputation that remains on earth, and they enjoy indestructible wealth throughout their life. || 118 ||

If the tenth house from the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the rising sign on the eastern horizon at birth</term> or the Moon is occupied by a benefic planet, the 'Amala' yoga is formed. The fame of a person born in this yoga remains steady as long as the moon and stars exist. He is honored by kings, a great enjoyer of pleasures, a donor, beloved by his kinsmen, philanthropic, and virtuous. || 119-120 ||

### Now, the Vasi and related Yogas.

By planets situated in the houses of expenditure and wealth from the Sun, the Vasi, Veshi, and Ubhayachari yogas are formed. If these planets are in their own signs, friends' signs, or exaltation signs, those born become endowed with great wealth and happiness, equal to kings. || 121 ||

Now he describes the **Vasi**, **Veshi**, and **Ubhayachari** yogas—with the verse "Expenditure," etc. From the Sun <note>original: "Dinesha," Lord of the Day</note>, the Vasi and Veshi yogas occur through planets in the houses of expenditure <note>12th house</note> and wealth <note>2nd house</note>. When there is a planet in the 12th house from the Sun and the 2nd house is empty, it is **Vasi Yoga**; when there is a planet in the 2nd house from the Sun and the 12th is empty, it is **Veshi Yoga**. By being situated in both places—meaning when there are planets in both the 2nd and 12th houses from the Sun—it should be known as **Ubhayachari Yoga**. In all three yogas, if the planets are in their own houses, a friend's house, or their sign of exaltation, then the men being born become endowed with much wealth and happiness and are equal to kings. || 121 ||

If there is a planet in the 12th from the Sun, it is 'Vasi' yoga; if in the 2nd, it is 'Veshi' yoga; and if there are planets in both the 12th and 2nd houses, it is 'Ubhayachari' yoga. If those planets are in their own signs, a friend's sign, or are exalted, the individuals born under these conditions are equal to kings, possessing great wealth and happiness. || 121 ||

### Results of Vasi and related Yogas—

One born in a benefic Veshi yoga is well-behaved, eloquent, wealthy, fearless, and a conqueror of enemies. If formed by a malefic planet, they are attached to wicked people, sinful, and devoid of wealth and happiness. || 122 ||
In Vasi yoga joined by a benefic, one is skillful, a donor, and rich in learning, wit, happiness, wealth, fame, and strength. If joined by a malefic, they may go abroad, be very foolish, lustful, interested in others' wives, and have a deformed face. || 123 ||
Those born in Ubhayachari joined by benefics are kings or equal to them in wealth, happiness, character, and compassion. If in a malefic Ubhayachari, they perform sinful deeds, are overcome by disease, engaged in others' work, and are poor. || 124 ||

Now he describes the results of the Vasi and other yogas with the three verses beginning "One born," etc. There, based on the distinction between benefics and malefics—meaning whether the planet causing the yoga is a benefic or a malefic—the respective results mentioned should be stated separately. These verses are clear in their meaning.

Notes—When planets are in the 2nd, 12th, or both from the Moon, they are known as Sunapha, Anapha, and Dhurudhura respectively—

Just as these occur [in relation to the Moon], similarly here, when planets occupy the second, the twelfth, or both houses from the Sun, they are to be known as **Veshi**, **Vasi**, and **Ubhayachari** yogas respectively. Furthermore, just as in the *Anapha* and other lunar yogas where the Sun is excluded from being a causative planet, here in the *Veshi* and related yogas, the Moon must be excluded from being the causative planet. So says <term>Parashara</term> <note>A foundational sage in Indian astrology, credited with the Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra</note>—

<margin>By the 12th and the end...</margin>
When planets other than the Moon occupy the twelfth house from the Sun, it is *Vasi*; when in the second house, it is *Veshi*. When planets occupy both [the 2nd and 12th], it is called *Ubhayachari* yoga by the ancients.

And likewise in the *Jatakadesha*:
> "Planets in the 12th from the Sun create *Vasi*;
> in the 2nd house, excluding the Moon, they create *Veshi*.
> When planets are situated in both, they are called
> *Ubhayachari* yogas." || 122-124 ||

<note>The page contains three astrological charts (Kundalis) demonstrating the placement of planets for specific yogas.</note>

A person born in a **Veshi Yoga** <note>original: "Veshi Yoga"; a configuration where a planet is in the 2nd house from the Sun</note> joined by a benefic planet will be well-behaved, an eloquent speaker, wealthy, fearless, and a conqueror of enemies. If the *Veshi Yoga* is joined by a malefic planet, the native will be a servant of wicked <unclear>speech</unclear>, a sinful soul, and destitute of wealth and happiness. || 122 ||

A native born with a **Vasi Yoga** <note>original: "Vasi Yoga"; a configuration where a planet is in the 12th house from the Sun</note> joined by a benefic planet will be clever, charitable, learned, always joyful, supremely happy, famous, and strong. If that same yoga is joined by a malefic planet, the native will live in a foreign land, be utterly foolish, lustful, murderous in intent, and have a distorted face. || 123 ||

A child born in an **Ubhayachari Yoga** <note>original: "Ubhayachari Yoga"; when planets occupy both the 2nd and 12th houses from the Sun</note> joined by benefic planets will be the best among men, equal to kings, possessed of all good qualities and character, and have a heart filled with compassion. If that same yoga is joined by malefic planets, the man will be a sinner, sickly, a servant to others, and impoverished. || 124 ||

### Now, the Shubha and other Yogas.

If at the time of birth the Ascendant is occupied by benefics or malefics, then [Shubha or Ashubha yogas occur].
When malefic or benefic planets occupy the 12th and 2nd houses from the Ascendant, they are called **Papakartari** and **Saumyakartari** [Benefic-Scissor] yogas. || 125 ||

One born in a *Shubha* [Benefic] yoga is eloquent, endowed with beauty, character, and virtue.
One born in an *Ashubha* [Malefic] yoga is lustful, a performer of sinful deeds, and eats the food of others. || 126 ||

One born in a *Shubhakartari* yoga possesses great luster, wealth, and strength.
In a *Papakartari* yoga, one becomes a sinner, a beggar, and remains filthy. || 127 ||

Now he describes the *Shubha-Ashubha* and *Shubhakartari-Papakartari* yogas with the verses starting "Shubhashubhadhye..." etc. When the birth ascendant is joined by a benefic planet, it is *Shubha Yoga*; when joined by a malefic, it is *Ashubha Yoga*. When malefics are situated in the 12th (expenditure) and 2nd (wealth) houses from the Ascendant, it is *Papakartari*; when benefics are so situated, it is *Shubhakartari*. Alternatively, if a malefic is in the 12th and a benefic in the 2nd, or vice versa, it should be called **Mishrakartari** <note>Mixed-Scissor yoga</note>. The results of these four stated yogas are clear. || 125-127 ||

# Chapter 7: On Royal Combinations (Raja Yoga)

If the birth <term>Ascendant (Lagna)</term> <note>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</note> is occupied by a <term>benefic planet</term> <note>Naturally auspicious planets like Jupiter, Venus, Mercury, or a waxing Moon</note>, it is a "Benefic Combination." If it is occupied by a <term>malefic planet</term> <note>Naturally harsh planets like Saturn, Mars, or the Sun</note>, it is an "Inauspicious Combination." If malefic planets occupy both the 12th and 2nd houses from the Ascendant, it is called <term>Papa-Kartari</term> <note>Literally 'Scissor' yoga; the house is 'snipped' between two harsh influences</note>. If benefic planets occupy those positions, it is a <term>Saumya-Kartari</term> (Gentle Scissor) combination. || 125 ||

A man born under a Benefic Combination is eloquent, handsome, virtuous, well-behaved, and full of good qualities. One born under a Malefic Combination is lustful, sinful, and lives off the wealth of others. || 126 ||

A person born in the *Saumya-Kartari* combination is radiant, wealthy, and very powerful. One born in the *Papa-Kartari* combination is a sinner, a beggar, and possesses a clouded or impure mind. || 127 ||

### Now, the Mountain Combination (Parvata Yoga)

If benefic planets are situated in the <term>Quadrants</term> <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses of a birth chart</note> and the 6th and 8th houses are either empty or occupied by benefics, the "Mountain" (*Parvata*) yoga is formed. Alternatively, if the lords of the 1st and 12th houses are in Quadrants relative to each other and are aspected by friendly planets, it is also called *Parvata* yoga. || 128 ||

One born in the Mountain yoga is fortunate, fond of learning and humor, and is a donor. He may be lustful and fond of playing with other men's wives, but he will be radiant, famous, and the leader of a town or city. || 129 ||

Now the author explains the Mountain yoga: "If benefics..." etc. Benefic planets should be in the Quadrants, and the 6th and 8th houses should be "pure" (free of planets) or occupied by benefics. Regarding "the lords of the 1st and 12th": if the lord of the Ascendant and the lord of the 12th house are in mutual Quadrants—meaning one is in a 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th position relative to the other—and both are viewed by friendly planets, then *Parvata* yoga is formed. As the <term>Yavana</term> <note>Refers to 'Yavanajataka,' an ancient Indian astrological text influenced by Greek (Ionian) traditions</note> says:
> "If all the lords of the planets in the Ascendant, 7th, 10th, and 4th houses are auspicious and not malefic, know this to be the Mountain yoga, fit for the birth of powerful kings." <note>original: "लग्नास्तमपुंरण्याः प्रशस्ताः सर्वे ग्रहेन्द्रा इह चेदपापाः । तं पर्वतं विद्धि बलाधिकानां महीपतीनां प्रसवाय योग्यम् ॥"</note>

And in the *Jataka Desha*: "If the 1st, 7th, 10th, and 4th houses are occupied by planets, and the 12th and 9th houses are pure, whatever yoga arises is called *Parvata*." <note>original: "उदयास्तं कर्महिबुके प्रहयुक्ते रि:फैनैवैर्नैः शुद्धे । यः कश्चिद्भवमगतो योगोऽयं पर्वतो नाम"</note>

The results for one born in the Mountain yoga are stated in the verse beginning with "Fortunate..." which has a straightforward meaning. || 128-129 ||

If benefic planets are in the <term>Kendra</term><note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses of a birth chart, considered the pillars of strength.</note> and the 8th house is unoccupied or joined by benefics, the "Parvata" (Mountain) Yoga is formed. A person born in this Parvata Yoga is fortunate, immersed in the joy of learning, a donor, lustful, prone to wandering after others' wives, radiant, famous, and the chief leader of a village. || 129 ||

### Now, the Kahala Yoga.

> If the <term>Guru-Bandhu-Nathau</term><note>The lords of the 9th and 4th houses.</note> are in mutual Kendras and the Lord of the Ascendant is strong, it is Kahala Yoga. Or, if the Lord of the 4th house is in its exaltation or its own sign and is joined by or aspected by the Lord of the 10th house, such a Yoga occurs. || 130 ||

> The man born in Kahala Yoga is energetic, courageous, foolish, endowed with a four-fold army <note>Traditional Indian military: chariots, elephants, cavalry, and infantry.</note>, and the lord of several villages. || 131 ||

Now the Kahala Yoga is explained—*Anyonya* etc. <term>Guru-Bandhu-Nathau</term> = the lords of the 9th and 4th houses; <term>Anyonya-Kendra-Grihagau</term> = should be placed in mutual Kendras, meaning one is in a Kendra from the other. If the <term>Lagnadhipe</term> = Lord of the Ascendant, is <term>Balyute</term> = endowed with positional strength etc., then "Kahala" Yoga occurs. Another variation is stated—<term>Karmeshwarena</term> etc. If the <term>Sukha-Pati</term> = Lord of the 4th house, is in <term>Svocche</term> = its own exaltation sign, or <term>Swake</term> = its own house, and is joined by or aspected by the <term>Karmeshwarena</term> = Lord of the 10th house, then "Kahala" Yoga occurs. As stated in the *Jatakadesha*:

> "When the lords of the 4th and 9th houses are in mutual Kendras and the Lord of the Ascendant is strong, the Yoga is named Kahala."

The result of Kahala Yoga is stated in the verse beginning with *Ojasvi* (Energetic) in plain meaning. || 130-131 ||

---

If the Lord of the 9th and the Lord of the 4th are in mutual Kendras and the Lord of the Ascendant is strong, "Kahala" Yoga occurs. If the Lord of the 4th is in its exaltation or its own house and is joined or aspected by the Lord of the 10th, "Kahala" Yoga occurs. || 130 ||

A child born in Kahala Yoga is strong, courageous, foolish, possesses a four-fold army, and is the master of some villages. || 131 ||

### Now, the Malika Yoga.

> If the seven planets occupy the seven houses starting from the Ascendant, the one born is a king, master of many elephants and horses. If starting from the 2nd house, he is a master of treasures, devoted to his father, steady, handsome, virtuous, and an emperor among men. || 132 ||

> When born in a Malika starting from the 3rd house, he is a king, brave, wealthy, yet sickly. If from the 4th house, he enjoys the fortune of many lands, is intent on great charity, and is a king. || 133 ||

If from the 5th house, the Malika makes one a king, a performer of sacrifices, and famous. If born from the 9th house, he may attain wealth and happiness but sometimes becomes poor. If the planetary garland (Malika) starts from the 10th house, he has associations with many women and is a king.

# Chapter 7: On Royal Yogas (Raja Yoga)

> From the eighth house, one becomes long-lived but devoid of wealth, a leader among men yet conquered by women. || 134 ||
> From the ninth house (Dharma), one becomes a garland of Brahman <note>original: "Brahmamalika"</note>, a treasury of virtues, a performer of sacrifices, an ascetic, and all-powerful.
> From the tenth house (Karma), one is devoted to religious duties and deeds, and is highly honored by virtuous people.
> <gloss>11</gloss>

> <gloss>12</gloss>
> Born from the twelfth house (Loss), one spends much wealth but becomes worthy of worship everywhere. || 135 ||

Now the author describes the **Malika Yoga** <term>Malika Yoga: A "garland" configuration where seven planets occupy seven consecutive houses</term> through the four verses starting with "From the Ascendant" (Lagnadi). Here, the Malika Yoga is described starting from each individual house. For instance, if the seven planets are situated one by one in each house starting from the Ascendant (Lagna) up to the seventh house, it is called **Lagna Malika**. If the seven planets are situated similarly starting from the second house up to the eighth, it is **Vitta Malika** (Wealth Garland). In this way, a Malika should be understood for every house. The results for each specific Malika Yoga have been stated separately by the teacher, and their meaning is quite clear. || 132–135 ||

---

If seven planets are placed in seven consecutive houses starting from any house, the Malika Yoga related to that house occurs. For example, if there are seven planets in the seven houses starting from the Ascendant, the **"Lagna Malika"** yoga is formed. A man born under this yoga becomes a king and the owner of many elephants and horses. If the planets are in the seven houses starting from the second (Wealth), he becomes wealthy, devoted to his father, patient, handsome, virtuous, and an emperor among men. || 132 ||

If one is born in a **Vikrama Malika** (starting from the 3rd house), he becomes a powerful king, wealthy, but prone to illness. If the seven planets are in the houses starting from the fourth (Happiness/Sukha), he becomes a king who is fortunate in many countries and a great donor. || 133 ||

If born in a Malika starting from the fifth house (Son/Putra), he becomes a king who performs sacrifices or becomes famous. If the Malika begins in the sixth house, the person born may sometimes obtain wealth and happiness and sometimes be impoverished. A person born in a Malika starting from the seventh house (Partnership) becomes the master of many women and a king. A person born in the Malika of the eighth house is long-lived, poor, a leader of men, but is defeated by women. || 134 ||

One born in the **Dharma Malika** (starting from the 9th house) is a repository of virtues, a performer of sacrifices, an ascetic, and capable. One born in the **Karma Malika** (starting from the 10th house) is absorbed in religious deeds and is well-honored by the righteous. One born in the **Labha Malika** (starting from the 11th house) is the owner of gems as sharp as weapons and is expert in all works. One born in the **Rihpha Malika** (starting from the 12th house) spends a lot of money and is worshipped everywhere. || 135 ||

### Now, the Chamara Yoga.

> If the Lord of the Ascendant <note>The planet ruling the first house of the zodiac chart.</note> is placed in a quadrant <note>Houses 1, 4, 7, or 10.</note>, is in its sign of exaltation, and is aspected by Jupiter, the combination is called **Chamara Yoga**. Alternatively, if two benefic planets are situated in the first, seventh, ninth, or tenth houses, it is also **Chamara**. || 136 ||
>
> One born in the **Chamara** yoga is honored by kings, is a scholar, an eloquent speaker, a wise man, or a ruler of the earth. He will be all-knowing, an authority on the *Vedas* and *Shastras* <note>Sacred scriptures and scientific treatises.</note>, and will live in this world for seventy years. || 137 ||

Now the author describes the **Chamara Yoga** and its results in the two preceding verses. *In its exaltation* = having reached its highest point of strength; when the Lord of the Ascendant is in a quadrant (any of the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses) and is *aspected by Jupiter*—meaning seen by the planet Jupiter—the yoga named **Chamara** occurs. He mentions another version: if in the Ascendant, or the *Kalatra* = the 7th house, or the 9th, or in the *Svaspada* = the 10th house, two benefics are placed, it is **Chamara Yoga**. The results are explained in the verses which are clear in meaning. || 136-137 ||

If the Lord of the Ascendant is in its exaltation sign, situated in a quadrant, and seen by Jupiter, then **"Chamara"** yoga occurs. If there are two benefic planets in the 1st, 7th, 9th, or 10th houses, it is **Chamara Yoga**. || 136 ||

A person born in Chamara Yoga is respected by royalty, a scholar, an orator, a pundit, or a king; he is omniscient, an authority on Vedic scriptures, and lives for 70 years. || 137 ||

---

### Now, the Shankha Yoga.

> If the lords of the 5th and 6th houses are in mutual quadrants and the Lord of the Ascendant is powerful, it is **Shankha Yoga**. Alternatively, they say it occurs when the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the 10th are in moveable signs <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn.</note> and the Lord of the 9th is powerful. || 138 ||
>
> One born in **Shankha** is fond of pleasures, compassionate, possesses wives, sons, wealth, and lands, and performs meritorious deeds. He is a knower of the scriptures, follows right conduct, performs good deeds, and lives in this world for eighty years. || 139 ||

Now he describes the **Shankha Yoga** <note>Shankha means "Conch," a symbol of purity and auspiciousness.</note> and its results. *Lords of the 5th and 6th* = the rulers of the house of children and the house of enemies; *in mutual quadrants* = if they are in quadrants from each other; and if the Lord of the Ascendant is endowed with *strength* (positional strength, etc.), the yoga named **Shankha** occurs. Now he gives another version: when the Lord of the Ascendant and the *Lord of the Sky* = the ruler of the 10th house are in *moveable signs* (any of the signs 1, 4, 7, or 10), and the *Lord of Fortune* = the ruler of the 9th house is powerful, the wise say it is likewise **Shankha Yoga**. The results are stated in the verse beginning "One born in Shankha," which is clear in meaning. || 138-139 ||

# Chapter 7: On Royal Unions (Raja Yoga)

If the lord of the 5th house <note>the house of children and intelligence</note> and the lord of the 6th house <note>the house of obstacles</note> are positioned in mutual angles (Kendras) and the lord of the Ascendant (Lagna) is strong, the **"Conch" (Shankha) Yoga** is formed. Alternatively, if the lord of the Ascendant and the lord of the 10th house are in movable signs and the lord of the 9th house <note>the house of fortune</note> is powerful, the **Shankha Yoga** occurs. || 138 ||

One born under the Shankha Yoga is fond of pleasures, compassionate, wealthy, blessed with children and lands, a performer of meritorious deeds, possesses conduct and saintly actions guided by knowledge of the scriptures, and lives for 80 years in this world.

### Now, the Kettle-drum (Bheri) Yoga.

-> If planets are situated in the 2nd, 12th, 1st, and 7th houses, and the lord of the 10th house is endowed with strength, the Bheri Yoga is formed. Alternatively, if Venus and the lord of the Ascendant are in an angle (Kendra) from Jupiter, and the lord of the 9th house is powerful, the same should be declared. || 140 || <-

-> Those born under Bheri Yoga are long-lived, free from the fear of disease, and become lords of men (kings). They are famous and possessed of much wealth, land, sons, and wives. They are of good conduct, great happiness, and valor; they are noble-minded, skillful in all tasks, and of high birth. || 141 || <-

Now the Bheri Yoga and its results are explained: *If planets are in the 2nd, 12th, 1st, and 7th houses*—meaning the houses of wealth, loss, the self, and partnership—and the *lord of the 10th* (the house of action/career) is *strong*, Bheri Yoga occurs. Furthermore, if from *Jupiter*, *Venus and the lord of the Ascendant* are placed in an *angle* (the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th positions from him), and the *lord of the 9th* is *strong*, it is also called Bheri Yoga. The results of this Bheri Yoga, such as *long life*, etc., are described as bringing great happiness. || 140-141 ||

If planets are in the 2nd, 12th, Ascendant, and 7th houses and the lord of the 10th is strong, the 'Bheri' Yoga occurs. If Venus and the lord of the Ascendant are in an angle from Jupiter and the lord of the 9th is powerful, the "Bheri" Yoga occurs.
The person born in Bheri Yoga is long-lived, free from disease and fear, a king, joined with much wealth, land, sons, and wife, famous, well-behaved, fully happy, joined with prowess, noble, skillful in every work, and of noble lineage. || 141 ||

---

### Now, the Drum (Mridanga) Yoga.

-> If the lord of the Navamsha <note>a 1/9th divisional chart used for fine-tuning strength</note> occupied by an exalted planet is situated in an angle or a trine (Kendra or Kona), and is placed in its own or exalted sign and is powerful, and the lord of the Ascendant is also strong, the Mridanga Yoga is formed. It bestows auspiciousness, royal status, and fame. || 142 || <-

Now the Mridanga Yoga is described: *The lord of the Navamsha of an exalted planet*—meaning the planet that rules the specific 1/9th division where an exalted planet is sitting—if that ruler is in an *angle or trine* (1, 4, 7, 10, 5, or 9) from the Ascendant, and is *in its own or exalted sign* and powerful, and the *lord of the Ascendant* is strong...

<term>Raja Yoga: "Royal Union," a planetary combination indicating high status or success.</term>
<term>Bheri Yoga: Named after a traditional kettle-drum, signifying fame that resonates.</term>
<term>Mridanga Yoga: Named after a double-headed drum, signifying rhythm and harmony in life.</term>
<term>Shankha Yoga: Named after the sacred conch shell, signifying purity and victory.</term>
<term>Karmadhipa: The lord of the 10th house, governing career and public actions.</term>
<term>Kendra: The "angles" or pillars of a chart (houses 1, 4, 7, 10).</term>
<term>Bhagyesha: The lord of the 9th house, governing fortune and dharma.</term>

When [the planet] is so joined, the **Mridanga Yoga** <note>literally "Drum Union," named after the auspicious sound of a drum</note> occurs. Regarding what was said about the "lord of the exaltation sign navamsha," if two or many planets are in exaltation, the strongest one should be considered. The result of Mridanga Yoga is stated: it bestows auspiciousness, beauty, and fame equal to a king; this is quite clear. || 142 ||

If the lord of the Navamsha <note>a 1/9th divisional chart used for fine-tuning strength</note> occupied by an exalted planet is placed in a trine or a center house <note>houses 1, 4, 7, 10 (centers) or 1, 5, 9 (trines)</note>, and is in its own exaltation or its own sign, and is strong, and the lord of the Ascendant is also strong, then **"Mridanga"** Yoga is formed. This Mridanga Yoga gives auspiciousness, beauty, and fame similar to a king. || 142 ||

### Now, the Shrinatha Yoga.

> When the Lord of the Seventh is in the Tenth house, and the Lord of the Tenth is in its exaltation joined with the Lord of the Ninth,
> The **Shrinatha Yoga** <note>named after the Lord of Fortune/Vishnu</note> is then formed, giving good results; the person born is a protector of men, equal to Indra <note>the King of the Gods</note>. || 143 ||

Now the Shrinatha Yoga is described—"When the Lord of the Seventh...": When the Lord of the Seventh house (the Lord of Desires) has gone to the Tenth house (the house of Action), and the Lord of the Tenth is in its own exaltation sign joined with the Lord of the Ninth (the Lord of Fortune), the auspicious Shrinatha Yoga occurs. At that time (the period characterized by Shrinatha Yoga), the person born becomes a protector of men—a king—equal to Indra. || 143 ||

If the Lord of the Seventh is in the Tenth, and the Lord of the Tenth is situated in its exaltation sign along with the Lord of the Ninth, then **"Shrinatha"** Yoga occurs. The person born under this yoga is a king equal to Indra. || 143 ||

### Now, the Sharada Yoga.

> The yoga named **Sharada** <note>associated with the goddess of wisdom and the autumn season</note> occurs when the Lord of the Tenth is in the Fifth, and Mercury
> and the Sun are in center houses, the latter in its own house with great strength.
> Or if Jupiter is in a trine from the Moon, and Mars is in a trine from Mercury,
> or if Jupiter is in the eleventh house from Mercury, it is called Sharada. || 144 ||
> Those born in the world under the name Sharada are devoted to the happiness of wife, children, and kin, and to beauty and virtue; they are dear to kings, devoted to teachers, priests, and gods;
> they are knowers of sciences, wealthy in patience, character, and the power of penance, and devoted to their own duty. || 145 ||

Now the Sharada Yoga and its results are stated—"The yoga...": When the Lord of the Tenth is in the Fifth house, and Mercury (the son of the Moon) is in a center (houses 1, 4, 7, 10), and the Sun (the Lord of Day) is in its own house (Leo) endowed with great strength (full power), the yoga named Sharada occurs. Another version of the yoga is stated: when Jupiter (the Teacher of Indra) is in a trine (houses 5, 9) from wherever the Moon is located, and Mars is in a trine from Mercury, or if Jupiter (the Minister of the Gods) is in the eleventh (the house of Gain) from Mercury, that is the yoga known as Sharada. The result of Sharada Yoga is stated starting with "Wife, children..." and is quite clear. || 144-145 ||

## Chapter on Royal Unions (Raja Yoga) || 7 ||

1. ### Now, the Fish Union (Matsya Yoga).

> If malefic planets are in the Ascendant and the 9th house, and the 5th house is occupied by both benefic and malefic planets, and malefic planets are situated in the "four-cornered" houses <note>the 4th and 8th houses</note>, this union is called **Matsya** <note>Sanskrit for "Fish"</note>. || 146 ||
> One born of the Matsya Yoga is a knower of time <note>an astrologer or one with great foresight</note>, an ocean of compassion, virtuous, intelligent, strong, and handsome. He is famous, learned, and an ascetic. || 147 ||

Now the Matsya Yoga and its results are explained— **"If in the Ascendant and 9th..."** In the Ascendant and the 9th house from the Ascendant.

<margin>

Its result, "knower of time," is stated in the plain meaning. || 146-147 ||

The person born in Matsya Yoga is a knower of time, extremely kind, virtuous, wise, handsome, successful, learned, and an ascetic. || 147 ||

> If benefic planets are in the 7th, 5th, and 6th houses, situated in their signs of exaltation, own signs, or friendly divisions; and malefic planets are in the 3rd, 11th, and the Ascendant, staying in friendly or exalted signs, it is **Kurma Yoga** <note>Sanskrit for "Tortoise"</note>. || 148 ||
> One born in Kurma Yoga has world-renowned fame, enjoys royal pleasures, is highly righteous, and is dominated by the quality of goodness <term>Sattva-guna: the quality of purity, harmony, and wisdom</term>. He is brave, happy, a well-spoken benefactor, or a leader of men. || 149 ||

Now Kurma Yoga and its results are discussed— **"In the 7th..."** Having gone to their own, exalted, or friendly divisions and signs...

If benefic planets <note>planets like Jupiter, Venus, or Mercury that bring positive influence</note> are situated in a friend's house, their own sign, or their own <term>Navamsha</term> <note>a 1/9th divisional chart used for fine-tuning planetary strength</note> and occupy the 7th, 5th, or 6th houses; and if malefic planets <note>planets like Saturn or Mars that bring challenging influence</note> are placed in their exaltation or a friend's sign while occupying the 3rd, 11th, or 1st (Ascendant) houses, then the **Kurma Yoga** <note>literally "Tortoise Combination"</note> is formed. The result of this, as stated in the plain meaning, is that the person becomes world-renowned.

If benefic planets in their exaltation, a friend's division, or their own sign are in the 7th, 5th, and 6th houses, and malefic planets are in the 3rd, 11th, and the Ascendant in their friend's house or exaltation, the "Kurma" Yoga occurs. || 148 ||

### Now, the Khadga Yoga.

-> If the Lord of the 9th house is in the 2nd house, and the Lord of the 2nd house is in the 9th house, <-
-> and the Lord of the Ascendant is in a <term>Kendra</term> or <term>Kona</term>, it is called Khadga Yoga. <- || 150 ||
<note>Kendra refers to the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses; Kona refers to the 1st, 5th, or 9th houses.</note>

Men born in the Khadga <note>Sword</note> Yoga are endowed with the essence of the Vedas, scriptures, and all sacred traditions; they are attached to wisdom, majesty, strength, valor, and happiness. They are free from envy, great in their own prowess, skillful, and grateful. || 151 ||

Now, the plain meaning of the verse explains the Khadga Yoga and its results clearly: If the Lord of Fortune (9th) is in the house of Wealth (2nd), the Lord of Wealth (2nd) is in the sign of Fortune (9th), and the Lord of the Ascendant (1st) is situated in a <term>Kendra</term> or <term>Kona</term>, then Khadga Yoga occurs.

A person born in this Khadga Yoga will be a knower of the meaning of the Vedas, and a knower of the essence of all scriptures, astrology, and the <term>Tantras</term>. He remains happy through his intellect, majesty, strength, and valor. He is devoid of malice and is superior through his own efforts. A man born in Khadga Yoga is skillful in his duties and grateful. || 151 ||

### Now, the Lakshmi Yoga.

-> If the Lord of the 9th house is in a <term>Kendra</term>, in its <term>Mulatrikona</term> sign, or in its highest exaltation, <-
-> and the Lord of the Ascendant is powerful, it is called Lakshmi Yoga. <- || 152 ||
<note>Mulatrikona is a specific favorable placement for a planet, stronger than its own sign but less than exaltation.</note>

# Chapter on Royal Yoga || 7 ||

Now he describes the Lakshmi Yoga and its results—

In the center <note>original: "kendra"; refers to the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses of a horoscope</note>. When the Lord of Fortune <note>original: "bhagyesha"; the ruler of the 9th house</note> is situated in its Root-Trine <note>original: "mulatrikona"; a specific favorable sign position</note>, or is in its highest exaltation and placed in a Center, and the Lord of the Ascendant <note>original: "lagnadhipa"; the ruler of the 1st house</note> is endowed with strength <note>original: "baladhye"; possessing positional or other types of astrological strength</note>, the Lakshmi Yoga is formed. This has been stated by the wise. As it is said:
**"When the Lord of Fortune is in its highest exaltation, placed in a Center and aspected by a benefic, and the Lord of the Ascendant is strong, it is called Lakshmi Yoga."**
->From the *Jataka Desha* <note>A classical astrological treatise</note>.<-

And also—**"If both the Lord of Fortune and Venus are in their own signs or exaltation and occupy a Trine or a Center, it is called Lakshmi."**
->From the *Phaladeepika* <note>A famous 16th-century astrology text</note>.<-

The result of Lakshmi Yoga is described in simple terms in the verse beginning with "Delightful in qualities" || 152-153 ||
If the Lord of the 9th house is in its highest exaltation or Root-Trine and situated in a Center, and the Lord of the 1st house is strong, then "Lakshmi Yoga" occurs || 152 ||
In this Lakshmi Yoga, the person born will possess beautiful qualities, be the master of many lands, be endowed with knowledge and fame, and have a form as beautiful as the God of Love <note>Kamadeva</note>. He will be worshiped by kings in the ten directions, be an eminent ruler, and have many wives and sons || 153 ||

### Now, the Kusuma Yoga.

> **If Venus is in a Center in a fixed sign, the Moon is in a Trine other than the auspicious one <note>meaning the 5th house</note>, and Saturn is in the house of honor <note>the 10th house</note>, this combination is Kusuma. || 154 ||**

> **The one born in Kusuma Yoga will be a donor, worshiped by the lords of the earth, an enjoyer, the chief among kings of great lineages, possessing great fame in the world, majestic, and a leader of men. || 155 ||**

Now he describes the Kusuma Yoga and its results—In a fixed sign <note>original: "sthira-lagna"; Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius</note>. When Venus <note>original: "bhrigau"</note> is situated in one of these and placed in a Center; and the Moon is in a Trine <note>original: "trikonondau"</note> other than the "auspicious" one (the word "Trine" refers to the 5th and 9th houses; here, by "other than the auspicious," the 5th house alone remains, meaning the Moon is in the 5th house); and Saturn <note>original: "saure"</note> has reached the house of honor <note>the 10th house</note>, this combination becomes Kusuma. Its result is self-evident || 154-155 ||

If in a fixed Ascendant, Venus is in a Center, the Moon is in the more auspicious Trine (i.e., the 5th house), and Saturn is in the 10th, this is "Kusuma" Yoga || 154 ||
A person born in Kusuma Yoga is charitable, honored by kings, an enjoyer of life, born in a noble family, a leader among kings, successful in all worlds, and a majestic ruler || 155 ||

Now the author describes the **Parijata Yoga**—**In the Ascendant—**
The Lord of the Ascendant <note>Lagnanatha: the planet ruling the rising sign</note> stays in a certain sign; the ruler of that sign, or the ruler of the sign where *that* second ruler stays, or the ruler of the Navamsha <note>term: Navamsha (a 1/9th divisional chart used for fine-tuning planetary strength)</note> of the Lord of the Ascendant's position—if any of these are placed in a Cardinal house <note>term: Kendra (houses 1, 4, 7, 10)</note> or a Trinal house <note>term: Trikona (houses 1, 5, 9)</note>, or if the planet is in its sign of Exaltation <note>highest point of strength</note>, then the "Parijata" Yoga is known to exist. 

For example: In this illustration, Mars is the Lord of the Aries Ascendant and is placed in Cancer. The Lord of Cancer, the Moon, is at ten degrees in Taurus. In the sign of Taurus at ten degrees, it is the Navamsha of Jupiter. Therefore, the Navamsha Lord Jupiter is in a Trine, and the Lord of Taurus, Venus, is also in a Cardinal house. Thus, the definition of Parijata is met in two ways. The result is as clearly stated. || 156-157 ||

Its result is clearly stated in the verse beginning with "Amorous," etc. || 158-159 ||

### Now, the Partial Incarnation Yoga (Anshavatar Yoga).

> When Venus and Jupiter are in center houses, Saturn is in its sign of exaltation <note>Saturn is exalted in Libra</note> and also in a center house, and the birth occurs in a Moveable Sign <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn</note> as the Ascendant, this is the Incarnation-born Yoga. || 160 ||
> One born in the Partial Incarnation Yoga becomes a person of holy fame, a traveler to sacred pilgrimage sites, a connoisseur of arts, passionate, a master of his time, self-controlled, a knower of Vedanta philosophy, an authority on the Vedas and Scriptures, and a bearer of royal fortune. || 161 ||

Now the Partial Incarnation Yoga and its results are explained.
**Venus and Jupiter** = Venus and Jupiter should be in center houses <note>Houses 1, 4, 7, or 10</note> and placed in Moveable Signs (as it was stated "in a Moveable Ascendant").
**Saturn** = Saturn, being in its exaltation in Libra and in a center house.
**Moveable Ascendant** = When the birth occurs in any of the signs of Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn as the Ascendant, then this **Incarnation-born** Yoga is formed. A man born in this Yoga becomes:
A person of holy fame, a pilgrim, an expert in arts, passionate, a creator of his own destiny <note>literally "time-maker"</note>, self-controlled, a scholar of Vedanta, authorized in the Vedas and Scriptures, and one who holds royal splendor. || 160-161 ||

If Venus and Jupiter are in the centers, Saturn is situated in a center in its exaltation, and the birth is in a Moveable Ascendant, then this is called the 'Avatar' (Incarnation) Yoga. || 160 ||
The person born in the Partial Incarnation Yoga is of holy character, a servant of pilgrimage sites, an artist, inclined toward love, timely, a master of his senses, a knower of the essence of the Vedas, an authority on the Vedas and Scriptures, and a man possessed of royal fortune. || 161 ||

### Now, the Hari-Hara-Vidhi Yogas <note>The Yogas of Vishnu, Shiva, and Brahma</note>.

> If the benefic planets are placed in the 2nd, 12th, and 8th houses from the Lord of the 2nd house;
> If Jupiter, the Moon, and Mercury are in the 4th, 9th, and 8th houses from the Lord of the 7th house;
> If the Sun, Venus, and Mars are in the 4th, 10th, and 11th houses from the Lord of the 1st house;
> These are called the Hari, Hara, and Brahma Yogas by the ancients. || 162 ||
> One born in the Hari-Hara-Vidhi Yoga is a master of all Vedic knowledge, a speaker of truth, endowed with all happiness, possessed of beautiful speech, of a passionate nature, a conqueror of the multitude of his enemies, a benefactor to all living beings, and a performer of holy deeds. || 163 ||

Now he describes the Yogas of Hari (Vishnu), Hara (Shiva), and Brahma and their results—starting with "from the Lord of Wealth."
**Hari Yoga:** From the **Lord of Wealth** = from the ruler of the 2nd house, if **Benefic Planets** = (as far as possible) are placed in the **2nd, 12th, and 8th houses**, then it is Hari Yoga.

**Hara Yoga:** From the **Lord of Desire** = from the ruler of the 7th house, if **Jupiter, the Moon, and Mercury** are in the **4th, 9th, and 8th houses**, then it is Hara Yoga.

**Brahma Yoga:** From the **Lord of the Body** = from the ruler of the Ascendant (1st house), if **the Sun, Venus, and Mars** are in the **4th, 10th, and 11th houses**, then it is the Yoga named **Brahma**. These three Yogas were proclaimed by the ancient Seers and Sages.

The results of these three mentioned Yogas are easy to understand. || 162-163 ||

A person born under any of these three—Hari, Hara, or Vidhi <note>another name for Brahma</note>—Yogas will be a knower of all scriptures, a speaker of truth, an enjoyer of all comforts, pleasant in speech, passionate, a conqueror of all enemies, a benefactor to all living beings, and a performer of virtuous deeds. || 163 ||

## Now, the Nabhasa Yogas.
<note>Nabhasa Yogas are "Celestial" combinations based on the overall pattern of planets in the sky, regardless of the specific houses they occupy.</note>

The Yupa, Ishu, Shakti, Yava, Danda, Gada, Samudra, Chatra, Ardhachandra, Shakata, Ambuja, and Pakshi Yogas;
The Nau, Chakra, Vajra, Hala, Karmuka, Kuta, Vapi, and Shringataka—these are the twenty varieties of **Akriti** <note>Shape-based</note> Yogas. || 164 ||
The **Ashraya** <note>Support-based</note> Yogas are called Rajju, Musala, and Nala. The two **Dala** <note>Leaf/Group-based</note> Yogas are Srak and Sarpa.
The **Sankhya** <note>Numerical</note> Yogas are seven in number, starting with Veena, followed by Damini, Pasha, Kedara, Shula, Yuga, and Golaka. || 165 ||

Now the Nabhasa Yogas are described. Among them, the twenty starting with Yupa are the *Akriti* (Shape) Yogas. The three starting with Rajju are the *Ashraya* (Support) Yogas. Srak and Sarpa are the two *Dala* (Group) Yogas. The seven starting with Veena are the *Sankhya* (Numerical) Yogas. Thus, there are four categories.

Specifically, the **Shape Yogas** are: 1. Yupa <note>Sacrificial Pillar</note>, 2. Ishu <note>Arrow</note>, 3. Shakti <note>Spear</note>, 4. Yava <note>Barley grain</note>, 5. Danda <note>Staff</note>, 6. Gada <note>Mace</note>, 7. Samudra <note>Ocean</note>, 8. Chatra <note>Umbrella</note>, 9. Ardhachandra <note>Half-moon</note>, 10. Shakata <note>Wagon</note>, 11. Ambuja <note>Lotus</note>, 12. Pakshi <note>Bird</note>, 13. Nau <note>Boat</note>, 14. Chakra <note>Wheel</note>, 15. Vajra <note>Thunderbolt</note>, 16. Hala <note>Plough</note>, 17. Karmuka <note>Bow</note>, 18. Kuta <note>Hammer/Peak</note>, 19. Vapi <note>Pond</note>, 20. Shringataka <note>Mountain peak/Triangle</note>. These are the twenty yogas.

The **Support Yogas** are: 1. Rajju <note>Rope</note>, 2. Nala <note>Reed</note>, 3. Musala <note>Pestle</note>. These are three.
The **Group Yogas** are: 1. Srak <note>Garland</note>, 2. Sarpa <note>Serpent</note>. These are two.
The **Numerical Yogas** are: 1. Veena <note>Lute</note>, 2. Varadama <note>Garland/Damini</note>, 3. Pasha <note>Noose</note>, 4. Kedara <note>Field</note>, 5. Shula <note>Trident</note>, 6. Yuga <note>Pair</note>, 7. Golaka <note>Sphere</note>. These are seven yogas. Their definitions and results will be explained hereafter. || 164-165 ||

<note>The text repeats the list in Hindi for clarity, which is translated above in the English explanation.</note>

### In the Horashastra—

Now the definitions of the three Support Yogas and the two Group Yogas are given:
The sage Garga stated that the **Rajju**, **Musala**, and **Nala** Yogas arise from the Moveable, Fixed, and Dual signs respectively.
Parashara stated that the **Srak** and **Sarpa** Yogas are formed by the presence of benefics or malefic planets in the angles (Kendras). || 166 ||

Regarding Rajju and the others: By "Moveable and others" <note>original: "चराद्यैः"</note> it means that when all planets are situated in Moveable, Fixed, or Dual signs, they respectively form the Rajju, Musala, and Nala Yogas.

## Chapter on Royal Combinations (Raja Yoga) || 7 ||

The Master Satyacharya <note>A renowned ancient authority on astrology</note> has described the combinations arising from the "shelter" or placement of planets in specific types of signs. "Rope" (*Rajju*) occurs through the movable signs. When all planets are situated in one, two, three, or four movable signs <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn</note>, and among them there are planets in dual or uncertain states, it is called the **"Rope" (*Rajju*)** combination. When all planets are in one, two, three, or four fixed signs <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius</note>, and they are exalted or strong, it is the **"Mace" (*Musala*)** combination. Similarly, if all planets are in dual-natured signs <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces</note>, it is the **"Reed" (*Nala*)** combination. Whether one, two, three, or all planets are joined, when they take shelter in these signs, they become appropriate to their nature. The Mace combination in fixed signs brings satisfaction and pride to those born under it. Those sheltered in dual-natured signs are said to be afflicted.

Regarding the "Group" (*Dala*) combinations, the poet-astrologers say: if all the primary planets are in the centers <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses of a horoscope, known as Kendras</note>, then the **"Garland" (*Srak* or *Mala*)** combination occurs. When all planets are in the centers and they are exclusively benefic <note>Gentle or auspicious planets like Jupiter or Venus</note>, it is the Garland. If they are all malefic <note>Harsh planets like Mars or Saturn</note> in the centers, then it is known as the **"Serpent" (*Sarpa*)** combination; this is the sequence taught by the wise Parashara.

Notes—The Moon attains the status of being either benefic or malefic depending on the distinction between the waxing and waning fortnights. Therefore, during the waxing phase, the Moon along with Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus are considered benefics in the four centers. During the waning phase, due to the lack of "gentleness" in the Moon, they may be considered malefic in the four centers; otherwise, one must discern the presence of three benefics or malefics in the centers. || 166 ||

If all planets are in movable signs, the **"Rope" (*Rajju*)** combination occurs. If all planets are in fixed signs, the **"Mace" (*Musala*)** combination occurs, and if all planets are in dual-natured signs, the **"Reed" (*Nala*)** combination occurs. These three "shelter-born" combinations were spoken of by Satyacharya. The "Group" (*Dala*) combinations are of two types: Garland and Serpent. If all benefic planets are in the centers and no malefic planets are in the centers, it is the **"Garland" (*Mala*)** combination. If all malefic planets are in the centers and no benefic planets are in the centers, it is the **"Serpent" (*Sarpa*)** combination. So said Parashara. || 166 ||

## From the Jataka Parijata with Commentary

Now, the author explains the reason why some ancient authorities did not mention certain *Ashraya* <note>Support-based</note> and *Dala* <note>Petal-based</note> combinations:

**The combinations arising from "Support" reach equality with the Barley, Lotus, Bolt, Egg, and Globe combinations. The two known as "Petal" are said to have the same fruits as those described for planets occupying the Centers; thus, others say they do not have separate results. || 167 ||**

**Commentary:** Regarding the "combinations": The three *Ashraya* combinations—*Rajju* <note>Rope</note>, *Musala* <note>Pestle</note>, and *Nala* <note>Reed</note>—attain equality (similarity) with the *Yava* <note>Barley</note>, *Abja* <note>Lotus</note>, *Vajra* <note>Bolt</note>, *Andaja* <note>Egg</note>, and *Golaka* <note>Globe</note> combinations. (How they reach equality should be seen in the definitions of the *Yava* and other combinations). Therefore, they were not mentioned by others. 

The two called *Dala*—namely *Srak* <note>Garland</note> and *Sarpa* <note>Serpent</note>—possess the results described for planets situated in the *Kendras* <term>Centers: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses of a horoscope</term>. The *Srak* combination is said to occur when benefics <note>auspicious planets</note> are in the Centers. The *Sarpa* combination is said to occur when malefic <note>inauspicious planets</note> are in the Centers. Because of the teaching that "Benefics in Centers and Trines are praised, while in those same places malefics would not be givers of good," benefics in Centers give good results and malefics give bad results. Therefore, those two (*Srak* and *Sarpa*) do not have separate results (as the meaning is already stated). This is what other wise men have said. The idea is that they did not mention them for fear of the fault of repetition. || 167 ||

<margin>The results of the Support combinations (Rope, Pestle, Reed) are similar to the results of the Barley, Lotus, Bolt, Egg, and Globe combinations; therefore, other teachers did not mention them. The Petal (Garland-Serpent) combinations have results identical to the results of benefics and malefics in Centers. Because there is no distinction in the results, the ancients did not mention the Petal combinations. (Commentary by S. Sh.)</margin>

Now, he describes the five combinations: *Gada* <note>Mace</note>, *Shakata* <note>Cart</note>, *Vihaga* <note>Bird</note>, *Shringataka* <note>Cuckold/Triangle</note>, and *Hala* <note>Plough</note>:

**When all planets occupy two adjacent Center houses, it is called *Gada*. When they are in the Ascendant and the 7th, it is *Shakata*. In the 10th and 4th, it is *Vihaga*. When planets are situated in the 9th, 5th, and the Ascendant, it is *Shringataka*. When they are in other Trines excluding the Ascendant, the experts call it *Hala*. || 168 ||**

**Commentary:** "Adjacent": When all planets are placed in two nearby Center houses, the combination named *Gada* occurs. This should be understood as follows: in the four variations—1st and 4th, 4th and 7th, 7th and 10th, or 10th and 1st—if all planets are in any one of these pairs, then it is *Gada* yoga. 

When all planets are in the "Body and Setting" (the 1st and 7th houses), the combination named *Shakata* occurs. When planets are in the "Sky and Home" (the 10th and 4th houses), it is *Vihaga* (Bird) yoga. When all planets are situated in the 9th, 5th, and the Ascendant, they call it *Shringataka* yoga. When all planets are in mutual Trines <term>houses 120 degrees apart</term> other than the Ascendant, the experts of *Hora* <note>Astrology</note> call it *Hala* yoga. This means if all planets are in the 2nd, 6th, and 10th; or the 3rd, 7th, and 11th; or the 4th, 8th, and 12th, it would be *Hala* yoga. As it is said:

> "In the 1st and 4th, or 4th and 7th, or 7th and 10th, or 10th and 1st;
> Thus the *Gada* yoga is described in four ways by all planets, whether auspicious or inauspicious.
> Planets in the 1st and 7th are *Shakata*, while in the 4th and 10th they are *Vihaga*.
> Planets in the 1st, 5th, and 9th are known as *Shringataka*.
> Planets in the 2nd, 6th, and 10th; or 3rd, 7th, and 11th; or 4th, 8th, and 12th;
> Thus *Hala* is of three types." || 168 ||

<margin>If all planets are in two adjacent Centers, it is *Gada* yoga. This is of four types... [summarizing the Sanskrit verse above].</margin>
