Notes—Regarding the rule that if benefics <note>planets with positive influence like Jupiter or Venus</note> are in the 1st and 7th houses, and malefics <note>planets with harsh influence like Saturn or Mars</note> are in the 4th and 10th, it is called **Vajra** (Thunderbolt), and the reverse is **Yava** (Barley): this is actually contrary to the established principles of astronomy <term>Jyotisha-Siddhanta</term>. For Mercury and Venus to be in the 1st or 7th houses while the Sun (a malefic) is in the 4th or 10th would mean the distance between the Sun and Mercury/Venus is four signs <note>approx. 120 degrees</note>, which is highly inconsistent. Since the mean positions of Mercury and Venus are always near the Sun, their maximum possible distance is limited. Even considering their maximum retrograde and forward motions <note>equations of center</note>, the maximum distance for the Sun is **2° 1’ 21”** and for Mercury is **27° 33’ 57”**. Their combined maximum separation is only **29° 35’ 18”**, which is less than a single zodiac sign. The same applies to Venus. Therefore, Mercury and Venus can never be more than one sign away from the Sun. Why then did the ancients define these Yogas requiring a four-sign gap? Varahamihira <note>a famous 6th-century astronomer</note> says: "I have described Vajra and others following the ancient scriptures, but how can Mercury and Venus ever be in the fourth house from the Sun?" In reality, these specific combinations cannot occur. || 166 ||

If benefics are in the 1st and 7th houses (like the Shakata yoga) and malefics are in the 4th and 10th (like the Andaja yoga), it is **"Vajra Yoga."** In the opposite case (malefics in 1st/7th, benefics in 4th/10th), it is **"Yava"** yoga. If all benefics and malefics are in the <term>Kendras</term> <note>the four central houses: 1, 4, 7, 10</note> and none are in the <term>Panaphara</term> <note>succedent houses: 2, 5, 8, 11</note> or <term>Apoklima</term> <note>cadent houses: 3, 6, 9, 12</note>, it is **"Kamala"** (Lotus) yoga. If all planets are outside the Kendras, it is **"Vapi"** (Cistern) yoga. See the example charts above. || 169 ||

### Now, describing the Yupa, Ishu, Shakti, and Danda Yogas—

**When all planets occupy four houses starting from the Ascendant or other angles, they are called Yupa, Ishu, Shakti, and Danda respectively. || 170 ||**

Starting from the angles: "From the Horas" means from the Ascendant. Starting from the <term>Kendras</term> (angles), if all planets occupy four consecutive houses, these four yogas are formed. Specifically:
- If all planets are in the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 4th houses, it is **Yupa Yoga** <note>Sacrificial Post</note>.
- If all planets are in the 4th, 5th, 6th, and 7th houses, it is **Ishu Yoga** <note>Arrow</note>.
- If all planets are in the 7th, 8th, 9th, and 10th houses, it is **Shakti Yoga** <note>Spear/Power</note>.
- If all planets are in the 10th, 11th, 12th, and 1st houses, it is **Danda Yoga** <note>Staff</note>.

As it is said:
> 'All planets in the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 4th create Yupa. From the 4th to the 7th, Bana (Arrow) is produced.
> From the 7th to the 10th, it is known as Shakti. From the 10th to the 1st, it is called Danda.'

This is from the state of liberation. || 170 ||

## The Eight Varieties of the Half-Moon Configuration
It is said: Thus—

> From the second to the eighth,
> From the third to the ninth,
> From the fifth to the eleventh,
> From the sixth to the twelfth—the Moon-like <note>referring to the Half-Moon shape</note> is eightfold.
> — Thus from the *Jnana Sudhakara* <note>A classical astrological treatise</note>. || 171 ||

---

If there is one planet in each house from the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the rising sign or 1st house</term> to the seventh house, it is the **"Boat"** <note>original: "Nau"</note> configuration. If all planets are placed from the fourth to the tenth house, it is the **"Peak"** <note>original: "Kuta"</note> configuration. If all planets are from the seventh to the Ascendant, it is the **"Parasol"** <note>original: "Chhatra"</note> configuration. Similarly, if there is one planet in each house from the tenth to the fourth, it is the **"Bow"** <note>original: "Chapa"</note> configuration. If planets are in other positions, it is the **"Half-Moon"** <note>original: "Ardha Chandra"</note> configuration, which is of eight types:
1. From the 2nd house to the 8th house.
2. From the 3rd to the 9th.
3. From the 5th to the 11th.
4. From the 6th to the 12th.
5. From the 8th to the 2nd.
6. From the 9th to the 3rd.
7. From the 11th to the 5th.
8. From the 12th to the 6th.

### Now, the Ocean and Discus configurations are described—

> With planets in every second house starting from the second, the Ocean is formed in six houses.
> Starting from the Ascendant, it is the Discus; thus is the summary of Shape-born configurations. || 172 ||

**"In every second house"** means starting from the **second house**, skipping one house and occupying the next until the end, occupying six houses in total to form the **Ocean** <note>original: "Samudra"</note> configuration. This means: if the seven planets <note>The Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, and Saturn</note> are placed in the six houses—2nd, 4th, 6th, 8th, 10th, and 12th—it is called the Ocean configuration.

**The Discus is described—"Starting from the Ascendant"** means if all planets are arranged in six signs starting from the Ascendant in every second house, it is the **Discus** <note>original: "Chakra"</note> configuration. If the seven planets are in the six houses—1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th, 9th, and 11th—then the Discus configuration occurs. This completes the summary of the Shape-born <term>Akriti-ja: configurations based on the geometric pattern planets form in the birth chart</term> configurations. In the *Saravali* <note>A foundational 8th-century astrological text by Kalyanavarman</note>, the definitions of Ocean and Discus are also given as:

> From the Ascendant, if planets occupy six houses separated by one sign, it is the Discus.
> If they proceed similarly from the second house, the Ocean shape is formed. || 172 ||

# Chapter on Royal Yogas (Raja Yoga) || 7 ||

If all planets are placed in the even houses starting from the second house (2nd, 4th, 6th, 8th, 10th, and 12th), skipping one house each time, it is called **"Samudra"** (Ocean) yoga. If all planets are similarly placed in every other house starting from the Ascendant up to the eleventh (1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th, 9th, and 11th), it is called **"Chakra"** (Wheel) yoga. In this manner, the ancient teachers have compiled the "Shape" yogas. || 172 ||

->Now he describes the Numerical Yogas (Sankhya Yogas)<-

> **The Numerical Yogas are seven, formed by planets occupying seven signs. By decreasing the number of occupied signs one by one, they are named: Vallaki, Dama, Pasha, Kedara, Shula, Yuga, and Gola—provided they do not fall into the previously mentioned categories.** || 173 ||

Regarding the "Numerical" yogas: By "occupying seven signs"—meaning the seven planets <note>The seven traditional planets: Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, and Saturn</note> being situated in any seven houses—and then decreasing the count of houses one by one, the seven Numerical Yogas like Vallaki (Lute) and others are formed. This is what is meant: If the seven planets are spread across any seven houses, it is **Vallaki** (also called Veena) yoga. If all planets are in six houses, it is **Damini** (also called Dama) yoga. In five houses, it is **Pasha**. In four, **Kedara**. In three, **Shula**. In two, **Yugma**. If all seven planets are concentrated in a single house, it is **Gola** yoga. Furthermore, these yogas occur only when the previously mentioned "Shape" yogas are not present. One must consider this: if a numerical arrangement also matches one of the previously described Shape Yogas, then these Numerical Yogas are not recognized; in such cases, only the Shape Yogas should be accepted. || 173 ||

Numerical Yoga is of seven types. If seven planets are in any seven places, it is **"Vallaki"** yoga. If the seven planets are in six places, it is **"Damini"** yoga. If in five places, **"Pasha"** yoga. If in four places, **"Kedara"** yoga. If in three places, **"Shula"** yoga. If all planets are in two places, it is **"Yuga"** yoga. If all planets are in one place, it is **"Gola"** yoga. Thus, the Numerical Yogas are described. In instances where a Numerical Yoga and a previously mentioned yoga both appear, the previous yoga's results prevail; the Numerical Yoga does not give its result. Numerical Yoga only yields results when the previously mentioned "Support" (Ashraya) yogas are not applicable. || 173 ||

### Now, the Results of Support (Ashraya) and Part (Dala) Yogas.

> **One born in Rajju yoga is envious, fond of foreign lands, and constantly wandering. In Musala yoga, one is proud, wealthy, and surrounded by many servants. In Nala yoga, one may have a physical deformity but is firm, wealthy, and clever. In Srag yoga, one enjoys many pleasures. In Bhujanga yoga, one experiences much sorrow.**

### Now, the Results of Gada and Other Yogas.

> **In Gada yoga, one performs sacrifices, possesses wealth, and is always interested in earning. In Shakata yoga, one lives off that specific profession <note>likely referring to transport or carts</note>, is sickly, and has a difficult spouse. In Vihaga yoga, one is a messenger, a wanderer, and a quarrel-monger. In Shringataka yoga, one is happy for a long time and a farmer. In Hala yoga, one is also a farmer.** || 175 ||
> **In Vajra yoga, one is happy in the beginning and end of life, charming, and very brave. In Yava yoga, one is observant of purity and happy in the middle of life. In Padma yoga, one has famous glory and moderate happiness and virtues. In Vapi yoga, one has a stable body, is happy, a protector of wealth, and a donor of food.**
> **In Yupa yoga, one is self-sacrificing and performs great sacrifices. In Shara yoga, one is cruel, a prison official, or a maker of arrows. In Shakti yoga, one is lowly, lazy, and devoid of happiness and wealth. In Danda yoga, one is separated from loved ones and lives a menial life.** 177
> **In Chhatra yoga, one is happy at the beginning and end of life, and possesses wealth and strength. In Nau yoga, one is famous and earns a living from water. In Chakra yoga, one is a famous king. In Samudra yoga, one is like a king, earns from the sea, and is a lord of the earth. In Ardhendu yoga, one is a seeker of pleasure. In Kuta yoga, one wanders in mountains and forests and performs cruel deeds. In Chapa yoga, those born are forest-dwellers, thieves, and of low character.** || 178 ||
> **In Veena yoga, one is skilled in all actions and fond of music and dance. In Damini yoga, one is helpful to others, though sometimes of difficult intellect, and is famous for learning and wealth. In Pasha yoga, one is very clever in earning wealth through good conduct, talkative, and has children. In Kedara yoga, one possesses agricultural wealth, has a slow intellect, and is helpful to kinsmen.** || 179 ||

> In the **Shula** <note>Spear</note> yoga, one is prone to anger, greedy for wealth, brave, scarred, and poor.
> In **Yava** <note>Barley</note>, one lives on alms, suffers from diseases in youth, is very fickle, a heretic, and a drunkard.
> In **Gola** <note>Globe</note>, one is destitute, dirty, a wanderer, short-lived, and of ignorant mind.
> These thirty-two yogas were described by the teacher Varahamihira. ॥ 180 ॥

Now, through these six verses, the results of the previously mentioned thirty-two yogas (comprising twenty *Akriti* yogas, three *Ashraya* yogas, two *Dala* yogas, and seven *Sankhya* yogas—totaling thirty-two) are explained. The verses are clear in their meaning, so there is no need for excessive elaboration. ॥ 174-180 ॥

A person born in the **Rajju** <note>Rope</note> yoga is envious of others' well-being, constantly resides in foreign lands, and always takes pleasure in traveling on the road.

One born in the **Musala** <note>Pestle</note> yoga is proud, wealthy, and possesses many servants.

A person born in the **Nala** <note>Reed</note> yoga is physically deformed <note>literally "limb-less"</note>, firm in resolve, wealthy, and examines all tasks with a keen, subtle eye. These three are the results of the **Ashraya** <note>Refuge</note> yogas.

One born in the **Mala** <note>Garland</note> yoga is a seeker of pleasure. A person born in the **Sarpa** <note>Serpent</note> yoga suffers many kinds of miseries. ॥ 174 ॥

The person with **Gada** <note>Mace</note> yoga performs sacrifices <note>Yajnas</note>, enjoys wealth, and is industrious in accumulating riches.

A person arising from the **Shakata** <note>Cart</note> yoga earns a living through carts, chariots, etc.; they are perpetually sickly, and their wife is beautiful.

The person with **Vihanga** <note>Bird</note> yoga works as a messenger and is quarrelsome.

The person with **Shringataka** <note>Triangle/Water-caltrop</note> yoga remains happy for a long time.

The person with **Hala** <note>Plough</note> yoga knows the work of farming and animal husbandry very well. ॥ 175 ॥

One born in the **Vajra** <note>Thunderbolt</note> yoga is happy in the first and final stages of life, miserable in the middle, beloved by all, and extremely courageous.

The person with **Yava** <note>Barley-corn</note> yoga is strong and remains happy in the middle stage of life.

One arising from the **Padma** <note>Lotus</note> yoga has widespread fame and possesses great happiness, virtue, and knowledge.

The person with **Vapi** <note>Pond</note> yoga experiences small amounts of happiness for a long duration, increases their wealth, and is a miser. ॥ 176 ॥

A person born in the **Yupa** <note>Sacrificial Pillar</note> yoga is charitable, egoistic, and performs sacrifices. In the **Shara** or **Ishu** <note>Arrow</note> yoga, one is violent, a jailer <note>literally "one who guards the bound"</note>, and a maker of arrows.

In the **Shakti** <note>Power/Spear</note> yoga, one performs lowly deeds, is lazy, miserable, and poor. In the **Danda** <note>Staff</note> yoga, one is deprived of loved ones (such as sons) and follows the occupation of a servant <note>term: Shudra-vritti - historically referring to service-oriented labor</note>.

The person arising from the **Chatra** <note>Umbrella</note> yoga is happy in the beginning and end of life, possesses incomparable wealth, and is powerful.

One born in the **Nau** <note>Boat</note> yoga earns a living from the water. The person of **Chakra** <note>Wheel</note> yoga becomes a glorious king. One with the **Jaladhi** <note>Ocean</note> yoga becomes a king whose livelihood is connected to the sea.

A person born in the **Ardhendu** <note>Half-moon</note> yoga is fond of luxuries. One born in the **Kuta** <note>Hammer/Peak</note> yoga lives in mountains and forests and performs cruel deeds. One born in the **Chapa** <note>Bow</note> yoga is a forest-dweller, a thief, and of low character. ॥ 178 ॥

A person born in the **Veena** <note>Lute</note> yoga is clever in all actions and fond of music and dance. One born in the **Damini** <note>Cord</note> yoga is philanthropic, sharp-witted, famous for learning, and wealthy. One born in the **Pasha** <note>Noose</note> yoga is well-behaved, clever at earning money, talkative, and has sons. One born in the **Kedara** <note>Field</note> yoga is devoted to agricultural work, wealthy, of a slow/lazy intellect, and a benefactor to his kinsmen. ॥ 179 ॥

# Chapter on Royal Yogas || 7 ||

A person born under the **Shula Yoga** <note>original: "शूल योग"; a configuration where planets are situated in only three signs</note> is possessed by anger and dreams, has an interest in wealth, is a fighter, talkative, and poor. One born in the **Yuga Yoga** <note>planets in only two signs</note> is extremely bright, a hypocrite, and a drunkard. One born in the **Gola Yoga** <note>planets in only one sign</note> is poor, lazy, a wanderer, short-lived, and of ignorant intellect. These 32 yogas were described by the venerable teacher Varahamihira in the *Brihat Jataka*. Thus says the author of the *Suta-Shastra*. || 180 ||

The Royal Yogas, the five-fold *Ruchaka* yogas, the *Bhaskara* yogas, the *Kemadruma*, *Adhama*, *Sama*, and *Graha-Malika* yogas; the *Lakshmi*, *Hari-Hara-Vidhi*, *Kahal*, and *Nabhasa* yogas—these have all been proclaimed by the grace of the Sun and other deities. || 181 ||

# Now begins the Chapter on the Conjunction of Two or More Planets || 8 ||

Now, the chapter on the conjunction of two or more planets is explained. First, the conjunctions of two planets:
> One born when the **Sun is with the Moon** is subject to the influence of women and is skilled in actions. When the **Sun is in Mars**, one is radiant, possessed of strength and courage, a speaker of untruths, and a sinner. When the **Sun is with Mercury**, one is endowed with knowledge, beauty, and strength, but is of unsteady mind. When the **Sun is with Jupiter**, one is devoted to faith and ritual, a favorite of kings, and wealthy. || 1 ||
>
> One born when the **Sun is with Venus** earns wealth through women and possesses many kinsmen and wisdom. When the **Sun is joined with Saturn**, one is of dull intellect and falls under the control of enemies. When the **Moon is with Mars**, one is brave, born of a good family, knows religion and wealth, but is a censurer of virtues. When the **Moon is with Mercury**, one is righteous, devoted to the scriptures, and possesses various excellent qualities. || 2 ||
>
> One born when the **Moon is joined with Jupiter** is a refuge for holy people and is highly intelligent. When **Venus is with the Moon**, one is a sinful soul but skilled in buying and selling. When the **Moon is with Saturn**, one is a hunchback, a reviler of the father, and has lost their wealth. When **Mars is with Mercury**, one is eloquent and skilled in medicine, crafts, and the sciences. || 3 ||

> One born when **Mars is with Jupiter** is lustful, endowed with worshipful qualities, and a knower of mathematics. When **Venus is with Mars**, one is devoted to archery, a lover of worldly affairs, and a rogue. When **Mars is joined with Saturn**, one is a debater, a knower of the joy of music, and of dull intellect. When **Mercury is with Jupiter**, one is eloquent, endowed with beauty and virtue, and exceedingly wealthy. || 4 ||
>
> One born when **Venus is with Mercury** is a scholar, a lover of music and humor. When **Saturn is with Mercury**, one is distinguished by knowledge and wealth, and possesses religious virtues. When **Jupiter is with Venus**, one is radiant, a favorite of kings, highly intelligent, and brave. When **Saturn is with Jupiter**, one is a craftsman or a minister. When **Venus is with Saturn**, one is a keeper of cattle or a wrestler. || 5 ||

When the Sun<gloss>1</gloss> is joined with the Moon (the yoga of Sun and Moon), the person born is subject to the influence of women and is clever and skilled in practical affairs. In this manner, Sun-Venus<gloss>5</gloss>, Sun-Saturn<gloss>6</gloss>, Moon-Mars<gloss>7</gloss>, Moon-Mercury<gloss>8</gloss>, Moon-Jupiter<gloss>9</gloss>, Moon-Venus<gloss>10</gloss>, Moon-Saturn<gloss>11</gloss>, Mars-Mercury<gloss>12</gloss>, Mars-Jupiter<gloss>13</gloss>, Mars-Venus<gloss>14</gloss>, Mars-Saturn<gloss>15</gloss>, Mercury-Jupiter<gloss>16</gloss>, Mercury-Venus<gloss>17</gloss>, Mercury-Saturn<gloss>18</gloss>, Jupiter-Venus<gloss>19</gloss>, Jupiter-Saturn<gloss>20</gloss>, and Venus-Saturn<gloss>21</gloss>—thus twenty-one variations of two-planet conjunctions are possible. Now the results of the conjunctions of two planets are described: One who has the Sun joined with the Moon at the time of birth follows the lead of women and is skilled in action. If the Sun is joined with Jupiter, the man is skilled in faithful religious rites, a favorite of the King, and wealthy. || 1 ||

If the Sun is joined with Venus, wealth is obtained through women and he is surrounded by kinsmen. If the Sun is joined with Saturn, it generally makes the man dull-witted and subject to his enemies. If the Moon is with Mars, the man is brave, of noble birth, virtuous, wealthy, and possessed of good qualities. If the Moon is joined with Mercury, the man is a performer of dharma <note>righteous duty</note>, a knower of the scriptures, and possessed of extraordinary virtues. || 2 ||

If the Moon is joined with Jupiter, the person born relies on holy men and is perfectly wise. If the Moon is joined with Venus, that person is of a sinful soul but skilled in buying and selling. If the Moon is joined with Saturn, that person has a wicked wife, is a slanderer of his father, and is a person devoid of wealth. If Mars is joined with Mercury, that person is an orator, a knower of medicine, and skilled in the arts and crafts. || 3 ||

If Mars is joined with Jupiter at the time of birth, the man is lustful, worthy of worship, virtuous, and a knower of the science of mathematics. If Mars is joined with Saturn, the man is argumentative, a lover of singing and music, and dull-witted. If Jupiter is joined with Mercury, the man is an orator, handsome, virtuous, and very wealthy. || 4 ||

If Jupiter is joined with Venus, the person born is radiant, dear to the King, extremely intelligent, and powerful. <header>From the Jatakabharanam with Commentary</header>

If the **Sun**, the **Moon**, and **Mars** are all in one place, the native <note>the person whose birth chart is being read</note> will be a slayer of enemies, wealthy, and knowledgeable in ethics and law. If the **Sun**, **Moon**, and **Mercury** are gathered together, he will have fame equal to a king and be a scholar. If the **Sun**, **Moon**, and **Jupiter** are gathered together, he will be virtuous, learned, and beloved by kings. If the **Sun**, **Moon**, and **Venus** are in one place, he will be an adulterer <note>original: "parastrigami" - one who goes after others' wives</note>, cruel, fearful of enemies, and wealthy. || 6 ||

If **Saturn**, the **Moon**, and the **Sun** are in one sign, the native will have a wicked mind, be deceitful, and fond of foreign lands. From the presence of the **Sun**, **Mars**, and **Mercury** in one sign, the native will be devoid of happiness but possessed of a wife and sons. By the gathering of **Jupiter**, the **Sun**, and **Mars**, he will be especially beloved by the people and become a minister or a general. If the **Moon**, **Sun**, and **Venus** are gathered, he will be afflicted with eye diseases, a seeker of pleasure, of noble birth, and powerful. || 7 ||

By the gathering of **Saturn**, the **Sun**, and **Mars**, he will be deprived of kinsmen, foolish, wealthy, and sickly. If **Jupiter**, the **Sun**, and **Mercury** are gathered, he will be of clever intellect, a famous scholar, and wealthy. If the **Sun**, **Mercury**, and **Jupiter** are gathered <note>This repeats the previous combination with a slight variation in description</note>, he will have a delicate body, be learned, famous, and happy. From **Saturn**, the **Sun**, and **Mercury**, he will be without kinsmen, penniless, an enemy to others, and of wicked conduct. || 8 ||

By the gathering of **Jupiter**, the **Sun**, and **Venus**, he will be possessed of sons and a wife, wise, afflicted with eye disease, and wealthy. From **Saturn**, **Jupiter**, and the **Sun**, he will be fearless, a favorite of the king, and of a virtuous <term>Sattvic</term> <note>pure, balanced, and harmonious nature</note> temperament. If born when the **Sun**, **Venus**, and **Saturn** are gathered, he will be of wicked character, proud, and arrogant. If the **Moon**, **Mars**, and **Mercury** are gathered, he will be always devoted to eating, a doer of evil deeds, and a slanderer of others.

If **Jupiter**, the **Moon**, and **Mars** are gathered, he will speak angry words, be lustful, and handsome. If the **Moon**, **Mars**, and **Venus** are gathered, he will be ill-behaved, without sons, and a wanderer. If the **Moon**, **Saturn**, and **Mars** are gathered, he will be of fickle mind, a wicked soul, and one who harms his mother. By the gathering of **Jupiter**, the **Moon**, and **Mercury**, he will be immensely wealthy and a favorite of the king. || 10 ||

By the gathering of **Venus**, **Mercury**, and the **Moon**, he will be a scholar, a performer of lowly deeds, and worthy of being served. If the **Moon**, **Mercury**, and **Saturn** are gathered, the native is charitable, honored by kings, and virtuous. By the gathering of **Venus**, the **Moon**, and **Jupiter**, the native is wise, has good daughters, and is skilled in the arts. By the gathering of **Jupiter**, the **Moon**, and **Saturn**, the native is a scholar of the scriptures <term>Shastras</term>, devoted to older women, and equal to a king. || 11 ||

If **Venus**, the **Moon**, and **Saturn** are gathered, he will be a knower of the Vedas, a royal priest, and exceedingly fortunate. By the gathering of **Jupiter**, **Mercury**, and **Mars**, he becomes an expert in the <term>Gandharva Vidya</term> <note>the celestial arts of music, poetry, and drama</note>. If **Venus**, **Mars**, and **Mercury** are gathered, the native will have a physical deformity <note>original: "hinanga" - missing or weakened limb</note>, be born of a wicked lineage, and be of fickle mind. By the gathering of **Mercury**, **Mars**, and **Venus**, he will be a messenger, suffer from eye disease, and always be wandering. || 12 ||

If **Venus**, **Mars**, and the **Moon** are gathered, he will be a friend of the king, have good daughters, and be happy. If **Jupiter**, **Mars**, and **Saturn** are gathered, he will have a lean body, be proud, and of wicked conduct. From the gathering of **Saturn**, **Mars**, and **Jupiter**, he will have wicked daughters and always reside in foreign lands. If **Venus**, **Mercury**, and **Jupiter** are gathered, he will be a conqueror of enemies and possessed of fame and majesty. || 13 ||

From the gathering of **Jupiter**, **Mercury**, and **Saturn**, he will be especially happy, prosperous, and beloved by his wife. From the gathering of **Saturn**, **Mercury**, and **Jupiter**, he will be a liar, wicked, and an adulterer. By the gathering of **Jupiter**, **Venus**, and **Saturn**, he will be of clear intellect, famous, and endowed with happiness. If the **Moon** is joined with malefic planets, the native will have little happiness; if the **Sun** is joined with malefic planets, know that his father will have little happiness. || 14 ||

### Now, the Conjunctions of Four Planets

If the **Sun, Moon, Mars, and Mercury** are together in one house, the person becomes a minister, yet lacks skill, works as a scribe <note>original: "lipikara" - a clerk or copyist</note>, and suffers from illness. If the **Moon, Mars, Sun, and Jupiter** are combined, one becomes wealthy, a scholar of scriptures <note>original: "shastri"</note>, illustrious, a favorite of the king, and free from sorrow and disease. || 14 ||

With the combination of **Mars, Sun, Moon, and Venus**, one is blessed with children, a wife, and wealth; they are learned, moderate in eating, happy, disciplined, and compassionate. With the **Sun, Moon, Saturn, and Mars** <note>The text uses synonyms for the Sun and Saturn</note>, one is peaceful, yet driven, and lacks family or wealth. || 15 ||

Through the combination of **Mercury, Moon, Mars, and Jupiter**, one is blessed with beloved children and a wife, is wealthy, possesses good fame and strength, and is generous. With **Venus, Moon, Sun, and Mercury**, one is physically impaired <note>original: "vikala" - could mean a missing limb or a specific disability</note> but serves as a minister. With **Saturn, Moon, Mars, and the Sun**, one is poor and ungrateful. || 16 ||

One who has the **Sun, Moon, Jupiter, and Venus** together is honored by kings, enjoys life's pleasures, has large eyes, much wealth and sons, and is a leader among men <note>original: "varanganapati"</note>. || 17 ||

With **Saturn, Moon, Sun, and Venus**, one is weak, very timid, and intent on seeking wealth and food through the shelter of women. With **Mars, Sun, Mercury, and Jupiter**, one is strong but faces calamities, yet possesses a wife and wealth, though they may suffer from eye diseases and lack proper conduct. || 18 ||

With the **Sun, Mars, Mercury, and Jupiter**, one is attached to others' wives, has unsteady eyes or a tremor, a thieving mind, and lacks courage. || 19 || <note>The numbering skips or merges in the original manuscript</note>

With the **Sun, Mars, Mercury, and Saturn**, one becomes a commander of an army <note>term: "chamupa" - a general or military leader</note>, a minister to a king, or performs lowly deeds while enjoying pleasures. || 20 ||

With the **Sun, Mars, Jupiter, and Venus**, one is equal to a king, famous, highly honored, and wealthy. With **Jupiter, Mars, Saturn, and the Sun**, one loses wealth, wanders, but has friends and relatives. With **Mars, Sun, Venus, and Saturn**, one faces humiliation, performs improper deeds, and lacks good qualities. With **Venus, Sun, Mercury, and Jupiter**, one becomes a chief minister, foremost in wealth and fame. || 21 ||

With **Jupiter, Mercury, Saturn, and the Sun**, one is quarrelsome, proud, and of bad conduct. With the **Moon, Mars, Mercury, and Venus**, one has a good wife and son, is wise, but physically unattractive, yet happy. With **Saturn, Mars, Moon, and Mercury**, one has two mothers and a father <note>likely referring to an adoptive mother or an aunt</note>, is brave, and has many wives and sons. With the **Moon, Mars, Jupiter, and Venus**, one is skilled in unrighteousness, sleepy, and anxious for money. With **Jupiter, Mars, Saturn, and the Moon**, one is firm-minded, brave, happy, and a scholar. || 23 ||

With **Venus, Mercury, Moon, and Jupiter**, one is deaf but learned in the scriptures and wealthy. With the **Moon, Saturn, Mercury, and Jupiter**, one is very wealthy, dear to relatives, and righteous. With the **Moon, Mercury, Venus, and Saturn**, one is hated by many and pursues others' wives. With **Jupiter, Moon, Saturn, and Venus**, one is devoid of happiness, faith, and compassion. || 24 ||

With **Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus**, one is wealthy but criticized by others. With **Mercury, Jupiter, Saturn, and Mars**, one is mediocre and lacks wealth. If **Jupiter, Venus, Saturn, and Mercury** are situated in one house, the person born attains extraordinary wealth, knowledge, and good character. || 25 ||

If the **Moon, Sun, Jupiter, Mercury, and Venus** are in one sign, the person will be a minister, wealthy, and one who punishes others through his majesty. ### Now, the Conjunctions of Six Planets.

> If the **Sun, Moon, Mercury, Mars, Jupiter, and Venus** are in one sign, the person becomes a pilgrim <note>original: "tirthakrit"</note>, a dweller in forests and mountain regions, yet endowed with a wife, children, and wealth. If **Venus, Moon, Mercury, Jupiter, the Sun, and Saturn** <note>original: "dinakrit-putra" - the son of the Sun, i.e., Saturn</note> are together, he suffers from head diseases, has a manic temperament, lives in deserted lands, and goes to foreign countries. ॥ 36 ॥
>
> With **Jupiter, Mercury, the Sun, Mars, Venus, and Saturn**, he will be a wanderer and wise. With the **Moon, Mercury, Mars, Venus, Saturn, and Jupiter**, he will go on pilgrimages and be observant of vows. With **Jupiter, Mars, Moon, Sun, Mercury, and Saturn**, he will be a thief, devoted to other men's wives, a leper, censured by kinsmen, childless, a fool, and gone to a foreign land. ॥ 37 ॥
>
> One becomes lowly, engaged in others' work, afflicted by consumption and chronic cold, and contemptible if the **Mars, Sun, Moon, Venus, Saturn, and Mercury** are together. One becomes a minister, though lacking the joy of wife, wealth, and children, yet peaceful, if **Venus, Saturn, Mars, Sun, Jupiter, and the Moon** are together. ॥ 38 ॥

Now the results of the six-planet conjunctions are described. Therein, the sequence is: (1) Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus. (2) Sun, Moon, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn. (3) Sun, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn. (4) Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn. (5) Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Saturn. (6) Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Venus, Saturn. (7) Sun, Moon, Mars, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn. These seven conjunctions and their results have been stated. The verses are of simple meaning. ॥ 36-38 ॥

If the **Sun, Moon, Mars, Jupiter, Mercury, and Venus** are in one sign, he will be a pilgrim, a dweller in forests and mountains, and possessed of a wife, son, and wealth. If **Venus, Moon, Sun, Mercury, Jupiter, and Saturn** are together, he will have pain in the head, a manic nature, reside in divine lands <note>or deserted places</note>, and reach foreign countries. ॥ 36 ॥

If **Jupiter, Mercury, Sun, Mars, Venus, and Saturn** are together, he will be a wanderer and a scholar. If the **Moon, Mercury, Mars, Venus, Saturn, and Jupiter** are together, the native will be a pilgrim and one who keeps vows...

# Chapter 8: On the Combination of Two or More Planets
**Page 271**

If Jupiter, Mars, the Moon, the Sun, Mercury, and Saturn are all in one sign, the person will be a thief, devoted to others' wives, afflicted with leprosy <note>likely referring to general skin diseases or social exclusion in this historical context</note>, despised by kinsmen, childless, a fool, and a foreigner. ॥ 37 ॥

If Mars, the Sun, the Moon, Venus, Saturn, and Mercury are in one sign, the person born will be of low status, absorbed in the work of others, and distressed by suffering on all sides. If Venus, Saturn, Mars, the Sun, Jupiter, and the Moon are in one sign, the person will be a minister, yet lacking in wives, wealth, sons, and joy, though they will be of a peaceful temperament. ॥ 38 ॥

# With the Commentary on Jataka Parijata

If **Mars** is in its own sign <note>Aries or Scorpio</note>, the person gains wealth from the king, through agricultural activities, or through travel. If in the house of **Venus** <note>Taurus or Libra</note>, there is an increase in desire. If in the house of **Mercury** <note>Gemini or Virgo</note>, the person speaks humble words, is a favorite of the king in their work, and is wealthy. In **Aquarius**, they are served by wicked people. In **Capricorn**, they become a king or like a king. || 40 ||

In **Virgo**, they are a mine of beautiful qualities and fearless. In **Sagittarius**, they are dear to the king. In **Pisces**, they are defeated by servants. In the houses of **Saturn** <note>Capricorn or Aquarius</note>, they become an artisan <term>Shilpi: a craftsman or architect</term> and a messenger. || 41 ||

If **Jupiter** is in the houses of **Mars** <note>1. Aries, 8. Scorpio</note>, the person possesses a large army, wealth, and sons; they are virtuous and charitable. In the houses of **Venus** <note>Taurus or Libra</note>, they are radiant. In the houses of **Mercury** <note>Gemini or Virgo</note>, they possess attendants and friends. In **Cancer**, they are wise and wealthy in sons. In **Aquarius**, they are a seeker of pleasure. In **Leo**, they are famous. In its own houses <note>Sagittarius or Pisces</note>, they are a king or like a king. In its debilitation <note>Capricorn</note>, they are a wanderer with a distressed intellect. || 42 ||

If **Venus** is situated in **Aries** etc.: In **Aries**, one is a <unclear>Kinara</unclear> <note>likely 'Kinara' refers to a marginalized person or a specific class of singer</note>. The results stated for the **Moon** in **Aries** etc., as well as the results of the **Navamsha** <term>Navamsha: the 1/9th divisional chart used for fine-tuning predictions</term>, should be considered by the wise. || 45 ||

### Regarding the Results of Aspects

> If a planet traveling in the sky is aspected by a malefic, the person born is afflicted with foul diseases and is devoid of their own religion, virtue, wealth, and fame.
> If joined with malefics, they will be greedy for others' wealth and wives, harsh-spoken, cunning in intellect, and lazy. || 46 ||
> If a planet is aspected by a benefic, the person born will possess sons and wealth, be a seeker of pleasure, handsome, and honored by kings.
> If a planet is joined with a benefic, they will be free from humiliation, a conqueror of enemies, a follower of religious conduct, and a knower of hidden intentions. || 47 ||

Now the results of aspects <term>Drishti: the 'glance' or influence of one planet upon another</term> are described. "Traveling in the sky" refers to the planet (here, the word "planet" should be understood as the significator planet). "Aspected by a malefic" means seen by a malefic planet. The rest is clear enough and requires no further elaboration. || 46-47 ||

If the significator planet is seen by a malefic planet, the person will be afflicted with foul diseases and be devoid of their religion, virtue, wealth, and fame. If joined with a malefic planet, they will enjoy the wealth and wives of others, use dry/harsh speech, possess a deceitful intellect, and be lazy. || 46 ||

If a planet is joined with the aspect of a benefic planet, the person will possess sons and wealth, be a seeker of pleasure, handsome, honored by kings, and free from defeat. If joined with a benefic, they will be a conqueror of enemies, a follower of religious conduct, and wise. || 47 ||

### Regarding the Results of Aspects on the Moon

> When the Moon is in Aries and is aspected by Mars and other planets, the person becomes a king,
> a scholar, like a king, possessed of all virtues, a thief, or poor respectively.
> Similarly, when in Taurus, the person is penniless, healthy, a respected king, wealthy, or a servant.
> When in Gemini, they are disabled, a king, highly intelligent, courageous, wicked, or poor. || 48 ||

# Chapter on the Aspects and Conjunctions of Planets etc. || 8 ||

When the Moon is in Cancer and aspected <note>aspected: in astrology, this refers to the angular relationship between planets that allows them to influence one another</note> by Mars and the others, the person born is courageous, a preeminent poet, a king, one who lives by iron-work <note>original: "ayojīvī"</note>, or suffers from eye diseases. In Leo, they become a king, a learned speaker, wealthy, a lord of men, a sinner, or a servant. In Virgo, they are wealthy, a servant, equal to a lord, learned, ill-behaved, or happy. || 49 ||

When the Moon is in Libra and aspected by Mercury and the other auspicious planets in order, one becomes a king, a goldsmith, or a merchant; if aspected by Mars, the Sun, or Saturn, one becomes a captive. When the Moon is in Scorpio, one has two mothers and fathers, is a favorite of the king, a performer of low deeds, sickly, impoverished, or a minister to the king, when aspected by Mercury and the other planets. || 50 ||

When the Moon is in Sagittarius and joined with the aspect of auspicious planets, one is rich in knowledge, wealth, wisdom, fame, and strength. If aspected by Mars, the Sun, or the son of the Sun <note>Saturn</note>, one becomes a rogue or is devoted to prostitutes. || 51 ||

A king, a lord of the earth, a scholar, a wealthy man, an impoverished man, or a servant—these are the results when the Moon is in Capricorn and aspected by Mars and the other planets. || 52 ||

When the Moon is in Aquarius and aspected by auspicious planets, one possesses fame and wealth. If viewed by malefic planets, the person born is lustful for the wives of others. || 53 ||

When the Moon is in Pisces and viewed by auspicious planets, one is a lover of humor, a king, or a scholar; if viewed by malefic planets, one becomes harsh-spoken and sinful. If in a malefic division <note>original: "pāpāṃśe" - referring to the Navamsha or 1/9th divisional chart</note> and viewed by the wicked, one is of a deceitful mind and devoted to another's wife. If in a gentle division and viewed by auspicious planets, the person born becomes famous. || 54 ||

Whatever results are given for the aspects on the Zodiac signs should also be applied to the divisional signs <note>Navamshas</note>. All planets become givers of good when joined with the conjunction of auspicious planets. || 55 ||

Previously, the results of aspects were spoken of in a general sense; now, the results of planetary aspects are stated according to the specific position of the Moon. When the Moon has gone to the sign of Aries and is aspected there by Mars and the other wandering stars, the person born becomes a king, a scholar, or like a king, and possesses all virtues. This is what is meant: if at the time of birth the Moon in Aries is aspected by Mars and the other planets, then the person born becomes, in order: a king, a scholar, like a king, endowed with all virtues, a thief, or poor. Thus, everything is clear. Just as the results of aspects on the Moon were stated according to the Zodiac sign, the same results should be understood according to the specific division <note>Navamsha</note> as well. In that regard, if there is a conjunction or aspect of an auspicious planet, it is favorable; otherwise (by malefic conjunction or aspect), it is not good. || 48-55 ||

If the Moon is situated in the sign of Aries and Mars and the other planets do not aspect it <insert>the commentary here clarifies the order of planets</insert>, one becomes in sequence: a king, a scholar, like a king, endowed with all virtues, a thief, or poor. If Mars aspects the Moon in Taurus, one is penniless; if Mercury aspects, a king; by the aspect of Jupiter, respected; by the aspect of Venus, a king; by the aspect of Saturn, wealthy; by the aspect of the Sun, a messenger. || 48 ||

If the Moon is in Gemini and there is an aspect from Mars, one is distressed; by the aspect of Mercury, a king; by the aspect of Jupiter, wise; by the aspect of Venus, a hero; by the aspect of Saturn, wicked; by the aspect of the Sun, poor. If the Moon is in Cancer and if Mars aspects it, one is powerful; by the aspect of Mercury, a great poet; by the aspect of Venus, a king; by the aspect of Saturn, one who lives by iron; by the aspect of the Sun, one has eye disease. If there is an aspect of Mars and the others on the Moon in Virgo, the result is as follows: by the aspect of Mars, wealthy; by the aspect of Mercury, a servant (all-pervading); if there is an aspect of Jupiter, like a lord; if there is an aspect of Venus, a scholar; if there is an aspect of Saturn, devoid of character; if there is an aspect of the Sun, one is happy. || 49 ||

# Jataka Parijata with Commentary

<page-num>274</page-num>
<header>From the Jataka Parijata with Commentary—</header>

If Mercury aspects <note>original: 'drishti' - the astrological gaze or influence of one planet upon another</note> [the Moon in Scorpio], the person becomes a king; if Jupiter aspects, a goldsmith; if Venus aspects, a merchant <term>Vaishya</term>. If Mars, the Sun, or Saturn aspect, the person becomes a deceiver. If the Moon is in Scorpio and is aspected by Mercury and other planets, the results are: by Mercury's aspect, one has two mothers; by Jupiter's aspect, one is dear to the king; by Venus's aspect, one performs lowly deeds; by Saturn's aspect, one is sickly; by the Sun's aspect, one is impoverished; and by Mars's aspect, one becomes a minister to the king. ॥ 50 ॥

If the Moon is in Sagittarius and is aspected by or joined with auspicious planets, the native is strong in learning, wealth, knowledge, and the performance of sacrifices <term>yajna</term>. If aspected by Mars, the Sun, or Saturn, the person is a rogue in assemblies and consorts with prostitutes.

The results of Mercury and other planets aspecting the Moon in Capricorn are as follows: if Mercury aspects, one is a king; if Jupiter aspects, a king; if Venus aspects, a scholar; if Saturn aspects, wealthy; if the Sun aspects, poor; and if Mars aspects, one becomes powerful and all-pervading <term>vibhu</term>. ॥ 52 ॥

If the Moon is situated in Aquarius and is seen by auspicious planets, the native possesses the merit of sacrifices and wealth; if seen by inauspicious <note>malefic</note> planets, the person enjoys the wives of others. ॥ 53 ॥

If the Moon is in Pisces and auspicious planets see it, the person is fond of humor, a king, or a scholar. If inauspicious planets see it, the person is harsh-spoken and sinful. If the Moon is in an inauspicious division <term>papansha</term> and inauspicious planets see it, the person is of wicked intellect and enjoys the wives of others. If the Moon is in an auspicious division and auspicious planets see it, the native becomes famous. ॥ 54 ॥

The results described for the signs should also be applied to the ninth-part divisions <term>navamsha</term>. By the aspect or conjunction of auspicious planets, all planets become auspicious. ॥ 55 ॥

## Now, the Results of Planets in the Second House.

-> One is a donor, possessing mineral wealth, having cherished enemies, and eloquent when the Sun is in the house of wealth. Lustful, lovely, sweet-spoken, an expert in gestures, learned, well-behaved, and wealthy when the Moon is in the house of wealth. ॥ 62 ॥ <-
-> Devoted to alchemy, agriculture, and wandering, and prone to anger when Mars is in the house of wealth. Possessing wealth earned through intellect, well-behaved, virtuous, and a saintly person among kin when Mercury is in the house of wealth. ॥ 63 ॥ <-
-> Eloquent, enjoying good food and vast wealth, and a donor when Jupiter is in the house of wealth. Possessing knowledge, desire, arts, luxury, and wealth when Venus is in the house of wealth. ॥ 63 <note>The original text repeats the number 63 for these two verses</note> ॥ <-
-> A liar, restless, a wanderer, poor, and a deceiver when Saturn is among the family <note>the second house</note>. One is prone to opposition when Rahu is in the house of wealth, and a criminal against people when Ketu is in the second. ॥ 64 ॥ <-

Here, the results of planets situated in the second house are stated in three verses. The verses are clear in their meaning.

If the Sun is in the second house, the subject will be a donor, possess wealth in metals/minerals, have "desired" enemies <note>enemies who are ultimately beneficial or easily overcome</note>, and be talkative. If the Moon is in the second house, one will be lustful, have a radiant form, beautiful speech, be intelligent, learned, and wealthy. ॥ 62 ॥

If Mars is in the second house, one will be intent on alchemy, farming, and wandering, and be angry. If Mercury is in the second house, one will have wealth, character, and virtues earned through intelligence, and be a saintly person. If Jupiter is found in the second house, one will be eloquent, enjoy good food, be exceptionally wealthy, and a donor. If Venus is in the second house, the child will be a knower of science, desire, and arts, and be wealthy. ॥ 63 ॥

If Saturn is in the second house, one will be a liar, fickle, a wanderer, poor, and a cheat. If Rahu is in the wealth house, one will be argumentative. If Ketu is in the second house, one will be an offender against the public. ॥ 64 ॥

## Now, the Results of Planets in the Third House.

-> Brave, served by wicked people, very wealthy, and a donor when the Sun is in the third. When the Moon is in the house of siblings, one has little wealth, is dear to kinsmen, and is of pure <italic>Sattvic</italic> nature. Famous, of boundless valor, but of a deceitful mind when Mars goes to the third house. Devoted to illusory works, a wanderer, extremely restless, and miserable when Mercury is in the house of younger siblings. ॥ 65 ॥ <-
-> When Jupiter goes to the house of brothers, one loses wealth, is defeated by women, and commits sins. When Venus is among siblings, one speaks with anger, is sinful, and is defeated by women. A small eater, but possessing wealth, character, and the virtues of his lineage when the son of the Sun <note>Saturn</note> is in the house of brothers. When Rahu is in the house of valor, one is very powerful and wealthy; when Ketu is there, one is virtuous and wealthy. <-

<header>In the Annotated Jataka Parijata—</header>

> If Venus is in the third or sixth house, it bestows sorrow, disease, and fear.
> In those same positions, it becomes a bringer of auspiciousness if it is ahead of the Sun. || 67 ||

The results of planets situated in the third house have been stated in these three verses. The meanings of the verses are straightforward. || 65-67 ||

If the **Sun** is in the third house <note>The house of siblings and courage</note>, the person is powerful, served by wicked people, exceptionally wealthy, and charitable. If the **Moon** is in the third house, they have little wealth, are dear to their kinsmen, and possess a virtuous <term>Sattvic</term> <note>Pure, balanced, and harmonious quality</note> nature. If **Mars** is in the third house, they are immensely powerful and possess a crafty intellect. If **Mercury** is in the third house, they are deceitful, a wanderer, extremely restless, and humble. || 65 ||

If **Jupiter** is in the house of brothers <note>the 3rd house</note>, the person is devoid of wealth, defeated by women, and a committer of sins. If **Venus** is in the third house, they speak words filled with anger, are sinful, and are defeated by women. If **Saturn** is in the third house, they are a light eater, endowed with wealth, character, and a good lineage, and are virtuous. If **Rahu** is in the third house, they are extremely strong and wealthy. If **Ketu** is there, they are virtuous and wealthy. || 66 ||

If **Venus** is in the third or sixth house, it gives sorrow, disease, and fear; however, in those same places, if Venus is positioned ahead of the Sun, it gives auspicious results. || 67 ||

### Now, the results of planets in the fourth house.

> If the **Sun** is in the house of happiness <note>the 4th house, relating to home and mother</note>, one suffers from heart disease, lacks wealth, grain, and intellect, and is cruel.
> If the **Moon** is in the fourth, one is endowed with learning, character, and happiness, but is lustful after others' wives.
> If **Mars** reaches the house of kinsmen, one is devoid of relatives, defeated by women, yet courageous.
> If the son of the Moon (**Mercury**) is in the house of kinsmen, one is without brothers but possesses pure knowledge, wealth, and scholarship. || 68 ||
>
> One born with the teacher of the gods (**Jupiter**) in the house of happiness is eloquent, wealthy, and possesses happiness, fame, strength, and beauty, but is of a crafty nature.
> If the son of Bhrigu (**Venus**) has gone to the house of kinsmen, one is defeated by women, yet possesses happiness, fame, wealth, knowledge, and is talkative. || 69 ||
>
> If the son of the Sun (**Saturn**) is in the house of happiness, one is devoid of good conduct, deceitful, and afflicted by distress regarding the mother.
> If **Rahu** is in the fourth, one opposes their wife and other people.
> If **Ketu** is in the house of happiness, one is a slanderer of others. || 70 ||

The results of planets situated in the fourth house have been stated in three verses. The meanings of the verses are clear. || 68-70 ||

If the **Sun** is in the fourth house, the person has heart disease, is devoid of wealth, grain, and intellect, and is cruel. If the **Moon** is in the fourth house, they are endowed with education, character, and happiness, and pursue the wives of others. If **Mars** is in the fourth house, they are bereft of family, defeated by their wife, and courageous. If **Mercury** is in the fourth house, they are without family <note>original: vibandhu</note>, a possessor of supreme knowledge, wealthy, and a scholar. || 68 ||

If **Jupiter** is in the house of happiness, they are talkative, wealthy, and possess happiness, fame, beauty, and strength, but have a crafty nature. If **Venus** is in the fourth house, they are defeated by women, yet possess happiness, fame, wealth, and education, and are talkative. || 69 ||

If **Saturn** is in the house of happiness, they are devoid of proper conduct, deceitful, and experience distress related to their mother. If **Rahu** is in the fourth, they are an obstructor of their wife and other people. If **Ketu** is in the house of happiness, they are one who blames others. || 70 ||

### Now, the results of planets in the fifth house.

> If the **Sun** is in the house of children <note>the 5th house</note>, one is dear to the king, possesses a restless intellect, and is fond of traveling.
> If the **Moon** is in the house of the son, one's mind is attached to the practice of mantras, and one is merciful, wealthy, and wise. || 71 ||
>
> If the son of the Earth (**Mars**) is in the fifth, one is cruel, restless, daring, irreligious, a seeker of pleasure, and wealthy.
> If **Mercury** is in the house of the son, one is skilled in mantras and incantations, and is endowed with children, a wife, wealth, education, fame, and strength. || 72 ||
>
> If the teacher of the gods (**Jupiter**) has gone to the house of the son, one is a counselor, virtuous, and endowed with the essence of prosperity, but has few children.
> If **Venus** is in the house of the self <note>the 5th house</note>, one possesses good sons, friends, wealth, grain, and beauty, and is a leader of armies. || 73 ||

<header>Chapter 8: On the Conjunctions of Two or More Planets</header>

> One born with Saturn in the fifth house is intoxicated <note>original: "matta" - can also mean prideful or exuberant</note>, long-lived, happy, fickle, and righteous, having certainly conquered his enemies. If the Lord of Snakes <note>Rahu</note> is in the fifth, one is timid, compassionate, and wealthy. If Ketu is there, one is deceitful, afraid of water, and suffers greatly from disease. || 74 ||

In these four verses, the results of planets situated in the fifth house <note>the house of children, intelligence, and past merits</note> are described. The verses are easy to understand. || 71-74 ||

If the **Sun** is in the fifth house, the person is dear to the king, possesses a restless intellect, and resides in foreign lands. If the **Moon** is in the fifth house, their mind is devoted to mantras and rituals; they are compassionate, wealthy, and high-minded. || 71 ||

If **Mars** is in the fifth house, the person is cruel, a wanderer, fickle, courageous, irreligious, an enjoyer of pleasures, and wealthy. If **Mercury** is in the fifth house, they are skilled in mantras and incantations <note>original: "abhichara" - often refers to tantric or magical rites</note>, and are endowed with children, a wife, wealth, knowledge, fame, and strength. || 72 ||

If **Jupiter** is in the fifth house, the person becomes a minister, virtuous, possessed of the essence of wealth, but has few children. If **Venus** is in the fifth house, they have good sons, are wealthy, extremely handsome, and are a master of armies and horses. || 73 ||

If **Saturn** is in the fifth house, the person is intoxicated, long-lived, devoid of happiness <note>Note: The Hindi commentary here says "devoid of happiness" while the Sanskrit verse says "happy"; such variations are common in manuscript traditions</note>, fickle, and a righteous soul. If **Rahu** is in the fifth, they are timid, compassionate, and poor. If **Ketu** is in the 5th, they are deceitful, afraid of water, and particularly sickly. || 74 ||

## Now, the results of planets in the sixth house.

> When the Sun goes to the house of enemies <note>the sixth house</note>, one is lustful, brave, honored by kings, proud, famous, and prosperous. If a waning Moon is in the enemy house, one is short-lived; if the Moon is full, one is a great enjoyer of life and long-lived. || 75 ||
> If the Son of Earth <note>Mars</note> is in the enemy house, one is a master, a destroyer of enemies, possesses a strong digestive fire <note>original: "jatharagni" - metabolic strength</note>, is prosperous, and endowed with fame and strength. If the Son of the Moon <note>Mercury</note> goes to the enemy house, one is a lover of learning and amusement, fond of quarrels, intelligent, but devoid of helpfulness toward kinsmen. || 76 ||
> If the Teacher of the Immortals <note>Jupiter</note> goes to the enemy house, one is lustful, a conqueror of enemies, but physically weak. If the Son of Bhrigu <note>Venus</note> is in the enemy house, one is beset by grief and scandal. If the Son of the Sun <note>Saturn</note> is in the enemy house, one eats much, has a difficult temperament, fears enemies, is lustful, and wealthy. || 77 ||
> If Rahu is in the enemy house, one is a conqueror of enemies, long-lived, extremely happy, and of noble birth. If Ketu is in the enemy house, one is dear to kinsmen, generous, famous for virtues, learned, and renowned. || 78 ||

In these four verses, the results of planets in the sixth house are told. The verses have clear meanings. || 75-78 ||

If the **Sun** is in the sixth house, one is lustful, brave, honored by the king, proud, famous, and prosperous. If a **waning Moon** is in the enemy house (sixth), one is short-lived; if it is a **full Moon**, one is a great enjoyer and long-lived. || 75 ||

If **Mars** is in the sixth house, one is a leader of men, a destroyer of enemies, has a strong digestive fire, is prosperous, and joined with fame and strength. If **Mercury** is in the sixth house, one delights in knowledge, is fond of disputes, lacks character, and is devoid of service to the family. || 76 ||

If **Jupiter** is in the sixth house, one is lustful, a conqueror of enemies, and weak. If **Venus** is in the sixth house, one is joined with grief and ill-repute. If **Saturn** is in the sixth house, one is a heavy eater, has a crooked intellect, is fearful of enemies, lustful, and wealthy. || 77 ||

If **Rahu** is in the enemy house, one is a destroyer of enemies, long-lived, especially happy, and of noble lineage. If **Ketu** is in the sixth house, one is dear to relatives, generous, famous for qualities, a scholar, and successful. || 78 ||

## Now, the results of planets in the seventh house.

> If the Day-Maker <note>the Sun</note> is situated in the house of passion <note>the seventh house, governing marriage and partnerships</note>, one hates women, is extremely irritable, and wicked. If the **Moon** goes to the house of passion, one is compassionate, a wanderer, submissive to women, and an enjoyer of pleasures. If **Mars** is in the house of passion, one causes grief to women and has a taste for battle. If the Son of the Stars <note>Mercury</note> is in the setting house <note>the seventh house</note>, one is deformed <note>original: "vyanga"</note> but clever in arts, crafts, and amusements. || 79 ||

## With Commentary on the Jataka Parijata

-> If Jupiter is in the seventh house, one is courageous and possesses a beautiful wife, yet is hostile toward their father and teachers. If Venus is in the seventh, one is a lover of courtesans and women, handsome, but possesses some bodily deformity <note>original: "vyanga," often implying a missing limb or physical mark</note>. If Saturn is in the seventh, one is distressed by the exhaustion of carrying loads on long journeys, yet remains steady and wealthy. If Rahu <note>the North Node of the Moon</note> is in the seventh, one is arrogant, a leader among adulterers, and sickly. || 80 || <-

-> If Ketu <note>the South Node of the Moon</note> occupies the seventh house, one has a low-born wife or is deprived of the pleasures of a wife; they are sleepy, lacking in character, speak pitifully, wander constantly, and are foremost among fools. || 81 || <-

In these three verses, the effects of planets in the seventh house are described. Among them: *one who laments due to women* means one whose heart is tormented by grief caused by women. *Distressed by the exhaustion of carrying loads on long journeys* means one whose mind is troubled by the fatigue of the road arising from carrying burdens, yet they are steady and wealthy. *A crest-jewel among paramours* means the crown-jewel or leader of those devoted to the wives of others. All other terms are clear. || 79-81 ||

If the **Sun** is in the seventh house, one is an enemy to their wife, exceptionally angry, and wicked. If the **Moon** is in the seventh, one is compassionate, fond of wandering, under the influence of their wife, and enjoys life's pleasures. If **Mars** is in the seventh, one laments because of their wife and finds delight in battle. If **Mercury** is in the seventh, one has a physical deformity, is knowledgeable in the arts and crafts, is humorous, and clever. || 79 ||

If **Jupiter** is in the seventh house, one is courageous, has a lovely wife, and is an enemy to their father and teacher. If **Venus** is in the seventh, one is a master of courtesans, beautiful, and deformed. If **Saturn** is in the seventh, one is distressed by walking while carrying loads, yet is steady and wealthy. If **Rahu** is in the seventh, one is proud, the leader among philanderers, and sickly. || 80 ||

If **Ketu** is in the seventh, one has an inferior wife or lacks the enjoyment of a wife, lacks character, is drowsy, speaks words of distress, is always wandering, and is foremost among the ignorant. || 81 ||

-> When **Ketu** occupies the eighth house, the person born desires the wealth of others, is sickly, devoted to bad conduct, and very greedy. However, if aspected by a benefic planet, they become very wealthy and long-lived. || 85 || <-

The simple meaning of the effects of planets in the eighth house is stated in these four verses. || 82-85 ||

If the **Sun** is in the eighth house, one is very beautiful and clever in disputes. If the **Moon** is in the eighth, one is eager for a fight and characterized by charity, pleasure, and learning. || 82 ||

<margin>Mars</margin> If **Mars** is in the eighth house, one has a modest dress, is wealthy, and a chief.

If Ketu <note>The South Node of the Moon</note> is in the eighth house, the native is devoted to the wealth and spouses of others, is sickly, wicked, and exceptionally greedy. However, if beneficial planets aspect it, the person will be wealthy and long-lived. || 85 ||

# Results of Planets in the Ninth House

> If the Sun is in the ninth, one hates fathers and teachers and follows a false religion.
> If the Moon is in the ninth, one is devoted to ancestral and divine rites, is charitable, and respects elders.
> If Mars is in the ninth, one is intent on harming the father but is famous.
> If Mercury is in the ninth, one is rich in virtue, a scholar of the scriptures, and of good conduct. || 86 ||
> If Jupiter is in the house of penance <note>The 9th house</note>, one is wise, devoted to religion, and a minister to kings.
> If Venus is in the ninth, one possesses knowledge, wealth, a spouse, children, and grandeur.
> If Saturn is in the house of fortune, one is famous on the battlefield, wifeless, and wealthy.
> If Rahu <note>The North Node of the Moon; original: "Bhujaga" or Serpent</note> is in the ninth, one hates religious people but possesses fame and wealth. || 87 ||
> If Ketu is in the house of the teacher <note>The 9th house</note>, one is angry, eloquent, irreligious, and a slanderer of others.
> One is brave, a hater of the father, extremely hypocritical in conduct, lacking enthusiasm, and arrogant. || 88 ||

In simple terms <note>original: "Saralarthe"</note> <note>Likely 'tribhih' (by three) in original intent</note>, the results of the planets in the ninth house are proclaimed here in three verses. || 86-88 ||

If the Sun is situated in the ninth house, one hates the father and teacher and lives under the shelter of a false religion. If the Moon is in the ninth house, one is engaged in ancestral rites (libations and funeral ceremonies) and divine rites (twilight prayers, worship, chanting, and sacrifices) and is a donor. If Mars is in the ninth house, one causes harm to the father and is famous. If Mercury is in the dharma (ninth) house, one is rich in virtue, a scholar of scriptures, and possesses good conduct. || 86 ||

If Jupiter is in the ninth house, one is wise, intent on religion, and a minister of the king. If Venus is in the ninth house, one is endowed with knowledge, wealth, a spouse, and children. If Saturn is in the house of fortune (ninth), one is famous in battle, without a wife, and wealthy. If Rahu is in the ninth house, one is an enemy of religious people and is successful. || 87 ||

If Ketu is in the ninth house, one is angry, talkative, irreligious, a slanderer of others, brave, an enemy of the father, particularly hypocritical, absorbed in laziness, and arrogant. || 88 ||

# Results of Planets in the Tenth House

> If the Sun is in the house of honor <note>The 10th house</note>, one has the father's wealth and character, and is endowed with knowledge, fame, and strength, like a protector of the earth <note>a king</note>.
> If the Moon goes to the tenth, one is restless with wealth, grain, clothes, ornaments, and the pleasures and arts of women. || 89 ||
> If Mars is in the Midheaven <note>original: "Meshurana", a Greek-derived term for the 10th house</note>, the native is famous for great valor and wealth.
> If the son of the Moon <note>Mercury</note> is in the house of business, one is characterized by all knowledge, fame, wealth, and a playful nature. || 90 ||
> If Jupiter <note>original: "Chamarajya", teacher of the gods</note> is in the house of honor, one succeeds in undertakings, has virtuous conduct, follows his own religion, is learned and wealthy.
> If Venus is in the house of action <note>10th house</note>, one obtains wealth and power through farming or through women. || 91 ||
> If Saturn is in the tenth, one is a punisher, proud, wealthy, the glory of his family, and brave.
> If the Lord of Serpents <note>Rahu</note> goes to the house of honor, one has a mind skilled in the acts of thieves and is fond of battle. || 92 ||
> If Ketu is in the house of action, one is intelligent, strong, a knower of crafts, self-aware, loved by the people, yet of a contrary nature.
> One is of a phlegmatic temperament, the foremost among brave men, and always wandering. || 93 ||

For easy understanding, the results of the planets in the tenth house are stated here in five verses. || 89-93 ||

If the Sun is in the tenth house, one obtains the father's wealth and character, is endowed with knowledge and fame, and is like a king. If the Moon is in the tenth house, one is endowed with wealth, grain, clothes, and ornaments, is a lover of women, and a knower of arts. || 89 ||

### Now, the Results of Planets in the House of Gains.

->If the Sun has gone to the house of gains <note>the 11th house</note>, one is endowed with abundant wealth, a wife, sons, and servants.<-
->If the Moon is situated in the house of gains, one is contented, of a melancholic disposition, and wealthy.<-
->If the son of the Earth <note>Mars</note> is in the house of income, one is clever in speech, lustful, wealthy, and courageous.<-
->If Mercury has gone to the house of gains, one is of expert intellect, famous for learning, and wealthy. || 94 ||<-

->If the Minister of the Immortals <note>Jupiter</note> is in the house of income, one is of powerful intellect, of famous name, and wealthy.<-
->If the son of Bhrigu <note>Venus</note> is in the house of gains, one is happy, wandering in pursuit of others' wives, and wealthy.<-
->If the son of the Sun <note>Saturn</note> has reached the house of acquisition, one is an enjoyer of life and possesses abundant wealth obtained from the King.<-
->If Rahu is there, one is a destroyer of hearing <note>deaf</note>, a praiser of the battlefield, wealthy, and a scholar. || 95 ||<-

->If Ketu has gone to the penultimate house <note>the 11th house</note>, one is majestic, dear to others, and saluted by other people;<-
->of a contented mind, a lord, an enjoyer of few things, and devoted to auspicious deeds and conduct. || 96 ||<-

In these three verses, the results of the planets in the house of gains (11th) are stated. Among them—<term>Paravadhu-lolatanah</term> = one whose mind is fickle or longing for the wives of others (meaning a lecher for others' wives) and who is of a wandering nature. <term>Shrotra-vinashakah</term> = devoid of ears, meaning deaf. <term>Ranatala-shlaghi</term> = a lover of battle. Everything else is quite clear. || 94-96 ||

If the Sun is in the gain (eleventh) position, one is endowed with abundant wealth, wife, son, and servants. If the Moon is in the gain house, one is contented, sorrowful, and wealthy. If Mars is in the gain house, one is a speaker of clever words, lustful, wealthy, and powerful. If Mercury is in the gain house, one is of expert intellect, possessing learning and fame, and wealthy. || 94 ||

If Jupiter is in the gain house, one is of powerful intellect, famous name, and wealthy. If Venus is in the gain house, one is happy, devoted to others' wives, a wanderer, and wealthy. If Saturn is in the gain house, one is an enjoyer and possesses abundant wealth obtained from the King. If Rahu is in the gain house, one is without hearing, eager for battle, wealthy, and a scholar. || 95 ||

If Ketu is in the gain house, one is majestic, dear to others, worthy of worship by other people, of a contented mind, capable, an enjoyer of few things, and possesses auspicious actions and conduct. || 96 ||

# Chapter 8: On the Combinations of Two or More Planets
## Page 281

> When Rahu <note>original: "Vidhuntuda" (the Rahu/Eclipse-maker)</note> is placed in the twelfth house <note>original: "Rippha," a Greek-derived term for the 12th house</note>, the person is devoid of character, yet wealthy, restless, and virtuous. He destroys his ancestral wealth. When Ketu <note>original: "Shikhi"</note> is in the house of expenditure (12th), he is fickle and lacks character. || 96 ||

The following verses clearly state the results of planets in the twelfth house (12). It should be understood that if the planets in the aforementioned houses are in their own signs, their signs of exaltation, or their own divisions <note>varga</note>, then these results manifest fully. Conversely, if they are in their signs of debilitation or associated with malefic planets, the results may be reversed. || 97-99 ||

If the **Sun** is in the twelfth house, the person will have sons, may have a limb deformity, but will be handsome, courageous, fallen from status, and a wanderer. If the **Moon** is in the final house (12th), he will live in a foreign land. If **Mars** is in the 12th, he will be hostile and deprived of wealth and a wife. || 97 ||

If **Mercury** is in the twelfth, he will be an enemy to his kinsmen, wealthy, but lacking in intelligence. If **Jupiter** is in the twelfth, he follows the Materialist <note>original: "Charvaka," an ancient school of Indian materialism</note> philosophy, is fickle, a wanderer, and has a wicked mind. If **Venus** is in the twelfth house, he destroys his kinsmen, has a lustful mind, and is poor. If **Saturn** is in the twelfth house, he is of unsound mind, foolish, yet wealthy and a deceiver. || 98 ||

If **Rahu** is in the twelfth, he is devoid of character, wealthy, restless, virtuous, a destroyer of previously acquired wealth; and if **Ketu** is in the 12th, he is fickle and lacks character. || 99 ||

---

->**Now, the Results of Planets in Exaltation.**<-

> If the Sun <note>original: "Dinanayaka" (Lord of the Day)</note> is in exaltation, one is wealthy; if the Moon <note>original: "Shitagu" (Cold-rayed)</note>, a commander of an army.
> If Mars <note>original: "Bhunandana" (Son of the Earth)</note>, one enjoys sweets, fine clothes, and ornaments, and is brave.
> If Mercury <note>original: "Saumya" (Son of the Moon)</note>, he increases his lineage, is a leader of men, wise, a conqueror of enemies, and happy.
> If Jupiter <note>original: "Jiva"</note>, he is the founder of a dynasty, well-behaved, clever, learned, and dear to kings. || 100 ||

> If **Venus** is in its sign of exaltation, one is fond of luxury, music, and dance.
> If **Saturn** <note>original: "Manda" (The Slow One)</note>, one is the lord of villages, cities, and forests, but devoted to young girls.
> If **Rahu**, one is a leader of thieves, the best of his clan, brave, a doer of bad deeds, and wealthy.
> If **Ketu**, one is fond of thieves and becomes dear to a lowly ruler. || 101 ||

> A single planet in its highest exaltation, if aspected by a friendly planet,
> Makes a man a ruler of the earth, worshipful, prosperous, and endowed with friends. || 102 ||

> With one planet in exaltation and strong, one is blessed and wealthy.
> With two, a vassal; with three, one becomes a king.
> With four planets in exaltation and placed in the angles <note>Kendra: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note>, one is a powerful King of Kings.
> With five heavenly bodies reaching their exalted houses, one becomes a Lord of the World. || 103 ||

Now the results of planets in their signs of exaltation are described. At the time of birth, if even one planet is in its highest exaltation and is aspected by its friendly planet, the person born becomes a king. If one planet is in exaltation and strong but not aspected by a friend, the person is blessed and wealthy, but not a king at that time. With two planets in exaltation, the person becomes a vassal or a provincial governor <note>original: "Mandaleshvara"</note>. With three planets in exaltation, the person becomes a sovereign king. If four planets are in exaltation and also placed in the angles (Kendras), the person becomes a powerful King of Kings or an Emperor (<term>Badshah</term> <note>Persian/Urdu term for Emperor, used here to explain the Sanskrit "Bhupalarat"</note>). If five planets are in exaltation, the person becomes a Lord of the World or a Universal Emperor (<term>Chakravarti</term> <note>An ideal universal ruler in Indian philosophy</note>). Everything else is self-explanatory. || 100-103 ||

If the **Sun** is in its sign of exaltation, one is wealthy; if the **Moon**, a commander; if **Mars**, endowed with sweets, clothes, and ornaments, and is valiant. If **Mercury**, he increases the lineage, is a master of people, wise, a conqueror of foes, and happy. If **Jupiter**, he is the creator of a dynasty, well-behaved, clever, learned, and beloved by the king. || 100 ||
