# With the Commentary on the Jataka Parijata

If **Venus** is in its sign of exaltation <note>Pisces</note>, the person will be a great lover of women, music, and dance. If it is **Saturn** <note>exalted in Libra</note>, he will be a ruler of villages, cities, and marketplaces, and one who enjoys the company of young women. If it is **Rahu** <note>the North Node</note>, he will be a leader of thieves, the best of his lineage, a doer of misdeeds, and wealthy. If it is **Ketu** <note>the South Node</note>, he will be fond of thieves and a favorite of a lowly king. || 101 ||

Even if a single exalted planet is aspected by <term>aspected: a "drishti" or planetary gaze where one planet influences another from a distance</term> or joined with a friendly planet, it produces a child who is a king, venerable, and endowed with wealth; that is, one born under such a combination becomes a wealthy and respected ruler. || 102 ||

If one planet is powerful in exaltation at birth, the person becomes blessed and wealthy. If there are two such planets, he becomes a <term>Samanta: a local chieftain or subordinate king</term>. If there are three, he becomes a king. If four powerful exalted planets are in the <term>Kendras: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, considered the pillars of a horoscope</term>, he becomes a great emperor. If five planets are exalted, he becomes a <term>Chakravarti: a universal monarch whose wheels of power roll everywhere</term>. || 103 ||

### Now, the Results of Planets in Mula-Trikona
<note>Mula-Trikona is a specific favorable position for a planet, slightly less powerful than exaltation but stronger than its own sign.</note>

->If the **Sun** is in its Mula-Trikona house <note>Leo</note>, the person born is wealthy and praised;<-
->In the **Moon** <note>Taurus</note>, endowed with wealth and happiness; in **Mars** <note>Aries</note>, angry and devoid of mercy.<-
->In the **Son of the Moon (Mercury)** <note>Virgo</note>, wealthy and meditative; in the **Teacher of the Gods (Jupiter)** <note>Sagittarius</note>, a seeker of pleasure and dear to kings.<-
->In **Venus** <note>Libra</note>, the lord of villages and cities; in the **Son of the Sun (Saturn)** <note>Aquarius</note>, a hero; and in **Rahu**, wealthy. || 104 ||<-

Now the results of planets in their respective Mula-Trikona positions are stated. The meaning of the verse is clear. || 104 ||

If the **Sun** is in its Mula-Trikona house (Leo), one is wealthy and worthy of praise. If it is the **Moon**, one is endowed with wealth and happiness. If **Mars** is in its Mula-Trikona, one is angry and merciless. If it is **Mercury**, one is wealthy and an ascetic. If it is **Jupiter**, one is a pleasure-seeker and beloved by kings. If it is **Venus**, one is the master of villages and cities. If it is **Saturn**, one is a warrior, and if it is **Rahu**, one is wealthy. || 104 ||

### Now, the Results of Planets in Their Own Signs

->If the **Sun** is in its own sign <note>Leo</note>, one has a beautiful mansion but is ill-behaved and excessively lustful; in the **Moon** <note>Cancer</note>,<-
->one is endowed with brilliance, beauty, and wealth; in **Mars** <note>Aries/Scorpio</note>, famous for agriculture and strength; in **Mercury** <note>Gemini/Virgo</note>, a scholar.<-
->In **Jupiter** <note>Sagittarius/Pisces</note>, devoted to poetry, arts, and the traditional scriptures; **Venus** <note>Taurus/Libra</note> makes one high-minded and wealthy;<-
->In **Saturn** <note>Capricorn/Aquarius</note>, one has fierce valor but is devoid of happiness; in **Rahu**, one possesses fame and wealth. || 105 ||<-
->One becomes more venerable and wealthy than their own kin, highly affluent, or a king equal to a lord of the earth,<-
->according to the sequence of one or more planetary lords occupying their own signs. || 106 ||<-

In these two verses, the results of planets in their own respective signs are told. He in whose birth one or more planets are in their own signs becomes a man who is "more venerable and wealthy than his own kin, highly affluent, and a king equal to a lord of the earth," as stated in the sequential order. This is what is meant: with one planet in its own sign, one is equal to his kin; with two planets in their own signs, one is "superior to the clan" (better than his family); and in this order, if all planets are in their own signs, he becomes a king. The rest is clear. || 75-106 ||

If the **Sun** is in its own house, one will have a lovely temple-like home, but be ill-behaved and very lustful. If it is the **Moon**, one is wealthy in brilliance and beauty. If it is **Mars**, one is famous for farming and physical power. If it is **Mercury**, one is a learned scholar. If it is **Jupiter**, one is dedicated to poetry, arts, and the Vedas. If it is **Venus**, one is high-minded and wealthy. If it is **Saturn**, one has fierce courage but lacks happiness; and if it is **Rahu**, one is successful. || 105 ||

If one or more planets are in their own places, then in sequence, one becomes equal to his family, the best in his caste, most respected, wealthy, very wealthy, like a king, and a king. (According to the author of S. Sh.) || 106 ||

### Now, the Results of Planets in a Friend's Sign

->When the **Sun** is in a friend's sign, one becomes a firm friend, a donor, and famous;<-
->When the **Lord of the Night (Moon)** is there, one is born with great respect, happiness, and wealth, delighting the earth.<-

# Chapter 8: On the Combinations of Two or More Planets

->If the Sun's son <note>Saturn</note> is in a friendly sign, one is wealthy and dear to friends; if Mercury, a leader in cleverness and humor; if Jupiter, devoted to the virtuous; if Venus, happy with children; if Saturn, wealthy through the food of others. (107)<-
->Famous, happy, loved by friends, clever and virtuous, wise, a seeker of pleasure, and one who eats the food of others—these are the results of the seven planets from the Sun onwards when placed in a friendly sign. (108)<-
->One who has one planet in a friendly house enjoys the wealth of others. With two in friendly houses, one enjoys the wealth of friends. With three, one enjoys wealth earned by oneself. (109)<-
->With four planets in friendly signs, one is a donor. With five, a leader of a group. With six, a commander of an army. With seven planets, one becomes a lord of the earth <note>a king</note>. (110)<-
->With three planets in exaltation <term>Ucha; the highest point of strength for a planet</term>, one is a king. With three in their own signs, a minister. With three combust <term>Asta; hidden by the Sun's rays</term>, a slave. With three in debilitation <term>Nicha; the weakest point for a planet</term>, one is dull-witted. (111)<-

Now the results of planets in their respective friendly signs are explained. If at the time of birth three planets are in exaltation, the person born becomes a king. If three planets are in their own signs, the person becomes a king's minister. If three planets are combust—meaning overwhelmed by the Sun's rays—the person becomes a slave or servant. If three planets are in their signs of debilitation, the person becomes dull-witted. The rest is self-explanatory. (107-111)

If the Sun is in a friendly house, one is firm in friendship, a donor, and famous. If the Moon, one is highly respected, happy, and wealthy. If Mars, one is dear to wealth, home, and friends. If Mercury, one is clever and a leader in humor. If Jupiter, a lover of good people. If Venus, happy with sons. If Saturn, wealthy through the food of others. (107)

Famous, happy, affectionate toward friends, clever and virtuous, wise, a seeker of pleasure, and one who eats the food of others—these are the results of the seven planets from the Sun onwards when placed in friendly signs. (108)

One planet in a friendly sign makes one an enjoyer of others' wealth; two in friendly houses make one an enjoyer of friends' wealth. Three make one enjoy wealth created by oneself. (109)

Four in friendly houses make one a donor. Five planets make one a chief. Six planets make one a general. Seven planets make one a king. (110)

Three planets in exaltation make one a king. Three planets in their own signs make one a minister. Three planets combust make one a slave, and three planets in debilitation make one dull-witted. (111)

---

# Now, the Results of Planets in Inimical Signs.

->If the Sun is in an enemy's sign, one abandons paternal happiness and is intent on service. If the Moon, one is devoted to the mother's sorrow and suffers from heart disease. If Mars, one is deformed, ungrateful, and base. If Mercury, happy but with a sinful mind. If Jupiter, devoted to auspicious things. If Venus, a servant. If Saturn, distressed by the sorrows of the road. (112)<-
->Five planets in enemy signs give mixed results. Six planets give diminished happiness. Seven planets cause all kinds of sorrow. Combust planets likewise produce inauspiciousness. (113)<-

Now the results of planets situated in enemy signs are explained in two verses. If at the time of birth five planets are in enemy signs, they give mixed results—a combination of good and bad. Six planets in enemy signs make the person devoid of happiness. Seven planets in enemy signs cause all kinds of sorrow—giving various types of pain. In the same manner, combust planets—those hidden by the Sun—bring about inauspiciousness for the person. The rest is clear. (112-113)

If the Sun is in an enemy's sign, one abandons paternal happiness and becomes a servant to others. If the Moon is there, then...

# With the Commentary on Jataka Parijata
## Page 284

If the Moon is afflicted, the person causes distress to their mother and suffers from heart disease. If Mars is so placed, they are disabled, ungrateful, and impure. If Mercury, they are happy but possess a sinful mind. If Jupiter, they are devoted to good deeds. If Venus, they are a servant. If Saturn, they are overwhelmed by grief during travels. ॥ 112 ॥

If five planets are in the house of enemies <note>the 6th house</note>, they give mixed results; six planets there make one devoid of happiness; seven planets cause all kinds of suffering; and combust planets <note>planets too close to the Sun</note> always produce inauspicious results. ॥ 113 ॥

->**Now, the Results of Debilitated Planets**<-
<note>Debilitation, or 'Neecha', refers to the sign where a planet is at its weakest.</note>

> When the Sun is debilitated, the person is fallen, without kinsmen, and fond of living abroad.
> When the Moon is so, they are sickly, with little merit or wealth. When Mars, they are ungrateful yet wealthy.
> When Mercury, they are mean and quarrel with relatives. When Jupiter, they are a slanderer and wicked.
> When Venus, they suffer from misery. When Saturn, they are deprived of wealth and wife, distressed, and cruel. ॥ 114 ॥
> In their preferred signs of exaltation, planets give full results; in their own divisions <note>Navamsha</note>, the result is like being in their trine.
> In a friend's division, the result is equal to being in their own sign; in debilitation, enemy signs, or combustion, the result is like being in an enemy's sign. ॥ 115 ॥
> From exaltation, trine, own sign, friend's sign, enemy's sign, to debilitation—these eight states—
> The results are respectively: full, three-quarters, half, one-quarter, very little, and fruitless. ॥ 116 ॥
> All auspicious planets situated in the angles <note>1st, 4th, 7th, 10th houses</note> or trines <note>5th, 9th houses</note> are givers of good if they are strong.
> Malefic planets, if strong and placed in the 3rd, 6th, or 11th houses, also become auspicious. ॥ 117 ॥
> Through these various combinations of six, five, three, four, or two types of planetary contacts,
> The results of planets in exaltation and other states are declared, by the grace of the light-bestowing masters. ॥ 118 ॥

Now, the proportion of results is explained alongside the description of debilitated planets. In their preferred signs of exaltation, the planets give "complete" or full results for that house. In the divisions <note>Navamsha</note>, whether in their own sign or exaltation, they give results similar to being in a trine <note>Moolatrikona</note>. In a friend's division, they give results equal to their own sign. Those planets that are debilitated, in an enemy's sign, or combust <note>hidden by the Sun's light</note>, give results equal to being in an enemy's sign.

Now the mathematical proportion of results is determined:
*   In Exaltation: Full result <gloss>1</gloss>
*   In Trine (Moolatrikona): Three-quarters <gloss>3/4</gloss> result
*   In a Friend's House: Half <gloss>1/2</gloss> result
*   In an Enemy's House: One-quarter <gloss>1/4</gloss> result
*   In Debilitation: Very little <gloss>1/8</gloss> result
*   In Combustion (with the Sun): Fruitless <gloss>0</gloss> result.

Strong auspicious planets placed in the angles or trines (1, 4, 7, 10, 5, 9) are all givers of good. If malefic planets are strong and placed in the 3rd, 6th, or 11th houses, they become "splendid," meaning they grant auspicious results. Everything else is clear. With the 118th verse, this chapter is concluded. ॥ 114-118 ॥

The *Sudha* (Nectar) commentary on the *Parijata* was composed by Kapileshwara. This eighth chapter on planetary combinations is now complete. ॥ 8 ॥

<margin>Summary of Hindi translation of verses 114-116</margin>
If the Sun is in its sign of debilitation <note>Libra</note>, the person is fallen, friendless, and a traveler. If the Moon is debilitated <note>Scorpio</note>, they are sickly, have little religious merit, but are wealthy. If Mars <note>Cancer</note>, they are ungrateful but rich. If Mercury <note>Pisces</note>, they are lowly and oppose their family. If Jupiter <note>Capricorn</note>, they are a slanderer and wicked. If Venus <note>Virgo</note>, they are miserable. If Saturn <note>Aries</note>, they are poor, henpecked, troubled, and cruel. ॥ 114 ॥

Planets in their exaltation sign give full results. In their own Navamsha, they act as if in their Moolatrikona. In a friend's Navamsha, they act as if in their own sign. In debilitation, an enemy's house, or when combust, they act as if in an enemy's sign. ॥ 115 ॥

The results of the Sun and other planets are as follows: full in exaltation; one-quarter less in trine; half in a friend's sign; one-quarter in an enemy's house; very little in debilitation; and a combust planet gives no result at all. ॥ 116 ॥

<header>Chapter on the Results of Mandi, Years, etc. || 6 ||</header>

All auspicious planets <note>benefics like Jupiter, Venus, Mercury, and the Moon</note> are powerful when situated in the <term>Kendra</term><note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</note> or <term>Trikona</term><note>the 1st, 5th, and 9th houses</note>. If the inauspicious planets <note>malefics like Saturn, Mars, and the Sun</note> are in the 3rd, 6th, or 11th houses, they produce good results || 117 ||

The results of the conjunctions of six, five, four, three, or two planets—that is, the results of <term>Yoga</term> involving multiple planets—as well as the results of planets in various houses and their positions in exaltation, etc., have been described in this 8th chapter by the grace of the Sun and other deities || 118 ||

# Now begins Chapter 9: Results of Mandi, Years, etc.

Now, the chapter on the results of Mandi, years, and so on is being explained. First, the results of Mandi <note>also known as Gulika, a mathematical point in the sky considered the "son of Saturn"</note> situated in the twelve houses will be told, followed by the results of years and other cycles—

> I speak of the results of Mandi and the years. When Gulika is in the <term>Ascendant</term><note>the 1st house</note>, the person is dull-witted and sickly; if joined by a malefic planet, they are deceitful, lustful, and of bad conduct.
> In the second house, they are obsessed with sensual pleasures, a wanderer, angry, and prone to foul speech. If joined by malefic "sky-goers" <note>planets</note>, they are destitute or devoid of knowledge. || 1 ||
> Possessed of qualities like estrangement, pride, and arrogance, with great anger and anxiety regarding the acquisition of wealth; free from sorrow and fear, yet without brothers—this occurs when the son of Saturn <note>Gulika</note> is in the third house. || 2 ||
> Situated in the fourth house, the son of Saturn makes one devoid of learning, wealth, home, happiness, and relatives, and a wanderer of fields. In the fifth house, the son of Saturn makes one devoid of character, fickle-minded, sinful in thought, with few sons and a short life. || 3 ||
> A destroyer of many enemies, a delighter in the lore of spirits <note>exorcism or occultism</note>, and brave if the son of Saturn is in the sixth house. In the seventh house, the grandson of the Sun <note>Gulika</note> makes one a quarreler, lustful, generous, an enemy to all people, dull-witted, and ungrateful. || 4 ||
> With defective eyes and a distorted or small body in the eighth; a destroyer of elders and father, performing lowly deeds in the ninth. Accompanied by a hundred misfortunes when the son of Saturn is in the tenth, performing deeds harmful to one's own family, devoid of proper conduct, and without honor. || 5 ||
> Possessed of great happiness, wealth, splendor, and beauty in the eleventh, the son of the Sun's son <note>Gulika</note> kills the elder brother of the native. In the twelfth house, the son of Saturn makes one devoid of sensual enjoyment, poor in speech, yet skillful, though a thief of all wealth. || 6 ||

"Results of Mandi, years, etc." In this chapter, I speak of the results of Mandi and the years; "I perform" is the implied completion. When Gulika is in the <term>Ascendant</term>, the <term>native</term><note>the person whose birth chart is being read</note> is dull-witted and sickly. If Gulika is joined by a malefic planet there, the native is deceitful, lustful, and of bad conduct. In the "wealth house" (the second house), the native is obsessed with sensual objects, a wanderer, angry, and a "bad-talker" (one who speaks crudely). If Gulika is joined by malefic planets there, the native is "lost-wealth" (poor) or devoid of knowledge. The others are clear in meaning. || 1-6 ||

The results of <term>Gulika</term> in the houses are stated: If Gulika is in the <term>Ascendant</term>, the <term>native</term> is dull-witted and sickly. If Gulika is joined by a malefic planet there, they are a cheat, angry, and of bad conduct. If Gulika is in the wealth house, they are obsessed with pleasures, a wanderer, angry, and a speaker of foul nonsense. If Gulika is joined by a malefic planet there, they are poor or a fool. || 1 ||

If Gulika is in the third house, the person possesses bad qualities like estrangement and ego, has a particularly angry temperament, is anxious about collecting wealth, is free from sorrow and fear, and is without brothers. || 2 ||

If Gulika is in the fourth house, the person is devoid of learning, wealth, home, happiness, and family. They also live in foreign lands. If Gulika is in the fifth house, they are devoid of character, fickle-minded, of sinful intellect, with few sons and a short lifespan. || 3 ||

<header>From the Jataka Parijata with Commentary</header>

If Gulika is situated in the house of enemies <note>the 6th house</note>, the person will be a slayer of many foes, a lover of the occult sciences <note>literally "rejoicing in the knowledge of spirits"</note>, and very courageous. If Gulika is in the seventh house, the person becomes quarrelsome, possesses a wicked wife, is an opponent to all people, has a dull intellect, and is ungrateful. || 4 ||

If Gulika is in the eighth house, the person will have defective eyes and face, and a short stature. If in the ninth, they will be a performer of low deeds and a slayer of elders and ancestors <note>metaphorically, one who brings ruin or dishonor to them</note>. If Gulika is in the tenth house, the person will be engaged in hundreds of inauspicious deeds, devoid of conduct beneficial to their own lineage, and without honor. || 5 ||

If Gulika is in the 11th house, the person born is very happy, wealthy, radiant, and beautiful, but may be a slayer of their elder brother. If Gulika is in the twelfth house, the person wears clothes devoid of sensual appeal <note>ascetic or unkempt</note>, is proficient in pitiful speech, and steals the wealth of others. || 6 ||

-> If the Ascendant falls in a trine from Mandi, or in its twelfth-division or ninth-division; or if planets are associated with Mandi, or if they are the lords of the sign occupied by Mandi—all these always produce unfavorable results. || 7 || <-

The Ascendant <term>Lagna: the rising sign at birth</term> falling in a trine <note>the 5th or 9th positions</note> from where Mandi/Gulika is stationed, or the planets situated in the <term>Dwadasamsha: 1/12th division of a sign</term> or <term>Navamsha: 1/9th division of a sign</term> of Mandi; the planets joined with Gulika; and the <term>Rashipati: the planetary lord of the sign</term> in which Mandi resides—all these are always harmful to the person born. || 7 ||

# Results of Mandi Joined with Other Planets

-> If Gulika is joined with the Sun, the person hates their father; with the Moon, they cause distress to the mother; with Mars, they are deprived of younger siblings. With Mercury, they are insane; with Jupiter, they are a hypocrite and a critic; with Venus, they are afflicted by diseases caused by women and are fond of low-born women. || 8 || <-

-> When the son of Saturn <note>Gulika</note> is joined with Saturn, the person is devoted to ease; with the Serpent <note>Rahu</note>, they give poison to others; with the Crested One <note>Ketu</note>, they are an arsonist. Even if born in a royal family, if Gulika is in a house joined with a "poisonous canal" <note>Visha-Nadi: specific inauspicious degrees</note>, they certainly become a beggar. Planets joined with the sub-planets produce unfavorable results for the native. || 9 || <-

Now the results of Mandi's conjunction with planets are described: If birth occurs when Gulika is joined with the Sun, the native hates their father. Joined with the Moon, they cause pain to the mother. Joined with Mars, they are without brothers. Joined with Mercury, they are possessed by insanity <note>original: "pagal"</note>. Joined with Jupiter, the teacher of the gods, they become a hypocrite, an atheist, and a fault-finder in others. Joined with Venus, they are struck by diseases <note>such as gonorrhea or other ailments</note> caused by women, and they love women of low lineage. || 8 ||

When Gulika is joined with Saturn, the person is intent on their own comfort. Joined with Rahu, they are a giver of poison to others. Joined with Ketu, they set fire to the houses of others. Furthermore, if Gulika is in a sign joined with a "poisonous canal" <note>Visha-Nadi</note>, even one born of a royal line will surely become a beggar living on alms <note>refer to the commentary on Chapter 5, Verse 12 for details on Visha-Nadi</note>. Planets joined with the sub-planets like <term>Dhumra: "smoky," one of the secondary shadow planets</term> and others give adverse results. All houses and planets associated with Gulika are indeed harmful. It has been said so—

It emphasizes that Gulika generally acts as a malefic force, causing physical defects, social dishonor, or family strife.</summary>

# Chapter 6: On the Results of Mandi and the Years

->The conjunction of Gulika <note>A mathematical point in the sky considered a "son" of Saturn; usually seen as malefic.</note> should always be declared as indicating defects. In contrast, the conjunction of Yamakantaka <note>Considered the "son" of Jupiter; usually seen as auspicious.</note> should always be declared as auspicious.<-

->In providing affliction, Gulika is more powerful; in providing auspiciousness, Yamakantaka is superior. All other secondary planets, in providing misfortune, possess less strength than that attributed to Mandi <note>Another name for Gulika, or a closely related mathematical point.</note>. (6)<-

If Gulika is joined with the Sun, the person opposes their father. If joined with the Moon, they cause distress to the mother. If joined with Mars, they are deprived of younger siblings. If joined with Mercury, they become insane. If joined with Jupiter, they are a hypocrite and a slanderer of others. If joined with Venus, they are struck by diseases born of women and become the husband of a low-class woman. If the son of Saturn (Gulika) is joined with Saturn himself, the person is endowed with happiness. If joined with Rahu <note>The North Node of the Moon.</note>, they are a poisoner. If joined with Ketu <note>The South Node of the Moon.</note>, they are a burner of houses and the like. If Gulika is in a house associated with the Brahmin pulse <note>A technical term referring to specific divisions of the zodiac (Nadis).</note>, even a king will certainly become a beggar. At the time of birth, planets joined with secondary planets (Upagrahas) produce inauspicious results for the native. (8-9)

### Now, the Results of the Years (Samvatsaras)

Born in the <gloss>1</gloss> **Prabhava** year, one is courageous, truthful, endowed with all virtues, a knower of time, and righteous.
Born in the <gloss>2</gloss> **Vibhava** year, one is lustful, pure, eternally content, endowed with great wealth, and famous for their relatives and learning. (10)

In the <gloss>3</gloss> **Shukla** year, one becomes an adulterer, devoid of strength, but charitable and high-minded.
Born in the year named <gloss>4</gloss> **Pramoda**, one is a minister, intent on their work, and very clever in speech.
Born in <gloss>5</gloss> **Prajotpatti**, one is righteous, devoted to charity, possesses children and wealth, and is peaceful.
In the <gloss>6</gloss> **Angirasa** year, one is a knower of ethics, skillful, compassionate, and constantly wealthy. (11)

Born in the <gloss>7</gloss> **Shrimukha** year, one is fond of others' wives, pure, and wealthy.
In the <gloss>8</gloss> **Bhava** year, one is a yogi, a tax-collector (or servant of the king), and famous for great wealth and strength.
In the <gloss>9</gloss> **Yuva** year, one is greedy, of fickle mind, has a lean and sickly body, is angry, and is a physician.
Born in <gloss>10</gloss> **Dhata**, one is devoted to others' wives, speaks only for the sake of their own interests, and is a rogue. (12)

One is wealthy in the <gloss>11</gloss> **Ishvara** year, endowed with strength and intelligence, and a perceiver of merit.
Born in the <gloss>12</gloss> **Bahudhanya** year, one performs good deeds, is an enjoyer of life, and follows the profession of a merchant.
In the <gloss>13</gloss> **Pramathi** year, one is cruel, devoted to sin, angry, without relatives, yet happy.
Born in the <gloss>14</gloss> **Vikrama** year, one is wealthy, a commander of an army, and valorous. (13)

In the <gloss>15</gloss> **Vrisha** year, one is poor, shameless, and performs improper deeds.
In <gloss>16</gloss> **Chitrabhanu**, one possesses brilliance and beauty like the Sun.
In <gloss>17</gloss> **Subhanu**, one follows the learning, conduct, and religion of their own family.
In the <gloss>18</gloss> **Tarana** year, one is endowed with much wealth and strength and is wise. (14)

Born in the <gloss>19</gloss> **Parthiva** year, one is a lord of men (king), wealthy, incomparable, and happy.
In the <gloss>20</gloss> **Vyaya** year, one is lustful, timid, but endowed with character, wealth, and virtue; [alternatively] one is a sinner.
In the <gloss>21</gloss> **Sarvajit** year, one is eloquent, very powerful, a scholar, virtuous, and a knower of truth.
Born in <gloss>22</gloss> **Sarvadhari**, one is prosperous, an artisan, and dear to the king. (15)

In the <gloss>23</gloss> **Virodhi** year, one is sorrowful, intent on wickedness, devoted to great sinners, and cruel.
Born in <gloss>24</gloss> **Vikriti**, one is deceitful, overcome by passion, and has a mind for mantras, rituals, and tantra.
In the <gloss>25</gloss> **Khara** year, one is free from delusion but devoid of virtue, speaks very piteously, is a sinner and a rogue.
In <gloss>26</gloss> **Nandana**, one causes joy to all, is dear to the king, and knows the meaning of mantras. (16)

In the <gloss>27</gloss> **Vijaya** year, one is righteous and endowed with truth.
If born in the <gloss>28</gloss> **Jaya** year, one is like a king or is a king.
In the <gloss>29</gloss> **Manmatha** year, one is agitated by passion and sexual desire, and has conquered their enemies.
In the <gloss>30</gloss> **Durmukha** year, one is devoid of virtue and wealth and is of bad character. (17)

# Page 288
## From the Jataka Parijata with Commentary

One born in the year **Hemalamba** <note>31st year of the cycle; "Golden Pendant"</note> is wicked-minded and eager for agricultural work. One born in the year **Vilamba** <note>32nd year; "Delaying"</note> is wealthy, supported by the learned <note>original: "Vipra" or Brahmins</note>, but gives up the fruits of his labor and is prone to procrastination. One born in the year **Vikari** <note>33rd year; "Transforming" or "Deformed"</note> is sickly, timid, lacks wealth, is fickle-minded, and of low character. One born in the year **Sharvari** <note>34th year; "Night"</note> is courageous, very wealthy, enjoys life, is good-hearted, and follows the vows of truth. || 18 ||

One born in the year **Plava** <note>35th year; "Boat" or "Flood"</note> is peaceful, generous, a mine of compassion, brave, and takes refuge in his own duty <note>Dharma</note>. One born in the year **Shubhakrit** <note>36th year; "Doing Good"</note> is wealthy but deceived by people, a doer of auspicious deeds, wise, and possesses a handsome body and a good intellect. One born in the year **Shobhakrit** <note>37th year; "Doing Splendidly"</note> is wise, possesses the qualities of a king, and is fond of learning and recreation. One born in the year **Krodhi** <note>38th year; "Angry"</note> is a sufferer, a pursuer of others' wives, of deceitful mind, and filled with anger. || 19 ||

One born in the year **Vishvavasu** <note>39th year; "Universal Wealth"</note> is honorable, fond of humor, and praises those with virtuous wealth. One born in the year **Parabhava** <note>40th year; "Defeat"</note> is addicted to wicked speech, born as a target for humiliation, and a destroyer of his lineage. One born in the year **Plavanga** <note>41st year; "Leaping" or "Monkey"</note> is lustful, devoted to his relatives, fond of children, and of dull intellect. One born in the year **Kilaka** <note>42nd year; "Wedge" or "Pin"</note> is intent on worshipping the gods, very fortunate, and endowed with bravery. || 20 ||

One born in the year **Pramadi** <note>47th year; "Careless"</note> creates estrangement among relatives and is lustful for others' wives. One born in the year **Ananda** <note>48th year; "Joy"</note> is of a joyful soul, devoted to all the scriptures and Vedas <note>Agama and Shruti</note>, and a knower of reality. One born in the year **Rakshasa** <note>49th year; "Demonic"</note> is sinful, engages in useless talk, and harms the virtuous. One born in the year **Anala** <note>50th year; "Fire"</note> is a donor, endowed with the virtue of charity, peaceful, and of good conduct. || 22 ||

One born in the year **Pingala** <note>51st year; "Tawny"</note> is a yogi, of conquered mind, and becomes an ascetic. One born in the year **Kalayukta** <note>52nd year; "Joined with Time"</note> is a knower of time, wealthy, enjoys life, and performs good deeds. One born in the year **Siddharthi** <note>53rd year; "Successful"</note> has his goals accomplished, is devoted to teachers and gods, and is wise. One born in the year **Raudra** <note>54th year; "Terrible"</note> is an adulterer, of crooked mind, arrogant, and of bad conduct. || 23 ||

One born in the year **Durmati** <note>55th year; "Evil-minded"</note> is lustful, of dull intellect, afflicted by grief, and wicked. One born in the year **Dundubhi** <note>56th year; "Drum"</note> has a large belly, arms, and head, and is a man of enjoyment. One born in the year **Rudhirodgari** <note>57th year; "Vomiting Blood"</note> is wise, devoted to truth, happy, and wealthy. One born in the year **Raktakshi** <note>58th year; "Red-eyed"</note> is peaceful, loved by relatives, very fortunate, and of good character. || 24 ||

One born in the year **Krodhana** <note>59th year; "Wrathful"</note> is an adulterer, follows a bad path, hates relatives, and is a thief. One born in the year **Kshaya** <note>60th year; "Decay" or "Final"</note> is of disciplined conduct, very cheerful, handsome, honorable, and free from enemies and disease. || 25 ||

# Chapter 6: On the Results of the Years and Months

<page-num>289</page-num>

<header>Chapter 6: Results of the Years and Months</header>

<gloss>51</gloss> Pingala, <gloss>52</gloss> Kalayukta, <gloss>53</gloss> Siddharta, <gloss>54</gloss> Raudra, <gloss>55</gloss> Durmati, <gloss>56</gloss> Dundubhi, <gloss>57</gloss> Rudhirodgari, <gloss>58</gloss> Raktakshi, <gloss>59</gloss> Krodhana, <gloss>60</gloss> Kshaya.

These sixty <term>Samvatsaras</term> <note>The 60-year Jovian cycle used in Hindu astrology</note> are produced by the mean transit of Jupiter through the zodiac signs. This is based on the authority of Bhaskara and others who state, "The experts in the Samhitas <note>astrological compendiums</note> speak of the years based on Jupiter's mean transit." To calculate them, take the total revolutions of Jupiter on the current day, multiply by twelve, add the current sign Jupiter is occupying, and divide by sixty. The remainder indicates the year, counting from Vijaya and so on. This is according to the words of the **Surya Siddhanta** <note>The "Sun Precept," a foundational Sanskrit text on Indian astronomy</note>: "The revolutions of Jupiter multiplied by twelve, added to the current signs, and divided by sixty, give the years starting from Vijaya." However, nowadays, the Shaka era year is divided by sixty, and the remainder indicates the year counting from Prabhava, because the Shaka era began with the year named Prabhava. The results for a person born in any of these sixty years are stated here. The verses are simple in meaning. || 10-25 ||

**Now the results of the years (Prabhava etc.) are told:**

If one is born in the **Prabhava** year, they are courageous, truthful, endowed with all virtues, a knower of time, and righteous. If born in the **Vibhava** year, they are lustful, pure, always content, possessed of great wealth, and endowed with relatives, knowledge, and fame. || 10 ||

If born in the **Shukla** year, they pursue the wives of others, are powerful, charitable, and high-minded. If born in the **Pramoda** year, they are a minister, absorbed in their work, and clever in speech. One born in the **Prajapati** year is a performer of religious duties, intent on charity, has children, is wealthy, and peaceful. One born in the **Angira** year is a master of policy, skillful, constantly compassionate, and rich. || 11 ||

If born in the **Shrimukha** year, they are fickle toward the wives of others, pure, and wealthy. If born in the **Bhava** year, they are a yogi, a ruler, very wealthy, very powerful, and famous. If born in the **Yuva** year, they are greedy, of restless intellect, lean, have a diseased body, are irritable, and a physician. If born in the **Dhata** year, they are devoted to the wives of others, a deceptive talker regarding work and money, and a rogue. || 12 ||

If born in the **Ishvara** year, they are prosperous, powerful, intelligent, and appreciative of virtues. If born in the **Bahudhanya** year, they are a performer of good deeds, an enjoyer of pleasures, and a merchant. If born in the **Pramathi** year, they are cruel, sinful, angry, without relatives, and happy. If born in the **Vikrama** year, they are wealthy, a commander of an army, and valorous. || 13 ||

If born in the **Vrisha** year, they are poor, shameless, and lazy. If born in the **Chitrabhanu** year, they are as radiant as the sun and handsome. If born in the **Subhanu** year, they are endowed with the knowledge and conduct of their own lineage. If born in the **Tarana** year, they are very wealthy, powerful, and wise. || 14 ||

If born in the **Parthiva** year, they are a king, prosperous, and incomparably happy. If born in the **Vyaya** year, they are lustful, cowardly, devoid of character, wealth, and virtue, and a sinner.

If born in the **Sarvajit** year, they are talkative, extremely powerful, a scholar of the scriptures, virtuous, and a philosopher. If born in the **Sarvadhari** year, they are prosperous, a craftsman, and a favorite of the king. || 15 ||

If born in the **Virodhi** year, they are sorrowful, devoted to wickedness, a doer of particularly sinful acts, and cruel. If born in the **Vikrita** year, they are deceitful, overcome by lust, and possess an intellect for mantras, rituals, and tantra. One born in the **Khara** year is detached (in a negative sense), devoid of virtue, speaks very humble/pitiful words, is a sinner, and a villain. A person born in the **Nandana** year brings joy to all, is a favorite of the king, and knows the meaning of mantras. || 16 ||

If born in the **Vijaya** year, they are religious, truthful, and wealthy. If born in the **Jaya** year, they are like a king or are a king. If born in the **Manmatha** year, they are restless for love and a conqueror of enemies. If born in the **Durmukha** year, they are devoid of virtue and devoid of character. || 17 ||

If born in the **Hemalambi** year, they are an evil soul and eager for work such as agriculture. **Vilambi**...

# Chapter 6: On the Results of Human Birth Years and Other Cycles

## Now, the Results of the Seasons.

> One born in the **Spring** season is long-lived, wealthy, and fond of fragrances.
> In the **Summer** season, one is clever at utilizing deep waters, a seeker of pleasure, slender-bodied, and highly intelligent.
> Born in the **Rainy** season, one enjoys salty, milky, and pungent foods, possesses pleasant speech, and has a clear mind.
> If born in the **Autumn** season, one is a virtuous soul, handsome, happy, and amorous. || 27 ||
> One born in the **Early Winter** season is a practitioner of yoga, slender, a farmer, a seeker of pleasure, and capable.
> Born in the **Late Winter** season, one is devoted to the rites of bathing and charity, follows their own duty <note>Dharma</note>, is proud, and becomes famous. || 28 ||

Now the results of the seasons are explained. Regarding this, it is said: "From the sun's passage through two signs starting from Capricorn, the six seasons occur, beginning with Late Winter and Spring." Thus, when the sun moves through Capricorn and Aquarius, it is the Late Winter season <note>Shishira</note>. In Pisces and Aries, it is Spring <note>Vasanta</note>. In Taurus and Gemini, it is Summer <note>Grishma</note>. In Cancer and Leo, it is the Rainy season <note>Varsha</note>. In Virgo and Libra, it is Autumn <note>Sharad</note>. In Scorpio and Sagittarius, it is Early Winter <note>Hemanta</note>. These are the six seasons. The results for those born in these seasons are stated here, such as "long-lived" and so on. The meaning of these two verses is clear. || 27-28 ||

*If a child is born in the Spring season, they will be long-lived, wealthy, and fond of perfumes. If born in the Summer, they will be a user of deep waters, clever, a pleasure-seeker, thin-framed, and a scholar. A person born in the Rainy season will be a lover of salty, milky, and pungent items, possess good speech, and a clear intellect. A child born in the Autumn season will be a virtuous soul, have a beautiful face, be happy, and lustful. One born in Early Winter will be a yogi, thin-bodied, a farmer, a pleasure-seeker, and powerful. A person born in Late Winter will be devoted to the acts of bathing and giving, follow their own religion, be honorable, and illustrious.* || 27-28 ||

---

## Now, the Results of the Months.

> In **Chaitra** <note>March-April</note>, one is devoted to all arts, traditional scriptures, and the Vedas, always celebrating and devoted to Lakshmi <note>Goddess of wealth</note>.
> In **Vaishakha** <note>April-May</note>, one is skilled in all sciences, independent, and like a king.
> In the month of **Jyeshtha** <note>May-June</note>, one is long-lived, has many sons, and is an expert in the rituals of mantras.
> In **Ashadha** <note>June-July</note>, one is very wealthy, compassionate, a constant seeker of pleasure, yet hateful of others. || 29 ||
> Born in the month of **Shravana** <note>July-August</note>, one is devoted to the worship of gods and the earth-gods <note>Brahmins</note>.
> Born in **Bhadrapada** <note>August-September</note>, one enjoys various countries, is a musician <note>original: tantri - player of stringed instruments</note>, and a dreamer.
> In the month of **Ashwayuja** <note>September-October</note>, one hates their own kin, is poor, and fickle.
> In **Kartika** <note>October-November</note>, one has a nourished body, is a farmer, has large eyes, and possesses much wealth. || 30 ||
> Devoted to the Guru, gods, and ancestors in **Margashirsha** <note>November-December</note> and virtuous; wealthy, virtuous, and strong in **Pushya** <note>December-January; also called Pausha</note> with a prominent nose.
> Of a wicked mind yet following very religious conduct in the month of **Magha** <note>January-February</note>; a daily benefactor and fond of music in **Phalguna** <note>February-March</note>. || 31 ||

Now the results of the months are explained. Since it is said, "The months and lunar days are determined by the measure of the moon," only the lunar months should be accepted here. A lunar month is the period between two new moon endings <note>Amanta system</note>, based on the authority: "A month is the limit of the new moon." Here, this should be understood—the period from the end of the Chaitra new moon to the end of the Vaishakha new moon is one lunar month. When the sun moves in the sign of Aries, that lunar month is named Chaitra. Similarly, from the end of Vaishakha to the end of Jyeshtha, while the sun moves in Taurus, it is the month of Vaishakha, and so on for the other months.

> "Whichever lunar month is completed while the sun resides in Aries and the following signs, 
> that month should be known as Chaitra and so forth." 

The results for those born in these twelve months, Chaitra and the rest, are stated here. The verses are clear in their meaning. || 29-31 ||

*If birth occurs in the month of Chaitra, one will be a knower of all arts, scriptures, and Vedas, and remain engaged in daily festivities and wealth. If birth is in Vaishakha, one will be skilled in all sciences, independent, and...*

## From the Annotated Jataka Parijata

...he becomes a king. If born in the month of **Jyaistha** <note>mid-May to mid-June</note>, he will be long-lived, wealthy, possessed of sons, and an expert in the practice of sacred chants <term>Mantra-kriya: the ritual application of Vedic hymns</term>. If the birth is in the month of **Ashadha** <note>mid-June to mid-July</note>, he will be exceptionally rich, compassionate, a constant enjoyer of pleasures, and one who harbors enmity toward strangers. || 29 ||

If the birth is in the month of **Shravana** <note>mid-July to mid-August</note>, he will be devoted to the worship of the "gods of the earth" <note>original: "Bhumideva" meaning Brahmins</note> and the deities. If born in **Bhadrapada** <note>mid-August to mid-September</note>, he will be absorbed in various countries <note>likely meaning a traveler</note>, a musician <term>Tantri: one who plays stringed instruments</term>, and a dreamer. If born in the month of **Ashvin** <note>mid-September to mid-October</note>, he will be an enemy to his own people, poor, and restless. If in **Kartika** <note>mid-October to mid-November</note>, he will have a sturdy body, be a farmer, have large eyes, and possess great wealth. || 30 ||

If the birth is in the month of **Margashirsha** (Agahan) <note>mid-November to mid-December</note>, he will be a devotee of the gods, teachers, and ancestors, and be a righteous soul. If born in **Pausha** <note>mid-December to mid-January</note>, he will be powerful in wealth, virtue, and strength, and have a prominent nose. If born in **Magha** <note>mid-January to mid-February</note>, he will have a mischievous mind but perform great religious deeds. If born in the month of **Phalguna** <note>mid-February to mid-March</note>, he will be a daily benefactor to others and skilled in singing. || 31 ||

### Results of the Lunar Fortnight (Paksha)

> If born in the bright fortnight, one has many sons, grandsons, and wealth, is devoted to righteousness, and is compassionate. If born in the dark fortnight, one is argumentative in his own affairs, devoted to his mother, but an enemy to his own kinsmen. || 32 ||

Now the results of the lunar fortnight are described. Every month has two fortnights based on the division of "Bright" and "Dark." From the end of the New Moon to the end of the Full Moon is the **Bright Fortnight** <term>Shukla-paksha</term>. From the end of the Full Moon to the end of the New Moon is the second, the **Dark Fortnight** <term>Krishna-paksha</term>. The results for one born in these two fortnights are stated here. Regarding the word "Valaksha" <note>used in the Sanskrit verse</note>: according to the Amarakosha dictionary, "Valaksha, Dhavala, and Arjuna" are all synonyms for white or bright. The rest is self-explanatory. || 32 ||

If the birth is in the **Bright Fortnight**, he will be endowed with many sons, grandsons, and wealth, absorbed in righteousness, and compassionate. If the birth is in the **Dark Fortnight**, he will be one who disputes his own interests, a devotee of his mother, and an enemy to his family. || 32 ||

### Results of the Time of Day (Kala)

> Born at dawn, one is devoted to his duty, lives by good deeds, and is happy. If at midday, he possesses qualities equal to a king. Born in the afternoon, he is wealthy. Born at twilight, he is fond of perfumes and women, has a wicked soul, and is a wanderer. At night, the results are the same as twilight. Born at sunrise, he possesses great happiness. || 33 ||

Now the results of the time of birth are described. "At dawn" means at the face of the day (early morning). The results such as being devoted to one's duty are all quite clear. || 33 ||

If the birth is in the **morning**, he will be engaged in his duty, live a life of good deeds, and be happy. If born at **midday**, he will be like a king and virtuous. If born in the **afternoon**, he will be wealthy. A person born at **twilight** is fond of fragrances and women, is mischievous, and a wanderer. For a man born at **night**, the results are the same as twilight, and if born at the moment of **sunrise**, he will have much happiness. || 33 ||

### Results of the Lunar Day (Tithi)

> One born on the **first** lunar day is very industrious and of holy conduct.
> On the **second**, he is abundant in splendor, cattle, strength, fame, and wealth.
> On the **third**, he is strongly righteous but fearful, and eloquent in speech.
> On the **fourth**, he is ambitious, clever at wandering, and an expert in sacred consultations. || 34 ||
> On the **fifth**, he is devoted to all scriptures and Vedas, lustful, thin-bodied, and restless.
> On the **sixth**, he has no small strength, is like a lord of the earth, wise, but very prone to anger.
> On the **seventh**, he has harsh and loud speech, is a leader of men, of phlegmatic temperament, and strong.
> On the **eighth**, he is very lustful, fond of his sons' wives, and of a "Kapha" (phlegmatic) nature. || 35 ||

# Chapter 6: On the Results of Birth in Various Eras and Times

->**The Results of the Lunar Days**<-

One born on the **ninth** lunar day is famous, possesses a divine body, has a difficult wife and son <note>original: "kudara-tanayah"; implies domestic strife</note>, and is lustful. On the **tenth**, one is righteous, eloquent, blessed with a wife and children, illustrious, and wealthy. On the **eleventh** <note>the day of Vishnu</note>, one is a worshiper of gods and priests, possesses servants, and is affluent. On the **twelfth**, one is engaged in extremely meritorious deeds, is charitable, wealthy, and a scholar. || 36 ||

On the **thirteenth**, one is of a greedy nature, very lustful, and wealthy. On the **fourteenth**, one is prone to anger, covets the wealth and wives of others, and lacks mental resolve. On the **New Moon** <note>Amavasya</note>, one is full of desires yet devoted to the worship of ancestors and gods. If born on the **Full Moon** <note>Purnima</note>, one is wealthy, brings glory to their lineage, and is of a cheerful mind. || 37 ||

Now the results of the lunar days <term>Tithi-phala: the astrological effects of the lunar date of birth</term> are explained. In one lunar fortnight <note>Paksha</note>, there are fifteen lunar days. These are equal to a twelve-degree separation between the Sun and the Moon. Since at the end of the New Moon there is no distance between the Sun and the Moon, it is said: "The New Moon is the meeting of the Sun and Moon." At the end of the Full Moon, the distance between them is six signs <note>180 degrees</note>. Therefore, 1 lunar day = 180° / 15 = 12°. The results for those born in these fifteen lunar days are stated here, beginning with "Great Effort," etc. These verses are clear in their meaning. || 34-37 ||

If birth is on the **first** lunar day, one is very industrious and follows righteous conduct. Born on the **second**, one is radiant and possesses abundant cattle, strength, and performs sacrifices. Born on the **third**, one is strong in merit, fearful <note>perhaps cautious or god-fearing</note>, and speaks with wisdom. Born on the **fourth**, one follows the orders of others, travels often, is clever, and devoted to sacred chants <note>mantras</note>. || 34 ||

Born on the **fifth**, one is devoted to all the traditional scriptures and Vedas, yet is lustful and physically weak. Born on the **sixth**, one is strong as a horse, like a king, intelligent, and irritable. Born on the **seventh**, one has sturdy thighs, speaks harsh words, is a leader of men, has a phlegmatic temperament <note>Kapha nature</note>, and is primarily strong. Born on the **eighth**, one is especially lustful, absorbed in wife and children, and of a phlegmatic temperament. || 35 ||

Born on the **ninth**, one is famous, has a divine body, but has a wicked wife and son, and is lustful. Born on the **tenth**, one is righteous, clever in speech, endowed with wife and children, illustrious, and wealthy. On the **eleventh**, one worships gods and priests, has servants, and is rich. On the **twelfth**, one is engaged in highly meritorious acts, is a renunciant, wealthy, and a scholar. || 36 ||

Born on the **thirteenth**, one is greedy, very lustful, and wealthy. Born on the **fourteenth**, one takes the wealth and wives of others and is of low intelligence. Born on the **New Moon**, one is full of hope and remains devoted to the worship of ancestors and deities. If born on the **Full Moon**, one is wealthy, famous in the family, and has a happy heart. || 37 ||

### Now, the Results of the Days of the Week

One born on **Sunday** <note>the day of the Sun</note> is proud, has reddish-brown hair and eyes, and is a powerful leader. One born on **Monday** <note>the day of the Moon</note> is lustful, has a beautiful body, and is always compassionate. One born on **Tuesday** <note>the day of Mars/Son of Earth</note> is cruel, fond of daring speech and actions, and always active. One born on **Wednesday** <note>the day of Mercury</note> is a worshiper of gods and priests and speaks kindly. || 38 ||

One born on **Thursday** <note>the day of Jupiter/the Guru</note> is a performer of sacrifices, a favorite of kings, virtuous, and famous. One born on **Friday** <note>the day of Venus/the Bright One</note> possesses grain, land, and wealth, is loved by all, and has a sensual mind. One born on **Saturday** <note>the day of Saturn/the Slow One</note> is of dull intellect, consumes the food and wealth of others, is prone to arguments and rumors, is hateful, and skilled at obstructing his kinsmen. || 39 ||

Now the results of the days of the week <term>Vara-phala</term> are explained. There are seven days named after the seven planets starting from the Sun, beginning at sunrise...

The measurement of time is contained within these. "The interval between two sunrises is called a solar day" <note>original: "arkasāvana dinama"</note>. These are the seven weekdays: Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, and Saturday, occurring in that order. This follows the sentiment of the *Surya Siddhanta* <note>An ancient, authoritative Indian treatise on astronomy</note> which states: "Starting from Saturn, the lords of the days follow in descending order of every fourth planet." The results of being born on these seven weekdays are described below. The two verses are clear in their meaning. || 38-39 ||

If birth is on **Sunday**, the person is honorable, has reddish-brown hair, eyes, and body, and is capable. If born on **Monday**, they are lustful, have a beautiful body, and are compassionate day and night. If born on **Tuesday**, they are cruel, always speaking boldly, and devoted to their work. If born on **Wednesday**, they are a worshiper of gods and Brahmins <note>the priestly/scholarly class</note> and a speaker of kind words. || 38 ||

If born on **Thursday**, they perform sacrifices, are a favorite of kings, virtuous, and famous. If born on **Friday**, they possess grain, land, and wealth, are loved by all, and have a sensual nature. If born on **Saturday**, they are generally slow-witted, possess the wealth or food of others, are involved in disputes, are hostile, and are skilled at restraining their kinsmen. || 39 ||

### Now, the Names of the Nakshatras <note>Lunar Mansions</note>.

> The Horse, the Dasras, the Ashvi-pair, and Ashvini are synonyms; Yama, Kritanta, Bharani, and Yamya-bham are the same.
> Hutashana, Agni, Bahula, and Krittika; Vidhi, Virinchi, Shakata, and Rohini. || 40 ||
>
> Saumya, Chandra, Agrahayani, Udu, and Mrigashirsha; the star of Rudra is Ardra.
> Aditi's star is Punarvasu; the Mother of Gods, Tishya, Pushya, and Amarejya are synonyms.
> Ashlesha is Ahi and Bhujanga; the Pitris are the fathers of Magha; Phalguni is Bhagya-bham.
> Aryaman’s is called the Latter (Uttara); Bhaga is the name for the former; Bhanu, Hasta, Aruna, and Arki are synonyms. || 41 ||
>
> Tvashtar is Chitra; Sukhavriddhaki is Swati, also called Marut, Dhata, and Samirana.

> and the Lord of Gods is Jyeshtha; the highest is Mula, the consumer of sacrifices.
> Payas, Purvashadha, Salila, Jala, and Toya are synonyms;
> Uttarashadha is Vishva; the assembly of sages call the next Abhijit. || 43 ||
>
> Shrona, Vishnu, Hari, Shruta, and Shravana are names for the same; Shravishtha is Vasu.
> Prachetas, Shatataraka, and Varuna-bham; Ajaikapada is Ajapat.
> Purva-Proshthapada is the first; then Ahirbudhnya is Uttara-Proshthapada.
> Pushan, Revati, and Paushna-bham are proclaimed in order by the sages. || 44 ||

Now the names of the <term>Nakshatras<note>The 27 (or 28) divisions of the sky along the ecliptic that the moon passes through</note></term> are stated. First, what is meant by the word "Nakshatra"? That which "does not decay" <note>na ksharati</note> or "does not move" <note>na gacchati</note> is a Nakshatra. This means that while planets like the Sun are seen moving in their respective paths, the Nakshatras do not move in that way; they are fixed. The ancient teachers divided the <term>ecliptic<note>krāntimaṇḍala; the sun's apparent path</note></term>, which consists of 21,600 <term>minutes of arc<note>kalā</note></term>, into twenty-seven equal parts of 800 minutes each. These were named "Nakshatras" for the purpose of predicting results and measuring planetary motion. These twenty-seven divisions of the ecliptic are called the twenty-seven Nakshatras. They should be understood as established in the following order:

1. Ashvini, 2. Bharani, 3. Krittika, 4. Rohini, 5. Mrigashirsha, 6. Ardra, 7. Punarvasu, 8. Pushya, 9. Ashlesha, 10. Magha, 11. Purva-Phalguni, 12. Uttara-Phalguni, 13. Hasta, 14. Chitra, 15. Swati, 16. Vishakha, 17. Anuradha, 18. Jyeshtha, 19. Mula, 20. Purvashadha, 21. Uttarashadha, 22. Shravana, 23. Dhanishtha, 24. Shatabhisha, 25. Purva-Bhadrapada...

<header>With the Commentary on Jataka Parijata</header>

### Regarding the Gandanta Stars

> The junction between Mula and Jyeshtha, Magha and Ashlesha, and Revati and Ashvini, lasting for the duration of one <term>Prahar</term><note>A period of approximately 3 hours</note>, is called <term>Gandanta</term>. It bestows great misfortune upon living beings. The specific minutes at the junction of Jyeshtha and Mula are known as <term>Abhukta</term>. Women, sons, cattle, or servants born during those pulses of time become the destroyers of their lineage. || 45 ||

Among the previously mentioned <term>Nakshatras</term><note>Lunar mansions or star clusters</note>, certain portions are designated by the term "Gandanta." These are explained here. The junction of Mula and Jyeshtha, Magha and Ashlesha, and Revati and Ashvini for the duration of one <term>Prahar</term>—which equals seven and a half <term>Ghatikas</term><note>One Ghatika is 24 minutes; 7.5 Ghatikas equals 3 hours</note>. This means: three and three-quarter Ghatikas at the end of Jyeshtha and three and three-quarter Ghatikas at the beginning of Mula. Combined, this duration of seven and a half Ghatikas (7:30) is the time known as Gandanta. This Gandanta is said to be extremely inauspicious and harmful to living beings. Ramacharya has spoken similarly of Gandanta, though limiting it to four Ghatikas: "**The final two Ghatikas of Jyeshtha, Revati, and Ashlesha, and the first two Ghatikas of Mula, Ashvini, and Magha are declared to be the Gandanta.**"

Now, the <term>Abhukta</term> minutes are described: The junction minutes of the Nakshatras Jyeshtha and Mula (specifically one Ghatika comprising the end of Jyeshtha and the start of Mula) are named <term>Abhukta</term>. Those born during this "Abhukta" time—whether they be women (daughters), sons, four-legged animals, or servants—become destroyers of the clan; meaning, they bring about the ruin of the family into which they are born. Regarding these Abhukta minutes, Ramacharya states in the *Muhurta Chintamani*:

> Narada says the Abhukta-Mula consists of four Ghatikas at the end of Jyeshtha and the beginning of Mula. Vashistha declared it to be one or two Ghatikas, while Brihaspati says it is the measure of only one Ghatika. Others say the first, eighth, and final five Ghatikas of Mula and Jyeshtha are included. A child born then should be abandoned, or the father should not look upon its face for eight years.

In the case of a birth during Abhukta, the best course of action to pacify the defect is abandonment. If unable to do so, the father should not look at the face of that son or daughter for a period of eight years. As Narada said:

> One should abandon a son or daughter born in Abhukta-Mula. Or, the father should not behold that child's face for eight years.

<margin>The Gandanta occurs at the junction of Mula-Jyeshtha, Magha-Ashlesha, and Revati-Ashvini for the duration of one Prahar; this is very harmful to creatures. One Ghatika at the junction of Jyeshtha-Mula is called Abhukta. Daughters, sons, cattle, and servants born in that Abhukta pulse destroy the lineage. || 45 ||</margin>

### Regarding the Results of Jyeshtha

> If the total duration of the Jyeshtha Nakshatra is divided into ten parts: in the first part, it affects the maternal grandmother; in the second, the maternal grandfather. || 46 ||
> In the third, the maternal uncle; if in the fourth, the mother. In the fifth, the child itself is affected; in the sixth, it destroys the paternal clan. || 47 ||
> In the seventh, both families (maternal and paternal); in the eighth, it destroys the lineage. In the ninth, it kills the father-in-law; and in the tenth part, it destroys everything. || 48 ||
> Born in Jyeshtha on a Tuesday, she takes the life of the husband's elder brother. Born in Mula on a Sunday, she takes the life of the father-in-law. || 49 ||
> Born in the first quarter of Jyeshtha, one quickly kills the elder brother; in the second quarter, the younger brother. In the third quarter, one kills the father; and born in the fourth quarter, the person themselves meets death. || 50 ||

# Chapter 6: Results of the Years of Life

Now, the results for one born under the **Jyeshtha** <note>The 18th lunar mansion, associated with the star Antares</note> nakshatra are described according to its specific divisions. The total duration of the Jyeshtha nakshatra <note>The total time the moon spends in this constellation</note> should be divided into ten equal parts. Thus, ten equal segments of the total duration are formed. Among these:

In the **first tenth**, the person born (male or female) causes the destruction of the maternal grandmother <gloss>the mother's mother</gloss>.
In the **second tenth**, the maternal grandfather <gloss>the mother's father</gloss>.
In the **third tenth**, the maternal uncle <gloss>the mother's brother</gloss>.
If the birth occurs in the **fourth tenth**, the mother of the newborn meets her end.
In the **fifth tenth**, the child who is born dies themselves.
In the **sixth tenth**, the one born becomes a destroyer of the lineage <gloss>one who ends their own family line</gloss>; no further offspring are born from them.
In the **seventh tenth**, the one born destroys both families <gloss>the mother's family and the father's family</gloss>.
In the **eighth tenth**, they cause the destruction of the clan <gloss>their own immediate family line</gloss>.
In the **ninth tenth**, the one born strikes down their father-in-law.
In the **tenth tenth**, the one being born destroys everything <gloss>all their worldly and practical affairs entirely</gloss>.

As stated by the Lord Bharadvaja:
> In the first part of Jyeshtha, one strikes the maternal grandmother; in the second, the maternal grandfather. In the third, one strikes the maternal uncle; in the fourth, the mother.
> One strikes oneself in the fifth; in the sixth, the destruction of the lineage occurs. In the seventh, there is destruction of the family; in the eighth, the elder sibling.
> In the ninth, one strikes the father-in-law; and in the tenth, everything.

The results mentioned here should be understood to apply to the birth of both sons and daughters. Furthermore, regarding the combination with Tuesday: if a girl is born in **Jyeshtha** <gloss>when the Jyeshtha nakshatra falls on a Tuesday</gloss>, she may take away (cause the death of) her elder brother. Similarly, if a girl is born in **Mula** <gloss>born in the Mula nakshatra combined with a Sunday</gloss>, she may take away her father-in-law. Here, "elder brother" should also be understood to include the husband's elder brother.

> "A girl born in Mula destroys the father-in-law; one born in Ashlesha <note>original: 'Vyala'</note> destroys the mother-in-law.
> One born in Jyeshtha <note>original: 'Aindri'</note> destroys the husband's elder brother; one born in Vishakha <note>original: 'Dvidaivata'</note> destroys the husband's younger brother." — Thus says the Sage Narada.

Now, the results for one born according to the quarters <term>Charana: the four quarters or 'padas' of a nakshatra</term> of Jyeshtha. The duration of Jyeshtha <note>the total time of the star's influence</note> is divided by four to create four quarters. Among these:
In the **first quarter**, the one born strikes down the elder brother <gloss>their own elder brother, very quickly</gloss>.
If birth occurs in the **second quarter**, they strike the younger one <gloss>the one born after them</gloss>.
One born in the **third quarter** strikes down their own father.
In the **fourth quarter**, the one born meets death themselves <gloss>they die</gloss>. || 46-50 ||

-> (The following section repeats the above Sanskrit rules in Hindi for the reader's convenience) <-

Divide the total duration of Jyeshtha into ten parts. If born in the first part, the maternal grandmother <note>Nani</note>; in the second, the maternal grandfather <note>Nana</note>; in the third, the maternal uncle <note>Mama</note>; in the fourth, the mother; in the fifth, oneself; in the sixth, the lineage is destroyed. The seventh part destroys both families. The eighth destroys the clan. The ninth part destroys the father-in-law, and the tenth part destroys everything. || 46-48 ||

A girl born in the combination of Jyeshtha nakshatra and Tuesday destroys her elder brother. A girl born in the combination of Mula nakshatra and Sunday destroys her father-in-law. || 49 ||

One born in the first quarter of Jyeshtha destroys the elder brother. If born in the second quarter, they destroy the younger brother. Born in the third quarter, they destroy the father, and born in the fourth quarter, the newborn dies themselves. || 50 ||

# Chapter 6: On the Results of Inauspicious Birth Timings, etc.

<page-num>266</page-num>

The "Mother-Ganda" <note>original: *matri-ganda*; a dangerous astrological period for the mother</note> means that one born in the third quarter <note>original: *charana*; a quarter or 'foot' of a lunar mansion</note> causes the death of the mother. In the fourth quarter, it is "Father-Ganda," meaning the father meets his end. As it has been said:

->In the first quarter of Ashlesha <note>original: *sarpa*, referring to the serpent deity of the Ashlesha constellation</note>, there is kingship; in the second, loss of wealth.<-
->In the third, the destruction of the mother; and in the fourth, the death of the father. // 56 //<-

In the constellation of Ashlesha, there is no *Ganda* <note>inauspiciousness</note> in the first quarter. The second quarter is the *Ganda* of wealth. The third quarter is the *Ganda* of the mother, and the fourth quarter is the *Ganda* of the father (the fourth is harmful for the father, the third for the mother, the second for wealth, and the first is auspicious). // 56 //

->Now, the transition points <note>original: *gandanta*</note> for Ashlesha, Magha, Jyeshtha, Mula, Revati, and Ashwini are described:<-

->In the first quarters of Mula, Magha, and Ashwini, it affects the father; in the fourth quarters of Revati <note>original: *paushna*</note>, Jyeshtha <note>original: *aindra*</note>, and Ashlesha <note>original: *phanina*</note>,<-
->It causes the destruction of the mother, the father, or one's own body, respectively, whether born at night, during the day, or during the two twilights.<-
->One born by day kills the father; one born at night, the mother;<-
->And one born during the two twilights kills themselves. In *Ganda*, there is no reversal of these effects. // 58 //<-

One born in the first quarter of the constellations Mula, Magha, or Ashwini causes the destruction of the father. In the fourth quarters of Revati, Jyeshtha, and Ashlesha, they cause the destruction of the mother, father, and their own body respectively. Specifically, one born in the fourth quarter of Revati causes the mother's destruction; in the fourth of Jyeshtha, the father's; and in the fourth of Ashlesha, their own. Here, it is not just the quarter, but also the timing: **at night, during the day, and during the two twilights.** The sense is that birth in the fourth quarter of Revati at night, Jyeshtha during the day, and Ashlesha during the morning or evening twilights causes the destruction of the mother, father, and self, respectively. // 57 //

The previous statement is confirmed by this verse. In these *Ganda* points, there is no reversal of the stated results; the results will certainly come to pass. To remove these defects, a peace ritual <note>original: *shanti*</note> must be performed. As the scripture says: "...auspiciousness comes through peace rituals." // 58 //

In the first quarters of Mula, Magha, and Ashwini, suffering is predicted for the father. In the fourth quarters of Revati, Jyeshtha, and Ashlesha, harm is predicted for the father <note>The Hindi commentary here clarifies the specific timings</note>. Birth in the 4th quarter of Revati at night, 4th of Jyeshtha during the day, and 4th of Ashlesha during the twilights causes the destruction of mother, father, and self respectively. // 57 //

A child born in the said *Ganda* during the day destroys the father; at night, the mother; and during both twilights, themselves. There is no reversal in the *Ganda* defect. // 58 //

->If birth occurs at the end of a constellation at night, or at the beginning during the day,<-
->Or at the junction of constellations during the twilights, this is the definition of *Ganda*. // 59 //<-

If birth occurs at the end of a constellation at night, or at the beginning of a constellation during the day, or at the junction of constellations (the transitions between Cancer/Leo, Scorpio/Sagittarius, or Pisces/Aries) during the twilights, this is the definition of *Ganda*, meaning it yields the previously mentioned inauspicious results. // 59 //

At the end of a constellation at night, at the beginning during the day, or at the junction of constellations during both twilights—this is also a sign of *Ganda*, meaning inauspicious results are predicted here as well. // 59 //

->Born in Purva Ashadha with Sagittarius rising, one destroys the father.<-
->In Pushya with Cancer rising, one becomes the cause of the father's death. // 60 //<-
->In Purva Ashadha and Pushya, a child may kill the father, mother, son,<-
->Or maternal uncle, respectively, based on the three-month portions. // 61 //<-
->If in the first quarter of the star Uttara Phalguni,<-
->Or if in both middle quarters of the Pushya <note>original: *tishya*</note> constellation... // 62 //<-

> In the third quarter of Chitra, in the first half of Bharani <note>original: "Yamabhasya," the star of Yama</note>, in the third part of Hasta <note>original: "Arkatara," the star of the Sun</note>, and in the fourth part of the final constellation <note>Revati</note>; if a boy is born, he destroys the father, and if a girl is born, she destroys the mother. || 63 ||

A child born in the constellation of Purva Ashadha when Sagittarius is the rising sign <term>Lagna|The zodiac sign ascending on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</term> becomes the destroyer of the father. In that situation, the father of the one born dies. Similarly, one born in the constellation of Pushya when Cancer is the rising sign becomes the cause of the father's death. || 60 ||

In the constellations of Purva Ashadha and Pushya, according to the sequence of the first parts (quarters): a child born destroys the father, mother, the child itself, and the maternal uncle respectively. A boy born in the first quarter of Purva Ashadha or Pushya becomes the destroyer of the father. In the second quarter, he destroys the mother. In the third quarter, the child himself is destroyed, and in the fourth quarter, he destroys the maternal uncle. || 61 ||

In the first quarter of Uttara Phalguni; in the two middle quarters (the second and third) of the Tishya (Pushya) constellation; in the third quarter of Chitra; in the first half of Bharani; in the third part (third quarter) of Hasta; and in the fourth part (fourth quarter) of the final constellation, Revati—a boy so born destroys the father. If, however, a girl is born there, she destroys the mother. || 62-63 ||

### Regarding the Period of the Junction (Ganda-kala)

> Sixteen years for the beginning of Ashvini <note>original: "Turangadye"</note>; eight years for the beginning of Magha. || 64 ||
> One year in Jyeshtha <note>original: "Shakratara"</note>; four years for Chitra <note>original: "Tvashtra"</note> and Mula. In Ashlesha <note>original: "Sarpe"</note>, two years; and in Revati, one year. || 65 ||
> Two months for the fault of Uttara; three months for the Pushya constellation. In the ninth month, one born in Purva Ashadha takes the father. || 66 ||
> If born in the Hasta constellation, he destroys the father in the twelfth year. A son born in Abhukta Mula <note>the most inauspicious core of the Mula constellation</note> destroys the father instantly. || 67 ||
> If a human born in Abhukta Mula survives, he becomes the enhancer of his lineage, wealthy, or the commander of a great army. || 68 ||

It is explained here how many days or years it takes for the inauspicious results of the "Ganda" <note>junction points between certain zodiac signs and constellations</note> to manifest. These verses are clear in their meaning. To remedy these faults, a "Shanti" <note>propitiatory rite or peace-making ritual</note> must be performed for each. The procedure for these rites should be looked up in the "Shanti Paddhati" <note>Manual of Propitiatory Rites</note>. || 64-68 ||

# Chapter 6: On the Results of the Year, Month, and Other Divisions

If a child is born when the *Moola* <note>The 19th lunar mansion or Nakshatra</note> asterism has not yet ended its influence, and the child survives, they will become the founder of their lineage, wealthy, and the commander of a great army. || 68 ||

### On the Defects of the Lunar Day (Tithi-Dosha)

In the dark fortnight <note>The waning phase of the moon</note>, on the fourteenth lunar day (*Chaturdashi*), if the day is divided into six parts: the first part is auspicious. In the second part, it destroys the father; in the third, the mother. || 69 ||

In the fourth part, it destroys the maternal uncle; in the fifth, it causes the destruction of the brother. If born in the sixth part, it destroys the infant; this is known as the *Ganda* defect <note>A spiritual blemish or "knot" in time believed to cause misfortune</note>. || 70 ||

Regarding those born on the New Moon day (*Amavasya*)—whether they be elephants, horses, cows, buffaloes, or especially humans—they should be abandoned. || 71 ||

For those born during *Sinivali* <note>The New Moon day when a sliver of the moon is still visible</note>, abandonment is always prescribed. Especially for those born during *Kuhu* <note>The New Moon day when the moon is completely invisible</note>, one should perform a pacification ritual (*Shanti*) according to the prescribed rules. Except for humans, the abandonment of all others is ordained. || 72 ||

Now the *Tithi-Ganda* <note>The critical junction point of a lunar day</note> is explained. In the dark fortnight, the duration of the fourteenth lunar day should be divided by six. Birth in the first of these six parts is auspicious; the meaning is that the *Ganda* defect does not occur in that first part. The rest is clear. Regarding those born on the New Moon day—elephants, horses, cows, buffaloes, and especially humans—abandonment should certainly be carried out. This applies if that New Moon is *Sinivali*. Furthermore, for those born on the New Moon known as *Kuhu*, one should perform a pacification ritual according to the established procedures to remove the defect.

The meaning is this: elephants and other animals born during *Sinivali* should be abandoned; those born during *Kuhu* should especially be abandoned. Here, the distinction between *Sinivali* and *Kuhu* is explained: The New Moon on which a small digit of the moon is visible is *Sinivali*; essentially, this is the New Moon joined with the fourteenth day. The New Moon on which the digits of the moon have completely vanished is named *Kuhu*; essentially, this is the "pure" New Moon.

> "The moon seen is *Sinivali*; the moon's digits vanished is *Kuhu*."
<note>original: "सा दृष्टेन्दुः सिनीवाली सा नष्टेन्दुकला कुहूः" — a quote from the Amarakosha, a famous Sanskrit thesaurus.</note>

In that case, if one is unable to perform the abandonment <note>due to emotional attachment</note>, a pacification ritual must be performed to quiet the defect. Since the abandonment of a human being is difficult due to emotional attachment, the best course of action prescribed is the abandonment of all other animal species like elephants, etc., excluding the human species. || 69-72 ||

The first sixth part of the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight is auspicious. The *Ganda* defect of the second part destroys the father; the third part, the mother; birth in the fourth part destroys the maternal uncle; birth in the fifth part destroys the brother. The *Ganda* of the sixth part destroys the child. || 69-70 ||

Misfortune occurs for elephants, horses, cows, buffaloes, and especially humans born on the New Moon. If born on a *Sinivali* New Moon, one should always abandon them; if born on a *Kuhu* New Moon, one should especially abandon them. If there is emotional attachment preventing abandonment, perform a pacification ritual according to the rules. Except for the human form, abandon all others. || 71-72 ||

### On the Defects of Planetary Combinations (Yoga-Dosha)

One born in the father's birth asterism or the father's "action" asterism <note>The 10th Nakshatra from the birth star</note> causes the destruction of the father. || 73 ||

One born in the same sign or ascendant as the birth asterism's portion causes immediate death. One born in the *Musala* or *Mudgara* combinations <note>Specific configurations of planets</note> causes the destruction of auspiciousness. || 74 ||

Birth during *Vishti* <note>An inauspicious period or 'Karana'</note> indicates poverty; during *Gullika* <note>A mathematical point in the sky associated with Saturn's son</note>, it indicates being limb-deficient. On "Empty" days (*Rikta*), they become sixth-rate; during *Yamaghantaka* <note>A specific inauspicious time of day</note>, one becomes lame. || 75 ||
