# Jataka Parijata with Commentary

->A child born under a <term>Nakshatra</term><note>A lunar mansion or star sign in Vedic astrology.</note> afflicted by a planet will be plagued by disease.<-
->If born when a planet has just left a constellation or during a specific ritual <note>original: "Kanchit-kritya"</note>, the son may become an adopted child.<-
->Born in the <term>Vyatipata</term><note>An inauspicious astronomical yoga.</note> yoga, one may have physical disabilities; in <term>Parigha</term>, one meets death.<-
->In <term>Vaidhriti</term>, the child destroys the father; in <term>Vishkambha</term>, he causes loss of wealth.<-
->In <term>Shula</term>, one suffers from colic or sharp pains; in <term>Ganda</term>, one suffers from goiter or glandular swellings.<-

Now, the results of births in specific yogas and junctions are described. A child born in the same Nakshatra as the father's birth star, or in the 10th Nakshatra from it (known as the <term>Karma-kshetra</term>), becomes the destroyer of the father. Likewise, one born in the same <term>Navamsha</term><note>A one-ninth divisional chart used for fine-tuning predictions.</note> or the same rising sign as the father's birth sign brings immediate death to the father. Other points are self-explanatory.

A child born in the father's birth star or the 10th star destroys the father. A child born in the same Navamsha or rising sign as the father's birth sign gives immediate death to the father. Those born in <term>Musala</term> and <term>Mudgara</term> yogas destroy auspiciousness. A child born during <term>Bhadra</term><note>A specific timing in the lunar calendar often avoided for auspicious works.</note> will be poor. One born in <term>Gulika</term><note>A "shadow planet" considered malefic.</note> will have missing limbs. A child born on a <term>Rikta</term><note>The 4th, 9th, or 14th lunar days, considered "empty."</note> day will be impotent. A boy born in <term>Yamaghanta</term> yoga will be lame. A child born in a Nakshatra afflicted by planets remains troubled by disease. Birth during a planet's exit or certain rituals leads to being an adopted son. In <term>Vyatipata</term>, one is disabled. In <term>Parigha</term>, death occurs. Birth in <term>Vaidhriti</term> yoga destroys the father. Birth in <term>Vishkambha</term> destroys wealth. One born in <term>Shula</term> suffers from colic. One born in <term>Ganda</term> suffers from glandular disease.

### On the Results of the Appearance of Teeth

->A child born with teeth already present destroys the family lineage. If teeth appear at the end of the four-month period starting from the second month, it causes the death of the father. If they appear in the sixth month, it causes the death of the child; after that, it is auspicious.<-

Now the results of the child's teething are described. If a child is born with teeth, he destroys the family. From the second month up to the fifth month, the appearance of teeth causes the father's death. Teething in the sixth month causes the death of the child himself. From the seventh month onwards, the appearance of teeth should be declared auspicious. However, there are variations in the results of teething seen elsewhere:

> "If born with teeth in the first month, the child himself perishes. In the following months, he destroys in order: younger brother, sister, mother, and elder brother. From the sixth month onwards, he attains incomparable enjoyment, the father's happiness, physical strength, wealth, and a life of comfort. If born with teeth in the upper jaw, he destroys his father and others."

This is according to the words of the sage Ramacharya. Furthermore:

> From teething in the first month, he himself perishes. In the second, he kills the brother; in the third, the sister. In the fourth, he kills the mother; in the fifth, his own elder brother. In the sixth, he becomes a counselor; in the seventh, he gives happiness to the father. In the eighth, he brings nourishment; in the ninth, he gains wealth. He gains happiness in the tenth or eleventh month. In the twelfth month, the result of teething is the acquisition of wealth. This is according to the words of Chandeshwara.

A child born with teeth destroys the family. Teething from the 2nd to the 5th month destroys the father; in the 6th, it destroys the infant. Teething from the 7th month onwards is auspicious.

->The 18th is known as <term>Samudaya</term>, and the 19th is <term>Adhana</term>.<-

# Chapter 6: On the Results of Doubtful and Other Portents

->The twenty-third lunar mansion is known as the *Vainashika* (Destructive).<-
->The twenty-fifth and following are called the *Jati* (Caste), *Desha* (Country), and *Abhisheka* (Consecration) mansions.<-
->If a person's birth star or others are pierced by malefic planets,<-
->It causes immediate death; if pierced by benefics, they grant auspicious results.<-

Now, certain lunar mansions <term>Nakshatras; the 27 divisions of the sky through which the moon passes</term> are described by other names known as "Stars." The mansion in which one is born is the first, called the *Janma* (Birth) star. The tenth mansion from the birth star is named *Karma* (Action). Sages call the sixteenth *Sanghatika* (Dangerous). The eighteenth is named *Samudaya* (Aggregate). The nineteenth (19) is named *Adhana* (Conception). The twenty-third is named *Jati* (Caste) <note>The Hindi commentary below suggests the 23rd is Vainashika; the Sanskrit text here uses Jati, showing a common variation in astrological schools</note>. The twenty-sixth is called *Desha* (Country), and the twenty-seventh is called *Abhisheka* (Consecration). 

The purpose of this is explained: "If a person's birth star..." etc. For a person born, if the defined stars—Birth star and the others—are "pierced" <term>Viddha; an astrological aspect where planets align on a specific grid</term> by malefic planets <note>original: "papaviyaccharaih"</note> on the *Sapta-Shalaka* <term>A seven-line astrological chart used to calculate obstructions</term>, it brings about death very quickly. If these stars are pierced by benefic planets, they provide auspicious results to the newborn. — 79-81

The name of the birth star is **"Adya"** (First), the tenth is **"Karma,"** the sixteenth is **"Sanghatika,"** the eighteenth is **"Samudaya,"** the nineteenth is **"Adhana,"** and the twenty-third is **"Vainashika."** The twenty-fifth and following are named **"Jati," "Desha,"** and **"Abhisheka."** — 79-80

If one's birth star etc. is pierced by a malefic planet, death occurs immediately; if pierced by a benefic planet, the birth stars give auspicious results. — 81

### Now, the Exception to the Ganda Fault
<note>Ganda-dosha refers to "knots" or inauspicious transition points between lunar mansions and zodiac signs.</note>

->In the months of Vaishakha, Shravana, Magha, and Phalguna, the Ganda is of the Sky.<-
->In Ashadha, Pausha, Margashirsha, and Jyeshtha, it is of the Human world.<-
->In Ashvin, Chaitra, Kartika, and Bhadrapada, it is of the Underworld.<-
->The Ganda fault causes death in the Human world; it does not exist in the Underworld or the Sky.<-
->As soon as a son is born, the father should look upon his face.<-
->By seeing the son's face, he is liberated from his debt to the ancestors.<-

The exception to the previously mentioned *Ganda* faults is now stated. In the four months of Vaishakha, Shravana, Magha, and Phalguna, the *Ganda* is said to be "Sky-born" <note>original: "vyomasambhavam"</note>. In the months of Ashadha, Pausha (called *Pushya* here), Margashirsha (called *Saumya*), and Jyeshtha, the *Ganda* is "Human-born." In the four months of Ashvin (called *Ashvayuj*), Chaitra, Kartika, and Bhadrapada (called *Bhadra*), the *Ganda* is "Underworld-born" <note>original: "bilasambhavam"</note>. 

The meaning is this: For one born in the "Human" months (Jyeshtha, Ashadha, Margashirsha, Pausha), the *Ganda* fault results in death. In the "Underworld" months (Chaitra, Bhadrapada, Ashvin, Kartika) and the "Sky" months (Vaishakha, Shravana, Magha, Phalguna), the *Ganda* fault does not apply. The idea is that the *Ganda* only causes harm in the realm where it originates.

Next, the duty of the father is described. As soon as a boy is born, the father should immediately look at the boy's face. The reason for looking at the son's face is given: that father is liberated from the "Debt to the Ancestors" <term>Pitri-rina; the spiritual obligation to continue the family line and perform rites</term>. According to the etymology of the word *Putra* (Son)—"one who saves from the hell named Put"—he who has no son remains burdened by the ancestors and goes to hell. 

Because of the saying, "There is no path for the sonless, nor is there heaven," it is only through the rise of a son that a father is protected from hell; therefore, one must look at the son's face as soon as he is born. — 83-84

In the months of Vaishakha, Shravana, Magha, and Phalguna, the *Gandanta* <note>A "spiritual knot" or transitional period between certain zodiac signs and lunar mansions, considered inauspicious</note> resides in the heavens. In the months of Ashadha, Pausha, Margashirsha, and Jyeshtha, the *Gandanta* resides in the mortal world. In the months of Ashvina, Chaitra, Kartika, and Bhadrapada, the *Gandanta* resides in the underworld. If the *Gandanta* defect is present in the mortal world, death occurs. If it resides in the underworld or the heavens, there is no defect. || 82-83 ||

Upon the birth of a son, the father should look at his face immediately, because by looking at the face of a son, he is released from the debt to his ancestors. || 84 ||

## Now, the Results of the Lunar Mansions.

> One born in **Ashvini** is highly intelligent, wealthy, humble, wise, famous, and happy.
> In **Bharani**, one is distressed, devoted to others' wives, cruel, ungrateful, but wealthy.
> In **Krittika**, one is energetic, has many children, is like a king, yet without a king's faults, and is wealthy in knowledge.
> In **Rohini**, one knows the weaknesses of others, has a slender body, is enlightened, but devoted to others' wives. || 85 ||
> In **Mrigashira**, one has a gentle mind, is a wanderer, has a squinted gaze, is lustful, and prone to illness.
> In **Ardra**, one is poor, fickle, possesses great strength, and engages in mean-spirited actions.
> In **Punarvasu**, one is a dull soul <note>original: "mudhatma"</note> yet famous for wealth and strength, a poet, and lustful.
> In **Pushya**, one is dear to priests and gods, wealthy, wise, a favorite of kings, and has many kinsmen. || 86 ||
> In **Ashlesha**, one is dull-witted, speaks ungratefully, is angry, and behaves wickedly.
> In **Magha**, one is proud, devoted to meritorious deeds, controlled by his wife, honorable, and wealthy.
> In **Purva Phalguni**, one is fickle, of bad character, yet charitable, firm, and lustful.
> One born in **Uttara Phalguni** is sickly, yet honorable, grateful, and wise. || 87 ||
> In **Hasta**, one is devoted to desire and righteousness, a wise benefactor, and wealthy.
> In **Chitra**, one is devoted to very secret conduct, honorable, and devoted to others' wives.
> In **Svati**, one is a doer of good for gods and priests, a seeker of pleasure, wealthy, but slow-witted.
> One born in **Vishakha** is proud, controlled by his wife, a conqueror of enemies, and very prone to anger. || 88 ||
> In **Anuradha**, one has pleasant speech, is wealthy, enjoys happiness, is worshipful, famous, and powerful.
> In **Jyeshtha**, one is very angry, attached to others' wives, deluded, and unrighteous.
> In **Mula**, one is clever in speech, devoid of auspiciousness, a rogue, ungrateful, yet wealthy.
> One born in **Purva Ashadha** is of erratic character, proud, happy, and of peaceful mind. || 89 ||
> One born in **Uttara Ashadha** is honorable, of peaceful qualities, happy, wealthy, and a scholar.
> In **Shravana**, one is devoted to the service of priests and gods, a kingly person, wealthy, and righteous.
> One born in **Dhanishtha** is hopeful, wealthy, has a thick neck and thighs, and is happy.
> One born in **Shatabhisha** is a knower of time <note>perhaps an astrologer or one who is punctual</note>, peaceful, eats little, and is courageous. || 90 ||
> In **Purva Bhadrapada**, one is bold in speech, a rogue, afflicted by fear, yet gentle.
> A human born in **Uttara Bhadrapada** has gentle qualities, is charitable, wealthy, and a scholar.
> In **Revati**, one has a body with prominent marks, is lustful, beautiful,
> A minister, endowed with sons, wife, and friends, stable, and devoted to prosperity. || 91 ||

Now, the results of the lunar mansions are stated in seven verses of simple meaning. Among them, the result should be inferred based on the lunar mansion of the day of birth—that is, the mansion in which the moon resides at birth. || 85-91 ||

If a child is born in the **Ashvini** mansion, they will be endowed with great intelligence, wealth, humility, knowledge, and fame, and will be happy. If born in the **Bharani** mansion, they will be distressed, a pursuer of others' wives, cruel, ungrateful, and wealthy.

If birth occurs in **Kruttika** <note>The Pleiades</note>, one will be energetic, like a lord, wise, and wealthy in knowledge. If birth is in **Rohini** <note>Aldebaran</note>, one will be a seeker of others' faults, thin-bodied, wise, and prone to pursuing others' wives. || 85 ||

Born in **Mrigashira** <note>Orion's head</note>, one has a gentle mind, is a traveler, possesses a crooked gaze, is lustful, and sickly. Now, the results of the *Yogas* are explained in four verses with clear meanings. First, what is called a *Yoga*? It is explained thus: The combined longitudes of the Sun and the Moon, when divided by 800 minutes <note>The span of one Nakshatra or Yoga</note>, give the resulting *Yogas*. As stated by Ganesha <note>Referring to the astronomer Ganesha Daivajna</note>: "Add the longitudes of the Sun and Moon, divide by 800, and the quotient indicates the elapsed Yogas." These Yogas, for the purpose of predicting results, are:

| | | |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |

These are known by these twenty-seven names. The result of the specific *Yoga* present at the time of birth should be understood and declared. || 98-101 ||

If birth occurs in **Vishkambha** Yoga, one will be a conqueror of enemies, wealthy, and possess cattle. A child born in **Priti** Yoga remains under the influence of another's wife. # With the Commentary on Jataka Parijata

<page-num>308</page-num>

If one is born in the **Shula** <note>Spear</note> Yoga, they will be under the influence of anger and prone to quarreling. Born in **Ganda** <note>Obstacle</note> Yoga, they will be of bad conduct. A child born in **Vriddhi** <note>Growth</note> Yoga will speak like a scholar. One born in **Dhruva** <note>Constant</note> Yoga will be exceptionally wealthy. Born in **Vyaghata** <note>Striking</note> Yoga, they will be a killer. One born in **Harshana** <note>Joyful</note> Yoga will be wise and possess great fame. Born in **Vajra** <note>Thunderbolt</note> Yoga, they will be wealthy and lustful. Born in **Siddhi** <note>Success</note> Yoga, they will be a refuge for all and like a lord. A child of **Vyatipata** <note>Calamity</note> will be deceitful. || 99 ||

One born in **Variyan** <note>Excellent</note> Yoga will have wicked desires. One with **Parigha** <note>Iron Bar</note> Yoga will be hateful yet wealthy. A child born in **Shiva** <note>Auspicious</note> Yoga will be a knower of scriptures, wealthy, peaceful, and dear to the king. A child born in **Siddha** <note>Perfected</note> Yoga will be devoted to dharma <note>righteousness/duty</note> and the performance of sacrifices. One born in **Sadhya** <note>Achievable</note> Yoga will have virtuous conduct. A child of **Shubha** <note>Auspicious</note> Yoga will have restless limbs, be wealthy, lustful, and of a phlegmatic <term>Kapha: one of the three bodily humors in Ayurveda</term> constitution. || 100 ||

A child born in **Shukla** <note>Bright/White</note> Yoga will be devoted to dharma, a clever speaker, irritable, restless, and a scholar. One born in **Brahma** Yoga will be proud, possess great hidden wealth, be charitable, and be the best among the wise. A child born in **Aindra** Yoga will be a benefactor to all, all-knowing, intelligent, and wealthy. One born in **Vaidhriti** Yoga will be deceitful, a slanderer of others, powerful, charitable, and wealthy. || 101 ||

->**Now, the Results of the Karanas.**<-

> One born in **Bava** Karana is childlike in actions and majestic. In **Balava**, one has a modest character and dress, and is honored by the king. Possessing elephants and horses in **Kaulava**, one performs beautiful deeds. In **Taitila**, one speaks soft and clever words and is of virtuous character. || 102 ||
> Born in **Gara** Karana, one is without enemies and majestic. In **Vanija**, one is an expert speaker but restless for the wives of others. Born in **Vishti**, one is an enemy to all, a performer of sinful deeds, a slanderer, yet honored by his own people and independent. || 103 ||
> Born in **Shakuni**, one knows the times, is steadily happy, but causes harm. In **Chatushpada**, one is all-knowing, possesses refined intelligence, fame, and wealth. In **Naga**, one is energetic, very wealthy, strong, and talkative. In **Kimstughna**, one does the work of others, has a fickle mind, and is fond of humor. || 104 ||

Now, the results of the *Karanas* <term>Karana: half of a lunar day or Tithi</term> are stated in three verses. What is called a *Karana*? It is said: a *Karana* is half of a *Tithi* <note>lunar day</note>, or there are two *Karanas* in one *Tithi*. This is calculated by dividing the longitudinal difference between the Sun and the Moon by six. Among them, **Bava, Balava, Kaulava, Taitila, Gara, Vanija,** and **Vishti** are the seven "movable" *Karanas*. Likewise, **Shakuni, Chatushpada, Naga,** and **Kimstughna** are known as the four "fixed" *Karanas*.

> <note>original Latin/Sanskrit quote from Bhaskara regarding the calculation of Tithis and Karanas</note> "Subtract the Sun from the Moon, multiply by... the results are the Tithis and Karanas..."

According to the statement of Bhaskara: in the dark fortnight <note>waning moon</note>, the second half of the 14th day is **Shakuni**. The first half of the New Moon (*Amavasya*) is **Chatushpada**, and the second half is **Naga**. The first half of the 1st day of the bright fortnight <note>waxing moon</note> is **Kimstughna**. Therefore, the difference between the Sun and Moon divided by six, adjusted by the sequence, gives the measure of the *Karanas* starting from **Bava**. Because from the second half of the 1st day, **Bava** Karana begins. The results mentioned for the *Karana* at the time of birth should be declared for the subject. The verses 102-104 are clear in their meaning.

A child born in **Bava** Karana performs actions like a child and is majestic. In **Balava** Karana, the child is of modest character and honored by the king. One with **Kaulava** Karana possesses elephants and horses and has a beautiful character. One with **Taitila** Karana speaks with gentle cleverness and is a virtuous soul. || 102 ||

A child born of **Gara** Karana is without enemies and majestic. One born in **Vanija** Karana is a speaker, modest, and restless. A child born in **Vishti** Karana is an opponent of all, a performer of sins, a slanderer, honored by all people, and independent. || 103 ||

# Chapter 6: On the Results of the Year, Month, and Other Divisions

A child born in the **Shakuni** <term>Karana: the first of the four fixed lunar half-days</term> will be a knower of time (astrologer), possess stable happiness, but may be a "storehouse of misfortunes" <note>original: "अनिष्टका भण्डार" - likely implying they attract or manage difficulties</note>. A child born in the **Chatushpada** Karana will be all-knowing and possess good intellect, fame, and wealth. A person born in the **Naga** Karana will be radiant, wealthy, exceptionally strong, and eloquent. A person born in the **Kinstughna** Karana is one who performs work for others, possesses a restless intellect, and is fond of laughter. || 104 ||

---

### Now, the Results of the Ascendant (Lagna).

> One born when **Aries** is rising is a hater of kinsmen, a wanderer, thin-bodied, angry, fond of disputes, proud, has weak knees, unstable wealth, and is brave. One born in the **Taurus** ascendant possesses cattle, is devoted to worshipping gods, teachers, and priests, has few children, a peaceful mind, is engaged in the pursuit of knowledge, a wanderer, handsome, and lustful. || 105 ||
>
> One born when **Gemini** is rising is an enjoyer, devoted to kinsmen, very compassionate, fortunate, virtuous, a knower of reality <note>original: "तत्त्वविद्" - a philosopher or one who understands the true nature of the universe</note>, of a yogic soul, dear to good people, very handsome, and sickly. One born in the **Cancer** ascendant is an enjoyer of sweets, possesses fine clothes and ornaments, has elegant speech, a cunning mind, is righteous, has a stout body, and enjoys staying in the houses of others. || 106 ||
>
> One born in the **Leo** ascendant has few children, a contented mind, is a harmer <note>original: "हिंसकः" - can mean predatory or aggressive</note>, brave, subdues kings, conquers enemies, is lustful, and goes to foreign lands. One born in the **Virgo** ascendant is skilled in actions, fortunate, wise, a scholar, intelligent, a connoisseur of feminine charms, dear to kinsmen, and of a pure (Sattvic) nature. || 107 ||
>
> One born in the **Libra** ascendant has a beautiful face and eyes, is honored by kings, is a scholar, restless with desire and passion, possesses wealth and lands, has sparse teeth, a peaceful mind, is prone to sorrow, has a fickle mind, and is very timid. || 108 ||
>
> One born in the **Scorpio** ascendant is foolish, has cruel eyes, is very restless, proud, long-lived, wealthy, a scholar, a hater of good people, and fond of disputes. One born in the **Sagittarius** ascendant is wise, the best of his lineage, fortunate, famous, and wealthy. One born in **Capricorn** is fond of women, deceitful, and speaks piteously. || 109 ||
>
> One born in **Aquarius** is deceitful at heart, fond of playing and dallying with the wives of others, of a miserly nature, and wealthy. When **Pisces** is rising, one has little sexual desire, is favorable to beloved people, possesses great radiance and strength, and has much grain, wealth, and scholarship. || 110 ||

---

Now the results of the <term>Lagna: the Ascendant; the specific zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</term> are stated. First, what is called "Lagna"? It is said: "The rising of the signs is the Lagna; those signs are Aries, Taurus, etc." Based on the authority of Amarasimha <note>A famous 4th-century Sanskrit grammarian and lexicographer</note>, at any given time, the specific area of the zodiac (the ecliptic) that is rising (connected to the eastern horizon) is the Lagna for that moment, because the entire circle of signs rotates over a day and night. The method for calculating that Lagna should be seen in the appendix at the end of the book. Whatever Lagna is present at the time of birth, its stated results should be inferred for the person born. The verses themselves are clear in meaning, so there is no need for further elaboration. || 105-110 ||

The person whose birth is in the **Aries** ascendant is a hater of kinsmen, a wanderer, has a weak body, is angry, fond of disputes, proud, has weak knees, unstable wealth, and is powerful. The person whose birth is in the **Taurus** ascendant possesses cattle (wealth in livestock), is intent on worshipping gods, teachers, and priests, has few children, a peaceful mind, is engaged in the debate of knowledge, a wanderer, beautiful, and lustful. || 105 ||

The person whose birth is in the **Gemini** ascendant is an enjoyer, devoted to kinsmen, very compassionate, fortunate, virtuous, a knower of the elements, of a yogic soul, dear to good people, very beautiful, and sickly. The person whose birth is in the **Cancer** ascendant is an eater of sweets, possesses clothes and jewelry, has beautiful speech, a deceptive intellect, is righteous, has a heavy body, and finds pleasure in the homes of others. || 106 ||

# With the Commentary on Jataka Parijata

<header>With the Commentary on Jataka Parijata—</header>

A person born in the **Leo** <term>Lagna</term><note>The ascending sign or zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the time of birth.</note> will have few children, be content, prone to violence, brave, one who influences kings, a conqueror of enemies, lustful, and a traveler to foreign lands. A person born in the **Virgo** Lagna will be skilled in actions, wealthy, a scholar, intelligent, a lover of feminine pleasures, dear to his kinsmen, and of a virtuous <note>original: "Sattvic"</note> nature. || 107 ||

A person born in the **Libra** Lagna will have a charming face and eyes, be honored by kings, learned, fickle in matters of desire, a master of women, wealth, and lands, have gaps between the teeth, be handsome, of a calm mind, occasionally sorrowful, of a restless nature, and very timid. || 108 ||

A person born in the **Scorpio** Lagna will be foolish, have cruel eyes, be especially restless, proud, long-lived, wealthy, learned, an enemy to good people, and fond of disputes. A person born in the **Sagittarius** Lagna will be intelligent, famous, and wealthy. If born in the **Capricorn** Lagna, one is fickle in the company of women, deceitful, and speaks mean words. || 109 ||

A person born in the **Aquarius** Lagna is inwardly deceitful, eager to dally with the wives of others, of a miserly disposition, and wealthy. A person born in the **Pisces** Lagna has a small appetite, is favorable to his loved ones, possesses great splendor, strength, wealth, and grain, and is a scholar. || 110 ||

### Regarding the Results of the Hora.

> If born in the **Sun's** <term>Hora</term><note>A division of a zodiac sign into two halves of 15 degrees each.</note> in an odd-numbered sign: one is cruel, lustful, wealthy, and honored by kings.
> If it be the **Moon's** Hora in an odd sign: one is eloquent, charitable, has a beautiful body, is compassionate, but also a paramour <note>original: "Jar"</note> and of a feminine nature. || 111 ||
> Born in the **Sun's** Hora in an even sign: one is a respected minister, grateful, fickle, and very timid.
> Born in the **Moon's** Hora in an even sign: one is bold in speech, lazy, and devoted to a virtuous wife. || 112 ||

The results of the Hora are stated in these two verses, the meaning of which is clear. Half of a sign is a Hora; thus, there are two Horas in every sign. In the **odd** signs (1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11), the first 15 degrees belong to the Sun, and the next to the Moon. In the **even** signs (2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12), the first belongs to the Moon and the next to the Sun. One should analyze and declare the results according to these rules at the time of birth. || 111-112 ||

If birth occurs in the Sun's Hora in an odd sign, the person is cruel, lustful, wealthy, and honored by kings; if in the Moon's Hora in an odd sign, the person is eloquent, a donor, has a beautiful body, is compassionate, a lecher, and has feminine traits. || 111 ||

If birth occurs in the Sun's Hora in an even sign, the person is a minister, grateful, fickle, and very fearful. If it is the Moon's Hora in an even sign, the child born therein is skilled in speaking, lazy, and devoted to a chaste wife. || 112 ||

### Regarding the Results of the Drekkana.

> The <term>Drekkanas</term><note>A subdivision of a zodiac sign into three equal parts of 10 degrees each, also known as a decan.</note> at the end of Leo, Aries, Aquarius, Scorpio, and Capricorn; the beginning of Pisces, Scorpio, Leo, and Libra; and those situated in the middle of Cancer and Scorpio, are called **Cruel** by the wise. || 113 ||
> The Drekkanas in the beginning of Cancer and Pisces; the middle of Pisces and Virgo; and the final third of Taurus and Gemini, are the six **Water-dwelling** Drekkanas. || 114 ||
> The first parts of Aries, Taurus, Aquarius, and Capricorn; the first parts of Libra and Gemini; and the final parts of Sagittarius, Virgo, and Aquarius—these Drekkanas are known as **Gentle**. || 115 ||
> The final Drekkanas of Capricorn, Aries, and Cancer; the first parts of Taurus and Sagittarius; and the middle parts of Gemini and Leo—these are called **Mixed**. || 116 ||
> One born in a **Cruel** Drekkana is wicked-minded, a wanderer, a performer of sinful deeds, and a slanderer.
> One born in a **Water** Drekkana is a donor, an enjoyer of life, compassionate, and gains wealth through agriculture and water, but lacks character.
> One born in a **Gentle** Drekkana is happy, wealthy, has children, is handsome, and compassionate.
> One born in a **Mixed** Drekkana has bad character, is devoted to others' wives, has cruel eyes, and a restless soul. || 117 ||

Now, wishing to describe the results of the <term>Drekkanas</term><note>A Drekkana is a "decanate" or a 10-degree division of a zodiac sign. The first Drekkanas of Leo, Aries, Aquarius, Scorpio, and Capricorn; the third Drekkanas of Pisces, Scorpio, Leo, and Libra; and the second (middle) Drekkanas of Cancer and Scorpio—these eleven are known as the **Cruel** (<term>Krura</term>) Drekkanas; so say many wise men. The first Drekkanas of Cancer and Pisces; the second Drekkanas of Pisces and Virgo; and the third parts (Drekkanas) of Taurus and Gemini—these six are called the **Water-dwelling** (<term>Toyachara</term>) Drekkanas by the learned. The second Drekkanas of Aries, Sagittarius, Taurus, Aquarius, and Capricorn; the first parts of Libra, Virgo, and Gemini; and the third Drekkanas of Sagittarius, Virgo, and Aquarius—these eleven arise as the **Gentle** (<term>Saumya</term>) Drekkanas. The third Drekkanas of Capricorn, Aries, and Cancer; the first Drekkanas of Taurus and Sagittarius; and the second Drekkanas of Gemini, Libra, and Leo—these eight are called the **Mixed** (<term>Vimishra</term>) Drekkanas; so the wise agree. The results of being born in these Drekkanas are now stated. The meaning of "born in a Cruel Drekkana" is clear. One should state the results based on whichever Drekkana is rising at the time of birth. || 113-117 ||

## Now, the Results of the Navamsa.
<note>The Navamsa is the 1/9th division of a sign, considered the most important divisional chart in Vedic astrology for determining the true strength and fruit of a planet.</note>

**Born in the Sun's portion, one is wicked-souled, yet strong and wealthy with sons, having yellowish eyes and a lustful nature.**
**In the Moon's portion, one is a seeker of pleasure, devoted to others' wives, a scholar, and rich in cattle.**
**In Mars's portion, one performs cruel deeds, is fickle-minded, a wanderer, suffers from bile-related illnesses, and is greedy.**
**In Mercury's portion, one is generous, prone to illness, has a graceful body, is highly renowned for learning, and is famous.** || 118 ||

**If in Jupiter's portion, one has hair and a body like gold, is excellent, wise, and handsome;**
**A counselor with the speech of a scholar, a cheerful face, and a favorite of the king of kings.**
**In Venus's portion, one is devoted to the wives of others, generous, happy, and a scholar.**
**In Saturn's portion, one has a sinful mind, is impoverished, has large teeth, and is sickly.** || 119 ||

Now, in these two verses, the results of the planets' <term>Navamsas</term> are described. One should understand that the result depends on which planet's <term>Navamsa</term> the rising sign <note>the Ascendant</note> falls into at birth. The meaning of these verses is straightforward. || 118-119 ||

A person born in the <term>Navamsa</term> of the Sun is a wicked soul, but powerful, blessed with sons and wealth, possessing yellow eyes and a passionate nature. One born in the Moon's <term>Navamsa</term> is expert in enjoyment, dallies with the wives of others, is a scholar, and is full of cattle and wealth. One born in the <term>Navamsa</term> of Mars performs cruel deeds, has a restless intellect, is a traveler, suffers from <term>Pitta</term><note>The "fire" humor in Ayurvedic medicine, often manifesting as acidity or inflammation.</note> diseases, and is greedy. One born in Mercury's <term>Navamsa</term> is charitable, sickly, has a delicate body, is particularly famous, a scholar, and successful. || 118 ||

One born in Jupiter's <term>Navamsa</term> has hair and a body resembling gold, is superior, highly intelligent, handsome, a minister, speaks like a scholar, has a pleasant face, and is beloved by great kings. A person born in Venus's <term>Navamsa</term> goes after others' wives, is charitable, happy, and a scholar. One born in Saturn's <term>Navamsa</term> has a sinful intellect, is poor, has thick teeth, and is prone to disease. || 119 ||

## Now, the Results of the Dvadasamsa.
<note>The Dvadasamsa is the 1/12th division of a sign, representing 2 degrees and 30 minutes each.</note>

**Born in the Aries portion, one is a wicked soul, a thief, and attached to sinful conduct.**
**In the Taurus portion, one is wealthy through a woman's riches but sickly. In the Gemini portion, one is a gambler but of good character.** || 120 ||

**In the Cancer portion, one has wicked conduct but is an ascetic. In the Leo portion, one is engaged in royal service and is very brave.**
**In the Virgo portion, one is a gambler and devoted to women. In the Libra portion, one is a merchant and very wealthy.** || 121 ||

**In the Scorpio portion, one has a taste for wealth and is a leader of rogues. In the Sagittarius portion, one is a devotee of ancestors, priests, and gods.**
**Born in the Capricorn portion, one is a lord of grain and has servants. In Aquarius, one is wicked. In Pisces, one is wealthy and a scholar.** || 122 ||

Now, the results of the <term>Dvadasamsas</term> are told in three verses. The result should be predicted for the person based on which sign's <term>Dvadasamsa</term> is in the birth ascendant. The verses are clear in their meaning. || 120-122 ||

A person born in the <term>Dvadasamsa</term> of Aries is a wicked soul, a thief, and intent on sinful behavior. A person born in the <term>Dvadasamsa</term> of Taurus is wealthy through his wife's money and is sickly. A man born in the <term>Dvadasamsa</term> of Gemini is a gambler and of good character. || 120 ||

One with the Cancer <term>Dvadasamsa</term> has wicked conduct and is an ascetic. One with the Leo <term>Dvadasamsa</term> is devoted to royal duties and is of good character. A child born in the Virgo <term>Dvadasamsa</term> is a gambler and absorbed in women. A child born in the Libra <term>Dvadasamsa</term> is a merchant and wealthy. || 121 ||

<header>Chapter 9: Results of the Slow-Moving Planets and Others</header>

One born in the Twelfth-part <note>original: "Dvadasamsa," a 2.5-degree division of a zodiac sign</note> of Scorpio is one who desires to kill and is a leader of cunning thieves. If born in the Twelfth-part of Sagittarius, they are a devotee of fathers, gods, and Brahmins. If born in the Twelfth-part of Capricorn, they possess grain and have servants. ### Now, the Results of the Thirty-part (Trimsamsa).

> In the Thirty-part <note>original: "Trimsamsa," a 1-degree division used to determine character</note> of Mars, one is fickle, harsh-spoken, and cruel-minded. In Saturn’s, one is intent on wandering and has a dull mind. In Jupiter’s, one is wealthy. In Mercury’s, one is devoted to gurus and gods, dear to the virtuous, and possesses kinsmen. In Venus’s, one is lustful, has a beautiful body, and is happy. || 123 ||

Now the results of the Thirty-part are described. At the time of birth, the result associated with whichever planet’s Thirty-part the Ascendant falls into should be declared for the native. The verse is clear in its meaning. The method for knowing the Hour (Hora), Decan (Dreshkana), Ninth-part (Navamsa), Twelfth-part (Dvadasamsa), and Thirty-part (Trimsamsa) has already been explained in the previous description of the Ten-fold Divisions (Dashavarga). || 123 ||

If the birth is in the Thirty-part of Mars, the person is fickle, speaks harsh words, and is cruel-minded. In Saturn’s Thirty-part, they are a wanderer and dull-witted. In Jupiter’s Thirty-part, they are wealthy. In Mercury’s Thirty-part, they are engaged in devotion to gurus and gods, liked by the holy, and have many relatives. If born in Venus’s Thirty-part, they are lustful, have a beautiful body, and are happy. || 123 ||

### Now, the Results of the Time-periods (Vela).

> One born in the *Sattva* <note>The quality of purity/goodness</note> period is eloquent, follows traditional conduct and religion, is an ascetic, always enthusiastic, pure, charitable, majestic, learned, handsome, truthful, and free from enemies. || 124 ||
> One born in the *Rajas* <note>The quality of passion/activity</note> period is happy, wealthy, famous, handsome, and strong; they conquer enemies but are lustful and do not care for their kinsmen. || 125 ||
> One born in the *Tamas* <note>The quality of darkness/ignorance</note> period covets others' wealth and wives, lacks happiness, is a master of deceit, opposes relatives, priests, and gurus, and has a fickle mind. || 125 ||
> Darkness (*Tamas*), Purity (*Sattva*), and Passion (*Rajas*)—these periods occur in sequence for the days starting with Sunday, divided by half-watches <note>original: "ardha-yama," a period of about 1.5 hours</note>. || 126 ||

Now the results of the Time-periods (Vela) are described. Here, what is called a "Vela" is explained. Starting from Sunday and the other days of the week, in sequences of half-watches (half-prahara), the periods of *Tamas*, *Sattva*, and *Rajas* occur. Every day there are sixteen such periods. On Sunday, starting with *Tamas*, the sixteen follow as *Tamas*, *Sattva*, *Rajas*, *Tamas*, *Sattva*, *Rajas*, and so on. On Monday, the sixteen follow as *Sattva*, *Rajas*, *Tamas*, *Sattva* in order. Thus, it should be known for every day in the stated order. Each segment is half a watch; thus, in eight watches (24 hours), there are sixteen segments. As shown in the chart:

<header>From the Jataka Parijata with Commentary</header>

One born during the **Sattva** <note>The quality of purity, light, and harmony</note> period is eloquent, well-behaved, righteous, ascetic, constantly enthusiastic, pure, charitable, radiant, learned, virtuous, truthful, and without enemies.

One born during the **Rajas** <note>The quality of passion, activity, and movement</note> period becomes wealthy, happy, famous, handsome, strong, a conqueror of enemies, possessed of a passionate intellect, but may lack family and friends. One born during the **Tamas** <note>The quality of darkness, inertia, and ignorance</note> period seizes others' wealth and wives, is devoid of happiness, a leader of the wicked, an opponent of kinsmen, priests, and teachers, and possesses a fickle mind. || 125 ||

Starting from Sunday, the periods of Tamas, Sattva, Rajas, Tamas, Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas prevail in sequence, each lasting for half a *Prahar* <note>A Prahar is approximately 3 hours; half a Prahar is about 90 minutes</note>. || 126 ||

### Now, the Results of the Planetary Hours (Kala Hora).

> Jupiter, Mars, Sun, Venus, Mercury, Moon, and Saturn;
> Starting from the day-lord, the hours proceed, and at night from the fifth day-lord. || 127 ||
> Distress and toil; wealth; sorrow and disease; knowledge and money; all prosperity and lordship;
> Marital health; and loss of wealth—these are the results of being born in the hours of the Sun and the others respectively. || 128 ||
> The results arising from the Sun’s son (Saturn) and others, based on the year, the solstice, and the beginning of the seasons,
> As well as those produced by the divisions of hours, are proclaimed by the grace of the Sun and the other chief deities. || 129 ||

Now, wishing to explain the results of the *Kala Horas* <term>Kala Hora: An astrological system where each hour of the day is ruled by a specific planet</term>, the hours themselves are first described, followed by their results. In one full day and night consisting of sixty *Ghatis* <note>24 hours</note>, there are twenty-four *Kala Horas*. Twelve occur during the day and twelve at night. Each segment lasts two and a half *Ghatis* <note>60 minutes</note>. As stated by the sage Vashistha:

> "The lords of the hours are said to begin from the lord of the day in sequence.
> Every two and a half measures of time, the lord is the sixth one thereafter, repeatedly."

And as stated by Ramacharya:

> "From the day-lord, the half-Ghatis are divided... the lords of the hours follow the sequence of the seventh from the day-lord." <note>original: "वारादर्धघटिका..." - this refers to the mathematical calculation of planetary sequences</note>

By this rule, starting from the day-lord, every sixth planet becomes the lord of the next hour. For example, on Thursday, the first hour belongs to Jupiter; the second belongs to Mars (the sixth from Jupiter); the third belongs to the Sun (the sixth from Mars), and so on as stated in the verse. Similarly, at night, it begins from the fifth planet from the day-lord. For instance, on Sunday night, the first hour is Jupiter's, the second is Mars'; on Monday night, the first is Venus', the second is Mercury's. This should be understood for all. For clarity, the chart <note>Refers to a chart on the following page</note> * should be consulted. The results of the hours are explained clearly. || 127-129 ||

Jupiter, Mars, Sun, Venus, Mercury, Moon, and Saturn—these hour-lords follow every sixth from the day-lord, and at night, they start from the fifth day-lord. For example, on Sunday: first Sun, then Venus, then Mercury, etc. On Monday: first Moon, then Saturn, then Jupiter, etc. This is how it should be known for all. || 127 ||

The results for one born in the hours of the Sun and others are as follows: If born in the hour of the Sun, one spends their time in distress. If born in the hour of the Moon, one becomes wealthy. If born in the hour of Mars, there is sorrow and disease. If born in the hour of Mercury, there is knowledge and wealth. If born in the hour of Jupiter, there is all prosperity and lordship...

# With the Commentary on Jataka Parijata

Remembering the ancient saying "marmamu," and having reached the appropriate occasion for the **Ashtakavarga** <note>A system of points used to determine the auspiciousness of planetary transits</note> of the fixed planets, we now describe these charts to determine the good and bad results of each celestial body as they travel through the various zodiac signs in transit relative to the Ascendant and all other planets. In these Ashtakavarga charts, auspicious places are assigned for each of the planets. Those places not mentioned are considered inauspicious. The auspicious places are marked with dots (**bindus**), and the inauspicious ones are marked with lines (**rekhas**). How many of these auspicious marks (in the form of dots) belong to each planet is explained in the following two verses.

By drawing a chart starting from the Ascendant and the Sun—meaning the seven planets plus the Ascendant, totaling eight—and placing the planetary circle as it stood at the time of birth, one calculates the "letters" (auspicious marks) derived from the eight factors (Sun to Ascendant). When these are totaled, they become the total dots generated by the individual Ashtakavargas. The specific totals for each planet are given using the *Katapayadi* system <note>An ancient Indian mnemonic system to represent numbers with letters</note>:

*   **The Sun:** *Deva* = 48
*   **The Moon:** *Dhava* = 49
*   **Mars:** *Dhiga* = 39
*   **Mercury:** *Vasha* = 54
*   **Jupiter:** *Tama* = 56
*   **Venus:** *Rama* = 52
*   **Saturn:** *Dhuli* = 39

These are the individual totals of auspicious dots for the seven planets from the Sun onwards. When these are combined, the "Community Total" of dots is *Salola* = 337. For verification, the calculation is: 48 + 49 + 39 + 54 + 56 + 52 + 39 = 337. Regarding the term "Community Total" used here, it refers to the **Sarvashtakavarga** (the collective chart). Now, in this context, the Ashtakavargas for each planet as taught by Varahamihira are written down:

> From the Moon, [Venus is auspicious] in the 1st, 11th, 3rd, 4th, 5th, 8th, 9th, and 12th houses; from Saturn in the 3rd, 6th, 5th, and 12th; from Mercury in the 3rd, 5th, 6th, and 11th; from the Sun in the 8th, 11th, and 12th; and from the Ascendant in the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th, 8th, 9th, and 11th. || 5 || <note>This verse describes the favorable positions for Venus relative to other planets.</note>

**The Ashtakavarga of Venus:** From the Ascendant, the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th, 8th, 9th, and 11th houses; from the Moon, the same plus the 12th; from itself (Venus), the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th, 8th, 9th, 10th, and 11th; from Saturn, the 3rd, 4th, 5th, 8th, 9th, 10th, and 11th; from the Sun, the 8th, 11th, and 12th; from Jupiter, the 5th, 8th, 9th, 10th, and 11th; from Mercury, the 3rd, 4th, 5th, 6th, 9th, 11th, and 12th; and from Mars, the 3rd, 5th, 6th, 9th, 11th, and 12th. || 6 ||

**The Ashtakavarga of Saturn:** Saturn is auspicious from itself in the 3rd, 5th, 6th, and 11th houses; from Mars in the 3rd, 5th, 6th, 11th, and 12th; from the Sun in the 1st, 2nd, 4th, 7th, 8th, 10th, and 11th <note>original: "upachaya" refers to houses of growth (3, 6, 10, 11), but specific numbers are listed here</note>; from the Ascendant in the 1st, 3rd, 4th, 6th, 10th, and 11th; from Mercury in the 6th, 8th, 9th, 10th, 11th, and 12th; from the Moon in the 3rd, 6th, and 11th; from Venus in the 6th, 11th, and 12th; and from Jupiter in the 5th, 6th, 11th, and 12th. || 7 ||

Thus are the favorable positions declared; others are unfavorable. These results manifest specifically based on the strength of the planets at birth. Planets in "Upachaya" <term>Upachaya: Houses 3, 6, 10, and 11, associated with growth and improvement</term> houses give full results, while those in "Apachaya" <term>Apachaya: Houses other than 3, 6, 10, and 11</term> houses may lead to loss of wealth. || 1-2 ||

Now we consider the Ashtakavarga: By drawing the charts of the seven planets including the Ascendant and marking points <note>original: "bindu" (dots/points)</note> according to the following verses, the auspicious Ashtakavarga points are determined. || 1 ||

The points for the planets starting with the Sun are respectively: 48, 49, 39, 54, 56, 52, and 39. That is, the Sun has 48, the Moon 49, Mars 39, Mercury 54, Jupiter 56, Venus 52, and Saturn 39 points. The total sum is 337. This is known as the *Sarvashtakavarga* <term>Sarvashtakavarga: The collective total of all auspicious points in the eight-fold system</term> community. || 2 ||

The houses from Aries onwards that receive a high number of <term>Bindus</term> <note>Literally "dots" or points; these represent units of auspicious energy in a horoscope.</note> result in the nourishment, strength, and growth of that specific house's significations. Houses containing six, five, or seven points are considered givers of auspicious results, while those with three, two, or one point are not favorable. || 3 ||

A mixed result occurs when there are four points <note>original: "sāgara-bindu" or "ocean-dots," a poetic term for the number four.</note>. If a house has zero points, it brings disease, infamy, and fear. I shall now declare the full results arising from the individual <term>Ashtakavargas</term> of the Sun and other planets, starting with the effects of a single point. || 4 ||

->A single point causes various types of diseases, sorrows, fears, and aimless wandering.<-

# With the Commentary on Jataka Parijata

<page-num>320</page-num>

->Two points bring mental distress, and destruction caused by kings, thieves, fire, and disputes.<-
->With three points, the mind is troubled by the hardships of wandering and lack of support.<-
->The "Ocean-point" (four points) yields mixed results: expenditure of wealth and gain of wealth.<-
->Seven points produce a multitude of gains, the cherishing of children, the company of holy people, knowledge, and wealth.<-
->Six points bring a new and enchanting form and character, victory in battle, wealth, fame, strength, and vehicles.<-
->Seven points bring horses and other luxuries, armies, wealth, power, and splendor.<-
->Eight points manifest the majesty of a king, delightful with the seven virtues.<-

Now, the results of the houses and planets are described based on the number of <term>Bindus</term> <note>literally "dots" or "points," representing auspicious units</note> in the desired <term>Ashtakavarga</term> <note>a system of points used to calculate planetary strength</note>. Through the following six verses starting with "Aries etc.," it is explained that if eight points (auspicious marks) are found in a house like Aries according to the previously mentioned analysis, those eight points strengthen that house. This should be understood as follows: in whichever house the Ashtakavarga is being considered, if there is auspiciousness from all planets (meaning all eight points are present), then that house is nourished by that planet. That is to say, when that planet arrives in that house during its transit or during its major period (<term>Dasha</term>), an increase in the fruits of that house should be predicted. Similarly, houses with six, five, or seven points give auspicious results. In whichever house five, six, or seven points occur, auspicious results should be declared. In the case of an "Ocean-point" yoga (combination)—where there are four points in a house—the result is mixed, meaning both auspicious and inauspicious. Those houses which are "zero-houses"—meaning those in which not even one auspicious point exists, but instead all eight are <term>Rekhas</term> <note>literally "lines," representing inauspicious units</note>—those houses bring disease, infamy, and fear. Therefore, I, the author, shall declare all the results, auspicious and inauspicious, arising from the individual Ashtakavargas of the Sun and other planets possessing one or more points. The rest is clear and need not be further elaborated.

Here, regarding the auspicious and inauspicious results mentioned based on the points, the method of understanding the points is explained. In whichever house a planet is situated, it is considered to have as many points as there are planets from which it receives auspiciousness. As many planets as it receives inauspiciousness from, that many lines (<term>Rekhas</term>) should be written. Thus, by taking the difference between the points and the lines, the auspicious or inauspicious result should be stated based on what remains. In that regard, for auspicious results, the points must be greater than the lines. For the sake of illustration, the chart for the <term>Ashtakavarga of Mars</term> <note>Bhauma</note> is written:

| | | |
| :--- | :---: | ---: |
| | Sun: |||||ooo | 11: ||||||oo |
| Moon, Merc. | 1 | |
| |||||ooo | Asc. 12 Venus | Mars 10 |
| 2 | ooo||||| | ||o8ooo |
| | 3 | 9 |
| 4 | |||ooo | ||||||oo |
| ||||oooo | | |
| Jup. | | |
| | 5 | 8 |
| | |||ooooo | o||||||| |
| | 6 | Sat. 7 |
| | . |||||| . | |||ooooo |

<note>The chart above represents an Ashtakavarga diagram for Mars (Bhauma). Circles (o) represent Bindus (auspicious) and vertical lines (|) represent Rekhas (inauspicious).</note>

In this example—following the verse "Mars is in its exaltation etc." from the *Brihat Jataka*—in Aries, there are three points and five lines; the difference leaves two lines. Therefore, by transit, when Mars is in Aries, it will be inauspicious by two-eighths. In Taurus, there are three points and five lines; the difference leaves two lines, so when Mars enters Taurus by transit, an inauspicious result of two-eighths should be predicted. It is the same in Gemini. In Cancer, there are four points and four lines; since nothing remains after the difference, it is neither auspicious nor inauspicious. In Leo, there are five points and three lines; the difference leaves two points, so Mars transiting through Leo would be auspicious by two-eighths. Similarly, in Virgo, it is inauspicious by four-eighths. In Libra, it is auspicious by two-eighths. In Scorpio, it is inauspicious by six-eighths. In Sagittarius, it is inauspicious by four-eighths. In Capricorn, it is auspicious by two-eighths. In Aquarius, it is inauspicious by one-eighth. In Pisces, it is inauspicious by two-eighths.

# Chapter 10: The Chapter on Ashtakavarga
## Page 321

In the signs starting from Aries, any house <note>Bhava</note> containing 8 points <note>Bindus</note> becomes a source of nourishment, strength, and growth. Houses containing 6, 5, or 7 points are also givers of auspicious results. Those houses containing only 1 or 2 points are not auspicious. || 3 ||

I shall now describe the complete results arising from the individual Ashtakavarga charts of the Sun and other planets, starting from one point:
A single point causes various types of disease, sorrow, fear, and aimless wandering. Two points cause mental distress, trouble from authorities <note>original: "Raja" or King</note> and thieves, scandals, and difficulty in obtaining food. Three points cause obstacles in moving about effectively, a physical wasting of the body, and mental agitation. Four points provide a mix of happiness and sorrow, and the income and expenditure of wealth; in other words, the good and bad are balanced. || 5-6 ||

Five points grant the acquisition of excellent objects, the joy of raising children, the company of holy people, and wealth through knowledge. Six points grant a new and captivating appearance, good character, victory in battle, wealth, the performance of sacrifices, strength, and vehicles. || 7 ||

Seven points grant the riding of horses and similar mounts, command over armies, wealth, grandeur, and splendor. Eight points manifest a royal glory that is supreme in the quality of goodness <note>Sattva-guna</note>. || 8 ||

-> A planet situated in its own division in a sign containing five or more points is always a giver of auspiciousness. <-
-> Otherwise, it yields no fruit; a planet transiting a sign with zero points leads to negligence and error. || 9 || <-
-> Even if planets are in their signs of exaltation, friend's signs, or divisions, and possess strength by being in the centers <note>Kendras</note>, <-
-> they all give undesirable results if they are associated with very few points. || 10 || <-
-> Even those situated in "bad houses" <note>Dusthanas: the 6th, 8th, or 12th houses</note> or in signs and divisions of debilitation or enmity, <-
-> are always givers of auspiciousness if they are associated with many points. || 11 || <-
-> When Saturn, in the divisions of the Sun and other primary planets, enters a house with zero points, <-
-> it causes extreme disease, enemies, and fear for the significations of that house, such as the father and others. || 12 || <-

Now, the results are explained based on the position and the number of points in the Ashtakavarga. A planet residing in its own division, when situated in a sign containing "five or more points"—meaning where five, six, seven, or eight points exist—will always be a giver of auspicious results whenever it passes through that sign during its transit <note>Gocharas</note>. Otherwise, if a planet lacking its own divisional strength is situated in signs with fewer than five points, it is "fruitless" or ineffective. When a planet arrives via transit in a sign with "zero points," the person becomes "negligent" or prone to wandering and confusion.

The text further states that even planets with high status are useless if they have few points: "Even if planets..." etc. Those planets that may be in their exaltation or friendly divisions, and even if they possess strength from being in the centers <note>1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note>, if they have "few points" in the Ashtakavarga (less than half, i.e., less than 4), then all such planets become givers of undesirable results. Conversely, planets situated in "bad houses" (the 6th and others) or in signs and divisions of debilitation or enmity, if they are "associated with many points" (more than half), then they all become givers of auspicious results. The essence is that a high number of points never brings harm.

Now, the specific characteristic of Saturn is mentioned: In the divisions of the Sun and the other six primary planets, when Saturn transits into a "zero house" (a house without any points) in the Ashtakavarga, it causes extreme disease, enemies, and fear for the "father and others"—meaning the relatives signified by that specific house. || 9-12 ||

A planet in its own division situated in a sign with five or more points is always auspicious. Otherwise, it gives bad results during transit. A planet with zero points causes negligence and failure. || 9 ||

<note>The "Bindu" system acts as a weightage filter; a planet might look strong in a standard chart, but if it has low points in this specific system, its power to do good is neutralized.</note>

# Commentary on the Jataka Parijata

Even if planets are positioned in their signs of exaltation or friendly divisions and possess strength through their placement in angular houses <note>Kendras: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</note>, they will produce unfavorable results if they are associated with very few points <note>bindus</note>. || 10 ||

Conversely, all planets situated in "bad houses" <note>Dusthanas: the 6th, 8th, or 12th houses</note>, or those in signs and divisions of debilitation or enmity, will always grant auspicious results if they are endowed with many points. || 11 ||

In the planetary divisions of the Sun and others, if Saturn is found in a house with zero points, it causes disease, fear of enemies, and distress to those born under that influence, particularly affecting the father and related significations. || 12 ||

### Results of the Sun

If the Sun is in the Ascendant <note>Lagna</note> in the division of an enemy or a sign of debilitation, and is joined by two or three points, the person born will be sickly. If the Sun is in the Ascendant with five or more points, or is in its sign of exaltation or its own house, the person will be a long-lived king. || 13 ||

->If the Sun is in an angle or a trine <note>Trikona: the 1st, 5th, or 9th houses</note> with six, five, seven, or eight points in its Ashtakavarga,<-
->then in the years corresponding to the codes *Rudra*, *Amala*, *Nila*, and *Chala*, either the person born or his father will face death. || 14 ||<-

When the Sun is in an angle accompanied by the Moon, Saturn, and Mercury, and possesses two points remaining after the reduction process <note>Shodhya-pinda: a mathematical reduction used in Ashtakavarga</note>, the noble sages say that after ten years, the father of the native will attain prosperous royal fortune. || 15 ||

Now, the author explains the results of the Sun’s Ashtakavarga based on its position: *Lagnamiti*. If the Sun is in the Ascendant, in the Navamsha <note>ninth-part sub-division</note> of an enemy sign or a sign of debilitation, and is accompanied by two or three points, the native becomes sickly. This occurs whenever the Sun transits that Ascendant sign. Now, if the Sun is with five, six, seven, or eight <gloss>five-six-seven-eight</gloss> points and is situated in the rising sign <gloss>Ascendant</gloss> in its exaltation sign <gloss>Aries</gloss> or its own house <gloss>Leo</gloss>, then the native will be a long-lived <gloss>living a long life</gloss> king.

Furthermore, if the Sun is in an angle <gloss>1, 4, 7, 10</gloss> or a trine <gloss>1, 5, 9</gloss> and is joined by six, five, seven, or eight <gloss>6, 5, 7, 8</gloss> points, then respectively in the years *Rudra*, *Amala*, *Nila*, and *Chala*, the death of the native or the native's father occurs. This means: if the Sun has six points in an angle or trine, death occurs in the *Rudra* <gloss>22nd</gloss> year; if five points, in the *Amala* <gloss>35th</gloss> year; if seven points, in the *Nila* <gloss>30th</gloss> year; and if eight points, in the *Chala* <gloss>36th</gloss> year. This applies when the Sun transits those specific signs on the corresponding day of the week.

Furthermore, if the Sun is with the Moon, Saturn, and Mercury in an angle, and possesses two points remaining after the reduction of the trines and the reduction for planets in the same sign, then after ten years, the noble ones say the father of the native will receive abundant royal prosperity. || 13-15 ||

If the Sun is in the Ascendant in the Navamsha of an enemy or debilitated sign and has three or four points, the person is sickly. If the Sun is in the Ascendant in its exaltation or its own house with five or more points, he becomes a long-lived king. || 13 ||

If the Sun is in an angle or a trine with six, five, seven, or eight points, then in the 22nd, 35rd, 30th, and 36th years respectively, the father of that native may die. || 14 ||

If the Moon, Saturn, Mercury, and the Sun are in an angle with two points remaining after reduction, then after ten years, the father of that native is granted royal fortune endowed with all kinds of prosperity; so say the great scholars. || 15 ||

### Results of the Moon

In the Ashtakavarga of the Sun and the Moon, a house with zero points—its corresponding month and sign—should be avoided for all auspicious works. If the Moon is in the Ascendant with only one, four, or five points, and is joined by two or three other planets, death occurs in the thirty-seventh year. || 16 ||

# Chapter 10: The Chapter on Ashtakavarga
<page-num>323</page-num>

> If the Moon is positioned in a <term>Kendra</term><note>Angular houses: 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th</note>, a <term>Trikona</term><note>Trinal houses: 5th and 9th</note>, or the house of gain (11th), but is in its sign of debilitation, an enemy's sign, or is waning in its digits <note>the dark fortnight</note>, and possesses only two or three dots (<term>Bindus</term>), the experts say this causes the destruction of that house's influence. || 17 ||

> If the Moon is strong and possesses four or more dots while situated in the four corners <note>the Kendras</note>, the trines, or the house of gain, there is an increase in the prosperity of that house. If the Moon is in an angular house with eight dots, those born are kings, mighty in knowledge, fame, wealth, and strength. || 18 ||

Now, the author explains the results of the Moon's <term>Ashtakavarga</term> <note>A system of points used to predict the strength of planets</note> based on specific positions: Regarding the "empty house"—having understood the empty signs (those signs where not even a single dot is present) in the Ashtakavarga of the Sun and the Moon, the sages say that the corresponding month (for the Sun) and the sign (for the Moon) should be abandoned for all auspicious works. This should be noted: when the Sun transits through a sign that lacks dots (auspicious marks) in the Sun's Ashtakavarga, one should not perform auspicious deeds during that solar month. Similarly, when the Moon transits a sign that is void of dots in the Moon's Ashtakavarga, auspicious work must not be done. 

Furthermore, if the Moon is in the <term>Lagna</term> <note>The Ascendant or 1st house</note> with only one, three, or two dots, one should predict lethargy associated with pulmonary disease <note>original: "yakshma," often referring to consumption or tuberculosis</note>. If such a Moon is also joined by two or three other planets, the death of the native should be predicted in the thirty-seventh year. 

Regarding the verse "If in Kendra, Trikona, or Gain": If the Moon is in its debilitation sign, an enemy's sign, or lacking increasing digits (the dark fortnight) and is placed in a Kendra, Trikona, or the 11th house (1, 4, 7, 10, 5, 9, or 11), and if it has only two or three dots, then the experts—the astrologers—say this destroys the significance of that house. 

Regarding "Four or more": If the Moon is strong (possessing positional strength, etc.) and is associated with four, five, six, seven, or eight dots, and is placed in a trine (5, 9), a square (1, 4, 7, 10), or the house of gain (11), then the prosperity of that house increases. Now, the specific result of eight dots is given: if the Moon with eight dots is in an angular house, the men born are kings, powerful in wisdom, reputation, wealth, and physical strength. || 16-18 ||

**Hindi Translation**
In the Sun's Ashtakavarga, the sign which has no dots represents a month (solar month), and in the Moon's Ashtakavarga, an empty sign should be avoided for all auspicious work. If the Moon is in the Ascendant with 1, 3, or 2 dots, there may be laziness caused by pulmonary illness. If that same Moon is with 2 or 3 planets, death may occur in the 37th year. || 16 ||

If the Moon is in a trine or angle, in its debilitation sign, an enemy's sign, or waning, and is joined by two or three dots, the destruction of that house occurs; so say the wise. || 17 ||

If a strong Moon with 4, 5, 6, 7, or 8 dots is in a trine, angle, or the house of gain (these are 7 houses in total), it increases the prosperity of that house. A Moon with 8 dots in an angle makes one a king powerful in knowledge, fame, wealth, and strength. || 18 ||

### Now, the Results of Mars (Bhauma).

->**The Results of Mercury**<-

> If Mercury is in a quadrant or a trine <note>houses 1, 4, 7, 10 or 5, 9</note> with eight points, the person will possess great enjoyment and excel in the traditional knowledge of their class.

> When Saturn passes through a house that is empty of Mercury’s points in the transit, there is destruction of wealth, kinsmen, and relatives. **(22)**

Now the results of Mercury’s Ashtakavarga are explained: **If Mercury is with eight points** in a quadrant (1, 4, 7, 10) or a trine (5, 9), the person born is **endowed with traditional knowledge and great enjoyment**—meaning they possess the knowledge of their family lineage and enjoy many pleasures. **In its exaltation and so on**: when Mercury is in its exaltation, its root-trine <note>Moolatrikona</note>, or its own sign, even with only one, two, or three points, there is an **increase of that house** (the house characterized by these traits flourishes), and there is no loss of that house's significance. Conversely, if Mercury is in its sign of debilitation or an enemy's sign with few points, the house suffers. **Abundance of points**: In the Ashtakavarga, whichever sign has the most points for Mercury, the solar month corresponding to that sign is the best time for the **commencement of education** <term>Vidyarambha: a traditional ceremony marking the start of a child's formal schooling</term>; if begun then, the person becomes a "mine of all knowledge." Furthermore, if a sign has zero points for Mercury, and **Saturn** <note>Manda</note> arrives there by **transit** <term>Gochara: the current movement of planets across the zodiac</term>, one should predict the destruction of the person's wealth and relatives. **(21-22)**

If Mercury is in a quadrant or trine with eight points, one possesses traditional knowledge and great enjoyment. If in its exaltation etc. with one, two, or three points, that house increases and does not suffer loss. **(21)**

If points are many, begin education in the month of that house to become a master of all sciences. If Saturn transits through Mercury's empty house, brothers, family, and wealth are destroyed. **(22)**

### Now, the Spread (Prastara).

Having drawn a chart with nine horizontal lines and thirteen vertical lines, there will be a spread of ninety-six cells consisting of eight rows produced from the Ashtakavarga system. || 33 ||
The Ascendant, Moon, Mercury, Venus, Sun, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn are the lords of the eight rows starting from the bottom, and they shall sequentially bestow the results of their dots. || 34 ||
A planet with a dot shall bestow all its results; one without a dot shall be fruitless. Even if a planet has a dot, if it is in an enemy's sign, debilitated, or set <note>combust by the Sun</note>, it causes the destruction of results. || 35 ||

Now, the method for the Spread (Prastara) in the Ashtakavarga system is described: "Having drawn..." Since there are eight factors (the seven planets plus the Ascendant), nine horizontal lines are required. To accommodate the twelve signs from Aries onwards, thirteen vertical lines must be drawn. In this way, a chart of ninety-six cells is drawn. As follows:

### The Spreadsheet (Prastara Chart)

| | Ari. | Tau. | Gem. | Can. | Leo | Vir. | Lib. | Sco. | Sag. | Cap. | Aqu. | Pis. |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Saturn** | | | | | | | | | | | | |
| **Jupiter** | | | | | | | | | | | | |
| **Mars** | | | | | | | | | | | | |
| **Sun** | | | | | | | | | | | | |
| **Venus** | | | | | | | | | | | | |
| **Mercury** | | | | | | | | | | | | |
| **Moon** | | | | | | | | | | | | |
| **Ascendant** | | | | | | | | | | | | |

In this chart, the Ascendant, Moon, Mercury, Venus, Sun, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn are the lords of the eight rows starting from the bottom. This means: dividing each sign into eight parts, the planets (including the Ascendant) become the lords of each of the eight segments in the order of their orbits <note>the "Kakshas" or orbital divisions</note>. One-eighth of a sign is equal to 3 degrees and 45 minutes. Therefore, in every sign, Saturn rules up to 3°45'. Then Jupiter rules up to 7°30'. Then Mars up to 11°15'. Then the Sun up to 15°0'. Then Venus up to 18°45'. Then Mercury up to 22°30'. Then the Moon up to 26°15'. Finally, the Ascendant is considered the lord (the giver of results) up to 30°0'. These planets bestow the results of the dots they have obtained in those specific positions. A planet with a dot in its designated section gives the stated result. It follows logically that a planet without a dot is fruitless. Furthermore, even if a planet has a dot, if it is in an enemy's sign, a debilitated sign, or joined with the Sun, that planet becomes fruitless. In this spread, a higher number of dots generated by all planets is desired for auspiciousness. If there are fewer than half <note>less than 4 dots per sign</note>, it is not auspicious. As stated in the Phaladeepika:

> When a dot is present, to determine the timing of the realization of its fruit in the Ashtakavarga, others say the result should be told by dividing the sign into eight parts according to the order of the orbits.

### Now, the Rectification of the Trines <note>Trikona Shodhana</note>.

> Draw five lines toward the East and five transverse lines, leaving the central four squares empty.

Now the author explains the rectification of trines in the Ashtakavarga system through three verses starting with "Five..." The three corners (among the twelve signs, the 1st, 5th, and 9th from any sign are called its "Trines" <note>Trikona</note>) and their mutual reduction is called "Rectification of Trines" <note>Trikona Shodhana</note>. For that purpose, first, the construction of the chart is necessary: Five lines toward the East (horizontal) and five transverse lines (vertical), leaving the four central segments empty. By doing this, a twelve-celled chart is produced. In this, the twelve sky-dwellers (the zodiac signs) starting with Aries are known as the lords of the directions. # With the Commentary on Jataka Parijata

The points <note>bindus</note> obtained by subtracting the smallest value from the points located in each of the triangular groups <term>Trikona: groups of three signs 120 degrees apart</term> are the reduced points. This is what is meant: in the Ashtakavarga of each planet, among the four triangular groups, the smallest number of points found in any of the three signs within a group should be subtracted from the points in all three signs of that group. The remaining values are the points resulting from the Triangular Reduction <term>Trikona Shodhana</term>.

For example, in a hypothetical case in the Mars-Ashtakavarga <note>refer to the chart in the commentary for verses 3-8</note>: Aries has 3 points, Leo has 5 points, and Sagittarius has 2 points. Among these three places, the smallest value is 2 (in Sagittarius). Subtracting this from all three places, we get: 1 in Aries, 3 in Leo, and 0 in Sagittarius.

Next, Taurus has 3 points, Virgo has 2 points, and Capricorn has 5 points. Here, the smallest (2) is subtracted from the three, leaving 1 in Taurus, 0 in Virgo, and 3 in Capricorn.

Similarly, Gemini has 3 points, Libra has 5, and Aquarius has 3. Subtracting the smallest (3) from all three leaves 0 in Gemini, 2 in Libra, and 0 in Aquarius.

Likewise, Cancer has 4 points, Scorpio has 1, and Pisces has 3. Subtracting the smallest (1) from the three leaves 3 in Cancer, 0 in Scorpio, and 2 in Pisces. Thus, the point results for the twelve signs in the Mars-Ashtakavarga after Triangular Reduction are:

| Ar. | Ta. | Ge. | Ca. | Le. | Vi. | Li. | Sc. | Sa. | Cp. | Aq. | Pi. | Signs |
|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---|
| 3 | 3 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 2 | 5 | 1 | 3 | 5 | 3 | 3 | Points |
| 1 | 1 | 0 | 3 | 3 | 0 | 2 | 0 | 0 | 3 | 0 | 2 | Reduced Points |

Now, he explains a specific rule for Triangular Reduction: when the smallest value is subtracted from the three, that smallest value becomes zero, and the other two (if they were 5 or 6, for example) become the remaining points after the smallest is removed. If any one sign in the triangle (the three houses) already has zero points, then the others remain exactly as they are; because subtracting zero results in no change, the reduction should not be performed in that case. If all three places have an equal number of points, then all should be cleared. In that case, all three places become zero, as equal values are subtracted everywhere. As stated in the *Parashariya*:
> "In the triangles, subtract the value equal to the minimum from all three. If one house is empty (zero), that triangle should not be reduced. If there is equality in all houses, then all should be cleared." || 36-38 ||

<note>The following is a Hindi summary/translation of the Sanskrit rules above</note>
Draw 5 horizontal lines and 5 vertical lines to create 16 squares. Discard the middle 4; the remaining 12 squares represent the zodiac cycle starting from Aries in the East. || 36 ||
In the Ashtakavarga of the Sun and others, the smallest point value found in the corners—Aries-Leo-Sagittarius, Taurus-Virgo-Capricorn, Gemini-Libra-Aquarius, and Cancer-Scorpio-Pisces—is subtracted. || 37 ||
In a triangular group, reduce the two other houses by the one that has fewer points. If a house has no points, do not subtract from the others. If the numbers are equal, discard them all. || 38 ||

## Now, the Reduction Based on Dual Lordship

<term>Ekadhipatya Shodhana: Reduction based on planets that own two signs</term>

Excluding Leo <note>the Sun's sign</note> and Cancer <note>the Moon's sign</note>, the points located in the pairs of signs inhabited by Mars and the other planets <note>who own two signs each</note> become the "Remainder after Dual Lordship Reduction" when they are made equal, zero, or reduced based on whether the signs are occupied by planets. || 39 ||
If both signs are occupied by planets, do not reduce. If one of the two is empty (zero), also do not reduce. If one has more points and is occupied by a planet, discard the points of the other. If both are empty of planets and have equal points, discard both. || 40 ||
If the points are equal between a sign with a planet and one without, subtract the points of the planet-occupied sign from the other. When writing the points for the two signs, the lesser and greater should be made equal to the lesser. || 41 ||

It also introduces Ekadhipatya Shodhana, the second reduction based on planetary ownership of dual signs.</summary>
