# With the Commentary of Jataka Parijata

When the fifth house <note>The house of children and intelligence</note> is occupied or aspected by Rahu or Ketu <note>The North and South Nodes of the Moon, often associated with karmic debts</note> and is devoid of strength, or if its lord (the ruler of the fifth house) is similarly situated (joined or aspected by Rahu or Ketu and weak), then the loss of sons occurs due to the "Curse of the Serpent" <note>original: *sarpa-dosha*; often interpreted as a spiritual affliction resulting from harming a snake in a past life</note>. || 36 ||

If Jupiter, the lord of the fifth house, the lord of the seventh house, and Mars are all joined together in one place, the wise say that the destruction of both daughters and sons occurs due to the affliction of an "Evil Deity" <note>original: *durdeva-pīḍayā*; refers to the influence of a hostile or unfavorable spirit/god</note>. || 37 ||

**Notes** — Having understood the cause of obstacles to progeny in the birth chart, one should perform worship and remedies for the respective unfavorable deities to remove that defect. Then, even if obstructive combinations exist, the birth of offspring becomes possible, as it is said: "Through peace-making rituals, everything becomes auspicious" and "Attainment comes from the root of righteousness." || 32-37 ||

If a malefic planet aspects the house of sons, one should declare the destruction of sons due to a "Divine Curse." If the house of sons is joined or aspected by the lord of the sixth house <note>The house of enemies and disease</note>, the destruction of sons is due to the "Curse of a Brahmin." || 32 ||

If the lord of the fifth house is joined with Mars and aspected by the lord of the sixth house, without any aspect from a benefic planet, one should know the loss of sons is due to "Fault of Weapons" <note>Violence or injury</note>. || 33 ||

If a malefic planet is in the 9th house, the lord of the 5th is joined with Saturn, and Gulika <note>A shadow planet considered the son of Saturn</note> is in a trine, the loss of sons is due to a "Father's Curse." || 34 ||

If the 4th house is joined with a malefic, the lord of the 5th is joined with Saturn, and the 12th house is occupied by a malefic, the loss of sons is due to a "Mother's Fault." || 35 ||

If the fifth house is joined or aspected by Rahu or Ketu and is weak, and its lord is also in the same condition, the loss of sons is due to the "Serpent's Fault." || 36 ||

If Jupiter, the lord of the 5th, the lord of the 7th, and Mars are combined, one should declare the destruction of daughters and sons due to the affliction of an "Evil Deity." || 37 ||

> If any planet with full strength is located in the house of sons,
> but is not aspected by the lord of the fifth house,
> then the sons will be adopted or of other secondary types. || 38 ||
>
> When the Moon is in a sign owned by a malefic, the lord of the 5th is in the 9th,
> and the lord of the ascendant is in a trine,
> the attainment of an adopted son occurs. || 39 ||
>
> If the lord of the 5th is in an even-signed ascendant, or in the 4th house,
> and is placed in the Navamsha <note>The ninth divisional chart</note> of Saturn,

> If the lord of the 5th is in an even Navamsha or Saturn's Navamsha,

Now, the author explains some combinations for an adopted son <note>original: *datta-putra-yoga*</note> through the six verses starting with "If any planet..." If any planet possessing full strength (as previously described) is in the fifth house, but is not aspected by the lord of the fifth house, the children of that person will be adopted and not biological. || 38 ||

If the Moon is in a sign of a malefic planet, the lord of the fifth house is in the ninth house, and the lord of the ascendant is in a trine <note>The 1st, 5th, or 9th houses</note>, then the attainment of an adopted son occurs. || 39 ||

If the lord of the fifth house is in an even-signed ascendant <note>Taurus, Cancer, Virgo, Scorpio, Capricorn, or Pisces</note>, or is in the fourth house and situated in the Navamsha of Saturn (either Capricorn or Aquarius), then the person will have an adopted son. || 40 ||

# Chapter 13: Results of the Fifth House (Progeny)

->**The Yoga (Combination) for Adoption**<-

If the Lord of the Fifth House <note>the planet ruling the house of children</note> is joined with the Sun and the Moon, and is placed in an even-signed Navamsha <note>a 1/9th divisional chart sign</note> or in the Navamsha of Saturn (Capricorn or Aquarius), then in this combination, the birth of an adopted son will occur. || 41 ||

If the Lord of the Fifth House is in the Navamsha of Saturn (Capricorn or Aquarius), and Jupiter and Venus are in their own signs (Jupiter in Sagittarius or Pisces; Venus in Taurus or Libra), then the person first obtains an adopted son, and after that, a biological son is born from his wife. || 42 ||

If the birth occurs during the Bright Fortnight <note>Shukla Paksha, the waxing moon phase</note> and the planets with the most strength (three or more) are situated in Saturn’s Navamsha, and if Jupiter is in the fourth house, then the person’s lineage continues through an adopted son. || 43 ||

**Notes—** Here, the word "even" (Yugma) can also refer to the sign of Gemini. Therefore, "rising in an even sign" can mean Gemini Ascendant, and "even Navamsha" can mean Gemini Navamsha. Since the terms "Saturn’s Navamsha" and "Son of the Sun’s Navamsha" appear later, it should be considered that including Gemini in the definition of "even" is not a mistake. || 38-43 ||

<margin>If any planet with full strength is in the house of children and the Lord of the Fifth is combust <note>too close to the sun</note>, there will be an adopted son. || 38 ||</margin>

<margin>If the Moon is in the house of a malefic planet, the Lord of the Fifth is in the ninth, and the Lord of the Ascendant is in a trine, an adopted son is obtained. || 39 ||</margin>

<margin>If the Lord of the Fifth is in an even sign or the fourth house and in Saturn’s Navamsha, there will be an adopted son. || 40 ||</margin>

If the Lord of the Fifth, joined with the Sun and Moon, is in an even Navamsha or Saturn’s Navamsha, an adopted son is obtained in this yoga. || 41 ||

If the Lord of the Fifth is in Saturn’s portion, and Jupiter and Venus are in their own signs, first an adopted son is born, then a son is born from the wife. || 42 ||

If strong planets of the Bright Fortnight are in Saturn’s portion and Jupiter is in the house of children <note>Note: The Sanskrit commentary says 4th house, the Hindi says 5th</note>, there will be an adopted son. || 43 ||

> If Mars is in the Ascendant and the Sun is in the eighth house,
> Or if the Sun is in the fourth house and aspected by a benefic, a son is born after a long time. || 44 ||
> If Saturn is in the Ascendant and Jupiter is in the eighth house,
> While the fifth house is weak and Mars is in the twelfth, a son is born after a long time. || 45 ||

Now the combinations for delayed progeny are described in two verses. When Mars is in the Ascendant, and the Sun is in the eighth house or the fourth house and is aspected <note>glanced at</note> by a benefic planet, a son is born after a long time (at an advanced age). As stated in the *Horaratna*:

> "If Mars goes to the Ascendant or Saturn is in the eighth sign,
> Or the Sun is in the house of children, a son is born after a long time."

When Saturn is in the Ascendant, Jupiter is in the eighth house, the fifth house is weak, and Mars is in the twelfth house, a son is born after a long time. And in the *Parashariya*: "With Saturn in the Ascendant, Jupiter in the eighth, and Mars in the twelfth, if there is a benefic aspect or it is in its exaltation, he obtains a son after a long time." || 44-45 ||

If Mars is in the Ascendant and the Sun is in the eighth or fourth house with a benefic aspect, a son is born after a long time. || 44 ||

If Saturn is in the Ascendant <note>Lagna</note>, Jupiter is in the 8th house, and a weak Mars is in the 5th or 12th house, then a son is born after a long interval of time. || 45 ||

> One should consider sons from the 5th house, brothers from the 3rd, wives from the 7th, 
> female servants from the 4th, and male servants and friends from the 2nd house. 
> Multiply the number of passed Navamshas <note>A 1/9th division of a sign, used for precision</note> by the strength of the aspect of benefic planets. 
> Divide that by two hundred; the resulting number indicates the quantity of sons and others. || 46 ||

Now, the author explains the houses for considering sons, brothers, wives, male servants, female servants, and friends, as well as the method for knowing their number—"Sons etc." From the 5th house (counting from the Ascendant), one should consider sons. From the 3rd house (the house of siblings), brothers. From the 7th house, wives are to be considered. From the 4th house, consider female servants. From the 2nd house, consider male servants and friends. Regarding "passed": the Navamshas that have been passed or consumed in those respective houses (5th, 3rd, etc.) <gloss>as many Navamshas as have been traversed</gloss> should be multiplied by the "benefic sight" (the aspectual strength of auspicious planets) and then "placed" or established. Then, divide those by "sky-sky-hands" (the number 200) <note>In the Katapayadi system, 'sky' is 0 and 'hand' is 2; read right-to-left or as a code for 200</note>. The resulting quotient indicates the number of sons and so on. This is the point to be reflected upon: in the 5th, 3rd, 4th, 2nd, and 7th houses, whatever the strength of the aspect of benefic planets is <note>See Chapter 1, verses 10-31</note>, the passed Navamshas of that house should be multiplied by it and divided by two hundred. The resulting number tells the quantity of sons, etc. || 46 ||

**The Logic Here:** According to the words of the sage Garga—"The number is equal to the Navamshas occupied in the house of sons, if in a benefic division"—and also:

->“The number is always seen to be equal to the Navamshas in a benefic sign when aspected.” — From the words of Kalyanavarman<-

The product of the passed Navamshas in the houses of sons etc., and the relative strength of benefic aspects, is expressed in minutes <gloss>because aspectual strength is measured in minutes</gloss>. When divided by two hundred <gloss>because there are 200 minutes in one Navamsha</gloss>, the resulting number of sons etc. is correctly determined. || 46 ||

One should consider sons from the 5th house, brothers from the 3rd, the wife from the 7th, female servants from the 4th, and servants and friends from the 2nd. The method for knowing the number of all these is: multiply the aspectual strength <term>Drigbala: the mathematical strength of a planet's gaze</term> of benefic planets on that specific house <note>See Chapter 1, verses 10-31</note> by the number of passed Navamshas of that house. Dividing that by 200, the quotient indicates the number of sons etc. — Commentary by Sudhashalini. || 46 ||

> Excluding the sign, take the minutes of the 5th house, 3rd house, 7th house, 
> the Ascendant, and the 4th house. Multiply these by the aspectual strength 
> of benefic planets and divide by sixty. 
> Then divide by two hundred; this gives the number of sons, siblings, wives, 
> male servants, female servants, and friends. Those numbers resulting from 
> the aspectual strength of malefic planets indicate the destruction of sons and others. || 47 ||

"Sons etc.": The 5th house (sons), 3rd house (siblings), 7th house (wife), the Ascendant (self/birth), and 4th house (vehicles/home). "Excluding the sign" means leaving aside the number of the zodiac sign and taking only the minutes of the degrees of those houses separately. Multiply these by the measure of the aspectual strength of benefic planets, divide by 60, and then sequentially divide by "sky-sky-hands" (200) <gloss>divided</gloss> to find the individual numbers of sons, siblings, wives, male servants, female servants, and friends. In that calculation, the numbers arising from the aspectual strength of malefic planets <note>Planets like Saturn or Mars</note> provide the "destruction" of sons and others. This means: whatever number is calculated using the aspectual strength of malefic planets on those houses, one should predict the loss or death of that many sons, etc.

# Chapter 13: Results of the Fifth and Seventh Houses

The logic applied here is the same as that stated in the commentary for verse 46, so no further explanation is needed. || 47 ||

Take the zodiacal signs of the fifth, third, seventh, first <note>the Ascendant or Lagna</note>, and fourth houses and convert them into minutes of arc <term>liptā: a unit of measurement where 1 degree equals 60 minutes</term>. Multiply this by the aspectual strength of the beneficial planets and divide by 60, then divide by 200. The resulting numbers represent, in order: sons, brothers, wives, male servants, female servants, and friends. If the aspectual strength comes from malefic planets, the children and others being born will be destroyed. || 47 ||

> When Jupiter reaches the sign or its trine <note>the 5th or 9th positions from a sign</note> formed by the sum of the longitudes of the lord of the house of children and the lord of the Ascendant, the birth of a son occurs. The number of sons corresponds to the number of Navamshas <note>a 1/9th division of a sign, used to determine strength and quantity</note> in the sum of the longitudes of Jupiter, the Moon, and the Sun. Alternatively, the number of sons equals the Navamshas in the sum of the lords of the 5th, 9th, and 4th houses; or the Navamshas in the sum of the planets situated in the 5th, 9th, and 4th houses. || 48 ||

Now, he describes another method for knowing the timing of the birth of a son and the number of sons: "The lord of the house of children..." etc. The sum of the longitudes of the lord of the 5th house and the lord of the 1st house <insert>calculated separately</insert> results in a specific sign and degree. When Jupiter <note>the planet of expansion and children</note> transits through that resulting sign or its trines (the 5th or 9th houses from it), the birth of a son is possible. Regarding the number of sons: the sum of the longitudes of Jupiter, the Moon, and the Sun results in a sign; the number of sons will equal the number of Navamshas passed in that sign. Alternatively, one may sum the longitudes of the lords of the 5th, 9th, and 4th houses and use the Navamsha count. Or, one may sum the longitudes of the planets actually located in the 5th, 9th, and 4th houses and determine the number of sons based on the Navamshas passed in that resulting sign. || 48 ||

->By adding the longitudes of the lord of the 5th and the lord of the 1st, one should predict the birth of a son when Jupiter arrives in that resulting sign or its trines. The number of sons is equal to the Navamshas passed in the sum of Jupiter, the Moon, and the Sun. Or, the number of sons is equal to the Navamsha count of the sum of the lords of the 5th, 9th, and 4th houses. Or, know the number of sons by the Navamshas in the sum of the planets situated in the 5th, 9th, and 4th houses.<- || 48 ||

> The fifth house from Jupiter, from the Moon, and from the Ascendant is the giver of children. The ninth house from those is also a giver of children. One should predict the birth of a son during the major or minor planetary periods <term>Dasha-Bhukti: time cycles in Vedic astrology</term> of the lords of those houses. Add the longitudes of the lords of the 5th and 7th houses; the major period of the planet ruling the resulting lunar mansion <term>Nakshatra</term>, or the periods of planets joined with or aspecting them, will grant a son. || 49 ||

"From Jupiter..." etc. The 5th house from the position of Jupiter, from the sign occupied by the Moon, and from the birth Ascendant is the place that grants children. Among these three, one should judge the presence or absence of children from the 5th house of the strongest planet. "And the house of piety from that..." means the 9th house from those (Jupiter, Moon, or Ascendant) also grants children. A wise man should predict the birth of a son during the major or minor periods of the lords of these child-granting houses. Furthermore, by summing the longitudes of the lords of the 5th and 7th houses, a specific lunar mansion <note>Nakshatra</note> is found. According to the <term>Vimshottari</term> system <note>a 120-year cycle of planetary periods</note>, the major period of the planet ruling that mansion grants a son. Additionally, the major or minor periods of planets joined with or aspecting the lords of the 5th and 7th houses are also givers of children. || 49 ||

The fifth house from Jupiter, the Moon, and the Ascendant gives children, and the 9th house from them is also a giver of children. Predict the birth of a son during the periods of the lords of those signs. By adding the longitudes of the lords of the 5th and 7th houses, the resulting lunar mansion's period and the periods of planets associated with them through conjunction or aspect will grant a son. || 49 ||

->If the lord of the house of children, the significator of children, the planet aspecting that house, and the planet occupying it are lords of "evil houses," are weak, or are placed in "evil houses," one should predict the loss of a son during the periods and sub-periods of those planets. If these four are powerful and auspicious, they bring about the birth of a son, the prosperity of children, and the favor of powerful people during their periods and sub-periods. 50.<-

Now, regarding the status of children, he speaks of favorable and unfavorable outcomes—"The lord of the house of children," etc. The planets consisting of:
<margin>1</margin> 1. The lord of the 5th house <note>the house of children</note>, 2. The significator <term>Karaka: a planet that naturally represents a specific life area; for children, this is Jupiter</term> of children, 3. The planet aspecting the 5th house, and 4. The planet situated in the 5th house—if these planets are "lords of evil houses" (the 6th, 8th, or 12th houses), or are weak, or are "poorly placed" (located in the 6th, 8th, or 12th houses), then during the "ripening" <note>Dasha: planetary period</note> and sub-period of such planets, one should predict the "destruction" or death of a son.
However, if those four planets are "powerful" (possessing strength) and "auspicious" (benefic planets), then during their periods and sub-periods, they bring about "attainment of a son" (birth), "wealth of children" (their prosperity), and the "affection of lords" (favor from kings and authorities). 50.

<note>The following is a Hindi translation/summary of the above Sanskrit verse</note>
If the four planets—the lord of the 5th house, the significator of children, the one aspecting the 5th house, and the one residing in the 5th house—are lords of evil houses (6, 8, 12), are weak, or are located in evil houses, then in their periods and sub-periods, predict the loss of a son. If these four planets are fully powerful and auspicious, then in their periods they grant the gain of a son, prosperity of children, and the pleasure of kings. 50.

->When Jupiter and Saturn, through their transit, reach the sign and Navamsha <note>a 1/9th division of a sign</note> resulting from the sum of the longitudes of the lord of the 5th, the significator, the planet occupying the house, and the planet aspecting it, they cause the birth and death of a son for the native. 51.<-

Now he describes the signs for the birth and death of a son—"The lord of the 5th," etc. By adding the specific longitudes (degrees, etc.) of the lord of the 5th, the significator of children, and the planets aspecting the 5th as they were at the time of birth, a specific sign and degree is produced. When, by "transit" (current movement), "the Lord of Speech" <note>Jupiter</note> and "the Son of the Sun" <note>Saturn</note> reach that sign or its Navamsha, they cause the birth or death of a son for the man. The meaning is this: when Jupiter transits the point calculated from the sum of these four planets, the birth of a son should be predicted. When Saturn transits that same point, the death of a son should be predicted.

**Notes**—Here, one should not judge the result solely by the arrival of Jupiter or Saturn at the calculated sign; one must also consider the age of the native. Otherwise, if the sum of the four planets is very low and close to the positions of Jupiter or Saturn at birth, it might lead to the impossible conclusion of a child being born to someone at an extremely young age. This must be reflected upon. 51.

### Regarding the Father

->If the lord of the house of the father is a benefic, and the significator is joined with a benefic, or if the house itself is joined with a benefic, one should predict happiness regarding the father. 52.<-

Now he discusses the father of the native—"The lord of the house of the father," etc. If the lord of the house of the father <note>Note: The text here identifies the 5th house for the father, though the commentary below clarifies the 9th</note> is a "benefic" (auspicious planet), and the "significator" (the Sun for the father) is joined with a benefic, or if the house itself is joined with a benefic, one should predict "paternal happiness." A man born under this combination enjoys happiness from his father.

# Chapter 13: Results of the Fifth and Sixth Houses
<page-num>406</page-num>

In this house, the <term>consideration of the father</term> <note>Sanskrit: Pitru-vichara</note> is performed. However, in this text, we see the pledge: "One should consider children, enemies, the king, the father, the intellect, and virtues from the fifth house." Furthermore, in the ninth house, the text mentions "fortune, influence, the teacher, religion, and penance," where the father is also considered. Therefore, in the present verse, "In the house of the lord of the father's place," I have explained it specifically regarding the fifth house. ॥ 52 ॥

If the lord of the father's house (the 5th lord) is a benefic planet, and the <term>significator of the father</term> <note>The Sun is typically the Pitru-karaka or significator for the father</note> is joined with a benefic planet, or if the fifth house itself is occupied by a benefic, then one should predict happiness from the father for the person. ॥ 52 ॥

> If the lord of that house and the significator are placed in <term>Paravata</term> <note>A specific high-quality strength in the Vaisheshikansha system</note> or similar divisions, or are in their exaltation or a friend's <term>divisional chart</term> <note>Navamsha</note>, one should predict a long life for the father. ॥ 53 ॥
> If the lord of the house and the significator are in the divisional charts of cruel planets or in their debilitation, or are joined with Saturn, Gulika, or Rahu, one should predict sorrow regarding the father. ॥ 54 ॥
> If a benefic planet or the lord of that house is in a debilitated, combust, or enemy sign, or in a <term>cruel sixtieth division</term> <note>Shashtyansha</note>, one should predict sorrow regarding the father. ॥ 55 ॥

These three verses are easy to understand and thus have not been elaborately commented upon in the prose. ॥ 53-55 ॥

If the 5th lord or the father-significator is in the *Paravata* or other *Vaisheshikansha* divisions, or is in its exaltation or a friend's *Navamsha*, the father has a long life.
If the 5th lord and the father-significator are in the *Navamsha* of a malefic or in debilitation, or are joined with one or more of Saturn, Gulika, or Rahu, then sorrow regarding the father should be predicted.
If a benefic planet and the 5th lord are debilitated, combust, in an enemy's house, or in a cruel *Shashtyansha*, then sorrow regarding the father should be predicted. ॥ 53-55 ॥

> One born in the <term>father's house of action</term> <note>The 10th house from the father's rising sign</note> possesses qualities equal to the father. One born in the third sign from the father's birth sign is obedient to the father. ॥ 56 ॥
> One born in the sixth or eighth from the father's sign will be an enemy to the father. If the lord of that house is in the <term>ascendant</term> <note>Lagna</note>, the son will be superior to the father. ॥ 57 ॥

Now, the results of the son's birth based on the father's birth chart are explained in two verses. "Born in the father's house of action" means: a child born in the sign that is tenth from the father's rising sign <note>Lagna</note> will possess qualities similar to the father. If the father is a scholar, the son will be a scholar. If the father is a fool, the son will be a fool; all virtues and vices will be similar. "Born in the third from the father's birth" means: a child born in the third sign from the father's rising sign will be a follower of the father's commands. However, the result should not be judged by this alone; one must also consider the strength and weakness of the respective houses in the child's own birth chart.

"In the father's sixth or eighth" means: a child born in the sixth or eighth sign from the father's rising sign will be an enemy to the father. A child born in this planetary combination will harbor hatred toward the father. "If the lord of that house" means: if the lord of the 5th house from the child's own rising sign is placed in the child's rising sign, the son will be superior to the father. A child born in this combination will be more distinguished and respected in qualities than the father. ॥ 56-57 ॥

If the birth occurs in the 10th sign from the father's rising sign, that person has qualities like the father. If the father is a scholar, he is a scholar; if the father is a fool, he is a fool. Similarly, he is joined with virtues and vices like the father. A child born in the 3rd sign from the father's birth sign is obedient to the father.
A child born in the 6th or 8th sign from the father's rising sign becomes the father's enemy. If the lord of the 5th house from the child's rising sign is in the child's own rising sign, then that person is superior in qualities and more respectable than the father. ॥ 56-57 ॥

# With the Commentary on Jataka Parijata—

### If Saturn, Mars, and Rahu are situated in the 11th or 9th houses from the Ascendant, they cause the death of the father.
### If Saturn and Mars are in the 8th or 7th houses, they cause the death of the child.
### If Mars, the Sun, Saturn, and the Moon are in the 10th or 5th houses,
### they quickly cause the destruction of the maternal uncle, father, child, and mother respectively. || 58 ||

**From the Ascendant:** Saturn, Mars, and Rahu <note>original: "Shani-Mahi-Putra-Agavah"</note>, if situated in the 11th or 9th houses from the birth Ascendant, cause the death of the father <note>original: "Tatasya"</note>. This means the father of the person born under this combination dies. Saturn and Mars <note>original: "Arkaja-Bhusutau"</note>, when in the 8th or 7th houses from the Ascendant, cause the death of the child <note>original: "Balasya"</note>. Furthermore, if Mars, the Sun, Saturn, and the Moon <note>original: "Kuja-Ravi-Chhaya-Kumara-Indavah"</note> are positioned in the 10th <note>original: "Mane"</note> or 5th houses, they quickly destroy the maternal uncle, father, child, and mother in that specific order. Specifically, Mars in the 10th or 5th causes the death of the maternal uncle; the Sun causes the death of the father; Saturn causes the death of the child; and the Moon causes the death of the mother. This same meaning is stated in the *Sarvartha Chintamani*:

> "If Saturn and Mars are joined with Rahu <note>the King of Snakes</note> in the 11th or 9th houses, there is danger to the father.
> If Mars is in the 9th <gloss>9</gloss> or 10th <gloss>10</gloss> from the Ascendant and is aspected by a malefic, they speak of the death of the maternal uncle.
> If joined with Saturn, the death of the son; if with the Moon and a malefic, the death of the mother.
> If the Sun <note>Lord of the Day</note> is there, the death of the father occurs without doubt during a malefic planetary period." || 58 ||

If Saturn, Mars, and Rahu are in the 11th or 9th positions from the birth Ascendant, they cause the father's death. If Saturn and Mars are in the 8th or 7th, they cause the death of the native's son. If Mars is in the 10th or 5th, the maternal uncle dies quickly; if the Sun is in the 10th or 5th, the father dies; if Saturn, the son dies; and if the Moon, the mother dies. || 58 ||

---

### If the Lord of the 5th house (father's house) is strong,
### but the Lord of the Ascendant, the Moon, and the Lord of the 4th house are weak,
### they know the death of the mother will occur during childbirth. || 59 ||

**When strong:** If the Lord of the 5th house <note>representing the father in certain systems, or here used in a specific calculation</note> is endowed with strength, and the Lord of the Ascendant, the Moon, and the Lord of the 4th house <note>representing the mother</note> are weak, then the death of the mother occurs during the pains of labor <note>original: "garbhatah"</note>. The sense is that the mother of the person born under this yoga dies from pregnancy-related complications. || 59 ||

If the Lord of the 5th house is strong and the Lord of the Ascendant, the Moon, and the Lord of the 4th house (happiness/mother) are weak, his mother's death occurs from childbirth. || 59 ||

---

### The Lord of the 8th from the 9th, or the Lord of the 22nd Drekkana from the 9th—
### if such a planet is Saturn and is cruel in its "obstructions," it causes the father's death. || 60 ||

**From the 9th:** The Lord of the 8th house from the native's 9th house (which is the 4th house from the birth Ascendant), or the Lord of the <term>Khara</term> <note>the 22nd Drekkana, a specific 10-degree division of the zodiac associated with danger</note> calculated from the 9th house—if that Lord is Saturn, and if it is "cruel" in its <term>Vedha</term> <note>astrological "obstructions" or alignments that block a planet's positive influence</note>, it causes the death of the father.

Here, the *Vedha* should be considered from the birth sign <note>the sign occupied by the Moon at birth</note>. To understand *Vedha*, the following verses from the *Kalaprakashika* are cited:

> When the Sun enters the trine positions from the stronger of the sign or Navamsha occupied by the Lord of the Day (Sun), the father's death occurs; the mother's death occurs from the strength of the sign or Navamsha occupied by the Moon. // 61 //

**Commentary:** From the sign and the Navamsha where the Sun is situated, whichever is "stronger" (endowed with more vitality)—when the Sun transits the trine <note>Kona: the 5th or 9th house positions</note> from that stronger sign or Navamsha, the father's death occurs. Similarly, from the sign and Navamsha where the Moon is situated, when the Sun transits the trine (5th or 9th) of the stronger of the two, the mother's death occurs. First, one should determine the year of the parents' death through Jupiter or Saturn, and then use this verse to determine the specific month of the death. // 61 //

Whichever is stronger between the sign and the Navamsha where the Sun is located, when the Sun enters the 5th or 9th house from that, the father dies. When the Sun enters the 5th or 9th from the stronger of the Moon's sign or Navamsha, the mother dies. After knowing the year of death through Jupiter and Saturn, the month must be known through this verse. // 61 //

> When the Moon reaches the sign indicated by the Navamsha or the twelfth-part <term>Dwadasamsha: a 1/12th division of a sign</term> of the degree occupied by the Sun, death occurs for the mother and father respectively. // 62 //

# With Commentary on the Jataka Parijata

**The Sun's Position**
The Sun's position <note>original: "Bhanusthita"</note> refers to this: The lord of the <term>Navamsha</term> <note>a 1/9th division of a zodiac sign</note> in which the Sun is placed at the time of birth. When the Moon transits the sign associated with that lord's Navamsha or <term>Dvadasamsha</term> <note>a 1/12th division of a zodiac sign</note>, death occurs for the mother and father respectively. That is to say, when the Moon enters the sign where the Sun's Navamsha lord is situated, the mother's death should be predicted; when the Moon enters the sign of that lord's Dvadasamsha, the father's death should be predicted.

Notes—After determining the year and month of the parents' death, this verse allows for the determination of the specific lunar day <note>original: "tithi"</note>. || 62 ||

[Hindi Commentary Translation]: When the Moon enters the sign where the lord of the Sun's Navamsha is located, the mother dies. When the Moon enters the sign where the lord of the Sun's Navamsha is located in the Dvadasamsha, the father dies. Having first determined the year and month of the parents' death, one can use this verse to find the specific date. || 62 ||

The sense is that for one born under this alignment, the father dies while the child is an embryo. || 63 ||

If the Moon and the Sun are both in dual signs <note>original: "dvidehagau" - Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces</note> and are positioned in the angles <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note>, then the death and the cremation of the parents will occur at two different times. It is not the case that the cremation follows immediately after death. Rather, the cremation of the corpse occurs after a significant interval of time following the unfortunate death. Here it is appropriate to say: for a person at whose birth the Sun and Moon are in angles in dual signs, the parents die in the absence of their kin (such as in a foreign land), and therefore their death and cremation do not happen at the same time. By implication, if at the time of birth the Moon and Sun are in fixed signs in the angles, then the parents are cremated by the hand of the son at the very time of death. || 65 ||

If the Sun or the Moon are in movable signs (Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn) and are in an angle (1st, 4th, 7th, 10th houses), then the son does not perform the cremation (the post-mortem burning of the corpse) of the mother and father. If the Sun and Moon are in dual signs (Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces) and are in an angle, then the death and cremation of the parents do not happen at one time; rather, the cremation occurs some time (days) after the death. The conclusion is that if the Moon and Sun are in fixed signs in an angle, the son performs the cremation of his parents at the actual time of death. — From the author of *Subodha Jnana*. || 65 ||

> If the lords of the father and mother <note>the 9th and 4th houses</note> have gone to the invisible half, they cause the faces of the parents to be unseen. If the lord of the son <note>5th house</note> has gone to an invisible house, he causes the face of the son to be unseen at the final hour. || 66 ||

Now he describes the planetary combinations for not seeing the faces of the parents or the son at the time of death: "If they have gone to the invisible..." etc. If at the time of birth, the lords of the father and mother—the masters of the 9th and 4th houses—have gone to the invisible half <note>original: "adṛśyayātau" - the portion of the zodiac between the degree of the Ascendant and the degree of the 7th house, passing through the 12th, 11th, 10th, 9th, and 8th houses</note>, then they cause the faces of the parents to be unseen; meaning, in this combination, the person born does not see the faces of the parents [at death]. Furthermore, if the lord of the son—the master of the 5th house—similarly goes to an invisible house (the invisible half of the circle), then at the final hour—the moment of death—he causes the face of the son to be unseen. This means the person born under this combination does not see the son's face at the time of death. In both cases, it should be stated that this is due to being in a remote or hidden location. || 66 ||

If the lord of the 9th and the lord of the 4th are in the invisible half of the circle (between the rising degree of the 1st house and the setting degree of the 7th house), then the son does not see the faces of his mother and father (at the time of death). If the lord of the 5th is in an invisible sign, then at the time of death, the father and mother are unable to see the face of their son. The significance is that in both combinations, the death of the parents occurs in the absence of the son.

If any planet is situated in an **enemy's place = the sixth house**, then the person will be **surrounded by many enemies** = joined by numerous foes, and will have a **body marked by many wounds** = a physical form afflicted by many sores or scars. "Constantly" here means perpetually, as defined in the *Amarakosha* <note>A famous Sanskrit thesaurus</note>: '**satatanaratashrantasantatavihatanisham | nityanavaratajasram**' <note>original: "Always, without ceasing, untiringly, continuously, uninterruptedly, night and day; eternally, without pause, perpetually."</note>. If the Sun or Mars are in the 6th, then by a Kshatriya (warrior) enemy; if the Moon, then by a Vaishya (merchant); if Mercury, then by a Shudra (laborer); and if Saturn, then by a Mlechha (foreigner/outcaste) enemy. || 74 ||

If any planet is in its enemy's house, or in debilitation, or retrograde, or combust while in the sixth house, the native is joined by many enemies and has many wounds on his body. Similar results occur if the Lord of the 6th is so placed. When the Sun and other planets are in the sixth house, the native is afflicted by enemies of their respective classes. || 74 ||

> If the three sky-wanderers—the lord of the 6th, the occupant of the 6th, and the aspecting planet of the 6th—are malefic and weak, they cause loss of cattle and wealth, sickness, and fear of enemies from birth. If all of them are powerful and benefic, one should predict cattle, wealth, horses, etc., royal food with all instructions, and the destruction of disease and enemies. || 75 ||

Regarding the verse: **The lord, occupant, and aspector of the 6th** = 1. <term>Shastha-bhavesha (Lord of the 6th)</term>, 2. <term>Shastha-bhava-gata (Occupant of the 6th)</term>, and 3. <term>Shastha-bhava-darshi (Aspector of the 6th)</term>—if these three planets are **malefic sky-wanderers** = <term>Papagrahas (Malefics)</term> and are weak = devoid of strength, then they cause **loss of cattle and wealth** = destruction of cows and riches, **sickness** = disease, and **fear of enemies** = dread of foes, right from birth. However, if all those three—the <term>Lord of the 6th</term>, the <term>Occupant of the 6th</term>, and the <term>Aspector of the 6th</term>—are benefic = <term>Shubhagrahas (Benefics)</term> and are powerful = possessing strength, then one should predict cattle, wealth, horses, etc., royal food provided with various utensils, and the destruction of disease and enemies. || 75 ||

If the Lord of the 6th, the occupant of the 6th, and the aspector of the 6th are all malefic and weak, there is loss of cattle-wealth, disease, and fear of enemies from birth. Regarding the verse: Among those three **sky-wanderers** = the planets that are the **lord, occupant, or aspector of the 6th**, if two are **very benefic** and are situated in a <term>Kendra, Trikona, or Aya</term> (houses 1, 4, 7, 10, 5, 9, or 11), and if these two are also powerful, they cause the destruction of minor diseases for men = those born. If in the fifth house, wounds to the father and son; if in the fourth, to the mother; if in the seventh, to the wife. If in the ninth house, to the maternal uncle; if in the third, to the younger brother; if in the eleventh, to the elder brother; and if in the eighth, the person born will suffer from rectal disease.** || 77 || <-

**Malefic etc.**—When a malefic planet (**any one of the Sun, Mars, Saturn, or Rahu**) is in the **Ascendant** <note>Lagna: the rising sign or first house</note> while joined with the **lord of the sixth house <margin>Lord of the sixth = the ruler of the house of enemies and disease</margin>**, there will be a **wound on the body** of the native. If the malefic joined with the lord of the sixth is in the **fifth house**, there will be a wound on the bodies of the **native's father and son**. If in the **fourth house**, there will be a wound on the **mother's** body. If in the **seventh**, a wound on the **wife's** body. If in the **ninth house**, on the **maternal uncle**. If in the **third**, on the **younger brother**. If in the **eleventh house**, a wound occurs on the **elder brother**. Now, if the malefic planet joined with the lord of the sixth is in the **eighth house**, the native **himself** will be afflicted by **rectal disease (such as fistula, etc.)**. || 77 ||

If a malefic planet joined with the lord of the sixth is in the Ascendant, there is a wound on the man's body. If in the fifth, on the father and son. If in the fourth, on the mother. If in the ninth, on the maternal uncle. If in the third, on the younger brother. If in the eleventh, on the elder brother. If in the eighth, the native himself suffers from rectal disease (hemorrhoids). || 77 ||

-> **The Sun causes disease in the head, the Moon in the face, Mars in the throat, and Mercury below the navel. Jupiter grants health, while Venus causes eye disease. Saturn causes wind-related ailments, and Rahu and Ketu cause stomach disease. If the Lord of the Ascendant is Mercury, or is aspected by or joined with Mercury, it gives a secret wound.** || 78 || <-

**The Sun etc.**—If the **Sun** is joined with the lord of the sixth and is placed in the sixth or eighth house, then it causes **disease or wounds in the head**. The **Moon** in such a state affects the face; **Mars** affects the throat; **Mercury** <note>original: "Chandri" (son of the Moon)</note> causes disease in the **region below the navel**. **Jupiter** <note>original: "Suri"</note> creates **freedom from disease (health)**. **Venus** <note>original: "Bhargava"</note> in that state causes **eye disease**. **Saturn** <note>original: "Manda"</note> causes **wind-related ailments** <note>Vata: one of the three humors in Ayurveda, often associated with joints and nerves</note>, and **Rahu** <note>original: "Ahi" (the serpent)</note> and **Ketu** cause **stomach disease**. Furthermore, if the **Lord of the Ascendant is Mercury, or is placed in Virgo or Gemini, and is aspected by or joined with Mercury** while in the sixth house, then it **gives a secret wound (such as a fistula or other private ailments)**.

**Notes**—Here, "freedom from disease" is mentioned for Jupiter, but Parashara <note>A foundational sage of Indian astrology</note> has stated that Jupiter joined with the lord of the sixth in the sixth or eighth house causes nasal disease. His words are as follows:
If the lord of the sixth is a malefic and is situated in the body (Ascendant) or the eighth, then a wound occurs on the body; this rule also applies to the tenth house.
Similarly, if the lords of the houses for the father, etc., are joined with their respective significators <note>Karaka: a planet that represents a specific person or category</note>, and are joined with the lord of wounds or placed in the sixth or eighth:
Wounds should be predicted for them as well. The Sun causes head wounds; the Moon, the face; Mars, the throat; Mercury, the navel.
Jupiter causes wounds in the nose; Venus in the eyes or feet.
Saturn and Rahu in the belly, and Ketu likewise. || 78 ||

If the Sun is in the 6th or 8th house joined with the lord of the sixth, the disease is in the head; if the Moon, in the face; if Mars, in the throat; if Mercury, below the navel. If it is Jupiter, he destroys the disease. <unclear>...</unclear>

# From the Annotated Jataka Parijata

...eye disease; if Saturn is present, there is a wind-related disorder <note>original: "vatavyadhi" - often referring to gout, rheumatism, or nervous disorders</note>; if Rahu or Ketu are present, there is disease in the stomach. If the Lord of the Ascendant <term>Lagnesha: the planet ruling the first house of the self</term> is in a house of Mercury (Gemini or Virgo) and is aspected by or joined with Mercury, it causes ulcers or sores in the private parts. || 78 ||

### The Signs of the Body and Fear of Animals

**If Rahu (the Lord of Serpents) is in any sign starting from the Ascendant and is aspected by Venus, a mark will appear on the corresponding part of the body.**
**If the Lord of the House of Enemies is joined with Saturn and Rahu, the wise say there is fear from horses and other four-legged animals.** || 79 ||

*Commentary:* Regarding the verse beginning with "Lagnadi": If Rahu is placed in a sign relative to the Ascendant and is seen by Venus, a mark such as a scar or ulcer will appear on the limb corresponding to that sign (referencing the division of body parts by zodiac signs mentioned in Chapter 3, Verse 76). Furthermore, if the Lord of the Sixth House is joined with Saturn and Rahu, the learned say the native faces danger from horses and other quadrupeds. || 79 ||

### Suffering from Enemies and the Destruction of Foes

**When the Lord of the Sixth is weak, aspected by a malefic planet, or placed between two malefic planets, there will be suffering caused by enemies.**
**When the Lord of the Sixth House is in a bad state—debilitated, combust, or in an enemy's sign—and the Lord of the Ascendant is endowed with strength, the wise predict the destruction of enemies.**

*Commentary:* Now the author describes suffering from enemies and the destruction of enemies in two verses. If the Lord of the Sixth House is weak, aspected by a malefic, or "hemmed in" between two malefics <note>original: "papantargate" - the yoga known as Papa Kartari</note>, the native will experience pain and distress at the hands of enemies. In this yoga, no good can be expected from one's rivals.

Conversely, if the Lord of the Sixth is in a "dusthana" <note>a difficult house like the 6th, 8th, or 12th</note>, in its sign of debilitation, hidden by the sun's rays (combust), or in a hostile sign, while the Lord of the Ascendant is full of strength, the wise say the native's enemies will be destroyed or perish. || 80-81 ||

### Benefactor of One's Kin

**If the Lord of the Sixth is in the "Gopura" or higher division and is aspected by the Sun, and the Lord of the Ascendant is fully strong, the native becomes a benefactor to his kinsmen.**
**Thus ends the thirteenth chapter of the Jataka Parijata, composed by Vaidyanatha by the grace of the Nine Planets.** || 13 ||

*Commentary:* Now the author describes a native who helps his relatives. If the Lord of the Sixth House attains the "Gopura-amsha" <note>a specific strength measure where a planet is in its own or exalted sign in 4 out of 10 divisional charts</note>, is aspected by the Sun, and the Lord of the Ascendant is possessed of full strength, the person born will be a helper and benefactor to his own lineage and kin. || 82 ||

->**Thus end the results of the Sixth House.**<-

The "Sudha" commentary was composed by Kapileshwara for the Parijata.
With this thirteenth chapter, the results of the houses are completed. || 13 ||

**Thus ends the "Vimala" Hindi commentary on the results of the Fifth and Sixth Houses in the thirteenth chapter of the Jataka Parijata, composed by the astrologer Vaidyanatha.** || 13 ||

# Now begins the chapter on the fruits of the Seventh, Eighth, and Ninth Houses || 14 ||

->Regarding the fruits of the Seventh House.<-

> One should contemplate all matters of travel, children, and the happiness of a spouse from the seventh house;
> all that has been said regarding the arrival of happiness or unhappiness from children should also be declared from here. || 1 ||

**Regarding travel:** From the seventh house <note>The Seventh House is traditionally the house of partnerships and the "setting" sun, representing the 'other' and journeys away from home</note>, one should consider all happiness related to travel, children, and spouses. Furthermore, whatever was previously stated regarding the results of happiness or distress coming from children should also be predicted from the seventh house. Thus, it is said in the **Jataka Bharanam** <note>A classical 15th-century Sanskrit text on predictive astrology</note>—

> "The battlefield, commercial transactions, the wife, authority, arrivals, and departures;
> those proficient in the scriptures must consider all these from the House of the Spouse (7th)."

Likewise, in the **Jataka Ratna**—

> "From the place of the young woman (7th house), one considers marriage, the wife, the husband, messengers, curds, molasses, and milk;
> arrivals, rivers and such, the place of urination, and lost wealth." <gloss>1/2</gloss> ||

One should consider all happiness regarding travel, children, and women from the seventh house. Whatever results were previously mentioned regarding the arrival of happiness or sorrow from children, all those should also be told from the seventh house. || 1 ||

> If Venus is in the house of desire (7th), or if the lord of the seventh is with Rahu or Ketu, the person becomes an adulterer;
> but if the seventh house is occupied or aspected by a benefic planet or Jupiter, the person will not be an adulterer. || 1 ||

**Regarding the adulterer:** If Venus <note>original: "Sita"</note> is situated in the house of desire (the 7th house), the person born becomes an adulterer (one who goes to others' wives). Or, if the lord of the seventh house <note>original: "Madanapa"</note> is anywhere joined with Rahu or Ketu <note>original: "Sahidhvaja" - literally 'with the banner', a term for the lunar nodes</note>, the same result occurs. However, if the seventh house is a sign of a benefic planet and is joined with or aspected <note>viewed by</note> Jupiter <note>original: "Jiva"</note>, the person born will not be an adulterer, but rather will be of virtuous conduct. || 1 ||

If Venus is in the seventh, he is an adulterer (lusting after others' wives), or if the lord of the seventh is joined with Rahu or Ketu, he is also an adulterer. If the seventh is a benefic planet's sign and Jupiter is in it or looks upon it, he is not an adulterer. || 1 ||

> If the lord of the seventh is in a bad house, in the house of a malefic, aspected by or joined with a malefic,
> the results of that house of the spouse are mediocre; otherwise, all is auspicious.
> If the lord of the seventh is with Venus in a malefic sign, the mind is full of lust;
> if in a benefic sign, aspected by or joined with a benefic planet, the person possesses a white umbrella. || 2 ||

**Regarding the ill-placed:** If the lord of the seventh house is in a "bad house" <note>The 6th, 8th, or 12th houses, known as Dusthanas</note>, or in the sign of a malefic planet, or aspected by a malefic, or joined with a malefic, then all results for the house of the spouse for that person are mediocre. This means whatever is considered from the seventh house for one born under such a combination will yield middling results. Otherwise—meaning if the lord of the seventh is in an auspicious house, an auspicious sign, or is aspected/joined by benefics—all results for the house of the spouse will be auspicious. If the lord of the seventh house is joined with Venus and is in a malefic sign, the person born is lustful. If that same lord of the seventh is in a benefic sign and is aspected by or joined with a benefic planet, the person born possesses a "white umbrella" <note>original: "Sitachhatravan" - a traditional symbol of royalty or high status</note> (meaning he becomes a king). || 2 ||

If the lord of the seventh is in a bad place, in a malefic house, a malefic planet sees it, or it is joined with a malefic, then tell mediocre results for his seventh house. If it is not so, know all to be auspicious. If the lord of the seventh is with Venus in a malefic sign, he is lustful. If in a benefic sign, joined with a benefic, or if benefics see it, that person shall have a white umbrella (be a king). || 2 ||

<term>Saptamabhava: The seventh house of a horoscope, primarily governing marriage and partnerships.</term>
<term>Kalatra: Spouse or wife.</term>
<term>Jara: An adulterer or paramour.</term>
<term>Madanapa: The planetary ruler of the seventh house.</term>
<term>Sita/Shukra: The planet Venus.</term>
<term>Kamastana: The "place of desire," another name for the seventh house.</term>

->**With Commentary: Jataka Parijata**<-

<note>The following verses describe specific planetary alignments that ancient astrologers believed indicated a person's sexual temperament or likelihood of extramarital affairs.</note>

> If the lords of the second, seventh, and sixth houses, along with Venus, are located in the first house <term>Ascendant/Lagna</term> and are joined by malefic planets, the person will be highly lustful. Likewise, if the lords of the first and sixth houses are joined by malefic planets, the person is constantly devoted to women. If a malefic planet is in the seventh house joined by the lords of the sixth, second, and first houses, the person will be attached to the wives of others. If a malefic planet and the lords of the sixth and seventh houses are in the ninth house, the person becomes afflicted by intense desire. || 3 ||

**Commentary:** "If the lords of the second, seventh, and sixth houses..." refers to the rulers of the houses of wealth, marriage, and enemies. If these, along with Venus <note>the planet of desire</note>, are in the Ascendant and joined by "malefics" <note>typically Mars, Saturn, or the Sun</note>, the native is extremely lustful. If the lords of the first and sixth houses are joined by malefics, they will always be devoted to women. If a malefic (Sun, Mars, or Saturn) is in the seventh house <note>the house of partnership</note> along with the lords of the sixth, second, and first, the native will be "attached to the wives of others" <note>original: *parastriratah*</note>. Furthermore, if a malefic and the lords of the sixth and seventh houses are in the ninth house <note>the house of fortune/religion</note>, the native is born "tormented by desire." It should be understood that if these combinations are aspected <note>viewed</note> by "benefic" planets <note>Jupiter, Venus, Mercury, or the Moon</note>, these effects do not manifest in the same way.

And so it is said in the **Sarvartha Chintamani** <note>A famous 17th-century astrological text</note>:
> If the lords of the first, second, and seventh houses are in the Ascendant with Venus and joined by malefics, the native is devoted to the wives of others and follows a wicked path; however, if aspected by benefics, this is not so. If the lords of the eleventh and sixth houses are joined by malefics, the native is devoted to the wives of others. If the lord of the Ascendant is with the lords of the sixth and second houses, or with malefics in the seventh house, the native is devoted to the wives of others... || 3 ||

<note>The Hindi translation below the Sanskrit repeats these rules: if the lords of the 2nd, 7th, 6th, and Venus are in the 1st house with malefics, the native is lustful. If the 1st and 6th lords are with malefics, the same applies. A malefic in the 7th with the 6th, 2nd, and 1st lords leads to adultery.</note>

> If the lords of the tenth, second, and seventh houses are in the tenth house, the native is a paramour. If the lords of the fifth, ninth, and seventh houses—being indicators of children—are in "bad places" <note>the 6th, 8th, or 12th houses</note>, and the fifth house is aspected by malefics, the person will be childless. If Jupiter and Mercury, or the Moon and Venus, are in the seventh house, the native is devoted to many women. If a strong Venus is in the seventh house, the native is the husband of many wives. || 4 ||

**Commentary:** "If the lords of the tenth, second, and seventh houses..." are in the tenth house <note>the house of profession/public life</note>, the native becomes a "paramour" <note>original: *jara*</note>. If the lords of the fifth <note>children</note>, ninth <note>fortune</note>, and seventh <note>marriage</note> are in "dusthanas" <note>unfortunate positions</note> and the fifth house is viewed by malefics, the person will be without offspring. As stated in the **Sarvartha Chintamani**:
> "The lords of the 10th, 2nd, and 7th in the 10th house are called 'paramours.' If the lords of the 5th and 9th, along with the 7th lord, are in bad houses, weak, and not seen by benefics, while the 5th house is aspected by malefics, the sages say this is a yoga for childlessness despite having many wives."

Regarding "Jupiter and Mercury...": If Jupiter and Mercury, or the Moon and Venus, are in the seventh house, the native is attached to various women. If a strong Venus <note>full of planetary strength</note> is in the seventh house, the native becomes the husband of many wives. Whoever has a powerful Venus in the seventh house at birth will have many women. || 4 ||

<note>The Hindi text at the bottom breaks off, repeating that 10th, 2nd, and 7th lords in the 10th house make one a paramour, and childlessness results from the 5th, 9th, and 7th lords being in "evil" houses.</note>

...that there may be no offspring. If Jupiter, Mercury, or the Moon are in the seventh house, one enjoys many women. If a strong Venus is in the seventh house, one becomes the husband of many wives. ॥ 4 ॥

> If Venus and Mars are in the seventh house, one is without a wife; likewise if they are in the ninth or fifth houses.
> If the Moon and Venus are in the house of enemies <note>the 6th house</note>, there may be only one son.
> If malefic planets are in the first, seventh, and twelfth houses while a weak Moon is in the fifth,
> the man born becomes the husband of a barren woman or is left without a wife entirely. ॥ 5 ॥

**Venus and Mars:** If Venus and Mars are located in the seventh house, the person born is "without a wife" (meaning his wife has passed away). If those same two, Venus and Mars, are in the ninth or fifth houses, the result is the same: he will be without a wife. Thus it is said in the *Saravali* <note>A classic 8th-century astrological text by Kalyanavarman</note>:
-> "A man born with Mars and Venus in the seventh house has a distressed or missing wife." <-
-> "The wise should conclude the same if they are in the fifth or ninth houses." <-

**In the house of enemies:** If the Moon and Venus are in the house of enemies (the sixth house), the person born will have only one son. **In the first, seventh, etc.:** If malefic planets are situated in the first, seventh, and twelfth houses, and the Moon is weak (waning) and placed in the fifth house, the man born becomes the husband of a "barren woman" (a woman who cannot conceive), or he remains without a wife. In this planetary combination, the man's wife is barren, or the man himself remains without a partner. Thus it is said in the *Saravali*:
-> "With malefics in the first, twelfth, and seventh, and a waning Moon in the fifth," <-
-> "A man certainly becomes wifeless and is deprived of sons." ॥ 5 ॥ <-

If Venus and Mars are in the seventh, the person is without a wife. Know the same result if they are in the ninth or fifth. If the Moon and Venus are in the enemy's house <note>6th</note>, the person has one son. If malefic planets are in the first, seventh, and twelfth and a weak Moon is in the fifth, the person is the husband of a barren woman or is without a wife. ॥ 5 ॥

> The husband of a barren woman is one where Venus and the Sun are in the seventh or first house. If the Moon is in the Ascendant in an even sign, he has the appearance of a woman. ॥
> If in a masculine sign, the wife has masculine traits. If aspected by or joined with both male and female planets, the form is mixed. ॥ 6 ॥

**Husband of a barren woman:** If Venus and the Sun are in the seventh or the first house, the person born becomes the husband of a barren woman. **Moon in the Ascendant:** If the Moon is in the Ascendant (first house) and it is an even sign (2, 4, 6, 8, 10, or 12), the man born has a "feminine appearance" (a womanly nature). **In a masculine sign:** If the Moon in the Ascendant is in a masculine sign (1, 3, 5, 7, 9, or 11), the man's wife will have "masculine traits" (a male-like appearance). If that same Moon in the Ascendant is aspected by or joined with both a female and a male planet, the form is "mixed" (a combination of male and female traits). In this case, if the Moon is in an even sign, the man has a mixed appearance; if in an odd sign, the wife has a mixed appearance. ॥ 6 ॥

If Venus and the Sun are in the seventh or first, the person is the husband of a barren woman. If the Moon is in the Ascendant in an even sign, the person has a womanly form. If in a masculine sign (odd house), the wife has a masculine form. If aspected by mixed planets, the form is mixed. ॥ 6 ॥

> If the seventh house from the Ascendant, or the birth sign of women, falls in a Navamsha <note>a 1/9th divisional chart</note> of Mars or a sign of Mars,
> the wife will be a servant, or if in the Navamsha of a low or combust planet, she will be wicked or lose her husband in her youth. ॥ 7 ॥

**In the portion of Mars:** From the Ascendant (the man's birth chart), if the seventh house, or for women, the birth sign, falls in a Navamsha of Aries or Scorpio (the signs of Mars), or in a sign of Mars...

If the sign is Aries or Scorpio <note>original: "Rashau = Mesha-Vrishchika-anyatara-rashau"</note>, the wife <note>Jaya</note> becomes a servant <note>Dasi</note>. This means: if in a man's seventh house there is a Navamsha <term>Navamsha|A 1/9th division of a zodiac sign used for fine-tuned analysis</term> of Mars or a sign of Mars, his wife will be like a servant. Similarly, if in a woman's birth ascendant there is a Navamsha or sign of Mars, that woman will be a servant. > If the Navamsha or sign of Mars is in the 7th house from a man's birth ascendant, or in a woman's birth ascendant, the wife will be a servant. If the Navamsha of a planet in its fall or a combust planet is there, the wife will be wicked or a widow in her youth. || 7 ||

->**If in a sign or Navamsha of a benefic, she is endowed with good qualities; if aspected by benefics, the wife is most beautiful.**<-
->**Born in a Navamsha of the Moon or a sign of a weak Moon, she kills her husband; but if the Moon is strong, she is virtuous.**<- || 8 ||

"In a sign or Navamsha of a benefic": In that same 7th house for a man, or the 1st house for a woman, if there is a benefic Navamsha or a benefic sign, the wife (or the woman born) is endowed with excellent qualities. Furthermore, if in that 7th or 1st house there is a benefic sign/Navamsha and it is aspected <note>Drishte; "looked at" by the influence of another planet</term> by a benefic planet, the wife is exceedingly beautiful. Now, if she is born in a Navamsha of the Moon or in the sign of a weak Moon (Cancer), the woman becomes a "husband-killer" <note>Patighni; often interpreted as bringing ill-fortune to the husband</note>. However, if the Moon is strong (full or well-placed), the woman born is virtuous and devoted to her husband. || 8 ||

> If the aforementioned 7th or 1st house is in a benefic sign or Navamsha, the wife will have good qualities. If benefic planets aspect it, she will be very lovely. A woman born in the Navamsha of the Moon or a weak Moon-sign is a husband-destroyer. If born when the Moon is strong, she is virtuous. || 8 ||

->**In the Sun's Navamsha, she is unchaste; in her own exaltation sign, she is virtuous if aspected by benefics.**<-

"In the Sun's Navamsha": If the Moon <note>Shitakare</note> is situated in the ascendant or the 7th house <note>Madanabhe</note> and enters the Navamsha of Leo (the Sun's sign), the wife of the man born is unchaste <note>Kulata</note>. If that same Moon in the 1st or 7th is in its exaltation sign (Taurus) and is aspected by benefics, the wife is virtuous. However, if the Moon in the 1st or 7th is joined with planets in fall (Scorpio), in an enemy's sign, or combust by the Sun; or if it is in the <term>Drekkana|A 1/3rd division of a sign (10 degrees)</term> known as Malefic, Serpent, Bird, Noose, or Fetters <note>referencing Ch. 5, Verse 55</note>; or if it is in the <term>Riksha-sandhi|The junction points between water and fire signs (Cancer-Leo, Scorpio-Sagittarius, Pisces-Aries)</term>, the wife of the man born will be devoid of her religious vows (unfaithful) or become a widow. || 9 ||

> If the Moon is in the 1st or 7th house in the Sun's Navamsha, the wife is unchaste. If in its exaltation and aspected by benefics, she is virtuous. If it is in its fall, an enemy's house, or combust, and in the Drekkana of Malefic-Serpent-Bird-Noose-Fetters and in a sign-junction, the man's wife will be devoid of faithfulness and become a widow. || 9 ||

->**If the Lord of the Ascendant is in the 7th with a benefic, he desires a wife from a noble family.**<-
->**With malefics in the 7th, the Lord of the Ascendant brings a woman born of a low family.**<-
->**One should describe her color, form, qualities, and appearance according to the signs;**<-
->**The woman feels love for a man whose appearance matches the planet causing her ill-conduct.**<- || 10 ||

# Chapter 14: Results of the Seventh, Eighth, and Ninth Houses

**The Lord of the Ascendant in the Seventh:** If the <term>Lagnēśa</term><note>The ruling planet of the First House/Ascendant, representing the self.</note> is placed in the Seventh House in a beneficial sign and is joined by a <term>benefic planet</term><note>A naturally auspicious planet like Jupiter or Venus.</note>, the person born desires (and obtains) a wife born of a noble family. **In a Malefic Sign:** If the Lord of the Ascendant is in the Seventh House but in a <term>malefic sign</term><note>A sign ruled by a harsh planet like Mars or Saturn.</note>, he obtains a woman born of a lowly or dishonorable family. 

**Regarding the appearance of the wife:** One should describe the wife’s caste, color, form, qualities, and physical build according to the sign occupying the Seventh House and the planets associated with it. 

**Regarding infidelity:** If there is a combination for adultery in the chart, the woman will find pleasure with a man whose appearance matches the planet that causes the "wicked conduct" (the indicator of adultery) in the Seventh House. // 10 //

[The following section provides the results for various planets and "shadow planets" in the Seventh House:]

->If the Seventh House is joined by malefic or <term>invisible planets</term><note>Non-luminous mathematical points or "Upagrahas" like Dhuma or Vyatipata.</note>, the wife is of wicked conduct.<-
->If the Sun is there, she is barren; if the Moon is waning, she is unfaithful. // 11 //<-
->If Mars is there, she dies; if Saturn, she is ill-fated; if joined with Rahu,<-
->the man delights in others' wives, is indifferent to his own, lacks conception, and is childless. // 12 //<-
->With <term>Dhuma</term><note>A specific "shadow planet" or Upagraha.</note>, he remains unmarried; with <term>Kodanda</term>, he himself dies.<-
->With <term>Parivesha</term>, she is of bad character; with Ketu, she is barren but virtuous. // 13 //<-
->With <term>Kala</term>, he is without a wife; with a malefic, she suffers miscarriages.<-
->If the Moon is full, the wife is virtuous and gives birth to children. // 14 //<-
->With Mercury, she has good sons; with Jupiter, she is virtuous and has many sons.<-
->With a strong Venus, she is fortunate, wealthy, and endowed with strength. // 15 //<-

Now, the author explains the results of the planets and <term>Upagrahas</term><note>Secondary or "shadow" planets used in Vedic astrology.</note> in the Seventh House through these five verses. If the Seventh House is joined by a malefic or an "invisible" planet (as defined in Chapter 2, Verse 6), the wife of the native is attached to wicked people (immoral). If the Sun is in the Seventh, the wife is barren. If the Moon is waning, she is a "man-chaser" (unfaithful). The rest is quite clear and requires no further elaboration.

[The Hindi commentary repeats the Sanskrit results:] If Saturn is there, she is unfortunate. If Rahu is there, the man is interested in other women, indifferent to his own wife, lacks the ability to impregnate, and is childless. If Dhuma is present, he will be without marriage. If the "Bow" (Kodanda/Karmuka) is present, he dies. If Parivesha is present, she is ill-behaved. If Ketu is present, she is barren but remains a devoted wife. // 11-13 //

If Kala is in the Seventh, he is wife-less. If a malefic is there, there are miscarriages. If the Moon is full, she is well-behaved and bears daughters <note>The Sanskrit "prasūtā" implies general childbirth, while the Hindi commentary specifies daughters in this context.</note>. If Mercury is there, she has good sons. If Jupiter is there, she is virtuous and has sons. If Venus is strong, she is fortunate and a "Shrimati" (a lady of fortune). // 14-15 //

->If the Lord of the Seventh or Fifth is strong and aspected by a benefic,<-
->but is also joined or aspected by the Lord of the Sixth House,<-
->the wife obtains a son through a paramour; her husband, though having many wives, remains without a son of his own. // 16 //<-

**The Lord of the Seventh or Fifth:** If the <term>Saptamēśa</term> (Lord of the 7th) or <term>Pañcamēśa</term> (Lord of the 5th) is endowed with full strength and is seen by a benefic planet, but is also joined or aspected by the Lord of the Sixth House...

# Page 424
## Commentary on the Jataka Parijata

For the person born under this configuration, the **wife = woman, through a paramour = another man, attains the birth of a son = the production of offspring.** For that **woman, the husband = lord (the one whose birth chart possesses these specific characteristics) even if joined with many wives = accompanied by numerous women, would remain childless = without a son. The meaning is that no legitimate biological son would be born to him from any woman.**

**Notes —** If this combination appears in a woman's horoscope, then that woman attains offspring through a man other than her husband. Not by her own husband. It should be understood that if this combination is in a man's horoscope, it acts entirely as an obstacle to having children. || 16 ||

**If the lord of the seventh house <note>the house of marriage</note> or the powerful lord of the fifth house <note>the house of children</note> is aspected by a benefic planet and is with the lord of the sixth house <note>the house of enemies/debts</note>, or is aspected by the lord of the sixth, then the wife produces a son from a paramour; and even if her husband has many wives, he remains childless. || 16 ||**

> **If Jupiter is in its sign of debilitation in the seventh house, one loses their wife; similarly if Saturn is in Pisces in the seventh house.**
> **If Jupiter is in a Navamsha <note>a one-ninth division of a sign</note> belonging to Saturn or Mars, or is joined with the sons of the Sun <note>Saturn</note> or Mars, the person becomes a paramour <note>an adulterer</note>. || 17 ||**

**Debilitated etc.** When **Jupiter is in its debilitation (the sign of Capricorn) and situated in the seventh house = the house of passion, the person born becomes one who has lost his wife = a deceased spouse. This combination is possible in a Cancer ascendant. If Saturn = the son of the Sun, is in Pisces in the seventh house = the house of the wife, the result is the same, meaning the loss of the wife. This is possible in a Virgo ascendant. If Jupiter = the teacher of the gods, goes to a Navamsha of Saturn or Mars = the signs of Saturn or Mars, or is joined with the sons of the Sun or Mars = accompanied by either Saturn or Mars, the person born becomes a paramour.** Thus says Mantreshwara <note>author of the Phaladeepika</note>:

> **If Venus is in Scorpio in the seventh house, the wife dies; if Mercury is in Taurus in the seventh,**
> **there is the destruction of the wife; likewise if Jupiter is debilitated and situated in the seventh.**
> **If Saturn is in Pisces in the seventh house, or if Mars is there, the death of the wife occurs.**
> **If the Moon and Mars are in the sign of the Moon <note>Cancer</note> in the seventh, the <unclear>woman</unclear> is virtuous and beautiful. || 17 ||**

**If debilitated Jupiter is in the seventh house, his wife will die. If the seventh house is Pisces and Saturn is in it, know the result to be as previously stated. If Jupiter is in the Navamsha of Saturn or Mars, or is with Saturn or Mars, he becomes a paramour (adulterer). || 17 ||**

> **If a malefic is in the seventh or eighth house and Mars is in the twelfth,**
> **and if the lord of that house is invisible, one shall possess another wife.**
> **The first wife is born of a good family if the lord of the ascendant is joined with the lord of the seventh;**
> **if he is then overpowered by the light of the Sun, they say she is utterly lacking in beauty. || 18 ||**

**Now he describes the combination for two wives and their characteristics—in the two verses "Seventh etc." and "Born of a good family." If there is any malefic planet in the seventh or eighth house from the birth ascendant, and Mars = the son of the earth, has gone to the twelfth = the house of loss, and if the lord of that house = the lord of the house of the wife, is invisible = gone to the invisible half of the circle or is combust <note>too close to the sun to be seen</note>, the man born will be a partaker of another wife = entitled to another spouse. The meaning is that for one born in this yoga, there will be two wives. Regarding those two wives, the first wife should be known as born of a good family. This is if, in the aforementioned yoga, the lord of the ascendant = the ruler of the birth sign, is joined with the lord of the wife = the lord of the seventh house. But if the lord of the ascendant alone is overpowered by the light of the Sun = combust with the Sun, then the wise say the first wife is utterly = exceedingly, lacking in form = devoid of beauty = ugly. || 18-19 ||**

**If there is a malefic planet in the seventh or eighth and Mars is in the twelfth, and if the lord of the seventh is invisible, he will have a second wife. || 18 ||**
**If the lord of the ascendant is with the lord of the twelfth <note>Note: The Sanskrit commentary says lord of the 7th, the Hindi says 12th</note>, the first wife is born of a good family. If he is struck by the light of the sun, i.e., combust, then she is known as one devoid of beauty (ugly). || 19 ||**

> **When there are many malefics in the second house and the lord of the wife is situated likewise,**
> **and if Rahu <note>the Sanskrit text says Ketu, but Rahu is implied in some traditions</note> is in the house of enemies, he shall possess three wives. || 20 ||**

# Chapter 14: Results of the Seventh, Eighth, and Ninth Houses

### Chapter 14: Results of the Seventh, Eighth, and Ninth Houses

Now he describes the combination for having three wives—**Wealth** etc. If there is a "multitude of malefic planets" <note>original: papabahutve; referring to planets like Mars, Saturn, Rahu, or Ketu</note> in the second house from the Ascendant, and the Lord of the Seventh <term>Seventh Lord: the planet ruling the house of marriage</term> is similarly situated (meaning debilitated or combust), and Ketu is placed in the house of enemies (the sixth house), the native will possess three wives. A person born under this combination has three women. This "Three-Wife Combination" is also mentioned in the *Sarvartha Chintamani* <note>A famous 17th-century astrological treatise by Venkatesha Sharma</note>:

> "If there are many malefic planets in the second house, or if the seventh house is similarly afflicted, and its lord is aspected by malefics, one possesses three wives." || 20 ||

If many malefic planets are in the second house, the seventh lord is also joined by malefics, and Ketu is in the house of enemies (6th), the native shall have three wives. || 20 ||

->If the Lord of the Wife is in a quadrant or trine, in its exaltation, friend's sign, or its own division,<-
->or is aspected by the Lord of Action, he shall be accompanied by many women. || 21 ||<-

Now he describes the combination for many wives—*Quadrant* etc. If the Lord of the Wife (Seventh Lord) is in its exaltation, a friend's sign, or its own division <term>Varga: divisional charts used to determine planetary strength</term>, or is placed in a quadrant or trine (houses 1, 4, 7, 10, 5, or 9), or is aspected by the Lord of Action (the Tenth Lord), the man born will be "accompanied by many women," meaning he will have more than three wives. || 21 ||

If the seventh lord is in its exaltation, a friend's house, or its own division and placed in a quadrant or trine, or if the tenth lord aspects it, the native shall be joined with many women. || 21 ||

->If the Lord of the Wife is in a quadrant, aspected by a benefic planet,<-
->and in a benefic division or sign, the wife will be devoted to her vows. || 22 ||<-

Now he describes a wife devoted to her vows—*Wife* etc. If the Lord of the Wife (Seventh Lord) is in a quadrant (1, 4, 7, 10), in a benefic division <term>Navamsha: the 1/9th divisional chart</term>, or in a benefic sign, and is aspected by a benefic planet, the native's wife will be "devoted to her vows," meaning she strictly follows the rules of faithfulness to her husband. || 22 ||

If the seventh lord is in a quadrant, aspected by a benefic, and in a benefic division or sign, the native's wife will be dedicated to her vows (meaning she will be a devoted wife). || 22 ||

->If the Lord of the Wife is Mercury, joined with a malefic, in a debilitated or enemy division, in the house of enemies or destruction,<-
->placed between malefics and joined by a malefic aspect, the wife shall be a husband-killer and a destroyer of the lineage. || 23 ||<-

Now he describes a wife who kills her husband—*Lord of the Wife* etc. If Mercury <note>original: Somasuta; literally 'Son of the Moon'</note> is the Lord of the Wife (Seventh Lord) and is joined by any malefic planet, is in a debilitated or enemy division, or has gone to the house of enemies (6th) or destruction (8th), or is "between malefics" (meaning one malefic is joined with it, or one malefic is in the 2nd and another in the 12th from Mercury), or is joined by a malefic aspect, the native's wife will be a "husband-killer" (causing the husband's ruin) and a "lineage-destroyer" (uprooting the family). || 23 ||

If the seventh lord is Mercury and is with a malefic in a debilitated or enemy division, located in the 6th or 8th house, placed between malefic planets, and aspected by a malefic, his wife will be a husband-killer and a destroyer of the family. || 23 ||

->If the Lord is in a benefic division and aspected by a benefic, the wife is from a good family.<-
->If he is mounted by a malefic in a malefic division, his wife is from a bad family. || 24 ||<-

The meaning is clear. || 24 ||

If the seventh lord is in a benefic division and aspected by a benefic, the wife will be from a good lineage. If the seventh lord is with a malefic in a malefic division, his wife will be born of a bad lineage. || 24 ||

->In the house of desire, with planets, they tell the number of wives by the planets joined with Venus;<-
->a planet in its exaltation is not counted, nor are those joined with Venus...<-
