# On the Jataka Parijata with Commentary

-> If the Lord of the Seventh House is in a sign of Venus and situated in the Second House, the number of wives is equal to the number of planets conjoined with Venus. <-
-> Or, the native becomes the beloved of as many new brides as there are planets conjoined with Venus and the Lord of the Seventh House. ॥ 25 ॥ <-

Now the author describes the number of wives: "In the place of desire..." etc. When the <term>place of desire</term><note>The Seventh House, which governs marriage and partnerships.</note> is occupied by planets, the number of wives is said to be equal to the number of planets conjoined with Venus. The meaning is this: if there is a planet in the Seventh House, then there will be as many wives as there are planets associated with Venus. However, a planet that is in its own sign or in its sign of exaltation among those conjoined with Venus is not to be counted. As it is said, "they state the number of wives by the planets conjoined with Venus," the implication is that a planet in its own sign or exaltation should be excluded from the tally. The word "or" (<note>Sanskrit: *va*</note>) in the verse seems to indicate an alternative opinion which should be considered.

"The Lord of the Seventh..." etc. When the Lord of the Seventh House is in a sign of Venus (either Taurus or Libra) and is located in the <term>House of Wealth</term><note>The Second House, which also relates to the family unit.</note>, the number of wives should be declared as equal to the number of planets conjoined with Venus. Alternatively, the native becomes the husband of as many new brides as there are planets conjoined with both Venus and the Lord of the Seventh House. ॥ 25 ॥

<margin>If the Seventh House is occupied by planets, scholars say the number of wives equals the planets with Venus. Exalted planets are not counted. If the Seventh Lord is in a house of Venus (2nd or 7th sign) and in the 2nd house (e.g., Aries Ascendant with Venus in Taurus, or Virgo Ascendant with Jupiter in Libra), count the planets with Venus. Or, the number of new wives equals the planets with Venus and the Seventh Lord.</margin>

-> As many weak planets as are conjoined with the Lord of the Seventh or the Lord of the Second, <-
-> if they are lords of "evil houses," they cause the destruction of that many wives. <-
-> As many as are strong and auspicious, they provide happiness from that many wives. <-
-> If only one planet is endowed with strength, there may be only one wife. ॥ 26 ॥ <-

"By the Lord of the Seventh..." etc. As many weak planets (lacking strength) as are conjoined with the Lord of the Seventh or the Lord of the Second, if they are also lords of <term>evil houses</term><note>Dusthanas: the 6th, 8th, or 12th houses, usually associated with loss or suffering.</note>, they will cause the loss of that many wives. However, as many planets as are strong, auspicious, lords of good houses, or placed in good houses, and are conjoined with the Seventh or Second lords, they provide happiness from that many wives. Furthermore, if only one strong planet is conjoined with the Seventh or Second lord, the man born will have only one wife.

Notes—The number of wives should be declared based on the planets in the Seventh House. Malefic planets there cause the loss of wives, while benefics provide marital happiness. Even a malefic in the Seventh becomes auspicious if it is in its own sign or exaltation. Similarly, a benefic in the Seventh becomes inauspicious if it is in its sign of depression or an enemy's sign; this must be judged carefully. As Mantreswara <note>Author of the Phaladeepika, another famous astrological text.</note> says:

> The number of wives is determined by the planets in the seventh; the loss of wives by malefics and their survival by benefics. If the Seventh Lord is strong and a benefic, the wife is virtuous and endowed with good sons. Even a malefic in its own sign in the seventh is auspicious for the wife. Benefics in the seventh, excluding the Sun, provide happiness. ॥ 26 ॥

<margin>Weak planets with the 7th or 2nd lords destroy wives, especially if they rule bad houses. Strong benefics give happiness with wives. If only one planet is strong, there is only one wife.</margin>

# Chapter 14: On the Fruits of the Seventh, Eighth, and Ninth Houses

> If Jupiter is strong and placed in a friend's <term>Navamsha</term><note>A one-ninth division of a zodiac sign, used for fine-tuning predictions</note>, the person has one wife. If in its own Navamsha, two or three wives; and if in its exaltation Navamsha, the person is the lord of many women. || 27 ||

Now the timing of the native's marriage is described: Add the longitudes of the <term>Lagnasha</term><note>Lord of the Ascendant/First House</note> and the Lord of the Seventh House. When Jupiter, in its transit, passes through the resulting sign and degree, the marriage of the native should be predicted. Alternatively, take the longitude of the <term>Nakshatra</term><note>Lunar mansion</note> occupied by the Moon at birth and add it to the longitude of the Lord of the Seventh House. When Jupiter in transit reaches the resulting Navamsha, the marriage of the native should be predicted.

Regarding having a single wife: If at the time of birth, Jupiter is strong (possessing the strengths mentioned previously) and situated in a friend's Navamsha, the native is joined with one wife.

Regarding two or three wives: If strong Jupiter is in its own Navamsha (meaning the Navamsha of Sagittarius or Pisces), the native has two or three wives.

Regarding many wives: If that same strong Jupiter is in its exaltation Navamsha (the Navamsha of Cancer), the native becomes the lord of many women—meaning he has many wives. || 27 ||

-> When Jupiter in transit is in a sign equal to the sum of the longitudes of the Lord of the First House and the Lord of the Seventh House, marriage is said to occur. Or, when Jupiter is in the degree resulting from the sum of the Moon's mansion and the Lord of the Seventh House, marriage is predicted. If Jupiter is in a friend's Navamsha, there is one wife. In its own Navamsha, two or three wives. In its exaltation Navamsha, he is the master of many wives. || 27 || <-

> Marriage occurs during the <term>Dasha</term><note>Planetary period</note> of the stronger of the two: the lord of the sign or the lord of the Navamsha where the Seventh Lord is placed; or during the Dasha of the stronger between Venus and the Moon. This happens when Jupiter is in a <term>Trikona</term><note>A trine position: 1st, 5th, or 9th house</note> from the sign or Navamsha occupied by the Lord of the Seventh House. || 28 ||

Now another method for knowing the time of marriage is described: Look at the lord of the sign and the lord of the Navamsha where the Seventh Lord is situated. During the Dasha of whichever of these two is stronger, or during the Dasha of the stronger between Venus and the Moon, marriage (the "taking of the hand") should be predicted when Jupiter moves into a trine (5th or 9th position) from the sign or Navamsha occupied by the Lord of the Seventh House.

<note>Notes — Here, one should take the side of whichever is stronger between the Ascendant and the Moon. That is, if the Moon is stronger, then the Dasha of the stronger between Venus and the Moon is used. If the Ascendant is stronger, then the Dasha of the stronger between the lords of the sign and Navamsha where the Seventh Lord is placed is accepted. This is because the consideration of houses is prescribed from either the Ascendant or the Moon.</note>

Marriage is predicted during the Dasha of the stronger between the lords of the sign and Navamsha where the Seventh Lord resides, or the stronger of Venus and the Moon, when Jupiter is in a trine from the sign/Navamsha joined with the Seventh Lord. || 28 ||

> The period or sub-period of the Seventh Lord joined with Venus grants marriage. The taking of the hand also occurs in the period or sub-period of the lord of the seventh house from that sign. Marriage occurs in the periods of the lords of the tenth and fourth houses, or in the period of a planet joined with the Seventh Lord or situated in the seventh house. || 29 ||

Now other timings for marriage are described: The <term>Bhukti</term><note>Sub-period within a major planetary Dasha</note> of the Lord of the Seventh House when joined with Venus grants marriage. This means if at the time of birth the Seventh Lord is with Venus, marriage occurs during the Dasha or sub-period of that Seventh Lord.

<note>original: "सप्तमेश" (Lord of the 7th), "लग्नेश" (Lord of the 1st), "नवांश" (9th division), "गोचर" (Transit), "बृहस्पति" (Jupiter), "शुक्र" (Venus), "चन्द्र" (Moon), "त्रिकोण" (Trine), "विवाह" (Marriage), "कलत्र" (Wife/7th house), "द्यूनप" (Lord of the 7th), "पाणिग्रह" (Marriage/taking the hand), "भुक्ति" (Sub-period)</note>

<header>From the Jataka Parijata with Commentary</header>

**From the Ascendant:** The marriage <note>original: "panigraha," literally "taking the hand"</note> should be predicted during the major or minor planetary periods <note>term: Dasha-Bhukti (the chronological system of planetary influences in Indian astrology)</note> of the lord of the sign occupied by the lord of the second house <note>the house of wealth and family</note> from the birth ascendant.

**Action and Longevity:** Marriage should also be declared during the periods of the lord of the tenth house <note>house of action/karma</note> and the lord of the eighth house <note>house of longevity</note>.

Alternatively, if a planet situated in the house of the spouse <note>the 7th house</note> is joined with the lord of desire <note>the 7th lord</note>, then marriage should be predicted during the minor period of that planet situated in the seventh. It should be understood that these yogas <note>astrological combinations</note> are mentioned here in order of importance. || 29 ||

<gloss>The period of the 7th lord joined with Venus causes marriage. Marriage occurs in the period of the lord of the sign occupied by the 2nd lord. Marriage occurs sequentially in the periods of the 10th and 8th lords. Or, declare marriage in the period of a planet situated in the 7th house joined with the 7th lord.</gloss>

->A benefic planet situated in a favorable sign gives prosperity at the beginning;<-
->A benefic planet in a malefic sign gives marriage etc. in the middle of the period.<-
->A cruel planet in a malefic sign gives results at the end of the ripening;<-
->In a benefic sign, it gives results at all times; joined with a benefic, it is auspicious. || 30 ||<-

Now, the timing of results is explained based on the auspicious or inauspicious nature and placement of the planets. **A benefic planet:** If a benefic planet is placed in a favorable sign, it gives prosperity and auspicious wealth (such as marriage) at the very beginning of its major period. **A benefic planet:** If a benefic planet is placed in a malefic sign, it gives marriage and other good results in the middle of its period. **A cruel planet:** If a malefic planet is in a malefic sign, it gives results like marriage at the end of its "ripening" <note>the conclusion of the planetary period</note>. If a cruel planet is in a benefic sign, it should be known to give results throughout the entire period. If a cruel planet is joined with a benefic, it becomes auspicious.

**Notes**—The timing mentioned in the previous verse regarding "marriage in the Dasha-Bhukti" is further refined in this verse. One should observe the placement of the planet causing the marriage and then declare the timing. Here, "marriage" is just an illustration; the conclusion is that for all house inquiries, the results should be predicted based on the condition of the significator of that house. || 30 ||

<gloss>A benefic planet in a favorable house gives good results early in the period. A benefic in a malefic sign gives marriage in the middle. A malefic in a malefic house gives results at the end. A malefic in a favorable sign gives results throughout. If joined with a benefic, it is good.</gloss>

->When the Moon and Jupiter transit the sign of the lord of the Navamsha occupied by the Ascendant lord, marriage occurs.<-
->Or when Jupiter and the Moon transit the sign of the 7th lord or Venus, or are in a quadrant joined with Jupiter. || 31 ||<-

Now another timing for marriage is described. **Lord of the Ascendant:** Find the Navamsha <note>term: Navamsha (the 1/9th divisional chart used to assess the hidden strength of planets and marriage)</note> occupied by the lord of the birth ascendant. When the Moon and Jupiter <note>original: "Purandara-guru," the teacher of the gods</note> transit through the sign owned by that Navamsha lord, one should know it as the time of obtaining a spouse for the native. Alternatively, when Jupiter <note>original: "Amara-mantri," the minister of the immortals</note> and the Moon transit the sign where the 7th lord or Venus is located, or when they are in a quadrant (1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses) from the birth ascendant and joined with Jupiter, one should predict the gain of a wife.

**Notes**—This must also be adjusted according to the person's age. One should not predict the result based solely on the transit of Jupiter. || 31 ||

# Chapter 14: Results of the Seventh, Eighth, and Ninth Houses

If the Moon and Jupiter are in the 2nd sign from the lord of the Navamsha <note>A 1/9th division of a zodiac sign, used for fine-tuning predictions</note> occupied by the Lord of the Ascendant, the gain of a wife is predicted. When the Moon and Jupiter are in the house of the Lord of the 7th house or Venus, and Jupiter is in a quadrant <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note> during transit, the gain of a wife occurs. || 31 ||

**The number of the sign in the 7th house, counting from Aries, indicates the year of marriage;**
**Or, adding eight years to that number after the sacred thread ceremony, the auspicious time arrives. ||**
**A woman born in the sign or Navamsha occupied by the Lord of the 7th house from the Ascendant**
**Will be the one who brings joy to her husband’s heart; and the husband likewise to the woman. || 32 ||**

The author explains another timing for marriage and the nature of the wife: *Yat* etc. The "House of Desire" (*Kamabhavanam*) refers to the 7th house. Counting from Aries (*Ajadi*), whatever number that sign holds, in that year of life, or by adding eight years (*Sashtabde*), the auspicious time (*Kalyanakala*) for marriage occurs after the sacred thread ceremony (*Maunji-karma*). For example: if the 7th house is Cancer (the 4th sign), and the sacred thread ceremony was performed in the 8th year, then the marriage should be predicted in the 12th year (4+8) or the 20th year (4+8+8) from birth.

Now, regarding the one who brings joy to the husband's heart: From the Ascendant (*Lagnat*), the 7th house is the "Setting Sign" (*Astavilagnam*). A woman born in the sign or Navamsha (*Kshetranshake*) occupied by its lord (the Lord of the 7th) will be a "delighter of her husband's mind" (*Patimanomodini*). In the same way, a husband with those characteristics will be the delighter of the woman's mind. || 32 ||

<margin>The year of marriage is the number of the 7th house from Aries, or that number plus 8 after the thread ceremony. A wife born in the Navamsha of the 7th lord brings happiness.</margin>

**A woman born in the sign of the planet that occupies or aspects the 7th house from the Moon**
**Will be exceedingly fortunate and beloved by her husband. ||**
**In a woman’s horoscope, the husband brings joy to the bride in the same way;**
**The direction of the spouse's home is determined by the strength of the lord from Venus. || 33 ||**

*Kama* etc. From the Moon at birth, the planet situated in or aspecting the 7th house—the woman born in that planet's sign will be very fortunate and dear to her husband. This means: look at the planet in the 7th house from the Moon, or the planet with the strongest aspect on it; the woman whose birth sign matches that planet's sign will be very beautiful and the husband's favorite. In a woman's birth chart, if these same conditions exist, the husband will be the one who pleases the bride's heart.

Regarding direction (*Dik*): From Venus (*Bhrigusutat*), the direction associated with the Lord of the 7th house (see Chapter 2, Verse 23) indicates the direction or country of the spouse. One should consider this: in a man's birth chart, find the lord of the 7th house from where Venus is placed; the direction assigned to that lord is the direction from which his wife will come.

## Other methods for knowing the direction of the spouse:

> **The direction may be from the sign or Navamsha occupied by Venus.**
> **Or from the 7th house from Venus, or the direction of the Lord of the wife (7th Lord).**
> **Or from the planet situated in the 7th house, or its Navamsha, or the Lord of the Ascendant.**

**One should predict the direction of the spouse's birthplace based on the planet situated in the seventh house at birth; the lord of the seventh house also indicates the husband for a woman.**
**The sign and direction of the wife are indicated by the planets occupying the house of desire <note>the 7th house</note>, the lord of that house, and Venus.** **|| 33 ||**

### Now, the Compatibility of the Bride and Groom's Horoscopes.

Now, he describes the compatibility of the groom's and bride's horoscopes in the following fourteen verses—

**Mars situated in the second, twelfth, seventh, fourth, or eighth house in a man's birth chart is a "wife-killer" <note>Daraha: indicating early loss of the spouse</note>.**
**Similarly, if Mars is placed in these same positions from the birth ascendant of a girl, it causes harm to the husband.** **|| 34 ||**

Regarding "Dhana" <note>wealth/2nd house</note> etc.: In the birth of a man, if Mars (the son of the Earth) is placed in any one of the second, twelfth, seventh, fourth, or eighth houses, that man becomes a "wife-killer," meaning his wife may not live long.

If Mars is similarly placed in the 2nd, 12th, 7th, 4th, or 8th houses from the birth ascendant of a girl, it becomes a "giver of misfortune" or a cause of death for the husband. The implication is that a girl born under this yoga <note>astrological combination</note> also becomes a destroyer of her husband. Here, Mars in the birth ascendant of both the bride and groom is said to be inauspicious. A specific traditional verse is also found here:—

-> "Mars in the first, the twelfth, the fourth, the seventh, or the eighth; <-
-> A girl causes the destruction of the husband, and a husband causes the destruction of the girl." <- **|| 34 ||**

If a man has Mars in the second, twelfth, seventh, fourth, or eighth house, he is a destroyer of his wife. Similarly, if Mars is in the 2nd, 12th, 7th, 8th, or 4th house from the girl's ascendant, she causes harm to her husband. By reading "Lagna" <note>ascendant</note> instead of "Dhana" <note>2nd house</note>, this will align with other texts. Because in other texts, the positions 1, 4, 7, 8, and 12 are seen as harmful, as stated in the verse: "Mars in the first, twelfth, fourth, seventh, or eighth." || 34 ||

**A cruel planet <note>malefic</note> situated in the eighth house from the ascendant of women,**
**If placed in its sign of debilitation, an enemy's sign, or a malefic division, causes the death of the husband.** **|| 35 ||**

Regarding "Krura" <note>cruel</note>: If any malefic planet, while being in its debilitation, an enemy's sign, or malefic divisions, is situated in the eighth house from the birth ascendant of a woman, it causes the death of her husband. || 35 ||

If a cruel planet is in the eighth house from the woman's ascendant and is in a debilitated, inimical, or malefic division, it causes the death of the husband. || 35 ||

**If two malefic planets are situated in the seventh and second houses, they cause grief born of separation from the wife.**
**But if he is joined with a spouse who possesses a similar astrological combination, he lives endowed with sons, wealth, and so on.** **|| 36 ||**

Regarding "Dyun-kutumba" <note>7th and 2nd houses</note>: If two malefic planets are situated in the seventh and second houses (one in the seventh and one in the second), then they cause grief arising from separation from the wife. This means the wife of a man born under this yoga dies. However, if that man is joined with a wife who has a "similar door of yoga"—meaning in the woman's birth chart as well, malefic planets are in the second and seventh houses—then he lives with sons, wealth, etc. The meaning is that in such a case, there is no untimely death for the couple. || 36 ||

If malefic planets are in the seventh and second houses, both will give grief caused by separation from the wife. If his wife has a similar yoga, he will live possessed of sons, wealth, etc. || 36 ||

# Chapter 14: Results of the Seventh, Eighth, and Ninth Houses

> If the wife’s birth sign is among the three signs of the spouse, or in a trine <note>A trine refers to the 1st, 5th, or 9th positions in a zodiac chart, considered very auspicious.</note> from the sign occupied by the Lord of the Seventh House, the man will be blessed with sons. If the shadow planet Dhuma is in the seventh, or if the Lord of the Seventh is in a "bad house" <note>Houses 6, 8, or 12, associated with difficulties.</note>, she will have asymmetrical breasts (one larger than the other).

## From the Commentary on Jataka Parijata

If the Sun is in the seventh house, one approaches a barren woman. If Jupiter is in the seventh, one approaches a Brahmin woman <note>original: "vipravanitām"</note>. If Venus is so placed, one approaches a pregnant woman. If the children of the Sun, the Serpent, or the Crested One—namely Saturn, Rahu, or Ketu—occupy the seventh house, one engages with a low-born woman or one who is menstruating <note>original: "rajasvalām"</note>. || 39 ||

### On the Location of Sexual Union

-> If the Sun is in the house of happiness <note>the 4th house</note>, the place of sport is a forest; if the Moon, a beautiful private home; <-
-> if the Son of Earth <note>Mars</note>, he desires a wall <note>a hut made of wood or grass</note>; if Mercury, a place of recreation. <-
-> If Jupiter, a house of God; if Venus, near water; if Saturn or the Serpent <-
-> or Ketu, the place of union with a woman is a site dear to Vishnu, Shiva, the Goddess, or their sons. <- || 40 ||

Now the text indicates the places of sexual play for the native. If the Sun is in the "happiness" position (the fourth house), a forest or wilderness is the place of union. If the Moon is in the fourth, a lovely personal residence is indicated. If Mars is in the fourth, a hut made of grass and wood is the place. If Mercury is in the fourth, a playground or park. If Jupiter is in the fourth, a house of God, such as a monastery or temple. If Venus is in the fourth, the banks of a reservoir or body of water. If Saturn, Rahu, or Ketu are in the fourth, the place of union is a temple of Vishnu, Shiva, the Goddess, or Ganesha. || 40 ||

If the Sun is in the house of happiness, the sport occurs in a forest (a place outside the home). If the Moon, sport in a beautiful home. If Mars, enjoyment in a hut. If Mercury, enjoyment in a place specifically for recreation. If Jupiter, play in a temple. If Venus, sport near water. If Saturn, Rahu, or Ketu, one performs union in the temples of gods like Vishnu, Shiva, Devi, or Ganesha. || 40 ||

-> If Mars is in the seventh in a subdivision <term>Navamsha: a 1/9th division of a sign</term> of Venus, and the Lord of Desire <note>7th Lord</note> is in the fifth, <-

-> If the Lords of Desire and Family <note>7th and 2nd Lords</note> are with Venus in "bad houses" or the third, <-

Now the text describes the auspicious and inauspicious fates of the spouse. If Mars is in a subdivision of Venus while situated in the seventh house, and the Lord of the seventh is in the fifth, the native's wife suffers hardship. If the Sun is in the seventh, he gains wealth through his wife.

If the Lords of the 7th and 2nd houses are joined with Venus and placed in "bad houses" (the 6th, 8th, or 12th) or the 3rd house, then he destroys as many wives as indicated by the house number. However, if the Lords of the 2nd and 7th are endowed with strength, the native will possess wives <note>meaning the wives will live</note>. || 41 ||

If Mars is in the seventh in the Navamsha of Venus, and the 7th Lord is in the 5th, the wife suffers. If the Sun is in the 7th, he has the happiness of a wife. If the 7th and 2nd Lords are with Venus in a bad house or the 3rd, there is loss of that many wives. If the 2nd and 7th Lords are strong, the wife remains living. || 41 ||

# On the Yoga of Genital Kissing

The person born under this alignment practices genital kissing if the Lord of the 7th house <note>The 'Lord of the 7th' is the planet ruling the house of marriage and partnerships.</note> is aspected by or joined with Venus, or is placed in a sign owned by Venus <note>Taurus or Libra</note>. The same result occurs if the Lord of the 2nd house <note>The house of the family and mouth</note> is similarly situated. Likewise, if the Lord of the 10th house is with Venus and placed in the 7th house, this result follows. || 42 ||

Now the author describes the *Bhagachumbana Yoga* <note>original: "भगचुम्बनयोगः"; a specific astrological combination indicating oral-genital contact</note>—"The person born..." etc. 1. If the Lord of the 7th house is aspected by Venus or is placed anywhere in a house of Venus (either Taurus or Libra), the person born practices genital kissing. According to this definition, the man born will kiss the female genitalia. 2. If the Lord of the 2nd house (the Lord of the family/mouth) is possessed of the aforementioned characteristics (aspected by or joined with Venus, or in a house of Venus), the same occurs, meaning the person practices genital kissing. Furthermore, 3. if the Lord of the 10th house is joined with Venus and placed in the 7th house (the house of the spouse), the same result follows. || 42 ||

# On the Examination of the Woman’s Genitalia

> If the Lord of the 7th house is Jupiter or Venus, the young woman’s genitalia will be symmetrical and very beautiful. The genitalia will be small if the Lord of the 7th house is situated between Saturn, the Moon, and Mercury. || 43 ||

The woman’s secret parts will be moist if the Moon is in the 7th house and aspected by Venus; however, if joined with a malefic planet, they will be dry. || 44 ||

Now the author describes the examination of the genitalia of the native's wife—"The Lord of Desire..." etc. If Jupiter or Venus is the Lord of the 7th house (the house of desire), then the woman’s genitalia will be symmetrical—neither too small nor too large—and very "smooth" or beautiful. This combination is possible when the Ascendant is either Aries, Scorpio, Gemini, or Virgo. If the Lord of the 7th house is placed between Saturn, the Moon, and Mercury, the woman’s genitalia will be small in size. || 43 ||

"Large..." etc. If the Lord of the 7th house is in a water sign (the latter half of Capricorn, Pisces, or Cancer), the genitalia will be large in size. If the significator of the 7th house (Venus) is also in a water sign, the same result of large genitalia occurs.

**On Moisture:** When the Moon is situated in the seventh house <note>the house of marriage and the spouse</note> and is aspected by <note>viewed by</note> Venus, the female organ becomes moist or lubricated. ->**When Jupiter enters the house of the lord of the Navamsha occupied by the Lord of the Ascendant, one obtains a wife.**<-

**On the Lord of the Ascendant:** When Jupiter <note>Sanskrit: *Jiva*</note> enters the house belonging to the lord of the <term>Navamsha: a 1/9th divisional chart used for marriage</term> in which the Lord of the Ascendant is placed, the person obtains a wife.

When Jupiter travels through the resulting sign or its trines <note>1st, 5th, or 9th positions</note>, or when the longitude of the Seventh House is subtracted from the Ascendant and Jupiter reaches that resulting sign, one should predict the death of the native's wife. || 45 ||

When Jupiter is in the house of the Navamsha lord where the Lord of the Ascendant resides, a wife is obtained. If the Lord of the Ascendant is in a debilitated or enemy Navamsha, the wife may die or the man remains single. Subtracting the Ascendant from the clear longitude of the Seventh Lord gives a remainder; when Jupiter is in a trine from that sign, or when the Seventh Lord is subtracted from the Ascendant and Jupiter is in that remainder, the wife's death is predicted. || 45 ||

->**If the Seventh Lord and the significator are benefics and the Seventh House is very strong,**<-
->**The woman meets her death along with her husband, provided there are no malefic influences.**<-

->**A sign indicated by the Venus-Ashtakavarga, and Jupiter is in a corresponding division, the wife's death occurs. || 46 ||**<-

**From the Ascendant:** If the Lord of the Seventh and the significator <note>Venus for a wife</note> are both benefic planets and are in the seventh house, and if the seventh house is endowed with full strength and is free from the association or gaze of malefic planets, the woman <note>Sanskrit: *Abala*</note> meets her death at the same time as her husband. The meaning is that in this alignment, the couple dies together.

**Describing the death of the spouse:** During the <term>Dasha-Apahara: planetary period and sub-period</term> of the lord of the 8th house from the 7th (the "vulnerable" planet), and when Saturn <note>Sanskrit: *Bhanusuta*, son of the Sun</note> is in a sign calculated in the <term>Ashtakavarga: a system of points used to track transits</term> of Venus, and when Jupiter is in a corresponding division, the death of the wife will occur. || 46 ||

->This concludes the consideration of the Seventh House.<-

If the lord of the seventh house is in its own Parijata or similar division, is joined with or aspected by Jupiter, and is in an auspicious house, then the person obtains fine food with curd, honey, ghee, pulses, milk, and cooked items, and attains a lovely wife. || 47 ||

### Now, the Results of the Eighth House.

Now, desiring to explain the results of the eighth house, the author first mentions the factors to be considered and then describes the combinations for a short life—

> The lifespan and the causes of misfortune have been described through the lords of the ascendant, the tenth house, the eighth house, and Saturn; nevertheless, I shall speak again regarding the attainment of death. If there is a combination for short life, or if the lord of the eighth house is in the house of enemies <note>6th house</note> joined with malefic planets, or is joined with the lord of the ascendant and is weak, the man born will be short-lived. || 48 ||

Regarding **Lifespan** <term>Ayurdaya: the calculation of longevity</term>: Through the **lords of the ascendant, tenth, and eighth houses, and Saturn** <term>Udaya-vyoma-ayur-isha-arkajaih</term>, one should consider the lifespan of the newborn and the cause of misfortune (the cause of death); all this has been stated previously (in the chapter on longevity and Arishta), yet I shall speak again of the attainment of death. The point is that the consideration of life and death must be made through the lord of the eighth house and the eighth house itself.

Regarding short life: If the **lord of the eighth house** <term>Randhrape</term> is joined with malefic planets and is in the twelfth house, or is in the house of enemies (the sixth), the person born will have a short life. Furthermore, if the lord of the eighth house is in such a state, is weak, and is joined with the lord of the ascendant, the man born will be short-lived.

<margin>Notes—It is a general rule that whichever house's lord goes to the sixth or twelfth house, that house suffers loss. Since the eighth house is used to judge life, it is no wonder that if the eighth lord goes to the sixth or twelfth, there is a short lifespan. || 48 ||</margin>

The lifespan and causes of misfortune have been stated previously via the lords of the ascendant, tenth, and eighth houses, and Saturn; however, everything is stated again in the context of the eighth house. If the lord of the eighth house is in the twelfth or sixth house joined with a malefic planet, the native will have a short life. If the lord of the eighth house is weak in those same places (12th or 6th) and is with the lord of the ascendant, the native will be short-lived. || 48 ||

> If the lord of the eighth house is well-placed, there is long life. If the lords of the ascendant and the eighth house are both in the sixth or the twelfth, the man born attains long life and strength. If the lords of the tenth, the ascendant, and the eighth are in the angles, trines, or the eleventh house, there is long life; if they are weak, one should predict a short life. || 49 ||

Now he describes the combinations for long life—Regarding "well-placed": If the lord of the eighth house is "well-placed," meaning in its own sign (here, if either the Sun or Moon is the eighth lord, "well-placed" means in the eighth house itself), the person born will be long-lived.

If the **lords of the ascendant and the eighth house** <term>Udayacchidradhipau</term> are in the sixth or the twelfth house, then the man born attains the strength of a long life.

If the lords of the tenth, the ascendant, and the eighth houses are placed in the angles, trines, or the eleventh house (1, 4, 7, 10, 5, 9, 11), then the person born will have a long life.

<note>The following technical terms were used in this section:</note>
**Seventh House** (marriage), **Eighth House** (longevity/death), **Lord of the Eighth** (Randhrape), **Lifespan** (Ayurdaya), **Lord of the Ascendant** (Lagnesha), **Lord of the Tenth** (Dashamesha), **Short Life** (Alpayu), **Long Life** (Chirayu/Dirghajivi), **Weak** (Vibala), **In the house of enemies** (Ripugate/6th house), **In the house of loss** (Vyayage/12th house), **Angles** (Kendra), **Trines** (Trikona).

## With Commentary on Jataka Parijata

Now he describes short life—**Weak**, etc. If these same planets, as previously mentioned, are with the son of the Sun <note>original: "Suryaputra" (Saturn)</note> and are weak (lacking strength), then one should predict a short life. In such a case, the person born will have a short lifespan. || 49 ||

> If the Lord of the 8th house is in its own place, there is long life. If both the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the 8th are in the 6th or 12th houses, the native will have a long life. If the Lords of the 10th, the Ascendant, and the 8th are placed in a Quadrant <term>Kendra: houses 1, 4, 7, 10</term>, a Trine <term>Trikona: houses 1, 5, 9</term>, or the 11th house, there is long life. If they are with Saturn, predict a short life. || 49 ||

---

**If the Lord of the 10th, the Lord of the 8th, and the Lord of the Ascendant are powerful and free from association with the son of the Sun (Saturn), the native lives long. If only two are very strong, there is middle life; if only one is strong, a shorter life; and if none are strong, there is no life (very short). || 50 ||**

Now he explains the combinations for long, middle, short, and very short life—**Lord of the 10th**, etc.
**Long Life (Chirayu):** If the Lord of the 10th, the Lord of the 8th, and the Lord of the Ascendant <note>original: "Karmesha-Randhra-Tanupa"</note> are all full of strength and are free from association with the son of the Sun <note>original: "Inanandana" (Saturn)</note>, then the native is long-lived. It should be understood here that even if they are full of strength, if they are joined with Saturn, they do not grant such a long life.
**Middle Life (Madhyayu):** If among these three (Lords of the 10th, 8th, and Ascendant), any two are extremely strong, then there will be a middle lifespan.
**Short Life (Alpayu):** If among these three, only one is strong, then there is a shorter life—meaning a very short or limited lifespan.
**No Life/Very Short (Hinayu):** Otherwise, if none of them are strong—meaning the Lords of the Ascendant, 8th, and 10th are all weak—then there is "no life," meaning a very deficient lifespan. || 50 ||

> If the Lords of the 10th, 8th, and Ascendant are strong and there is no association with Saturn, the native is long-lived. If two of these are very strong, there is middle life. If one is strong, there is short life. If none of the three are strong, there is no life. || 50 ||

---

**If the Lord of the 8th is in a house of a malefic planet, or in a bad house <term>Dusthana: houses 6, 8, 12</term> joined with malefics, there is short life. If joined with benefics, in a favorable sign, or aspected by benefics while in the 8th, there is long life. || 51 ||**

Now he describes the combinations for short and long life—**Lord of the 8th**, etc. The meaning is clear. || 51 ||

> If the Lord of the 8th is in a malefic planet's sign, in a bad house, or joined with a malefic, there is short life. If that same planet is with a benefic in a good sign, or is in the 8th house aspected by a benefic, there is long life. || 51 ||

---

**If the Lord of the Ascendant or the Lord of the 8th is in the house of destruction (8th), joined or aspected by a malefic, combust, invisible, or in the house of an enemy, the native's life is gone (very short).**
**There is long life if the Lord of the Ascendant is in its own exaltation, joined with a benefic, or in a Quadrant or Trine; or if the Lord of the 8th is in the 8th and the Lord of the Ascendant is in the Ascendant. || 52 ||**

**In the house of destruction**, etc. If the <term>Tanupa</term> (Lord of the Ascendant) or the <term>Nidhanapa</term> (Lord of the 8th) is in the <term>Nashastha</term> (8th house), joined or aspected by any malefic, or is "blinded" <note>original: "Mudha" (combust)</note>—meaning it has become invisible by being within the degrees of the Sun—or is in the <term>Ripugriha</term> (6th house/enemy's house), the native is <term>Gatayu</term> (devoid of life), meaning they will not live long.
Now for **Long Life (Chirayu):** If that same Lord of the Ascendant or Lord of the 8th is joined with a benefic, is in its own exaltation <note>original: "Nijatunga"</note>, or is placed in a Quadrant or Trine, there is long life. Alternatively, if the Lord of the 8th is in the 8th and the Lord of the Ascendant is in the Ascendant (1st house), the native will be long-lived. || 52 ||

> If the Lord of the Ascendant is in the 8th, or the Lord of the 8th is joined with or aspected by a malefic and is combust or in an enemy's house, the native is without life. If the Lord of the 8th is in its exaltation sign joined with a benefic, or in a Quadrant/Trine, there is long life. Or, if the Lord of the 8th is in the 8th and the Lord of the Ascendant is in the 1st, the native is long-lived. || 52 ||

# Chapter 14: Results of the Seventh, Eighth, and Ninth Houses

If the lord of the <term>twelfth house</term><note>original: "antya-griha"</note> from the <term>Ascendant</term><note>original: "Lagna"; the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</note> is strong and placed in its own sign, the person born will be long-lived and happy. Likewise, if the lord of the Ascendant and the lord of the <term>eighth house</term><note>original: "randhra-pa"</note> are both strong and situated in <term>cardinal houses</term><note>original: "Kendra"; the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note>, the same result follows. If the <term>tenth house</term><note>original: "meshuranam"</note> from the eighth house of the <term>conception chart</term><note>original: "adhana-udaya-rashi"</note>, or the <term>Moon sign at birth</term><note>original: "janmabham"</note>, is aspected by or associated with Venus, Mercury, or Jupiter, the person will enjoy a long life and good health. || 53 ||

**Commentary:** Regarding the above: If the lord of the twelfth house from the Ascendant is strong and occupies its own sign, the native will be long-lived and happy. If the lord of the Ascendant and the lord of the eighth house are both strong and positioned in cardinal houses, then similarly, the native will be long-lived and happy.

From the Ascendant at the time of conception, or from the eighth house of the birth chart, the tenth house—or the Moon's sign at birth—if it is aspected by or joined with any of Venus, Mercury, or Jupiter, then the person will possess longevity and health. || 53 ||

> *If the lord of the 12th is strong in its own sign from the Ascendant, the native is long-lived and happy. If the lords of the 1st and 8th are strong and in centers, the result is the same. If the 10th sign from the 8th house of the conception-Ascendant, or the birth-Ascendant, is aspected by or joined with Venus, Mercury, or Jupiter, the native is long-lived and healthy.* || 53 ||

---

### Now, the Consideration of Death

If the lord of the eighth house is placed in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth houses, death occurs during its <term>major or minor planetary period</term><note>original: "paka-bhukti"</note>. Death may also be predicted during the major period of the lord of the sign occupied by Saturn, specifically during the minor period of the lord of the eighth house. Or, death may occur during the major period of the lord of the eighth house, in the minor period of a planet associated with it. One should declare all this after carefully weighing the strength and weakness of the planets. || 54 ||

**Commentary:** Now the consideration of death is performed:

1. When the lord of the eighth house is situated in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth houses, one should predict death for the native during the major or minor period of that eighth-house lord.

2. During the major period of the lord of the sign where Saturn was placed at the time of birth, and during the minor period of the lord of the eighth house, one should likewise predict the native's death.

3. Alternatively, during the major period of the lord of the eighth house, and the minor period of a planet joined with that eighth-house lord, one should predict the native's death.

In these three mentioned combinations, one must consider the strength and weakness of the planets causing the "death-combination," and after careful analysis, declare death during the specific major and minor periods where it is most probable. || 54 ||

> *If the lord of the 8th is in the 6th, 8th, or 12th house, death occurs in its period. In the major period of the lord of the sign where Saturn resides, death occurs in the minor period of the 8th lord. Or, in the major period of the 8th lord, death occurs in the minor period of a planet sitting in the 8th. Here, all results should be told after considering the strength and weakness of the planets.* || 54 ||

If the lord of the Ascendant is with Rahu <note>the North Node of the Moon</note> or with Ketu <note>the South Node of the Moon</note> and is placed in the eighth, sixth, or twelfth houses, the major period of a planet joined with the lord of the Ascendant or the lord of the eighth house brings death to the native. The major period of the lord of the sign occupied by those planets brings destruction to embodied beings, specifically in the major or minor periods of the <term>Serpent</term><note>original: "Phani"; referring to Rahu</note> that arrives first in sequence. || 55 ||

**Commentary:** Regarding the lord of the Ascendant: If the lord of the Ascendant is with Rahu or with Ketu and has gone to the eighth, sixth, or twelfth houses, the major period of a planet joined with either the lord of the Ascendant or the lord of the eighth house becomes a giver of death for the native.

# With the Commentary on Jataka Parijata

If no planet is conjoined with either the Lord of the Ascendant <note>Lagnēśa: the planet ruling the first house of the zodiac chart</note> or the Lord of the Eighth House <note>Aṣṭamēśa: the planet ruling the house of longevity and death</note>, then the period of the ruler of the sign occupied by them—meaning the period of the planet ruling the sign where the Lord of the Ascendant or the Lord of the Eighth House is placed—becomes the giver of destruction, or death, for living beings.

Now, he explains when death occurs during the aforementioned planetary periods: Among the planets causing the yoga <note>astrological combination</note>, death occurs during the sub-period <note>bhukti</note> of Rahu <note>the North Node of the Moon, referred to here as 'the serpent'</note> when it is encountered first in the sequence. It should be noted here: in the death-inflicting period, the sub-period of Rahu and others becomes the killer, not the periods prior to that. || 55 ||

If the Lord of the Ascendant is in the eighth or twelfth house, or is with Rahu or Ketu, then the period of the planet conjoined with the Lord of the Ascendant or the Lord of the Eighth House may give death. If no planet is with the Lord of the Ascendant or the Lord of the Eighth House, then the period of the ruler of the sign occupied by them causes the destruction of men. Among the aforementioned planets, death should be predicted when the sub-period of Rahu is first attained. || 55 ||

-> Among the Lords of the tenth, eighth, and first houses, and Saturn, whichever planet is weak and conjoined with Rahu, <-
-> during the period or sub-period of that planet, death occurs for men; or during the sub-period of a planet conjoined with or aspecting it. <- || 56 ||

**Commentary:** Among the four—the Lord of the Tenth, the Lord of the Eighth, the Lord of the Ascendant, and Saturn—whichever planet is powerless and conjoined with Rahu <note>original: Vidhuntuda</note>, during the period or sub-period of that planet, or in the sub-period of a planet conjoined with it or aspecting <note>looking at</note> it, the death of men should be declared. || 56 ||

When the Lord of the Tenth, Eighth, or First house, or Saturn, is weak and joined with Rahu, death occurs in that planet's period or sub-period. Or, death occurs in the sub-period of a planet that is sitting with it or casting an aspect upon it. || 56 ||

> When the Lord of the Eighth is in the eighth house, one suffers from disease during the period and sub-period of that planet.
> When the Lord of the Ascendant is in the Ascendant, one suffers bodily affliction during the period and sub-period of the Ascendant Lord.
> Afterwards, the destruction of disease, bodily comfort, and joy arise.
> If the Lord of the Eighth is endowed with strength, death occurs for living beings during the period of the Lord of the Ascendant. || 57 ||

**Commentary:** When the Lord of the Eighth <note>Nāśapati</note> is situated in the eighth house <note>Nāśa</note>, the person born attains sickness—meaning they become ill—during the period and sub-period of that planet. When the Lord of the Ascendant is in the Ascendant, the person born during the period and sub-period of the Lord of the Ascendant <note>Lagnapa</note> undergoes bodily affliction (illness).
However, between the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Eighth, if the Lord of the Eighth <note>Randhrēśa</note> is stronger, then afterwards, the destruction of sickness, bodily ease, and joy occur. Furthermore, death of the living being occurs during the period <note>Dāya</note> of the Lord of the Ascendant <note>Tanupa</note>. || 57 ||

If the Lord of the Eighth is in the eighth house, disease occurs when its period and sub-period are attained. If the Lord of the Ascendant is in the Ascendant, there is first pain in the body during its period and sub-period; afterwards, the disease is destroyed, and bodily happiness and joy occur. If the Lord of the Eighth is strong, death occurs in the period of the Lord of the Ascendant. || 57 ||

> If at the time of birth the Ascendant is weak, the periods of the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Eighth are extremely painful.
> Afterwards, great happiness is attained if the Lord of the Ascendant is endowed with strength; death occurs in the period of the Lord of the Eighth. || 58 ||

**Commentary:** If at the time of birth the Ascendant <note>Vilagna</note> is weak (powerless), the periods of the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Eighth are extremely painful or sorrowful for the native. In that situation, if the Lord of the Ascendant is endowed with full strength, great happiness follows. Likewise, death for that native will occur during the period of the Lord of the Eighth <note>Nidhanapa</note>. || 58 ||

If both are joined with any planet in a Center or Trine, death occurs in the period of the planet located in the eighth house. **59**

Also, if the Lords of the eighth and the first are joined with another planet, and that planet is the weakest among them, death is predicted during its major and minor periods. **60**

<header>Chapter 14: Results of the Seventh, Eighth, and Ninth Houses</header>

...there may be many diseases. If Mercury is in the tenth house and is joined by a very auspicious planet, the native will be full of joy and happy. || 63 ||

**In the Head-rising signs, starting with the Moveable ones, during the periods of the Lord of Wealth, the Lord of the Ascendant, or the Serpent;**
**In the Back-rising signs, during the periods of the Lord of the Decanate, or those who aspect or are joined with it, one should predict death. || 64 ||**

Now he describes the consideration of death according to the Moveable and other signs in the Ascendant — *In the Head-rising signs* <note>original: "shirshodayeshu"</note> etc. When Head-rising signs (see Chapter 1, Verse 14) are in the Ascendant, then in the Moveable, Fixed, and Dual signs respectively—one should predict death during the major or sub-periods <note>term: "dashapahare" — planetary periods and sub-periods that determine the timing of events</note> of the Lord of Wealth <note>the 2nd house lord</note>, the Lord of the Ascendant <note>the 1st house lord</note>, or the Serpent <note>original: "bhujagasya" — a poetic term for Rahu, the North Node of the Moon</note>. This is what is meant: among Gemini, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, and Aquarius, if Libra is the Ascendant, death occurs in the period of the 2nd lord; if Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius is the Ascendant, in the period of the Ascendant lord; if Gemini or Virgo is the Ascendant, in the period of Rahu.

Now, if there is a Back-rising sign <note>original: "prishtodaye"</note>—Taurus, Cancer, Aries, Sagittarius, or Capricorn (see Chapter 1, Verse 14)—in the Ascendant, then one should predict death during the period of the Lord of the Decanate <note>term: "drekkana" — a 10-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign</note> occupying the Ascendant, or the period of those planets aspecting or joined with that Decanate lord. Here too, a threefold division is implied based on Moveable signs etc.: if Aries, Cancer, or Capricorn is the Ascendant, death occurs in the period of the Lord of the Ascendant's Decanate; if Taurus is the Ascendant, in the period of the planet aspecting the Decanate lord; if Sagittarius is the Ascendant, in the period of the planet joined with the Decanate lord.

Notes — Here, if there is no aspect or conjunction of planets with the Lord of the Ascendant's Decanate, then only that Decanate lord should be considered. || 64 ||

In a Head-rising sign, in Moveable etc. signs, one should predict death in the periods of the Lord of Wealth, the Lord of the Ascendant, and Rahu respectively. In a Back-rising sign, in Moveable etc. signs, one should predict death in the periods of its Decanate lord, the one aspecting it, and the one joined with it. || 64 ||

->Thus ends the consideration of the results of the Eighth House.<-

# Now, the Results of the Ninth House.
## First, the consideration of Fortune.

Now the consideration of the results of the Ninth House is undertaken. First, after stating the subjects to be considered from the Ninth House and its significator <insert>(Jupiter)</insert>, he describes the "Yoga of Fortune" <note>a specific planetary combination indicating luck</note> —

> **One should contemplate Fortune, Influence, Elders, Religion, Penance, and Auspicious deeds through the Ninth House and the Priest of the Gods.**
> **When the Lord of Fortune and the Minister of the Gods have reached auspicious divisions, and the Ninth House is joined by a benefic planet, one attains Fortune. || 65 ||**

*Fortune, Influence,* etc. From the Ninth House from the Ascendant and from the Priest of the Gods <note>original: "devapurohita" — Jupiter</note>, one should contemplate: Fortune <note>original: "bhagyam" — destiny or luck</note>, Influence <note>power/capability</note>, Elders <note>teachers and initiators</note>, Religion <note>Dharma</note>, Penance, and Auspiciousness <note>good deeds</note>. The consideration of the good or bad results of these must be made through the Ninth House and Jupiter.

If the Lord of the Ninth House and the Minister of the Gods <note>Jupiter</note> are placed in auspicious divisions <note>term: "varga" — harmonic charts used to determine planetary strength</note>, and the Ninth House is joined by a benefic planet, the person born attains Fortune—meaning great prosperity. The meaning is that one born under these characteristics will be fortunate. || 65 ||

One should consider Fortune, Influence, Elders, Religion, Penance, and Auspiciousness from the Ninth House and Jupiter. If the Lord of the Ninth and Jupiter are in auspicious divisions, and the House of Fortune is joined by a benefic planet, the native is fortunate. || 65 ||

<vocab>Head-rising (shirshodaya): signs that rise with their head first; Back-rising (prishtodaya): signs that rise with their rear first; Moveable etc. (charabhadi): the classification of signs into Moveable, Fixed, and Dual; Lord of Wealth (vittapa): the planet ruling the 2nd house; Lord of Ascendant (lagnadhipa): the planet ruling the 1st house; Serpent (bhujaga): Rahu; Decanate (drekkana): a 10-degree division of a sign; Ninth House (navamabhava): the house of luck and religion; Yoga of Fortune (bhagyayoga): a planetary combination for prosperity; Jupiter (brihaspati): the planet of wisdom and significator of the 9th house.</vocab>

### **If the planets situated in the Ninth House are malefic, in enemy signs, debilitated, or combust, the person is devoid of fame, wealth, and righteousness.**
### **However, even a malefic planet, if placed in its exaltation, own, or a friend's sign in the Ninth House, constantly grants the fruits of good fortune to men. || 66 ||**

**Malefic and Enemy:** If the <term>Grahas</term> <note>planets</note> situated in the <term>Bhagya</term> <note>the Ninth House of fortune</note> are malefic, in their enemy's house, in their sign of debilitation, or are <term>combust</term> <note>hidden by the Sun's light</note>, then the people born under this influence are devoid of fame, wealth, and <term>Dharma</term> <note>righteousness/duty</note>. On the other hand, if even a malefic planet is in its exaltation, its own sign, or a friend's sign while placed in the Ninth House, it will constantly grant fortune and prosperity to men. The established principle of almost all authorities is that any planet—whether malefic or benefic—will nourish the house it occupies if it is in its exaltation, own, or a friend's sign. || 66 ||

**If malefic planets, debilitated planets, or combust planets are in the ninth house, the native is devoid of fame, religion, and wealth. Even a malefic planet, if in an exalted position or a friend's house in the ninth, makes a man constantly fortunate. || 66 ||**

### **The Ninth House, when occupied or aspected by its own lord or a benefic, grants fortune to living beings.**
### **The lord of the sign where the Ninth Lord is placed also becomes a creator of fortune.**
### **The Ninth Lord is the "ripener" (of effects), and the lord of the fifth from it is the "awakener."**
### **If these are in exaltation or their own signs, they grant long-lasting fortune. || 67 ||**

**Benefic and Lord:** If the Ninth House is occupied or <term>aspected</term> <note>viewed by a planetary "glance"</note> by a benefic planet or by its own lord, it becomes a giver of fortune and prosperity to those born under it.

**That:** The lord of the sign in which the Ninth Lord is situated—meaning the ruler of the sign occupied by the lord of the ninth—becomes a creator of fortune. The implication is that one must judge the good or bad fortune based on the favorable or unfavorable position of the planet ruling the sign where the Ninth Lord resides.

**Ninth Lord:** The Ninth Lord planet is the "ripener" (<term>Paripachaka</term>). This means the rise of fortune is likely during the <term>Dasha</term> <note>planetary period</note> of the Ninth Lord. The lord of the fifth from the ninth house (which is the <term>Lagnesha</term> <note>Lord of the Ascendant/First House</note>) is the "awakener" (<term>Bodhaka</term>), meaning it makes the fortune known. If all these aforementioned planets (the Ninth Lord, the ruler of the sign the Ninth Lord occupies, the planets in the ninth, and the Ascendant Lord) are in exaltation or their own signs, they provide fortune for the duration of one's life. || 67 ||

**If the ninth house is joined with or aspected by its own lord or a benefic planet, it brings about the rise of fortune for the native. The lord of the sign where the Ninth Lord is placed is also a factor for fortune. The Ninth Lord is the ripener of fortune, and the fifth lord from the ninth (the Ascendant Lord) is the awakener of fortune. If all these planets are in their exalted or own signs, they make one forever fortunate. — Su. Gna. Kar. || 67 ||**

### **If five planets are in the ninth house, situated in their ten-fold divisions, exaltation, or own divisions,**
### **The native becomes a king and attains vast wealth, especially if joined or aspected by the Ninth Lord.**
### **Four powerful planets in the ninth house grant fortune;**
### **If in exaltation or own divisions, wealth comes from one's own country; if in other divisions, from elsewhere. || 68 ||**

**Of Fortune:** If a group of five planets is situated in the ninth house and these planets are in <term>Vaisheshikansha</term> <note>specific high-quality divisional dignities</note>, exaltation, their own houses, or their own <term>Navamsha</term> <note>ninth-part divisional chart</note>, and if they are joined or aspected by the Ninth Lord, the person born will be a king and attain vast fortune characterized by various types of wealth.

Furthermore, if four powerful planets are in the ninth house and are in their exaltation or own Navamsha, they grant fortune and wealth derived from one's own country. If they are in the divisions of other planets, they grant wealth obtained from other places <note>foreign lands</note>. || 68 ||

If five planets, situated in their <term>Vaisheshikansha</term><note>A specific divisional strength in Vedic astrology where a planet gains auspicious points</note>, in their sign of exaltation, in their own house, or in their own <term>Navamsha</term><note>The 1/9th divisional chart, used to determine the real strength of a planet</note>, are located in the House of Fortune (9th House) and are aspected by or conjoined with the Lord of the Ninth, the person born will be a King, possessed of much wealth, and very fortunate.

### Now, the Results of Planetary Aspects on Jupiter in the Ninth House.

From here until verse 72, the results of various planets aspecting Jupiter when it is placed in the Ninth House are described—

> If the House of Fortune is aspected by or conjoined with its own Lord or a benefic planet, fortune is certainly attained.
> If Venus or the Moon are in the Ninth House conjoined with a malefic, the person is devoted to the teacher's wife.
> If Jupiter is aspected by the Sun, one becomes a King; by Mars, a Minister; by Mercury, wealthy;
> By Venus, a master of horses; by the Moon, happy; and by Saturn, a possessor of camels and such. || 69 ||

**Regarding Fortune:** If the Ninth House is aspected by or conjoined with its own Lord (the Lord of the Ninth) or by a "beautiful" (benefic) planet, the person born certainly attains fortune; this means they become fortunate. If <term>Bhrigu</term> (Venus) or <term>Shashin</term> (the Moon) goes to the Ninth House and is conjoined with a malefic planet, the person born will be "devoted to the teacher's wife," meaning attracted to the wife of their preceptor. Thus, it is said in the *Jataka Ratna*:

> If the Moon or the son of Bhrigu (Venus) is in the House of Dharma (9th) with a malefic, one goes to the teacher's wife.
> Likewise, if the Lord of the Ninth or the Lord of its Navamsha is so conjoined, one similarly goes to such a woman.

**Regarding the aspect of the Sun:** If Jupiter is aspected by the Sun, the person born becomes a King. If aspected by the "Son of the Earth" (Mars), the person becomes a Minister <gloss>( Minister )</gloss>. If aspected by Mercury, the person becomes wealthy. If aspected by Venus, the person becomes a "Master of Horses," meaning one who possesses wealth in the form of horses. If aspected by the Moon, one will be happy. If aspected by <term>Manda</term> (Saturn), the person born will be a "possessor of camels and such," meaning they will own four-legged animals like camels.

<note>Notes—Here, if Jupiter is specifically placed in the House of Fortune, the intensity of these planetary aspect results should be declared even more strongly. || 69 ||</note>

If the House of Fortune (9th House) is conjoined with or aspected by its own Lord or a benefic planet, the person is definitely fortunate.

If Venus or the Moon, conjoined with a malefic planet, is in the House of Fortune (9th), the person may be attracted to the wife of their teacher.

If Jupiter, located in the Ninth House, is seen (aspected) by the Sun, the person becomes a King. If Mars sees Jupiter, the person becomes a Minister. If Mercury sees it, they are wealthy. If Venus sees it, they possess horses. If the Moon sees it, they are happy. If Saturn sees it, they possess camels and other four-legged animals. — *S. Sha. Kar* || 69 ||

> One is a scholar, possessing elephants, cows, and horses, when Jupiter is aspected by the Moon and Sun.
> One possesses armies, vehicles, and gems when Jupiter is in the Ninth and aspected by Mars and the Sun.
> One is abundant in knowledge, debate, wit, and wealth when seen by the Sun and Mercury.
> One has humble speech when Jupiter is in the place of penance (9th) and aspected by Venus and the Sun. || 70 ||
> One is a reservoir of virtues, wise, and owner of many villages when Jupiter is aspected by Saturn and the Sun.

> One is virtuous, a debater, and gone to a foreign land when conjoined with or aspected by the Moon and Sun—

# In the Commentary on Jataka Parijata —

> If Jupiter is in the ninth house and aspected <note>aspected: in astrology, this refers to the angular relationship between planets that "glance" at one another</note> by Venus and Mercury, the person becomes highly learned.
> If aspected by all the planets, he becomes a leader among men, a king with great wealth.
> All planets situated in the house of penance <note>the ninth house</note> bestow good fortune, conduct, kingdom, and wealth. || 72 ||

**The Scholar:** If Jupiter is in the ninth house and aspected by the Moon and the Sun, the person born is a scholar and possesses elephants, cows, horses, and wealth. If Jupiter in the ninth is aspected by Mars and the Sun, the person possesses vehicles and gems. Everything else is clear enough.

**Notes—Jupiter in the ninth house, when aspected by all planets, makes the native a king endowed with much wealth. Even there, if Jupiter is in its sign of exaltation or its own house, the results are even more extraordinary. All benefic planets in the house of fortune give a stable kingdom; naturally, malefic planets in the ninth would be obstacles to fortune—this should also be considered. || 70-72 ||**

**If the Moon and Sun aspect Jupiter situated in the ninth house, the native is a pundit <note>a learned scholar</note> and is endowed with elephants, cows, horses, and various properties. If Mars and the Sun aspect it, he is endowed with an army, vehicles, and gems. If aspected by the Sun and Mercury, he delights in the discussion of knowledge and is very wealthy. If Venus and the Sun aspect Jupiter in the ninth, the native is extremely sweet-spoken.**

**If Saturn and the Sun aspect Jupiter in the ninth, the native is highly virtuous, a scholar, and owner of many villages (territories). If the Moon and Mars aspect it, he is highly illustrious, full of the happiness of an army and wealth. If the Moon and Mercury aspect it, he is endowed with various types of domestic happiness, excellent wealth, and comforts like fine bedding. If Venus and the Moon aspect it, he is childless, brave, wealthy, and a man of action.**

**If the Moon and Saturn aspect Jupiter in the ninth, the native is virtuous, argumentative, and a resident of foreign lands. If Mercury and Venus aspect it, he is an excellent scholar. If all planets aspect Jupiter in the ninth, he is a king worshipped among men and very wealthy. If all benefic planets are in the 9th house, they grant an immovable kingdom and wealth. Thus says the author of Sudhashalini. || 70-72 ||**

> If the Sun is with the son of the Moon <note>Mercury</note>, one has many enemies, is miserable, and always afflicted by disease. # Page 446
## Commentary on the Jataka Parijata

**The Scholar, etc.** (Mars and Mercury) — When Mars is joined with Mercury in the ninth house, the person born becomes a scholar <note>Sanskrit: *shastri*; one who studies and teaches the sacred scriptures</note>, a consumer of pleasures, and happy.

(Mars and Jupiter) — When Mars is joined with Jupiter <note>Sanskrit: *ijya*; a name for Jupiter meaning 'the teacher of the gods'</note> in the ninth house, the person born becomes wealthy and honored or respected by the people.

(Mars and Venus) — When Mars is joined with Venus in the ninth house, the person born will have two wives <note>Sanskrit: *dvivadhupati*; literally 'lord of two brides'</note>, be argumentative, and live in a foreign land.

(Mars and Saturn) — When Mars is joined with the son of the Sun <note>Sanskrit: *bhanusuta*; a common epithet for Saturn</note> in the ninth house, the person born is indeed a sinner and devoted to the wives of others.

(Mercury and Jupiter) — When Mercury <note>Sanskrit: *saumya*; the 'gentle' planet</note> is joined with the one worshipped by the immortals <note>Jupiter</note> in the ninth house, the person born is sharp-witted, learned, wealthy, and a wise man <note>Sanskrit: *pandita*; specifically one possessing the intellect to discriminate between the real and the unreal</note>. || 76 ||

[The following section repeats the above findings in Hindi for the reader's convenience:]
If Mars is with Mercury in the ninth, the native knows the scriptures and is a happy enjoyer. If Mars is with Jupiter in the ninth, he is wealthy and worshipful. If Mars is with Venus in the ninth, he has two wives, is a debater, and lives abroad. If Mars is with Saturn in the ninth, the native is a sinner and an adulterer. If Mercury is with Jupiter in the ninth, he is clever, learned, wealthy, and wise. || 76 ||

->Wise, fond of the pleasure of music, a scholar when the son of the Moon is with the son of Bhrigu;<-
->But when the Gentle One is joined with the Slow One, the body is sickly, wealth is great, and speech is false.<-
->When Jupiter is joined with Venus, there is long life and great prosperity; when Jupiter is with the Slow One,<-
->One is sickly but possesses wealth of gems; when the White One is joined with the Dark One, he becomes like a king.<- || 77 ||

**The Wise, etc.** (Mercury and Venus) — When the son of the Moon <note>Mercury</note> is joined with the son of Bhrigu <note>Venus</note> in the house of fortune (the ninth), the person born becomes a scholar, wise, and fond of music.

(Mercury and Saturn) — When Mercury is joined with the Slow One <note>Sanskrit: *manda*; Saturn</note> in the ninth house, the person born has a sickly body, but possesses much wealth and speaks untruths.

(Jupiter and Venus) — When Jupiter is joined with Venus in the ninth house, the person born is long-lived and possesses great fortune and abundant wealth.

(Jupiter and Saturn) — When Jupiter is with Saturn in the ninth house, the person born is sickly but possesses wealth in the form of gems.

(Venus and Saturn) — When the White One <note>Venus</note> is joined with the Dark One <note>Sanskrit: *asita*; Saturn</note> in the ninth house, the person born becomes equal to a king. || 77 ||

[Hindi translation of the verse:]
If Mercury is with Venus in the ninth house, the native is intelligent, fond of music, and a scholar. If Mercury is with Saturn in the ninth, he is sickly, very wealthy, and a liar. If Jupiter is with Venus in the ninth, he is long-lived and particularly prosperous. If Jupiter is with Saturn in the ninth, he is sickly but has wealth of jewels. If Venus is with Saturn in the ninth, he is like a king. || 77 ||

---

### Now, the results of Three-Planet Conjunctions in the Ninth.

From here until verse 86, the results of three planets joining in the ninth house are described:

->If the Sun, Moon, and Mars have reached the ninth, the body is scarred and one is deprived of father and mother.<-
->Cruel and performing improper deeds are those with Sun, Moon, and Mercury; Sun, Moon, and Jupiter bring happiness and vehicles.<- || 78 ||

**The Sun, Moon, and Mars, etc.** — If the Sun, Moon, and Mars are in the ninth house, the person born has a scarred or diseased body and is deprived of both father and mother.

(Sun, Moon, and Mercury) — If the Sun, Moon, and Mercury are in the ninth, the person born is violent <note>Sanskrit: *hinsi*; one who performs acts of injury</note> and performs improper deeds <note>Sanskrit: *vikarma*; acting against the traditional conduct of one's own family</note>.

# Chapter 14: Results of the Seventh, Eighth, and Ninth Houses
<page-num>457</page-num>

**(Sun, Moon, Jupiter)** — If the Sun, Moon, and Jupiter are in the ninth house, the person born will be endowed with happiness and vehicles. ||78||

If the Sun, Moon, and Mars are in the ninth, the person's body will have scars <note>original: "kshata" (wounds/scars)</note> and they will be deprived of their mother and father. If the Sun, Moon, and Mercury are in the ninth, they will perform violent acts and be devoid of family traditions. If the Sun, Moon, and Jupiter are in the ninth, the person will be full of happiness and possess vehicles. ||78||

---

->The Moon and Sun with Venus: a causer of quarrels with women, beloved by kings, a destroyer of wealth.<-
->In the house of fortune, the Sun and Moon with Saturn: a servant, an opponent of the virtuous.<-
->The Sun and Mars with Mercury there: handsome, angry, and fond of disputes.<-
->With Jupiter: beloved by gods and ancestors, endowed with children, a wife, and wealth. || 79 ||<-

**The Moon and Sun (Sun, Moon, Venus)** — If the Moon and Sun are with Venus in the house of fortune <note>The 9th House</note>, the man born will be a "causer of quarrels with women," beloved by the king, and a "destroyer of wealth" (one who wastes money).

**(Sun, Moon, Saturn)** — If the Sun and Moon are joined with Saturn in the house of fortune, the person born will be a servant (one who serves others) and an opponent of the "virtuous" (good people).

**(Sun, Mars, Mercury)** — If the Sun and Mars are with Mercury in that house of fortune, the person born will be "handsome" (having a beautiful body), angry, and fond of disputes.

**(Sun, Mars, Jupiter)** — If the Sun and Mars are with Jupiter in the house of fortune, the person born will be beloved by the gods and ancestors, and "endowed with children, a wife, and wealth" (joined with family and riches). || 79 ||

If the Sun, Moon, and Venus are in the 9th house, the person quarrels with his wife, is a favorite of the king, and a destroyer of wealth.

If the Sun, Moon, and Saturn are in the 9th, the person is a servant to others and an opponent of good men.

If the Sun, Mars, and Mercury are in the ninth house, the person is beautiful to look at, angry, and fond of arguments.

If the Sun, Mars, and Jupiter are in the 9th, they are dear to the deities and ancestors, and full of sons, wives, and wealth. || 79 ||

---

->Sun and Mars with Venus: devoted to disputes, angry, a defiler of women.<-
->With the son of Chhaya (Saturn): without kinsmen, poor, a holy man, a killer of the father.<-
->In the house of Dharma, the Sun and Mercury with Jupiter: beloved by kings, wealthy.<-
->With Venus: equal to a king. With the son of the Sun (Saturn): a sinner, a husband to others' wives. || 80 ||<-

**Sun and Mars (Sun, Mars, Venus)** — If the Sun and Mars are with Venus in the house of fortune, the person born is devoted to disputes, angry, and a defiler of women.

**(Sun, Mars, Saturn)** — If the Sun and Mars are with the "son of Chhaya" <note>A name for Saturn, the son of the shadow-goddess Chhaya</note> in the house of fortune, the person born is "without kinsmen" (lacking relatives), "wealthless" (poor), a "holy man" (virtuous/ascetic), and a "killer of the father" (meaning the father may die shortly after the child is born).

**(Sun, Mercury, Jupiter)** — If the Sun and the "son of the Moon" (Mercury) are with Jupiter in the house of Dharma <note>The 9th House</note>, the person born will be beloved by kings and wealthy.

**(Sun, Mercury, Venus)** — If the Sun and Mercury are with Venus in the house of Dharma, the person born will be "equal to a king" (like a ruler).

**(Sun, Mercury, Saturn)** — If the Sun and Mercury are with the "son of the Sun" (Saturn) in the ninth, the person born will be a sinner and "devoted to the wives of others." || 80 ||

If the Sun, Mars, and Venus are in the 9th house, the person is devoted to disputes, angry, and quarrels with women.

## Commentary on the Jataka Parijata

If the Sun, Mars, and Saturn are in the 9th house, the person will be without relatives, a mendicant <note>original: "sadhu"</note>, and fatherless.
If the Sun, Mercury, and Jupiter are in the 9th, the person will be dear to the King and wealthy. If the Sun, Mercury, and Venus are in the 9th, they will be like a King. If the Sun, Mercury, and Saturn are present, they will be a sinner and an adulterer. — From the author of *Su. Sha.* || 80 ||

->**If Jupiter and the Sun are joined with Venus, one is attached to others' wives, wealthy, and learned.**<-
->**If Saturn, Jupiter, and the Sun are in the house of penance, one is a leader of rogues.**<-
->**If the Sun, Saturn, and Venus go to the ninth, one is lowly and punished by Kings;**<-
->**Distressed in mind during childhood, but happy thereafter; likewise for Moon, Mars, and Mercury.**<- || 81 ||

(<term>Sun</term> <term>Jup.</term> <term>Ven.</term>) — Jupiter and Sun joined with Venus in the ninth: the person born is attached to the wives of others, wealthy, and a scholar.

(<term>Sun</term> <term>Jup.</term> <term>Sat.</term>) — Saturn with Jupiter and the Sun in the house of penance <note>The 9th house is traditionally called the 'Tapas-sthana' or place of spiritual practice.</note> (the ninth house): the person born becomes a leader of "vitas" (rogues or debauchees), meaning a king among the wicked.

(<term>Sun</term> <term>Ven.</term> <term>Sat.</term>) — Sun, Saturn, and Venus in the ninth: the person born is lowly, devoid of good qualities, and punished by Kings.

(<term>Moon</term> <term>Mars</term> <term>Merc.</term>) — Moon, Mars, and Mercury in the ninth: the person born is distressed in mind during childhood (infancy), but becomes happy later (in youth) || 81 ||

If <term>Sun</term> <term>Jup.</term> <term>Ven.</term> are in the 9th house, the person is devoted to others' wives, wealthy, and a scholar. If <term>Sun</term> <term>Jup.</term> <term>Sat.</term> are there, they are a king of rogues.

If <term>Sun</term> <term>Ven.</term> <term>Sat.</term> are in the ninth house, the person is without merit and punished by the King. If <term>Moon</term> <term>Mars</term> and <term>Mercury</term> are in the 9th house, the person is miserable in childhood and happy thereafter (in young adulthood).

->**Devoted to the worship of gods if the Moon, Mars, and Jupiter are in the ninth;**<-
->**One loses their wife and has a scarred body with Venus, Moon, and Mars.**<-
->**Mean and a destroyer of the mother, or like a lord of the earth with Moon, Mars, and Saturn;**<-
->**A teacher, wealthy, and powerful with the Moon, Mercury, and Jupiter.**<- || 82 ||

Regarding "Devoted to gods" etc.: (<term>Moon</term> <term>Mars</term> <term>Jup.</term>) — With Moon, Mars, and Jupiter in the ninth, the person born is intent on the worship of deities.

(<term>Moon</term> <term>Mars</term> <term>Ven.</term>) — With Venus, Moon, and Mars in the ninth, the person born has a lost wife (a deceased spouse) and a scarred or afflicted body.

(<term>Moon</term> <term>Mars</term> <term>Sat.</term>) — With Moon, Mars, and Saturn in the ninth, the person born is mean (a miser), a destroyer of the mother, yet also like a lord of the earth (kingly).

(<term>Moon</term> <term>Jup.</term> <term>Merc.</term>) — With the Moon, Mercury, and Jupiter in the ninth, the person born becomes a teacher <note>original: "Acharya"</note>, wealthy, and powerful || 82 ||

If <term>Moon</term> <term>Mars</term> <term>Jup.</term> are in the 9th, the person is absorbed in the worship of gods. If <term>Moon</term> <term>Mars</term> <term>Ven.</term> are in the 9th, they are without a wife and sickly. If <term>Moon</term> <term>Mars</term> <term>Sat.</term> are in the 9th, they are a miser and motherless. If <term>Moon</term> <term>Merc.</term> <term>Jup.</term> are in the 9th, the person is a venerable scholar, wealthy, and courageous || 82 ||

**Mother's = of one's own mother; co-wife's father = he will be the cause of a step-mother; powerful = he shall be capable.**

**(<term>Moon, Mercury, Saturn</term>) — If the Moon, Mercury, and the son of the Sun (Saturn) are situated in the ninth house, then the person born is a sinner and possessed of a mind fond of disputes = he becomes argumentative. || 83 ||**

->The Moon and the Priest of the Gods (Jupiter) with Venus make a king; with the son of the Sun (Saturn), one is of virtuous character and deeds.<-

If they are with Venus, one is a scholar of the scriptures, restless, and timid (fearful). If joined with Saturn, one is intent on dispute and incapable in actions. || 85 ||
