# With Commentary: Jataka Parijata —
<page-num>450</page-num>

If those same planets are in the ninth house with Venus <note>Sanskrit: *Kavi*</note>, the student will face many obstacles. If Jupiter, Venus, Mercury, and the Moon are in the 9th house, one becomes a wealthy king. || 86 ||

-> One born with the Sun, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn together in the House of Fortune earns wealth through daring and valor; with Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and the Moon, one is a hero and a connoisseur of all worldly virtues. With six, five, three, or four planets in the House of Fortune, one attains prosperity; if Mercury is among them, one attains kingship; but if those planets are devoid of Mercury and Jupiter, one meets with misfortune. || 87 || <-

**The Commentary:** (Sun, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn) — If the Sun, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn have gone to the House of Fortune (the ninth house), the person born will possess wealth earned through industry and valor <note>Sanskrit: *sāhasa-vikrama-ārjita-dhana*</note>.

(Moon, Mars, Jupiter, Venus) — If Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and the Moon are situated in the ninth, the person born will be a hero—meaning a lover of battle—and a connoisseur of the expansion of all virtues <note>Sanskrit: *sarva-guṇa-prapañca-rasika*, one who enjoys the manifold expressions of good qualities</note>.

Now he speaks generally of the results of combinations of three or more planets in the ninth house—"Six," etc. If the House of Fortune is joined by six, five, three, or four "sky-travelers" <term>planets</term>, the person born attains "Sri"—meaning various types of wealth. If Mercury is included among those planets in the ninth, he attains kingship. However, if those three or more planets are "devoid of the Teacher of Awakening" <note>original: *vibodhana-gurau*, referring to Mercury (the Awakener) and Jupiter (the Guru)</note>—meaning Mercury and Jupiter are absent—then he meets with "misfortune" or a lack of lordship. The sense is that if Mercury or Jupiter is in the ninth, one becomes fortunate. Even then, it should be considered that if both Mercury and Jupiter are present in a combination of three or more planets in the ninth, the result is especially significant. || 87 ||

In the ninth, if the Sun, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn are present, the subject produces wealth through daring and valor. If Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and the Moon are present, he is a warrior and a lover of all virtuous arts. If the House of Fortune is joined by six, five, three, or four planets, the subject attains Lakshmi <note>Goddess of wealth/prosperity</note>. If those planets are in the ninth with Mercury, kingship is obtained. If those planets are in the 9th without Mercury or Jupiter, he will be unfortunate. || 87 ||

-> Planets situated in the House of Fortune, if excluded from Jupiter and Mercury, produce a man who is mostly diseased, unattractive, devoid of kin, suffering from imprisonment, and extremely miserable. || 88 || <-

**The Commentary:** "They produce," etc. Planets numbering three or more, if excluded from Jupiter and Mercury—meaning lacking them—and situated in the House of Fortune (the ninth), produce a man who is "mostly diseased" (afflicted by various illnesses), "unattractive" (ugly), "devoid of kin" (lacking family, etc.), "suffering from imprisonment" (sharing the fate of jails, etc.), and extremely miserable. What is said here is this: three or more planets in the ninth house without Mercury and Jupiter do not cause good fortune. But if some combination of three or more planets includes Mercury or Jupiter, then they make the person born truly fortunate. || 88 ||

If planets other than Jupiter and Mercury are in the House of Fortune, the man is generally diseased, devoid of people, lacking luster, suffering from bondage, and extremely wretched. || 88 ||

-> When the Lord of Fortune is in the House of Destruction, aspected by a planet in its fall or an enemy planet, or is in a cruel division or a sign of debilitation, the man will be devoid of fortune. || 89 || <-

**The Commentary:** "The Lord of Fortune," etc. If the Lord of Fortune (the ruler of the ninth house) has gone to the House of Destruction (the eighth house), and is aspected by <unclear>his own enemy planet</unclear> or a planet in its fall, or is in a "cruel division" (a Navamsha <note>a 1/9th divisional chart used for fine-tuning strength</note> of a malefic planet), or is in a sign of debilitation (his sign of fall or his Navamsha of fall), the man born will be devoid of fortune. || 89 ||

If the Lord of the Ninth is in the eighth, and a debilitated or enemy planet looks upon him, or if he is in a cruel division or a sign of debilitation, etc., then the man is devoid of luck. || 89 ||

It also describes how a poorly placed Ninth Lord leads to a total lack of fortune.</summary>

<header>Chapter 94: Results of the Seventh, Eighth, and Ninth Houses</header>

->**If the Lord of Fortune is joined with a benefic planet and aspected by a benefic,**<-
->**and if that house has a benefic connection, the person will possess fame, wealth, and good fortune. || 90 ||**<-

Regarding the Lord of Fortune: When the Lord of Fortune (the ruler of the 9th house) is joined with a <term>benefic planet</term><note>A naturally auspicious planet like Jupiter, Venus, Mercury, or a strong Moon</note> and is aspected by a benefic, and there is a "benefic connection" to that house (meaning the 9th house is a sign owned by a benefic, or is aspected/occupied by one), the person born will be endowed with excellent fame, wealth, and prosperity. || 90 ||

If the ruler of the 9th house is with a benefic, is seen by a benefic, and the house itself has a connection to a benefic, then one becomes famous, wealthy, and fortunate. || 90 ||

->**If the Lord of Fortune is in the Simhasana division, and is aspected by the Lord of the Ascendant,**<-
->**and is also seen by the Lord of Action, the person will be a great donor of charity. || 91 ||**<-
->**The person may be a priest if born into a Brahmin family,**<-
->**or an assistant to the superintendent of charities; one should distinguish the results by caste. || 92 ||**<-

Regarding the <term>Simhasana division</term><note>Simhasanansha: A specific high-status position in the varga (divisional) charts, literally meaning "throne-portion"</note>: If the ruler of the 9th house has reached the Simhasana division (<gloss>see verse 45 etc.</gloss>) and is aspected (seen) by the <term>Lord of the Ascendant</term><note>Lagnansha: The ruler of the 1st house, representing the self</note>, and is also aspected by the <term>Lord of Action</term><note>Karmadhipa: The ruler of the 10th house, representing career and public deeds</note>, the person born will be a "Great Donor"—meaning extremely charitable.

Regarding the birth: In this specific planetary combination, if the person is born into a <term>Brahmin family</term><note>Brahmavansha: The priestly or scholarly lineage</note>, they will become a priest or ritual performer. Alternatively, they may serve as an assistant to the Superintendent of Charities (at a royal court) and do good for others. Here, one must "distinguish by caste"—meaning the specific authority or profession should be assigned according to the nature of the 9th house's zodiac sign. For example, a Brahmin would perform priestly duties, a Kshatriya (warrior/ruler) would lead an army, a Vaishya (merchant) would manage the treasury, and a Shudra (laborer) would perform service. || 91-92 ||

If the lord of the place of fortune is in the Simhasana division, the Lord of the Ascendant sees it, and the Lord of the 10th also sees it, that person will be a great giver of charity. || 91 ||
Or, if born in a Brahmin lineage, they will be a priest, a head of charities, and a philanthropist. Here, imagine the results based on the distinctions of caste. || 92 ||

->**If Jupiter is placed in that house, or if the Lord of the Navamsha is there,**<-
->**or if it is aspected by a benefic planet, the person will be devoted to their Guru. || 93 ||**<-

Regarding Jupiter: If Jupiter (<term>Brihaspati</term>) is placed in the 9th house, or if the <term>Lord of the Navamsha</term><note>The ruler of the specific 1/9th sub-division the planet occupies</note> is similarly placed in the 9th, or if Jupiter is aspected by a benefic planet, the person born will be full of devotion to their Guru (teacher). || 93 ||

If Jupiter is in the 9th house, or the Lord of the Navamsha is in the 9th, and it is seen by a benefic planet, one will be devoted to their Guru. || 93 ||

->**If the place of the Guru is joined by a benefic and possesses the Guru's divisions,**<-
->**and its lord is in a division of Jupiter, one is devoted to the Guru and happy. || 94 ||**<-
->**If placed in the Navamsha of Jupiter, Venus, or Mercury, and aspected by the Lord of Dharma,**<-
->**and situated between benefic planets, that man will be a performer of righteous deeds. || 95 ||**<-

Regarding the place of the Guru: If in the "place of the Guru" (the 9th house), there is a benefic planet and it is endowed with the <term>Varga</term><note>Divisional strength</note> of Jupiter, and the lord of that house is in a Navamsha of Jupiter, the person born will be intent on serving their Guru and will be happy. || 94 ||

Regarding Jupiter, Venus, etc.: If that 9th house falls in the Navamsha of either Jupiter, Venus, or Mercury, and is aspected by the <term>Lord of Dharma</term><note>Dharmanatha: Another name for the 9th house ruler</note> (<gloss>its own lord</gloss>), and is situated between benefic planets, the man born at that time will be a "Dharma-doer" (a performer of righteous and religious deeds). || 95 ||

...If Jupiter is in the Ascendant <note>Lagna</note> and in the ninth division <term>Navamsha: a 1/9th sub-division of a zodiac sign used for fine-tuning predictions</term>, the person will be devoted to their Guru and be happy. If the Ninth House or Mercury’s division is occupied by the lord of the Ninth, and is aspected by benefic planets...

### If a malefic is in the Ninth, one becomes a sinner; if the lord is joined with a malefic or in a cruel division, one is devoid of righteousness. || 66 ||

**In the Ninth, a malefic:** If any malefic planet <note>such as Mars or Saturn</note> is situated in the Ninth House (the house of Dharma), the person born becomes a **sinner** (one who partakes in sin). **With a defect:** If the lord of the Ninth House is **joined with a malefic** (associated with any natural malefic), or if it has entered a **cruel sixtieth division** <term>Shashtyamsa: a 1/60th sub-division, often used to determine the "temperament" of a planet</term>, the person will be **devoid of righteousness**—meaning they will engage in sinful deeds. || 66 ||

->If there is a malefic planet in the ninth, one is a sinner. If the lord of the Ninth is joined with a malefic or is in a cruel sixtieth division, one is devoid of religion. || 66 ||<-

### If the lord of the Ninth is strong in a center or trine, and the Ascendant is aspected by its lord, one attains a hundred blessings. If the lord of the Tenth is in Jupiter’s divisions, one becomes an ascetic devoid of worldly enjoyment. || 67 ||

**Strong:** If the **lord of the Ninth** (the house of fortune) is situated in a **center** <term>Kendra: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</term> or a **trine** <term>Kona: the 5th or 9th houses</term> from the Ascendant, and the **Ascendant** is **aspected by its own lord**, the person born attains **a hundred blessings** (various auspicious results). Alternatively, if the **lord of the Tenth House** is situated in the **ninth division** <gloss>Navamsha</gloss>, **thirtieth division** <gloss>Trimshamsa</gloss>, or **third division** <gloss>Drekkana</gloss> of **Jupiter**, the person will be **devoid of enjoyment**—having renounced pleasure, wealth, and property—and will become an **ascetic**. Specifically, if the Ninth lord is strong in a center/trine AND the Tenth lord is in one of Jupiter's divisions, they become a renounced ascetic. || 67 ||

->If the strong Ninth lord is in a center or trine, and the Ascendant is seen by the Ascendant lord, hundreds of auspicious things happen. Or, if the Tenth lord is in Jupiter's Navamsha, Trimshamsa, or Drekkana, the native will be an ascetic without worldly pleasures. || 67 ||<-

### All planets in their signs of exaltation in the house of fortune produce excellence and wealth in gold. If those planets are aspected by benefic lords, one destroys their enemies and possesses a divine body and great fame. || 68 ||

**All sky-dwellers:** This refers to any planet, whether malefic or benefic (though not literally all seven at once, as their simultaneous exaltation is impossible), being in its **sign of exaltation** <term>Uchcha: the specific zodiac sign where a planet is at its maximum strength</term>. If they are in the **house of fortune** (the Ninth House), they produce **excellence** and **abundance in wealth and gold**. If any **sky-dwellers** (planets) in the Ninth House are **aspected by benefic lords** (favorable planets), the person born will have **destroyed the side of their enemies**, possess a **divine body** (a beautiful physique), and have **great fame**.

<note>Notes are provided in a mix of Sanskrit and Hindi commentary style.</note>

**Notes —** At one single time, all the "sky-dwellers" (planets) cannot possibly be in their signs of exaltation. For example, if the Sun is exalted in Aries, it is mathematically impossible for Mercury to be in its exaltation in Virgo <note>original: "siddhanta-viruddha" - against astronomical principles</note>. Therefore, the phrase "all sky-dwellers" implies that whichever planets among the seven—be they benefic or malefic—are exalted in the Ninth House, they will grant abundance of wealth and gold. || 68 ||

->If at birth all planets are in their exaltation signs or in the Ninth House, they cause a great increase in wealth and gold. If benefic planets aspect the planets in the Ninth House, then one's enemies are destroyed and one gains great fame. || 68 ||<-

### If the lord of the father's house and the significator of the father are in bad houses, one does not see the face of their son. If those two planets are in a center or trine, one will indeed see the face of their son. || 69 ||

**Lord of the father:** The lord of the house representing the father <note>the 9th house</note>. **Significator of that:** The planet that naturally represents the father <term>Pitri-karaka: usually the Sun</term>. If these two **lords of the sky** (planets) are in **bad houses** <term>Dusthana: the 6th, 8th, or 12th houses, associated with loss and suffering</term>, then the **face of a son shall not be seen** <note>This implies either childlessness or a separation/estrangement from the lineage</note>. In this...

### Now he describes whether the father's death occurs during the day or at night—

> If the lord of the 4th house, Venus, and the Moon are strong and situated in the 6th house, the father's death occurs at night. If they are joined by the lord of the 6th house and are without the Moon, the death occurs during the day. || 100 ||

Regarding the father: if the lord of the 4th, Venus, and the Moon are powerful and positioned in the 6th house from the <unclear>Ascendant</unclear>, then the father's death should be predicted to occur at night. If those same three planets (the lord of the 4th, Venus, and the Moon) are joined by the lord of the 6th house and are without the Moon—meaning the lord of the 4th, the lord of the 6th, and Venus are strong and in the 6th house—then the father's death will occur during the day. || 100 ||

If the lord of the 4th, Venus, and the Moon are in the 6th house, the father dies at night. If the Moon is not there and they are joined by the lord of the 6th, the father dies during the day. || 100 ||

> When a benefic planet is the lord of the 9th, is endowed with strength, and occupies the first portion of a movable sign, and is joined or aspected by Jupiter and Venus, the person will be devoted to prayer, meditation, and spiritual absorption. || 101 ||

Regarding the benefic: if a benefic (meaning Mercury) is the lord of the 9th house, is strong, and occupies the first <term>Navamsha</term> <note>a 1/9th division of a sign</note> of a movable sign, and is joined or aspected by Jupiter and Venus, the person born will be devoted to <insert>prayer</insert>, meditation, and <term>Samadhi</term> <note>deep meditative absorption</note>. This yoga <note>planetary combination</note> occurs when the Ascendant is between Libra and Capricorn. || 101 ||

If a benefic lord of the 9th is strong and in the first Navamsha of a movable sign, and is aspected by or joined with Jupiter and Venus, the person will be one who practices prayer, meditation, and Samadhi. || 101 ||

> If the lord of the 10th or the lord of the 9th is in the Devaloka or similar division, and a benefic is in the Paravatansha, the person will be devoted to the knowledge of the Supreme Spirit. || 102 ||

Regarding the "Devaloka" division: if the lord of the 10th house or the lord of the 9th house is in the <term>Devaloka</term> <note>a specific high-quality division in the Vaisheshikansha system; see Chapter 1, verses 45-47</note>, and a benefic planet has attained the <term>Paravatansha</term> <note>a division where a planet resides in its own or exalted sign in six out of ten divisional charts</note>, the person born will be a <term>Brahmagnani</term> <note>one who possesses divine knowledge of the Ultimate Reality</note>. || 102 ||

If the lord of the 10th or a benefic lord of the 9th is in its Devaloka division, or in the Paravatansha, the subject will be intent on devotion to the Supreme Spirit. || 102 ||

> If the lord of the 9th is in the Paravata or similar division and is joined with Jupiter, and the lord of the Ascendant is aspected by Jupiter, the person will be a performer of great charities. || 103 ||

Thus ends the fourteenth chapter of the Jataka Parijata, composed by Vaidyanatha by the grace of the nine planets. || 14 ||

Regarding the "Paravata" division: if the lord of the 9th house is joined with Jupiter and has attained its own Paravata division, and the lord of the Ascendant is aspected by Jupiter, the person born will be a performer of great charities. || 103 ||

# Chapter 15: On the Results of the Tenth, Eleventh, and Twelfth Houses

->Results of the Tenth House<-

Now, the fifteenth chapter is explained. In this chapter, the results of the <term>Karma</term> (10th - Action), <term>Aya</term> (11th - Gains), and <term>Vyaya</term> (12th - Losses) houses are indicated. First, wishing to speak on the results of the tenth house, the author states the subjects to be considered regarding the tenth house:

> Command, honor, ornaments, clothing, business, sleep, agriculture, 
> renunciation, arrival, action, livelihood, fame, specialized knowledge, and learning; 
> these should be considered respectively through the Lord of the Tenth, the Sun, Mercury, Jupiter, and Saturn. 
> Leaving aside what was previously mentioned, if the tenth house is afflicted, the person becomes devoid of honor. || 1 ||

**Command:** (Authority/Rule), honor, jewelry, clothes, trade, sleep, farming, <term>Pravrajya</term> <note>Taking up the life of a wandering monk or ascetic</note>, income, work, life-sustenance, fame, science, and education—all these matters should be considered through the Lord of the Tenth, the Sun, Mercury, Jupiter, and Saturn respectively. Here, the word "respectively" means that in the absence of the former, the latter should be taken as the indicator. If the <term>Mana</term> (tenth house) is afflicted—meaning occupied or aspected by malefic planets—the person born will be "without honor," meaning lacking in prestige and disregarded by people. || 1 ||

->On the Consideration of Action<-

> If the Lord of the Tenth is devoid of strength, the person is of fickle mind and wicked conduct. 
> If Jupiter, Mercury, Saturn, and the Sun are weak and placed in bad houses, they grant improper actions. 
> If Rahu or the Sun is in the tenth, one attains the fruit of bathing in the Ganges. 
> If Pisces is in the tenth house and joined by Mercury and Mars, the person becomes liberated. || 2 ||

**Lord of the Tenth:** If the Lord of the Tenth house is weak, the person born will have an "unsteady intellect" and be a "doer of bad deeds" (wicked conduct). If Jupiter, Mercury, Saturn, and the Sun become weak and are "badly placed"—meaning they have gone to the 6th, 8th, or 12th houses—they grant "improper actions" to the native. The meaning is that one born under this yoga (alignment) will perform despicable deeds. If Rahu or the Sun is in the tenth, the person attains the merit of "bathing in the Ganges" <note>A metaphor for spiritual purification and the washing away of sins</note>. If the tenth house is in the sign of Pisces and is joined by the "Son of the Moon" (Mercury) and the "Son of the Earth" (Mars), that person becomes "liberated"—meaning their sins are washed away, or they become a <term>Jivanmukta</term> <note>One who is spiritually liberated while still alive</note>. || 2 ||

> If the Lord of the Tenth is joined with Venus and situated in a quadrant or in its exaltation, one is purified by such waters. 
> If Mercury is in the twelfth, or if the Lord of that house is in its exaltation, one partakes in similar merit. || 3 ||

**Lord of the Tenth:** If the Lord of the Tenth house is with Venus and is in a <term>Kendra</term> (quadrant: 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th house) or is "exalted" <note>at its highest point of strength</note>, the person born is "purified by such waters," meaning their body is made pure by the water of the Ganges. **In the Twelfth:** If Mercury is in the twelfth house, or if the Lord of that house (the 12th)...

# Chapter 12: Results of the Tenth, Eleventh, and Twelfth Houses

If the Lord of the Tenth House is in conjunction with Mercury, or is in the 12th house in its sign of exaltation <note>The highest point of a planet's strength</note>, the person born will be a partaker of great merit (it is said such a person shall attain liberation). || 3 ||

If the Lord of the Tenth is in a quadrant <term>Kendra: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</term> joined with Venus, and Mercury is in the 12th house, or if the Lord of the 12th is there and exalted, the person will similarly be a partaker of merit. || 3 ||

->**If the Moon is in the Tenth, one is purified by the waters of the Ganges;**<-
->**A weak malefic in the Tenth gives boldness in gambling.**<-
->**Weak benefics in the Tenth are destroyers of good deeds;**<-
->**One should predict the fruits of sacrifice by considering the Lord of the Tenth, Mercury, and Jupiter.**<- || 4 ||

*Regarding the Moon:* When the Moon of pure rays—meaning the full lunar disk—shines in the Tenth House (the house of action), the person born will certainly be purified of sins by the waters of the Jahnavi <note>Another name for the River Ganges</note>. *Regarding Malefics:* A weak malefic planet <note>such as Mars or Saturn</note> situated in the Tenth House produces excellence in the daring act of gambling (dice-play). *Regarding Benefics:* If weak or powerless benefic planets <note>such as Mercury, Jupiter, or Venus</note> are in the Tenth, they become destroyers of good deeds—meaning they hinder pilgrimages, baths in holy rivers, and the performance of sacrifices or vows. *Regarding the Lord of the Tenth, Mercury, and Jupiter:* If the Lord of the Tenth, Mercury, and Jupiter are placed in the Tenth House, one attains the fruit of performing sacrifices! One should deliberate carefully and announce all this based on the specific positions of the planets. || 4 ||

->**If the Lords of the First and Tenth are together, or if one planet rules both,**<-
->**The person performs great festivals and sacrifices with wealth earned by themselves.**<-
->**With Saturn, it is through the wealth of laborers; with Rahu or Ketu, through the low-born; with Jupiter, through kings;**<-
->**One performs these acts through the wealth of whichever planet—Sun and others—joins the Lord of the Tenth.**<- || 5 ||

*Regarding being in one place:* If the Lord of the First (Ascendant) and the Lord of the Tenth are together in any house, or if there is "single lordship"—meaning one planet rules both the First and Tenth houses—then the person performs great festivals and sacrifices with "virtuous wealth" earned by the strength of their own arms. Their wealth is never wasted on evil paths.

*Regarding Saturn and others:* If the Lord of the Tenth is joined with Saturn, one performs sacrifices with wealth obtained from the Shudra class <note>The laboring class in traditional Indian society</note>. If that Lord of the Tenth is with the Serpent (Rahu) or the Banner (Ketu), it is through the wealth of the "vile" or outcaste groups. If joined with Jupiter, one performs sacrifices using the wealth of kings (royalty).

*Regarding the significators:* When the Lord of the Tenth is joined with the Sun or other planets, the person performs great festivals and sacrifices using wealth acquired from the specific category or person signified by that planet.

**Notes**—Regarding "single lordship": The same planet rules both the First and Tenth houses only when the Ascendant is Virgo or Pisces. In a Virgo Ascendant, the tenth from it is Gemini; thus, Mercury is the single ruler of both. In a Pisces Ascendant, the tenth from it is Sagittarius; thus, Jupiter is the single ruler of both. || 5 ||

# Page 452
## From the Commentary on Jataka Parijata

If the Lord of the Ascendant <note>Lagnesha</note> and the Lord of the Tenth House <note>Dashamesha</note> are in the same location, or if both houses are ruled by the same planet (this occurs when the Ascendant is Virgo or Pisces), then the person born <note>Jataka</note> will perform sacrifices <note>Yajnas</note> using excellent wealth earned by their own efforts. If these planets are associated with Rahu or Ketu <note>the North and South Nodes of the Moon</note>, the sacrifices are performed with wealth from lower classes; if associated with Jupiter, the rituals are funded by the wealth of kings. The specific class or source of wealth for these rituals is determined by whichever planet (Sun, etc.) is associated with the Lord of the Tenth. ॥ 5 ॥

-> If many benefic planets occupy the tenth house, the accomplishment of the Vajapeya and other great sacrifices occurs. If the lords of the signs occupied by Venus and Mercury are weak, then even if the person has initiated the sacred rites, the merit of former deeds is lost; though performing great works, they become one whose conduct is like that of the demons. <-

**Commentary:** In the tenth house <note>the house of action and profession</note>, if there is a conjunction of many benefic planets, the completion of the *Vajapeya* <note>a high-ranking Vedic sacrifice</note> and other major sacrifices is achieved by the native. However, if the lords of the signs where Venus <note>Sita</note> and Mercury <note>Budha</note> reside are weak, then even if the person has performed the pressing of the Soma juice <note>Savana; the ritual extraction of sacred juice</note>, they become unable to complete the cycle due to the destruction of past merit or the onset of misfortune. Despite performing "great works," such a person may possess a demonic or cruel disposition. ॥ 6 ॥

If a strong benefic planet is in the tenth house from the Moon, situated in its sign of exaltation or a favorable division, and is joined with or aspected by Jupiter <note>the Lord of Speech</note>, the person becomes a leader among men, a performer of sacrifices <note>Yajva</note>, and famous. If the lords of the signs occupied by Jupiter, Mercury, and Venus have gone to destruction <note>the 8th house</note>, the native, though performing deeds with good intentions, does not attain the glory or the full fruit of their actions. ॥ 7 ॥

**Commentary:** When a strong benefic planet (such as Venus or Mercury) is in its exaltation <note>highest strength</note> and is placed in the tenth house relative to the Moon's position at birth, and is further influenced by the sight or presence of Jupiter, the native becomes an eminent man, a performer of rituals according to the law <note>original: "Yajva tu vidhineṣṭavān" - one who has sacrificed according to the rules</note>, and earns great renown in the world.

Regarding the second part: Jupiter, Mercury, and Venus are the planets. If the lords of the signs where these three are placed go to "destruction"—meaning the 8th house <note>the house of loss and obstacles</note>—then the native, even if performing actions that should yield good results, does not obtain the "Splendor of Action" <note>Karma-shri</note>. The essence is that in this specific planetary alignment, despite performing rituals according to the rules, one does not reach the successful conclusion or fruit of those deeds. ॥ 7 ॥

-> The Lord of the Tenth, Mercury, and Jupiter, when endowed with strength, grant the performance of sacrifices and good deeds. If they are aspected by or joined with a benefic planet, the native participates in the Vajapeya sacrifice. They grant the merit of restoring old temples, creation, building gateways <note>Gopuram</note>, tanks, and gardens. One becomes a performer of sacrifices if the Lord of the Tenth is a benefic, joined with the Moon, in the tenth house, and free from Rahu and Ketu. <-

**Commentary:** The Lord of the Tenth <note>Karmesha</note>, Mercury, and Jupiter: if these are powerful, they grant the performance of virtuous deeds like sacrifices. If these three are influenced by a benefic "sky-traveler" <note>planet</note>...

It also warns that if certain planetary lords are weak or placed in the 8th house, the spiritual merit of these actions may be lost or the person's character may remain flawed.</summary>

# Chapter 22: Results of the Tenth, Eleventh, and Twelfth Houses
<page-num>457</page-num>

If the planet is aspected by or conjoined with a bright or full Moon, the person born becomes a <term>Yajnakrit</term> <note>one who performs Vedic sacrifices</note> or a <term>Yajva</term> <note>a performer of rituals</note>. Furthermore, these planets enable the native to perform acts of public service such as <term>Jirnoddhara</term> <note>the restoration of ancient temples or monuments</note>, and the construction of cowsheds, gateways, tanks, and monasteries. This means the native will be a restorer of old temples and monasteries, a builder of famous cowsheds and gateways, and a creator of reservoirs and gardens, thereby performing many meritorious deeds. Regarding the verse "Dagbe...": If the Lord of the Tenth House is a benefic planet, conjoined with the Moon, situated in the Tenth House, and free from the influence of Rahu and Ketu <note>the North and South Nodes of the Moon</note>, the native becomes a performer of sacrifices. || 8 ||

If the Lord of the Tenth, Mercury, and Jupiter are strong, they grant the performance of sacrifices and good deeds. If they are aspected by or conjoined with benefic planets, they cause the native to perform great sacrifices like the <term>Vajapeya</term> <note>an important Vedic ritual of 'the drink of strength'</note>. They also grant the merit of restoring old structures and building cowsheds, ponds, and gardens. If the Lord of the Tenth is with a benefic planet and the Moon, and Rahu and Ketu are not in the 10th house, the native will be a performer of sacrifices. || 8 ||

> If Mercury is in its sign of exaltation, free from Rahu and Ketu, or placed in the Ninth House, or if the Lord of the Tenth is in the Ninth House, the person performs sacrifices and good deeds. If the Lord of the Tenth is in its own sign of exaltation conjoined with Mercury, or if Mercury is exalted in the Seventh House, the native certainly attains the fruits of performing rituals. || 9 ||

The meaning of "Uchchastha..." <note>exalted</note> is clear and requires no further elaboration. || 9 ||

If Mercury is in its exalted sign (Virgo) without Rahu or Ketu, or is in the 9th house, and the Lord of the Tenth is in the 9th, the person performs sacrifices. If the Lord of the Tenth is in its exaltation sign with Mercury, or if Mercury is exalted in the 7th house, the native will surely receive the rewards of sacrifice.

> If Mercury is in the Tenth House, the native prepares for sacrifices. If Mercury is with Rahu or Ketu, he becomes a destroyer of rituals. If the Lord of the Tenth is in the 6th, 8th, or 12th house, he becomes an obstructor of deeds. If Rahu is in the tenth house from the Lord of the Tenth (Mercury), he is a destroyer of sacrifices. Even if the Lord of the Tenth is in its exaltation, if it is placed in a "bad house," he destroys deeds. || 10 ||

Regarding "Karmastha...": If Mercury is in the Tenth House, the native becomes a <term>Savanakrit</term> <note>one who collects materials/herbs for a sacrifice</note>. If such a Mercury is conjoined with Rahu or Ketu, the native becomes a <term>Karmaha</term> <note>a destroyer of rituals</note>. Regarding "Karmesha...": If the Lord of the Tenth is in the 6th, 8th, or 12th house <note>the 'Dusthanas' or difficult houses</note>, he becomes an obstructor of the sacrifices or good deeds of others.

Regarding "Karmeshasya...": If Rahu is in the 10th house from Mercury (when Mercury is the Lord of the Tenth). This implies: if Mercury is the Lord of the Tenth, and Rahu is placed in the 10th house from wherever Mercury is situated, the native becomes a <term>Makhadhvamsaka</term> <note>a destroyer of sacrifices</note>. Note that Mercury can be the Lord of the Tenth only when Sagittarius or Virgo is the Ascendant.

Regarding "Tungasthanagato-api...": Even if the Lord of the Tenth is in its sign of exaltation, if it is placed in a "bad house" (6th, 8th, or 12th), the native becomes a destroyer of deeds. The essence is that the Lord of the Tenth in the 6th, 8th, or 12th house destroys the fruits of actions, even if it is exalted. || 10 ||

If Mercury is in the 10th, the native collects materials for sacrifice. If Mercury is with Rahu-Ketu, he harms rituals. If the Lord of the Tenth is in the 6th, 8th, or 12th, he obstructs deeds. If Rahu is in the 10th from the Lord of the Tenth (Mercury), he destroys sacrifices. Even if the Lord of the Tenth is exalted, if it is in a bad house (6, 8, 12), the native destroys deeds. || 10 ||

<header>With the Commentary on Jataka Parijata—</header>

### **If the houses of commerce and dharma are occupied by auspicious planets, and the lords of those houses, along with Jupiter and the lord of the ascendant, are powerful, then the person will be devoted to the practice of traditional conduct, virtue, and ritual acts, becoming preeminent among the priestly class. || 11 ||**

Regarding the "houses of commerce and dharma": Commerce refers to the 10th house <note>The house of profession and public action</note>. Dharma refers to the 9th house <note>The house of religion and fortune</note>. The rest is self-explanatory. || 11 ||

*If there are auspicious planets in the 10th and 9th houses, and the lords of those houses, Jupiter, and the lord of the ascendant are strong, the person will be engaged in and devoted to conduct, religion, virtue, and ritual methods, and will be a leader in the Brahmin community.* || 11 ||

---

### **If the five houses—the house of the preceptor, commerce, spouse, children, and the ascendant—are occupied by or aspected by benefics, and their lords are powerful, the person will be famous for their mastery of all philosophical truths, sciences, and the performance of sacrifices. || 12 ||**

Regarding "occupied by benefics": The houses of the preceptor, commerce, spouse, children, and the ascendant refer to the 9th, 10th, 7th, 5th, and 1st houses respectively. If these houses are occupied by or aspected <note>The astrological "glance" or influence of a planet from a distance</note> by auspicious planets, and if their lords—the rulers of the 9th, 10th, 7th, 5th, and 1st—are strong, then the person born will be superior in the knowledge of all fundamental truths <term>Tattva: the primary principles of reality</term>, a performer of sacrifices, and famous for all virtues.

*If these five houses—9th, 10th, 7th, 5th, and the ascendant—are joined with or seen by auspicious planets, and the lords of those places are strong, the person will become famous for all philosophical truths, great learning, and all sacrificial rites.* || 12 ||

---

### **If the lords of the ascendant, the 9th, and the 10th houses reside in the houses of knowledge and the sky and are endowed with the six-fold strength, the person born will be a knower of the six Shastras, a scholar of all the Vedas, and will receive initiation into divine knowledge. In the major or minor planetary periods of the lords of the 9th, 10th, and 1st houses, and of Mercury and Jupiter, the person will become a source of good deeds, right conduct, the fruits of all sacrifices, and Vedic wisdom. || 13 ||**

Regarding "residing in knowledge and the sky": "Knowledge and sky" refers to the houses of knowledge and the 10th house. Here, "knowledge" refers to the 2nd, 4th, and 5th houses, as knowledge is considered from these. "Sky" refers to the 10th house. Therefore, if the planets occupying the 2nd, 4th, 5th, and 10th houses are the lords of the 1st, 9th, and 10th houses, and are endowed with the "six-fold strength" <term>Shadbala: a mathematical calculation of six different sources of planetary strength</term>, then the person born becomes a knower of the six Shastras <note>The six systems of Indian philosophy</note>, a knower of all the Vedas <note>original: "Nigama"</note>, and attains initiation into spiritual knowledge.

Regarding "Dharma...": During the planetary periods <note>Dasha and Antardasha</note> of the lords of the 9th, 10th, and 1st houses, and of Mercury and Jupiter, the person born will be characterized by good deeds and conduct, will enjoy the fruits of all sacrifices, and will be a treasury of all Vedic knowledge and science. || 13 ||

*If the lords of the 1st, 9th, and 10th houses are situated in the houses of knowledge (2, 4, 5) and the 10th house with their full six-fold strength, the person will know the six Shastras, be an expert in all Vedas, and receive spiritual initiation. In the periods of the 9th, 10th, and 1st lords, Mercury, and Jupiter, they will attain all good deeds, conduct, sacrificial fruits, Vedic knowledge, and learning.* || 13 ||

---

### **When the Moon is in the third house in a water sign, the person performs meritorious acts such as the restoration of old monuments. If the lord of the 10th house from the ascendant is in the "Gopura" division, the person builds tanks, wells, and similar works. || 14 ||**

Regarding "in a water sign": When the Moon has entered a sign such as the latter half of Capricorn, Pisces, or Cancer <note>original: "refer to Ch. 1, Verse 17"</note> and is positioned in the 3rd house from the ascendant, the person performs the merit of "restoration"—the repair and renewal of old water reservoirs, groves, or temples.

When the lord of the 10th house is in the "Gopura" division <term>Gopuransha: a specific strength where a planet occupies its own or exalted sign in four different divisional charts</term>, the person born under this yoga <note>astrological combination</note> performs the merit of constructing tanks and wells. || 14 ||

# Chapter 15: Results of the Tenth, Eleventh, and Twelfth Houses
<page-num>456</page-num>

If the Moon is in a water-sign <note>Signs like Cancer, Scorpio, or Pisces</note> in the third house, the native will perform the meritorious act of restoring old structures. If the lord of the tenth house from the Ascendant is in the *Gopura* division <note>A technical strength in Varga charts where a planet occupies its own or exalted sign in four specific divisional charts</note>, the native will be a builder of tanks, wells, and similar public works. || 14 ||

## Now, the Combinations for Renunciation (*Pravrajya Yoga*)

Now, the combinations for renunciation are described in twenty-eight verses:

If five, four, or more powerful planets are situated together in a *Kendra* <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note> or a *Trikona* <note>The 5th or 9th houses</note>, the native enters the order of the most powerful planet among them. The orders associated with the Sun, Saturn, Jupiter, Venus, Mars, the Moon, and Mercury are respectively: the Forest-dweller (*Vanaprastha*), the Naked Monk (*Vivasa*), the Mendicant (*Bhikshu*), the Wanderer (*Charaka*), the Buddhist Monk (*Shakya*), the Teacher (*Guru*), and the Living-Seeker (*Jivaka*). || 15 ||

The Forest-dweller is an ascetic residing in forests and mountains; the Naked Monk is one who goes without clothes; the Mendicant is a great soul carrying a single staff (*Ekadandi*), constantly devoted to the truths of the Upanishads; the Wanderer is a chief among travelers, roaming through various countries; the Buddhist Monk is a practitioner who may be of ill-conduct or a deceiver; the Teacher is one possessed of royal splendor and fame; and the Living-Seeker is one primarily concerned with food and talkativeness. || 16 ||

Now, the characteristics of the renunciations for the seven planets from the Sun onwards are explained individually through these two verses. "By five, four, or more powerful planets" means when five or four planets are joined together and are strong; "situated in a *Kendra* or *Trikona*" means placed in the 1st, 4th, 7th, 10th or 5th and 9th houses. This should be considered: when five or four strong planets are joined in a *Kendra* or *Trikona*, the native will belong to the order (*Ashrama*) of the planet that is the most powerful among them.

Now, the orders of renunciation for the planets are stated: From the Sun, Saturn, Jupiter, Venus, Mars, Moon, and Mercury, one should know the renunciations of *Vanaprastha*, *Vivasa*, *Bhikshu*, *Charaka*, *Shakya*, *Guru*, and *Jivaka* respectively. Thus it has been said by the venerable Varahamihira <note>A famous 6th-century Indian astronomer and astrologer</note>:

> "A powerful planet among four or more in one house creates its own type of renunciation. If there are many such powerful planets, the native joins the order of the strongest. If a planet is defeated in planetary combat, the person may fall from that path." <note>Original Latin/Sanskrit reference: "Chaturadibhirekasthaih..." from the Brihat Jataka</note>

Now, the definitions of the aforementioned renunciations are given:

**Forest-dweller (*Vanaprastha*):** An ascetic whose home is the forests and mountains.

**Naked Monk (*Vivasa*):** One whose nature is to be without clothes (naked).

**Mendicant (*Bhikshu*):** A great soul who carries a single staff, is constantly devoted to the essence of the Upanishads <note>Ancient philosophical texts</note>, and is a seeker of Brahman (the Absolute).

**Wanderer (*Charaka*):** A chief among wanderers who habitually travels through various lands.

**Buddhist Monk (*Shakya*):** A practitioner of the Shakya sect, who may be of bad character or a deceiver.

**Teacher (*Guru*):** One who possesses royal wealth and is famous.

**Living-Seeker (*Jivaka*):** One who is focused only on filling his stomach and is a talkative person. || 15-16 ||

If five or four strong planets are situated in one place among the *Kendras* (1, 4, 7, 10) or *Trikonas* (5, 9), the native will belong to the order of the strongest planet. Here, from the Sun, Saturn, Jupiter, Venus, Mars, Moon, and Mercury, the order is respectively: Forest-dweller, Naked Monk, Mendicant, Wanderer...

## With Commentary on Jataka Parijata

The orders of Shakya, Guru, and Jivaka are formed (when the Sun is strong, one becomes a forest hermit <note>Vanaprastha</note>; from Saturn, a naked ascetic; from Jupiter, a religious mendicant <note>Bhikshuka</note>; from Venus, a wandering monk <note>Charaka</note>; from Mars, a Buddhist monk <note>Shakya</note>; from the Moon, a spiritual preceptor <note>Guru</note>; and from Mercury, a religious professional <note>Jivaka</note>). || 15 ||

Now the natures of these ascetic orders are described: The **Vanaprastha** is an ascetic who dwells in forests and mountains. The **Vivasa** <note>literally "without clothes"</note> always remains naked without garments. The **Bhikshu** carries a single staff <note>Ekadandi</note> and is a great soul constantly versed in the truths of the Upanishads. The **Charaka** is a type of ascetic who travels through various countries. The **Shakya-yogi** is of questionable conduct <note>Kushila</note>. The **Guru** is glorious and endowed with royal splendor. The **Jivaka** is eager for food and is a talkative person (one who speaks much).

**Regarding "Karmastha" etc.:** If three planets, being strong and situated in their own exaltation divisions <gloss>positioned in their own exaltation, Moolatrikona, or own sign divisions</gloss>, are in the tenth house <gloss>gone to the tenth house</gloss>, and if the lord of the tenth <gloss>the ruler of the tenth house</gloss> is exceedingly powerful, then the person born becomes an ascetic <gloss>one who has conquered the senses</gloss>. As Amarasimha states: "Those who have conquered the group of senses are called Yatin and Yati." Or, he becomes of a similar nature <gloss>possessing the temperament of an ascetic</gloss>.

# Chapter 15: Results of the Tenth, Eleventh, and Twelfth Houses

If the Lord of the Ascendant <note>Lagnēśvara: the planet ruling the first house of the birth chart</note> is aspected <note>aspected: "seen" by another planet's influence</note> by the Moon, the native becomes destitute = poor. Regarding the term "Beggar": if a planet is in its sign of exaltation <note>ucca-raśi: the sign where a planet is at its maximum strength</note> or if the Lord of the Ascendant is in its own exaltation and aspects the Lord of the Stars = the Moon, then the native becomes a beggar = a wandering ascetic. Regarding "situated in one place": if the Lord of the Ascendant is aspected by many (more than three) planets situated in a single house, the native becomes initiated = endowed with initiation (a renunciant). Regarding the timing of the results for these yogas, it is said: "That"—the results of the mentioned renunciation yoga should be predicted during the major period <term>Mahadasha: a long planetary period in Vedic astrology</term> or sub-period <term>Bhukti: a shorter division of a Mahadasha</term> of the planet that signifies that specific house. || 19 ||

If Venus and the Moon aspect a weak Lord of the Ascendant, one becomes poor. If any planet, situated in its exaltation degree, aspects the Moon, one becomes a beggar (monk). If many planets are situated in one place and aspect the Lord of the Ascendant, one becomes initiated. All these results occur during the Dasha-Bhukti of the yoga-producing planet and the house-significator. || 19 ||

## If the Lord of the Moon's sign or the Lord of the Ascendant is aspected by the Son of the Sun (Saturn), one becomes initiated.
## If the Moon is in a sign of Mars, in a decan <note>Drekkana: a 10-degree division of a zodiac sign</note> of Saturn, and is aspected by Saturn, one becomes an ascetic. || 20 ||

Regarding "the Lord of the Moon's sign": if the Lord of the sign occupied by the Moon at birth is aspected by the Son of the Sun = Saturn, or if the Lord of the Ascendant = the ruler of the birth-lagna aspects it, then the native becomes initiated = a renunciant.

Regarding "in a sign of Mars": if the Cold-Rayed One = the Moon, is in a sign of Mars = either Aries or Scorpio, or is in a decan or ninth-part <term>Navamsha: a 3-degree 20-minute division of a sign</term> belonging to Saturn, and furthermore, is aspected by Saturn = seen by Saturn, the native becomes an ascetic = a wandering monk who has conquered his senses. On this, Varahamihira <note>A famous 6th-century Indian astronomer and astrologer</note> also says:
> "If the Lord of the Birth (Ascendant) is not aspected by others but aspects the Son of the Sun (Saturn), or aspects the Lord of the Moon's sign <unclear>strength...</unclear> one receives initiation; likewise if the Moon is in a decan of Saturn or in a portion (Amsha) of Mars or Saturn and is aspected by Saturn." This should be considered. || 20 ||

If Saturn or the Lord of the Ascendant aspects the ruler of the sign where the Moon is placed, one becomes initiated. If the Moon is in a sign of Mars, in a decan of Saturn, and Saturn aspects it, one becomes an ascetic. || 20 ||

## When Jupiter, Mars, Saturn, and the Ascendant are aspected by or joined with Saturn,
## and Jupiter is in the 9th house from the Ascendant, even in a Kingly Yoga, one becomes a "Tirthakrit." || 21 ||

Regarding "Jupiter, etc.": if Jupiter, Mars, Saturn, and the Ascendant are aspected by Saturn, and furthermore, Jupiter is in the "Dharma" house = the 9th house from the Ascendant, then even if there is a Kingly Yoga <term>Raja Yoga: a combination indicating power and status</term> in the native's chart, they become a "Tirthakrit" = a composer of scriptures <note>Tirthakrit usually refers to a Tirthankara or a great spiritual teacher who "makes a ford" across the river of worldly life</note>. Here, in the phrase "Jupiter, Mars, Saturn, and the Ascendant," a doubt arises: if Saturn is to aspect Saturn, it is logically inconsistent. Therefore, the correct interpretation is: if the *signs* of Jupiter, Mars, and Saturn (Sagittarius, Pisces, Aries, Scorpio, Capricorn, and Aquarius) are aspected by Saturn. This, along with the connection to the influence of Saturn's region arising from the organs of action, should be reflected upon. || 21 ||

If Saturn aspects the signs of Jupiter, Mars, and Saturn, and Jupiter is in the 9th house from the Ascendant, then even if a Raja Yoga exists, one becomes an ascetic who visits holy places (a Tirthakrit). || 21 ||

## If the Moon is in the ninth house and is not aspected by any other planets,
## even if born in a Kingly Yoga, the native becomes an initiated King. || 22 ||

Regarding "in the ninth house": If the Moon is in the ninth house from the Ascendant and is not aspected by any other planet, then even if born into a Kingly Yoga, the native becomes an initiated = a king who has taken up renunciation. Just as today, one might be a Lord of a Province (Mandaleshvara) or a great leader, yet become a wandering monk. || 22 ||

# With Commentary on the Jataka Parijata

If no planets aspect <note>aspect: in astrology, the angular relationship between planets that allows them to influence one another</note> the Moon in the ninth house, even one born into a Royal Yoga <note>Yoga: a specific planetary configuration or "union" that produces a particular result</note> will become an initiated ascetic king. || 22 ||

### If Jupiter, the Moon, and the Ascendant are aspected by Saturn, and Jupiter is in the ninth house, one born under a Royal Yoga becomes a founder of sacred teachings.
### If Saturn is situated in the ninth house and is not aspected by any other planets, even if there is a Royal Yoga, the lord of the earth becomes an initiated ascetic. || 23 ||

**Regarding "If Jupiter, the Moon, and the Ascendant":** Jupiter (the teacher of the gods), the Moon, and the Ascendant (the rising sign) being aspected by Saturn (the son of Arka), and furthermore, if Jupiter is in the ninth house (the house of Dharma), then a person born under a Royal Yoga becomes a "Tirthakrit"—a creator of scriptures or sacred systems. As the specific saying goes:

> If Jupiter, the Moon, and the Ascendant are aspected by Saturn, and Jupiter is in the ninth house,
> one born of a royal birth becomes a maker of scriptures and not a secular king.

**Regarding "Situated in the ninth house":** Saturn (the slow-mover, called *Mandaga* because he moves slowly) being in the ninth house and not being seen (aspected) by other planets—even if a Royal Yoga is present, the person born becomes an initiate (one who has taken up the life of a wandering monk), a King of Kings who has renounced. In the absence of a Royal Yoga, a person born under this configuration would simply enter the life of renunciation. As it is said:

> "If Saturn is placed in the ninth house, free from the sight of all other planets,
> even a king born of a Royal Yoga becomes endowed with initiation.
> In the absence of a Royal Yoga, a man born in this configuration
> will undoubtedly become an initiate through the power of this yoga." || 23 ||

If Jupiter, the Moon, and the Ascendant are aspected by Saturn and Jupiter is in the ninth, even one born in a Royal Yoga becomes a creator of sacred paths (scriptures). If Saturn is in the ninth house and not seen by any others, even in a Royal Yoga, one becomes an initiated King of Kings. || 23 ||

---

Now, the different types of renunciation based on the combination of planets are described from here until verse thirty-nine.

### If Venus, the Sun, Mars, and Saturn are very powerful; or Jupiter, Mars, the Sun, and Saturn;
### or Mars, the Moon, Jupiter, and Saturn—if these come together, they produce an ascetic. || 24 ||

**Regarding "Venus, the Sun...":** 
1. Venus, the Sun, Mars, and Saturn. Or—
2. Jupiter, Mars, the Sun, and Saturn. Or—
3. Mars, the Moon, Jupiter, and Saturn—

If these are "very powerful" (possessing full strength) and "come together" (conjoined in any single house), they produce an ascetic (a forest-dwelling hermit). This means a person born under any of these combinations becomes a practitioner of austerities. || 24 ||

If Venus, the Sun, Mars, and Saturn; or Jupiter, Mars, the Sun, and Saturn; or Mars, the Moon, Jupiter, and Saturn are in one place with full strength, they produce an ascetic (the person born in these three yogas becomes a practitioner of penance). || 24 ||

# Chapter on the Results of the Tenth, Eleventh, and Twelfth Houses || 12 ||

### If the Lord of the Tenth House is joined by four planets and situated in a Quadrant or a Trine, the person is liberated.
### If four planets are situated in the Tenth House, the person born attains Renunciation; so it has been stated by the Great Sages. || 25 ||

*If the Lord...* If the Lord of the Tenth House <note>the house of career and action</note> is joined by any four planets and is placed in a Quadrant <note>houses 1, 4, 7, or 10</note> or a Trine <note>houses 1, 5, or 9</note>, the person born shall be liberated <note>attain Moksha or spiritual freedom</note>. If any four planets are situated in the Tenth House, the person born attains Renunciation <note>Pravrajya; the life of a wandering monk</note>; so it is said by the Great Sages. In that case, it should be said that the person attains the specific type of renunciation associated with whichever of the four planets is the strongest. || 25 ||

->If the Lord of the Tenth House is with four planets in a Quadrant or Trine, one becomes liberated. If four planets are in the Tenth, the person becomes an ascetic; so say the sages. || 25 ||<-

### By Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus; or by Moon, Mars, Saturn, Jupiter, Mercury, and Sun;
### Or by Mars, Moon, Sun, Saturn, Venus, and Mercury; joined together, a man becomes a keeper of vows. || 29 ||

*By Sun...* 1—By Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus; or 2—By Moon, Mars, Saturn, Jupiter, Mercury, and Sun; or 3—By Mars, Moon, Sun, Saturn, Venus, and Mercury; by these planets being joined in a single place, a man becomes a keeper of vows. One born in any of these combinations is a person who observes strict rules and religious vows. || 29 ||

->If Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus are in one sign; or Moon, Mars, Saturn, Jupiter, Mercury, and Sun are in one sign; or Mars, Moon, Sun, Saturn, Venus, and Mercury are together, the person born in these yogas becomes a practitioner of religious vows. || 29 ||<-

# With the Commentary of Jataka Parijata

<page-num>466</page-num>

If the Lord of the Ascendant <note>Lagnadhipa: the planet ruling the first house of the birth chart</note> sees Saturn, or if the Son of the Sun (Saturn), being strong, sees the Lord of the Ascendant who is devoid of strength, then indeed this is a **Yoga for Renunciation** <note>Sanyasa Yoga: a planetary combination indicating one will become a monk or ascetic</note>. The meaning is that one born under this yoga will certainly become a wandering mendicant <note>Parivrat</note>. Here, Varahamihira <note>A famous 6th-century Indian astronomer and astrologer</note> has stated that the Lord of the Moon-sign <note>Janmadhipa</note> may be considered in place of the Lord of the Ascendant. Thus, his statement:

> "If a planet other than the Lord of the Moon-sign sees the Son of the Sun (Saturn), or if Saturn sees the Lord of the Moon-sign, provided they are strong, the person receives initiation. This also occurs if the Moon is in a decan <note>Drekkana: a 10-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign</note> of Saturn, or in a Navamsha <note>A 3-degree 20-minute subdivision</note> of Mars or Saturn, and is aspected by Saturn." || 40 ||

If the Lord of the Ascendant sees Saturn and no other planets see the Lord of the Ascendant, or if Saturn sees a weak Lord of the Ascendant, a Renunciation Yoga occurs. That is, the person born in this yoga becomes an ascetic. || 40 ||

> If the Moon is in a decan of Saturn and is aspected by Saturn, the person becomes a beggar-monk. Likewise, if the Moon is in a Navamsha of Saturn or Mars and is aspected by Saturn, the same result follows. If the planet bestowing renunciation is joined with Gulika <note>A mathematical point in the sky considered malefic</note>, or with Rahu or Ketu <note>The North and South Nodes of the Moon</note>, or enters a cruel subdivision, it surely makes the ascetic one who has fallen from proper conduct. || 41 ||

Regarding the Moon: if the Moon has entered a decan of Saturn anywhere in the chart and is aspected by Saturn, the person born becomes a beggar-monk (a wandering mendicant). Or, if the Moon enters a Navamsha belonging to either Saturn or Mars and is aspected by Saturn, he becomes a beggar-monk.

The "planet bestowing renunciation" refers to the planet causing the yoga for wandering. If it is joined with Gulika, or with the "Serpent-Flag" (Rahu or Ketu), or if it enters a cruel Navamsha <note>A subdivision ruled by a malefic planet</note>, then it certainly makes the man among ascetics one who is "devoid of conduct"—meaning he is fallen or corrupt. Thus it is said in the *Sarvartha Chintamani*:

> "When the Friend of the Night-Lily (the Moon) is seen by Saturn, they call it such a yoga. Likewise, if the Moon is in a Navamsha of Saturn or Mars and is seen by Saturn. If the Lord of the Renunciation Yoga is with Rahu, in a cruel subdivision, or joined with Gulika, they speak of the failure of renunciation; his vows will be broken if devoid of the influence of benefic planets." || 41 ||

If Saturn aspects the Moon in a decan of Saturn, or if Saturn aspects the Moon while it is in a Navamsha of Saturn or Mars, the person becomes a beggar-monk (ascetic). If the planet giving renunciation is with Gulika, Rahu, or Ketu, and is in a cruel subdivision, the person becomes an ascetic devoid of proper conduct. || 41 ||

> Those born when the planets are eclipsed by the Sun's rays are not initiated, though they may be devoted to those paths. If the planets are defeated or aspected by others, they are only "initiated" in name or speech. || 42 ||

Now he states an exception to the previously mentioned types of wandering life arising from planetary yogas: "Eclipsed by the Sun's rays." In the aforementioned yogas involving four or more planets, if those strong planets are "lost in the Sun's rays" (combust), men are "uninitiated"—meaning they do not obtain full renunciation—but they remain devoted to those paths. The point is this: among the four...

# Chapter 15: Results of the Tenth, Eleventh, and Twelfth Houses

Among the planets starting with the Sun, as many as are strong, so many types of <term>Pravrajya</term><note>Renunciation or entering a religious order</note> do they create. However, if those planets are "combust" <note>original: "astamita"; rendered invisible by being too close to the Sun</note>, they do not grant their specific type of renunciation, though the person may remain a faithful follower of those who have taken such vows.

**Initiation by Request Only:** If those planets are strong but "defeated" <note>original: "nijitai"; losing in a planetary war/conjunction</note> or are aspected <note>seen</note> by other planets, the individuals become those who merely request initiation <note>original: "abhiyachita-matra-dikshita"</note>; they seek the vows but do not actually attain or maintain them.

<margin>Notes—A planet becomes combust when it is within a certain number of degrees from the Sun. This distance varies for each planet. Even if it is in the second sign from the Sun, if it falls within these degrees, it is combust. The degrees of combustion are as follows:</margin>

The Moon at 12, Mars at 17, Jupiter at 11, Saturn at 15, Mercury at 13, and Venus at 10. <note>original: "Daseindavah..."</note> It is stated in the *Siddhanta Shiromani* <note>A famous 12th-century mathematical astronomy text by Bhaskara II</note> that for Mercury and Venus, when in retrograde motion, these limits are reduced by 2 degrees (to 12 and 8 respectively).

Furthermore, the characteristics of a "defeated" planet are described by Varahamihira <note>A 6th-century polymath and astrologer</note>:
> "A planet is considered defeated if it is situated to the south, looks harsh, is trembling, is retreating, appears small, is overtaken, looks unnatural, is lusterless, or is discolored."

The fruition of the mentioned renunciations should be understood to occur during the <term>Dasha</term><note>Planetary period</note> of the planet causing the yoga.
> "A person definitely receives initiation during the period of the planet that is strong and capable of giving initiation." || 42 ||

*If the planets causing renunciation are combust with the Sun, the person becomes an uninitiated ascetic (without a mantra). If those planets are strong, they will have faith in that path (but not be an ascetic). If they are defeated in war and seen by others, they take initiation only by begging for it.* || 42 ||

### On the Yogas for Livelihood

Now, in this section on "Livelihood Yogas," the author explains how the subject will earn wealth and by what profession they will spend their life.

> Wealth is obtained from the father, mother, enemy, friend, brother, wife, or servant, according to the Sun and other planets occupying the tenth house from the Ascendant or the Moon. Alternatively, the profession is determined by the lord of the Navamsha <note>The 1/9th divisional chart</note> occupied by the lord of the tenth house from the Ascendant, Moon, or Sun. || 43 ||

**Obtaining Wealth:** From the <term>Hora</term><note>The Ascendant or rising sign</note> and the Moon, one should consider the planets in the tenth house. From the Sun and others, wealth comes respectively from: the father, mother, enemy, friend, brother, wife, and servant. For example: if the Sun is in the tenth from the Ascendant or Moon, one should predict wealth from the father. If the Moon is in the tenth, from the mother. If Mars is in the tenth, from an enemy. If Mercury is in the tenth, from a friend. If Jupiter is in the tenth, from a brother. If Venus is in the tenth, from a wife. If Saturn is in the tenth, from a servant or laborer. Here, one must examine the planets in the tenth from both the Ascendant and the Moon. If there are planets in both, consider both. Both planets will provide wealth during their respective major and sub-periods. Among them, the stronger planet will be more significant.

Now, what if the tenth house from both the Ascendant and the Moon is empty (without planets)? The text says: "By the lord of the <term>Navamsha</term>..." One must look at the lords of the tenth houses from the Ascendant, Moon, and Sun. Find which Navamsha signs these lords have gone into; the lords of those Navamshas will determine the profession or source of wealth. This must be carefully weighed. The lords of the tenth from the Ascendant, Moon, and Sun...

<header>With the Commentary on the Jataka Parijata—</header>

In whichever <term>Navamsha</term><note>A sub-divisional chart where a sign is divided into nine parts; used to determine the hidden strength of planets.</note> the planets are situated, the person’s income comes through the nature and occupation associated with the lord of that Navamsha.
And so it has been said—
Those planets situated in the tenth house from the Ascendant or from the Moon are all known to be givers of wealth during their respective periods (<term>Dashas</term>).
The planet that is the lord of the tenth house from the Ascendant, the Sun, or the Moon—whichever Navamsha that lord occupies at that time, one should predict wealth through the occupation of the lord of that Navamsha. When there are many such planets, they all certainly provide wealth during their own periods.

Now we consider the means of livelihood—A person’s livelihood is derived from the substances associated with the planet situated in the tenth house from the Ascendant or the Moon. If the Sun is in the tenth from the Ascendant or the Moon, wealth is obtained from the father. If it is the Moon, from the mother. If Mars, from an enemy. If Mercury, from a friend. If Jupiter, from a brother. If Venus, from a wife. If Saturn, from a servant. If there are planets in the tenth from both the Ascendant and the Moon, both will give results in their respective periods. If there are many planets in the tenth, all will give results in their periods. If there are no planets in the tenth from the Ascendant or the Moon, then one should predict the acquisition of wealth through the occupation of the lord of the Navamsha in which the ruler of the tenth house from the Ascendant, Moon, or Sun is placed. || 43 ||

-> One should predict the acquisition of wealth from whichever is stronger between the Ascendant and the Moon. Those who know this science say that livelihood is determined by the lord of the Navamsha sign in which the Lord of the Tenth House (<term>Karmesha</term>) is situated. || 43 || <-

*Acquisition of wealth:* Between the Ascendant and the Moon—whichever is more powerful at the time of birth—from that, one should predict the gain of wealth. This means that one should declare the gain of wealth based on the authority of the planet in the tenth house from the stronger of the two (Ascendant or Moon); if there is no planet in the tenth, then by the occupation of the Lord of the Tenth House.
As stated in the *Saravali* <note>A classic 8th-century Sanskrit text on astrology by Kalyanavarman.</note>:
> The profession arises from the nature of the planet in the tenth from the Ascendant or the Moon, whichever is stronger. Success or loss follows the strength or weakness of that lord.

In this context, it is not proper to take only the strongest planet, as a person is seen to have income from various sources. It is appropriate to say that wealth comes in abundance from a strong planet and in small measure from a weak one.

Now he describes the *Vritti* (Livelihood)—*Karmesha*, etc. The Lord of the Tenth (from the Ascendant or the Moon), in whichever Navamsha he stays, according to the lord of that Navamsha sign, the experts—the scholars who know destiny—have declared the livelihood. The life of the native should be described by the occupation of the lord of the Navamsha occupied by the Lord of the Tenth from the Ascendant or the Moon. || 43 ||

Between the Ascendant and the Moon, whichever is stronger, the lord of the tenth house from that point is situated in a certain Navamsha; one should predict the livelihood from the lord of that Navamsha. || 43 ||

### Now, the Occupations of the Planets.

> If the Navamsha lord is the **Sun**, the person lives by trading in medicines, wool, grass, water, grain, or gold, or through mutual mediation and the work of a messenger. || 44 ||

> If the Navamsha lord is the **Moon**, wealth comes from the purchase and sale of water-born products <note>such as pearls or shells</note>, from agriculture, from paths of entertainment like clay-modeling or arts, from the support of kings or women, or from the sale of clothes. || 45 ||

> If the Navamsha lord is **Mars**, the person lives through metallurgy <note>original: "dispute of metals"</note>, various types of battle, arguments involving fire, or by engaging in conflict; also through courageous deeds or even the life of a thief. || 46 ||

> If the Navamsha lord is **Mercury**, the profession is through crafts, poetry, traditional knowledge, the path of the scriptures, or through the knowledge of the movements of the stars <note>astronomy/astrology</note>. || 47 ||

> If the Navamsha lord is **Jupiter**, the livelihood is through the worship of priests and gods, through the path of teaching, through the Puranas, scriptures, traditional lore, and the path of ethics, or by giving religious instruction without usury. || 48 ||

> If the Navamsha lord is **Venus**, the ancients say life is sustained through gold, rubies, horses, the purchase of cows, or by the sale of molasses, cooked rice, alkaline substances, and curd, or through the attraction of women. || 49 ||

**In the Navamsha of Saturn, one earns through despicable paths, through crafts made of wood, through acts of violence and killing, through carrying heavy loads, through deceiving people, or through the root of mutual enmity.** ॥ 50 ॥

What was stated in the previous verse—"livelihood based on the sign of the Navamsha occupied by the Lord of the 10th House"—the specific occupations for the planets are now described: **Starting with medicine, etc.**

**In the Sun's Navamsha** = If the Sun is the lord of the Navamsha occupied by the Lord of the 10th House, the native lives by: **Medicine** = drugs; **Wool** = hair of sheep etc. <note>wool, silk</note>; **Grasses** = fodder; **Water-grains** = crops grown in water; **Gold** = bullion; by the trade of these = buying and selling; **Pearls etc.** = trade of pearls etc. <note>pearls etc.</note>; and by **mutual messenger work** = acting as a go-between or envoy here and there ॥ 44 ॥

**In the Moon's Navamsha** = If the Moon is the lord of the Navamsha occupied by the Lord of the 10th House: by the buying and selling of **water-born things** = things produced in water such as shells, pearls, and fish; from **agriculture** = farming work; from **the path of clay-pottery and entertainment** = through delighting others using earthen vessels; from the **patronage of royal women** = wealth obtained by seeking refuge with the wives of kings; or from the **purchase of garments** = buying and selling of clothes etc., one attains a livelihood ॥ 45 ॥

**In Mars's Navamsha** = If Mars is the lord of the Navamsha occupied by the Lord of the 10th House: from **disputes over metals** (gold etc.) = through legal dealings <note>original: "vivādo vyavahāraḥ syād" - Amarakosha defines 'vivada' as legal procedure or transaction</note>; from **types of battle** = war; from **the use of extinguished fire** = dealing in charcoal <note>extinguished fire/coals</note>; from **engaging in quarrels** = the business of open conflict; from **daring paths** = impulsive or reckless actions; and through **the occupation of a thief** = criminal acts, one spends their life ॥ 46 ॥

**In Mercury's Navamsha** = If Mercury is the lord of the Navamsha occupied by the Lord of the 10th House: through **crafts etc.** = making paintings, books, or clothes; through **poetry** = composing poems; from **the path of traditional sciences** = the Samhitas and other scriptures; through **knowledge of the stars** = calculating fortunes <term>Jyotish: Vedic astrology and astronomy</term>; through **studying and chanting the Vedas for others** = for the sake of another, studying Vedic mantras and performing Japa; and through **priestly duties and officiating sacrifices** = from the work of a family priest and performing rituals, one's inclination = livelihood arises ॥ 47 ॥

**In Jupiter's Navamsha** = If Jupiter is the lord of the Navamsha occupied by the Lord of the 10th House: through **worship of the gods on earth and the deities** = honoring Brahmins and gods; through **the path of a teacher** = the work of teaching students; from **the path of the Puranas, Scriptures, Traditions, and Ethics**; and through **religious instruction**, the wise say one's livelihood is earned without usury ॥ 48 ॥

**In Venus's Navamsha** = In the Navamsha of the son of Bhrigu: they say life is sustained through **the trade of gold, rubies, elephants, and horses**; from **the purchase of cows**; by **selling jaggery, rice, salt, and curd**; and through **the allure of women** ॥ 49 ॥

**In Saturn's Navamsha** = In the Navamsha of Saturn: through **despicable paths** = contemptible work; through **crafts made of wood** = making wooden carvings etc.; through **killing etc.** = hurting or killing others; from **carrying heavy loads** = physical labor; from **deceiving people** = the act of cheating; and from **the root of mutual enmity** = based on mutual hatred, one's occupation should be predicted ॥ 50 ॥

**Notes**—Here, generally, a despicable livelihood is mentioned for the Navamsha of malefic planets <note>Mars, Saturn, Sun</note> and a good livelihood for the Navamsha of benefic planets <note>Jupiter, Venus, Mercury, Moon</note>. However, one must speak of the degree of good or bad results only after observing the specific position of that Navamsha lord. For even a malefic planet, if strong and placed in a benefic division, attains goodness. Similarly, even a benefic planet, if weak and placed in a debilitated, inimical, or malefic division, will not be so auspicious. This must be considered ॥ 44-50 ॥

If the Lord of the 10th house from the Ascendant or the Moon is in the **Navamsha** of the Sun, one should predict a livelihood through medicine <note>drugs</note>, wool, grass, water-grains, gold, pearls etc., through trade, or through acting as a messenger. ॥ 44 ॥

## With Commentary on the Jataka Parijata

If the lord of the tenth house from the Ascendant <note>Lagna</note> or the Moon is situated in the Navamsha <note>a 1/9th divisional chart used for fine-tuning strength</note> of the **Moon**, the person earns a livelihood through trade in water-born goods (conch shells, oyster shells, pearls, water chestnuts, wild rice, or fish), through agriculture, through the making of clay toys or musical instruments for entertainment, through wealth received from the King's wife, or through the purchase and sale of textiles. || 45 ||

If the lord of the tenth house from the Ascendant or the Moon is in the Navamsha of **Mars**, the person lives by trading in metals (gold, silver, copper, brass, etc.), through warfare, by trading in coal and ash, through disputes, theft, or acts of daring. || 46 ||

If the lord of the tenth house from the Ascendant or the Moon is in the Navamsha of **Mercury**, the livelihood comes from crafts <note>manual arts or engineering</note>, poetry, the Puranas <note>ancient Hindu texts</note>, the path of Dharma-shastra <note>law and ethics</note>, the science of astrology, reciting the Vedas for others, chanting prayers <note>Japa</note>, performing priestly duties, or conducting sacrifices. || 47 ||

If the lord of the tenth house from the Ascendant or the Moon is in the Navamsha of **Jupiter**, the livelihood comes from serving Brahmins or deities, from being a teacher, from the ethical path of the Puranas and religious scriptures, or from religious preaching. || 48 ||

If the lord of the tenth house from the Ascendant or the Moon is in the Navamsha of **Venus**, the learned say the person lives by trading in gold, gems, elephants, horses, or cows; by buying and selling jaggery, rice, salt, and yogurt; or through the allurements of women. || 49 ||

If the lord of the tenth house from the Ascendant or the Moon is in the Navamsha of **Saturn**, the livelihood comes from despicable paths, woodworking, slaughtering, carrying heavy loads, cheating people, or through mutual enmity. || 50 ||

-> If the Benefics are placed in the four angles <note>Kendra houses: 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th</note>, the person becomes the best of their lineage, a sustainer of the family, and a ruler. <-
-> They will be endowed with omniscience, intellect, wealth, fame, and virtues, or they will be pleasing to kings. || 51 || <-

Now, he describes the Royal Yoga <note>Raja Yoga: a combination for success and power</note> when benefics are in the four angles: **"By Benefics..."** Benefics = auspicious planets (Jupiter, Mercury, Venus, and the waxing Moon). If they are situated in the four angles (1, 4, 7, 10) as far as possible, the person becomes the most respected in their family, a sustainer of the lineage, and a king endowed with omniscience, intellect, wealth, fame, and a multitude of virtues. Alternatively, they become men who bring joy to kings (such as good ministers). If malefic planets are in the four angles, the opposite results should be predicted. Thus, in some books, there is this reading:

> If Malefics are placed in the four angles, the person is devoted to low vows and conduct, and is destitute.
> They are fools, inclined toward the wives and wealth of others, though they may occasionally be brave and liked by the king. || 51 ||

If there are auspicious planets in all four angles, they make the person of noble lineage, or they make the person omniscient, wise, wealthy, famous, virtuous, and one who pleases the king. || 51 ||

-> If Benefics are in the tenth house or the tenth Navamsha, the person is always devoted to meritorious deeds. <-
-> If Malefics are there, the person is of a sinful nature; this applies from the Ascendant or the Moon. || 52 || <-

Now he describes the inclination toward merit or sin: **"Karma..."** If Benefics = auspicious planets are in the tenth house from the Ascendant or in its Navamsha (if there is no benefic in the tenth house, there should be one in the Navamsha of the tenth sign), then the person born is always devoted to merit = engaged in good deeds. If Malefics = inauspicious planets are in the tenth house or its Navamsha, the person is always of a sinful nature.

**"Or from the Moon..."** If there are no planets in the tenth or the tenth Navamsha from the Ascendant, then the same results occur based on the tenth house or Navamsha from the Moon. Here, a distinction in the results should be made based on the influence of benefics or malefics in the tenth house or the tenth Navamsha from either the Ascendant or the Moon. || 52 ||

If there is a benefic planet in the tenth house or the tenth Navamsha from the Ascendant or the Moon, the person is always devoted to merit. If there is a malefic planet in the same way, they become a sinner. || 52 ||

-> Where the lords of the tenth house and its Navamsha are placed, if the lord of that place is a malefic planet, <-
-> or is associated with "smoky" <note>Upagrahas or dark/shadow planets like Dhumadi</note> planets, the person becomes devoted to sin. || 53 ||
