# Chapter 12: Results of the Tenth, Eleventh, and Twelfth Houses

Now he describes the yoga <note>astrological combination</note> for being inclined toward sinful deeds: **The lord of the sign and Navamsha of the tenth house...** If the lord of the sign where the ruler of the tenth house's Navamsha <note>a 1/9th divisional chart used for fine detail</note> is located is a malefic planet, and is associated with a secondary planet <term>Upagraha; minor mathematical points like Dhuma</term> such as Dhuma, then the person born will be **inclined toward sin**, meaning they will enjoy performing sinful actions. || 53 ||

If the lord of the place where the ruler of the tenth house resides is a malefic planet and is associated with secondary planets like Dhuma, the person will be engaged in sin. || 53 ||

->**Success in undertakings when the Sun is in the tenth from the Moon; courageous and sinful-minded with Mars.**<-
->**A scholar with Mercury; like a king with Jupiter; a seeker of pleasure with Venus; and afflicted by grief with Saturn. || 54 ||**<-

Now he describes the results based on the placement of planets in the tenth house from the Moon, starting with the results of individual planets: **Success in undertakings...** From the **Moon-sign** <note>the sign where the Moon was located at birth</note>, if the **Sun** is in the **tenth house**, the person born has **success in undertakings**, meaning their resolutions reach fruition; in short, their desires are fulfilled. If **Mars** is in the tenth from the Moon, the person is **courageous**, meaning they act without overthinking, and they are also **sinful-minded**. If **Mercury** is so placed, they become a **scholar** or a learned man. If **Jupiter** is so placed, they become **like a king**, though not a king himself. If **Venus** is so placed, they are a **seeker of pleasure**, possessing various enjoyments. If **Saturn** is so placed, they are **afflicted by grief**, meaning their mind is filled with anxiety. || 54 ||

If the Sun is in the tenth from the Moon-sign, there is success in undertakings (whatever work they start will surely be completed); if Mars, courageous and sinful-minded; if Mercury, a scholar; if Jupiter, like a king; if Venus, a seeker of pleasure; and if Saturn, they will be tormented by grief. || 54 ||

->**With the Sun and Mars in the tenth from the Moon, one is intoxicated and devoted to others' wives—**<-
->**An astrologer with Mercury, and fond of water-wealth, women, and ornaments.**<-
->**With Jupiter, one's goals are achieved and they are honored by kings; with Venus,**<-
->**They enjoy the king's affection and an increase in women and wealth; with Saturn, they are miserable and poor. || 55 ||**<-

Now he describes the results of the Sun combined with Mars and others in the tenth from the Moon: **From the Moon...** If the **Sun** is in the tenth from the Moon along **with Mars**, the person is **intoxicated** and **devoted to others' wives**. If the Sun is **with Mercury** in the tenth from the Moon, they are an **astrologer**, meaning an expert in the science of Jyotisha, and **fond of water-wealth, women, and ornaments**, meaning they desire wealth from the water (such as shells and pearls), women (auspicious wives), and decorations (jewelry). If the Sun is **with Jupiter**, they are **successful in their goals** and **honored by kings**, meaning dear to the ruler. If the Sun is **with Venus**, they **enjoy the king's affection and an increase in women and wealth**. If the Sun is **with Saturn** in the tenth from the Moon, the person is **miserable**, having an unhappy face, and **poor**, meaning destitute. || 55 ||

If the Sun is with Mars in the tenth from the Moon, one is intoxicated and a pursuer of others' wives. With Mercury, an astrologer, fond of water-wealth, women, ornaments, etc. With Jupiter, successful (fulfilled desires) and honored by kings (a minister). With Venus, possessing the king's affection and growth in women and wealth; and with Saturn, unhappy and poor. || 55 ||

> If Jupiter is joined with Venus, one becomes a leader of the priestly class, beloved by kings, and a scholar.

Now he describes the results of Mars and other pairs of planets in the tenth from the Moon—"From the Moon," etc. When the son of the Earth (Mars) is joined with Mercury and is in the tenth house from the Moon, the person born lives by the scriptures <note>original: "shastropajivi"</note>—meaning they earn a livelihood through reading and teaching the sacred texts. This is like a modern person who considers himself a scholar. If Mars is joined with the Teacher (Jupiter) in the tenth from the Moon, one becomes a leader of low-born people <note>the uneducated or laboring classes</note>. If Mars is joined with the son of Bhrigu (Venus) in that position, one becomes a foreigner—living in a distant land—and a merchant or trader. If joined with the son of the Sun (Saturn), one becomes daring <note>enterprising</note> and childless.

### Now he describes the results of Mercury joined with Jupiter and others in the tenth from the Moon—"Of the Moon," etc.
When Mercury is joined with the Teacher (Jupiter) and situated in the tenth house from the Moon, the person born has a neuter-like body <note>lacking strong masculine or feminine traits</note>, speaks with humility or distress, is famous, and is a favorite of kings. When Mercury is joined with the son of Bhrigu (Venus) in the tenth from the Moon, the person born possesses knowledge, a wife, and wealth. When Mercury is joined with the son of the Sun (Saturn) in the tenth from the Moon, the person born becomes a scribe (book-writer), or is inclined toward irregular conduct—meaning they lean toward contrary behavior (like a modern "reformist" person).

### Now the results of Jupiter joined with other pairs in the tenth from the Moon—"Jupiter," etc.
If Jupiter is joined with Venus and placed in the tenth from the Moon, the person born is a leader of the priestly class <note>original: "viprajanapa"</note>, a favorite of the king (a royal minister), and a scholar or wise man. If Jupiter is joined with the son of the Sun (Saturn) in that position, one is clever at causing distress to all people—meaning they are skilled and intent on troubling others or capable of crushing all folk—yet they possess a mind of firm resolve in starting tasks.

### Now the result of the conjunction of Venus and Saturn in the tenth from the Moon—"Fragrant," etc.
When Saturn is joined with the teacher of the demons (Venus) and is in the tenth house from the position of the Moon, the person born becomes a painter using fragrant blue powders and such, a physician (doctor), or a merchant (trader). || 56-58 ||

# Chapter 15: Results of the Tenth, Eleventh, and Twelfth Houses

Now, the consideration of the native's **authority** is being made:

In the **place of authority** <note>the Tenth House from the Ascendant</note>, if there is a **benefic planet** <note>a naturally auspicious planet like Jupiter or Venus</note>, or if that house is joined with or aspected by a benefic, or if the Lord of the Tenth is in a **beautiful division** <note>a Navamsha or sub-division ruled by a benefic</note>, the person born becomes a **giver of orders** <note>one who holds executive power or command</note>. 
<margin>The Amarakosha dictionary defines "Agya" (authority) as: instruction, direction, command, edict, discipline, and order.</margin>

If the **Lord of Authority** <note>Lord of the Tenth House</note> is **joined with Saturn**, aspected by the **Lord of the Eighth House**, or is in a **cruel division** <note>a sub-division ruled by a malefic</note> or situated in a cardinal sign, that native carries out **cruel orders** <note>reprehensible or harsh commands</note>. || 59-60 ||

**If the Lord of the Tenth is a benefic, is joined by a benefic, is aspected by a benefic, or reaches a benefic division, the native will be one who gives orders. || 59 ||**

**If the Lord of the Tenth is joined with Saturn, is aspected by the Lord of the Eighth, and is in a cruel division or a cardinal sign, he exercises cruel authority. || 60 ||**

### Now, the consideration of Fame, Honor, Agriculture, Trade, and Sleep.

->If the Lord of the Night (Moon) is in Cancer, aspected by Jupiter and Venus,<-
->and situated in a Paravata or similar division, one becomes possessed of good fame and wealth. || 61 ||<-

Regarding **"situated in Cancer"**: When the **Lord of the Night** <note>the Moon</note> is in **Cancer** <note>its own home sign</note>, aspected by **Jupiter and Venus**, and has reached the **Paravata or other special divisions** <note>technical Vaisheshikansha grades of planetary strength</note>, the native becomes a possessor of **good fame** <note>one who performs spiritual or altruistic deeds</note> and **wealthy**. || 61 ||

**If the Moon is in the sign of Cancer, aspected by Jupiter and Venus, and the Moon is in its Paravata division, the native will be wealthy and possess good fame. || 61 ||**

->If the Lord of Honor is joined with a benefic, or placed between benefics,<-
->or in the division of a benefic planet, one is famous and dignified. || 62 ||<-

Regarding **"Lord of Honor"**: The **meaning is clear**. || 62 ||

**If the Lord of the Tenth is joined with a benefic, or is between benefics, or is in the division of a benefic, the native will be famous, honorable, and dignified. || 62 ||**

->If the Tenth House is aspected by a malefic, joined by a malefic,<-
->and the Lord of Honor has attained a state of weak strength,<-
->the native becomes a slanderer, devoid of dignity, and lacking in the power and fame of their own work. || 63 ||<-

Regarding **"aspected by a malefic"**: If the **Tenth House** from the Ascendant is **aspected by a malefic planet**, or **joined by a malefic**, and the **Lord of Honor** <note>Lord of the Tenth</note> has **attained weakness** <note>debility</note> anywhere, the person born is a **slanderer** <note>full of scandal</note>, **devoid of dignity**, and also becomes **lacking in their own work, brilliance, strength, and fame**. || 63 ||

**If a weak Lord of the Tenth is in the tenth house, aspected by a malefic and joined by a malefic, the native will be a slanderer, without dignity, and devoid of the fruits of their labor, brilliance, strength, and fame. || 63 ||**

Now, the combination for many wives: Regarding **"Lord of the Tenth"**: If the **Lord of the Tenth and the Lord of its Navamsha** <note>the ruler of the sub-division where the 10th Lord sits</note> are both **connected to Saturn** <note>aspected by, joined with, in the sign of, or friends with Saturn</note>, and are **joined or aspected by the Lord of the Sixth**, then the person born will be **possessed of many wives** <note>associated with many women</note>. || 64 ||

**If the Lord of the Tenth and its Navamsha Lord are both related to Saturn and are seen by or joined with the Lord of the Sixth, he will have many wives. || 64 ||**

> If Mars and the Lord of the Fourth House are strong and positioned in a Quadrant, Trine, or the Eleventh House, and if the Lord of the Tenth House is aspected by or conjoined with Venus and the Moon, the person will possess wealth derived from agriculture and cattle. Now the author discusses the considerations for agriculture, cattle-wealth, commerce, and sleep—*If Mars and the Lord of the Fourth House...* If Mars <note>original: "Bhusunu"</note> and the Lord of the Fourth House <note>original: "Kshitirashipa"</note> are both strong and situated in the 1st, 4th, 7th, 10th, 5th, 9th, or 11th houses; and if the Lord of the Tenth House <note>the house of profession</note> is aspected by or conjoined with Venus and the Moon, the native will possess wealth from farming and livestock.

Regarding commerce—*If Mercury...* If Mercury <note>original: "Shashisuta," literally 'Son of the Moon'</note> is related to the Tenth House through any of the four types of astrological relationships, the native will be a <term>Vanijyashila</term> (one habitually engaged in trade).

Regarding sleep—*If benefics or malefics...* If the Tenth House is joined by a benefic or a malefic, the sleep will be <term>Sattvic</term> or <term>Tamasic</term> respectively. For instance, with a benefic in the tenth, one has pure sleep like a yogi; with a malefic, one has "dark" sleep (excessive or disturbed, like a sick person). If mixed—with both benefics and malefics—the sleep is <term>Rajasic</term> (restless/passionate, like a man of the world). || 65 ||

### Now, the Fruits of the House of Gains.

Now begins the analysis of the <term>Labha Bhava</term> (the Eleventh House of gains). First, the author describes the general nature of the house and the wealth granted by the Sun and other planets situated there:

> All authorities desire to see the acquisition of all types of collections through the House of Gains from the Ascendant. Any planet reaching the House of Gains while possessing full strength becomes a giver of wealth. If it is the Sun, wealth comes from one's own kin; if the Moon, from the mother's side; if Mars, from brothers, enemies, kings, or scholars. || 66 ||
> Jupiter grants wealth through the Vedas, scriptures, sacrifices, traditional conduct, and sons. Venus through women, theater, arts, and music. Saturn grants abundant grain and wealth earned through servants and agricultural labor. If aspected by or conjoined with planets like Brahmins (Jupiter/Venus), those classes become the givers of wealth. || 67 ||

*Through the House of Gains...* All experts in the science of horoscopy <note>Jyotisha</note> look to the Eleventh House from the Ascendant to determine the accumulation and gain of all types of wealth. The implication is that all increases in fortune should be judged from this house.

Any planet that is <term>Sakala-balayuta</term> (possessing full strength) and occupies the Eleventh House will be a <term>Vittada</term> (wealth-giver).

# Chapter 15: Results of the Tenth, Eleventh, and Twelfth Houses

### On the Sources of Wealth from the Eleventh House

If a planet is situated in the Eleventh House <note>The House of Gains or *Labha-sthana*</note> and possesses full strength, the individual gains wealth from their kinsmen. If the **Moon** is so placed, they acquire great wealth from the maternal side—specifically from the mother, maternal grandmother, or maternal aunts. If **Mars** is so placed, wealth comes from one's own efforts and from brothers. If **Mercury** <note>original: *Chandri* or *Budha*</note> is so placed, wealth is obtained through beloved ones, masters (employers), deities, Brahmins, friends, and the maternal uncle.

If **Jupiter** <note>original: *Jiva* or *Guru*</note> is in the House of Gains with full strength, the person gains wealth through the study and teaching of the Vedas and Scriptures, the performance of sacrifices <note>original: *Yajna*</note>, and through their sons. If **Venus** is so placed, wealth is acquired through women, poetry, drama, the arts (such as crafts), and music. If **Saturn** is in the House of Gains with full strength, the person attains prosperity in wealth and grain through the labor of female and male servants and through agricultural activities.

#### Wealth According to Social Class
Now, the acquisition of wealth according to social class <note>original: *Jati*</note> is described: If the Eleventh House is occupied or aspected by planets associated with specific classes, those classes become the givers of wealth. Specifically, if Jupiter and Venus are strong in the Eleventh House or aspect it, the person gains wealth through **Brahmins** <note>the priestly/scholarly class</note>. If the **Sun** and **Mars** are so placed, wealth comes through the **Kshatriyas** <note>the ruling/warrior class</note>. If the **Moon** is so placed, it is through the **Vaishyas** <note>the merchant/landowner class</note>. If **Mercury** is so placed, it is through the **Shudras** <note>the laboring class</note>. If **Saturn** is so placed, wealth is said to come from the **outcastes** <note>original: *Antyajas* or *Mlecchas*</note>. || 66-67 ||

-> Now the consideration of the House of Gains is explained in the vernacular: All teachers agree that the acquisition of all wealth should be judged from the eleventh house from the Ascendant. A planet endowed with strength in the House of Gains bestows wealth. If the Sun is strong there, wealth is gained from one's own community. If the Moon, from the maternal side. If Mars, from brothers. If Mercury, from masters, gods, friends, and maternal uncles. || 66 || <-

-> If it is Jupiter, wealth comes from the conduct of Vedas, Scriptures, and sacrifices, and from sons. If Venus, from women, poetry, drama, arts, and music. If Saturn, one is endowed with wealth and grain earned through servants and farming. If the House of Gains is joined or aspected by planets of the Brahmin class, etc., wealth is gained from those classes. || 67 || <-

> If a **benefic planet** <note>original: *Shubha-khechara*</note> resides in the House of Gains, the wealth is earned through virtuous means; if a **malefic** <note>original: *Papa*</note>, it is earned through sinful means. If the planets are mixed, the wealth is of a mixed nature; thus should the astrologer speak. If the planet in the House of Gains is exceptionally strong and well-disposed, the person born will possess all virtues, have many friends, and excel in vehicles, ornaments, clothing, the enjoyment of women, and knowledge. || 68 ||

Regarding the verse "If in the House of Gains...": The meaning is clear and requires no further elaboration. || 68 ||

> If the Lord of the Second House <note>Wealth</note> and the Lord of the Eleventh House <note>Gains</note> are friendly toward the Lord of the Ascendant <note>the Self</note>, then the person's wealth will be fit for **charity** toward good deeds, the worship of gods, the education of Brahmins, and meritorious causes <note>such as pilgrimages</note>. However, if the Lord of the Eleventh is weak, defeated in planetary war, in its sign of debilitation, in an enemy's sign, or in a "dusthana" <note>unfavorable house like the 6th, 8th, or 12th</note>, it creates a "Rekha Yoga" <note>a combination for poverty</note>, and the person may have to wander for alms daily. || 69 ||

Regarding the verse "If the Lord of Wealth...": If the Lords of the 2nd and 11th houses are friends of the Lord of the 1st house, then the person's wealth is spent on noble actions like sacrifices, honoring the gods, supporting scholars, and holy works.

**Regarding the source of income:** If a planet is weak, defeated in planetary war <note>original: "graha-yuddha"; a calculation where two planets occupy the same degree</note>, or is the lord of a "bad house" (6th, 8th, or 12th) and is situated in the 11th house (the house of gains), it creates a *Reka Yoga* <note>a configuration indicating poverty</note>. Such a person will suffer from poverty and may have to wander daily for alms. The essence is that a person born under this yoga becomes a beggar. || 69 ||

If the Lord of the 2nd house (Wealth) and the Lord of the 11th house (Gains) are friends of the Lord of the Ascendant, then the person's wealth is fit to be used for good deeds, deities, Brahmins, and meritorious charities. However, if a weak, defeated, debilitated planet, or one residing in an enemy's house or ruling a bad house, is placed in the 11th house, the person becomes a daily beggar. || 69 ||

**If the Lord of the 11th is the Sun or the Moon, wealth is obtained through the patronage of kings or those equal to kings.**
**If Mars, wealth comes through ministers, elder or younger brothers, and agriculture.**
**If Mercury, through education, relatives, and children. If Jupiter, through one's own righteous conduct.**
**If Venus, through gems, women, and animals like elephants. If Saturn, wealth is acquired through wicked means.** || 70 ||

Now, the results when the Sun and other planets are the Lords of the 11th house are explained. The meaning of "The Lord of the 11th is the Sun..." is clear as stated. || 70 ||

If the Sun or Moon is the Lord of the 11th, one gains wealth through the shelter of a king-like wealthy person. If Mars is the Lord, wealth is obtained from ministers, elder/younger brothers, and farming. If Mercury, from knowledge, kin, and sons. If Jupiter, from personal character. If Venus, from jewels, wives, and livestock. If Saturn, wealth comes through "bad livelihoods" <note>unethical or low-status work</note>. || 70 ||

**When the Lord of the 11th house is situated in a Quadrant (1, 4, 7, 10) or a Trine (1, 5, 9) from the Ascendant,**
**Or if a malefic planet is in the 11th house while the Lord of the 11th is in its exaltation sign or division, the person is wealthy.**
**One should predict wealth based on the strength of the specific significator <term>Karaka</term> and the specific Yoga.**
**Wealth should be predicted during the major or minor periods <term>Dasha-Antardasha</term> of that planet, and in the direction ruled by that planet.** || 71 ||

Regarding the Lord of the 11th: If the ruler of the 11th house is in a Quadrant or Trine from the birth Ascendant, or if a malefic planet is present in the 11th house, or if the Lord of the 11th is in its exaltation <note>highest strength</note> sign or Navamsha <note>ninth-part divisional chart</note>, the person born will be wealthy. As stated in the *Sarvartha Chintamani*: "If the Lord of Gains is in a Quadrant or Trine, or if the 11th house is occupied by a malefic, one should declare the arrival of wealth."

How to predict the nature of wealth? It is said: based on the strength and the specific configuration (*Yoga*). One should predict gains according to the category of the planet that creates the wealth-giving yoga. When and where? During the major or minor periods of that yoga-forming planet, and in the direction <note>e.g., East for Sun, South for Mars</note> ruled by that planet. || 71 ||

If the Lord of the 11th is in a Quadrant or Trine from the Ascendant, or if a malefic is in the 11th, or if the Lord of the 11th is in its exaltation, the person is wealthy. One should describe the gain through the nature of that planet. The gain occurs during the periods of that planet and in its respective direction. || 71 ||

->Thus ends the consideration of the 11th House (Gains).<-

# Chapter 15: Results of the Tenth, Eleventh, and Twelfth Houses
<page-num>477</page-num>

> From the house other than the Ascendant <note>The 12th House</note>, its lord, the Sun, and Saturn, one should contemplate travel to distant lands, misfortune, charity, the luxury of comforts like beds, and the depletion of wealth. If a mobile planet is in the twelfth house, or if the lord of a "bad station" <term>Dusthana: the 6th, 8th, or 12th houses associated with suffering</term> is in a mobile sign, or if it is joined or aspected by Saturn, the person will surely wander through various countries and forests. || 72 ||

**From the Ascendant, etc.:** Travel to distant lands = roaming in far-off countries; misfortune = suffering; charity = the act of giving (renunciation); luxury of comforts like beds = the possession of pleasures such as couches; depletion of wealth = the wasteful spending of money. These should be considered from the twelfth house, the lord of the twelfth house, and Saturn.

**In the twelfth, etc.:** A mobile planet = a planet of a moving nature, namely the Moon (see Ch. 2, Verse 47); or if the lord of a bad station = the lord of the 6th, 8th, or 12th houses, is in a mobile sign; and if that planet has entered the twelfth house and is joined or aspected by Saturn, the person born will certainly be one who wanders through various lands and forests. || 72 ||

*Now the consideration of the Twelfth House (House of Expenditure) is stated:* One should judge distant travel, misfortune, charity, comforts of the bed, splendor, and loss of wealth from the 12th house, its lord, and Saturn. If a mobile planet is in the 12th, or the lord of a bad house is in a mobile sign in the 12th, and is joined or aspected by Saturn, the native will wander in various countries and forests. || 72 ||

### Now, the Consideration of Expenditure (Vyaya)

> If a benefic planet is in the twelfth house, joined by a benefic and aspected by a gentle planet, and its lord is weak or in an enemy’s or debilitated sign, the native experiences an absence of wealth expenditure <note>i.e., they accumulate wealth</note>. If a weak planet is in the twelfth and the lord of the twelfth is endowed with strength, the native is a destroyer of wealth. If joined by mixed celestial bodies, the expenditure of humans is entirely mixed. || 73 ||

**In the twelfth house, etc.:** Joined by a benefic = accompanied by some auspicious planet; a benefic = any auspicious planet having entered the twelfth house; aspected by a gentle planet; and its lord = the lord of the twelfth; being weak = devoid of strength, or in an enemy’s or debilitated sign; the person born experiences an absence of wealth expenditure (he becomes a saver of wealth).

**Now, the combination for loss of wealth:** If a weak planet has gone into the twelfth house, and the lord of the twelfth is endowed with strength, the person born will be a destroyer of wealth.

**Mixed, etc.:** If that lord of the twelfth or the twelfth house itself is joined by mixed celestial bodies = accompanied by both malefic and benefic planets, then for humans, one should predict entirely mixed expenditure = ordinary spending of money (on both good and bad paths). || 73 ||

*If a benefic is in the 12th, joined and aspected by benefics, and its lord is weak, debilitated, or in an enemy's house, there is no expenditure of wealth. If a weak planet is in the 12th and the 12th lord is strong, it causes loss of wealth. If the 12th house or its lord is joined by mixed planets (benefic and malefic), the expenditure is mixed (spent on both good and bad things).* || 73 ||

> Auspicious expenditure occurs when the lord of the twelfth occupies a favorable divisional chart <term>Varga: a sub-divisional map used for fine-tuning strength</term> or is joined/aspected by a strong planet. Evil expenditure occurs if it is joined or aspected by a weak planet. The native meets with misfortune from the person or color associated with the significator planet during the period or sub-period of a planet lacking strength. || 74 ||

Now the consideration of auspicious and inauspicious expenditure is stated—**Auspicious expenditure, etc.:** If the twelfth house or its lord has reached a favorable divisional chart, or is joined/aspected by a strong planet, the native performs "desired expenditure" = spending money on the right path. Alternatively, if joined/aspected by a weak planet, "evil expenditure" = spending on the wrong path occurs.

# With the Commentary on Jataka Parijata

**On the period of a weak planet:** If the lord of the twelfth house, or a planet situated in the twelfth house, is weak during its major or minor planetary periods <note>Dasha and Antardasha</note>, the person suffers misfortune or downfall caused by the class of people represented by that planet's nature <note>The "karaka" or significator of the planet</note>. || 74 ||

-> If the lord of the twelfth house is in a favorable division <note>Shubha-varga</note>, the expenditure is for good purposes. If it is joined or aspected by a weak planet, the expenditure is for evil purposes. During the period of a weak planet, the person suffers distress through the social class or caste associated with that planet. <-

> If a strong malefic planet, being the lord of the sixth or eighth house, occupies the twelfth house, there will be destruction of agriculture, wealth, and social standing. If the twelfth house is a four-footed sign and is occupied by a four-footed planet, the person suffers the loss of all livestock and servants. || 75 ||

**On malefic planets:** If the lord of the sixth or eighth house <note>houses of enemies and death</note> is a strong malefic <note>Papa-graha</note> and is placed in the twelfth house <note>the house of loss</note>, the person born will see the destruction of their farming, wealth, and position.

**On the signs:** If the twelfth house is a **four-footed sign** <note>such as Aries, Taurus, Leo, or the latter half of Sagittarius</note> or a **two-footed sign** <note>such as Gemini, Virgo, Libra, or Aquarius</note>, and is occupied by a corresponding planet—a four-footed planet <note>Saturn or Mars</note> or a two-footed planet <note>Jupiter or Venus</note>—then the person suffers the loss of all cattle, animals, and servants. || 75 ||

-> If the lord of the 6th or 8th house is a strong malefic in the 12th, agriculture, wealth, and home are destroyed. If a four-footed or two-footed sign is in the 12th house and contains a similar planet, all livestock and servants are lost. <-

> If the twelfth house is joined by a priestly planet, loss occurs through prominent priests; if joined by a feminine planet, through women. If the twelfth house contains a masculine planet, loss is through enemies; if that masculine planet is in a friendly sign, the loss of wealth occurs through friends. || 76 ||

**On priests and others:** If the twelfth house is joined by a "priestly" planet <note>Vipra</note>, expenditure of wealth should be predicted through Brahmins and the like. Specifically: if Jupiter or Venus is in the 12th, loss is through Brahmins; if Mars or the Sun, through the warrior class; if the Moon, through the merchant class; if Mercury, through the laboring class; and if Saturn, Rahu, or Ketu, through foreigners or outsiders. If a feminine planet <note>Moon or Venus</note> is in the 12th, loss is through women. If a masculine planet <note>Sun, Mars, or Jupiter</note> is there, loss is through enemies. However, if that masculine planet is in a friendly sign, the loss of wealth happens because of one's own friends. || 76 ||

### Now, the Consideration of Charity

> One is a donor, a farmer, and righteous if a benefic planet is in the twelfth; but if a malefic is in the final house, one is quarrelsome, suffers eye disease, wind-disorders, and is restless. If that malefic is in its sign of exaltation, its own sign, or a friend's sign, the person is philanthropic. || 77 ||

**On the donor:** If the twelfth house is joined by a benefic planet <note>Shubha-graha</note>, the person is a **donor** <note>charitable</note>, a farmer, and a righteous soul. If a malefic planet <note>Papa-graha</note> occupies the "final house" <note>the 12th</note>, the person is prone to disputes, suffers from "wind" <note>Pavan/Vata</note> ailments, has eye diseases, is fickle, and wanders aimlessly. However, if that malefic in the 12th house is in its **exaltation**, **own sign**, or **friend's sign**, the person will be a philanthropist who helps others. || 77 ||

# Chapter 12: On the Results of the Tenth, Eleventh, and Twelfth Houses
<page-num>476</page-num>

If the Sun or the weak Moon is in the twelfth house, wealth is destroyed by kings <note>original: "nripaih"; likely referring to government taxes, fines, or legal seizures</note>. Mars, when joined or aspected by Mercury, destroys wealth in various ways. If Jupiter, the Moon, and Venus are in the twelfth house, they act as the protectors of wealth. If Mercury is joined or aspected by Venus, men obtain the comfort of a bed <note>referring to peaceful sleep and physical comforts</note>. || 78 ||

Now he describes the loss of wealth, the protection of wealth, and the comfort of the bed: If the Sun, or the weak Moon <note>Sanskrit: *krisha-shitagu*</note>, is in the twelfth house <note>the house of expenditure</note>, one should predict the destruction of wealth by kings. If Mars <note>Sanskrit: *bhauma*</note> is in the twelfth and joined or aspected by Mercury <note>Sanskrit: *induja*</note>, he destroys wealth through various means.

If Jupiter <note>Sanskrit: *vagisha*</note>, the Moon, and Venus together occupy the twelfth house, they become the protectors of wealth. In such a case, one should not predict the loss of money.

If Mercury <note>Sanskrit: *saumya*</note> is joined with or aspected by Venus and is in the twelfth house, then for men <note>Sanskrit: *animishatam*</note>, the comfort of the bed—meaning the joy of a couch—arises. || 78 ||

If the Sun or a weak Moon is in the twelfth house, wealth is destroyed by the king. If Mars is joined or seen by Mercury, wealth is destroyed in many ways. If the Moon, Venus, and Jupiter are in the twelfth house, they are protectors of wealth. If Mercury is joined or seen by Venus, men obtain the comfort of the bed. || 78 ||

### Now, the Consideration of the State after Death

> If the lord of the eighth house is joined with Saturn, Rahu, or Ketu in the twelfth house, or is aspected by the lord of the sixth house, the person reaches a miserable state after death.
> A person born goes to the Supreme State if Jupiter is in the Ascendant, Venus is in the seventh house, the Moon is in Virgo, and the Ascendant is Sagittarius with an Aries sub-division. || 82 ||

Now he explains the consideration of the state after death for the native: "Manda-ahi..." means if the lord of the eighth house <note>the house of death</note> is joined with Saturn, Rahu, or Ketu in the twelfth house <note>the house of the afterlife</note>, or if that lord is aspected by the lord of the sixth house, the person attains a miserable state <note>original: "durgatim"; suffering or a hellish realm</note> at the time of death.

Next, he describes the Supreme State: "Jato..." means if Jupiter <term>Suraguru: the teacher of the gods</term> is in the Ascendant <note>the sign rising at birth</note>, Venus is in the seventh house, and the Moon is in the sign of Virgo, the person reaches the Supreme State <term>Param Padam: the state of Nirvana or spiritual liberation (Moksha)</term>. This is the place from which one does not return, as the Blessed Lord said in the Bhagavad Gita:
<note>original: "yad gatva na nivartante tad dhama paramam mama" — "That place from which they do not return, that is My supreme abode."</note>

In this specific combination, the Ascendant is defined as being in the sign of Sagittarius and the sub-division <term>Navamsha: a one-ninth division of a sign</term> of Aries (8s 3° 12' 0"). In this state, Jupiter is in its own sign in the Ascendant, Venus is in its own sign in the seventh house, and the Moon is in the sixth house in Virgo. This is clearly stated. || 82 ||

Now he describes the auspicious and inauspicious nature of the houses based on planetary positions: "Dusthe..." means if the lord of a "bad house" (the sixth, eighth, or twelfth) is endowed with full strength and situated in one of those "bad houses," one should say that the themes of that house are "nourished" <note>in this context, it often refers to the strengthening of the house's specific karmic role</note>. ->Thus ends the consideration of the results of the twelve houses.<-

The *Sudha* <note>meaning "Nectar"</note> commentary on the *Parijata* treatise, composed by Kapileshvara, has reached its completion in the fifteenth chapter regarding the results of the houses. || 15 ||

If the lord of a "bad" house <note>specifically the 6th, 8th, or 12th houses associated with struggle, death, and loss</note> is situated in another "bad" house, it is said to strengthen that house's theme <note>this is a paradox in Vedic astrology called Viparita Raja Yoga where two negatives create a positive</note>. Where the lord of the house of longevity remains powerless, that house is destroyed. A strong lord of the Ascendant, when aspected by or joined with a benefic planet, brings special auspiciousness to whichever house it occupies. If it is in its sign of debilitation or an enemy’s house, it gives the opposite (inauspicious) result. || 83 ||

->Thus ends the 'Vimala' Hindi commentary on the fifteenth chapter of the Jataka Parijata. || 15 ||<-

## Now begins the Chapter on Women’s Horoscopy || 16 ||

> We declare this science of birth <term>Jataka: natal astrology</term>, which increases wealth, strength, health, offspring, knowledge, and fame, and is calculated through the lunar dates, constellations, and the positions of the planets. || 1 ||
> For men, there is no helper like the horoscope in the acquisition of wealth; it is a boat in the ocean of calamity, and a counselor at the time of a journey; there is nothing else besides the horoscope. || 2 ||
> This illustrious birth-chart—which bestows long life, children, the happiness of a husband, and vast wealth and fame—is written for the benefit of others by experts. It includes the precise positions of the celestial bodies, the five limbs of the calendar <term>Panchanga: the traditional Hindu almanac</term>, the eightfold division of points <term>Ashtakavarga: a system of calculating planetary strength</term>, the sixfold planetary strengths <term>Shadbala</term>, as well as calculations for longevity, transits, planetary combinations, house results, and the cycle of planetary periods <term>Dashas: the timeline of a person's life</term>. || 3 ||

Now, the chapter on women's horoscopy is being explained. First, the description of a horoscope is given in three verses: "Shri-balarogya..." etc. This means: wealth, bravery, health, children, knowledge, and fame—since the increase of these can be known from the horoscope, we, the authors, declare this birth-system which arises from the power of the lunar date <term>Tithi</term>, the constellation <term>Nakshatra</term>, and the planets. The meaning is that all auspicious and inauspicious results occur solely due to the planets, lunar dates, and constellations at the time of birth.

This horoscope acts as a helper for men in the acquisition of wealth; that is, anyone who begins the pursuit of wealth at a time recommended by the horoscope acquires it with ease. Or, by the power of astrology, the wealth of men who know astrology (astrologers) is successfully achieved. "A boat in the ocean of calamity" means that the ocean is the misfortune or trouble, and the horoscope is the vessel or ship within it. The idea is that the science of astrology shows the means of protection during a person's state of distress.

"A counselor at the time of a journey" — just as a minister advises a king, "Now you should act by this method, now this should be performed," and points out the path to victory, in the same way, this science of astrology reveals the skillful path for men traveling on their destined road. Therefore, as a helper in earning money, a boat in the sea of trouble, and a counselor during travel, there is nothing else besides the horoscope; rather, everything will be accomplished for those born through the power of the horoscope.

In the third verse, the tools for writing a birth-chart <note>original: "Janma-patrika"</note> are shown. Wise men write the illustrious birth-chart, which gives long life, children, the happiness of a husband, and great wealth and fame, including: the precise positions of the planets at that moment, the planets' positions in the almanac, the eightfold point systems of the planets, the sixfold strengths of planets beginning with their placement, longevity, planetary combinations, house results, and the cycles of planetary periods. || 1-3 ||

Now we describe the horoscope, joined with the lunar date, constellation, and planet, which increases wealth, strength, health, offspring, knowledge, and fame. || 1 ||

There is no other helper for men in the acquisition of wealth, no other ship in the ocean of misfortune, and no other counselor during travel besides the horoscope. || 2 ||

<page-num>482</page-num>
<header>In the Jataka Parijata with Commentary</header>

For the benefit of others, this "Shri Jataka" <note>a natal horoscope or birth chart</note> has been written to indicate long life, sons, a husband, the happiness of a wife, abundant prosperity, and fame. Within it are shown the calculations for the eightfold strength of all planets <term>Ashtakavarga: a system using points to determine planetary strength</term>, the sixfold strength <term>Shadbala: a mathematical method to weigh a planet's power</term>, longevity, transits <term>Gochar: the current movement of planets</term>, the results of the houses, and various planetary period cycles <term>Dasha-chakra: time-cycles that determine when specific karma unfolds</term>. || 3 ||

> Whatever birth results or combinations for men <note>original Sanskrit: *nṛ-yoga*</note> are stated, those should be applied to her husband.
> The physical well-being or suffering of women should be judged from the Moon or the Ascendant <note>the sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</note>, whichever is stronger.
> Their husband's vices and virtues are seen from the seventh house, and his death from the eighth.
> After considering the strength and weakness of the benefics and malefic planets, one should declare the entire result. || 4 ||

Now the results for women’s horoscopes are being explained. The birth results—meaning the auspicious or inauspicious outcomes arising from the time of birth—which were previously described as "combinations for men" <note>original: *puruṣa-sambhavam*</note>, should all be applied to her husband <note>original: *patāu*</note>. This means that if a result is described in a woman's chart that seems incompatible with a woman's traditional role (such as combinations for kingship or "Royal Yogas"), those results should be understood to apply to her husband instead. 

Furthermore, the physical auspiciousness or inauspiciousness—meaning the bodily health and suffering of these women—is determined from the Moon <note>original: *himakara*, literally "the ice-maker"</note> and the Ascendant <note>original: *lagna*</note>. Between these two, whichever is more powerful determines the physical state. If the Moon or Ascendant is occupied by benefic planets, there is physical happiness. If they are weak or occupied by cruel planets, one should predict physical hardship. 

The vices and virtues of their husbands should be considered from the seventh house relative to the birth Ascendant. The death of those husbands is to be judged from the eighth house <note>often called the house of "Mangalya" or marital longevity in a woman's chart</note>. Everything else should be declared after carefully weighing the strength of the benefics <note>planets like Jupiter and Venus</note> and malefics <note>planets like Saturn and Mars</note>. If the strength of benefics is greater, the result is auspicious; if the strength of malefics is greater, it is inauspicious. 

As the sage Varahamihira <note>a famous 6th-century Indian astronomer and astrologer</note> says on this matter:

> Whatever results are incompatible for women in a male-centric birth reading should be applied to the husband. Her husband's death is seen from the eighth house, her body from the Ascendant and Moon, and her husband's beauty and nature from the seventh. || 4 ||

The results of combinations stated for men should be interpreted for the husband when they appear in a woman's chart. A woman’s physical state is judged by whichever is stronger: the Ascendant or the Moon. From the seventh house, judge the husband's virtues and flaws. From the eighth house, judge the husband's death. All these results should be stated after considering the relative strength of the auspicious and inauspicious planets. || 4 ||

> In a woman’s birth, between the Ascendant and the Moon, whichever is stronger:
> From that, judge her wealth, beauty, and strength. From the ninth house, declare her sons, income, and growth.
> Auspiciousness <note>original: *saumaṅgalya*, referring to the husband's life</note> and misfortune are from the eighth house, and the husband's prosperity from the seventh.
> Some masters of horoscopy <note>original: *horāvidaḥ*</note> desire to judge the husband's well-being from the ninth house. || 5 ||

> Widowhood is known from the eighth house; from the Ascendant house comes radiance, fame, and wealth.
> Some know the son from the fifth house and the husband's happiness from the seventh.
> Even the religious life <note>original: *pravrajyām*, referring to asceticism or renunciation</note> and great happiness of women are known from the planets in the ninth house.
> All other results arising from the houses and combinations are the same for both women and men. || 6 ||

In a woman's birth, whichever is stronger between the Ascendant and the Moon determines her wealth, beauty, and physical prowess. From the ninth house, one should declare the growth of sons and the gain of wealth. Marital auspiciousness or "widowhood" <note>original: *aniṣṭam*, literally "the undesired"</note> should be judged from the eighth house. From the seventh house, consider the husband's prosperity. Here, some experts in the science of horoscopes prefer to see the husband's well-being from the ninth house. However, because the text uses the phrase "some say" <note>original: *kecit*</note>, it implies that the author's preferred view is to judge the husband's state from the seventh house. || 5 ||

<page-num>४८३</page-num>
<header>Chapter 16: Female Horoscopy || 16 ||</header>

From the house of death <note>original: *nidhanena*; the 8th house</note> in a woman's chart, her widowhood—the death of her husband—should be considered. From the house of the Ascendant <note>original: *lagnabhavanāt*; the 1st house</note>, her radiance <note>original: *tejaḥ*; physical luster or charm</note>, fame, and wealth should be judged. From the fifth house, one should contemplate her children. From the house of desire <note>original: *kāmena*; the 7th house</note>, the happiness derived from her husband should be considered. Thus some wise sages have said. From the planets situated in the house of fortune or increase <note>original: *dharmopacayagata*; the 9th house</note>, depending on the strength of the planets there, one should judge the renunciation <note>original: *pravrajyām*; taking up a spiritual or monastic life</note> of women, as well as their great happiness. The remaining results for the other houses and the results generated by planetary combinations are entirely the same for both women and men. There is no difference between them in those matters. || 6 ||

From the Ascendant and the Moon at the time of a woman's birth, whichever is stronger, one should predict her wealth, beauty, and strength. From her ninth house, predict the increase of children and income. From the eighth house, declare auspicious or inauspicious outcomes <note>regarding her longevity and marriage</note>. From the seventh house, judge the good or bad fortune of the husband. Some are of the opinion that the husband's good or bad fortune should be judged from the ninth house. || 5 || <note>This paragraph provides a vernacular summary of the preceding Sanskrit principles.</note>

Consider widowhood from the eighth house, and radiance, fame, and wealth from the Ascendant. Consider children from the fifth house. Some believe the happiness of the husband is judged from the seventh. Judge renunciation and the special happiness of women from the planets found in the ninth. The results of the remaining houses are the same for women and men. || 6 ||

->If both the Ascendant and the Moon are in even signs, the woman born is beautiful and possessed of good character.<-
->If they are joined with or aspected by benefics, she is virtuous, faithful, and endowed with wealth.<-
->In an odd sign, she has a masculine form, is fickle, acts like a man, and is sinful.<-
->If these are seen by or joined with a malefic planet, she becomes one of bad conduct.<- || 7 ||
->If the Ascendant and the Moon are in odd signs but are joined with or aspected by a benefic planet,<-
->The woman is born with mixed qualities and appearance, and she possesses stability, grace, and wisdom.<-
->If they are in even signs but are joined with or seen by malefics,<-
->The wise say all results are determined by the strength of the lords of those signs and the planets aspecting them.<- || 8 ||

Now the results for women based on the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</term> and the Moon <note>original: *indu* or *niśākara*</note> are explained. If both the birth Ascendant and the Moon are in even signs <term>Yugma-rashi: Taurus, Cancer, Virgo, Scorpio, Capricorn, or Pisces</term>, then the woman born is possessed of excellent beauty and character. If that Ascendant and Moon in even signs are aspected by or joined with benefics <note>auspicious planets like Jupiter, Venus, or Mercury</note>, then the woman is virtuous, a faithful wife, and wealthy. Regarding the "odd signs": if the Ascendant and Moon are in odd signs <term>Oja-rashi: Aries, Gemini, Leo, Libra, Sagittarius, or Aquarius</term>, then the woman born has a masculine appearance and nature, is fickle, behaves like a man <note>or is "man-chasing"</note>, and is sinful. If the Ascendant and Moon are in odd signs and are seen by or joined with a malefic planet <note>such as Mars or Saturn</note>, then the woman becomes one of bad conduct and a doer of evil deeds. As it is said in the *Phaladeepika* <note>a classic 13th-century astrological text</note>:

> "If the rising sign and the Moon are both in even signs and seen by benefics, she has good sons, a good husband, ornaments, wealth, and excellent character. If they are joined with or seen by malefics and are in odd signs, she has a masculine nature, a crooked mind, is unhealthy, is treated poorly by her husband, and is poor."

If the Ascendant and Moon are in odd signs but are joined with or aspected by a benefic planet, then the woman born is of mixed qualities and appearance <note>possessing both feminine grace and masculine strength</note> and is endowed with a sense of direction, place, time, and wisdom. If those same two, the Ascendant and Moon, are in even signs but are joined with or seen by malefics, then she also possesses the mixed qualities mentioned above. Furthermore, regarding the strength of the lord of the sign <note>original: *rāśīśa*; the planet that rules the sign where the Moon sits</note> and the planets joined with or aspecting it: those who know the science of horoscopy <term>Hora-shastra: the study of time and its effects on destiny</term> say that the entire result corresponds to the strongest planet among them. || 7-8 ||

If both the Ascendant and the Moon are in even signs, then the woman is endowed with the beauty and character of an excellent woman. If benefic planets see them, she is virtuous, faithful, and wealthy. If the Ascendant and Moon are in odd signs, she has a man's appearance, is fickle, and behaves toward other men...

...one who acts wickedly and is a sinner. If [the Ascendant or Moon] is aspected by or joined with malefic planets <note>original: *pāpagraha*; planets considered naturally harmful, like Mars or Saturn</note>, that woman becomes unchaste. || 7 ||

If the Ascendant <note>original: *lagna*; the sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</note> and the Moon are in odd signs <note>original: *vishama rāśi*; signs like Aries, Gemini, Leo, etc., which are considered masculine</note>, are joined by benefic planets <note>original: *śubhagraha*; helpful planets like Jupiter or Venus</note>, and are aspected by benefics, then the woman will possess mixed qualities in her appearance, status, gait, and intellect. Even if both are in even signs <note>original: *yugma rāśi*; signs like Taurus, Cancer, Virgo, etc., considered feminine</note> but are joined by or aspected by malefic planets, these same mixed qualities are said to occur. At that time, the wise declare all results based on the strength of the planet that is in conjunction with or aspecting the lord of the birth sign. || 8 ||

->**If the Ascendant is in an odd sign and the male planets are exceptionally strong, and the Moon, Mercury, Venus, and Jupiter are also powerful, while Saturn possesses only average strength, the woman born will certainly have many husbands.**<- || 9 ||

Now the author describes the combination for an unchaste woman <note>original: *kulaṭā-yoga*</note>: When the birth Ascendant is in an odd sign <note>original: *oje*</note>, and the male planets (the Sun, Mars, and Jupiter) are situated anywhere with great strength <note>original: *baliṣṭhaiḥ*</note>, and the Moon, Mercury, and Venus are also powerful, while Saturn <note>original: *sūryaputre*; literally "son of the Sun"</note> possesses only ordinary strength—a woman born under this combination will surely have many husbands. In this yoga, the girl born will choose multiple partners, meaning she becomes unchaste. || 9 ||

If the Ascendant is in an odd sign, male planets are strong, the Moon, Mercury, and Venus are powerful, and Saturn has average power, the woman born will have many husbands. || 9 ||

->**If the Ascendant is in an even sign and Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus are very strong, the girl born then will certainly be one of famous name, renowned for her intellect in understanding the essence of all matters, and a virtuous woman.**<- || 10 ||

Now the author describes the combination for a virtuous woman <note>original: *sādhvī-strī-yoga*</note>: When the Ascendant is in an even sign <note>original: *yugme*</note>, and Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus are powerful regardless of their position, the girl born at that time will certainly have a famous name, be sung of among the people, be renowned for her sharp intellect in grasping the essence of all things, and be a virtuous <note>original: *sādhvī*; a woman of noble character</note> and well-behaved person. || 10 ||

In an even-sign Ascendant, if Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus are strong, the girl born will surely have a famous name, be renowned for her understanding of all truths and meanings, and be a virtuous woman. || 10 ||

->**If Saturn is of medium strength, the Moon, Venus, and Mercury are devoid of power, and the remaining planets are endowed with strength, and the birth occurs in an odd-sign Ascendant, she becomes a promiscuous woman. If the Ascendant sign is even and Jupiter, Mars, Venus, and Mercury are strong, she will be famous, skilled in the logic of all scriptures, and even a seeker of the Absolute.**<- || 11 ||

Now the author explains the "promiscuous" <note>original: *puruṣiṇī*; literally "having many men"</note> and "seeker of the Absolute" <note>original: *brahmavādinī*</note> combinations: If Saturn <note>original: *saure*</note> has medium strength, the Moon, Venus, and Mercury are weak, and the remaining planets (Sun, Mars, Jupiter) are strong, and if an odd sign is rising in the Ascendant (signs 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, or 11), then the woman born becomes promiscuous. 

Regarding the seeker of the Absolute: When Jupiter, Mars, Venus, and Mercury are strong anywhere, and the birth Ascendant is in an even sign (2, 4, 6, 8, 10, or 12), the woman born will be famous and skilled in the logic and discernment of all the various scriptures; she becomes a *Brahmavadini* <note>original: *brahmavādinī*; a woman who discourses on the nature of the ultimate reality or Brahman</note>, proficient even in the science of liberation <note>original: *mokṣa-śāstra*</note>. || 11 ||

If Saturn is moderately strong, the Moon, Venus, and Mercury are weak, and the other planets are strong, a birth in an odd-sign Ascendant makes her a promiscuous woman. If the first Ascendant is in an even sign and Jupiter, Venus, and Mercury are strong, that woman will have a famous name, be skilled in the logic of all scriptures, and be a female philosopher. || 11 ||

## Now, the Results of the Trimsamsa Divisions.

> If the Ascendant or the Moon is in a sign owned by Mars <note>Aries or Scorpio</note>, and Mars is the stronger of the two, a woman born in a **Trimsamsa** <note>original: *triṃśāṃśa*; a one-thirtieth division of a zodiac sign used to refine predictions</note> of Mars will be prone to misconduct. In a Trimsamsa of Saturn, she becomes a servant; in one of Jupiter, she is virtuous and well-behaved; in one of Mercury, she is deceptive or impure; and in a Trimsamsa of Venus, she becomes a woman who follows the path of infidelity. || 12 ||

> When the Ascendant is in a sign of Venus <note>Taurus or Libra</note>: in a Trimsamsa of Mars, she is quarrelsome and wicked; in a Trimsamsa of Jupiter, she is virtuous and blessed with children; in one of Saturn, she is a remarried woman <note>original: *punarbhū*; a woman who marries a second time, which carried specific social connotations in historical India</note>. Born in a Trimsamsa of Mercury, she is a lover of all arts, music, and instrumental performance; in a Trimsamsa of Venus, she becomes beloved by her husband, fortunate, and popular among people. || 13 ||

> If the Ascendant is in a sign of Mercury <note>Gemini or Virgo</note>: in a Trimsamsa of Mars, she is endowed with children; in one of Saturn, she becomes a widow, loses her children, is of an indeterminate nature, or is unchaste. In a Trimsamsa of Jupiter, she is devoted to her husband; in one of Mercury, she is a young woman of famous brilliance; and in a Trimsamsa of Venus, she becomes very beautiful and famous for her fine clothing, jewelry, cattle, and wealth. || 14 ||

> If the Ascendant is in the Moon’s sign <note>Cancer</note> and is strong: in a Trimsamsa of Mars, she is fond of the pleasures of infidelity (especially if the Moon is aspected by malefic planets); in a Trimsamsa of Saturn, she is abandoned or helpless; in one of Jupiter, she has a short life and few children; in one of Mercury, she is skilled in crafts and arts; and in a Trimsamsa of Venus, she is driven by desire. || 15 ||

> If the Ascendant or Moon is in the Sun’s sign <note>Leo</note>: in a Trimsamsa of Mars, the woman possesses a masculine nature and is unchaste; in a Trimsamsa of Saturn, she is sorrowful; in one of Jupiter, she is virtuous and beloved by a king; in one of Mercury, she behaves like a man; and in a Trimsamsa of Venus, though she may be wicked or diseased, she remains affectionate toward a difficult husband. || 16 ||

> When the Ascendant is in a sign of Jupiter <note>Sagittarius or Pisces</note>: in a Trimsamsa of Mars, she is famous and has many attendants; in a Trimsamsa of Saturn, she becomes poor. In a Trimsamsa of Jupiter, she possesses wealth, fine clothes, and jewelry; in one of Mercury, she is highly respected; and in a Trimsamsa of Venus, she is virtuous, has children, and is adorned with excellent garments and ornaments. || 17 ||

> If the Ascendant is in a sign of Saturn <note>Capricorn or Aquarius</note> and is strong: in a Trimsamsa of Mars, she is full of grief; in a Trimsamsa of Saturn, she is unfortunate but remains devoted to the traditions and conduct of her family; in a Trimsamsa of Jupiter, she is all-knowing/wise; in one of Mercury, she is unchaste; and in a Trimsamsa of Venus, she is barren but virtuous. These results should be declared based on the precise degree of the Ascendant and the Moon. || 18 ||

Now the results of the **Trimsamsa** in a female nativity are discussed. In this context, one must understand the results for the Ascendant as it passes through the Trimsamsa of the various planets within each sign. "Stronger" <note>original: *vīryādhike*</note> means the more powerful of the two—either the Ascendant or the Moon. If they are in a house of Mars <note>Aries or Scorpio</note>, and fall within the Trimsamsa of Mars, the woman born <note>original: *abala*; literally 'the one without strength,' a poetic term for a woman</note> will be engaged in misconduct or unchaste acts. The rest is self-explanatory. One should consult the chart for this purpose. || 12–18 ||

If the Ascendant or Moon is in a sign of Mars (1 or 8) and is strong, then falling in the Trimsamsa of Mars makes her prone to misconduct. If in the Trimsamsa of Saturn, she becomes a female messenger or go-between. In Jupiter's, she is virtuous. In Mercury's, she is impure. In the Trimsamsa of Venus, the woman practices the vows of a paramour (she becomes unfaithful). || 12 ||

If the sign of Venus (2 or 7) is in the Ascendant: in the Trimsamsa of Mars, she is a wicked woman who creates quarrels. If it is Jupiter's Trimsamsa, she is virtuous and has children. If it is Saturn's portion, she is a remarried woman. If it is Mercury's portion...

...then she will be a lover of all arts, music, and instrumental performance. If she is born in a **Trimsamsa** <note>original: *aṃśa*; a divisional portion of the sign</note> of **Venus**, she will be the wife of a scholar, beautiful, and highly respected in society. || 13 ||

If the Ascendant is in a house owned by **Mercury** (Gemini or Virgo): in a Trimsamsa of **Mars**, she will be endowed with sons. In a Trimsamsa of **Saturn**, she will be a widow or one whose children have died; she may be of an indeterminate gender or nature <note>original: *napuṃsaka*; often referring to someone who does not fit traditional gender roles or is sterile</note> and sinful. In a Trimsamsa of **Jupiter**, she will be devoted to her husband. A woman born in a Trimsamsa of **Mercury** will be famously brilliant. In a Trimsamsa of **Venus**, she will be famous for her beautiful clothes, ornaments, and refinement. || 14 ||

If the Ascendant is in the house of the **Moon** (Cancer): in a Trimsamsa of **Mars**, the woman will be strong. If the Moon is also aspected by <note>original: *dekhā jātā*; viewed by the astrological 'gaze' or aspect of a planet</note> a malefic planet at that time, the girl born will delight in the company of lovers. In a Trimsamsa of **Saturn**, she becomes a widow <note>original: *viśvastā*; can mean a widow or a trusted woman, but in this malefic context, historical commentaries often suggest a woman living alone</note>; in a Trimsamsa of **Jupiter**, she will have a short life and few sons. In a Trimsamsa of **Mercury**, she will be skilled in the manual or fine arts; in a Trimsamsa of **Venus**, she will be exceptionally passionate. || 15 ||

If the Ascendant or the Moon is in the house of the **Sun** (Leo): in a Trimsamsa of **Mars**, the woman will have a masculine nature and be unchaste. In a Trimsamsa of **Saturn**, she will be sorrowful. In a Trimsamsa of **Jupiter**, she will be the wife of a king and virtuous. In a Trimsamsa of **Mercury**, she will be desirous of men. If she is in a Trimsamsa of **Venus**, she will be wicked, devoted to a secret lover, and sickly. || 16 ||

If the Ascendant is in a house owned by **Jupiter** (Sagittarius or Pisces): in a Trimsamsa of **Mars**, she will be fortunate, famous, and surrounded by family. In a Trimsamsa of **Saturn**, she will be poor. In a Trimsamsa of **Jupiter**, she will possess wealth, fine clothes, and ornaments. In a Trimsamsa of **Mercury**, she will be well-respected. In a Trimsamsa of **Venus**, she will be a saintly woman, blessed with sons and beautiful clothing and jewelry. || 17 ||

If the Ascendant is in a house owned by **Saturn** (Capricorn or Aquarius): in a Trimsamsa of a strong **Mars**, she will be full of grief. In a Trimsamsa of **Saturn**, she will be unfortunate. In a Trimsamsa of **Jupiter**, she will be devoted to her family's traditional conduct. If born in a Trimsamsa of **Mercury**, she will be all-knowing <note>highly intellectual</note> yet unchaste. In a Trimsamsa of **Venus**, she will be barren but devoted to her husband. The results of all these Trimsamsas are determined by the combined influence of the specific Ascendant and the Moon. || 18 ||

<header>Chapter on Women’s Horoscopy || 16 ||</header>

> If malefic planets are placed in the seventh house, the woman becomes a widow. If the planets there are mixed (both malefic and benefic), she becomes a remarried woman. If a weak malefic planet is in the seventh house and is aspected by a benefic planet, she is abandoned by her husband. If Venus and Mars are in each other’s divisional portions, she becomes attached to another man. If those two are joined with the Moon in the seventh house, she does so with her husband's permission. || 16 ||

Now, the author explains the combinations for widowhood, remarriage, and being abandoned by a husband. "With fiery ones" refers to <term>malefic planets</term> <note>original: *pāpagraha*; planets like Mars, Saturn, or the Sun</note>. When these are in the "setting sign" or <term>seventh house</term> <note>the 7th house represents marriage and the spouse</note>, widowhood occurs. If there are "mixed" planets—meaning both auspicious (benefic) and inauspicious (malefic) planets in the seventh—the woman becomes a **remarried woman** (the definition of a <term>punarbhū</term> is provided in the next verse); she is married again to another man. If a "weak malefic" is in the seventh house and is "aspected" or seen by a <term>benefic planet</term> <note>original: *śubhagraha*; planets like Jupiter or Venus</note>, the woman is "cast off" or abandoned by her husband. Regarding "each other's portions": if Venus is in a divisional portion (*navamsha*) of Mars, and Mars is in a divisional portion of Venus, then that woman becomes "attached to another," meaning she seeks lovers. Alternatively, if Venus and Mars are together with the <term>Moon</term> in the seventh house, then the woman approaches another man not by her own will, but by the "husband's instruction" or permission. Thus, it is said in the *Jataka Bharanam*:

> If Mars and Venus are situated in each other's divisional portions, the woman will surely be attached to another. If Venus and Mars are in the house of desire (the 7th) along with the Moon, she follows the command of her lord. || 19 ||

<note>The Hindi commentary repeats these points: Malefics in the 7th = widow; mixed = remarried or having multiple husbands; a weak malefic aspected by a benefic = abandoned. The Mars-Venus exchange indicates infidelity.</note>

> A woman who leaves her husband and, out of desire, seeks a man of her own caste is an independent woman. A woman whose "gate of progeny" is uninjured and who is consecrated again by marriage is a remarried woman. || 20 ||

Now, the characteristics of the independent woman (<term>svairiṇī</term>) and the remarried woman (<term>punarbhū</term>) are described. A woman who leaves her own husband and, by her own desire, seeks another man of the "same caste" <note>original: *savarṇa*; belonging to the same social or ritual rank</note> is called an **independent woman**. Regarding "uninjured": if a married woman's "gate of progeny"—that is, the place from which children emerge, the womb or vagina—remains "uninjured" (meaning it has not known sexual union) and she is "consecrated" or married again to another man, she is then called a **remarried woman**. || 20 ||

<note>Historical context: In ancient Hindu law and astrology, a *punarbhu* was a specific legal category of a woman who married a second time. This verse distinguishes between one who leaves a husband out of lust and one who remarries because her first marriage was never consummated.</note>

> If the Ascendant is in a sign of Saturn or Mars and contains the Moon and Venus, and is aspected by a malefic, she is unchaste along with her mother. If the seventh divisional portion belongs to Mars and is seen by Saturn, she has a diseased womb; if it belongs to a benefic, she has beautiful hips and is beloved. || 21 ||

Now the combinations for unchastity involving the mother, a diseased womb, and a woman who is a favorite are described. "In a sign of Saturn or Mars" refers to <term>Capricorn, Aquarius, Aries, or Scorpio</term>. If the <term>Ascendant</term> <note>the sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</note> falls in one of these signs and is occupied by the Moon and Venus, and is further "aspected" (seen) by any malefic planet, the woman born will be "unchaste along with her mother," meaning both consort with other men. Regarding "Mars' portion": if the divisional portion (*navamsha*) of the seventh house from the Ascendant belongs to Mars and is aspected by <term>Saturn</term>, the woman will have a <term>diseased womb</term> <note>original: *vyādhi-yoni*; literally 'diseased female organ'</note>. However, if that seventh house falls in the divisional portion of a benefic planet, the woman will have "beautiful hips" (a graceful waist) and be "greatly beloved" or dear to her husband. As stated in the *Saravali*:

<vocab>Strijataka-adhyaya (Chapter on Women's Horoscopy), Vidhava (Widow), Punarbhu (Remarried woman), Svarini (Independent/Wanton woman), Punshchali (Unchaste woman), Saptama Bhava (Seventh House), Navamsha (9th-part divisional chart), Shani (Saturn), Bhauma (Mars), Shukra (Venus), Chandra (Moon), Vyadhi-yoni (Diseased reproductive organs)</vocab>

It also details astrological combinations that predict abandonment, infidelity, and physical health of the reproductive organs.</summary>

<header>In the *Jataka Parijata* with Commentary—</header>

### If the Ascendant is in a sign of Saturn or Mars, and both the Moon and Venus are placed there, the woman born becomes unchaste along with her mother. If this combination is aspected by malefic planets, this result is certain.
### If the seventh house is in a divisional portion of Mars and is aspected by Saturn, the woman suffers from a diseased womb. 
### If the seventh house falls in the portion of a benefic planet, she will have beautiful hips and be beloved by her husband. || 21 ||

If the <term>Ascendant</term> <note>the rising sign at birth</note> is in a sign owned by Saturn (Capricorn or Aquarius) or Mars (Aries or Scorpio), and Venus is joined with the Moon in that sign, and malefic planets <note>original: *pāpagraha*; such as Mars, Saturn, or the Sun</note> cast their gaze (aspect) upon them, the woman will be unchaste alongside her mother. If the <term>Navamsha</term> <note>a one-ninth divisional chart used to see the inner strength of planets</note> of the seventh house belongs to Mars and is aspected by Saturn, there will be disease in the reproductive organs. However, if the seventh house is in the portion of an auspicious planet, the woman’s waist and hips will be lovely, and she will be cherished by her husband. || 21 ||

### If a weak malefic planet is in the seventh house and is aspected by a benefic planet, 
### she is abandoned by her husband. If that malefic is in its sign of debility or an enemy's sign, she becomes an enemy to her husband. || 22 ||

This verse is easy to understand, and its second part was already covered in the explanation of the 16th verse. || 22 ||

If a weak <term>malefic planet</term> is situated in the seventh house (the house of marriage) and is seen by a <term>benefic planet</term> <note>original: *śubhagraha*; such as Jupiter, Venus, or a strong Moon</note>, the woman will be cast off by her husband. If that malefic planet is in its <term>sign of debility</term> <note>the sign where a planet's influence is at its weakest</note> or in the sign of its planetary enemy, she will act as an adversary to her husband. || 22 ||

### Abandoned is she when the Sun is in the house of desire and aspected by an enemy planet. 
### If Mars is there, the woman is untrustworthy, or there is mutual enmity between the couple. 
### If the seventh house is occupied by both benefic and malefic planets, she becomes a remarried woman. If Saturn 
### is in the seventh house and aspected by an enemy, she grows old as a non-widow (remaining a virgin). || 23 ||

Now, the results of the seventh house in a woman's chart are explained based on specific planets:
**Abandoned:** If the **Sun** (the "Maker of Day") is in the <term>seventh house</term> <note>original: *madana-sthite*; the house of passion and partners</note> and is aspected by an enemy planet, the woman is abandoned or rejected by her husband. 
**Untrustworthy:** If **Mars** (the "Earth-born") is in the seventh house and aspected by an enemy planet, the woman is untrustworthy, or there is mutual hatred and constant quarreling between the husband and wife. 
**Remarried:** If the seventh house is occupied by a mix of both auspicious and inauspicious planets, the woman becomes a <term>punarbhū</term> <note>original: *punarbhūḥ*; a woman who marries a second time or has a second partner</note>. 
**Unmarried:** If **Saturn** is in the seventh house and is aspected by an enemy planet, the woman reaches old age as an "un-widowed" person—meaning she remains a virgin and never marries in the first place. This implies that Saturn, when afflicted in the house of marriage, causes such a great delay or obstruction that marriage never occurs. 

As stated in the *Brihat Jataka*:
> "Abandoned if the Sun is in the seventh; a widow in childhood if Mars is there; 
> she remains a virgin and grows old if Saturn is in the seventh and aspected by a malefic." || 23 ||

If the Sun is in the seventh and seen by its enemy, she is abandoned. If Mars is there, she lacks trust or there is mutual enmity. If both good and bad planets are in the seventh house, she remarries. If Saturn is in the seventh and seen by an enemy, she stays a maiden until old age. || 23 ||

### If the seventh house is a sign of a malefic planet and Saturn is placed there, the woman becomes a widow.
### If Venus and Mars occupy each other's signs or divisional portions, she becomes a woman devoted to lovers and sensual play.
### If the Moon is in the house of desire, she commits misconduct along with her husband.
### If Saturn and Mars' signs are in the Ascendant, and the Moon and Venus are... [text continues] || 24 ||

**Widowhood:** When the seventh house is a sign owned by a malefic planet and **Saturn** is situated there, the girl born will face widowhood (the death of her husband). 
**Adultery:** Now, regarding unchastity: If **Venus** and **Mars** are in "each other's signs or portions"—meaning Venus is in a sign or *navamsha* of Mars, and Mars is in a sign or *navamsha* of Venus—the woman becomes devoted to other men and seeks sensual pleasures. 
**Joint Misconduct:** If the **Moon** is in the seventh house (the house of desire), the woman commits "bad conduct" along with her husband. If the Moon is in the seventh in a woman's chart, she...

<header>Chapter 16: On Women’s Horoscopy</header>

...she becomes unchaste, and her husband also becomes unchaste. Now, the author discusses barrenness. If the <term>Moon and Venus</term> <note>original: *shashi sitau*</note> are situated in the <term>Ascendant</term> <note>the sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</note> when that sign is owned by Saturn or Mars (Aries, Scorpio, Capricorn, or Aquarius), and if a malefic planet—such as the Sun, Mars, or Saturn—is placed in the fifth house (the house of children), the woman born under this combination will be <term>barren</term> <note>original: *vandhyā*</note>, meaning she will have no offspring and will never bear a child. As stated in the *Hora Ratna*:

->If Venus and Mars are in each other’s <term>Navamshas</term> <note>a 1/9th divisional chart used to see the inner strength of planets</note>, the woman will be attached to a paramour. Likewise, if the Moon is in the seventh house, she will be of bad character along with her husband.<-

->When the Moon and Venus are in the Ascendant in a sign belonging to Saturn or Mars, and a malefic planet occupies the fifth house, that woman becomes barren. || 24 ||<-

If the seventh house is a malefic sign and Saturn is placed there, the woman may become a widow. If Venus and Mars are in each other's signs (Mars in Taurus or Libra, or Venus in Aries or Scorpio), she will be lustful and devoted to a paramour. If the Moon is in the seventh house, both the woman and her husband will be unchaste (both being libertines). If the Moon and Venus are in an Ascendant falling in a sign of Saturn or Mars, and a malefic planet is in the fifth house, she will be barren. || 24 ||

->If Mars is in the portion of the seventh house and is aspected by Saturn, the maiden suffers from a diseased womb.<-

->If Mars is in the portion of Venus in the seventh house and is aspected by a benefic planet, she will be beloved by her husband. || 25 ||<-

Now, the author explains the combinations for being unfortunate or beloved by the husband. If Mars <note>original: *mahīje*; literally 'born of the earth'</note> is in a <term>Navamsha</term> belonging to the seventh house and is aspected (viewed) by Saturn, the girl born will suffer from a diseased or malformed reproductive organ <note>original: *durbhagā* - meaning unfortunate or having physical ailments</note>. This implies she will be unhappy in marriage. Conversely, if Mars is in the seventh house but in a Navamsha belonging to Venus, and is aspected by a benefic (lucky) planet, the woman will be the beloved and favorite of her husband. || 25 ||

If Mars is in the Navamsha of the seventh house and is seen by Saturn, the girl will be "Durbhaga" (having a diseased womb). If Mars is in the seventh house in the portion of Venus and is seen by auspicious planets, she will be beloved by her husband. || 25 ||

->If the Moon and Venus are in the Ascendant in a sign of Mars, the woman hates her husband.<-

->If the Moon and Mercury are there, she is skilled in debating the ultimate truth. If Mars and Mercury are there, she is fond of pleasures.<-

->If the Moon, Mercury, and Venus are in the Ascendant, she is endowed with happiness and wealth.<-

->If Jupiter is in the Ascendant, she will have good sons and be adorned with wisdom. || 26 ||<-

If the Moon and Venus are in the birth Ascendant in a sign of Mars (Aries or Scorpio), the woman born will be a hater of her husband <note>original: *patidveṣiṇī*</note>. If the Moon and Mercury are in the Ascendant in a sign of Mars, she will be skilled in <term>theology and philosophy</term> <note>original: *paratattvavāda*; the study of the ultimate reality or salvation</note>. If Mars and Mercury are in a sign of Mars at the Ascendant, she will be a seeker of pleasure and comfort. If the Moon, Mercury, and Venus are all together in the Ascendant (in any sign), the woman will possess wealth and happiness. If Jupiter <note>original: *vāgīśo*; 'the lord of speech'</note> is in the Ascendant, she will have good sons and be endowed with wisdom and fine ornaments. || 26 ||

If the Moon and Venus are in a sign of Mars at the Ascendant, the woman will be hostile toward her husband. If the Moon and Mercury are there, she will be clever in discussing the supreme truth (divine knowledge). If Mars and Mercury are there, she will be a woman of pleasure. If the Moon, Mercury, and Venus are in the Ascendant, she will possess happiness and wealth. If Jupiter is in the Ascendant, she will have beautiful children, intelligence, and jewelry. || 26 ||

->Planets in their signs of exaltation bring good results. If the eighth house contains a malefic planet, the woman faces widowhood, especially if it is a malefic sign aspected by malefic planets.<-

->If the lord of the Navamsha of the eighth house is a malefic, the woman will undoubtedly become a widow.<-

->If benefics are in the eighth house, the young woman will die before her husband. || 27 ||<-
