<header>From the Annotated Jataka Parijata—</header>

Regarding "Those standing in exaltation": If benefic planets <gloss>auspicious planets</gloss> are located anywhere in the chart but are exalted <gloss>situated in their highest signs of strength</gloss>, while the eighth house <gloss>the house of longevity and the husband's life</gloss> contains a malefic planet, is a sign owned by a malefic planet, and is aspected by a malefic, the woman born under this combination will face widowhood. This means she will become a widow.

The author describes another combination: if the lord of the eighth house <note>the planet ruling the 8th house</note> resides in a <term>Navamsha</term> <note>a one-ninth division of a sign</note> whose ruler is a malefic planet <gloss>a cruel planet like Mars or Saturn</gloss>, the lady <gloss>woman</gloss> will undoubtedly <gloss>certainly</gloss> become a widow.

Regarding death while the husband is still living: if benefic planets <gloss>auspicious planets</gloss> are situated in the eighth house <gloss>the house of death</gloss>, the young woman <gloss>wife</gloss> will meet her death before <gloss>earlier than</gloss> her husband <gloss>lord</gloss>. This means a woman born with this combination dies as a <term>Sadhava</term> <note>a woman whose husband is still alive</note>. || 27 ||

If auspicious planets are in their respective exalted positions, but the 8th house is in a malefic sign, contains a malefic planet, and is aspected by a malefic, the woman becomes a widow. If the lord of the 8th house resides in a malefic Navamsha, she will definitely be a widow. If a benefic planet is in the 8th, she will die before her husband. || 27 ||

->**If auspicious planets are in the ninth house, and a malefic is in the seventh or eighth,**<-
->**she lives for a long time accompanied by her husband, fortune, many sons, happiness, and prosperity.**<-
->**If cruel planets occupy the house of friends (the fourth), the woman will have many sons;**<-
->**if Sagittarius or Cancer is the Ascendant, she has a husband and sons but is beset by poverty. || 28 ||**<-

Regarding "Standing in the house of fortune": If auspicious planets <gloss>Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, or the waxing Moon</gloss> are in the ninth house <gloss>the house of fortune</gloss>, and a malefic <gloss>any one of the Sun, Mars, or Saturn</gloss> is in the seventh <gloss>house of marriage</gloss> or the eighth house, the woman lives for a long time <gloss>a great duration</gloss> along with her husband, wealth, many sons, happiness, and power. Under this combination, she possesses all comforts and attains a long life.

If cruel planets <gloss>malefics</gloss> occupy the fourth house <gloss>the house of the home and relatives</gloss>, the woman <gloss>lady</gloss> will have many sons <gloss>be blessed with numerous offspring</gloss>. If the <term>Ascendant</term> <note>the rising sign at birth</note> is Sagittarius <gloss>the Archer</gloss> or Cancer <gloss>the Crab</gloss>, the woman will have a husband and sons <gloss>possess a family</gloss> but will be poor <gloss>destitute</gloss>. As it is said:

> “If a benefic is in the house of fortune and a malefic is in the seventh or eighth, she does not live for a long time <note>original: *na jīvati*; likely a scribal variant or specific condition</note> without the happiness of husband and sons.”
> “If the Ascendant is Sagittarius or Cancer, she gives happiness to husband and sons,” says Yavana. || 28 ||

If auspicious planets are in the 9th house and malefic planets are in the 7th or 8th, that woman lives for a very long time with her husband, wealth, many sons, happiness, and prosperity. If cruel planets are in the 4th house, that woman will have many sons. If Sagittarius or Cancer is the rising sign, she will have a husband and sons but be poor. || 28 ||

->**With the Moon in the fifth house in Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Virgo, she has few sons;**<-
->**with malefics in the seventh, ninth, first, or eighth, she is distressed by poverty and grief.**<-
->**With a mix of benefics and malefics, the results are mixed; with only benefics, she has virtue and wealth.**<-
->**If the lord of the fifth is in the sixth and the lord of the sixth is in the Ascendant, death occurs by a weapon. || 29 ||**<-
<note>Verse 29 is misnumbered as 26 in the source text.</note>

Regarding "Taurus, Leo, etc.": If the Moon is situated in the fifth house <gloss>the house of children</gloss> in any of the signs of Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Virgo, the woman born will have few sons. Thus says Garga:
> “If the Moon stays in the fifth house in Leo, Scorpio, Taurus, or Virgo, one should know there will be few children; the same should be said for men.”

Regarding "By malefics": If malefic planets are situated in the seventh, ninth, first, and eighth houses, the woman will be distressed by poverty and grief. If these same houses are occupied by both benefics and malefics <gloss>auspicious and inauspicious together</gloss>, she will have mixed results <gloss>possessing both good and bad outcomes</gloss>. If these houses are occupied only by benefics, she will possess virtue and wealth.

Regarding a woman’s death by a weapon: If the lord of the fifth house <note>original: *putresha*</note> is in the sixth house <gloss>the house of enemies</gloss> and the lord of the sixth house <gloss>the ruler of the house of enemies</gloss> is in the Ascendant <gloss>the first house</gloss>, the woman's death will be caused by a weapon. || 29 ||

If the rising sign is Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Virgo and the Moon is in the 5th, there will be few sons. If malefic planets are in the 7th, 9th, Ascendant, or 8th, she will be troubled by the grief of poverty. Benefics and malefics together...

If both types of planets <gloss>benefic and malefic</gloss> are present, the results will be mixed. > If all malefic planets are in the setting position <gloss>the 7th house</gloss> from the rising sign, she will become a widow. If there is a mixture of planets <gloss>both auspicious and inauspicious</gloss> in the 7th, the girl born will be a <term>Punarbhu</term> <note>a woman who marries a second time or is "twice-born" in marriage</note>. If malefic planets are weak in strength, she will be abandoned by her husband. || 30 ||

<note>original: "श्लोकोऽयं स्पष्टार्थः..."</note> This verse is clear in its meaning and carries the same intent as the first half of the 19th verse. || 30 ||

If all malefic <gloss>sinful</gloss> planets are in the 7th house from the <term>Lagna</term>, she becomes a widow. If mixed planets are in the 7th, the girl born in this combination is a <term>Punarbhu</term>. If malefic planets are devoid of strength, her husband may abandon that woman.

> If the Moon is in the 7th house from the woman's birth <term>Lagna</term> and is joined by Venus and Mars, the girl born will seek other men with her husband's permission. The same result occurs if the aforementioned Moon is situated in a <term>Navamsha</term> <note>a one-ninth sub-division of a zodiac sign</note> of Saturn or Mars. || 31 ||

The meaning is clear. <note>original: "१९ तमरलोकोत्तरार्द्धतुल्यश्वेति"</note> This is similar to the second half of the 19th verse. || 31 ||

If the Moon is in the 7th house from the woman's birth <term>Lagna</term> and is joined by Venus and Mars, that woman will conduct herself with other men by her husband's order. If the previously mentioned Moon is in a <term>Navamsha</term> of Saturn or Mars, the result is the same. || 31 ||

> When planets situated in the signs or <term>Navamshas</term> of Saturn or Mars are joined with Venus and the Moon and are aspected <gloss>viewed</gloss> by malefic planets, the woman born will be devoid of family conduct and virtues, and she will be unchaste along with her mother. || 32 ||

Regarding the phrase "Saurara..." <note>original: "सौरारभांशोपगतग्रहेषु"</note>: Wherever planets are situated in the signs or <term>Navamshas</term> of Saturn or Mars—namely Aries, Scorpio, Capricorn, or Aquarius—and are joined by Venus and the Moon while being aspected by a malefic <gloss>inscribed as a "sinful" planet</gloss>, this is what is said: if other planets joined with Venus and the Moon go into the portions of Mars and Saturn anywhere in the chart and are seen by some malefic planet, then the woman born will lack family virtues and be an adulteress along with her mother. In this planetary combination, the girl is not only a wrong-doer herself, but her mother is also of bad character. || 32 ||

If planets are in the signs or <term>Navamshas</term> of Saturn and Mars, joined with Venus and the Moon and seen by malefic planets, the girl will be devoid of family conduct and will be an adulteress alongside her mother. || 32 ||

> If the <term>Navamsha</term> of Mars is in the 7th house from the <term>Lagna</term> and is aspected by the Sun and Mercury, she will be born with a disease of the reproductive organs. If the <term>Navamsha</term> of a benefic <gloss>good</gloss> planet is in the 7th house, she will be fortunate and have sons; otherwise, she will be unfortunate. || 33 ||

The simple meaning of this verse is: || 33 ||

If the <term>Navamsha</term> of Mars is in the 7th house from the <term>Lagna</term>, and the Sun and Mercury are looking at it <gloss>aspecting</gloss>, there will be disease in the reproductive organs. If a benefic planet's <term>Navamsha</term> is in the 7th house, she will be very fortunate and have sons; otherwise, she will be ill-fated.

> If two malefic planets are in the 7th house, she will be lustful, strong-minded, and a widow. If three malefic planets are in the 7th house, she will eventually kill her husband and be of ill-repute. If a benefic planet is in the 7th, she will be the wife of a royal official. If there are three benefic planets in the 7th, she will be virtuous and become the queen of a king. || 34 ||

The simple meaning: in a woman's horoscope, malefic planets in the 7th house produce bad results, while benefic planets in the 7th house produce good results. || 34 ||

If two malefic planets are in the 7th, she will be attached to desire, strong-willed, and a widow. If three malefic planets are in the 7th, she will kill her husband after some time and be of bad character. If there is a benefic planet in the 7th, she will be the wife of a king's servant. If there are three benefic planets in the 7th place, she will be virtuous and the queen of a king. || 34 ||

> If Venus and Saturn are in each other's <term>Navamshas</term> or aspect each other, or if a woman is born in the 8th part of Aquarius, she will be tormented by lust.

Regarding widowhood: If a malefic <gloss>sinful</gloss> planet is in the <term>Madasthana</term> <note>the 7th house, also known as the house of passion</note> from the sign occupied by the Moon, the woman attains widowhood <note>original: "vaidhavya"</note>, meaning the death of her husband. If a benefic planet <gloss>such as Mercury, Jupiter, or Venus</gloss> reaches the 7th house from the Moon, then she or her husband is granted a kingdom and <term>Aspada</term> <note>position or prestige</note>. The essential meaning in female horoscopy is that a malefic in the 7th from the Moon gives inauspicious results, while a benefic gives auspicious ones. || 35 ||

If Venus and Saturn are in each other's divisions and aspect each other, or if a woman is born in the eighth Navamsha of Aquarius, she is tormented by the fire of desire. If there is a cruel planet in the seventh from the Moon, she becomes a widow. If there is a benefic planet in the seventh house from the Moon, it grants the rank of a kingdom. || 35 ||

This verse is simple in its meaning. To summarize: the presence of the Moon and Venus together, or even the Moon alone, in a woman's birth <term>Lagna</term> is always beneficial. || 36 ||

If Venus is joined with the Moon in a woman's birth <term>Lagna</term>, she possesses a temper but is also a partaker of happiness. # Chapter on Women’s Horoscopy || 16 ||

A woman becomes knowledgeable in various weapons and arts, a connoisseur of tastes <note>original: "rasajnah," meaning one who understands aesthetics or alchemy</note>, clever, famous, and radiant. From the rising sign <term>Lagna</term> <note>the zodiac sign ascending on the eastern horizon at birth</note>, if there are three or more planets situated in the seventh house <gloss>the house of partners</gloss> or the ninth house <gloss>the house of dharma and religion</gloss>, a woman attains renunciation <term>Pravrajya</term> <note>monastic life or taking religious vows</note>. In such cases, she will take up the specific type of renunciation associated with the strongest planet among them. This should be considered at the time of her birth, at her marriage <gloss>joining of hands</gloss>, and during the selection of a husband.

**It is said—If the Moon is in the rising sign and Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus are strong:**
->**The woman will be a divine scholar, a seeker of Truth, and skilled in many sciences.**<-
->**If a malefic planet is in the seventh house and there is a planet in the ninth,**<-
->**she surely attains the path of renunciation caused by that malefic planet.**<-
->**At the time of birth, marriage, inquiry, and the selection of a groom,**<-
->**what is predicted for women should also be applied to their husbands. || 40 ||**<-

If the Moon is in the sign of Cancer in the ascendant, and Venus, Mercury, Jupiter, and the Moon are strong, she will be famous, radiant, and clever in various sciences, arts, and aesthetics. One should judge the yoga <gloss>planetary combination</gloss> for renunciation at the time of birth and marriage based on the planets in the seventh or ninth houses from the ascendant. || 40 ||

**If a malefic is in the setting house <gloss>the 7th house</gloss>, she attains the form of renunciation belonging to the planet in the ninth house without a doubt.**
**In marriage, in the ritual of selecting a groom, at the time of giving the bride away, and in astrological inquiries, all of this must be considered. || 41 ||**

->**At birth, at the time of marriage, during an inquiry, and at the selection of a groom,**<-
->**the analysis regarding women mentioned by the wise also applies to their husbands. || 42 ||**<-

Now he describes the combination for a woman's renunciation: "If a malefic is in the setting house." When a malefic <gloss>sinful</gloss> planet is in the seventh house from a woman's birth ascendant, the young woman attains a form of renunciation corresponding to the planet situated in the ninth house, without any doubt. All of this—renunciation and so on—should be considered during the marriage ceremony, the selection of the bride, the time of the girl's donation <note>original: "kanyadana," the ritual giving away of the bride</note>, and during astrological questioning. As stated by Gunakara:

->If a malefic is in the seventh, the woman attains the renunciation of the planet in the ninth.<-
->At the time of giving, marriage, and questions, the astrologer should apply this logic.<-

In this context, the types of renunciation associated with the planets are stated: Among the planets forming the yoga, if the Sun is strongest, she becomes a forest hermit <term>Tapasa</term>. If it is the Moon, she becomes a skull-bearing ascetic <term>Kapalika</term> <note>a follower of a specific Shaivite ascetic path</note>. If Mars is strong, she wears red robes <term>Raktapata</term> <note>often associated with Buddhist or certain ascetic sects</note>. If Mercury, she carries a single staff <term>Ekadandi</term>. If Jupiter, she becomes a mendicant with a triple staff <term>Tridandi</term> or <term>Bhikshu</term>. If Venus, she becomes a wandering religious student <term>Caraka</term>. If Saturn, she becomes a naked ascetic <term>Nagna</term> <note>referring to the Digambara Jain tradition</note>. Thus are the renunciations to be told. So it says in the *Svalpa-Jataka*:

> "Hermits, aged disciples, red-robed ones, mendicants, wanderers, and those without bonds."

Regarding the verse beginning with "Birth," the meaning is straightforward. || 41-42 ||

If a malefic planet is in the seventh house, the woman will undoubtedly attain renunciation similar to the planet in the ninth house. Therefore, consider all this during a woman's marriage, the selection process, the time of giving the bride, and in inquiries. || 41 ||

The consideration of renunciation is mentioned for women at the time of birth, marriage, questioning, and selection. This renunciation also applies to the woman's husband. || 42 ||

**If a cruel planet is in the eighth house, widowhood is predicted; this occurs at an age corresponding to the division <gloss>Navamsha</gloss> occupied by the lord of the eighth house.**
**If benefics are in the second house, she herself dies before her husband; and with the Moon in Virgo, Scorpio, Leo, or Aries, there are few children. || 43 ||**

Now he describes the combinations for a woman's widowhood and her own death: "If a cruel planet." If a malefic is situated in the eighth house, and the lord of the eighth house is in the ninth division <term>Navamsha</term> of a certain planet, then during the planetary period <gloss>Dasha</gloss> of that planet, widowhood <note>original: "vaidhavata"</note>—meaning the death of the husband—is predicted. Regarding the benefics: If at that time (in a woman's birth chart) benefic <gloss>auspicious</gloss> planets are in the second house—

If benefics are situated in the second house <gloss>the house of wealth</gloss>, the woman herself will die. The woman dies herself (during the period of a strong planet). The scholars of astrology say that if the eighth house has equal strength and is aspected or joined by both benefic and malefic planets, the couple (husband and wife) will die at the same time. Regarding the timing: the planet situated in the eighth house, the lord of the eighth house, or the lord of the ninth-division <term>Navamsha</term> occupied by the eighth house (specifically the 64th Navamsha lord)—among these three, the one who is strongest will cause her death during its sub-period <term>Apahara</term>. Now, the author describes the planetary combinations for a woman obtaining brothers with the following two verses. If the lord of the third house <gloss>the house of siblings</gloss> is a male planet <note>original: "pud-graha," referring to the Sun, Mars, or Jupiter</note>, and is situated in a masculine sign <note>original: "pud-graha-rkshe," such as Leo, Aries, Scorpio, Sagittarius, or Pisces</note>, or is joined with a male planet, or is aspected by any male planet; or if the lord of the third house is strong and placed in the second house <gloss>the house of wealth</gloss>, or in an angle <term>Kendra</term> <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note>, or in a trine <term>Kona</term> <note>the 5th or 9th houses</note>, then the woman born under this alignment obtains a brother born of the same mother who provides her with great wealth and happiness. Furthermore, if the lords of the third and eleventh houses are placed in the fifth house <gloss>the house of children</gloss> from the rising sign <term>Lagna</term> of the woman's birth, then the woman obtains a brother who possesses the splendor, virtues, and form of a king <note>original: "nrpalasya," meaning like a ruler</note>. || 46-47 ||

If the lord of the third house is a masculine planet, is in a masculine sign, is joined with a male planet, or is aspected by a male planet, or is strong in the second house, an angle, or a trine, then that girl will have a brother possessing much wealth and happiness. || 46 ||

If the lord of the third and eleventh houses are in the fifth house from the rising sign, the woman will obtain a brother who has splendor, virtue, and form equal to a king. || 47 ||

## Now, the Characteristics of the Husband

> If in a woman's chart the seventh house <gloss>the house of desire</gloss> is devoid of strength, empty of planets, aspected by malefics, and lacks the aspect or presence of benefic planets, her husband will be a base man <note>original: "ka-purusha," a contemptible or cowardly man</note>. If Mercury is in the seventh house, the husband will be impotent. If Saturn is in the seventh house, the young woman will be unfortunate or barren. If a movable sign <term>Chara-rashi</term> is in the seventh house, the husband will always be away on travels. || 48 ||

Now the characteristics of the husband for women are stated. If in a woman's "temple of love" <gloss>the seventh house</gloss>, it is weak, empty <gloss>devoid of planets</gloss>, and aspected by "sky-dwellers" who are cruel <gloss>malefic planets</gloss>, and if it lacks the aspect of benefic planets, then the husband <note>original: "bharta"</note> or lord of that woman will be a "what-sort-of-man" <note>original: "ko-narah," meaning a base or cowardly man</note>. Regarding impotence: if Mercury <note>original: "shashisuta," the son of the Moon</note> is in the seventh house, the husband will be a eunuch <note>original: "kliba"</note>. If Saturn <note>original: "arkatmaja," the son of the Sun</note> is in the seventh house, the young woman becomes "ill-fated" <note>original: "durbhaga," meaning one with a spoiled womb or generally unfortunate</note> or barren <note>original: "vandhya," unable to conceive</note>. If the seventh house from the rising sign is a movable sign <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn</note>, the husband will always be "travel-bound" <note>original: "pravasanvitah," meaning he stays in foreign lands and never remains at home</note>. By implication, if the seventh house is a fixed sign, he stays at home; if it is a dual sign, he is partly at home and partly traveling. So says Varahamihira:

> If the seventh house is empty, the husband is a base man; if weak and not aspected by benefics, he is a coward. Mercury and Saturn in the seventh make him impotent; a movable sign makes him always a traveler. || 48 ||

If a woman's seventh house is without strength, empty, and devoid of the aspect of benefic planets, her lord will be a base man (coward). If Mercury is in the 7th with Saturn, the husband will be impotent, or the woman will be barren and unfortunate. If there is a movable sign in the seventh house, the husband will always be a traveler. || 48 ||

> If the Sun is in the seventh house in its own ninth-divisional sign <term>Navamsha</term>, the husband is a gentle lover who delights in romantic play. If the Moon is there, she attains happiness from her husband. If Mars is in its own ninth-divisional sign in the seventh house, the husband is an adulterer devoted to other women. If Mercury is there, he is a learned man. If Jupiter is in the seventh house, he is a master of his senses. If Venus is there, he has a handsome body and is happy. If Saturn is there, he will be old and very foolish. || 49 ||

Regarding "in its own ninth-divisional sign" <note>original: "svamsha"</note>: If the Sun <note>original: "bhasvati"</note> is in its own Navamsha and is situated in the seventh house, the husband is a gentle lover who delights in play. If the Moon is in its own Navamsha in the seventh, the woman attains happiness from her husband. If Mars <note>original: "bhumi-tanaye," son of the Earth</note> is in its own Navamsha in the seventh, the husband is an adulterer <note>original: "jara"</note>, devoted to other women...

...and he becomes lustful after other women. If the Son of the Moon <note>original: "candrasute," referring to Mercury</note> is so placed <gloss>in the seventh house in its own Navamsha</gloss>, the husband will be a learned scholar. If Jupiter <note>original: "jive," the "Living One"</note> is in the seventh house in its own Navamsha, the husband will be the best among those who have conquered their senses <note>original: "jitendriyāṇāṃ varaḥ"</note>. If Venus is so placed, the husband will be happy and possess a beautiful body <note>original: "kāntavapuḥ," or a charming form</note>. If the Son of the Sun <note>original: "ravije," referring to Saturn</note> is in the seventh house in its own Navamsha, the husband will be old and extremely foolish. 

Similarly, in the *Horaratna* <note>a classic 15th-century astrological text</note>:
> If the Sun is in the seventh house in its own Navamsha or its own sign, the husband is devoted to pleasure and is gentle. If the Moon is in the seventh house in its own sign or Navamsha, the husband is gentle and controlled by the god of love.
> If Mars is in the seventh house in its own Navamsha or sign, the husband is a seeker of women and is poor.
> If Mercury is in the seventh house in its own Navamsha or sign, the husband will be learned and happy.
> If Jupiter is in the seventh house in its own Navamsha or sign, he will be virtuous and self-controlled. If Venus is in the seventh house in its own Navamsha or sign, the husband of the girl will be fortunate and happy.
> If Saturn is in the seventh house in its own Navamsha or sign, the husband will be old and foolish. One should state the results for women based on the planets situated in the seventh sign in this manner.

If the Sun is in its own Navamsha in the seventh house, the woman's husband will have a gentle intellect and be fond of amorous play. If the Moon is in its own Navamsha in the seventh, she obtains happiness. If Mars is in its own Navamsha in the seventh, the husband will be a paramour devoted to that woman. If Mercury is in its own Navamsha in the seventh, the husband will be a Pandit <note>a scholar or teacher</note>. If Jupiter is in its own Navamsha in the seventh house, the husband will have mastered his senses. If Venus is in its own division in the seventh, the husband will have a beautiful body and be happy. If Saturn is in its own Navamsha, the husband will be old and especially foolish.

-># The husband of a woman born in the Navamsha of the seventh house is soft-limbed, virtuous, and clever.<-
-># If Saturn is in the seventh house in its own Navamsha or sign, her husband is indeed old and extremely foolish. || 50 ||<-

**Commentary:** If a woman is born in the Navamsha of the seventh house <note>original: "jāmitra-rāśy-aṃśakajā," meaning the rising Navamsha at birth is the same as the sign in the seventh house of the main chart</note>, her husband's body will be soft <note>original: "mārdavāṅgaḥ"</note>, and he will be virtuous and clever <note>original: "pragalbhaḥ"</note>. An example is given here: if the rising sign <term>Lagna</term> is Aries, then the seventh house is Libra. If the woman is born in the Libra Navamsha, this rule applies; this logic should be applied to all signs. The meaning of "If Saturn..." is clear and carries the same meaning as verse 49: "If the son of the Sun is present, he becomes old and extremely foolish." || 50 ||

A woman born in the Navamsha of the sign in her seventh house (for example, a woman with an Aries ascendant born in a Libra Navamsha) will have a husband with soft limbs, good virtues, and cleverness. If Saturn is in the seventh house in its own sign or Navamsha, the husband of that woman will be old and very foolish. || 50 ||

-># If the Lord of the Ninth and Jupiter are in difficult houses, the husband will have a short life.<-
-># If they are in a trine or an angle, he will be long-lived and wealthy.<-
-># If they are joined with Mercury or the Lord of the Fourth, he is a scholar; if with Mars or Saturn, he is a farmer.<-
-># If joined with Rahu or Ketu, he is wicked; if with the Lord of the Sixth, he is a master of thieves. || 51 ||<-

**Commentary:** If the Lord of the Ninth House <note>original: "dharma-gṛheśa," the house of religion and fortune</note> and Jupiter <note>original: "deva-sacivau," the counselor of the gods</note> are in "difficult houses" <note>original: "duḥsthau," referring to the 6th, 8th, or 12th houses</note>, then the woman's husband will have a short life <note>original: "gatāyuḥ," meaning his life has departed</note>. If those two are placed in a trine <term>Trikona</term> <gloss>the 5th or 9th houses</gloss> or an angle <term>Kendra</term> <gloss>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</gloss>, then the husband will be long-lived and wealthy. If those two—the Lord of the Ninth and Jupiter—are joined with Mercury <note>original: "bodhana"</note> and the Lord of the Fourth House <note>original: "vāhaneśa," the lord of vehicles</note>, the husband becomes a scholar. If the Lord of the Ninth and Jupiter are joined with Mars <note>original: "sāra"</note> and Saturn <note>original: "arkajau," the sun-born</note>, the husband will be a farmer <note>original: "karṣakaḥ," one who plows</note>. If those two are joined with Rahu <note>original: "svarbhānu"</note> and Ketu <note>original: "dhvaja"</note>, the husband will be wicked <note>original: "khalaḥ"</note>. If either the Lord of the Ninth or Jupiter is joined with the Lord of the Sixth House <note>original: "ari-śvareṇa," the lord of enemies</note>, the husband will be a "King of Thieves" <note>original: "corarāṭ"</note>, meaning a great thief. || 51 ||

If the Lord of the Ninth House and Jupiter are in bad houses, the husband will have a short life. If both are in a trine or an angle, he will be long-lived and wealthy. If they are joined with Mercury or the Lord of the Fifth <note>the Hindi text says "suteśa" or Lord of the 5th, while the Sanskrit commentary says "caturtheśa" or Lord of the 4th</note> in an angle or trine, he will be a scholar. If joined with Mars or Saturn, he will be a farmer. If joined with Rahu or Ketu, he will be wicked. If joined with the Lord of the Sixth, he will be a leader of thieves. || 51 ||

<header>Chapter on Women's Horoscopy :: 16</header>

->Chapter on Women's Horoscopy :: 16<-

> If the Sun is in the setting sign <note>the seventh house, where the sun sets</note>, the husband is fair-bodied, lustful, and has angry eyes. If the Moon is there, he is endowed with beauty and virtue, but has a thin body, is a seeker of pleasure, and is prone to illness. If Mars <note>original: "Kuja"</note> is in the seventh house, he is shameless <note>original: "nagna," literally "naked"</note>, of a cruel nature, lazy, a clever speaker, and has a reddish complexion. If Mercury <note>original: "Saumya"</note> is in the house of passion <note>the seventh house</note>, he is a lover of learning, wealth, and the complexities of various virtues. ॥ 52 ॥

> If Jupiter <note>original: "Guru"</note> is in the seventh house, the husband is long-lived, possesses wealth and power equal to a king, and is lustful from his youth. If Venus <note>original: "Kavya"</note> is there, he is handsome, a poet, a king, and clever in daily amusements and play. If Saturn <note>original: "Manda"</note> is in the house of passion, the husband has an aged body, an unstable frame, and is sinful. If Rahu or Ketu <note>original: "Shikhini"</note> are situated there, he is dull-witted, lowly, or like one of low status. ॥ 53 ॥

Now, the characteristics of the husband are stated according to the specific planet in the seventh house—**Fair-bodied** etc., in these two verses with simple meanings.
If the Sun is in the seventh house, the husband will be of fair complexion, lustful, and have a wrathful gaze. If the Moon is in the seventh place, the husband will be endowed with beauty and good qualities, but will have a weak body, be a seeker of pleasure, and be sickly. If Mars is in the seventh house, the husband will be shameless, of a cruel disposition, lazy, a clever talker, and have a reddish-fair complexion. If Mercury is in the seventh house, he will be a connoisseur of learning, finance, and the world of virtues. ॥ 52 ॥
If Jupiter is in the seventh house, the husband will be long-lived, wealthy like a king, and lustful even in childhood. If Venus is in the seventh house, he will be radiant, a poet, a king, and clever at performing daily amusements. If Saturn is in the seventh, the husband will have an old body, a trembling or unsteady frame, and be a sinner. If it is Rahu or Ketu, he will be of impure intellect, lowly, or equal to the lowly. ॥ 53 ॥

> The qualities arising from direction, country, status, religion, and profession that are described in the horoscopes of men should, in truth, be applied to the husbands in the horoscopes of women. The number of sons will be equal to the Navamshas <note>a one-ninth division of a zodiac sign</note> of the strongest planet among those occupying the seventh house. If the Lord of the Seventh <note>original: "Kamapati"</note> is in an angle <note>original: "Kendra," the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note>, he brings about great auspiciousness and celebratory times. ॥ 54 ॥

### Thus ends the Sixteenth Chapter in the Jataka Parijata composed by Vaidyanatha by the grace of the Nine Planets. ॥ 16 ॥

Regarding "Direction, country...": In a male's horoscope, the qualities of direction, country, status, religion, and action that are mentioned should also be specified in the birth of women. Furthermore, in a woman’s horoscope, these mentioned qualities of direction, etc., are to be specifically applied to her own husband. This is in accordance with the statement by Varahamihira: "Whatever results are said for the eighth house and others in a man's chart, all of that should be applied to the husbands in the case of women." Regarding "The Navamsha...": However many planets there are in the Navamsha <term>Navamsha: a 3°20' division of a sign used to determine hidden strengths</term> of the seventh house, the number of sons will be equal to the Navamsha count of the strongest planet among them. This means: in whichever sign the seventh house from the Ascendant falls, one looks at the planets in that Navamsha; the one who is strongest of all will indicate the number of sons based on the number of the Navamsha it occupies in that sign. Regarding "In an angle...": The Lord of the Seventh House, if placed in a Kendra <note>an angular house</note>, creates a time of great prosperity and celebration. ॥ 54 ॥

> The "Vimala" nectar-commentary on the Parijata was delighted by Kapileshwara.
> With this sixteenth chapter, this work on Women's Horoscopy reaches its completion. ॥ 18 ॥

The auspicious or inauspicious qualities such as direction, country, status, religion, and profession that are found in a man's horoscope should also be told for women. Similarly, in a woman's horoscope, these should be told for her husband. The sons should be said to be equal to the Navamsha of the strongest planet among those in the Navamsha of the seventh house. If the Lord of the Seventh is in a Kendra, it brings about a time of great welfare. ॥ 54 ॥

### Thus ends the "Vimala" Hindi commentary on the Chapter on Women's Horoscopy, the sixteenth chapter of the Jataka Parijata. ॥ 16 ॥

# Now begins the Chapter on the Timing of the Wheel of Time (*Kalachakra Dasha*) :: 17

> Having bowed to the Supreme Soul, Shiva, the ultimate cause, 
> who dwells in the center of the wheel of planets <note>original: "khecharam chakramadhyastham"</note> and is the embodiment of the sixty-four arts, ॥ 1 ॥
> 
> The Goddess Sarvamangala <note>An epithet for Parvati, meaning "All-Auspicious"</note> asked the Lord of Lords, the Great Controller: 
> "O Lord! Please tell me in detail the entire movement of the Wheel of Time (*Kalachakra*)." ॥ 2 ॥

Now, the chapter on the Timing of the Wheel of Time (*Kalachakra Dasha*) is explained. First, we find the Goddess's question to Lord Shankara regarding the movement of the Wheel of Time in the two verses starting with "Having bowed," which are simple in meaning. ॥ 1-2 ॥

Seeing the Lord of Lords, the Great Controller, Lord Shiva—who is the supreme cause, the Supreme Soul, who resides in the center of the planetary wheel, and possesses the sixty-four arts—Goddess Sarvamangala (Gauri) bowed and said: "O Lord! Speak to me of the movement of the entire Wheel of Time in detail." ॥ 1-2 ॥

---

->The Lord spoke:<-

> "I am in the form of the Sun, and you are called the Moon. 
> Through our union and separation, the world of the moving and the unmoving arises." ॥ 3 ॥

Hearing the Goddess's previously mentioned question regarding the Wheel of Time, Lord Mahadeva <note>The Great God, Shiva</note> gives the answer: "I am indeed the Soul of all, in the form of the Sun." This is because the scriptures state, "The Sun is the Soul of the moving and unmoving world." "And you, O Goddess, are called the Moon, because you are the Mind of all." This is supported by the Vedic hymn which says, "The Moon was born from the Mind," and the astrological rule that "The Sun is the Soul and the Moon is the Mind." Therefore, by the union and separation of the Soul and Mind, the world—moving and unmoving—becomes manifest or disappears. The implication is this: the Sun and the Moon alone are taken as the primary causes for these planetary periods (*Dashas*), as they allow us to understand the constellations (*Nakshatras*) and Time itself. ॥ 3 ॥

Lord Shankara said: "I am the form of the Sun, and you are the visible Moon. Through our union and separation, the entire world of moving and unmoving things is created and dissolved." ॥ 3 ॥

> One should draw a lotus with horizontal lines, excluding the four inner squares, to create the divisions. ॥ 4 ॥
> 
> The twelve signs starting from the east are the lords of the zodiacal wheel, beginning with the Sun. ॥ 4 <note>continued</note> ॥
> 
> Mars, Venus, Mercury, Moon, Sun, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Saturn, and Jupiter: 
> The wise say these are the lords of the signs and the lords of the divisions (*amshas*) starting from Aries. ॥ 5 ॥
> 
> Five, twenty-one, seven, nine, ten, sixteen, and four: 
> These are the years assigned to the Sun and others respectively, based on the lords of the signs. ॥ 6 ॥
> 
> In the constellations of Ashwini, Punarvasu, Chitra, Mula, and Purva Bhadrapada, etc., 
> one should count the divisions starting from Aries in a clockwise direction. ॥ 7 ॥
> 
> In Rohini, Magha, Vishakha, and Shravana, etc., 
> one should count the divisions starting from Scorpio in a counter-clockwise direction. ॥ 8 ॥
> 
> For the twelve divisions of the southern constellations, 
> having circled the wheel clockwise, one should place them ending with Pisces. ॥ 9 ॥
> 
> The three northern constellations should be counted clockwise starting from Scorpio. 
> Having reached the end of Sagittarius, one should understand the distinction between south and north. ॥ 10 ॥
> 
> Following the clockwise and counter-clockwise paths in groups of three constellations starting from Ashwini, 
> the 'Body' <note>original: "Deha," the starting point of the dasha</note> is counted in the clockwise movement, and the 'Soul' <note>original: "Jiva," the end point</note> is counted in the counter-clockwise movement. ॥ 11 ॥

<vocab>Kalachakra Dasha (Wheel of Time period), Shiva, Sarvamangala (Parvati), Aditya (Sun), Chandra (Moon), Jyotisha (Astrology), Savya-apasavya (Clockwise and counter-clockwise), Rashinatha (Lord of the zodiac sign)</vocab>

<header>Chapter on the Timing of the Wheel of Time (*Kalachakra Dasha*) :: 17</header>

# Chapter on the Timing of the Wheel of Time (*Kalachakra Dasha*) :: 17

> The maximum longevity is declared for the divisions within the houses of Aries, Taurus, Gemini, and Cancer. 
> [The values are] 100, 85, 83, and 86 respectively; one should say the same for their corresponding corner houses (trines). ॥ 12 ॥ 
> Having thus understood the calculation of lifespan, and having determined the *Deha* <note>The 'Body' point—the starting point of the calculation</note> and the *Jiva* <note>The 'Soul' or 'Life' point—the concluding point of the calculation</note>; 
> in the direct (clockwise) wheel, the first division is called the *Deha*. ॥ 13 ॥ 
> The *Jiva* is the final quarter in all cases; in the indirect (counter-clockwise) wheel, this is reversed.

Now the sequence of the Wheel of Time is explained with the phrase "Five eastern..." and so on. The method of drawing the wheel will become clear upon seeing the diagram itself. In the Wheel of Time, the years of the planetary periods (*Dashas*) for the Sun and others are assigned in a specific order. Specifically:
*   The Sun = 5 years
*   The Moon = 21 years
*   Mars = 7 years
*   Mercury = 9 years
*   Jupiter = 10 years
*   Venus = 16 years
*   Saturn = 4 years

These years are to be understood for each of the nine subdivisions of a sign, according to the lords of the signs (following the "Pau-Ra-Na-Bo..." mnemonic sequences for direct and indirect movement described below).

### Mnemonic Sentences for the Direct Wheel (*Savya-Chakra*)
<note>These phonetic syllables are coded triggers used by practitioners to remember the complex sequence of zodiac signs that govern the time-periods.</note>

1.  *Pau-ra-nya-bo-ma-tta-sa-ho-dhi*
2.  *Na-ksha-tra-da-si-cha-cha-na-shah*
3.  *Ru-po-shra-dhu-ni-dha-ya-ra-jnyam*
4.  *Vani-cha-sthan-da-dhi-jnya-ksha-tram*
5.  *Ham-sash-cha-da-shan-va-ra-pa-tram*
6.  *Ksha-ksha-dhi-ka-ra-go-bho-ma-cha*
7.  *Su-da-vi-na-ksha-shra-jnya-si-tah*
8.  *Va-ma-jnya-ra-ko-tra-shru-ni-dhih*

In the specified wheel—starting from the lunar mansions (*Nakshatras*) of Ashvini, Punarvasu, Hasta, Mula, and Purvabhadrapada—one should count the divisions starting from Aries in order. This is called the clockwise order or the "Direct Path" (*Savya-marga*).

In the lunar mansions of Rohini, Magha, Vishakha, and Shravana, one should count the divisions starting from Scorpio in reverse order. This is called the counter-clockwise order or "Indirect Path" (*Apasavya-marga*).

The practical application is as follows:
For the five mansions—Ashvini, Punarvasu, Hasta, Mula, and Purvabhadrapada—the first, second, third, and fourth quarters (*padas*) are placed respectively in the divisions of **Aries, Taurus, Gemini, and Cancer**.

For the next five—Bharani, Pushya, Chitra, Purvashadha, and Uttarabhadrapada—the four quarters are placed in **Leo, Virgo, Libra, and Scorpio**.

For the five—Krittika, Ashlesha, Svati, Uttarashadha, and Revati—the four quarters are placed in **Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, and Pisces**. This constitutes the Direct Order (*Savya-krama*).

Now for the Indirect Order: For the four mansions—Rohini, Magha, Vishakha, and Shravana—the four quarters are placed in **Scorpio, Libra, Virgo, and Leo**.

For Mrigashira, Purvaphalguni, Anuradha, and Dhanishtha, the four quarters are placed in **Cancer, Gemini, Taurus, and Aries**.

For Ardra, Uttaraphalguni, Jyeshtha, and Shatabhisha, the four quarters are placed in **Pisces, Aquarius, Capricorn, and Sagittarius**. Everything else will become clear by looking at the diagram of the Wheel.

### Now the Maximum Longevity for the Divisions of the Signs is Stated

In the houses of Aries, Taurus, Gemini, and Cancer:
*   In the divisions of Aries: 100 years <note>original: "jnyanakam" - a mnemonic for 100</note>
*   In Taurus: 85 years <note>original: "madah" - mnemonic for 85</note>
*   In Gemini: 83 years <note>original: "gajah" - mnemonic for 83</note>
*   In Cancer: 86 years <note>original: "tada" - mnemonic for 86</note>

In the "corner houses" (*konabhavaneshu*), meaning the trines (the 5th and 9th houses from the first four signs), one should say the same. 

That is to say: 
1.  **Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius** have a full lifespan of **100 years**.
2.  **Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn** have **85 years**.
3.  **Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius** have **83 years**.
4.  **Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces** have **86 years**.

<summary>This page defines the mathematical framework for the Kalachakra Dasha, assigning specific years to planets and calculating total longevity based on the zodiac signs. It introduces the complex system of "Direct" and "Indirect" movement through the lunar mansions (Nakshatras).</summary>
<keywords>Kalachakra Dasha, planetary years, Savya, Apasavya, Deha, Jiva, maximum longevity, Nakshatra quarters, zodiac trines</keywords>

<header>From the *Jataka Parijata* with Commentary—</header>

# Now, the Timing of the Wheel of Time (*Kalachakra Dasha*)

->Clockwise (*Savya*) Constellations: 1, 2, 3, 7, 8, 9, 13, 14...<- 
<note>In this system, the 27 lunar mansions are divided into 'Clockwise' and 'Counter-clockwise' groups to determine the order of the zodiac signs in the life-cycle.</note>

--- Page 526 ---
<meta>This page continues the technical mathematical explanation of the Kalachakra (Wheel of Time) dasha system. While the previous page provided mnemonic tables for specific lunar mansions, this page defines the fundamental concepts of "Body" (Deha) and "Soul" (Jiva) and provides the underlying rules for both the Direct (Savya) and Indirect (Apasavya) cycles, concluding with a practical example of how to calculate a person's starting planetary period.</meta>

<page-num>504</page-num>
<header>In the annotated Jataka Parijata—</header>

Now, **the knowledge of the Body (Deha) and the Soul (Jiva) is discussed**. In every zodiac sign, there are nine subdivisions (known as <term>Amshas</term> or portions). In the direct (clockwise) movement, the first subdivision is designated as the "Body" and the final subdivision is the "Soul." In the reverse (counter-clockwise) movement, this is inverted: the first portion is the "Soul" and the last is the "Body." The method for drawing this wheel is described in the *Parashariya* <note>The school or teachings of the sage Parashara, the traditional father of Indian astrology</note>:

> One should draw a wheel with twelve spokes, equal in length and height. Twelve houses are created in the clockwise wheel in successive order.
> In the second and following boxes, one should write the zodiac signs starting from Aries. Thus, the wheel of time known as the twelve-sign cycle is proclaimed.
> O learned one, Purva Bhadrapada and Revati are clockwise stars. This should also be observed for the quarters of the eight stars beginning with Ashvini.
> Listen, O Parvati! <note>The text is written as a dialogue where Lord Shiva instructs the Goddess Parvati</note> The specific method is clearly explained: the "Body" and "Soul" are Aries and Sagittarius for the clockwise quarters.
> From Aries to Sagittarius, the lords of the signs are the masters of the <term>Dashas</term> (planetary periods). For the "Body" and "Soul" of Capricorn and Gemini, the rulers are the directions, the lords, the Sun, the Earth, and the Mountains. <note>original: "digisharkashtabhudharah"—these are numerical codes for the number of years assigned to planets</note>
> The rulers of the six, four, five, and worlds <note>representing 6, 4, 5, and 14 years</note> are the lords of the periods. For the third quarters of the ten stars beginning with the South...
> Taurus is the "Body" and Gemini is the "Soul." The portions are calculated by two, twelve, one, and five. These are the rulers of the periods in order.
> In the fourth quarters of the ten stars beginning with Ashvini, Cancer and Pisces are the "Body" and "Soul." The nine lords from Cancer onwards are the masters of the periods; know this as certain, O Parvati!
> Bharani, Pushya, Chitra, Purvashadha, and Uttara Bhadrapada—the quarters of these seven stars should be observed starting from Bharani.
> For the first quarter of the southern group, Scorpio and Aries are the "Body" and "Soul." The lords are the serpents, the mountains, the seasons, the women, the bows, the Sun, the Moon, and the masters of action.
> For the second quarter of the southern group, Aquarius and Virgo are the "Body" and "Soul." The lords are Rudra, the Sun, the beautiful ones, the moons, the eyes, the Rama-fires, the oceans, the arrows, and the flavors.
> For the third quarter of the southern group, Libra and Virgo are the "Body" and "Soul." The lords of the signs are seven, eight, limbs, directions, the Sun, and the elephants.
> For the fourth quarter, Cancer and Sagittarius are known as the "Body" and "Soul." The lords are the Vedas, arrows, fires, eyes, the Moon, the Sun, the lords of directions, and the nines.
> Know this to be the clockwise order; now the reverse order is described:
> Draw a wheel with twelve spokes, equal in length and height. In the second and following boxes, write the signs in reverse starting from Scorpio.
> Rohini, Magha, Vishakha, and Shravana—these four should be viewed like the Creator (Brahma). The "Body" and "Soul" are Cancer and Sagittarius.
> Nine, ten, Rudras, the Sun, the Moon, the eyes, the fires, the moons, and the lords of the earth. In the second quarter of the Creator's stars, Libra and Gemini are the "Body" and "Soul."
> Six, seven, eight, the Sun, the Rudras, the directions, and the mountain signs are the lords. In the third quarter of the Creator's stars, Aquarius and Virgo are the "Body" and "Soul."
> Six, five, four, three, two, one, the nines, and the prominent lords. In the final quarter of Rohini, Scorpio and Aries are the "Body" and "Soul."
> The Sun, Moon, directions, qualities, oceans, tastes, mountains, and eight are the sign lords. Mrigashira, Arudra, Punarvasu, Purva Phalguni, Hasta, Swati, Anuradha, Jyeshtha...
> This group of eight stars should be understood in the same way as the Moon's stars. For the first quarter of Mrigashira, Cancer and Pisces are the "Body" and "Soul."
> The lords of the periods are the ten signs in reverse from Pisces to the end. Taurus is the "Body" and Gemini is the "Soul" in the second quarter of the Indra-star (Jyeshtha).
> Three, the Moon, Indra, Rudra, directions, the Sun, the Moon, and the lords of the houses. The "Body" and "Soul" are Capricorn and Gemini in the third quarter of Mrigashira.
> Three, five, four, six, eight, the Sun, and the ten sign lords. Aries and Sagittarius are the "Body" and "Soul" in the fourth quarter of the Indra-star.
> The ten lords are the signs in reverse from Sagittarius to Aries. Thus, the periods of the Body and Soul should be known in the reverse order.

---

-> This has been clearly told before you, O Parvati, my life-breath! <-

In this context, the method for determining the portions of the signs based on the birth star is written here. The number of the passed <term>Nakshatra</term> (lunar mansion) at birth should be divided by three. The remainder should be multiplied by four. To this, add the current quarter (pada) of the birth star. The resulting number indicates the <term>Rashi-mana</term> (measure of the sign portion). The <term>Purnayu-mana</term> (total lifespan measure) of that sign is the full lifespan for that individual. 

Furthermore, the <term>Bhukta-mana</term> (portion already elapsed) of the current quarter of the birth star should be multiplied by the total lifespan of the Ashvini cycle and divided by nine hundred. The result is the <term>Bhukta-dasha-mana</term> (measure of the planetary period already passed). Subtracting this from the total lifespan gives the <term>Bhogya-dasha-mana</term> (the measure of the planetary period remaining to be experienced).

---

-> Here is an example: <-

Suppose a person's birth occurs in the fourth quarter of the <term>Krittika Nakshatra</term>. In that fourth quarter, the elapsed time (Bhukta-mana) is 7 <term>Dandas</term> and 8 minutes. Then—
> "The passed stars divided by three, the remainder multiplied by four, added to the current quarter, becomes the portion of the signs."

According to this rule: The number of passed stars = 2 <note>Krittika is the 3rd star, so 2 have passed: Ashvini and Bharani</note>. Divided by 3, the remainder is 2. This multiplied by four becomes = 8.

(2 x 4) = 8. When added to the current quarter of the Krittika <term>Nakshatra</term> <note>A lunar mansion; Krittika is the third of the 27 lunar mansions</note> = (4), the result is (8 + 4) = 12. Therefore, the birth occurred during the <term>Dasha</term> <note>Planetary period</note> of the Pisces portion (<term>Meenansha</term>). The full lifespan for this portion is 86 years. Now, the elapsed portion of the fourth quarter of Krittika—(7|8)—is multiplied by the full lifespan of the Pisces portion (86): (7|8) x 86 = 4285 x 86 = 368,085. This is divided by nine hundred (900). The resulting elapsed Dasha in years and units is 40 years, 10 months, 23 days, and 12 <term>ghatis</term> <note>A traditional Indian unit of time equal to 24 minutes</note>. This is subtracted from the full lifespan (86 years): 86 – (40 years, 10 months, 23 days, 12 ghatis) = a remaining Dasha of 45 years, 1 month, 6 days, and 48 ghatis. For further clarity, one should consult the chart.

Draw five lines from East to West (vertical) and five lines crosswise (horizontal), creating 16 squares. If the four central squares are removed, a wheel of 12 squares is formed. Within these, the lords of the twelve signs from Aries to Pisces, starting from the East and moving toward the Northeast, should be understood as the lords of each square. || 3 ||

The sages declare that the lords of the signs from Aries onwards, and their corresponding subdivisions (<term>Navamshas</term>), are Mars, Venus, Mercury, the Moon, the Sun, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Saturn, and Jupiter respectively. || 5 ||

The Dasha years for the planets starting from the Sun are 5, 21, 7, 9, 10, 16, and 4. The years assigned to a zodiac sign are the same as the years assigned to the planet that rules it. For example: (Leo 5, Cancer 21, Aries/Scorpio 7, Gemini/Virgo 9, Sagittarius/Pisces 10, Taurus/Libra 16, Capricorn/Aquarius 4). || 4 ||

For the quarters of Ashvini, Punarvasu, Hasta, Mula, and Purva Bhadrapada (and the groups of three stars following them), one should count the portions from Aries in the <term>Savya</term> <note>Clockwise or direct</note> order. For Rohini, Magha, Vishakha, and Shravana, count the portions starting from Scorpio in the <term>Apasavya</term> <note>Counter-clockwise or indirect</note> order. In the direct movement, write the 12 signs from Aries to Pisces across the four quarters of the three stars. In the indirect movement, write the signs in reverse order from Scorpio to Sagittarius across the four quarters of each star. In the groups of three stars starting from Ashvini, the direct movement determines the "Body" (<term>Deha</term>) and the indirect determines the "Soul" (<term>Jiva</term>). This should be clarified using the Sanskrit wheel diagram. || 7-11 ||

In the portions of Aries, Taurus, Gemini, and Cancer, the full lifespans are said to be 100, 85, 83, and 86 years respectively. These same values represent the full lifespan within their respective angular houses.

Having thus understood the lifespan, one should evaluate the results by identifying the "Body" and the "Soul." The first portion is designated as the "Body" (<term>Deha</term>), and the very last is the "Soul" (<term>Jiva</term>). In the indirect movement, this is reversed (the first is the Soul and the last is the Body). || 13 ||

> When Rahu, Ketu, Mars, or the Sun are situated in the Body or the Soul, || 14 ||
> then death may occur in that period, or disease will take hold of the body.
> When the houses of the Body and Soul are occupied by Mercury, Jupiter, or Venus, || 15 ||
> everything brings happiness and prosperity, and grief and disease are destroyed.
> If occupied by a mixture of planets, one obtains mixed results. || 16 ||

Now the results of the previously defined "Body" and "Soul" are explained through the verse beginning with "Deha-Jiva." When specific planets occupy the defined Body or Soul positions, the stated results should be predicted. As stated in the *Brihat Parashara*:

> In the conjunction of the Body and Soul, if Mars, the Sun, or Saturn are present, a single conjunction brings death; what then to say if there are many?
> In whichever place the Soul is joined with the Body, if malefic planets are present there, death occurs during that Dasha.
> Great affliction occurs in the Body-conjunction, and the Soul-conjunction brings death. There is no doubt that one is struck down by the mere conjunction of the two.
> When Rahu, Saturn, Mars, or the Sun are in the Soul, one should recognize the arrival of the time of death and perform the prescribed atonement rituals (<term>Shanti</term>).
> When the Moon, Mercury, or Venus are in the Soul, they provide happiness and destroy disease and death.

When the Dasha of a house ruled by a malefic planet occurs, the Body and Soul bring suffering. During the Dasha of a benefic house or a benefic conjunction, good results occur. If the Body is joined with benefic planets, wealth and ornaments are certain. If the Soul is joined with benefic planets, one obtains sons and a wife. || 10–16

Regarding the "Time of the Lion’s Gaze": The movements known as the **Lion’s Gaze** and the **Frog’s Leap** will be described further ahead (in verses 89-91). 

"The ancient sages have determined three types of movement in the **Wheel of Time** (<term>Kalachakra</term>): the **Frog’s Leap** <note>original: "Manduka-gamana"</note>, **Backward movement**, and the **Lion’s Gaze** <note>original: "Simhavalokana"</note>, which is a 'looking back' or returning movement. Backward movement occurs between Cancer and Leo. The Lion’s Gaze occurs between Pisces and Scorpio, and between Sagittarius and Aries. The Frog’s Leap occurs between Virgo and Cancer, and between Leo and Gemini."

Furthermore, in the <term>Parashari</term> <note>referring to the system of the sage Parashara</note>: "The first movement is the Frog’s Leap, the second is the Monkey’s Leap... The movement known as the Lion’s Gaze... In Virgo or Cancer, or in Leo and Gemini, the movement is called the Frog’s Leap; this is a cause of disease. In Pisces or Scorpio, or in Sagittarius and Aries, it is the Lion’s Gaze; one receives results accordingly."

The meaning here is as follows: when such a transition occurs during the planetary periods of the Wheel of Time, the corresponding results must be predicted. To understand these movements, one must examine the Wheel itself. The results should be deduced by carefully analyzing the planets <term>distinguished by these characteristics</term> <note>original: "lakshana-lakshite"</note>; there is no need for further elaboration. || 17 ||

When a <term>Frog’s Leap</term> occurs during the time of the **Lion’s Gaze**, there is a fear of **untimely death** <note>original: "apamrityu"</note>; this is averted by performing rites of atonement or peace. (The details of the Lion’s Gaze, Frog’s Leap, and Backward movement will be explained later in verses 89-91). || 17 ||

When moving from Sagittarius to Aries, the death of a son and a friend may occur. If <term>benefic planets</term> <note>auspicious influences like Jupiter or Venus</note> are present in this transition, there is no fear; however, if <term>malefic planets</term> <note>harsh influences like Mars or Saturn</note> are present, fear arises. || 20 ||

In the period of moving from Leo to Gemini, one should abandon travel to the East. For the successful completion of a task, one should undertake a pleasant journey toward the Southwest. || 22 ||

In the <term>Savya</term> <note>clockwise or "right-handed"</note> wheel, the transition from Cancer to Leo causes loss of work and disease. One should seek refuge in the South before returning. || 23 ||

> For the signs of Sagittarius, Leo, and Aries, Aries is the "Body" (<term>Deha</term>) and Sagittarius is the "Soul" (<term>Jiva</term>). > For the signs of Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius, the Bull (Taurus) is the Body and Gemini is the Soul, as stated by the great sages. For Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces, the Fish (Pisces) is the Soul and Cancer is the Body sign in the clockwise wheel. || 27 ||

Now, the author explains the definitions of "Body" and "Soul" for the twelve signs within the previously mentioned Wheel of Time periods. For the group of Sagittarius, Leo, and Aries: Aries (ruled by Mars) is designated as the Body, and Sagittarius (ruled by Jupiter) is the Soul. For the group of Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn: the "Akokera" <note>an ancient term for Capricorn</note> (ruled by Saturn) is the Body, and the Twins (Gemini, ruled by Mercury) is the Soul. This is the rule for the clockwise (<term>Savya</term>) wheel. In the counter-clockwise (<term>Apasavya</term>) wheel, the reverse should be understood: for Sagittarius, Leo, and Aries, Sagittarius becomes the Body and Aries the Soul; for Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn, Gemini is the Body and Capricorn the Soul.

For the "angles of the Twins" (Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius), the "Ox" (Taurus, ruled by Venus) is the Body, and Gemini (ruled by Mercury) is the Soul, according to the great sages. This specific rule remains the same for both the clockwise and counter-clockwise wheels. Finally, for the group of Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces: Pisces (Jupiter) is the Soul and Cancer (the Moon) is the Body sign. This applies to the clockwise wheel. In the counter-clockwise wheel, the reverse applies: for Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces, Pisces is the Body and Cancer is the Soul. See the chart for clarity.

In the clockwise wheel, for Aries, Sagittarius, and Leo, Aries is the Body sign and Sagittarius is the Soul sign. For Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn, Capricorn is the Body and Gemini is the Soul. In the counter-clockwise wheel, know this to be reversed. The lords of these signs should be known as the "Lord of the Body" (<term>Dehesha</term>) and the "Lord of the Soul" (<term>Jivesha</term>). Refer to the chart for clarity. || 26 ||

In the clockwise wheel, for Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius, the great sages have named Taurus as the Body and Gemini as the Soul. For Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces, Pisces is the Soul and Cancer is the Body. Here too, understand the Lord of the Body and Soul to be the respective planetary rulers of those signs. In the counter-clockwise wheel, this is reversed. || 27 ||

### Technical Terms Summary
*   **Kalachakra Dasha:** The "Wheel of Time" system of planetary periods.
*   **Deha (Body):** A sensitive zodiac sign in the chart representing physical health.
*   **Jiva (Soul):** A sensitive zodiac sign representing the life force and mental state.
*   **Savya / Apasavya:** The clockwise and counter-clockwise directions the wheel can turn based on birth constellations.
*   **Benefics / Malefics:** "Good" and "bad" planets (e.g., Jupiter vs. Saturn).

In this <term>Kalachakra</term> <note>the "Wheel of Time" predictive system</note>, specific signs are defined as the "Body" (<term>Deha</term>) and the "Soul" (<term>Jiva</term>). One should predict the results based on the presence of Mars, Saturn, the Sun, or Rahu within these signs. If even one such planet is present, death may occur; if many such planets are combined, death is certain to be declared. For example, as in the previous illustration, during the period of the Pisces portion (<term>amsha</term>), the "Body" is Cancer (ruled by the Moon) and the "Soul" is Pisces (ruled by Jupiter). ### Now, the Results of the "Body" and "Soul" Signs

> The Sun causes various calamities: the loss of wealth, intense fever, fear of enemies, and loss of position. The essence is that only Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus provide auspicious results in these positions. These verses have a simple meaning and therefore have not been explained in great detail to avoid making the text too long. || 37-46 ||

### End of the Results for the "Body" and "Soul" Signs

If the Sun is in the "Body" or "Soul" sign, it causes various calamities, loss of wealth, pain, fever, fear of enemies, loss of position, and diseases such as <term>gulma</term>, <term>grahani</term>, consumption, and ear diseases resulting from biliary disorders. It also causes the death of cattle and family members, and the destruction of brothers. || 37 ||

The Moon, when positioned in the Body or Soul points, brings about meetings with kinsmen, the birth of a daughter, and general health. It provides ornaments, fine clothing, and honor from the king. Mercury, in the Body or Soul points, grants great happiness through friends. Jupiter, situated in the Body or Soul points, provides various kinds of wealth and happiness, high status, and "royal consecration" <note>original: *rajyabhisheka*; a coronation or high promotion</note>. Venus, in the Body or Soul points, brings the gain of love and pleasure from women, various garments, and wealth in the form of cattle, vehicles, and collections of gems. Saturn, in the Body or Soul points, causes quarrels, emaciation of the body, and even death. It causes suffering from poison, loss of honor and wealth, and the destruction of one's dignity, spouse, and children. It also leads to the ruin of the home, wealth, agriculture, trade, and livestock. || 44 ||

If Rahu is in the Soul or Body points, it is said that men suffer from enemies, distress to kinsmen, mental agony, and ailments such as <term>paksaghata</term> <note>paralysis or stroke</note>, as well as fear from the state. || 45 ||

If Ketu is in the Body or Soul points, one suffers from fire and "falling blood" <note>original: *rakta girna*; could refer to hemorrhaging or blood disorders</note>. It causes poverty, the loss of kinsmen, loss of one's place of residence, and the depletion of wealth. || 46 ||

Now, the author discusses the results of the <term>Kalachakra Dasha</term> <note>a complex Hindu timing system based on the moon's position in a specific lunar mansion</note> in relation to the <term>Bhavas</term> <note>astrological houses</note>. Here, the following should be understood: Based on the quarter of the <term>Nakshatra</term> <note>lunar mansion</note>, the cycle moves in either a clockwise or counter-clockwise <note>original: *savya-apasavya*</note> direction. The specific sign associated with that portion of the cycle will yield results based on which house (such as the Ascendant) that sign occupied in the birth chart. If that sign is auspicious and associated with beneficial influences, the results are very favorable; otherwise (if in an inauspicious sign or with harsh planets), the results should be declared as unfavorable. The verses themselves are clear in meaning and thus further elaboration is set aside. || 47-75 ||

During the timing cycle <note>original: "Chakra-dasha"</note> of the **Fifth House** (The House of Children), one attains high status <note>original: "Rajyaprapti"; literally "attainment of a kingdom"</note>, receives honors from the ruler, and gains a spouse and children. This period brings patience, good health, the ability to provide for relatives, the giving of food in charity, and the acquisition of fame and auspiciousness. One performs good deeds for others and gains wealth, vehicles, clothing, and jewelry. Here too, the results should be declared as favorable or unfavorable based on whether the house is an auspicious or inauspicious sign and its association with various planets. || 58-60 ||

In the timing cycle of the **Sixth House**, there is a fear of fire, thieves, enemies, poison, and the government <note>original: "Raja"; literally "kings"</note>. One suffers from physical pain, loss of one's place or home, and faces great danger from diseases such as diabetes, abdominal tumors, anemia, dysentery, and tuberculosis <note>original: "Prameha, Gulma, Pandu, Grahani, and Kshaya"</note>. This period may bring dishonor to the spouse, the loss of children and relatives, imprisonment, or the accidental consumption of toxic substances. One is also burdened by debt and poverty. If the Sixth House is an auspicious sign, these ill effects are lessened; if it is an inauspicious sign, these results manifest in full. || 61-63 ||

During the timing cycle of the **Seventh House**, one experiences marriage, happiness from a spouse, the birth of a son, and the enjoyment of beautiful, delicious food. There is gain through agriculture, livestock, vehicles, and ornaments, alongside honors from the ruler and a beautiful reputation. The presence of auspicious signs and planets significantly enhances these benefits. || 64-66 ||

In the timing cycle of the **Eighth House** (The House of Death), one must predict great sorrow, loss of wealth, loss of one's home, loss of friends, and diseases of the rectum or stomach. It brings poverty, a lack of appetite, a shortage of food, and fear of enemies. If the Eighth House is an inauspicious sign and is joined by malefic planets, these negative results will manifest fully. || 66-67 ||

During the timing cycle of the **Ninth House**, favorable results are certain. One acquires children, friends, a spouse, wealth, land for farming, livestock, a home, and jewelry. One achieves success in good works and develops a love for the company of virtuous people. If there are auspicious signs and planets involved, these rewards are even more pronounced. || 68-69 ||

In the timing cycle of the **Tenth House**, one attains high status, receives honors from the ruler, and sees the rise of fame, spouse, children, and friends. It is a time of rising auspiciousness, authority, freedom from disease, the company of the virtuous, and the performance of beautiful deeds. If the sign is auspicious, these results will be exceptionally wonderful. || 70-71 ||

During the timing cycle of the **Eleventh House** (The House of Gain), there is gain of wealth, health, jewelry, and beautiful objects. One acquires household materials and sees the prosperity of spouse, children, friends, and relatives. There is the recovery of debts, love from the ruler, and the company of the virtuous. || 72-73 ||

In the timing cycle of the **Twelfth House** (The House of Expenditure), there is physical pain, loss of position, and fear from thieves, fire, or the anger of the government. One suffers at the hands of relatives, the spouse, and the ruler. There is a destruction of industry, laziness, losses in farming and livestock, poverty, and failure in one's actions. If the sign is inauspicious and joined by malefic planets, these results are intensified.

Regarding all the results mentioned above, this distinction must be understood: if the house is an auspicious sign and joined by auspicious planets, the good results are magnified. If it is an inauspicious sign joined by malefic planets, the bad results are magnified. If the conditions are mixed, the results should be interpreted accordingly. || 74-75 ||

### Special Considerations for the Results of the Wheel Timing System

> The results of the houses from the Ascendant <note>original: "Lagna"</note> to the twelfth have been described thus. 
> There is a special rule here, which is now being told specifically. || 76 ||
> One should apply the results appropriately based on the strength of the Lord of the Sign <note>original: "Rashisha"</note>. 
> If the Lord of the Sign is powerful, in its sign of exaltation, in its own sign, or in its own field of action, || 77 ||
> and if it is joined by friends and aspected by auspicious planets, then the good results mentioned should be predicted. 
> But if the Lord is weak, placed in an enemy's sign or a sign of debilitation, or oppressed by the rays of the Sun <note>original: "Dineshakarapidite"; meaning the planet is combust</note>, || 78 ||
> or if it is placed in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth houses and aspected by malefic enemies, 
> then the person born will experience the suffering associated with that sign's results. || 79 ||
> In such a case, the suffering is doubled, and even the good results of the sign become tainted. 
> If the strength of the Lord is weak, one may indeed encounter great misfortune. || 80 ||

**Now, the author explains the specific nuances regarding the results of the twelve house timing cycles—beginning with the Ascendant:** Regarding the previously mentioned results for the twelve houses <term>Bhava; the twelve areas of life such as wealth, siblings, children, etc.</term> starting from the Ascendant, I shall now describe the specific details in depth. One should apply the results appropriately according to the strength of the ruler of that zodiac sign. (The implication is that the degree of the stated results—whether more or less—depends entirely on the strength of the house ruler.) 

When the **ruler of the sign** (the lord of the specific house) is endowed with strength, is in its sign of exaltation, is in its own or a friend's divisional chart <term>Varga; a mathematical sub-division of a sign used to determine planetary strength</term>, is associated with friends, or is aspected by benefic planets, then the results declared will be auspicious. 

Conversely, if the ruler of the sign is weak, or is in an enemy sign, or is debilitated, or is "combust" <note>original: "Dineshvara-pidite"; literally "afflicted by the Lord of Day (the Sun)," meaning too close to the Sun to be seen</note>, or is hidden in the "blind darkness" of the 6th, 8th, or 12th houses <note>these are the "Dusthanas" or difficult houses in astrology</note>, or is aspected by a malefic or an enemy, then the results arising from that sign during its timing cycle <term>Chakra Dasha</term> will be difficult and inauspicious. 

If the ruler of the house is weak, then even if the sign's inherent result is good, it will instead yield double the difficulty and misfortune. However, if the ruler of the house possesses great strength, then the auspicious results of that sign will be doubled in their goodness. There is no doubt or uncertainty in this. The essence is that the strength of the house ruler is required for the house to produce good results. 

If the house ruler is in a moveable sign, or even in a moveable sub-division <note>Navamsha</note>, or if the timing cycle belongs to a moveable sign, then that period brings travel to foreign lands for the individual. 

**In the timing cycle, if even one factor is moveable** (meaning the house is a moveable sign, or the house ruler is in a moveable sign, or in a moveable sub-division, etc.), then for the **entire duration of that cycle** (specifically during the sub-periods of other moveable signs), one should predict travel abroad or the attainment of one's place—meaning the gain of a position signified by that sign. || 76-83 ||

**The results of the Wheel of Time timing cycles for the twelve houses, starting from the Ascendant, have been described in this manner.** What is specific here is now explained in detail. || 76 ||

**One should plan the appropriate results according to the strength of each house's respective ruler.** If the ruler of the sign is strong, in its exaltation, in a friendly sign, in its own divisional chart, joined with a friend, or seen by a benefic planet, then the results mentioned will manifest fully and correctly. If the house ruler is weak, in an enemy or debilitated sign, afflicted by the Sun, located in the 6th, 8th, or 12th houses, or seen by malefic or enemy planets, then the results of that house's timing cycle will be painful. || 77-79 ||

**If the result of a house-sign is inherently bad, then the result of an inauspicious timing cycle for that house is twice as bad.** Furthermore, if the lord of that house is also weak, then even greater calamities (bad results) occur. || 80 ||

**If the strength of the house ruler is exceptional and the result born of the sign is also good, then the timing cycle result is twice as auspicious;** of this, there is no doubt. || 81 ||

**If the house ruler is in a moveable sign, or in the sub-division of a moveable sign, then the timing cycle of that moveable sign-house will cause foreign travel.** || 82 ||

**If even one factor is moveable—that is, if the house or the house ruler is in a moveable sign or a moveable sub-division—then throughout that entire timing cycle, one should know there will be foreign travel or the attainment of one's own place.** || 83 ||
