->**Whatever has been stated regarding the "Yogas of Royalty" and the results of "Lunar Yogas," as well as what has been said regarding the "Celestial Yogas" and the aspects of beneficial or harmful planets; || 85 ||**<-

->**Whatever has been stated by the ancient sages regarding the "Great Yogas" of the planets—a wise scholar should, by using their own intellect, apply all of those to the specific timing cycles of the Zodiac Wheel. || 86 ||**<-

The author now explains the timing for the fruition of all previously mentioned results within the "Wheel of Time" cycle <term>Chakra Dasha; a complex system where life events are timed based on the movement through the zodiac signs</term>. Starting from the "Chapter on Definitions" up to this point, whatever results have been gathered based on the houses, zodiac signs, and planets—a wise scholar should distinguish and apply the timing of those results during the periods of the respective zodiac signs within the direct and indirect cycles <term>Savya-Apasavya; "Savya" refers to the clockwise/direct wheel, while "Apasavya" refers to the counter-clockwise/indirect wheel</term>. Indeed, all planets and zodiac signs grant their respective good or bad results only during their own specific timing periods <term>Dasha</term>. As the sage Varahamihira <note>A famous 6th-century Indian astronomer and astrologer</note> says:
> Whatever substance was assigned to a planet in the "Chapter on Definitions," and whatever livelihood was taught in the "Chapter on Career," and whatever arises from the positions of the houses and planetary combinations—all of that must be applied during that planet's specific timing period. || 84-86 ||

<gloss>The Hindi commentary clarifies that results from planetary aspects, "Celestial Yogas" <note>original: "Nabhasa-yogas"</note>, and combinations for power must be analyzed intellectually to see how they fit into the timing wheel.</gloss>

->**One should place the zodiac wheel starting from Aries on the ground toward the south; and for the northern wheel, one should indicate it starting from the end. || 87 ||**<-

->**Whether a result is fruitful or fruitless, whether in the East or other directions, or from the specific divisional directions of the zodiac signs—one should indicate it there. || 88 ||**<-

->**In this manner, following the path of the traditional teachings, the results for all factors are determined. || 3/4 ||**<-

**Regarding "Place the wheel":** One should draw the zodiac wheel from Aries to Pisces for the southern or "direct" path. Similarly, one should draw the wheel starting from the end—meaning Scorpio—for the northern or "indirect" path (moving in reverse from Scorpio toward Sagittarius). A wise person should then indicate the results or lack thereof from that diagram. In that context, whatever result pertains to a specific house or sign is obtainable from the direction associated with that sign in the wheel; this should be indicated for all planets and signs following the traditional path of instruction. This is what is being said: in either the direct or indirect wheel, when one must predict the good or bad results during the timing period of a specific sign, one should declare the attainment of that result in the specific direction where that sign falls on the wheel. || 87-88 3/4 ||

<gloss>The Hindi commentary explains that the practitioner should draw the direct cycle (Aries onwards) and the indirect cycle (Scorpio backwards) on the ground. By looking at which direction (East, West, etc.) a planet or sign occupies in this physical map, the astrologer can predict the direction from which results will come.</gloss>

# The Three Types of Movement in the Wheel of Time

->**The movement of the Wheel of Time is determined to be of three types by the ancient sages: || 89 ||**<-

->**The "Frog’s Leap," "Moving Backward," and the "Lion’s Gaze"—which is a form of returning. || 90 ||**<-

->**"Moving Backward" occurs between the signs of Cancer and Leo. The "Lion's Gaze" movement occurs between Pisces and Scorpio, and between Sagittarius and Aries. || 91 ||**<-

->**The "Frog’s Leap" movement occurs between Virgo and Cancer, and between Gemini and Leo. || 1/2 ||**<-

<note>These "movements" are technical terms for when the timing cycle skips signs or jumps across the zodiac. These transitions are traditionally considered very intense or "turbulent" periods in a person's life.</note>

<vocab>Kalachakra Dasha, Raja Yoga, Chandra Yoga, Nabhasa Yoga, Manduka-gamana (Frog's Leap), Simhavalokana (Lion's Gaze), Prishthato-gamana (Backward Movement), Varahamihira</vocab>

The author now describes the three types of movements within the timing cycle of the Wheel of Time: **The movement of the Wheel of Time.** The **ancient sages** = such as Garga and Parashara, have **determined** = decided that the movement of the Wheel of Time is **threefold** = of three types. He identifies them as: 1. **The Frog Leap** <term>Manduka-gamana; jumping over one sign</term>, 2. **The Backward Movement** <term>Prishthato-gamana; also called the Monkey Leap, moving back to a previous sign</term>, and 3. **The Lion's Glance** <term>Simhavalokana; a long leap forward or backward where the planet "looks back" at the sign it left</term> (this is also called the "Return"). The characteristics of these movements are as follows: From **Cancer and Leo**, the movement is backward. Between **Pisces and Scorpio**, and between **Sagittarius and Aries**, the movement is the **Lion** = the Lion's Glance. Between **Virgo and Cancer**, and between **Leo and Gemini**, the movement is the Frog Leap. This is explained as follows: In both the direct <term>Savya</term> and indirect <term>Apasavya</term> wheels, the movement of Cancer to Gemini or Leo to Cancer is called the "Backward Movement" <note>This mimics a monkey's erratic backward hop</note>. Similarly, the reciprocal movement between Pisces and Scorpio, or Sagittarius and Aries—which are the ninth and fifth positions from each other—is called the Lion's Glance. Likewise, the movement from Leo to Gemini or Virgo to Cancer is the Frog Leap <note>The "frog" jumps over one sign to reach the next</note>. As stated in the *Parashariya* <note>The classic text attributed to the sage Parashara</note>:

->In the first instance, the movement is the Frog; in the second, it is the Monkey. Up to the end of the "Arrow-Forest" <note>A poetic reference to certain degrees or divisions in the cycle</note> section, the movement is the Lion's Glance.<-
->When moving between Virgo and Cancer, or Leo and Gemini, it is known as the Frog Leap, which causes disease.<-
->Between Pisces and Scorpio, or Sagittarius and Aries, it is the Lion's Glance, and one receives the results accordingly.<-

This should be understood when analyzing the sub-periods <term>Antardasha</term> of the results. If, during someone's major period, the sub-period moves from Cancer to Gemini, or from Leo to Cancer, it is called the Backward Movement (or Monkey Leap). This logic should be applied everywhere. The results of these movements should be known according to the methods described hereafter. || 89-91 1/2 ||

The experts have said this movement of the Wheel of Time is of three types: 1. Frog Leap, 2. Backward (Behind) Movement, and 3. The Lion's Glance, which is also called the "Return." || 89-90 ||

Cancer and Leo have a backward movement. Moving from sign 5 (Leo) to 4 (Cancer), or from 4 (Cancer) to 3 (Gemini), is backward movement. The movement of Pisces-Scorpio and Sagittarius-Aries is the Lion's Glance (going from Pisces to Scorpio and Sagittarius to Aries is called the Lion's Glance). The movement of Virgo-Cancer and Leo-Gemini (moving from 6 to 4 or 5 to 3) is called the Frog Leap. || 91 1/2 ||

Now, the results of the Lion's Glance and the "Period-Gap" are described. The **wise** (**the learned**) say that a **cruel planet's** period, or a period of a planet that is **combust** (joined with the Sun), **debilitated**, or in **decline** (with diminished rays), is a "Period-Gap" <note>A vulnerable transition point between two major life chapters</note>. The rest is clear as stated. || 91 1/2 - 94 1/2 ||

(During the Lion's Glance, one should predict distress from fever, loss of place, loss of love from kinsmen, pain from equals, falling into water or a well, fear of poison, weapons, and fire, and falling from a vehicle (like a horse, etc.) if it occurs during a "Period-Gap." ### Now, he speaks of the results of the Frog's Leap:

During the previously mentioned "Frog's Leap" <note>Sanskrit: *Manduka-gati*; a jump over one sign in the sequence</note> within a sub-period, the death of one’s **Teacher** (*Guru*)—meaning a superior elder—or one's **parents** (both mother and father) occurs. Furthermore, there is danger from **poison, weapons, fire, fever, and thieves**. In the **Direct Cycle** (*Savya-chakra*), during the Frog's Leap period, **peers** (such as brothers and friends) will experience suffering. Specifically, in the "Lion-Pair Frog Leap"—meaning a leap from **Leo into Virgo** or from **Gemini into Cancer**—one should predict the **death of the mother**. In such cases, one should also predict the subject's own death, **political troubles**, **delirious fever**, and fear of **enemies** (the foe). || 95-97 ||

**During the Frog's Leap in the Indirect Cycle, the teacher dies, or the mother and father die. There is fear from poison, weapons, fire, fever, thieves, and snakes. In the Frog's Leap of the Direct Cycle, people like oneself (peers) suffer. In a leap from Leo or Gemini, the mother dies, and there is personal death, royal punishment, delirium, and fear of enemies. || 95-97 ||**

> In the Lion's Glance of the Direct Cycle, there is fear from four-legged animals and fire.
> In the Backward Movement of the Direct Cycle, there is the destruction of wealth, grain, and cattle. || 98 ||
> The death of the father, laziness, or the death of those equal to oneself occurs.
> In the Frog's Leap of the Indirect Cycle, there is distress for the wife and son, and great exhaustion. || 99 ||
> One suffers from burning fever, fear of wild animals, loss of position, and fear of enemies.
> In the Lion's Glance of the Indirect Cycle, there is displacement from one’s home and the death of the father. || 100 ||
> In the Backward Movement of the Indirect Cycle, one predicts fear of water, loss of status,
> The ruin of the father, the anger of the King, and wandering through difficult fortresses and forests. || 101 ||

The meaning of these verses (98-101) is clear.

**In the Lion's Glance of the Direct Cycle, there is fear from four-legged animals and fire. In the Backward Movement of the Direct Cycle, there is loss of wealth, grain, and animals; the father dies, or laziness and the death of peers occur. In the Frog's Leap, there is distress for the wife and son, hard labor, burning fever, fear of deer (wild animals), loss of position, and fear of enemies. In the Lion's Glance of the Indirect Cycle, one loses their place and the father dies. In the Backward Movement of the Indirect Cycle, there is fear of water, loss of position, destruction of the father, the King’s anger, and wandering through fortresses and forests. || 98-101 ||**

"...*Mu* 5, *Kshamadhikaragomimach* 6, *Sudadhinakshatrajnah Sitah* 7, *Vamangarakotrakshunidhih* 8" <note>These are mnemonic code-sentences (Vakyas) where each syllable corresponds to a specific numerical value and zodiac sign in the Kalachakra system.</note>—these are known as the final sentences of the **Direct Cycle** (*Savya-chakra*). Here, the following should be carefully noted: The durations of the periods (*Dashas*) for the first, second, third, and fourth quarters (*Charanas*) of **Ashwini, Punarvasu, Hasta, Mula, and Purva Bhadrapada** are identical to those of the quarters of **Krittika, Ashlesha, Swati, Revati, and Uttara Ashadha**. 

The only difference between them is as follows: the first, second, third, and fourth quarters of Ashwini, Punarvasu, Hasta, Mula, and Purva Bhadrapada are related respectively to the signs of **Aries, Taurus, Gemini, and Cancer**. In contrast, the first, second, third, and fourth quarters of Krittika, Ashlesha, Revati, Swati, and Uttara Ashadha are related respectively to **Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, and Pisces**. However, in both cases, the duration of the periods and their planetary lords are the same. 

Furthermore, the first, second, third, and fourth quarters of **Chitra, Uttara Bhadrapada, Bharani, Purva Ashadha, and Pushya** are related to the signs of **Leo, Virgo, Libra, and Scorpio** respectively. Their period years are to be understood through the last four sentences of the Direct Cycle. This is how the **Direct Cycle** (*Savya-chakra*) operates.

Now, the **Indirect Cycle** (*Apasavya-chakra*) is described: For the lunar mansions of **Vishakha, Rohini, Magha, and Shravana**, the first four sentences of the Indirect Cycle are: "1. *Dhanakshetrayam parajnamiva*, 2. *Tasadrakshunidhirhasa*, 3. *Chamibhogo-rayadhanaksham*, 4. *Trayoragimametasaha*." 

Likewise, for the lunar mansions of **Shatabhisha, Anuradha, Jyeshtha, Mrigashira, Dhanishtha, Purva Phalguni, Uttara Phalguni, and Ardra**, those who know the science say that the final sentences of the Indirect Cycle are: "5. *Trakshunidhirhassastameva*, 6. *Mirayudhanakshatraparah*, 7. *Gomavachi-sadatrikshunne*, 8. *Dhijah Sitomivangariaka*."

This should also be understood: In the **Indirect Cycle**, the first, second, third, and fourth quarters of **Vishakha, Rohini, Magha, and Shravana** are related respectively to **Scorpio, Libra, Virgo, and Leo**. Their period years are determined by the first four sentences of the Indirect Cycle. 

Furthermore, the durations for **Mrigashira, Purva Phalguni, Anuradha, and Dhanishtha** are the same as the durations for **Ardra, Uttara Phalguni, Jyeshtha, and Shatabhisha**. The only difference is that the quarters of the former group (Mrigashira, etc.) relate to **Cancer, Gemini, Taurus, and Aries**, while the quarters of the latter group (Ardra, etc.) relate to **Pisces, Aquarius, Capricorn, and Sagittarius**. If one does not observe all of this within the Wheel of Time sequence, the calculations will be useless. || 102-105 ||

<header>Chapter 17: The Chapter on the Wheel of Time Periods (Kalachakra Dasha)</header>

Through these eight sentences, nine sub-periods (*Antardashas*) are described for each sign in the **Direct Cycle** (*Savya-chakra*). Among the twelve zodiac signs, the first four signs and the final four signs have identical measures; therefore, the first four sentences indicate the periods for these eight signs. Similarly, the four sentences in the middle serve to explain the periods of the four signs situated in the center. As stated previously, the periods of these signs arise based on the quarters (*Charanas*) of the lunar mansions (*Nakshatras*) falling into the Direct and Indirect categories. Now, in all eight of these sentences, the numerical values for the signs must be understood according to the values assigned to the letters. As the ancient rule states: **"The numbers are indicated by the letters of the Ka, Ta, Pa, and Ya groups, specifically the final letter of the combined syllable."** <note>original: "कटपयवर्गभवैरिरिह पिण्डान्त्यैरक्षरैरङ्काः" — This refers to the *Katapayadi* system, an ancient Indian alphanumeric code used to preserve numerical data in poetic verses.</note>

By this rule: *Pau* = 1, *Ram* = 2, *Ga* = 3, *Vo* = 4, *Ma* = 5, *Ta* = 6, *Sa* = 7, *Ho* = 8, *Dhi* = 9. Thus, in the first sign (**Aries**) of the Direct Cycle, there are sub-periods of nine signs. The lords of these periods and sub-periods are: Mars, Venus, Mercury, Moon, Sun, Mercury, Venus, Mars, and Jupiter. <note>These correspond to the planetary lords of Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, and Sagittarius respectively.</note> The years for these periods will be mentioned in a later verse. In this same manner, the numbers for all eight sentences—and consequently the signs and their lords—should be understood through the values of the letters. For the sake of clarity, one should consult the Period Chart itself. ॥ 1-8 ॥

For the sake of confirmation, the chart itself should be consulted. ॥ 1-8 ॥

### Now, the Years of the Wheel of Time Periods (Kalachakra Dasha)

> Five, twenty-one, seven, nine, ten, sixteen, and four
> Are the years for the Sun and others in order,
> Based upon the lordship of the signs. || 106 ||

The years of the periods (*dashas*) for the planets starting with the Sun in the Wheel of Time system are now stated. By the phrase "Five, twenty-one...", it is explained that based on the lordship of the signs, the periods for the Sun and the other planets are 5, 21, 7, 9, 10, 16, and 4 years respectively. <note>In this system, each planet is assigned a specific number of years which then dictates the length of time a person spends under the influence of the signs that planet rules.</note> One must understand that because a planet owns a particular sign, that sign also takes on the same number of years for its period. Accordingly:
*   **Sun** (rules Leo) = 5 years
*   **Moon** (rules Cancer) = 21 years
*   **Mars** (rules Aries and Scorpio) = 7 years
*   **Mercury** (rules Gemini and Virgo) = 9 years
*   **Jupiter** (rules Sagittarius and Pisces) = 10 years
*   **Venus** (rules Taurus and Libra) = 16 years
*   **Saturn** (rules Capricorn and Aquarius) = 4 years

<gloss>The Hindi commentary notes: According to the lordship of the signs, the years for the Sun and other planets are 5, 21, 7, 9, 10, 16, and 4 in order. This verse was already mentioned as verse 6 in this same chapter.</gloss>

### Now, the Method for Calculating Sub-periods (Antardashas)

> Multiply the [major] period by the sub-period sign's years,
> And divide by the total lifespan [of that cycle].
> The result should be known as the sub-period,
> Consisting of years, months, and days. || 107 ||

<note>This mathematical formula allows an astrologer to break down a major life-period into smaller segments. You take the length of the current major period, multiply it by the specific value of the sub-sign, and divide by the total sum of all sign-years in that specific soul's cycle.</note>

<page-num>521</page-num>
<header>Chapter 17: The Chapter on the Wheel of Time Periods</header>

Now, the method for determining the sub-periods <note>term: Antardasha; the secondary period of a planet or zodiac sign within a major period (Mahadasha)</note> is described. It is said: In the major period of each planet or zodiac sign, there is a sub-period belonging to every planet or zodiac sign. This is what is meant by the word "Antardasha." 

The method for calculating it is as follows: When the sub-period of a particular planet is required within the major period of another planet, one should multiply the respective period values <note>original: "dashamana"</note> of those two planets. That is, multiply the major period years of one by the years of the other. The product of this multiplication should then be divided by the "Total Lifespan" <note>term: Purnayu; the total sum of years assigned to a specific zodiacal sequence in the Kalachakra system</note>—specifically, the full lifespan associated with the zodiac sign for which the sub-period is being calculated. The resulting figures in years, months, and days represent the sub-period.

**Example—** Suppose someone is born in the fourth quarter of the *Mula* constellation. In that case, the birth falls within the Cancer sequence of the direct cycle <note>original: "Savya-chakra"</note>, where the total lifespan <note>original: "purnayu-mana"</note> is 86 years. If, within that sequence, one needs to find the sub-period of Saturn in Capricorn during the major period of Jupiter in Sagittarius: The years for Jupiter in Sagittarius (10) are multiplied by the years for Saturn in Capricorn (4), resulting in 40. This is divided by the total lifespan of 86. This yields the years, months, days, and sub-divisions <note>term: Ghatika; a unit of time equal to 24 minutes</note> of the Saturn sub-period within Jupiter’s major period as 0 years, 5 months, 17 days, and 26 ghatikas. This method should be understood for all cases.

The mathematical logic <note>term: Upapatti</note> is this: In the total lifespan, which is the sum of all planetary periods, the specific period for each planet is stated. Now, within the period of a single planet (treated as a relative "total lifespan"), the sub-period of each is to be calculated. For this, the following proportion is used: If the sub-period planet's years are obtained out of the total lifespan of all planets, then what would be obtained out of the specific major period planet’s years? (<insert>Major Period $\times$ Sub-period Years</insert> / Total Lifespan = Sub-period). Thus, the sub-period of the desired planet within the current major period is established. || 107 ||

**Multiply the major period years by the sub-period years and divide by the total lifespan (Purnayu); the result is the sub-period in years, months, and days. || 107 ||**

> Multiply the years of the cycle-lord by the years of the sub-period sign-lord, and divide by the lifespan assigned to that sign.
> The results are years, months, days, and minutes; lords of "bad houses" <note>term: Dusthana; the 6th, 8th, or 12th houses associated with difficulty</note> will bring grief and disease. || 108 ||
> Similarly, multiply the days of the major period by the major years to find the sub-periods within a period.
> Again, when that is divided by the maximum lifespan years, the result is the sub-period within the sub-period. || 109 ||
> Having converted the constellation's time into small units <note>original: "vinadi"</note>, multiply by their respective years.
> Divide by the total lifespan to find the precise micro-period result. || 110 ||
> The years and days of the planets, multiplied by the fixed constants of the maximum lifespan, 
> And multiplied by their own years, give their own maturation; this should be considered in all planetary maturations. || 111 ||

->Thus ends the seventeenth chapter of the Jataka Parijata, composed by Vaidyanatha by the grace of the nine planets.<-

These verses (108-111) carry the same meaning as verse 107.

The *Sudha* commentary on the *Parijata*, authored by Kapileshwara, is now complete for this chapter titled the Wheel of Time Periods. 17.
**Multiply the year of the cycle-lord by the year of the sub-period sign-lord and divide by the full lifespan of that second sign to clarify the years, months, days, and minutes. The lord of an evil house causes pain and illness.**
**In this way, multiply the major period years of one by the major period years of the other and divide by the maximum lifespan (120) to get the sub-period within the major period. || 109 ||**
**Convert the minutes/seconds of the constellation into smaller units, multiply by the full lifespan of that constellation, and divide by the total lifespan value; the result will be the precise micro-period in years. || 110 ||**
**To find the sub-period of a desired planet within a planet's period, divide the period years by the total lifespan and multiply by the desired planet's years; thus, the sub-periods for each are found.**

->Thus ends the 'Vimala' Hindi commentary on the seventeenth chapter, titled the Wheel of Time Periods, in the Jataka Parijata. || 17 ||<-

# Chapter 18: The Results of the Planetary Periods

> The great sages say that all the auspicious and inauspicious results of a birth are determined by the planetary periods <note>term: Dasha; a system of time-blocks in a person's life ruled by specific planets</note>. Having extracted the essence of these teachings, I shall now explain the various distinctions within these periods in detail. || 1 ||
>
> Just as planetary combinations <note>term: Yoga; specific alignments of planets that produce particular life results</note> manifest according to the strength of the planets, the periods themselves manifest according to those combinations. All results experienced by humans are derived from the results of these periods, much like the social classification of people into different orders <note>original: "varna"; referring to the traditional social structure of ancient India</note>. || 2 ||

Now, the chapter on the results of the planetary periods is explained. It is stated that all the good and bad results for a person born under the stars manifest specifically during the major and minor periods <note>term: Dashas and Antardashas</note> of the planets. Therefore, the consideration of these periods is essential. Since the total experience of individuals is produced by the results of these planetary periods, they are described here. The two verses above are clear in their meaning.

Because the sages state that the auspicious or inauspicious results of a birth chart are favorable to the period, I am collecting the essential portions regarding the types of periods and stating them here in this 18th chapter. || 1 ||

Just as "Yogas" occur according to the strength of the planets, the period is obtained according to those Yogas. All results for humans come from the results of the periods. Just as the status of a priest or other class is determined by their social order <note>original: "vipradi"; referring to Brahmins and other groups</note>, so are life results determined by these periods. || 2 ||

## The Vimshottari Major Period

> The Sun, Moon, Mars, Rahu, Jupiter, Saturn, Mercury, Ketu, and Venus are the nine lords of the constellations starting from Krittika. Their period years—expressed by the code-words *Teno, Naya, Sina, Daya, Tata, Dhanya, Sevya, Sena,* and *Nara*—follow the sequence of the Sun and the others. || 3 ||

Now the years of the major periods for the Sun and other planets in the Vimshottari <note>note: "Vimshottari" literally means "one hundred and twenty," referring to the 120-year cycle of this system</note> system are stated. Starting from the constellation *Krittika*, the period lords are the Sun, Moon, Mars, Rahu, Jupiter <note>original: "Sureshamantri"; literally 'the advisor to the gods'</note>, Saturn, Mercury, Ketu, and Venus. In the first set of nine constellations starting from Krittika, these nine planets are the lords. This sequence repeats three times throughout the circle of constellations <note>note: there are 27 constellations in total, so each planet rules three of them</note>.

Specifically:
- The Sun rules *Krittika, Uttara Phalguni,* and *Uttara Ashadha*.
- The Moon rules *Rohini, Hasta,* and *Shravana*.
- Mars rules *Mrigashira, Chitra,* and *Dhanishta*.
- Rahu rules *Ardra, Svati,* and *Shatabhisha*.
- Jupiter rules *Punarvasu, Vishakha,* and *Purva Bhadrapada*.
- Saturn rules *Pushya, Anuradha,* and *Uttara Bhadrapada*.
- Mercury rules *Ashlesha, Jyeshtha,* and *Revati*.
- Ketu rules *Magha, Mula,* and *Ashvini*.
- Venus rules *Purva Phalguni, Purva Ashadha,* and *Bharani*.

The years for these periods are given using the *Katapayadi* system <note>term: Katapayadi; a Sanskrit alphanumeric code where specific letters represent numbers</note>.
- For the Sun, *Teno* = 6 years.
- For the Moon, *Naya* = 10 years.
- For Mars, *Sina* = 7 years.
- For Rahu, *Daya* = 18 years.
- For Jupiter, *Tata* = 16 years.
- For Saturn, *Dhanya* = 19 years.
- For Mercury, *Sevya* = 17 years.
- For Ketu, *Sena* = 7 years.
- For Venus, *Nara* = 20 years.

The total sum of all these is 6 + 10 + 7 + 18 + 16 + 19 + 17 + 7 + 20 = 120. This is why it is called the "Vimshottari" (One-Hundred and Twenty) system. || 3 ||

### Table for Understanding the Vimshottari Periods of Planets

| Period Lords | Sun | Moon | Mars | Rahu | Jupiter | Saturn | Mercury | Ketu | Venus |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Constellations** | Krittika, U. Phalguni, U. Ashadha | Rohini, Hasta, Shravana | Mrigashira, Chitra, Dhanishta | Ardra, Svati, Shatabhisha | Punarvasu, Vishakha, P. Bhadrapada | Pushya, Anuradha, U. Bhadrapada | Ashlesha, Jyeshtha, Revati | Magha, Mula, Ashvini | P. Phalguni, P. Ashadha, Bharani |
| **Period Years** | 6 | 10 | 7 | 18 | 16 | 19 | 17 | 7 | 20 |

# Now, the Auspiciousness and Inauspiciousness of the Lord of the Period

> **Planets that possess increasing strength, have a high number of points in the system of eight-fold divisions <note>term: Ashtakavarga; a system where planets gain points (bindus) based on their positions relative to others</note>, and are situated in the tenth, eleventh, or first houses—as well as those in their signs of exaltation and possessing the six-fold strength <note>term: Shadbala; a mathematical calculation of a planet's six types of strength</note>—will provide auspicious results during their periods. || 4 ||**

> **Those planets that are the lords of the sign where Mandi <note>term: Mandi; also called Gulika, a sensitive point in the chart associated with malefic or "poisonous" influences</note> is located, or are placed in the same house as Mandi, or have few points in the eight-fold divisions, or are in enemy signs, or are in their signs of weakness <note>original: "neecha"; debilitation</note>, or are combust <note>term: combustion; being so close to the Sun that the planet's influence is weakened</note>, or are joined by malefic planets, or are situated at the junctions <note>original: "sandhi"; the sensitive border between two signs or houses</note>—these will provide undesirable results. || 5 ||**

> **If the Lord of the Period <note>term: Dashapati</note> is located in the Ascendant <note>original: "Lagna"; the rising sign</note>, or is in the third, sixth, tenth, or eleventh house from the Ascendant; or if its divisional strength <note>term: Saptavarga; the seven types of divisional charts</note> or its friend is in the Ascendant, or if a benefic planet is in the Ascendant, then that period will be auspicious. || 6 ||**

> **If the Moon is in the house of a friend to the Lord of the Period, or in its exaltation sign, or is in the seventh, the trines <note>the 5th or 9th houses</note>, or the houses of growth <note>original: "upachaya"; the 3rd, 6th, 10th, and 11th houses</note> relative to the Lord of the Period, then the Moon certainly grants excellent results. || 7 ||**

> **The house—such as the first (body), second (wealth), and so on—in which the Moon is situated at the time of birth, when placed in the signs mentioned above, becomes prosperous. It is said that the Moon causes growth for those specific houses for men; however, if the Moon is placed in other signs, it causes the loss of the results of those houses. || 8 ||**

> **The results that the ancient sages <note>note: This refers to masters like Varahamihira</note> have described for the Moon when it is in its own home or other favorable positions at the time of birth should be applied at the start of a period. Indeed, the Moon grants results called "auspicious" or "inauspicious" by taking the form of the mind <note>note: This suggests that the Moon’s primary influence is on a person’s psychological state and perception of happiness</note>. || 9 ||**

> **Whatever auspicious or painful results were previously determined for a planet based on its strength and condition must be applied accordingly to the periods of living beings, whether they be good or bad. || 10 ||**

> **When auspiciousness is intense, men experience good results; when inauspiciousness is intense, they experience bad results. When they are equal, the results are certainly mixed. This principle should be applied everywhere. || 11 ||**

Now, the auspiciousness and inauspiciousness of the planets that rule the periods is explained through the verses starting with "Planets that possess...". Those "celestial travelers" (planets) which have increasing strength, are equal to the house, have many points (meaning high auspicious marks in the Eight-fold Division/Ashtakavarga), and are in the "houses of action, gains, and rising" (meaning the 10th, 11th, and 1st houses), or are in exaltation divisions and possess the "six-fold strength" (Shadbala), provide good results during their periods. 

On the other hand, those planets that are the lords of the sign occupied by Mandi, or are located in the house where Mandi resides, or have few points in the Eight-fold Division, or are in an enemy’s sign, or are debilitated, or are "extinguished" (combust/hidden by the Sun), or are joined with malefic planets, or are at the junction of houses or the junction of signs—these planets provide undesirable results.

Furthermore, the Lord of the Period—the planet whose period results are being considered—if it is in the Ascendant at that time, or is in the 3rd, 6th, 10th, or 11th from the Ascendant, or if its divisional strength (Saptavarga), or its friend, or a benefic planet is in the Ascendant, then that period will be a giver of good results.

Regarding the Moon: if it is in a friend’s sign relative to the current Lord of the Period, or in its exaltation sign relative to the Lord, or is in the 7th, the trines (5th or 9th), or the growth houses (3rd, 6th, 10th, or 11th) from the Lord of the Period, it gives "excellent results" (auspicious outcomes).

In the aforementioned signs, the house occupied by the Moon—be it the house of the body (1st), wealth (2nd), and so on from the time of birth—becomes "with its house" (meaning it becomes fruitful). This means that the Moon, when in the described signs, causes the growth of that particular house. If that Moon is in "other signs" (signs other than those mentioned), it is said to cause the loss of that house for men. This means that for whatever house the Moon is in, the loss of that house's benefits should be predicted.

Regarding the Moon <note>original: "Himadyutau"; literally 'the cool-rayed one'</note> at the time of birth, when it is in its own home, exaltation, or its primary triangle <note>term: Moolatrikona; a specific favorable placement for a planet</note>, the results described by the sages such as Varahamihira and others—the results known as good or bad—should be spoken of at the start of its period...

# The Effects of Planetary Periods

...certainly, the Moon gives results in the form of one's mental state and fullness of being. Here, the mention of the Moon serves as a general illustration; this rule should be known to apply to all planets.

The two verses regarding what has been produced and the intensity of desired results are clear in their meaning. || 4-11 ||

Planets that possess high <term>Aroha-virya</term> <note>original: "aroha-vīrya"; the strength a planet gains as it moves toward its exaltation point</note>, are <term>Bhava-sadrisha</term> <note>original: "bhāva-sadṛśa"; compatible with the nature of the house they occupy</note>, have a high number of points (bindus) in the <term>Ashtakavarga</term> <note>a system of eight-fold points used to calculate planetary strength</note>, are situated in the 10th, 11th, or 1st houses, have reached their exaltation or favorable divisions, and possess <term>Shadbala</term> <note>the six-fold mathematical strength of a planet</note>—these provide auspicious results during their period. || 4 ||

The lord of the sign occupied by <term>Gulika</term> <note>a malefic mathematical point in the chart, also known as Mandi</note>, those associated with Gulika, planets with few points in the eight-fold divisions, or those situated in enemy signs, signs of weakness, or those that are combust—as well as planets joined by malefic influences, those placed at a <term>Bhava Sandhi</term> <note>the junction or "joint" between two astrological houses</note> or a <term>Riksha Sandhi</term> <note>the junction between two zodiac signs, particularly the transition from water to fire signs</note> in the <term>Navamsha</term> <note>the ninth divisional chart used to see the hidden strength of a planet</note>—these provide undesirable results in their period. || 5 ||

If <term>Brihaspati</term> <note>the planet Jupiter</note> is in the Ascendant, and if the <term>Ashtakavarga</term> of the <term>Dashapati</term> <note>the Lord of the Period</note> or its friend is in the 3rd, 6th, 10th, or 11th house from the Ascendant, or if a benefic planet is in the Ascendant, the period is auspicious. || 6 ||

If the Moon is in a friend’s sign or the exaltation sign of the <term>Dashadhisha</term> <note>the Lord of the Period</note>, or is in the 7th, a <term>Trikona</term> <note>the 5th or 9th auspicious houses</note>, or an <term>Upachaya</term> <note>the 3rd, 6th, 10th, or 11th houses of "growth"</note> position from the Lord of the Period, it will certainly grant auspicious results during that period. || 7 ||

The specific house (such as the 1st house of self or 2nd house of wealth) that the Moon occupies within these auspicious signs will see growth during that period. However, if the Moon is in other, less favorable signs, that house will suffer loss. || 8 ||

The excellent results described by the learned when the Moon is in its own home or similar favorable positions are certainly granted by the Moon at the start of the period through the person's mental state and disposition. || 9 ||

The auspicious and inauspicious results of the planets that were described previously will manifest as the good or bad fortunes of men during their respective periods. || 10 ||

When auspicious results are in excess, men experience good fortune; when inauspicious results are in excess, they experience hardship. When balanced, the results are certainly mixed. This calculation should be applied everywhere. || 11 ||

->Whatever substance was mentioned for a planet in the Chapter on Definitions, and whatever livelihood was taught for it;<-
->Whatever results arise from its house position, location, aspect, and conjunction—all of that should be applied to its planetary period. || 12 ||<-

Now, the author describes the manifestation of these various results during the periods of the planets that cause those combinations: *In the Chapter on Definitions...* In the <term>Samjna Adhyaya</term> <note>Chapter on Definitions</note>, whatever substance was assigned to a planet (such as "copper" or "gems"), and whatever livelihood or occupation was taught for that planet—along with the results of its house, its placement, its <term>Aloka</term> <note>aspect or "gaze" of a planet</note>, and its conjunctions—all of that must be applied to the period of that specific planet. During an auspicious period, one acquires those substances; during an inauspicious period, those substances are lost. This is according to the <term>Brihat Jataka</term> <note>a foundational 6th-century astrological text by Varahamihira</note>. || 12 ||

In the <term>Samjna Adhyaya</term>, whatever substance is mentioned; in the <term>Karmajivadhayaya</term> <note>Chapter on Livelihoods</note>, whatever advice is given; and whatever <term>Bhava-phala</term> (house results), <term>Yoga-phala</term> (conjunction results), and <term>Drishti-phala</term> (aspect results) are stated—all these should be factored into its period. || 12 ||

->In a period that gives auspicious results, the inner self similarly produces great happiness and the arrival of wealth for men.<-
->By the ripening of the stated results, one should infer the current state; the prediction of results also transforms into dreams and thoughts when strength is lacking. || 13 ||<-

Now, the author explains the method of understanding the period through the manifestation of one's own internal state: *In a period that gives auspicious results...* In a period that grants good fruits, the <term>Antaratma</term> <note>the "Inner Self" or soul-consciousness</note> of humans becomes similarly auspicious (meaning cheerful and pleasant). At that time, it generates various kinds of happiness and the arrival of wealth for men. In an auspicious period, the hearts of men appear very serene, and they experience diverse comforts and financial gains. By observing such symptoms, one should infer that a period is auspicious. From this, it follows that in an inauspicious period, the inner self of men becomes averse and troubled, leading to various sorrows and the loss of wealth. In a mixed period, the results are mixed. Therefore, by observing the ripening of the stated results, one can judge the current...

# Chapter 18: On the Effects of Planetary Periods

<page-num>525</page-num>

One should not merely guess whether a planetary period <note>original: "daśā"</note> will be auspicious or inauspicious. When a planet’s period is said to produce a certain type of good or bad result, one should observe the person’s current circumstances; if those results are appearing, that period should be understood to belong to that specific planet. Now, it is explained that the results of planets lacking strength do not fully manifest. The predicted effects of weak planets <note>original: "avīryaiḥ"</note> result only in dreams or mental desires. This means that the good or bad fruits promised by weak planets are only experienced during sleep—in the form of dreams—or as a longing in the mind. For example, if a weak planet is destined to give the result of "ascending a throne," the astrologer should predict that this result will occur in a dream. In such a case, the person might experience a dream where they think, "I am sitting on a throne," or they might simply daydream about it without it ever becoming a reality. || 13 || <note>The author quotes the *Brihat Jataka*, a foundational 6th-century astrological text by Varahamihira, to support this idea.</note>

->During an auspicious planetary period, the person’s inner spirit remains positive, and they acquire various forms of happiness and wealth. The current period should be identified by observing these manifested results. If the planets are weak, the predicted results should be expected only in the dream state.<-

---

->**If the Lord of the Period is in the Ascendant, or in a friend’s sign, or in a benefic division,**<-
->**the period begins auspiciously; the same applies if the Lord is in the 3rd, 6th, 10th, or 11th houses.**<-
->**When the Moon is situated in the period lord's friend's sign, exaltation sign, an "upachaya" house,**<-
->**a trine, or the seventh house, it signals the arrival of good results; otherwise, the results are harmful. || 14 ||**<-

This verse describes the auspiciousness or inauspiciousness of a period. The "Lord of the Period" <note>original: "pākasvāmī" or "pākeśa"</note> refers to the planet currently ruling the person's life-cycle. If, at the moment the period begins, the Period Lord is located in the <term>Ascendant</term> <note>original: "lagna"; the sign rising on the eastern horizon</note>, or in a sign belonging to its friend, the period will be beneficial. Alternatively, the period is favorable if the Lord is in its own <term>Varga</term> <note>original: "varga"; divisional charts like the Shadvarga (6-fold), Saptavarga (7-fold), or Dashavarga (10-fold) which provide nuanced views of a planet's strength</note>, or if a benefic planet occupies the Ascendant. Furthermore, if the Period Lord is in the 3rd, 6th, 10th, or 11th houses <note>known as the Upachaya or "houses of growth"</note> from the Ascendant, it brings good fortune. Additionally, the Moon’s position at the start of the period is vital: if the Moon is in the Period Lord’s friend’s sign, its exaltation sign <note>original: "ucca"</note>, the growth houses (3, 6, 10, 11), the <term>Trines</term> <note>original: "trikoṇa"; the 5th or 9th houses</note>, or the 7th house <note>original: "madana"</note>, the Moon indicates the production of excellent results. If the Moon is placed otherwise, it produces "sins" or inauspicious effects. Note that verses 6 and 7 of this text follow a similar logic. || 14 ||

->If the Period Lord is in the Ascendant, a friend's house, or a benefic division, the beginning period gives good results. If the Period Lord is in the 10th, 6th, or 11th house, and the Moon is in the Lord's friend's sign, exaltation, trine, or 7th house, it makes the good results known. If otherwise, it causes harm.<-

---

->**If the Period Lord is in a favorable house from the Ascendant, in its own sign, its exaltation, or a friend's sign,**<-
->**and is aspected by or joined with benefic or friendly planets, then its sub-period is auspicious.**<-
->**If it is in a center or a trine, it is extremely beneficial. Malefics in the 3rd, 6th, or 11th houses**<-
->**who are strong and in exaltation or growth houses—their periods bring prosperity. || 15 ||**<-

Regarding the Ascendant: the Period Lord <note>original: "pākeśaḥ"</note>, if situated in a desired house from the Ascendant at the start of the period—such as its own sign, its exaltation sign, or a friend’s sign—and is "seen" (aspected) by or joined with a benefic or friend, then during that planet's <term>Bhukti</term> <note>original: "bhukti"; a sub-period within the major planetary cycle</note>, the person will experience auspicious results related to that specific house. Furthermore, if the Period Lord is in a <term>Kendra</term> <note>original: "kendra"; the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, considered the pillars of the chart</note> or a Trine, it becomes exceptionally fortunate. Additionally, if "malefic" planets <note>original: "pāpāḥ"; such as the Sun, Mars, and Saturn</note> were placed in the 3rd, 6th, or 11th houses at birth, and if these planets are strong and positioned in their exaltation or "upachaya" (growth) signs, their periods will bring auspicious results to those born under them. Conversely, it follows that malefics in other houses, or planets that are weak...

# With Commentary on the Jataka Parijata

...one should consider that if planets are devoid of strength in terms of their position and other factors, their period <note>original: "daśā"</note> will yield inauspicious results. Thus, it is stated in the *Phaladeepika* <note>A famous 13th-century astrological treatise by Mantreswara</note>:

->Whichever house the Lord of the Period occupies during its transit from the Ascendant—provided it is in its sign of exaltation or a friend’s sign—<-
->it causes the prosperity of that house at that time, especially if it was also powerful in the native's birth chart. || 15 ||<-

If the <term>Dasha-pati</term> <gloss>Lord of the Period</gloss>, being a benefic planet, is situated in a favorable house—such as its own house, its sign of exaltation, or a friend's house—relative to the Ascendant, and is aspected by or joined with friendly planets, then the <term>Bhukti</term> <gloss>sub-period</gloss> of that planet will be auspicious. If it is placed in an angle <note>houses 1, 4, 7, or 10</note> or a trine <note>houses 1, 5, or 9</note>, it will be extremely auspicious. If malefic planets are placed in the third, sixth, or eleventh houses and are strong or in their "Upachaya" <note>houses of improvement</note> or exaltation signs, their periods also become auspicious. || 15 ||

->When two mutually friendly planets, both endowed with "Six-fold Strength," have their periods and sub-periods intersect, the result is auspicious.<-
->However, if the two planets are mutual enemies and are weak, their major period and sub-period will bring misfortune. || 16 ||<-

The commentary explains: "Mutually" refers to the relationship between the two. When the <term>Shadbala</term> <gloss>Six-fold Strength; a complex calculation of a planet's power</gloss> is high for both planets, and they are mutual friends, then both the major period and the <term>Antardasha</term> <gloss>sub-period</gloss> will yield good results. This means that whichever planet's sub-period occurs during a major period, if those two lords are friendly toward each other and both possess their respective six-fold strengths, then that time should be declared auspicious. On the other hand, if they are mutual enemies and lack strength, then during their <note>original: "pākāpahāre"</note> period and sub-period, "unfortunate" or inauspicious results will occur. || 16 ||

Planets in a state of mutual friendship give auspicious results during their sub-periods. If both planets are mutual enemies, disaster occurs during their periods. || 16 ||

->A planet produces auspicious or inauspicious results according to the house it occupies during its own maturation.<-
->The wise say that during the period of a benefic planet, results are good; during the period of a malefic, they are bad. || 17 ||<-
->The period of a planet joined by a benefic is extremely auspicious, while one joined by a malefic becomes fruitless during its time of maturation.<-
->When a planet is joined by mixed planets and possesses mixed strength, its period and sub-period yield mixed results. || 18 ||<-

The commentary states: The <term>Pakapati</term> <gloss>Lord of the sub-period</gloss> (also called the <term>Antardashesh</term>) produces auspicious or inauspicious results based on its house position relative to the Lord of the Major Period. The rules for these results are as follows: During the sub-period of a benefic planet, the results are good; during the "Daya" <gloss>period</gloss> of a malefic, the results are bad—so say the sages. Furthermore, within a benefic major period, a benefic sub-period makes the results even better; within a malefic major period, a malefic sub-period makes them even worse; and with mixed influences, the results are mixed. As it says in the *Phaladeepika*:

->The Lord of the sub-period will produce results belonging to the house it occupies relative to the Lord of the Major Period.<-
->If it occupies the enemy, twelfth, or eighth house from the major lord, it causes suffering; otherwise, it brings happiness.<-
->The verse beginning with "Joined by a benefic" is self-explanatory and requires no further elaboration. || 17-18 ||<-

A planet produces the good or bad results of the specific house it inhabits during its period. It is said that the period of a benefic planet is good, while that of a malefic planet is bad. || 17 ||

The period of a planet associated with a benefic gives auspicious results. The period of a planet associated with a malefic gives inauspicious results during its <term>Paripaka</term> <gloss>time of fruition or maturation</gloss>. When a planet has mixed strength or is joined by both types of planets, the results are mixed. || 18 ||

->During the period and sub-period of a planet ruling a specific element, the wise say one experiences wealth or distress related to that element.<-
->A malefic planet causes the depletion of that element, while a benefic causes that element to flourish. || 19 ||<-

This refers to the <term>Dhatus</term> <gloss>bodily tissues or constituent elements</gloss> such as <term>marrow, nerves, and fat</term> <note>original: "majjā-snāyu-vasetyādyuktasya"</note> which are ruled by the various <term>Khetas</term> <gloss>planets</gloss>. During the period or sub-period of such a planet, the wise <note>original: "maryah"</note> say the person experiences the maturation of that specific physical element. If it is the sub-period of a malefic planet, that specific tissue or element is depleted; if it is the period of a benefic, that element thrives. || 19 ||

<summary>This page outlines how the interaction between major and sub-period planetary lords determines a person's fortune, emphasizing that mutual friendship and physical strength (Shadbala) lead to prosperity. It also links specific planets to the health and growth of bodily tissues (dhatus) during their respective periods.</summary>

# Chapter 18: The Fruits of Planetary Periods

Page 527

The wise have stated that during the period of a planet associated with a specific metal, the individual will acquire that very metal and associated wealth. During the period of a malefic planet, there is a loss of that metal. During the period of a benefic planet, there is an increase in that metal. || 19 ||

->In the sub-period of a planet that has entered an enemy's sign, one should predict an increase in enemies and the loss of all wealth. During the period of a planet that is the "doer" of a certain action, the wise declare the successful accomplishment of that very action. || 20 ||<-
->During the period of a planet that performs a specific task, one should predict the fulfillment of that task for men. If that planet is a benefic, there is success; if it is a malefic, then there is only the destruction of that task. || 21 ||<-

Regarding the verse beginning with "In the sub-period": during the ripening <note>original: "pāka", meaning the planetary period or sub-period</note> of a planet situated in an enemy’s house, an increase in enemies and the loss of all wealth must be predicted. During the ripening of a planet that acts as the significator <note>original: "kāraka"</note> of a specific deed, the learned scholars declare the successful accomplishment of that auspicious or inauspicious deed. || 20 ||

The meaning of verse 21, beginning with "In the period of a planet that performs a specific task," is self-evident and requires no further explanation. || 21 ||

->The period of the lord of the house of sovereignty <note>the 10th house</note> or of the significator of sovereignty bestows royal favor. During the period of a celestial planet representing a deity, one should worship that deity. Upon the arrival of the period of the lord of the house of righteousness <note>the 9th house</note>, one should declare success in penance and religious deeds. During the sub-period <note>original: "apahāra"</note> of the lord of action <note>the 10th house</note>, one should speak of festivals involving sacrifices and rituals. || 22 ||<-

Regarding sovereignty: the period of the Lord of the Tenth House or of the planet that signifies sovereignty <note>the Sun or Jupiter, depending on context</note> bestows royal favor. If the native is a prince, they obtain the kingdom during that period. An ordinary person receives the favor of the king <gloss>the king's pleasure</gloss>. During the period and sub-period of a "celestial planet" <gloss>situated in the 5th house</gloss> representing a particular deity, the worship of that specific deity should be advised. Upon the arrival of the period of the Lord of the Ninth House, one should predict the success of penance and similar religious deeds. During the sub-period <note>original: "daśāpahar-samaye"</note> of the Lord of the Tenth House, the celebration of rituals like sacrifices <note>original: "yajña"</note> should be mentioned. The intent is that if the prescribed deeds are performed during the periods of these respective planets, they will reach fruition. || 22 ||

->During the major and minor periods of planets possessing the qualities of <term>Sattva</term> and others, the respective quality arises in the person. The period of a planet situated in the first nine stars <note>Nakshatras</note> starting from the birth star brings about results that are already past. The period of a strong planet situated in the nine stars starting from the "action star" <note>the 10th star from birth</note> brings about future results. Any results from planets in the "conception" group <note>the 19th star onwards</note> should be declared as fruitless or yielding results only much later. || 23 ||<-

Regarding the <term>Gunas</term> <note>the three qualities of nature: Sattva (purity), Rajas (passion), and Tamas (inertia)</note>: During the major and minor periods of planets characterized by the qualities of Sattva, etc. <gloss>see Chapter 2, Verse 26 for the classification of planets by quality</gloss>, the corresponding quality arises in the person <gloss>in the period of a Sattvic planet, a person becomes Sattvic; in a Rajasic period, Rajasic; and in a Tamasic period, Tamasic</gloss>. "The period of a planet in the nine stars starting from the birth star": the star in which one is born is the "Birth Star" <note>original: "janma-nakṣatra"</note>; the period of a planet situated within the nine stars from that point brings about "past results." This means: if a planet at the time of birth is within the first nine stars from the birth star, its period is said to give results that have already passed—meaning the results will not be experienced in the present. "The period of a planet in the nine stars from the action star": counting from the star—

### Results based on Constellation Groups

The tenth constellation from the birth star is called the "Action" constellation <note>original: "Karma-nama"; in Vedic astrology, the 10th Nakshatra from the Moon's position at birth marks the beginning of the second group of nine stars</note>. One should predict the future results <note>original: "bhaviṣyat-phalam"</note> during the period <note>original: "Dashā"</note> of a strong planet situated in the nine constellations beginning with this "Action" star. 

Now, regarding the "Conception" planet <note>original: "Ādhāna-graha"</note>: the nineteenth constellation from the birth star is designated as the "Conception" <note>original: "Ādhāna"</note> star. If a planet is positioned in the nine constellations beginning with that "Conception" star, one should declare all the fruits of its period to be fruitless or a failure <note>original: "aphalam"</note>. This means that only the results of planets situated within the "Action" and "Conception" sequences are truly manifest. || 23 ||

The period of a planet possessing the qualities of Purity, Passion, or Ignorance <note>original: "Sattva, Rajas, Tamas"</note> will produce those very qualities in the individual. The period of a planet situated in the first nine constellations from the birth star manifests results from the past. The period of a strong planet in the nine "Action" constellations manifests results for the future. For planets situated in the nine constellations beginning with "Conception," all results are said to be without fruit. || 23 ||

->A planet situated in a head-rising sign gives its results at the beginning of its period.<-
->A planet in a hind-rising sign gives results at the end, and one in a "both-ways" rising sign gives results throughout. || 24 ||<-

Regarding the verse beginning with "situated in a head-rising sign": the meaning is clear. || 24 ||
<note>In astrology, signs are classified by how they rise on the horizon. "Head-rising" (Shirshodaya) signs include Gemini, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, and Aquarius. "Hind-rising" (Prishthodaya) signs include Aries, Taurus, Cancer, Sagittarius, and Capricorn. Pisces is "Both-ways rising" (Ubhayodaya).</note>

### Results of the House Lords

->The period of the lord of the sixth house causes lamentation. The period of the lord of the house of destruction—the eighth house—causes death.<-
->During the period or sub-period of a planet that is "set" <note>combust, or hidden by the sun's light</note> or situated in the setting house <note>the 7th house</note>, one should predict the death of kinsmen.<-
->During the sub-periods of the lords of Prosperity, Success, and Friendship stars, as well as the Great Friendship and Security stars, one should predict an increase in wealth and prosperity. || 25 ||<-

Regarding the verse beginning "The lord of the sixth": The period of the lord of the sixth house from the birth ascendant <note>the house of enemies, debt, and disease</note> causes lamentation and brings sorrow. During the period of the lord of the eighth house <note>the house of death and transformation</note>, death occurs. During the period or sub-period <note>original: "Pāka" or "Apahāra"</note> of a planet that has "set" <note>original: "Asta-vyomacara"; planet rendered invisible by proximity to the Sun</note> or has entered the seventh house <note>the "setting" house</note>, or the lord of the seventh house itself, the death of relatives should be predicted. 

In this context, the increase or decrease of these results must be weighed against whether the house lord is naturally a benefic <note>gentle</note> or malefic <note>harsh</note> planet. 

Furthermore, regarding the lords of the Prosperity <note>the 2nd, 11th, and 20th stars from birth</note>, Success <note>the 6th, 15th, and 24th stars</note>, and Friendship <note>the 8th, 17th, and 26th stars</note> constellations, as well as the Great Friendship <note>9th, 18th, and 27th stars</note> and Security <note>4th, 13th, and 22nd stars</note> stars: during the sub-periods <note>original: "Antardashā"</note> of these planets, one should predict an increase in wealth and assets for the person. 

As stated in the *Phaladeepika* <note>a classic 16th-century astrological text by Mantreshwara</note>:

> During the period of the sixth lord, men suffer from fear of thieves, oppression by enemies, many diseases, the results of bad deeds, servitude, insults, and infamy. 
> When the lord of the seventh house is weak, one finds delight in falsehoods and experiences the suffering of a son-in-law, separation from a spouse, calamities caused by women, genital diseases, and aimless wandering. 
> During the life-period of the lord of the eighth house, one should predict grief, delusion, pride, envy, the height of fainting or mental instability, poverty, grueling toil, infamy, and unbearable diseases leading to death. || 25 ||

The period of the sixth lord causes weeping. The period of the eighth lord causes death. The period or sub-period of a "set" planet causes the death of kinsmen. During the sub-periods of the lords of Prosperity (2), Success (6), Friendship (8), Great Friendship (9), and Security (4), predict the flourishing of wealth. || 25 ||

->If a weak malefic planet sits in one of the three circles,<-
->one should know that death occurs in its period; if it is with a benefic, the result is auspicious. || 26 ||<-

### During the period of a planet situated at the junction of two signs, there is suffering from grief, disease, and the like. A planetary period that has reached the thirtieth degree of a sign yields the result of death. || 27 ||

These two verses should be seen in the fifth chapter, verses 45 and 46. || 26-27 ||
If even a single weak malefic planet <term>pāpa-graha; naturally inauspicious planets like Mars or Saturn</term> is in the thirtieth degree, one should anticipate death during its period. If it is associated with a benefic planet <term>śubha-graha; naturally auspicious planets like Jupiter or Venus</term>, the result may be favorable. || 26 ||
During the period of a planet situated in the junction of signs <note>original: "rāśi-sandhi"; the sensitive border where one zodiac sign ends and the next begins</note>, there is the pain of grief and disease. The period of a planet that has reached the 30th degree <note>original: "triṃśādbhhāga"</note> of any sign gives the result of death. || 27 ||

### A planet that is debilitated at birth, or a planet joined with it, is not capable of giving auspicious results. A planet joined with Rahu, or situated in Rahu’s sign, or the lord of the sign where Rahu is placed, brings misfortune during its period. || 28 ||

Regarding "situated in debilitation" <note>original: "nīcasthita"</note>: In the birth chart <gloss>= at the time of birth</gloss>, whichever planet is in its sign of debilitation <gloss>= having reached its lowest point of strength</gloss>, that debilitated planet and the planet joined with it <gloss>= the planet in the same sign as the debilitated one</gloss> are not capable <gloss>= not powerful</gloss> of giving good results. The intention is that such a planet produces a lack of auspiciousness. A planet joined with Rahu <note>the North Node of the Moon</note>, or one situated in its field <gloss>= in a sign ruled by Rahu, though traditionally Rahu rules no sign, some systems assign it Aquarius or Virgo</gloss>, or the lord of the sign joined with Rahu <gloss>= the ruler of the sign where Rahu resides</gloss>, creates misfortune <gloss>= inauspicious</gloss> results during its period. || 28 ||

At the time of birth, a planet situated in its sign of debilitation and any planet joined with it does not give auspicious fruits. A planet joined with Rahu, as well as the lord of Rahu's sign and a planet placed in its house, gives undesirable results. || 28 ||

### One should declare the destruction of the first house and others during the period of a planet that is the Great Enemy of the lord of that house, or a planet situated in a sign with zero points in the Ashtakavarga. Thus have the Great Sages spoken. || 29 ||

Regarding "that specific house" <note>original: "tat-tat-bhāva"</note>: Whichever planet is the Great Enemy <note>original: "adhi-śatru"; a planet that is an enemy both naturally and based on its current position</note> of the lord of a particular house being considered, or if that planet is in a sign possessing zero points in the <term>Ashtakavarga; a system of points used to measure planetary strength</term>, then during the period of that planet, one should declare the destruction of the first house <gloss>= the physical body</gloss> and subsequent houses. Thus have the ancient Great Sages spoken. During the period of the Great Enemy of the lord of the 1st house, there is destruction of the body; during the period of the Great Enemy of the lord of the 2nd house, there is loss of wealth. This should be considered for all houses. || 29 ||

The Great Sages have said that during the period of a planet that is the Great Enemy of the lord of a specific house and is situated in a sign with zero points, the destruction of that house (starting from the 1st house/ascendant) occurs. || 29 ||

### The period of a planet joined with the lord of the Obstruction House brings grief and disease. During the sub-period of a planet situated in a square from that lord, there is distress and wandering in foreign lands. If the lords of the major and sub-periods are in a mutual sixth-eighth relationship, one should predict fear, exile from one's country, and calamity; but if they are auspicious benefics, the results are mixed. || 30 ||

Regarding the "lord of the obstruction house" <note>original: "bādhā-sthāna-pa"</note>: The obstruction houses were mentioned previously (Chapter 2, Verse 48). The period of the lord of one of those houses, or the period of a planet joined with that lord, brings grief and disease. This means: for whichever house is being analyzed, the period of its obstruction lord or a planet joined with it brings grief to that house. During the sub-period <gloss>= the minor period within a major period</gloss> of a planet situated in a square <gloss>= the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th position from that obstruction house</gloss>, there is distress and wandering in foreign lands. When the lords of the major period and sub-period are in a mutual <gloss>= to each other</gloss> sixth-eighth position <gloss>= one is six signs away from the other, and the other is eight signs away from the first</gloss>, one should predict fear, abandonment of one's country, and misfortune. However, if those two planets in the sixth-eighth relationship are friends or auspicious planets, one should declare the results to be mixed <gloss>= both good and bad</gloss>.

Here, as a relevant addition, are the Obstruction Houses:
> For a Movable sign, the 11th sign is the obstruction; for a Fixed sign, the 9th is the obstruction. 
> For a Dual sign, the 7th sign <note>original: "kāma-gṛha"</note> is the obstruction. Some say the squares to these three also act as obstructions.

**In Movable, Fixed, and Dual Ascendants, the lords of the 11th, 9th, and 7th houses respectively, and any planets situated in those houses, are called "Obstructions" (Badhaka). || 30 ||**

The period <term>dasha; a specific block of time in a person's life ruled by a planet</term> of the lord of the "Obstruction" house, as well as any planet associated with it, brings grief and disease. During the period of a planet situated in a cardinal house <term>kendra; the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses from the Obstruction lord</term> relative to that lord, one experiences suffering and travel to foreign lands. During the periods of planets placed in the 8th or 6th houses from each other, fear, exile from one's country, and calamities are predicted. However, if both planets are friends or naturally auspicious, the results are said to be mixed. || 30 ||

->Now the results of planetary periods based on the planet's condition are described:<-

**In the period of a "Blazing" (Dipta) planet, one becomes a king, possessing wealth, fame, generosity, and enjoyment of learning. In the period of a "Healthy" (Swastha) planet, one follows right conduct and religion, listens to sacred texts, and possesses great happiness, health, and wealth. || 31 ||**
**One gains royal favor, prosperity, and happiness during the period of a "Happy" (Mudita) planet. In the period of a "Calm" (Shanta) planet, one attains health, happiness, fortune, the favor of the king, and great enthusiasm. || 31 ||**
**In the period of a "Powerful" (Shakta) planet, there is learning, humility, wealth, success in penance, and an inclination toward religion. The period of an "Afflicted" (Pidita) planet brings fear from thieves, enemies, and rulers, and the death of a younger brother. ||**
**In the period of a "Miserable" (Dina) planet, there is poverty. The period of a "Mutilated" (Vikala) planet bestows grief and disease. The period of a "Wicked" (Khala) planet brings daily mental distress caused by enemies, and the period of a "Frightened" (Bhita) planet brings constant fear. || 32 ||**

Regarding the "Period" <note>original: "pāka"; another term for dasha</note>: The definitions for "Blazing" <note>Dipta; a planet in its exaltation sign</note> and the other states should be seen in the second chapter (Chapter 2, Verses 16–18). The rest is self-explanatory. || 31-32 ||

In the period of a "Blazing" planet, one becomes a king and enjoys wealth, sacrifices, learning, and entertainment. In the period of a "Healthy" planet <note>Swastha; a planet in its own sign</note>, one is endowed with good conduct, religious study, abundant happiness, health, and wealth. In the period of a "Happy" planet <note>Mudita; a planet in a friend's sign</note>, there is royal favor, prosperity, and happiness. In the period of a "Calm" planet <note>Shanta; a planet in an auspicious subdivision</note>, one attains health, comfort, wealth, the king’s pleasure, and enthusiasm. || 31 ||

In the period of a "Powerful" planet <note>Shakta; a planet that is bright and not eclipsed</note>, there is success in learning, humility, wealth, and penance, and a focus on religion. In the period of an "Afflicted" planet <note>Pidita; a planet defeated in planetary war or at the very end of a sign</note>, there is fear of thieves, enemies, and kings, and the death of a younger brother. In the period of a "Miserable" planet <note>Dina; a planet in its debilitation sign</note>, one faces poverty; the period of a "Mutilated" planet <note>Vikala; a planet eclipsed by the sun's rays</note> brings grief and disease. The period of a "Wicked" planet <note>Khala; a planet in a cruel subdivision</note> causes daily mental distress, and the period of a "Frightened" planet <note>Bhita; a planet in its highest acceleration</note> brings fear. || 32 ||

**Among the stars of the Ascendant, the Moon at birth, the phonetic Name, and the Moon at the time of a query—the wise say the results, whether good or bad, should be predicted according to the period of the one that is strongest. || 33 ||**

Now, to satisfy the questioner's curiosity regarding good or bad results, the method for determining the planetary period is given. <term>Vilagnatara</term> (Ascendant-star) = the constellation the Ascendant was in at the time of birth. <term>Indubham</term> (Moon-star) = the constellation the Moon was in at birth. <term>Namatara</term> (Name-star) = the constellation corresponding to the phonetic sound of one's given name. <term>Prashnendunakshatra</term> (Query-Moon-star) = the constellation the Moon is in at the moment a question is asked. Among these groups of constellations, <term>Baladhikartridashakramena</term> (by order of the strongest lord) = according to the sequence of whichever constellation's planetary lord is the strongest of all! The meaning is this: after determining the period lord for each of the aforementioned stars, one should state the auspicious or inauspicious results for the questioner based on the sequence of the lord who is most powerful. This is what the sages have said. || 33 ||

Great scholars have said that the auspicious or inauspicious results should be determined by the sequence of the strongest planetary lord among the birth Ascendant star, the birth Moon star, the phonetic name star, and the Moon star at the time of a query. || 33 ||

Again, explaining the sequence of period results in a different way, and the general results at the end of a period:

**The results of planetary periods may also follow the sequence starting from the "Produced Star" or from the birth Ascendant. At the conclusion of their periods, all planets generally produce inauspicious results for mankind. || 34 ||**

Regarding "Produced": The <term>Utpanna Nakshatra</term> (Produced Star) will be defined later <gloss>= "the fifth star from the birth star is called the 'Produced' star"</gloss>. From the <term>Vilagna</term> (Ascendant) = the star associated with the birth Ascendant. <header>Chapter on the Results of Periods || 18 ||</header>

The results of the periods <term>dasha; a planetary time-cycle</term> should be understood to occur in their proper sequence. Furthermore, all planets—whether naturally beneficial or harmful—generally produce unfavorable or "common" results for humans during the final portion of their periods. The core meaning is that toward the end of any planet's dasha, it usually bestows inauspicious results. || 34 ||

The results of the period will follow the sequence from the birth star or the Ascendant. At the conclusion of a period, all planets provide common, unfavorable results to mankind. || 34 ||

Now, the author explains the knowledge of the "Death-inflicting Period" for those with short, medium, or long lifespans—

->The period arising from the 5th star from the birth star is called "Produced" (Utpanna).<-
->The "Conception" (Adhana) period comes from the 8th star, and the "Great" (Maha) period from the 4th star.<-
->Death for living beings should be predicted at the end of these periods,<-
->occurring during the "Execution," "Calamity," or "Counter-agent" periods for those with long, short, or medium lifespans respectively. || 35 ||<-

Regarding the verse: The dasha related to the 5th star from the birth star <term>Janma Nakshatra; the star the Moon was in at birth</term> is designated as the "Produced" (Utpanna) dasha. The period related to the 8th star from the birth star is known by the name "Conception" (Adhana). The period related to the 4th star from the birth star is called the "Great" (Maha) dasha. 

For example: If someone's birth star is Rohini, then the period related to the star Pushya (the 5th star) is their "Produced" dasha. The period related to Purva Phalguni (the 8th star) is the "Conception" dasha. The period related to Punarvasu (the 4th star) is the "Great" dasha. 

The purpose of these names is then stated: At the conclusion of these "Produced," "Conception," or "Great" periods, during the final portion of one's life, they bring about death for humans. If one of these periods occurs when a person's life is nearing its natural end, death will occur during that dasha. 

Now, the specific timing for different lifespans is given: For those with a short lifespan (under 32 years), a medium lifespan (between 32 and 60 years), and a long lifespan (over 60 years), death should be predicted during the end of the "Calamity" (Vipat), "Counter-agent" (Pratyari), and "Execution" (Vadha) periods respectively. <note>These terms refer to the 3rd, 5th, and 7th stars in the 'Navatara' system used to categorize the relationship between stars.</note> 

As the sage Parashara also says:
> "Predict death in the 'Calamity' (Vipat) period for one born with a short-life combination. For one born with a medium-life combination, death occurs in the 'Counter-agent' (Pratyari) period. For those born with long-life combinations, death occurs in the 'Execution' (Vadha) period." || 35 ||

The 5th star from the birth star is the Utpanna dasha. The 8th is the Adhana dasha, and the 4th from the birth house is called the Mahadasha. One should predict death at the end of these periods. In a short-life combination, death occurs in the 3rd star's period; in a medium-life combination, in the 5th star's period; and in a full-life combination, death occurs in the 7th star's period. || 35 ||

### The Nirvana Period (The Period of Liberation)

->If birth is by day, calculate the Nirvana period from the star resulting from the sum of the Sun and Saturn.<-
->For a night birth, the period preceding the star resulting from the sum of the Moon and Rahu brings misfortune. || 36 ||<-

<insert>This verse was already explained in the chapter on Longevity (Chapter 5, Verse 72, Page 60). || 36 ||</insert>

If it is a day birth, one should calculate the "Liberation" (Nirvana) period from the star obtained by adding the clear longitudes of the Sun and Saturn. In a night birth, the Nirvana period is determined from the sum of the clear longitudes of the Moon and Rahu. || 36 ||

### The Gulika Period

->The period of the star in which Gulika is situated is also calculated.<-
->The lords of the sign and the Navamsha <note>a 1/9th divisional chart</note> where that star is located also assist in bringing about death. || 37 ||<-
