### The Period of Gulika based on its Longitude and Star

The following verse describes the "Gulika Dasha" <term>Gulika Dasha; a timing cycle based on Gulika, a mathematical point in the chart considered the son of Saturn and often associated with karmic debts and death</term>. The period is determined by the specific star (*Nakshatra*) in which Gulika is positioned at the time of birth. One should understand it this way: the planetary period sequence that begins with the star occupied by Gulika is designated as the "Gulika Dasha." During this time, the lords of the zodiac sign and the sub-division (*navamsha*) <term>navamsha; a 1/9th division of a zodiac sign, used to see the hidden strength of planets</term> where Gulika resides, along with any planets associated with them, become "death-inflicting." To put it simply: death is predicted during the periods of the lord of the sign Gulika occupies, the lord of the *navamsha* it occupies, or any planet that forms a relationship with Gulika. || 37 ||

One should calculate the period from the star in which Gulika is located. The lords of the sign and the sub-division associated with it, as well as their associates, bring death. || 37 ||

### Now, the Shula Dasha <note>Shula means "Trident," a weapon of Shiva. In astrology, Shula Dasha is a "death-inflicting" period.</note>

> The lords of the 3rd and 8th houses, the Sun and Venus, and the Moon and Mars are known as the significators (*karakas*). When the period of the "Trident" sign (*the 8th*) from these significators occurs... || 38 ||

<gloss>"The lifespan of the native is determined by the lords of the 3rd and 8th houses; the Sun and Venus signify the father, while the Moon and Mars signify the mother."</gloss>

> In all signs, beginning with the house where the significator is placed, when combined with years equal to half the cycle, there is happiness if the significator is strong and aspected by benefics. If the significators are in debility, enemy houses, or joined with malefics, the results are said to be unfavorable. || 39 ||

Regarding the phrase "The lords of the day" (*Dineshau*): Here, using the *Katapayadi* system <note>original: "कटपयवर्गत्वैरिरिहे" — a traditional alphanumeric code where 'Di' and 'ne' represent the number 8</note>, this refers to the 8th house. Their lords are the lord of the 8th and the lord of the 3rd (which is the 8th house from the 8th house). *Inashukrau* refers to the Sun and Venus. *Rajaro* refers to the King (Moon) and Mars (*Ara*). These are designated as significators. The core meaning is: the lords of the 3rd and 8th houses are the significators of longevity. The Sun and Venus are significators for the father. The Moon and Mars are significators for the mother. This meaning is clarified by the author in prose: (The lifespan of the native depends on the lords of the 3rd and 8th; Sun and Venus are father-significators, Moon and Mars are mother-significators). Furthermore: 

"The Sun and Venus signify the father; the Moon and Mars signify the mother," according to the sage Jaimini <note>original: "रविशुक्रयोः प्राणी जनकः । चन्द्रारयोर्जननी" — a quote from the Jaimini Sutras, an ancient foundational text of Indian astrology</note>. The purpose of this is explained in the second half of the verse: "in the Trident sign from the significator." This refers to the 8th sign from the respective significator. When the period of that 8th sign arrives, it brings death to that specific relative. The essence is that one should predict death during the period corresponding to the 8th house from each respective significator. || 38 ||

Regarding "In the house where the significator is placed": This means wherever a planet signifying a specific house is located. "In all signs": this rule is universal. "Combined with years equal to half the cycle": this refers to adding half the years of the *Kala-chakra-dasha* <term>Kala-chakra-dasha; the "Wheel of Time" period system, considered one of the most complex and accurate timing systems</term>. If the significator is strong, aspected by benefics, or joined with benefics, the wise say it brings happiness to that relative. If the significator is in its sign of debility, an enemy's house, or joined with malefics, misfortune is predicted. The meaning is: take the sign where the significator of a theme (good or bad) is located, add a half-cycle (6 signs), and in those resulting years, judge happiness or distress based on the nature of that significator. || 39 ||

The lord of the 3rd and 8th houses are the significators of life; the Sun and Venus signify the father, and the Moon and Mars signify the mother. When the period of the 8th (Trident) sign from these significators arrives, it brings death to that respective person. 
Whichever sign the significator occupies, add 6 signs to it. In those corresponding years, if the significator is aspected by or joined with benefics, predict happiness. If the significator is in debility, an enemy's house, or joined/aspected by malefics, misfortune should be predicted. || 39 ||

### Now, a Special Mahadasha <term>Mahadasha; a major planetary period that can last for years</term>

> The lord of the sub-division (*navamsha*) where the Moon is placed—if the Moon is aspected by or joined with that lord—the cycle-period of those planets gives special results, which I shall now describe.

# Chapter 18: On the Results of the Planetary Periods
<page-num>533</page-num>

> **If the Body sign is occupied by a malefic, there is great disease; if the Spirit sign is so occupied, there is confusion of the mind.** 
> **If both of these are joined by weak planets, death occurs during that period for men. || 40 ||**

Regarding this: The Moon—the indicator of the mind—is considered here. If the Moon is aspected by or joined with the lord of the constellation-portion (*Nakshatra-amsha*) where it is placed in the "Cycle Period" <term>Chakra Dasha; a specific timing system where the signs of the zodiac act as the time-lords</term>, then that particular portion of the cycle gives special results. Therefore, one should predict illness under such conditions. If the "Spirit" sign <note>In certain dasha systems, the starting sign is called the 'Body' (Deha) and the ending sign is called the 'Spirit' (Jiva).</note> is occupied by a malefic planet, it causes "spirit-confusion" or mental instability for the native. This occurs during its own sub-period. Furthermore, if both the "Body" and the "Spirit" signs are joined by planets lacking strength, one should predict the death of the person during that period. || 40 ||

If the lord of the constellation-portion where the Moon is situated aspects or is joined with the Moon, then that Cycle Period yields significant results. I shall describe them: If the "Body" sign is joined with a malefic planet <term>Papagraha; planets like Saturn, Mars, or the Sun that typically cause challenge</term>, there will be excessive disease in the body. If the "Spirit" sign is afflicted, there is mental confusion. If both these signs are joined by weak planets, the death of the person is predicted during that period. || 40 ||

### Now, the Specific Results of the Sub-periods

> **If a malefic planet is placed in the Ascendant, then during its major period and a malefic sub-period, there is much grief and disease.**
> **Loss of wealth and fear from the King and enemies occur for men; for a benefic planet, the sages say all these results are mixed. || 41 ||**

Now the author describes the specific results within a sub-period <term>Antardasha; a smaller time-unit within a major planetary period</term>. If a malefic—meaning one of the Sun, Mars, or Saturn—is placed in the Ascendant <term>Lagna; the rising sign at the time of birth</term>, then during its major period (specifically the period of a malefic in the Ascendant), and during a malefic sub-period, sages say there will be great grief, illness, loss of wealth, and fear of the King (government) and enemies. However, if during that time there is a sub-period of a benefic planet <term>Saumya; "gentle" planets like Jupiter, Venus, or Mercury</term>, the sages say the results mentioned above will be mixed (a combination of good and bad). || 41 ||

If a malefic planet is in the Ascendant, during the sub-period of a malefic within its major period, there will be much grief and illness. There will be destruction of wealth and fear from the government and enemies. In the sub-period of a benefic planet, the results are mixed; so say the holy sages. || 41 ||

> **During the period of the Lord of the Ascendant, in the sub-period of Saturn, loss of wealth,**
> **And disputes with dear kinsmen will occur; of this, there is no doubt. || 42 ||**

Now the author describes the result of Saturn’s sub-period during the major period of the Ascendant Lord. During the period of the Lord of the Ascendant, in the sub-period of Saturn <note>Original: "Manda-bhukti" – Manda is a name for Saturn, meaning "the slow one."</note>, one should predict the loss of wealth. Disputes with dear kinsmen will also occur. There is no doubt in this; it will certainly happen this way. Here, if Saturn and the Sun are also the lords of the Ascendant, one should consider this combination to be even more powerful. || 42 ||

During the period of the Lord of the Ascendant, in the sub-period of Saturn, there will undoubtedly be loss of wealth and opposition from beloved family members. || 42 ||

> **If the Lord of Wealth is a malefic planet, then during the sub-periods of Saturn, Mars, Rahu, and the Sun,**
> **They say destruction of wealth occurs; likewise if the second house is joined by malefics. || 43 ||**
> **If a malefic planet is placed in the house of wealth and is also its lord, in that period, due to the anger of the King,**
> **Loss of honor and wealth, imprisonment, displacement from one's position, and enmity with friends occurs. || 44 ||**

Now the results for the sub-periods during the period of the Lord of Wealth <term>Dhanadhipa; the planet that rules the 2nd house of the horoscope</term> are described. If the Lord of Wealth (the ruler of the 2nd house) is a malefic planet—one of the Sun, Mars, or Saturn—then during that major period, in the sub-periods of Saturn, Mars, Rahu, or the Sun, the great teachers say that destruction of wealth occurs. If the 2nd house itself is joined by malefic planets, the result is the same: loss of wealth during those malefic sub-periods. || 43 ||

If a certain malefic planet is placed in the 2nd house and is also the lord of that house, then during that period, due to the "wrath of the protector of the earth" (the King's anger), the person experiences loss of honor and wealth, and may face imprisonment...

(<gloss>Royal punishment [rajadanda] = death penalty/hanging</gloss>), displacement from one’s place = loss of position, enmity with friends = conflict with relatives, one should predict. || 44 ||

If the lord of the house of wealth <term>Dhanesha; the ruler of the 2nd house</term> is a malefic planet, then during the sub-periods of Saturn, Mars, Rahu, and the Sun, the destruction of wealth is said to occur. If the lord of the third house is a malefic planet and is joined by a malefic, then during the sub-periods of malefic planets, there is misery from enemies and thieves. Even if joined by benefics, the same result occurs. || 45 ||

During the major period of the lord of the third house, in the sub-periods of Saturn, Mars, Ketu, and the Sun, one should predict the destruction of siblings and conflict with younger brothers. || 46 ||

**During the major period of the lord of the fourth house when it is not a benefic, and during the sub-period of a malefic planet, the sages say there will be displacement, conflict with relatives, and destruction of agriculture, cattle, and wealth. || 47 ||**

Now he describes the results of the period of the lord of the fourth house <term>Chaturthesha; the ruler of the house representing the home, mother, and lands</term> in a verse of simple meaning. || 47 ||

If the lord of the fourth house is a malefic planet, then during the sub-period of a malefic planet, the teachers say there will be displacement, conflict with relatives, and destruction of agriculture and cattle-wealth. || 47 ||

**In the sub-period of a malefic during the major period of the lord of the house of children, they say there is fear from the king and suffering for the beloved son. During the sub-period of a benefic, there is gain of children and wealth, affection from the king and relatives, and the fulfillment of desires. || 48 ||**

Now he describes the results of the sub-periods in the major period of the lord of the fifth house. <gloss>The lord of the house of children [sutarashipasya] = the owner of the fifth house</gloss>; <gloss>in the period [pake] = during the major dasha</gloss>; <gloss>in the sub-period of a malefic [papapaharasamaye]</gloss>; <gloss>fear of the king [nripalabhayam]</gloss>; <gloss>suffering of the beloved son [ishtasutarti] = affliction of friends and sons, so they say</gloss>. Furthermore, in that same period of the lord of the fifth house, <gloss>during the sub-period of a benefic [saumyapaharasamaye]</gloss>, <gloss>gain of children and wealth [sutavittalabham]</gloss>, <gloss>affection from the king and relatives [urvishabandhujanalalanam] = love from the king and kinsmen</gloss>, <gloss>fulfillment of desires [ishtasiddhim] = success of one’s wishes and goals</gloss>, so say the wise. || 48 ||

During the sub-period of a malefic in the major period of the lord of the fifth house, fear of the king and suffering for the beloved son is mentioned. In the sub-period of a benefic planet, there will be gain of children and wealth, and the king and relatives will show love, and desires will be fulfilled. || 48 ||

**During the major period of the lord of the sixth house, in the sub-period of non-benefics, there is fear from the king and fire, addictions, and disease. In the period of the lord of the house of the spouse, during the sub-period of a malefic, the wise say there is the destruction of the wife and wandering. || 49 ||**

Now he describes the results of the sub-periods in the major periods of the lords of the sixth and seventh houses. Here, since the results during malefic sub-periods are said to be inauspicious, one should consider that during benefic sub-periods, the results must be auspicious. || 49 ||

In the major period of the lord of the sixth house <term>Shashthesha; the ruler of the house of debt, enemies, and illness</term>, during the sub-period of planets other than benefics, fear of the king, fear of fire, addiction, and disease occur. In the major period of the lord of the seventh house, during the sub-period of a malefic, the destruction of the wife and disease occurs. In the major period of the lord of the seventh house, during the sub-period of a malefic, the learned say there is destruction of the wife and traveling to foreign lands. || 49 ||

**When the period of the lord of the eighth house arrives, in a malefic sub-period, one should predict fear of enemies, the destruction of life, wealth, and fame, wandering, or displacement for men. In the period of the lord of the house of fortune, during the sub-period of a malefic, there is the death of the father, loss of religious merit, imprisonment, and [loss of] the accumulation of wealth. || 50 ||**

# Chapter 18: The Results of Planetary Periods (Dasha-phala)

Now he describes the results during the major periods of the lords of the eighth and ninth houses when a malefic planet’s sub-period occurs. Here, inauspicious results are stated for the sub-periods <term>Antardasha; a secondary cycle within a major period</term> of malefic planets. By implication, during the major period of the lord of the eighth house, one should predict auspicious results during the sub-period of a benefic planet. || 50 ||

During the major period of the lord of the eighth house <term>Ashtamesha; the ruler of the house of longevity and transformations</term>, in a malefic sub-period, a person may experience victory over enemies but also the destruction of life and wealth, travel to foreign lands, or displacement from one's position. During the major period of the lord of the ninth house <term>Dharmesha; the ruler of the house of fortune and religion</term>, there may be the death of parents or a tendency toward unrighteousness; specifically, during the sub-period of Rahu <note>The North Node of the Moon, often associated with sudden disruptions.</note>, imprisonment and the loss of wealth occur. || 50 ||

**During the major period of the lord of the tenth house, if it is a malefic planet, and during the sub-periods of other malefic planets, one experiences distress to loved ones, loss of position, loss of happiness and fame, and the depletion of wealth. During the major period of the lord of the eleventh house, in the sub-periods of Saturn, the Sun, Rahu, and Mars, the wise understand that there will be a loss of happiness, the destruction of agriculture and other ventures, fear of the king, and the loss of wealth. || 51 ||**

Now he states the results for the sub-periods of the lords of the tenth and eleventh houses with a verse of simple meaning. || **If the lord of the tenth house <term>Karmesha; the ruler of the house of career and actions</term> is a malefic planet and its sub-periods are also ruled by malefic planets, there will be pain for loved ones, loss of position, destruction of happiness and reputation, and loss of money. During the major period of the lord of the eleventh house <term>Labhesha; the ruler of the house of gains</term>, in the sub-periods of Saturn, Mars, the Sun, and Rahu, one should recognize the destruction of happiness, crops, etc., fear of the government <note>original: "nṛpa-bhayaṃ" or fear of the king/authorities</note>, and loss of wealth. || 51 ||**

**During the major period of the lord of the twelfth house, in the sub-periods of the Sun, Saturn, and Mars, there is enmity with one’s wife, children, and relatives. There is a loss of strength, honor, and wealth. In the sub-period of Rahu, they say there is a danger of poison. || 52 ||**

With this verse, he describes the results for the period of the lord of the twelfth house <term>Vyayesha; the ruler of the house of loss and liberation</term>. The meaning of the verse is clear. Regarding the results of all the aforementioned house lords, one must consider this: in the major period of any house lord, malefic sub-periods bring inauspicious results, and benefic sub-periods bring auspicious results. If the house lord itself is a malefic, then the inauspicious results in a malefic sub-period should be predicted in full. Similarly, during the major period of a benefic house lord, the results in a benefic sub-period will be even more auspicious. However, if a benefic period has a malefic sub-period, or a malefic period has a benefic sub-period, mixed results should be predicted after careful comparison.

**In the major period of the lord of the twelfth house, during the sub-periods of the Sun, Saturn, and Mars, enmity with wife, son, and family, loss of physical strength, and loss of honor and wealth are predicted; in the sub-period of Rahu, the fear of poison <note>This could refer to literal poisoning, venomous bites, or metaphorical "toxic" situations.</note> is mentioned. || 52 ||**

**When two planets are in a mutual sixth-eighth relationship, during their overlapping major and sub-periods, men suffer loss of position or death. When two weak planets are situated together in the same house, one should predict death during the time of their overlapping periods. || 53 ||**

Regarding the mutual relationship: When two planets are placed in the sixth and eighth positions from each other <note>This "Shashtashtama" position is considered highly medicinal or antagonistic in Vedic astrology.</note>, during their overlapping major and sub-periods, men will face displacement or death. "Situated together" means if two planets are in the same house and are "powerless" <term>durbala; lacking structural strength</term>, during their overlapping periods, one should predict the death of the person. || 53 ||

**In the mutual sub-periods of the lord of the sixth and the lord of the eighth, men experience loss of position or death. If both are in one place, death is predicted during their period. The same result is predicted during the period of a weak planet. || 53 ||**

**When the sub-period of a malefic planet arrives during the major period of a malefic planet, the death of that person will undoubtedly occur. || 54 ||**

The meaning is clear. However, death should not be predicted during the period of just any ordinary malefic planet; rather, it must be considered that if this malefic is the lord of a "difficult house" <note>Specifically the 2nd, 7th (marakas or death-inflicting houses), 6th, 8th, or 12th houses.</note>, then such a result should definitely be spoken. || 54 ||

**If a malefic sub-period is reached during a malefic major period, that native will undoubtedly die. ||**

**Malefic planets situated in malefic signs, aspected by enemies, and joined with enemy planets—one should recognize death during their period. || 55 ||**
**During the sub-periods of a planet that is an enemy to the lord of the major period, the time of death will certainly occur, especially if that planet is a malefic. || 56 ||**

Now the death-inflicting periods are described. Malefic planets <term>Papa-grahas; planets like Mars, Saturn, Rahu, and Ketu that typically bring challenges</term>, if situated in cruel signs <note>original: "krura-rashi"; signs like Aries or Scorpio or those ruled by malefics</note>, or if aspected by or conjoined with enemy planets, then during their major period and within a malefic sub-period, a person’s death may occur.

If that enemy planet is also a malefic, death is certain to occur during its sub-cycle. The implication is that the person will surely pass away at that time. || 55-56 ||

*If malefic planets are in cruel signs, are aspected by their enemies, or are joined with enemy planets, death occurs in their period.* || 55 ||

*The time of death will definitely be in the sub-period of a planet that is an enemy to the major period lord (specifically in a malefic sub-period).* || 56 ||

> When a malefic planet enters its major period, the results stemming from its exaltation and similar dignities manifest at the beginning. Results stemming from its house position manifest in the middle of the period. The wise say that results arising from the aspects of all malefic planets manifest at the end of the period. || 57 ||

Now he explains when the results generated by the exaltation, house position, and aspects of malefic planets come to fruition. For a malefic planet, results from its exaltation, root-trine <note>original: "mula-trikona"; a specific high-strength position for a planet</note>, or its own sign manifest at the very beginning of the major period's commencement. Results related to the house it occupies manifest in the middle of the period. The wise say that for all malefic planets, results arising from their aspects manifest at the very end of the period.

*The results of a malefic planet's exaltation occur at the start of the dasha; the house-based results of malefics occur in the middle; and great people say the results of the aspects of all malefic planets occur at the end.* || 57 ||

> For benefic planets, the results of their house position occur at the start of the period; those arising from their specific sign placement occur in the middle. At the end of the period, results from aspects manifest. In this way, all the teachers describe the distinctions within the stellar periods. || 58 ||

Now he explains when the results generated by the house, sign, and aspects of benefic planets <term>Shubha-grahas; planets like Jupiter, Venus, and a waxing Moon</term> come to fruition. For benefic planets, house-based results occur at the beginning of the period. Results from the specific sign position occur in the middle. Results arising from aspects occur at the end. All the great teachers describe the variations in the stellar periods <term>Nakshatra-dasha; time cycles based on the Moon's position in the lunar mansions</term> in this exact manner. || 58 ||

->This concludes the collective results of the stellar periods.<-

*The house-born results of a benefic planet occur at the beginning of the dasha. The sign-based results of that planet occur in the middle. Results arising from aspects occur at the end. In this way, scholars describe the sub-divisions for all stars.* || 58 ||

## Chapter 18: Results of Planetary Periods

### Now, the Calculation of Sub-periods.

> Multiply the years of the major period by the years of the sub-period lord. The first digit of the result (the units place) multiplied by three gives the days; the remaining digits represent the months. This is the sequence for determining sub-periods. || 60 ||

Now, the author explains the method for calculating the sub-period <term>Antardasha; a shorter time cycle nested within a major planetary period</term> which was mentioned previously (Chapter 17, Verse 107). To find the sub-period of any planet within a specific major period <term>Dasha; a major life cycle ruled by a planet</term>, multiply the years assigned to the major period lord by the years assigned to the sub-period lord. In the resulting product, the first digit (the units place) should be set aside; the remaining digits are known as the months. Then, take that first digit which was set aside and multiply it by three; the result is the number of days. This is how the order of sub-periods is known.

**Example:** If one needs to calculate the sub-period of Mars within the major period of the Sun:
The Sun's major period = 6 years.
Mars's major period = 7 years.
Their product: 6 x 7 = 42.
In this result (42), the first digit is 2. The remaining digit (4) represents 4 months. The first digit (2) is then tripled: 2 x 3 = 6 days.
Therefore, the sub-period of Mars within the Sun's major period is 4 months and 6 days. This same result is reached using the method previously mentioned (Chapter 17, Verse 107), which uses the 120-year total cycle: 6 x 7 ÷ 120 = 0 years, 4 months, 6 days. || 60 ||

---

To find the sub-period of a planet within a major period, multiply the dasha years of both. In the product, triple the units digit to get the days, and the remaining digits represent the months. || 60 ||

### Now, the Results of Sub-periods within the Sun's Major Period.

**Sun–Sun:** One attains wealth through Brahmins <term>Dvija; the scholarly or priestly class</term>, kings, or the study of scriptures, but may suffer from mental distress and travel through foreign lands or forests.

->*When the Moon is in the Sun's major period.* || 62 ||<-

**Sun–Mars:** One acquires gems, gold, and wealth, and enjoys the affection of the King (or authorities). However, one may suffer from diseases related to bile <term>Pitta; one of the three humors in Ayurveda, associated with heat and metabolism</term>.
->*When Mars (Kuja) is in the Sun's major period.* || 63 ||<-

**Sun–Rahu:** One faces the fear of untimely death, suffering for one's kinsmen, loss of position, and mental grief.
->*Even though the Sun is powerful, when Rahu (the North Node) enters its period.* || 64 ||<-

**Sun–Jupiter:** One is respected by all, gains wealth through one's children, and engages in the worship of gods and Brahmins. This period brings good deeds and virtuous company.
->*When Jupiter (Guru) is in the Sun's major period.* || 65 ||<-

**Sun–Saturn:** One faces universal enmity, laziness, a decline in occupation, and mental illness. There is also fear of kings and thieves.
->*When Saturn (Shani) is in the Sun's major period.* || 66 ||<-

**Sun–Mercury:** One suffers from trouble to relatives, mental grief, and loss of wealth despite great enthusiasm; only a small amount of happiness is attained.
->*When Mercury (Budha) is in the Sun's major period.* || 67 ||<-

**Sun–Ketu:** One suffers from throat diseases, mental agony, or eye diseases, and faces the risk of untimely death.
->*When Ketu (the South Node) is in the Sun's major period.* || 68 ||<-

**Sun–Venus:** One attains wealth from water-related sources but suffers from exhaustion and the company of base women, and engages in useless or "dry" arguments.

# From the Jataka Parijata with Commentary

> When the Sun is in its sign of debilitation <note>original: "neeche"; the sign where a planet's influence is weakest—for the Sun, this is Libra</note> but resides in an exaltation <term>Navamsha; a one-ninth divisional chart used to see the hidden strength of a planet</term>, the native attains the splendor of a king during its major period. They experience happiness, though toward the end of the period, there may be a loss of wealth or even death. || 71 ||

Now, the results for the sub-periods <term>Antardasha; a shorter cycle nested within a major period</term> of all the planets during the major period of the Sun are described. The results given here are general. One should adjust the intensity of these results based on the specific house placement and strength of the planets in an individual's birth chart. Because these verses are straightforward, they are not explained in further detail. || 61 - 71 ||

**During the major period of the Sun, if the Sun is also in its sub-period, the person gains wealth through Brahmins, kings, or weapons. However, they may suffer from mental illness and travel through foreign lands or forests. || 61 ||**

**When the Moon’s sub-period occurs during the Sun’s major period, wealth is obtained from family and friends. There may be errors or negligence caused by friends, and suffering from <term>Pandu; an ancient term for jaundice or anemia-related conditions</term>. || 62 ||**

**If Mars’s sub-period occurs during the Sun’s major period, one acquires gems, gold, and wealth. It brings success in politics and auspicious events, but also an increase in <term>Pitta; the 'fire' humor in Ayurveda, often causing fever or inflammation</term>. || 63 ||**

**During the sub-period of Rahu in the Sun’s major period, there is the risk of untimely death, great distress, harassment of one's family, loss of rank or position, and mental sorrow. || 64 ||**

**When Jupiter’s sub-period occurs during the Sun’s major period, the person becomes highly respected. They gain wealth through their children, perform worship of gods and Brahmins, practice virtuous conduct, and enjoy good company. || 65 ||**

**If Saturn’s sub-period occurs during the Sun’s major period, everyone becomes an enemy. It brings laziness, a poor livelihood, mental illness, and fear of the government or thieves. || 66 ||**

**During the sub-period of Mercury in the Sun’s major period, there is trouble for relatives and mental grief. The person lacks motivation, loses wealth, and finds only the slightest amount of happiness. || 67 ||**

**In the sub-period of Ketu during the Sun’s major period, one suffers from throat diseases, mental agitation, and eye diseases, and faces the risk of untimely death. || 68 ||**

**When Venus’s sub-period occurs during the Sun’s major period, wealth from water-related sources is gained effortlessly. However, one may fall into the company of wicked women and engage in pointless arguments. || 69 ||**

**At the beginning of the Sun’s major period, the father may fall ill and wealth may be lost. In the middle of the period, all sorts of obstacles arise. It is only at the end of the period that happiness is achieved. || 70 ||**

**If the Sun is in its sign of exaltation but sits in a debilitated Navamsha, the results include disgrace, fear, and the death of children, wife, father’s kin, or relatives, along with losses in agriculture. Conversely, if the Sun is in its sign of debilitation but sits in an exalted Navamsha, the native gains royal wealth and happiness, though they may face loss of wealth or death as the period closes. || 71 ||**

The person becomes rich with flowers, fine clothing, ornaments, perfumes, and various grains. The native is surrounded by flowers, clothing, jewelry, perfumes, and many types of food. If the Moon is weak, it leads to financial loss and wind-related illnesses. || 72 ||**

### Now, the results of the sub-periods within the major period of the Moon.

**Moon-Moon**—During the sub-period <term>Antardasha; a minor cycle within a major planetary period</term> of the Moon within its own major period, the native finds delight in knowledge, women, singing, and music. One acquires silk garments and enjoys the company of virtuous people and physical comforts. Honored by kings, ministers, and army commanders, the person gains good fame, goes on pilgrimages, and receives affection from children and friends. This time brings gains of land, cattle, and horses, along with great wealth and prosperity. || 73 || <note>original: "himagu"; a poetic name for the Moon meaning 'the cool-rayed one'</note>

**Moon-Mars**—When Mars <note>original: "kuja"; meaning 'the one born of the earth'</note> enters the sub-period of the Moon, there is disease, a tendency toward conflict, loss of one's position or home, and a depletion of wealth. Distress arises due to friends and brothers. || 74 ||

**Moon-Rahu**—During Rahu's <term>the North Node of the Moon, often associated with sudden upheaval</term> sub-period within the Moon's major cycle, one suffers from fear of enemies and disease. There is a loss of relatives and wealth; the person finds no happiness at all. || 75 ||

**Moon-Jupiter**—Through Jupiter’s <note>original: "jiva"; meaning 'the living being' or 'source of life'</note> sub-period in the Moon’s cycle, one acquires various forms of wealth, including vehicles. Prosperity comes in the form of clothing and jewelry. Tasks are successfully accomplished through personal effort. || 76 ||

**Moon-Saturn**—In the sub-period of Saturn during the Moon’s major period, the native's mother suffers. There is mental grief and afflictions caused by <term>Vata and Pitta; the Ayurvedic biological humors representing air/motion and fire/metabolism</term>. The native may experience "stagnant speech" <note>likely referring to a stutter or being silenced</note> and arguments with enemies. || 77 ||

**Moon-Mercury**—When Mercury enters the sub-period of the Moon, wealth is gained through the mother’s family. The person finds refuge and support among learned people and acquires clothing and ornaments. || 78 ||

**Moon-Ketu**—During the sub-period of Ketu <term>the South Node of the Moon, often associated with detachment or hidden ailments</term>, there is illness related to women, loss of relatives, and suffering from stomach diseases. One experiences a loss of property and money. || 79 ||

**Moon-Venus**—During the sub-period of Venus <note>original: "bhrigu"; referring to the lineage of the sage Bhrigu</note> within the Moon’s cycle, one gains wealth through women, agriculture, and livestock. There is happiness and the arrival of pleasant news or speech. However, the mother may suffer from illness. || 80 ||

**Moon-Sun**—In the sub-period of the Sun <note>original: "ravi"</note> during the Moon’s major period, one attains splendor almost like that of a king. Diseases are cured, enemies are defeated, and the native experiences comfort and auspiciousness. || 81 ||

**Special Rule**—Experts say that at the beginning of a sub-period, the results of the "house" <term>Bhava; the specific area of life like career or family</term> are felt. In the middle, the results of the "zodiac sign" <term>Rashi; the constellation the planet resides in</term> manifest. At the end of the period, the results regarding the body and those based on "aspects" <term>Drishti; the influence planets cast upon each other</term> are realized. || 82 ||

Now, the results of all planetary sub-periods within the major period of the Moon are explained. These results are stated here in a general sense. However, one should adjust the intensity and specifics of these results based on the actual strength and placement of the planets in a specific birth chart. Since these verses are clear in their meaning, further commentary is omitted. || 73-82 ||

---

In the major period of the Moon, if it is the sub-period of the Moon: there is affection for knowledge, women, singing, and music; acquisition of silk clothes, the company of good people, bodily happiness, and honor from kings, ministers, and generals. One gains good fame, goes on pilgrimages, feels love from sons and friends, and gains land, cows, and horses, leading to great wealth and majesty. || 73 ||

In the major period of the Moon, if it is the sub-period of Mars: there is disease, a mind prone to opposition, destruction of one's place, loss of wealth, and distress through friends and brothers. || 74 ||

In the major period of the Moon, if it is the sub-period of Rahu: there is distress from enemies and disease, loss of kinsmen, depletion of wealth, and no happiness is attained. || 75 ||

In the major period of the Moon, if it is the sub-period of Jupiter: there is the acquisition of vehicles and various types of wealth, prosperity of clothes and jewelry, and the accomplishment of work through effort. || 76 ||

In the major period of the Moon, if it is Saturn: there is pain to the mother, sorrow in the mind, suffering from <term>Vata and Pitta</term> ailments, stagnant speech, and one becomes prone to arguing with enemies. || 77 ||

In the major period of the Moon, if it is the sub-period of Mercury: there is gain of wealth from the mother's side, excellent support from learned people, and the acquisition of clothes and ornaments. || 78 ||
